intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers corn (maize) farming as a complete process—land preparation, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling. It also includes growing corn specifically to produce seed grains, but excludes sweet corn farming.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, 100% foreign ownership is permitted for this activity. However, Bali specifically classifies it as a reserved basic agricultural sector, so a foreign-owned company (PMA) cannot be registered under this KBLI in Bali. Investors must look outside Bali or consider alternative structures.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Pertanian Jagung (01111)? This is classified as Medium-High risk with PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through the requirements.
intel_2026.baliContext: Agriculture in Bali centers around rice (subak system), coffee (Kintamani highlands), and tropical fruits/vegetables. Foreign investment in agriculture is common for farm-to-table concepts, organic farming, and agritourism. Land use requires coordination with local subak (irrigation cooperative) and compliance with spatial planning (RTRW).
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to run a large-scale corn cultivation or seed production business, but who are willing to operate outside of Bali due to the local restriction.

editorial.headline: Corn Farming With a Bali Registration Wall
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers ordinary corn cultivation and seed production, nationally open to foreign ownership but closed to PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign founder looking at corn farming in Bali, the practical answer comes before the agronomy: this activity cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today. The national record says the activity is open, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100, but the Bali layer changes the operational outcome. Bali marks the activity as TERTUTUP, and the stated reason is direct: reserved basic staple-crop agriculture is closed to PMA registration in the province. The moratorium is also broad, blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island.

Substantively, the activity is straightforward agricultural production of corn. It includes preparing land, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one integrated corn-farming operation. The scope also extends to corn seed activity, including cultivation to produce seed in grain form, as well as nursery and seed-production work connected to the corn crop. In plain English, this is not a narrow trading or processing category; it is the field-level business of growing corn, including the seed side, when the work remains part of the same cultivation chain.

The scale signal is unusually broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as open scales. That matters for domestic structuring, because the record does not reserve the activity to only one size band. But scale openness is not the same as location permission for foreign capital. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign ownership line reads 100, so the national investment table does not itself impose a lower foreign-share cap here.

The honest reading is therefore split but not ambiguous. On the national layer, this is an open corn-farming activity with full stated foreign ownership. In Bali, for PMA registration, it is blocked. A founder can use the scope to understand exactly what the activity covers, and can use the scale line to see that the activity is not confined to one enterprise size. But for a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the decisive field is the Bali status: TERTUTUP.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, for PMA registration, it is blocked.

l4_bali.reason: Reserved basic (staple-crop) agriculture — closed to PMA registration in Bali.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This group covers farming of cereal crops other than rice and corn, such as wheat, oats, sorghum, barley, rye, and foxtail millet. It includes the full cycle of land preparation, planting, cultivation, harvesting, and post-harvest activities performed as a continuous process. It also covers the cultivation of these non-rice, non-corn cereals specifically to produce seeds in the form of grains.

editorial.headline: Growing Non-Rice, Non-Maize Cereals Under KBLI 01112
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01112 covers integrated cultivation of cereals such as wheat, sorghum, barley, rye, and millet, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01112 is the agricultural code for cereal farming outside rice and maize. Its scope is not a narrow commodity label; it covers the working sequence of cultivation itself: land preparation, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one integrated farming activity. The record names wheat and oats, sorghum or cantel, barley, rye, millet, and similar cereals. It also includes seed production where the cereal crop is grown to produce seed in the form of grain.

That matters because this code is about an operating farm activity, not only the trading or handling of grain after someone else has grown it. A business using this code is identifying itself with the cultivation cycle: preparing the land, growing the crop, maintaining it through the season, harvesting it, and, where relevant, completing post-harvest work as part of the same agricultural chain. For founders, the practical reading is simple: the code belongs to businesses whose primary activity is growing these non-rice, non-maize cereals, including wheat seed cultivation where the same integrated field-to-post-harvest sequence applies.

The scale position is broad. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not reserved only for a single business size. Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also clear on the record: PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no foreign share cap below full ownership in the record, so the national reading is that foreign ownership is open up to 100% for this activity.

The Bali reading is more nuanced, but in this case it does not reverse the national position. The record states that Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently, but this activity is marked l4_bali_blocked: false. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In plain terms, the honest conclusion is not that every foreign-owned agricultural idea is automatically easy in Bali; it is that this specific code, on this record, is nationally foreign-open and is not currently marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Soybean Farming With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01113 covers the integrated cultivation of soybeans, with foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01113 is a clean agricultural classification for soybean farming. Its core activity is the practical chain of growing soybeans: preparing the land, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and carrying out post-harvest work when those steps form one connected farming operation. The record also brings soybean seed activity into the same frame when it is part of the soybean crop cycle. In plain terms, this is not a trading, processing, or advisory category; it is the agricultural work of producing soybeans from land to harvest, including the crop-handling steps that belong to that same farming sequence.

That integrated character matters because it defines who this code is for. A founder registering under it is not merely touching soybeans at one isolated point. The activity described is cultivation-led: land preparation, planting, crop care, harvest, and post-harvest as a single operational chain. The record opens this classification across every business scale listed: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means it is not reserved only for a large plantation-style setup, nor confined to the smallest agricultural operator. It can describe a small farming enterprise, a medium agricultural business, or a larger soybean cultivation operation, provided the registered activity remains within the scope stated in the record.

Nationally, the position on foreign investment is clear. Its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. So, on the national record supplied here, this is a classification a foreign-owned company may use without a foreign shareholding cap below full ownership. That is the decisive national point: the activity is open for PMA, and the ceiling given in the record reaches 100%. There is no basis in the slim record to add extra capital thresholds, licensing steps, special permits, tax treatments, or timing assumptions, so the clean reading is simply that the national PMA door is open for this soybean farming activity.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The record says this code is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but the Bali reason states that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a hidden warning dressed up as access: a foreign investor can read this record as nationally open and not Bali-blocked, while still staying within the exact agricultural scope of soybean cultivation and seed activity described here.

editorial.headline: Peanut Farming with a Clear PMA Path in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers peanut cultivation as an integrated farm operation, and the record treats it as open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Peanut farming under this activity is a practical agricultural classification: the growing of peanuts from land preparation through planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one continuous operation. The record also brings seed production into the same frame when it follows that integrated chain for peanut plants. In plain English, this is not merely the moment of harvest or a loose trading activity around peanuts. It is the farm-side cultivation cycle itself, including the preparatory and finishing work that belongs to a single peanut-growing enterprise.

That integrated nature matters for founders choosing how to register the activity. A business using this classification is describing a peanut cultivation operation, potentially including the seed-business side, so long as the work remains tied to the cultivation sequence described in the record. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which makes it unusually broad in the way it can fit different operating sizes. A small grower, a mid-sized agricultural operator, or a larger farming venture can all sit inside the scale range shown here, without the record forcing the activity into only one end of the business spectrum.

The national foreign-investment position is also straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under the stated Perpres source. That means the national reading is not a capped minority position; the record does not impose a reduced foreign-stake ceiling. For a PMA planning exercise, the clean national conclusion is therefore that this peanut-farming activity is foreign-open at the full percentage shown in the record, subject only to facts that are actually recorded here.

The Bali picture is often where agricultural classifications become more delicate, but this record gives a clear answer. Bali's moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, yet this activity is not marked as blocked. The stated reason is that OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical terms, the honest lede is not a warning that foreigners cannot register it in Bali today. It is the opposite: on the slim record provided, this activity is nationally open to PMA and has a Bali status of OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with no Bali PMA block recorded.

editorial.headline: Mung Bean Farming, Fully Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01115 covers the full farming cycle for mung beans, including seed activity, with access across all business scales and no Bali PMA moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01115 is a plain agricultural code, but not a narrow one. It covers mung bean farming as a complete field-to-post-harvest activity: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps form one integrated chain. The same scope also includes mung bean seed activity when it follows that same integrated agricultural cycle. In practical terms, this is not a code for a detached trading desk or an isolated processing business. Its center of gravity is cultivation, with post-harvest work included only where it remains part of the mung bean farming operation itself.

That scope matters because the record opens the activity across the full scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A local farmer, a small producer, a medium agribusiness, or a larger agricultural operator can all sit within this classification if the registered activity is genuinely mung bean farming and the post-harvest steps are part of the same farming sequence. The English reading should stay close to the Indonesian wording: this is agriculture for kacang hijau, including seed cultivation, not a general umbrella for every downstream mung bean product or commercial channel.

The national foreign-investment position is clean. With PMA status marked TERBUKA, foreign ownership may reach 100%. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the editorial conclusion should be equally direct: nationally, this activity is open to foreign-owned registration up to full foreign ownership. The source field is the investment-list reference, but the important operational point is the status and ceiling given in the record, not an invented layer of sectoral conditions.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is better than many low-risk activities face on the island. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration island-wide, but this record marks KBLI 01115 as not blocked. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That does not turn the code into a casual registration choice; it simply means the Bali-specific PMA block does not apply on the facts provided. The honest read is therefore straightforward: a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today under the record’s national openness and Bali status, provided the registered business is truly mung bean farming within this scope.

editorial.headline: Field Beans With a Clear Path for Bali PMA Registration
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01116 covers the full farming cycle for assorted horticultural beans, and the record shows it is open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01116 is a farming activity for assorted beans other than soybeans, peanuts, and mung beans. In practical terms, it is the cultivation of horticultural bean crops such as buncis, long beans, red beans, peas, winged beans, lentils, lupin, pigeon peas, cow peas, and other comparable varieties named in the record. Its scope is not a single field task. It covers the agricultural chain when handled as one integrated activity: land preparation, seeding or nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling.

That integrated character matters. A founder using this activity code is not simply describing trade in beans or a detached post-harvest service. The record points to farming itself, including nursery and seedling activities for assorted horticultural beans, and the field operations that make cultivation complete. It is a suitable frame for operators whose business identity is rooted in growing these crops, whether the operation is modest, expanding, or already structured at larger scale.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not reserved only for large agribusiness, nor confined to smallholders. It can describe a business across the full scale ladder recorded here, provided the registered activity remains within the stated farming scope: assorted bean cultivation, nursery or seedling work, and the connected land, planting, maintenance, harvest, and post-harvest sequence.

The foreign-investment picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. In Bali, the record does not show a PMA block. The Bali moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record’s Bali reason says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is simple: for this activity, the record supports a foreign-owned setup nationally, and it does not mark Bali as closed today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Oilseed Farming With a Bali Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers edible-oil seed cultivation, nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali registration depends on the exact OSS risk scope declared.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01117 is the farming lane for edible-oil seed crops.** Its scope is agricultural production of seeds used to make cooking oil, with the record naming sesame, canola, safflower, and sunflower seeds as examples. The activity is not just the moment of harvest. It can cover the full cultivation chain when those steps are carried out as one integrated activity: land preparation, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling. The record also brings seedling and seed-production activity for these oilseed crops into the same practical frame.

That makes this a production code for operators whose real business is growing the crop, not merely trading, processing, branding, or distributing the final oil. A registrant should be able to describe the agricultural activity in the language of the scope: preparing the land, planting and maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the immediate post-harvest stage as part of one farming sequence. The crop examples matter because they anchor the code in edible-oil-producing grains and seeds, rather than in a broader or more speculative agricultural description.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved only for large plantations or industrial operators. A small grower, a mid-sized agricultural venture, or a larger farming company may all sit within the scale field if the declared business activity remains the cultivation of edible-oil seed crops described above. Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is also clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the record supports full foreign ownership nationally.

Bali is more careful. The record does not mark this code as outright blocked for Bali PMA registration, but it does flag the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent). The reason is specific: OSS risk at Besar scale may be low for some scopes and higher for others, and Bali’s province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. So the honest reading is not “blocked everywhere” and not “automatically easy.” It is scope-dependent: a PMA registration in Bali may be possible only where the exact declared activity is treated as the higher-risk scope in OSS, and that must be verified live against the precise activity being registered.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not “blocked everywhere” and not “automatically easy”: Bali turns this into a scope test.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices
moratorium.virtual_office: requested in letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP; application not confirmed

l4_bali.rule: per-scala-Besar (OSS risk at scale Besar; PMA is Besar by law)

editorial.headline: Non-Edible Oilseed Farming That Bali Leaves Open to PMA
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated farming and seed production for non-edible oil-bearing grains, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01118 is a farming activity, but its focus is narrow and industrial rather than culinary. It covers oil-bearing grains that are not grown for cooking oil: cottonseed, flaxseed, mustard seed, niger seed, castor seed, and comparable non-edible oilseed crops named in the scope. The agricultural chain is also part of the definition. Land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work all sit within the activity when they are carried out as one integrated sequence. The same record also places nursery and seed-production activity for these non-edible oilseed plants inside the scope.

That matters because this is not merely a label for a crop. It is a registration home for operators whose business is the cultivation system around those crops, from seed or seedling activity through the field cycle and into post-harvest handling when those steps form one business line. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it is not reserved only for a single enterprise size. A small grower, a medium operator, or a larger agricultural company can all read the scale field as part of the same activity frame, provided the business remains within the stated non-edible oilseed scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical editorial terms, that means the slim record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The relevant source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and there is no separate number in the record that narrows the ceiling. The honest reading is therefore not a half-open category or a capped foreign stake; on the national data given here, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the stated maximum.

The Bali picture is also unusually direct. The province-wide moratorium described in the record blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The reason given is specific: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The national door and the Bali door are aligned here: the activity is foreign-open nationally, and the slim record does not put it inside Bali's PMA moratorium block. That does not add any permit, timeline, tax, or capital conclusion beyond the record; it simply means the Bali status field does not close the activity to PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: The national door and the Bali door are aligned here: the activity is foreign-open nationally, and the slim record does not put it inside Bali's PMA moratorium block.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Hybrid Rice Farming Without the Bali Moratorium Barrier
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the full hybrid-rice farming cycle, from land preparation to grain or seed output, and is open nationally and in Bali for foreign-owned registration.
editorial.body:
Hybrid rice farming under this activity is not a narrow planting label. It covers an integrated agricultural cycle: preparing the land, sowing, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and carrying out post-harvest work when those steps form one continuous operation until unhusked rice is produced. The record also makes room for hybrid-rice seed production, where the crop is planted to produce seed in the form of grain. In plain English, this is for operators whose business is the cultivation of hybrid rice itself, including the disciplined upstream work needed to bring a hybrid crop from field preparation to a defined agricultural output.

The defining point is the hybrid character of the rice. The scope describes hybrid rice as the first-generation offspring produced from crosses between two or more parent lines and/or homozygous inbred lines, with examples such as Bernas Super, Bernas Prima, Sembada B3, Sembada 626, Sembada 989, SL 11 SHS, Bridantara 3, and PP5. It also draws an important boundary: descendants of hybrid rice are not treated as hybrid rice for this activity. That matters because this registration is tied not simply to rice as a commodity, but to the specific biological and production logic of hybrid rice and, where relevant, hybrid-rice seed businesses that carry the process through to dry grain meeting seed-quality standards.

The scale profile is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can fit anything from a small farming setup to a larger agricultural enterprise, provided the registered activity genuinely follows the scope. Foreign ownership is also clear at national level: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under the stated national source. There is no foreign stake cap below full ownership in the record, so the national reading is straightforward rather than conditional.

The Bali reading is equally direct, and unusually clean. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not blocked in the record. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason given that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance: a foreign-owned company can register this activity in Bali, subject to the activity staying within the hybrid-rice farming and seed-production scope described here.

editorial.headline: Inbred Rice Farming, From Field Preparation to Dry Grain
editorial.standfirst: A clear national opening for inbred rice cultivation and seed production, with Bali not blocked under the stated moratorium record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01122 covers the cultivation of inbred rice: rice varieties developed through self-pollination, with a high level of purity or homozygosity.** In practical terms, this is not just the moment of planting. The record defines the activity as an integrated agricultural chain: land preparation, seeding, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps form one business activity up to the production of unhusked rice. It also includes the cultivation of inbred rice for seed in the form of grain.

The scope is deliberately agricultural and operational. It reaches both the production of harvested dry grain and inbred agricultural seed activity, provided the work remains part of the same cultivation-to-output chain described in the record. The examples in the scope show the breadth of what counts as inbred rice: named varieties such as Memberamo, Mekongga, Ciherang, IR-6, Inpari, Inpara, Inpago, Pak Tiwi, and IPB 15S, as well as local rice varieties cultivated across generations by farmers, including Rojo Lele, Pandan Wangi, and Pusaka Bhagasasi. The key distinction inside this record is that the activity is inbred rice, not hybrid rice.

For business registration, the code is open across all stated scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine the activity to a narrow enterprise size. A small farmer-led operation, a medium agricultural business, or a larger integrated rice cultivation and seed operation can all sit within the stated scale range, as long as the registered activity follows the scope: inbred rice farming and, where relevant, inbred seed production through the same agricultural sequence.

The national foreign-investment picture is also direct. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It does not state a foreign-ownership ceiling, so the editorial should not invent one. For Bali, the important point is equally clear: the Bali field is not blocked. The record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The moratorium rule itself blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this record’s Bali result is not a block. The honest conclusion is simple: this inbred rice farming activity is nationally open and, on the supplied Bali record, can proceed without a Bali moratorium block.

editorial.headline: Leaf Vegetable Farming as a Full Horticulture Chain
editorial.standfirst: A nationally open activity for growing edible leaves, stems, and flowers, with Bali PMA registration not blocked by the provincial moratorium note in this record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01131 covers leaf-vegetable farming as an integrated horticulture activity, not merely the act of planting greens in a field.** Its scope is the cultivation of vegetables whose leaves, flowers, or stems are eaten: artichoke, petsai or sawi, asparagus, cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, lettuce, celery, leeks, spinach, and kangkung are all named in the record. The description also reaches other edible-flower, leaf, and stem vegetables within the same farming pattern.

The operational idea is a complete crop cycle. Land preparation, nursery or seedling work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling belong here when they are conducted as one connected chain. That matters because the code is framed around farming activity as a sequence, not a detached service. Spinach and kangkung harvested with their roots remain inside the scope. So do seed-oriented activities: planting leaf-vegetable crops to produce seed, plus nursery and seed-production work for leaf-vegetable horticulture.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it is not written only for a smallholder profile or only for a large agricultural company. A founder reading this code should understand it as a broad agricultural classification for leaf-vegetable production, capable of describing anything from smaller cultivation to larger organized farming, provided the activity remains within the scope stated above.

The national and Bali picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does have a province-wide moratorium rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this slim record does not mark the activity as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stating that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. In plain terms: for this record, a foreign-owned company can read the national door as open and the Bali moratorium note as not blocking PMA registration today.

editorial.headline: Seasonal Fruit Farming With Room for Full Foreign Ownership
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01132 covers integrated seasonal fruit cultivation, from land preparation to postharvest, and is nationally open through every business scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01132 is for the farming of seasonal fruit crops. In practical terms, the record names watermelon, blewah, melon, and timun suri, while also leaving room for similar horticultural fruit activities. Its scope is not a loose label for trading fruit or handling produce after someone else has grown it. The activity is agricultural: preparing the land, sowing, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and carrying out postharvest work when those steps form one continuous cultivation chain.

The code also reaches into the seed side of the same activity. Where seasonal fruit crops are planted to produce seed in the form of biji, or where the work is described as nursery and seedling activity for horticultural fruit plants, the record keeps it inside this same agricultural frame. That makes the code useful for operators whose business model is built around the crop cycle itself, not only the finished fruit. The essential test is whether the work remains tied to seasonal fruit cultivation and its directly connected stages.

The scale position is unusually broad. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe anything from a small registered farm operation to a larger cultivation platform. Nationally, the investment position is also clean: the code is marked TERBUKA, with foreign ownership allowed up to 100%. For a foreign-owned PMA structure, that means the record does not impose a foreign-share ceiling below full ownership.

The Bali reading is equally important, because many codes that look open nationally can be stopped at provincial PMA registration if they fall under Bali's moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. This record does not do that. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: on this record, seasonal fruit farming under KBLI 01132 is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and it is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is that KBLI 01132 is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Fruit-Vegetable Farming With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01133 covers integrated horticultural farming for fruit vegetables, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01133 is the farming code for horticultural fruit vegetables: crops used as vegetables but botanically or commercially handled in this group as fruiting produce. The record names cucumbers, eggplants, tomatoes, vegetable starfruit, chayote, pumpkin, and gambas or oyong as examples. Its scope is not just the moment of planting. It covers the field cycle as one integrated activity: land preparation, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling when those steps are carried out as one business operation.

That integrated character matters. A founder using this code is not describing a trading desk, a restaurant supply brand, or a loose aggregation of small farms. The activity is agricultural production itself, including nursery and seed activities for these fruit-vegetable crops where the output is seed in the form of grain. The code therefore fits operators whose business identity sits in cultivation and crop production, with the practical farm work and immediate post-harvest stage treated as one connected undertaking rather than separate lines of business.

On scale, the record is unusually broad: the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, it can be registered from micro-scale farming through large-scale operations, so the classification is not reserved only for industrial agribusiness. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no capped foreign stake in the slim record; the national rule shown here allows full foreign ownership for this activity.

The Bali picture is equally important, because a national “open” status does not always settle the local PMA answer. Here, however, the record says Bali is not blocking this activity: l4_bali_blocked is false, with status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: a foreign-owned setup can look at KBLI 01133 nationally as fully open, and in Bali as not blocked by the stated moratorium rule.
editorial.pullQuote: A national “open” status does not always settle the local PMA answer, but for KBLI 01133 the Bali record is not blocked.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Root Vegetable Farming, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated farming of tuber and allium vegetables, from land preparation through post-harvest work, with full foreign ownership available nationally.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01134 is the farming code for root and bulb vegetables when the agricultural work is carried as one connected activity.** In practical terms, it covers crops such as potatoes, sweet potatoes, carrots, Chinese radish, bamboo shoots, garlic, onions, shallots, leeks, and other alliaceous vegetables. The scope is not limited to the moment of planting. It also includes land preparation, nursery and seed activities for these horticultural vegetables, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling when those steps form a single operating chain.

That integrated-chain point matters. A founder using this code is describing a farming activity, not merely trading vegetables after someone else has grown them. The record points to the productive cycle: preparing the land, sowing or seeding, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the post-harvest stage as part of the same horticultural operation. For a business plan, the centre of gravity is therefore cultivation of tuber and bulb vegetables, with the supporting nursery, seed, and post-harvest work attached to that farming activity rather than presented as a separate line of business.

The code is available across the full scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national investment list does not cap foreign ownership below full ownership for this activity. That does not, by itself, make every location and operating scale frictionless; it simply defines the national foreign-investment position contained in the record.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is not a hidden block. The provincial moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This record, however, marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is that this farming activity is nationally foreign-open and, on the record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by that moratorium. The caution is narrower: Bali’s status here comes from the risk position at Besar scale, so the registration analysis should stay anchored to the exact scale and activity chain being filed, not to a generic idea of agriculture.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Cassava Farming, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01135 covers cassava and related tuber cultivation from land preparation through post-harvest, open across all business scales and not blocked for Bali PMA registration.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01135 is an agricultural production code for cassava farming and the wider cultivation of palawija tubers when the work is run as one integrated activity.** Its scope starts at the soil: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling are all included when they belong to the same cultivation chain. In plain English, this is not a trading code and not a detached processing category. It is for the farming activity itself, with post-harvest work only inside the same agricultural sequence.

The record also gives this code a broader tuber-seed and tuber-crop character. It covers seed and nursery activity for mixed palawija tubers, including cassava, sweet potato, taro, ganyong and irut, gembili, iles-iles, porang, and other similar tuber crops, again from land preparation through planting, care, harvesting, and post-harvest where those steps form a single activity. That matters because a founder registering under this code should be describing a cultivation operation, not merely a distribution desk or a standalone downstream product business.

On scale, the code is unusually straightforward: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also clear. The slim record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign ownership ceiling as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the record itself does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The honest reading is therefore not a partial-opening story; nationally, this activity is open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is often where agricultural codes become less intuitive, but this record is explicit. editorial.headline: Mushroom Farming With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated mushroom cultivation from growing space and media preparation through harvest and post-harvest handling, open nationally to PMA and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
For KBLI 01136, the activity is mushroom agriculture in the practical, production-floor sense of the term. It covers cultivation of mushrooms such as merang, oyster, shittake, ear mushrooms, truffles, and similar varieties. The centre of gravity is not trading, processing, or restaurant supply; it is the farming chain itself, where the operator prepares the environment, manages the crop, and completes the harvest cycle as one connected agricultural activity.

The scope is broad enough to capture the normal working sequence of a mushroom farm. It includes making the **kubung**, preparing or processing the growing medium, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and carrying out post-harvest activities when those steps form one integrated chain. The record also includes nursery and seedling activities for mushroom plants. That matters because this is not just a label for a finished product; it is a registration home for operators whose business model sits inside the cultivation system, from setup and maintenance through the first handling after harvest.

On scale, the record is unusually clean: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** are all open. A founder reading this should treat the classification as available across the full range of business scales stated in the record, rather than only for a narrow smallholder or industrial profile. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited presidential regulations. There is no foreign stake cap below full ownership in the supplied record, so the national reading is straightforward: a foreign-owned setup can use this classification nationally, subject only to the facts actually stated here.

The Bali layer is where many KBLI readings become fragile, but this record does not produce a block. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the Bali status is recorded as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason given is that OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore positive but precise: this mushroom-farming activity is foreign-open nationally and, on the supplied Bali record, not moratorium-blocked for PMA registration in Bali today. That does not create extra permits, timelines, taxes, or capital requirements; it simply says the classification itself is not shut out by the Bali PMA moratorium recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Sugar Beet and Non-Cane Sweetener Farming, Read Precisely
editorial.standfirst: A farming classification for sugar beet, stevia, sweet sorghum, and similar non-cane sweetener crops, open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the agricultural classification for sugar beet and sweetener crops other than sugar cane. In practical terms, it covers the field work and crop-cycle work behind plants such as stevia and sweet sorghum: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one integrated farming operation. It also includes nursery and seedling work for sugar beet and other non-cane sweetener plants, so the code is not limited to harvesting mature crops. Its centre of gravity is the cultivation chain itself, not a detached trading or processing story.

The registration profile is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which means the classification can describe anything from a very small cultivation setup to a large organised farming operation, provided the actual activity remains within the stated agricultural scope. That breadth matters because it keeps the code anchored in what is being grown and how the farming cycle is organised, rather than in a narrow business size. A founder should read the scope closely: the post-harvest work belongs here only when it is part of the same sequence of activity around the crop.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. For PMA, the activity is TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. That means the record does not show a foreign stake cap below full ownership for this activity. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and nothing in the slim record adds a special capital figure, deadline, tax treatment, or separate operating permission. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: at national level, this is an open agricultural activity for a foreign-owned setup, so long as the registered activity genuinely matches sugar beet or other non-cane sweetener crop farming as described.

Bali does not overturn that conclusion on this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record states that the activity is not blocked by the moratorium because OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That is the key distinction. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is recorded as outside that blocked lane. The result is not a hidden prohibition but a cautiously open Bali picture: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership on the record, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium reason.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Chilli Farming as a Full-Cycle Agricultural Business
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01138 covers chilli cultivation from land preparation to post-harvest handling, and is nationally open to foreign ownership at every listed business scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01138 is the agricultural home for chilli farming. Its scope is not limited to harvesting mature plants; it covers the full chain of cultivation for Capsicum crops, including large chillies, bird’s eye chillies, curly chillies, and paprika. The activity begins with land preparation, seed sowing, nursery work, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling when those steps are carried out as one connected agricultural process.

The record also makes clear that this code includes chilli planting for seed production, specifically seed in the form of grain. That matters because the activity is not only about producing fresh vegetables for the market. It can also describe a cultivation operation whose output supports the next planting cycle through nursery and seed-related work, as long as the activity remains within the stated chilli-farming scope. In plain English, this is a code for operators who are actually growing chilli crops, managing the crop cycle, and handling the immediate post-harvest stage as part of the same farming business.

On scale, the code is broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe anything from a small farming operation to a larger agricultural enterprise, provided the registered activity remains chilli cultivation and its included nursery, seed, harvesting, and post-harvest sequence. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is equally direct: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, so the national reading is that a foreign-owned company may register this activity up to 100% foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a different reason than many low-risk activities. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, according to the recorded rule. This code, however, is not shown as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore simple: KBLI 01138 is nationally open to PMA at 100%, and the Bali record provided here does not block it under the stated moratorium.

editorial.headline: Other Tuber Farming, Without the Bali Moratorium Trap
editorial.standfirst: A broad farming category for sweet potato, taro, porang and similar tubers, open across business scales and available to full foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
This activity is the farming of tubers that sit outside the better-known main categories: sweet potato, taro, ganyong, irut, gembili, iles-iles, porang, and similar crops. The scope is not just the moment of harvest. It covers the agricultural chain when it is carried out as one integrated activity: preparing the land, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and handling post-harvest work. In plain English, this is a working farm code for growers whose business is rooted in miscellaneous tuber cultivation, including crops that may later become food, starch, or upstream agricultural supply.

The record also reaches into related growing activity where the work is still agricultural in character. It includes nursery and seed activities for other vegetable plants, except beet seed, and it captures integrated land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work for vegetables, fruits, and mixed tubers harvested more than once, as well as other vegetable farming. That makes the scope wider than a single crop label. A founder should read it as an agricultural production category, not as a trading, processing, export, or retail category; the source record gives farming activities, not downstream commercial permissions.

On scale, the code is unusually broad: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the same activity can be used by very small operators and by larger agricultural ventures, provided the registered activity genuinely matches the farming work described in the scope. The cleanest reading is practical rather than decorative: if the business is cultivating these crops and the land preparation, planting, care, harvest, and post-harvest steps form one operational chain, this is the field of activity the record describes.

For foreign ownership, the national position is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership shown in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The Bali picture is also clear, and here it is not the negative one: the record is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by Bali province's island-wide, permanent block on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: this activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and the Bali status in the record is not blocked by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Sugarcane Farming With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01140 covers integrated sugarcane cultivation, from land preparation through harvest and post-harvest work, and remains open nationally and in Bali for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01140 is the activity code for sugarcane farming as a complete agricultural operation. Its scope is practical and field-based: preparing the land, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one chain of sugarcane cultivation. It also includes sugarcane nursery and seedling activities, as well as land processing, sowing, planting, crop care, and harvest when they form a single sugarcane farming activity.

The code is therefore best understood as cultivation, not merely a trading label or an isolated service around the crop. A founder using it should be registering a business whose real activity is the growing of sugarcane, including the agronomic steps that make the crop possible. The record is broad enough to cover both the farming cycle itself and the propagation work that supports it, but its centre remains the same: organised sugarcane agriculture.

On scale, the code is open across the full range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not confined to smallholder registration or reserved only for larger operators. The record supports registration from micro-scale operations through large-scale businesses. For foreign investment, the national position is also straightforward: PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100% under the stated PMA source.

The Bali picture is unusually clean compared with activities that are caught by the province’s moratorium. The record says Bali blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this code is not blocked because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. In plain terms, the honest reading is that a foreign investor can register this sugarcane farming activity in Bali today, subject to the recorded national openness and the risk-status basis stated in the slim record. The important nuance is not a hidden restriction; it is the reason the Bali moratorium does not stop this code.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that a foreign investor can register this sugarcane farming activity in Bali today.

editorial.headline: Tobacco Farming, From Fieldwork to Seed
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01150 covers integrated tobacco cultivation, including land preparation, planting, harvest, post-harvest handling, and seed production.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01150 is the farming code for tobacco as an agricultural crop, not for the making of tobacco products. Its centre of gravity is the plantation or farm cycle: preparing land, sowing, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and carrying out post-harvest work when those steps form one continuous agricultural activity. The scope also includes cleaning and slicing tobacco when those activities cannot be separated from the farming operation itself. It is a field-based classification, concerned with cultivation and immediately connected handling, not downstream manufacturing.

That distinction matters because the record draws a clear boundary around what belongs here. Tobacco seed activity is included when the planting is done to produce seed in the form of grain, and the record also recognises tobacco nursery and seedling work. In practical registration terms, this is the code for an operator whose business is the growing of tobacco plants and the inseparable farm processes around them. It is not the code for a company whose main activity is transforming tobacco into finished tobacco products; the slim record expressly keeps that outside this classification.

The scale picture is broad. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the code is not framed only for smallholders or only for large plantation-style operators. A founder reading this should see the scale line as unusually straightforward: the classification can sit with micro, small, medium, or large business registrations, depending on the actual operating model. The same record also states that the national PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain English, at the national investment-rule level, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to full ownership.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it should not be made more complicated than the record makes it. The Bali moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently, but this record marks KBLI 01150 as not blocked. The stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by that moratorium. For this code, the honest national-versus-Bali reading is therefore aligned rather than contradictory: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked by the moratorium according to the record. The registration question still has to stay inside the exact tobacco-farming scope described above, but the Bali status itself is not a hidden prohibition.

editorial.headline: Fibre-Crop Farming With a Clean National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01160 covers fibre-crop cultivation for textile raw materials, open nationally to every business scale and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01160 is a farming classification for fibre crops: cotton, jute, kenaf, flax stems, ramie, sisal, abaca, and other textile raw materials from Agave and similar fibre-producing plants. Its scope is not limited to putting plants in the ground. The record describes an integrated agricultural chain: land preparation, sowing or planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps form one continuous fibre-crop operation. It also includes nursery and seed-production activity for fibre plants, including cultivation intended to produce seed in the form of grain.

That breadth matters because this is a primary-production code, not a downstream textile-manufacturing category. The centre of gravity is the farmed biological material: kapok, cotton, rosella, ramie, jute, linen, agave, abaca, kenaf, sisal, and other textile raw-material crops. A founder using this code is describing the cultivation of fibre-bearing plants and the immediate agricultural sequence around them. The code is strongest when the business activity can be explained as one farming system, from land preparation through harvest and related post-harvest handling, rather than as a separate trading, processing, or finished-goods activity.

Nationally, the record gives a clean opening. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, which means the foreign-ownership ceiling should be read plainly as 100%. The activity is also open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. In practical editorial terms, the national picture is not ambiguous in this slim record: fibre-crop farming under this classification is open to the full set of listed business scales, and the foreign share is not capped below full ownership.

For Bali, the position is equally clear, although it rests on a different basis. The record does carry Bali's moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, with the stated source being the governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. Yet this specific activity is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its l4_bali_status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore measured, not alarmist: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership in the record, open across all listed scales, and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Forage Crop Farming With a Bali Registration Caveat
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01191 covers the full field-to-post-harvest cycle for livestock feed crops, nationally open to PMA but conditional in Bali by exact OSS scope.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01191 is the classification for farming crops grown as livestock feed. Its scope is not the trading of feed or the management of livestock, but the agricultural production of green forage: feed grasses and leguminous plants such as elephant grass, king grass, odot grass, setaria, alfalfa, lamtoro, and Indigoferea zollingeriana. The record also brings seedling and seed activities for forage plants into view, alongside cover-crop cultivation, so the centre of gravity is clear: this is crop agriculture serving the feed chain.

The activity is described as an integrated farming sequence. It begins with land preparation, continues through planting and crop maintenance, then moves into harvesting and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one connected operation. That matters because the classification is anchored in the activity being performed, not in a marketing label. A founder using this code should be able to point to actual forage or cover-crop cultivation, and to the practical agricultural stages that make the activity real.

On the national investment picture, the record is straightforward. The PMA status is open, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and the code is open across Micro, Small, Medium, and Large scales. In plain terms, this is not a nationally closed activity for foreign-owned setup, and the record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The source cited for that national PMA position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, so the national reading is permissive within the limits of the activity as described.

Bali is the more careful part of the analysis. The province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA under an island-wide, permanent moratorium, and this record marks the Bali status as scope-dependent rather than simply open or blocked. It says the activity is not blocked outright, but that OSS risk at Large scale is low for some scopes and higher for others. The practical conclusion is narrow: PMA registration in Bali is possible only if the exact declared activity lands in the higher-risk scope; the live OSS classification must be checked against the precise activity before treating Bali as available.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali is not a simple yes or no here: the code is nationally open, but the exact declared scope decides whether PMA registration can pass locally.
