editorial.headline: Forage Seed Production Is Nationally Open, but Bali Is Closed
editorial.standfirst: This code covers seed production for livestock feed crops and non-sugar beet, open nationally across all business scales but blocked for foreign registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is about producing seed, not simply growing feed crops. The scope covers seed propagation for livestock forage plants and non-sugar beet, with the output defined as seed in the form of grain. The work is described as an integrated chain: land preparation, planting, crop care, harvesting, and post-harvest activity carried out as one sequence. In practical terms, it is the upstream agricultural activity that creates planting material for forage systems, rather than the downstream use of those crops as animal feed.

The Indonesian scope is concrete about the kinds of plants involved. Forage crops include grasses and leguminous feed plants, with examples such as elephant grass, king grass, odot grass, setaria grass, alfalfa, kaliandra, gamal, lamtoro, and Indigofera zollingeriana. That gives the code a clear agricultural identity: it sits in the seed-production side of livestock-supporting cultivation, covering both grass-based and legume-based forage seed activity. Non-sugar beet seed production is also included, while the record expressly frames the beet reference as outside sugar beet.

On the national investment reading, the code is open. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, and the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the national classification does not, on this slim record, reserve the activity away from foreign investment or limit it to a smaller ownership share. If a founder is looking only at the national PMA column, the immediate signal is therefore simple: this is a foreign-open activity, across the listed business scales, with no foreign-stake cap below full ownership in the provided data.

Bali changes the conclusion completely. The record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and says the activity is blocked because OSS risk at Besar scale is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah on every scope, triggering the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI used for PMA. So the honest reading is this: nationally, the activity is open to foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today under the stated Bali rule. That is not a contradiction in the business scope. It is a location-specific registration block that overrides the practical outcome for Bali planning.

editorial.headline: Cut Flowers, Open Capital, and Bali’s Cleaner Registration Signal
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01193 covers cut-flower and flower-bud farming, open across business scales and foreign ownership nationally, with Bali not blocking PMA registration under its moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01193 is the farming of flowers for harvest as cut flowers and flower buds. Its scope is practical and agricultural rather than decorative retail: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling are treated as one production chain. The record names orchids, carnations, gerbera, gladiolus, chrysanthemums, roses, jasmine, tuberose, and other flowers grown for the flowers themselves. The decisive point is the output. This activity is for flowers and buds taken from the plant; it is not the farming of live flowering plants as the final product.

That makes the code relevant for founders building a production-side floriculture operation rather than a nursery of living ornamental plants. It can describe a farm that grows flowers for cutting, manages the crop cycle, harvests the flowers, and handles the immediate post-harvest work as part of the same agricultural activity. The scope is broad enough to cover the named flower types and similar flowers harvested for their blooms, but it stays anchored to cultivation and production. It should not be stretched into downstream trade, floristry, or live-plant production unless those activities are separately supported by their own classification record.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the activity is not reserved in the record for only one business size. At the national level, PMA is classified TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national investment rule shown here does not impose a partial foreign-share cap. The cited source for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and there is no extra threshold, licence, capital minimum, or timing rule in the slim record to add beyond that.

The Bali reading is also clean, but for a different reason. Under the record’s Bali moratorium, PMA is permanently barred province-wide from every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. For this activity, however, the Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason states that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a hidden caveat: a foreign investor can read this record as nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Flower Seed Farming That Stays Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01194 covers flower seed farming for seed production, open across all business scales with full foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01194 is a narrow agricultural activity: the farming of flower-plant seed production, where the intended output is seed in the form of grain or seed stock. Its editorial core is not ornamental retail, landscaping, nursery display, or the broad trade in flowers. The activity is about producing the seed basis from which flower cultivation begins. That makes the classification useful for operators whose business model is upstream: organised cultivation, seed production discipline, and a clearly agricultural production chain.

The record also marks an important boundary. This code is for seed produced as seed, not for every possible form of flower propagation material. Vegetative materials such as stem cuttings, shoots, and seedlings for flower multiplication are described separately in the source scope, so they should not be casually folded into this registration. For founders, that distinction matters because the registration should match the real operating activity: a farm producing flower seeds is one thing; a business built around vegetative planting material is another. The safest reading is therefore precise and restrained: KBLI 01194 fits flower-seed farming where the harvest is seed.

On scale, the code is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the classification can support anything from a small agricultural operator to a larger seed-production venture, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope. Nationally, it is also marked TERBUKA for foreign investment, with pma_max_asing at 100. In plain English, a PMA company may hold up to full foreign ownership for this activity under the cited investment sources. There is no recorded foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, and no additional threshold, licence, capital floor, or timing rule should be inferred from it.

The Bali picture is also clean, but it needs to be stated accurately. Bali’s provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This record, however, says KBLI 01194 is not blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by the moratorium. The practical conclusion is that this is not one of the cases where a nationally open code becomes unusable for PMA registration in Bali. For this slim record, the honest answer is simple: flower seed farming under KBLI 01194 is foreign-open nationally, open across all listed scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Other Annual Crops, With Bali Depending on the Exact Scope
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to foreign ownership, but Bali registration turns on the risk profile declared in OSS for the precise activity.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01199 is a residual but important agricultural activity: it covers annual crop farming that is not otherwise classified, including planting activities aimed at producing seed in the form of grain. In operational terms, the scope is not limited to the crop standing in the field. It reaches the full basic cycle described in the record: preparing and processing land, sowing, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and post-harvest processing. It also includes seed activities for other annual crops that fall within this same residual category.

That breadth matters because this is the kind of code a founder may look at when the real activity is agricultural but does not sit neatly under a narrower label. The registrant could be small or large: the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, under the stated source Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no foreign-stake cap in the slim record below full ownership, so the national reading is straightforward: a foreign-owned company can in principle use this activity at the permitted scale.

Bali is the part that requires more careful handling. The record does not mark this activity as absolutely blocked for Bali; `l4_bali_blocked` is false. But the Bali status is not a clean open signal either: it is Blocked (scope-dependent). The reason given is precise and should shape the founder's expectations. OSS risk at scale Besar is low on some scopes, but higher on others, and registration as a PMA in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope. That means the practical question is not merely whether the national investment list is open. It is whether the exact activity entered in OSS lands on a risk profile that Bali will accept for PMA registration.

The background rule is strict: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, with the source recorded as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For this code, that does not produce a blanket no, but it does make the declared scope decisive. The honest reading is therefore conditional: nationally open, potentially registrable in Bali, but only if the live OSS declaration for the exact activity carries the higher-risk scope described in the record. A founder should treat the crop activity, the seed activity, the scale, and the OSS risk outcome as one joined question, not as separate boxes to tick.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is conditional: nationally open, potentially registrable in Bali, but only if the live OSS declaration carries the higher-risk scope described in the record.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pertanian buah anggur untuk konsumsi langsung atau untuk memproduksi wine, jus, cuka, dan buah yang dikeringkan, seperti kismis, zante currants, dan sultana. Pertanian buah anggur yang dimaksud mencakup kegiatan pengolahan lahan, penanaman, pemeliharaan, pemanenan, dan kegiatan pascapanen yang dilakukan sebagai satu rangkaian kegiatan. Kelompok ini juga mencakup penanaman tanaman anggur untuk menghasilkan benih berupa biji.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- pembuatan wine, lihat kelompok 11020;
- pengolahan dan pengawetan anggur, lihat subgolongan 1030.

editorial.headline: Grape Farming With a Clear Bali Registration Path
editorial.standfirst: Grape cultivation is open to foreign ownership nationally and, on this record, is not stopped by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Grape farming under this activity is first of all an agricultural registration, not a beverage or food-processing licence. Its centre of gravity is the vineyard itself: preparing the land, planting vines, maintaining the crop, harvesting grapes, and carrying out post-harvest work when that work is part of the same farming sequence. The record is broad enough to include grapes grown for direct consumption and grapes grown as raw material for wine, juice, vinegar, raisins, zante currants, and sultanas. It also includes grape planting aimed at producing seed.

That makes the code useful for founders whose real business asset is cultivation: land preparation, vine management, harvest discipline, and integrated post-harvest handling. The boundary matters. The slim record expressly keeps winemaking outside this activity, and it also excludes grape processing and preservation. A company should therefore not treat this registration as a catch-all for everything that may happen after grapes leave the farming chain. Its editorial meaning is narrower and cleaner: this is the code for growing grapes and managing the immediate agricultural cycle around them.

The scale picture is unusually open. The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as open scales, so the activity is not framed only for a large estate or only for a small local farm. It can describe anything from a smaller cultivation operation to a larger farming business, provided the registered activity remains grape agriculture. Nationally, the investment field is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the honest national reading is that a foreign-owned company can use this activity at full foreign ownership, subject only to the facts stated here.

The Bali question is where this record becomes especially important. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms: a foreigner is not barred by the Bali moratorium from registering this grape-farming activity today. That does not create extra permissions beyond the record, and it does not turn farming into processing. It simply means the national openness and the Bali registration position point in the same direction here: grape cultivation, at the stated scales, is a viable PMA registration path in Bali on this record.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreigner is not barred by the Bali moratorium from registering this grape-farming activity today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pertanian buah-buahan tropis dan subtropis, seperti alpukat, pisang dan pisang raja, kurma, buah ara, pepaya, nanas, rambutan, durian, duku, jambu biji, jambu air, lengkeng, nangka, mangga, manggis, sawo, belimbing, salak, sirsak, dan buah naga. Kelompok ini juga mencakup kegiatan penanaman tanaman buah tropis dan subtropis untuk menghasilkan benih berupa biji.

editorial.headline: Tropical Fruit Farming, From Field Preparation to Post-Harvest
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01220 covers the full cultivation cycle for tropical and subtropical fruit, nationally open to PMA and available across all business scales, including in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01220 is the business classification for farming tropical and subtropical fruit. Its scope is broad, but not vague: it covers the agricultural work behind crops such as avocado, banana and plantain, dates, figs, papaya, pineapple, rambutan, durian, duku, guava, water apple, longan, jackfruit, mango, mangosteen, sapodilla, starfruit, salak, soursop, dragon fruit, and similar produce. The classification is not only about the moment of harvest. It follows the activity as a chain, beginning with land preparation and planting, continuing through crop maintenance, and ending with harvesting and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one integrated activity.

The record also brings seed-related activity into view. Planting tropical and subtropical fruit crops to produce seed in the form of kernels or seeds sits inside this classification, as do nursery and seed-production activities for tropical and subtropical fruit plants, including the stated example of date seed production. In practical terms, this is a cultivation code for operators whose core activity is growing the fruit or preparing the plant material that supports that cultivation. It is not framed as a trading, processing, or hospitality activity; its centre of gravity is agricultural production and the connected cultivation cycle.

The scale position is unusually clear. The code is open to Micro, Small, Medium, and Large businesses, so it can fit both a modest farm operation and a larger structured agricultural business, provided the registered activity remains within this defined scope. For a founder, that matters because the classification is not reserved only for one size of operator. The same code can describe a small fruit-growing venture, a medium farming business, or a larger agricultural company working through land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvest, and post-harvest as a continuous production activity.

On foreign ownership, the national picture is straightforward: the PMA status is open, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the record does not impose a foreign-shareholding cap below full ownership. Bali is also not blocked on the facts given here. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is specific: OSS risk at Large scale is Medium-High or High, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium itself blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this record does not place KBLI 01220 inside that blocked outcome. The honest reading is therefore clean: nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked by the moratorium on the record supplied.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Citrus Farming, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01230 covers citrus cultivation from land preparation to post-harvest work, including seed production, and is open across business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01230 is the activity code for citrus fruit farming. Its scope is not limited to picking fruit from an existing orchard; it covers the full cultivation chain as one connected agricultural activity. The record includes land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling for citrus crops. It also includes planting citrus plants to produce seed in the form of biji, as well as nursery and seedling activities for citrus fruit plants.

In practical English, this is the code for businesses whose core activity is growing citrus: pomelo, lemon, lime, limau, orange, siam citrus, keprok, mandarin, tangerine, clementine, and other citrus fruit named in the scope. The emphasis is agricultural production, not a separate downstream story. A founder using this code should be looking at an orchard or cultivation operation where the field work, plant care, harvest, and immediate post-harvest steps belong to the same farming activity.

The scale picture is broad. The slim record says the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed only for large plantation-style operators; it can also describe smaller registered agricultural businesses, provided the activity remains within the citrus-farming scope. Nationally, the investment position is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. Rendered plainly, that means foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership in the record for this activity.

The Bali reading is equally important, and here the answer is clean rather than dramatic. For Bali, l4_bali_blocked is recorded as false, while the Bali status is listed as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its reason is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium, even though that moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest editorial conclusion is therefore that KBLI 01230 is nationally open and, on this record, not blocked for Bali PMA registration by the stated moratorium rule.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Where Pome and Stone Fruit Farming Fits in Indonesia’s KBLI Map
editorial.standfirst: This activity code covers the full farming cycle for apples, pears, plums, passion fruit, pomegranate and related pome and stone fruits.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01240 is a farming classification for pome and stone fruits: apples, apricots, cherries, peaches, nectarines, pears, quince, plums, sloe, passion fruit, kepel, tamarillo and pomegranate. Its scope is not merely the final harvest. The record describes a continuous agricultural chain, beginning with land preparation and planting, continuing through crop maintenance, and ending with harvesting and post-harvest work when those activities are performed as one integrated sequence. It also includes the cultivation of apple and stone-fruit plants for seed production.

That makes this a practical code for businesses whose centre of gravity is the cultivation of these fruit crops, including nursery and seedling activity tied to the same group of plants. A founder should read the scope as agricultural rather than trading, processing or hospitality-led: the defining activity is the preparation, growing, care, harvesting and post-harvest handling of the listed fruits. The language is broad enough to cover both familiar temperate names such as apple, pear, cherry and plum, and Indonesian-market crops such as markisa, kepel, terong Belanda and delima, provided the business is genuinely carrying out the farming cycle described in the record.

The scale picture is unusually open. The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar as open scales, so this classification is not reserved only for a large plantation operator. It can sit at micro and small scale, grow into a medium enterprise, or be registered at large scale where the business model and licensing profile justify it. For foreign investment, the national PMA status is also clear: TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity at the national level.

The Bali reading is also straightforward, and it matters because many agricultural categories can become more complicated once local registration practice is considered. Here, the record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and that the activity is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by the province-wide rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: nationally, this is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium.

editorial.headline: Berry Farming With a Clean National Opening
editorial.standfirst: This code covers berry cultivation from land preparation to postharvest work, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
Berry farming under this activity is not just the image of ripe fruit at harvest. The scope is broader and more agricultural: it covers the cultivation of berry crops such as blueberries, currants, gooseberries, kiwi, raspberries, strawberries, and other berries, including the full sequence of land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and postharvest activity when those steps are carried out as one chain of work.

The record also brings nursery and seed activity into the same frame. Planting berry crops to produce seed in the form of biji is included, as are pembibitan and pembenihan activities for berry plants. In practical registration terms, this makes the code suitable for operators whose business is centered on growing berry plants and managing the cultivation cycle itself, rather than treating cultivation, maintenance, harvest, and postharvest handling as disconnected activities.

The scale position is unusually straightforward. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That means the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. A foreign-owned setup can therefore read the national position plainly: this activity is open, and the ceiling stated in the record is full foreign ownership.

The Bali position is just as clear, although it rests on a reason many founders do not expect. The provincial moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This record, however, marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says the OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is not that Bali is frictionless, and not that the moratorium is irrelevant. It is narrower and more useful: on this record, berry farming is nationally foreign-open at 100%, open across all listed scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Edible Nut Orchards With a Clear Bali PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the full farming cycle for edible nut-bearing fruit crops, and it is open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01252 is a farming classification for edible nut-bearing fruit crops. Its scope is not limited to the final crop itself: it covers the practical agricultural chain that makes the crop possible, from land preparation and planting through maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those activities are carried out as one integrated sequence. The record names almonds, cashews, chestnuts, walnuts, hazelnuts, and pistachios as examples of the kind of edible nut crops included here.

The scope also reaches nursery and seedling activity for these nut-bearing crops. That matters because this is not merely a trading or processing label; it is an agricultural registration for operators whose business is rooted in cultivation. A founder using this code should be looking at an activity where the land, the crop cycle, and the production sequence are central to the business description. The Indonesian scope points to cultivation work that begins before the plant is in the ground and continues through harvest and post-harvest handling as part of the same agricultural activity.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the classification can describe anything from a small agricultural operation to a larger farming business, provided the activity remains inside this edible nut-crop farming scope. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clean: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no lower foreign-stake cap in the slim record, so the plain reading is that foreign ownership is allowed up to the full stated ceiling under the cited national source.

The Bali picture is also direct. Bali's moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, on a permanent island-wide basis. But this record does not mark the activity as blocked in Bali. The record assigns it Bali status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, leaving it outside the moratorium block. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning but a distinction: nationally this code is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked for PMA registration under the moratorium rule stated in the record.

editorial.headline: Perennial Vegetable Farming With a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01253 covers perennial vegetable farming from land preparation to post-harvest and seed work, open nationally to PMA up to 100% and not blocked for Bali on this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01253 is the activity code for farming perennial vegetable plants, not a catch-all for ordinary crop trading or food processing. The slim record describes a field-based agricultural activity centred on plants such as kluwih or timbul, breadfruit, vegetable jackfruit, petai, jengkol, melinjo, and similar crops. Its scope is the agricultural chain itself: preparing land, sowing or nursery work, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one connected operation. It also reaches seed-oriented cultivation, including nursery and seed production for perennial vegetables.

That matters because the code is about the production base, not merely the finished commodity. A founder using it should understand the activity as an operating farm category: the land is worked, plants are established and cared for, harvest is part of the same business line, and post-harvest handling belongs here when it remains within that continuous farming sequence. The record also makes room for cultivation aimed at producing seed in the form of biji, so the code can describe both crop output and the upstream plant material needed to reproduce the activity.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the category is not confined to a cottage-scale farm or reserved only for larger operators. It can describe a very small agricultural venture, a growing commercial operation, or a larger farm, provided the real activity remains within the scope described above. The national investment reading is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership stated in the record is 100%. In plain English, the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity.

The Bali reading is where many activity codes become difficult, but this one should not be overstated. Bali's moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province on a permanent island-wide basis. For this code, however, the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is simple: this is a nationally open PMA activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and the Bali record does not block it under the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Other Shrub Fruit Farming, With Bali Still Open to PMA
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01259 covers integrated farming of other shrub fruit plants, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01259 is a narrow agricultural classification for other shrub fruit farming. Its Indonesian scope points to the cultivation of other shrub plants, including locust beans, and treats the activity as an integrated farming chain rather than a single isolated step. The work begins with land preparation and nursery or seed activities, continues through sowing, planting, and crop maintenance, and extends to harvesting and post-harvest work when those activities are carried out as one continuous operation.

That matters because the code is not simply about trading fruit, running a farm-adjacent service, or processing a commodity after it has left the field. The record describes a production activity rooted in the cultivation cycle itself: preparing the land, establishing the plants, maintaining them, taking the harvest, and handling the immediate post-harvest stage as part of the same agricultural sequence. For founders, the clean reading is that this code belongs to operators whose business identity is the farming of other shrub fruit plants, including locust beans, not a downstream or unrelated commercial activity.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it is not confined to a single enterprise size in the slim record. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is equally clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a stated foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain English, the national classification allows foreign ownership up to the full recorded ceiling for this activity. There is no lower cap in the record to soften or reinterpret; the relevant source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali reading is also unusually clean. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance: for this record, the activity is nationally foreign-open and, on the Bali moratorium fields provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

editorial.headline: Coconut Farming With a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: A practical reading of coconut farming as a full agricultural cycle, open across business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01261 covers coconut farming as an integrated agricultural activity, not merely the act of planting coconut trees. Its scope runs from land preparation through nursery work, sowing, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps form one continuous farming chain. It also includes planting coconut crops to produce seed in the form of nuts, together with nursery and seedling activity for coconut fruit plants.

That breadth matters for founders because the code describes the operating substance of a coconut agriculture business. A registrant under this activity is not limited to the final crop alone; the record expressly includes the upstream fieldwork and propagation steps that make coconut production possible. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the activity can sit under a very small farming setup as well as a larger agricultural enterprise, provided the registered business is still genuinely doing the coconut farming cycle described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is straightforward: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The stated source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and that is the only basis this editorial can use for the national PMA reading.

The Bali position is also clean, but for a specific reason. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide on a permanent basis. This record, however, marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The result is an unusually usable reading: this coconut farming activity is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the record does not show a Bali moratorium block for PMA registration today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Oil Palm Cultivation With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01262 covers the full oil palm farming cycle, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01262 is the classification for oil palm farming as an integrated agricultural activity. Its scope is not limited to the visible plantation stage. The record describes a chain that begins with land preparation and continues through planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those activities form one connected operation. It also includes the planting of oil palm plants to produce seed in the form of kernels or seeds, as well as nursery and seedling activity for oil palm fruit plants.

That breadth matters because this code is about cultivation infrastructure, not a narrow trading label. A founder using it is describing an operation built around growing oil palm: preparing the land, raising or planting the crop, maintaining it through the production cycle, harvesting the fruit, and handling the post-harvest stage as part of the same agricultural sequence. The scope also makes room for seed-oriented planting and nursery work, so long as the activity remains within the oil palm farming frame set by the record.

Nationally, the investment signal is straightforward. The slim record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, and cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. In plain terms, the code is not presented here as a restricted national category, nor as one reserved only for a narrow business size. A foreign-owned setup can read the national position as open, with no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the data provided.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. But this code is marked l4_bali_blocked: false, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. That does not create extra promises beyond the record, but it does establish the core conclusion: for this activity, a foreigner is not blocked from PMA registration in Bali today on the moratorium ground described here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Oleaginous Fruit Farming, With Bali Still Open on the Record
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated farming of other oleaginous fruits, including olives, from land preparation through post-harvest work and seed production.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01269 is a farming classification for other oleaginous fruits: crops grown for oil-bearing fruit, with olives named in the record as the clearest example.** Its scope is not limited to harvesting. It covers the agricultural sequence as a single chain: land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps belong to the same operation. The record also includes nursery and seed-related activity for these other oleaginous fruit plants, including cultivation intended to produce seed in the form of biji.

In practical business terms, this is the code for an operator whose activity is agricultural production rather than trade, processing as a separate industrial activity, or a detached support service. The centre of gravity is the cultivation of the crop itself. A founder using this classification is describing a farm or plantation activity that manages the growing cycle of other oleaginous fruit plants, and may also handle the connected nursery, seedling, planting, maintenance, harvest, and immediate post-harvest stages where they form one continuous agricultural activity.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not written only for large plantation economics. It can describe a small agricultural undertaking as well as a larger formal investment, provided the registered business activity remains within the farming scope described above. Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling rendered as 100%. On the slim record alone, there is no foreign equity cap below full ownership to warn about.

The Bali picture is where the reading needs care, because Bali’s moratorium rule is broad: the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. This record, however, does not mark the activity as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore that Bali remains open to foreign registration for this activity today. On the supplied record, the national door is open, the maximum foreign stake is 100%, and Bali is not flagged as moratorium-blocked, although the Bali status itself still reads as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a casual all-clear.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Coffee Farming That Is Nationally Open and Bali-Clear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01271 covers the full coffee-farming cycle, from land preparation and seed work through cultivation, harvest, and integrated post-harvest activity.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01271 is the coffee-farming code, not a cafe, trading, roasting, or hospitality label.** Its scope is agricultural and begins in the field: land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one connected farming sequence. The record also brings coffee seed production into the same field of view, through nursery and seed activities for beverage crops. In plain English, this is the code for cultivating coffee as an agricultural activity, including the practical upstream work needed to raise the plant and bring the crop through harvest.

That breadth matters because it makes the code useful for operators whose real business is coffee production rather than merely handling coffee as a product. A founder registering under this activity is describing the cultivation system itself: preparing land, developing seedlings, planting coffee, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the immediate post-harvest work that belongs to the same farming chain. The slim record does not add processing thresholds, special licensing language, land-size rules, tax treatment, or capital figures, so the clean reading stays close to the activity description: agriculture first, with coffee as the crop and the farming sequence as the core.

The scale position is unusually straightforward. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the code is not confined, in the record, to a single business size band. A small grower, a growing medium enterprise, or a large-scale operator can all sit within the same activity description, provided the registered business is genuinely performing the coffee-farming work described. The important editorial distinction is that scale availability is not the same thing as an invented permission package. The record says which scales are open; it does not state extra conditions beyond the listed activity scope and the stated foreign-investment position.

For foreign ownership, the national picture is clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the national reading is that this activity can be foreign-owned up to the stated ceiling. Bali is equally clear, although the reason often surprises founders. The Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, yet this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is simple: on the record provided, a foreign-owned company can register this coffee-farming activity in Bali today, because the Bali moratorium does not block it.

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

editorial.headline: Tea Cultivation With a Clean National and Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: Tea farming is open across business scales, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block under this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01272 is the activity code for tea cultivation as an integrated agricultural operation. Its scope is not limited to the visible moment of harvest. The record covers land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and postharvest activity when these are carried out as one chain. It also includes the planting of tea plants to produce seed in the form of beans, and expressly names nursery and seed activities for beverage crops, including tea seed production.

That matters because this is a cultivation code, not a loose label for trading tea or presenting a tea brand. The centre of gravity is the agricultural life cycle of the tea plant itself: preparing the land, raising seedlings, managing the crop, and bringing the harvest through postharvest steps that remain part of the same farming sequence. A founder using this code should therefore see it as a field-level operating category for tea plantations or tea-growing ventures, including the upstream seed and nursery work described in the record.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the classification is not confined to either smallholder activity or large estates. Nationally, the investment reading is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national rule set in this record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no basis here to invent a lower threshold, a phased timeline, or a special capital condition; the only ownership number given is the full 100% ceiling.

The Bali picture is equally important, but it should be read precisely. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This record, however, is not marked as blocked. Because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, the record carries the Bali status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: a foreign-owned tea cultivation setup is nationally open, and this record does not show a Bali PMA moratorium block. The caveat is not a hidden prohibition; it is the risk-status distinction stated in the record.

intel_2026.baliContext: Agriculture in Bali centers around rice (subak system), coffee (Kintamani highlands), and tropical fruits/vegetables. Land use requires coordination with local subak (irrigation cooperative) and compliance with spatial planning (RTRW).

editorial.headline: Cocoa Farming, Read Clearly for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01273 covers cocoa cultivation from land preparation to harvest, with national PMA opening at 100% and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01273 is the agricultural code for cocoa: the growing of cocoa as a crop, from land preparation and planting through maintenance, harvest, and the post-harvest work when those steps form one continuous activity. Its scope also reaches the planting of cocoa plants to produce seed in the form of beans, plus nursery and seed-production work for beverage-crop material where the crop is cocoa. In plain English, this is not a narrow trading label or a downstream chocolate category. It is the cultivation base: preparing soil, raising seedlings, planting, tending, harvesting, and carrying the immediate post-harvest sequence tied to cocoa farming itself.

That breadth matters because the record opens the activity across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small grower, a mid-sized plantation operator, and a larger agricultural company are all within the scale vocabulary of this code, provided the activity remains the cocoa-farming sequence described in the scope. The seed element is also part of the code's center of gravity, but only as cocoa seed in the form of beans and nursery or seedling activity for beverage-crop planting material. The clean boundary is agricultural production and seed-related cultivation, not a claim about manufacturing, retail, or any separate commercial layer not stated in the record.

Nationally, the PMA status is straightforward: TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the record does not impose a foreign share cap below full ownership. The important editorial point is restraint: the national opening says what it says, and no more. It does not create a minimum-capital figure, a special timeline, a tax conclusion, or a local operating condition in this record. The foreign-ownership picture for this code is therefore clean at the national level: open, up to 100%, across the stated scales.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear, but for the opposite reason from many low-risk activities: the record marks l4_bali_blocked as false and gives the status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this activity is not caught by that block because at scale Besar the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Cocoa farming is nationally foreign-open at 100%, and the record does not place it under Bali's PMA moratorium block. The caution is simply to keep the reading anchored to the record's scope: cocoa cultivation, seed-bean production, nursery work, harvesting, and linked post-harvest activity as one farming sequence.

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

editorial.headline: KBLI 01279: Beverage-Plant Farming That Stays Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A clear lane for integrated farming of other beverage-material plants, open across all business scales and not caught by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01279 covers the farming of plants used as materials for beverages, in the category that sits outside the specifically named beverage crops. Its practical scope is agricultural rather than retail or processing as a standalone business: the activity includes preparing land, sowing, nursery and seedling work, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps form one connected farming sequence.

That integrated character matters. This is not merely the sale of a harvested commodity, and it is not a detached seed-trading label. The slim record frames the activity around cultivation itself, including pembibitan and pembenihan for these other beverage-material plants. In English, the clean reading is: a business registering this activity is positioning itself as the operator of the farming cycle, from land preparation and propagation through maintenance, harvest, and the immediate post-harvest stage when carried out as one chain.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not reserved only for a large plantation-style setup or only for a smallholder format. A local founder, a growing agricultural company, or a larger operator can all read the scale line directly: all four scale categories are present. Nationally, the foreign-investment treatment is also direct. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no minority cap in the record to soften or reinterpret.

The Bali picture is where this code needs careful reading, because Bali’s provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island. This record, however, is not marked as blocked. The Bali classification is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because the record cites Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi OSS risk at Besar scale, which means the moratorium does not block it. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: nationally, KBLI 01279 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, it is not caught by the stated PMA moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk activities.

editorial.headline: Pepper Farming With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01281 covers integrated pepper farming, from land preparation to post-harvest work, and is nationally open to PMA at every business scale.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01281 is a farming activity in the plain, agricultural sense of the word.** It covers pepper or merica cultivation under the Piper group, including the practical sequence that turns land into a producing crop: land preparation, sowing, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one connected operation. The scope also includes cabai jawa or cabai jamu farming, as well as pepper seedling and seed-production activities. In other words, this is not merely trading pepper, processing pepper as a separate factory activity, or using pepper as a label for a broader food business. The record points to cultivation and the immediate farming cycle around the plant itself.

That matters for founders because this code is open across the full scale spectrum stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A local operator can read that as a broad scale fit, from a smaller farming setup through to a larger agricultural operation. A foreign investor can read the national PMA position just as directly: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the national reading is clean. If the business activity really is pepper farming, including nursery, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and integrated post-harvest work, the national classification does not create a foreign-shareholding discount by itself.

Bali presents an equally clear picture, although the reason is different. The record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and that this activity is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which means it is not blocked by the moratorium described in the record. That moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently, but this activity does not fall into the blocked result stated here. So the honest lede is not a warning that foreigners cannot register it in Bali today. It is the opposite: based on this slim record, this pepper-farming activity remains nationally open to PMA and is not marked as blocked for Bali PMA registration.

The useful caution is therefore one of scope discipline, not invented licensing. The classification should be used when the business is genuinely farming pepper or cabai jawa/cabai jamu, including the cultivation chain and directly connected post-harvest work described in the record. The strength of KBLI 01281 is that the commercial story and the legal classification can line up without theatrical interpretation: a farm activity, open at all recorded scales, nationally open to full foreign ownership, and not stopped by the Bali PMA moratorium status shown here.

editorial.headline: Clove Farming, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01282 covers clove cultivation from land preparation to post-harvest work, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the supplied record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01282 is the activity of growing cloves as an integrated agricultural operation. The record describes a chain that begins with land preparation and continues through sowing, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when these are performed as one sequence. It also includes planting clove crops to produce seed in the form of grains, as well as nursery and seedling activities for clove plants. In plain English, this is not merely the act of selling cloves or managing a plantation nameplate; it is the cultivation work itself, from preparing the soil to bringing the harvested crop through the immediate post-harvest stage.

The scope is broad enough to suit operators at every formal scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because this activity is not reserved only for large estates. A small clove grower, a medium agricultural enterprise, or a larger plantation-style operation all sit within the same described activity so long as the substance remains clove farming and the related cultivation sequence. The record also keeps seed-oriented activity inside the same frame: planting clove plants to produce seed, plus nursery and seedling work, belongs here when it is part of the clove cultivation activity.

The responsible reading is therefore narrow but useful: for national classification purposes, this clove-farming activity is open to foreign investment up to the stated ceiling, across the scales listed in the record.

The Bali picture is also clear, but it should not be overstated. The record says this activity is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. editorial.headline: Nutmeg Cultivation, Clearly Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers nutmeg cultivation from land preparation through harvest, including integrated post-harvest work and seed production.
editorial.body:
01283 is the activity code for nutmeg agriculture. In plain English, it covers the cultivation of nutmeg as a complete agricultural activity: preparing land, sowing, nursery work, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and carrying out post-harvest work when those steps are part of one integrated operation. The record also makes room for nutmeg planting whose purpose is seed production, specifically seed in the form of nutmeg kernels. This is not a general spice-trading label or a loose plantation category; its center of gravity is the cultivation cycle itself, including nursery and seedling work where that is part of producing nutmeg plants or nutmeg seed.

For Indonesian business registration, businesses of every scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar—may undertake this activity. That means the code is not reserved only for a large estate model; it can describe a small agricultural operator, a middle-scale farming business, or a large-scale operation, so long as the registered activity remains within the stated scope. The useful editorial test is simple: if the business is actually doing nutmeg cultivation, including the land, crop-care, harvest, integrated post-harvest, nursery, or seed-production work described here, this is the substance the code is trying to capture.

The foreign-investment picture is also unusually clean at the national level. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling in the record is 100%. There is no partial cap to explain here: on the record provided, foreign ownership is not limited below full ownership. That should not be stretched into claims about permits, operating approvals, land rights, tax treatment, or practical timelines, because none of those facts appear in the record. The reliable point is narrower and stronger: nationally, this activity is open to PMA, with the listed ownership ceiling at 100%, under the cited presidential-regulation source.

Bali does not change that conclusion on this record. In Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, while l4_bali_blocked remains false. The stated reason is that OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this code is not caught by that block as presented. The honest national-vs-Bali picture is therefore direct: 01283 is foreign-open nationally, has a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling in the record, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium described here.
