editorial.headline: Aromatic Crop Farming With a Clear PMA Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01284 covers integrated aromatic-crop farming; nationally it is PMA-open up to 100%, and Bali is not marked as blocking it under the moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01284 is the agricultural frame for aromatic and freshening plants: serai wangi, nilam, menthol, kenanga, ilang-ilang, gandapura, lawang, gaharu, and kayu putih grown for its leaves. The record defines the activity as a farm sequence, starting with land preparation and moving through sowing, nursery work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried as a continuous activity. It can also cover the same aromatic-crop farming inside forest areas.

Registration is open across the full scale ladder recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes the code usable for a business whose registered activity is the production-side agriculture itself, whether the record is framed as seedling and seed production or as cultivation. The scope separately names Produksi Benih for seedling and seed activity, and Budi Daya for the cultivation of essential-oil plantation crops. Taken together, the named crop list and the process list make the activity concrete: plants, land, nursery, cultivation, maintenance, harvest, and post-harvest as an integrated farm cycle.

Nationally, the PMA signal is clean. The record marks the activity TERBUKA, sets pma_max_asing at 100, and cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, the foreign stake is not capped below full ownership in the slim record: the national ceiling is 100%. That is the most important national reading for a foreign founder or investor choosing a business activity. The registration analysis still has to stay inside the scope: the business being registered must be the agricultural activity described here, not an imagined adjacent activity.

For Bali, the record is direct. l4_bali_blocked is false, and l4_bali_status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is narrow: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the Bali moratorium does not block PMA registration for this activity. The moratorium described in the record is island-wide and permanent for all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, with the source listed as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. On this record, 01284 is genuinely open: foreign ownership is allowed up to 100% nationally, and Bali is not marked as blocking PMA registration.

editorial.headline: Rhizome Medicinal Farming With a Clean Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: A precise home for ginger, turmeric, ginseng and other rhizome biofarmaka cultivation, open nationally to PMA and not caught by Bali’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the farming of rhizome medicinal plants: the underground-stem crops that sit at the base of Indonesia’s biofarmaka economy. The record names ginger, turmeric, temulawak, temugiring, temuireng, temukunci, kencur, lengkuas, lempuyang and dlingo, and it also includes similar plants used as botanical pesticide materials. In practical terms, this is not a trading code or a processing-room code. Its center of gravity is cultivation: preparing land, sowing, planting, maintaining, harvesting and carrying out post-harvest activity when those steps form one connected agricultural sequence.

The scope also reaches into seed-oriented activity. Planting rhizome medicinal crops to produce seed is included, as are nursery and seed-production activities for these medicinal or biofarmaka rhizome plants. The record specifically names ginseng seed production and ginseng cultivation within the same agricultural chain. That matters because the code is broad enough to hold a serious farming operation, not just a single crop line. A founder registering it should be describing a real cultivation business around these rhizome plants, whether the emphasis is crop production, seed production, or the full field-to-post-harvest sequence described in the scope.

On scale, the opening is unusually wide. The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar as open scales, so the activity can sit with operators from micro farms through large-scale agricultural ventures. Nationally, it is also open to foreign investment: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap to soften or explain away here. Based on the slim record, a foreign-owned company can hold the full permitted foreign stake for this activity at the national level, provided the registration facts match the agricultural scope described above.

The Bali picture is equally important, because many founders misread “open nationally” as automatically clean on the island. For this code, the record says Bali is not blocking PMA registration: `l4_bali_blocked` is false. The reason is precise. At Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by Bali’s moratorium, which blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. That makes this a genuinely usable Bali candidate on the data given here: nationally foreign-open, 100% PMA-capable, open across the listed scales, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium recorded for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: For this code, Bali is not a hidden contradiction to the national opening; the record says it is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Non-Rhizome Medicinal Crops, From Fieldwork to Seed
editorial.standfirst: A farming code for non-rhizome medicinal and biofarmaka plants, open across business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the cultivation of non-rhizome medicinal plants: a practical agricultural category for crops such as cardamom, aloe vera, sambiloto, mengkudu or pace, mahkota dewa, and green lemongrass, including comparable plants used for botanical pesticide materials. Its scope is not limited to planting. The record describes a full farming cycle: land preparation, sowing, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one connected chain. It also reaches seed production by planting non-rhizome medicinal crops to produce seed in the form of grain.

The same scope also captures the cultivation and seed-production work for non-rhizome medicinal or biofarmaka plants named in the record: kina, adas pinang, and gambir. That matters because the code is written around the agricultural operation, not around a single finished product. A founder using it is not merely saying, “we trade herbal ingredients.” The registered activity is the farming process itself: preparing land, raising or propagating plants, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling the immediate post-harvest sequence where it remains part of the same agricultural chain.

On scale, the record is unusually clean: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clean. This activity carries TERBUKA PMA status with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In plain English, the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. A foreign-owned company can therefore read the national line as open, provided the real registered business is the cultivation of these non-rhizome medicinal plants and the integrated farming steps described in the scope.

The Bali picture is also honest but not obstructive. The province has a moratorium rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, island-wide and permanent. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked in the slim record. The reason is specific: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The result is a straightforward conclusion, without a hidden provincial contradiction: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, open across the listed scales, and in Bali not blocked by the cited moratorium status in this record.

editorial.headline: Cultivating Prohibited Plants: Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This integrated cultivation category is open across four enterprise scales, yet is closed to PMA nationally and blocked for foreign registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the cultivation of narcotic plants and prohibited medicinal plants. Its stated scope takes in the full agricultural chain: land preparation, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when these are carried out as one continuous sequence. That last qualification matters. The activity is framed as an integrated operation, joining work in the ground with the follow-on handling that belongs to the same run of activity. It is therefore not merely a label for planting; it describes the connected agricultural process set out in the record.

The category is available to businesses at every listed enterprise scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. The practical registrant is accordingly a business undertaking that full cultivation-and-post-harvest sequence, at any of those stated scales. Scale availability, however, answers only the size question. It should not be confused with the foreign-investment position. The record places enterprise scale and foreign ownership in separate fields, and they lead to different conclusions: all four scales are listed as open, while PMA is not.

Nationally, the foreign-investment status is TERTUTUP, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 0%. The implication is direct: this activity is closed to PMA registration at national level. There is no partial foreign stake within the stated ceiling; the ceiling itself is zero. For an investor assessing an Indonesian structure, that is the point on which the entry question turns. The availability of Micro through Large scales does not create a foreign-investment route, because the national ownership position remains closed.

Bali reaches the same result, rather than offering a regional opening. Its status is TERTUTUP, the record marks it as blocked for PMA, and the stated reason identifies the national closure and 0% position. Accordingly, a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali record also cites a provincial rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA across the island on a permanent basis. That provincial setting is relevant context for Bali registration, but the conclusion here is already unambiguous: national closure and Bali's recorded blocked status point in one direction. This is an activity whose listed business scales remain available, while foreign ownership does not.
editorial.pullQuote: This is an activity whose listed business scales remain available, while foreign ownership does not.

Its served per_skala (8 rows) cites pp28_sources=['01287'], but the pinned PP28 corpus records ABSENT for 01287 across all 21 lampiran files (11,208 pages, text-hunt; pp28/ABSENT.json) — the cited source is not retrievable. The row content is a GENERIC agriculture/estate-crop package (seed-producer attestations from UPT Pusat/UPTD, GAP cultivation guidance, no-burn land clearing) with no vocabulary specific to controlled/prohibited-crop cultivation. Found by the blind cross-family extractor (GLM 5.2) 2026-07-18; conductor-verified on the canonical payload and the vault ABSENT record. editorial.headline: Other Spice and Aromatic Crop Farming, Open Through the Bali Filter
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated cultivation and seed production for other spice and aromatic crops, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01289 is a farming code for other spice, aromatic, and refreshing crops: the record names candlenut, vanilla, cinnamon, ginseng, quinine, fennel, areca nut, and gambier as examples of the activity family. Its core is not trading or processing as a separate business line, but cultivation as an integrated agricultural sequence: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and postharvest work carried out as one connected operation.

The scope also reaches seed-oriented activity. Where the same crop family is grown to produce seed in the form of grains, the activity remains inside this code. That matters editorially because the record frames the code around the agricultural cycle itself: soil work, nursery or seedling work, planting, crop care, harvest, and seed production are all part of the same described field of work when they concern these other spice and aromatic crops.

On business scale, the code is broad. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can describe anything from a very small cultivation setup to a large-scale farming operation, provided the registered activity remains within this crop and cultivation scope. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity.

The Bali reading is also unusually clear. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this code is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance. For this activity, the record supports a clean national-and-Bali position: foreign ownership is open nationally up to 100%, and the Bali moratorium field does not block PMA registration for the code.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pertanian tanaman penghasil getah seperti karet dan tanaman penghasil getah lainnya, misalnya damar, pinus, dan kemenyan. editorial.headline: Rubber and Resin Cultivation With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers rubber and other sap-producing crops from planting to post-harvest, with foreign ownership nationally open and no Bali PMA block recorded.
editorial.body:
This activity is agricultural before it is industrial: the field work of growing rubber trees and other plants that produce sap or resin, including damar, pine, and kemenyan. Its scope is broad enough to follow the crop through the practical life of cultivation, from land preparation and planting to maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one continuous activity.

It also reaches into two important edges of the sector. First, it includes rubber and other sap-producing crop activity conducted inside forest areas. Second, it covers planting these crops to produce seed in the form of grains or seeds. In plain English, this is not merely a plantation label for mature rubber output; it can also describe the agricultural base that prepares, grows, maintains, harvests, and supports seed production for rubber and comparable sap-producing plants.

The registration audience is wide. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it is not reserved only for large plantation groups. A small agricultural operator, a mid-sized grower, or a larger structured business can all sit within the same activity description if the actual work matches the scope: cultivation of rubber or other sap-producing crops, including the connected land, planting, maintenance, harvest, post-harvest, forest-area, or seed-production activities described in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The Bali picture is equally important, and in this case it does not reverse the national answer. Bali's moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the province, but this record is not blocked: the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest reading is therefore clean: nationally open, up to full foreign ownership, and not recorded as blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pertanian tanaman tahunan lainnya, seperti cemara; tanaman jarak pagar; aren; kaliandra; gamal; tanaman yang utamanya untuk menganyam, seperti bambu dan rotan; serta tanaman berdaur pendek yang berkembang melalui trubusan sebagai tanaman energi, seperti poplar dan dedalu. Pertanian tanaman tahunan lainnya yang dimaksud mencakup kegiatan pengolahan lahan, penanaman, pemeliharaan, pemanenan, dan kegiatan pascapanen yang dilakukan sebagai satu rangkaian kegiatan. Kelompok ini juga mencakup kegiatan kegiatan pertanian tanaman tahunan tersebut yang dilakukan dalam kawasan hutan, serta penanaman tanaman tersebut untuk menghasilkan benih berupa biji.

editorial.headline: Other Perennial Crops, With Bali Open Only Above the Moratorium Line
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01299 covers a broad field of perennial crop farming, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for Bali PMA registration at higher-risk scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01299 is the residual but important home for **other perennial crop farming**: cultivation that does not sit neatly inside a narrower named activity, yet still has a real agricultural profile. The record points to cemara; jatropha; aren; calliandra; gamal; weaving-oriented plants such as bamboo and rattan; and short-cycle coppice energy plants such as poplar and willow. It is not just the act of planting. The scope runs across land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one connected agricultural activity.

That breadth matters. This code can cover perennial crop work inside forest areas, and it also covers planting these crops to produce seed in the form of grains. The record also frames the activity in two operational lenses: seed and nursery activity for cemara and other perennial crops, and cultivation of cemara and other perennial crops. In plain English, it is for businesses whose core activity is growing these long-lived plants, whether the output is crop material, seed, or a cultivation cycle that includes the practical field and post-harvest chain.

On the national investment reading, the code is straightforward: its PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with a foreign ownership ceiling of **100%**. The open scales are **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar**, so the record does not confine the activity to one size of enterprise. A foreign investor reading only the national line would see a fully open activity, including for larger operations. That is the clean national position, and the foreign-ownership point should be stated without unnecessary drama: the record shows no foreign share cap below full ownership.

The Bali picture is more specific, and more useful for a founder. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record is marked **l4_bali_blocked: false**. The reason is precise: OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practice, this is not a case where the code is nationally open but unusable for a foreign-owned Bali registration today. It is nationally open, and the Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** because the higher-risk reading keeps it outside the moratorium block. The honest conclusion is therefore measured: KBLI 01299 is available for PMA registration in Bali when treated on the higher-risk scale described in the record, without inventing extra licence, capital, tax, or timing requirements beyond the slim record itself.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Ornamental Plant Farming With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the cultivation of living ornamental foliage, flowers, and transplantable turf, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
This activity is the agricultural side of the ornamental plant economy: the cultivation of living foliage plants, flowering ornamentals, and plants grown for decorative use. The record gives a broad, concrete field of activity, from bonsai, monstera, philodendron, dracaena, cordyline, anthurium foliage, ferns, aglaonema, sansevieria, caladium, and palms to flowering plants such as orchids, roses, adenium, flowering anthurium, euphorbia, and ixora. It also covers planting for ornamental purposes and grassed land prepared for transplanting. In plain terms, this is not a retail shop category and not a landscape-design description; it is farming or cultivation where the product is ornamental life.

The operating scope is also written as an integrated agricultural sequence. It includes land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest activity when those steps are carried out as one chain of activity. That matters because the activity is defined by the cultivation process, not merely by the beauty or market value of the plants. A founder using this classification should be able to recognise a farm, nursery, or grower operation inside the wording: the work begins with soil or growing media and continues through care, harvest, and post-harvest handling.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the category is not framed only for large plantations or only for small growers; the same activity language can describe a modest ornamental nursery as well as a larger cultivation operation, provided the real business activity remains within the farming and cultivation scope described above. The national investment position is also direct: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no capped foreign stake in the record, so the national reading is a clean foreign-open position rather than a conditional minority opening.

The Bali picture is more specific, and here the honest answer is favourable. The province-wide moratorium described in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this activity is marked as not blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign founder, the practical editorial point is simple: this ornamental plant farming activity is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali moratorium field in the record does not close it. The remaining judgment is therefore not a hidden ownership warning; it is whether the planned operation truly fits the cultivation chain described in the scope.

editorial.headline: Wild Plant Propagation Is Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01302 covers the propagation of wild plants, with national PMA access up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block under the stated risk position.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01302 is a narrow but important activity: the propagation and breeding of wild plants. The Indonesian scope points to work that keeps plant reproduction going through practical propagation methods, including vegetative breeding from stem cuttings, plant pieces, and seedlings. In plain English, this is not a general farming label and not a broad trading category. It is for an operator whose registered activity is the controlled breeding or propagation of wild plant material so that the plants can continue to be developed and reproduced.

The record makes the scale picture unusually clean. This activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses. That means the classification is not reserved only for a large corporate operator, nor is it limited to a small local enterprise. A founder reading this should see it as a scale-flexible activity: the same activity description can sit across the stated business scales, provided the registered business is genuinely doing the propagation work described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clear. At the national level, PMA is classified as TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign ownership ceiling. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so there is no need to soften the sentence: at the national level, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That is the clean national baseline, and it matters because founders often confuse an open national classification with an automatically smooth local registration path.

For Bali, the honest reading is that this one is not blocked by the province’s PMA moratorium on the record provided. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. But the Bali reason given here says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The result is a more practical conclusion than a blanket warning: KBLI 01302 is nationally open, can reach 100% foreign ownership, and is not marked as Bali-blocked in this record. The caveat is not a hidden prohibition; it is simply that the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, which should be read exactly as stated rather than expanded into obligations the record does not give.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Other Plant Propagation, Read as a Real Production Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01309 covers the practical nursery work behind living planting material, and it is open nationally and in Bali for foreign-owned registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01309 is not a generic farming label. It is the activity of producing plant material for further propagation: vegetative seed production, cut stems, plant pieces, seedlings, grafting stock, cuttings, layers, tubers, roots, mushroom spawn and plant nurseries. In plain English, this is the business of preparing living plant material so another planting cycle can happen. The record also places chilli seedling activity inside this scope, which matters because it keeps the code anchored in nursery and propagation work rather than broad crop cultivation.

The commercial shape of the code is wide. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the same activity can describe a small propagation operation, a growing nursery business, or a larger production setup. That scale range should not be read as permission to stretch the activity beyond its stated scope. The centre of gravity remains the production and preparation of plant material for replanting, multiplication, grafting or nursery use. A founder registering this code should be able to explain the actual propagation process, the living plant outputs, and the role those outputs play in continued plant production.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the code is open to foreign-owned registration at the national level, with no foreign equity cap shown in the slim record. For a foreign founder, the honest reading is therefore not a partial-access code or a minority-stake category: on the national PMA line, it is open up to full foreign ownership.

Bali does not change that answer into a block. The provincial moratorium described in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked. The reason is also explicit: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The practical editorial conclusion is clean: a foreign investor can read KBLI 01309 as nationally open and not Bali-blocked, while still treating the registered activity as the specific propagation and nursery production work described in the scope.

Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Beef Cattle Built for Scale, Not Ambiguity
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers beef-cattle fattening and breeding, open across all business scales and nationally available to foreign ownership, including in Bali’s current PMA reading.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01411 is about the practical upstream work behind beef supply: raising beef cattle through fattening until the animals are ready for slaughter, and breeding beef cattle to produce breeding stock, semen, and embryos. Its scope is not framed as trading, retailing, or food service. It sits at the production end of the chain, where the business activity is the cultivation and breeding of beef cattle themselves.

That makes the code useful for operators whose registered activity is centered on livestock production rather than downstream distribution. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the category is not limited to one size of enterprise. A small holder, a growing breeding operation, or a larger cattle-fattening business can all read the scale field as part of the same activity family, provided the registered business genuinely matches the described scope.

The national foreign-investment position is also clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is recorded at 100%. In plain English, the activity is nationally open to foreign ownership up to full ownership, according to the cited source in the record. There is no partial cap in this slim record, and no basis here to invent one. For a foreign-owned setup, the decisive question is therefore not whether the activity is nationally closed; on this record, it is not.

Bali’s local moratorium picture does not overturn that conclusion for this code. The record says Bali blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but it also says this activity is not blocked because the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali status is therefore not a prohibition in this slim record: it is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false. The honest reading is that KBLI 01411 is nationally foreign-open, carries a 100% recorded foreign-ownership ceiling, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium logic supplied here.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 01411 is nationally foreign-open, carries a 100% recorded foreign-ownership ceiling, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Dairy Cattle Farming With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers dairy cattle cultivation, milk production, fattening, and breeding, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01412 is the activity space for dairy cattle as a productive herd, not merely as livestock ownership. The record describes three connected parts of the business: cultivating dairy cattle, fattening them, and producing milk; then the breeding work needed to generate dairy cattle stock, semen, and embryos. In practical terms, this is the code for operators whose core activity is the managed raising and breeding of dairy cows, with milk and breeding outputs sitting inside the same defined scope.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not framed as a category reserved only for industrial farms. A smaller dairy breeding operation and a larger integrated dairy cattle business both sit within the scale range stated in the slim record. That matters because the activity is defined by what it does, not by one single operating size: dairy cattle cultivation, fattening, milk production, and breeding remain the anchor points.

For foreign ownership, the national rule is straightforward on this record. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership value is 100. Stated plainly, the national position allows full foreign ownership for this activity, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial foreign-ownership ceiling in the record to soften or reinterpret; the ceiling is 100%, and that is the number founders should read before moving into location-specific checks.

Bali is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, according to the record. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason states that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest national-versus-Bali picture is therefore not a contradiction. Nationally, the code is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not block PMA registration under the moratorium because the stated risk position is higher than the blocked Low and Medium-Low band.

editorial.headline: Buffalo Fattening and Breeding With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01413 covers meat-buffalo cultivation, from fattening animals for slaughter to producing breeding stock, semen, and embryos, with full PMA access on the national record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01413 is a precise livestock activity, not a broad agricultural catch-all. Its scope is the cultivation of meat buffalo, including fattening animals until they are ready for slaughter and breeding work that produces meat-buffalo stock, semen, and embryos. In practical terms, this is the code for an operator whose core business is raising and developing buffalo for the meat chain, whether the activity is focused on production animals, breeding output, or both within the same defined scope.

The record opens this activity across the full business scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not confined, on this slim record, to a single operating size. A small rural operation, a mid-sized breeding setup, and a larger cultivation business all sit within the scale language provided here, as long as the registered activity remains the cultivation and breeding of meat buffalo described in the scope. The editorial point is discipline: this code is about buffalo fattening and breeding outputs, not adjacent livestock ideas or downstream assumptions that are not named in the record.

Nationally, the PMA signal is straightforward. With TERBUKA status, this activity permits foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no partial cap to soften or explain away: on the national record supplied here, foreign ownership may reach the full ceiling. The source attached to that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special licence, minimum capital rule, tax condition, or timing requirement, so those points should not be read into the classification. The nationally relevant message is simply that this KBLI is foreign-open, and the ceiling shown is complete rather than capped below control.

Bali is where many KBLI readings become more delicate, but this record does not show a moratorium block. The province-wide rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, and the stated Bali reason says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The Bali status is therefore not a green-light slogan; it is the more careful OK_or_HIGHER_RISK position. For founders, the honest reading is that KBLI 01413 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and, on the Bali fields provided here, it is not blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium because its larger-scale risk profile sits above the blocked Low and Medium-Low band.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 01413 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and the Bali record does not place it inside the province's PMA moratorium block.

Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. editorial.headline: Dairy Buffalo, Open on the Record
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01414 covers dairy buffalo cultivation, milk production and breeding, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01414 is a narrow agricultural code with a technical center of gravity. The Indonesian scope describes cultivation of dairy buffalo through fattening and milk production, then extends into breeding activity that produces dairy buffalo breeding stock, semen and embryos. Read in plain English, this is the code for an operator whose business is the dairy buffalo herd itself: raising the animals for milk output, and maintaining the breeding line that supplies future productive stock. The scope is not decorative language. It is the boundary of the article: dairy buffalo cultivation, dairy output and dairy buffalo breeding.

The scale field is unusually simple. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar, which means the code is available across the full scale ladder recorded here. A micro operator, a small or medium operator, and a large operator are all within the scale field when the declared activity stays inside this scope. That is the first practical reading for founders: the code is not reserved only for industrial-scale livestock capital, and it is not confined only to local smallholder form. Its registered size can follow the recorded business scale.

For PMA, the national signal is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In investor language, that is full foreign ownership, not a partial-ownership cap. There is no hidden percentage to infer from the record. The only defensible statement is narrower and stronger: nationally, the record treats this dairy buffalo cultivation and breeding activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion on the supplied record. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this code is recorded as not blocked in Bali. The reason matters: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is stated as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. That is the honest national-vs-Bali picture. Nationally, KBLI 01414 is open to full PMA ownership; in Bali, the record does not show a moratorium block. The editorial discipline is to keep the activity inside its stated scope: dairy buffalo fattening, milk production, breeding stock, semen and embryos.

editorial.headline: Horse Breeding and Equine Farming With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01420 covers the breeding and cultivation of horses and similar equines, open across business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01420 is a practical agricultural classification for the breeding and cultivation of horses and similar equines. Its scope is not limited to one kind of animal use: it covers horses raised for meat, milk, racing, riding, draught work, cavalry, polo, companionship, and related equines such as mules and hinnies. It also reaches the reproductive side of the activity, including breeding stock, semen, and embryos. In plain English, this is the code for producing horses and comparable equines as livestock and breeding assets, including the production of horse milk and similar milk.

The boundary matters. This code is about cultivation and breeding, not the management of sports riding or racing facilities. editorial.headline: Camel and Camelid Farming Under Indonesia's KBLI 2025
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to foreign ownership, including at large scale, and the Bali record does not show a moratorium block for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
Camel and similar-animal farming is a narrow but complete livestock activity. The record covers cultivation to produce slaughter camels, dairy camels, and comparable camelids such as llamas, alpacas, vicunas, and guanacos. It also reaches breeding work: producing breeding stock, semen, and embryos. Milk production from camels and similar animals sits inside the same activity, so the code is not only about keeping animals on land; it covers the productive chain around meat, milk, and genetic propagation.

That breadth matters for founders because the activity is not framed around one end product. A business may be oriented toward dairy output, meat production, breeding supply, or the biological inputs that support breeding. The Indonesian scope uses the language of cultivation and breeding, which means the core identity is agricultural production, not retail, logistics, food service, or veterinary work. The discipline in registration is therefore to keep the declared business activity anchored to the animals and outputs named in the scope, without importing side activities that the record does not state.

The scale picture is unusually broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open in the record. That makes the activity available across the formal size ladder, from small operators to large-scale livestock ventures. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure is 100%, so the record does not show a foreign-share cap. For a foreign-owned setup, the national reading is therefore clean: the activity is open, and the cited ownership ceiling is full foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a different reason than many founders expect. Bali's provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently. Here, however, the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is not that every operational detail is resolved; the record does not give permits, site rules, livestock-health requirements, timelines, tax treatment, or capital figures. It simply says that, on the fields provided, this activity is nationally foreign-open and not shown as blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Sheep Fattening and Breeding, Open at Every Scale
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers meat sheep fattening and breeding, and it is open nationally to foreign ownership, including PMA registration in Bali under the stated risk picture.
editorial.body:
**This code is about the practical business of producing meat sheep.** Its scope covers two connected activities: raising sheep through fattening so they become ready for slaughter, and breeding sheep to produce breeding stock, semen, and embryos. In plain English, it is not a generic livestock label. It is specifically for meat-oriented sheep cultivation and the upstream breeding work that supports that production chain.

That breadth matters because the record recognises the activity across the full business-size ladder. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. A small sheep operation, a growing breeding program, or a larger production business can all sit within the same activity description if the real activity remains meat sheep fattening and breeding. The scope is anchored in the animal and the production purpose: sheep intended for meat, plus the breeding inputs needed to reproduce and improve that herd.

For foreign investors, the national position is unusually clear. The PMA status remains TERBUKA, while the foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. There is no foreign stake cap in the slim record: a foreign-owned company can hold the full allowed percentage nationally under the cited PMA source. That does not create any extra licence, permit, timeline, capital threshold, or tax rule by itself; it simply means the investment-list status does not close the activity to foreign ownership and does not reduce the foreign share below full ownership.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a more specific reason. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, on a permanent island-wide basis. This activity is not marked as blocked for Bali. The reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms, the honest read is this: nationally open, foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied. The right caution is not to invent a hidden barrier, but to keep the classification tied tightly to the activity actually described: meat sheep fattening and breeding, including breeding stock, semen, and embryos.

editorial.headline: Goat Meat Breeding and Fattening Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01442 covers meat-goat fattening and breeding, open across business scales and nationally open to full foreign ownership, with Bali not blocking PMA registration under its moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01442 is a focused livestock activity: the cultivation and breeding of meat goats. Its scope covers fattening activities to produce goats for slaughter, and breeding activities to produce meat-goat livestock seed, semen, and embryos. In plain English, this is not a general animal-trading or mixed-farm category; it is the production side of the meat-goat chain, including both the growth of animals for meat output and the upstream reproductive material that supports herd development.

The record opens the activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That range matters because it means the code is not written only for a large industrial operator or only for a household-scale farm. It can describe a small goat-fattening setup, a growing breeder, or a larger operation, as long as the registered activity remains inside the stated scope: fattening for meat-goat output and breeding for livestock seed, semen, and embryos. The scale choice should therefore follow the actual business footprint, not a different interpretation of the code.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. Sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%. There is no partial foreign cap to explain here: the record gives a full ceiling. For a foreign-owned setup, the national reading is therefore straightforward: this activity is open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, provided the business is genuinely carrying out the activity described in the scope.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide on a permanent basis, according to the governor-letter source in the record. But this activity is not marked as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is that a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today under this record’s Bali status, which is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The point is not that Bali has no moratorium; the point is that this code, on the record provided, does not fall into the moratorium block.

editorial.headline: Dairy Goat Breeding Has a Clear PMA Path, Including Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01443 covers dairy goat cultivation and breeding for milk, livestock seed, semen, and embryos, open across all business scales with full foreign ownership allowed.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01443 is a compact but materially specific livestock category. Its centre of gravity is dairy goats: the cultivation activity that produces milk, and the breeding activity that produces dairy goat livestock seed, semen, and embryos. In plain English, this is not a broad food retail or general farming label. It is the code for operators whose business is built around raising dairy goats and developing the reproductive base behind that herd.

The scale profile is unusually straightforward. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the same activity can be registered by a small operator or a larger enterprise, provided the registered business genuinely matches the dairy-goat cultivation and breeding scope. The scope matters because the code is anchored in production and breeding, not in downstream claims beyond milk, livestock seed, semen, and embryos.

Nationally, the PMA reading is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with foreign ownership allowed up to 100%. That means the record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The source cited for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the editorial conclusion should stay within that boundary: this code is foreign-open nationally, without inventing any extra licence, timeline, capital threshold, or sectoral condition not stated in the record.

Bali’s position is equally clear, although it turns on a different reason than many founders expect. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, according to the stated rule. This code, however, is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest lede, therefore, is not that Bali closes the door. For this dairy goat cultivation and breeding activity, the record supports a PMA pathway nationally and does not show a Bali moratorium block.

editorial.headline: Dairy Sheep Breeding That Remains Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01444 covers dairy sheep farming and breeding, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01444 is a narrow agricultural activity: the cultivation of dairy sheep to produce milk, and the breeding work needed to produce dairy sheep stock, semen, and embryos. In plain English, this is not a general livestock category and not a catch-all for sheep trading. Its centre of gravity is dairy production from sheep, supported by breeding activity that improves or multiplies the herd itself.

That makes the code relevant for operators who are building an actual dairy-sheep production base rather than a loose rural supply chain. The record opens it across all four business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small farm, a growing breeding operation, or a larger integrated dairy-sheep enterprise can all sit inside the scale field given here, provided the registered activity remains within the scope: dairy sheep cultivation, dairy sheep breeding, breeding stock, semen, and embryos.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. PMA is classified TERBUKA, with the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded at 100%. That means the slim record does not show a foreign share cap below full ownership. The authority source attached to that status is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder reading this at national level, the key point is simple: the activity is not presented here as a restricted foreign-investment line.

For a different reason, Bali’s position is unusually clear as well. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration across the province. This code is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a caveat about Bali being closed; on this record, a foreign-owned setup can look at KBLI 01444 in Bali as nationally open and not moratorium-blocked, while staying tightly inside the activity’s dairy-sheep and breeding scope.

Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. editorial.headline: Raw Wool Production Is Open Nationally, Including in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01445 covers the farming activity of producing raw sheep wool, open across business scales and not caught by Bali’s PMA moratorium screen.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01445 is a narrow agricultural-production code: it covers livestock farming activity that produces raw sheep wool. The record points to the upstream act itself, not a finished textile, retail product, or broader processing chain. In plain English, this is the business of raising sheep for their wool output and registering that raw-wool production activity as the formal Indonesian business classification.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The code is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the classification is not confined to one business size in the slim record. A small local farm, a growing mid-sized operation, or a larger agricultural enterprise can all sit inside the same activity description when the registered business is the production of raw wool from sheep farming. That breadth matters because the code’s meaning stays anchored in the activity, while the permitted scale range tells founders how broadly the registration can be used.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is also clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the record, so the editorial conclusion should not invent one: for the national screen, this is a foreign-open activity up to full foreign ownership. The source field gives the legal reference, but the business takeaway is simpler: the record does not mark this KBLI as nationally closed or restricted below full foreign ownership.

The Bali reading is the decisive part, because Bali’s PMA moratorium can change the practical answer even where the national screen is open. Here, however, the record says l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is specific: the OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and therefore it is not blocked by the moratorium. Bali’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province on a permanent island-wide basis, but this code is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The honest conclusion is that a foreign-owned business can register this KBLI in Bali today under the record’s Bali screen, with no invented caveat added beyond the stated higher-risk status.

editorial.headline: Local Chicken Breeding With a Clear PMA Path in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01463 covers the breeding of local chickens and their crosses, with national foreign ownership open up to 100% and no Bali PMA block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01463 is a tightly defined poultry-breeding activity: the breeding of local chickens and their crosses to produce breeding stock and hatching eggs for local layer chickens, local broiler chickens, and their crossbred lines. Its centre of gravity is not general poultry trading, feed supply, or downstream meat and egg retail. It is the upstream work of producing the birds and hatching eggs from which those local production lines begin.

That makes the code relevant for operators whose business model is built around controlled breeding rather than simple flock ownership. The slim record opens it across **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so the activity is not framed as belonging only to large industrial players. A small breeding operation, a mid-sized hatchery-oriented business, and a larger corporate breeding setup can all sit within the same activity description, provided the registered activity remains the breeding of local chickens and their crosses for breeding stock and hatching eggs.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**. In plain terms, the national rule set does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. That is an important distinction for a founder or investor reading the code: the restriction is not hidden in a partial ceiling, and the PMA source is identified in the record as **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**.

The Bali picture is also clear, but it needs to be read precisely. Bali’s province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, according to the recorded moratorium rule. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked in Bali: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the recorded status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. The reason given is that OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so the Bali moratorium does not block it. The honest conclusion is therefore not that Bali is unavailable, nor that every scale is frictionless; it is that this KBLI is foreign-open nationally, can reach 100% foreign ownership, and is not recorded as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium logic supplied here.

KBLI 01464 is a poultry-farming classification, but its centre of gravity is specific: local chickens and their crossbreeds. The record frames the activity around raising these birds to produce three commercial outputs: pullets, local meat chickens ready for slaughter, and eggs for consumption. That makes it a production code, not a trading label or a general livestock umbrella. Its practical identity is the controlled cultivation of local poultry stock for farmers and operators whose business sits at the farm level.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the same classification can describe a small local poultry unit as well as a larger farm operation, provided the registered activity remains inside the stated scope. For founders, that breadth matters because the code is not reserved for one business size. It can follow the size of the operation rather than forcing the activity into a narrow registration lane.

Nationally, the position on foreign investment is unambiguous. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the slim record does not impose a reduced foreign share for this activity at the national level. The source given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the ownership figure should be read exactly as recorded: fully open, not partly capped.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a precise reason. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently, under the governor-letter source in the record. This activity is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning dressed as complexity. editorial.headline: Duck Farming and Breeding Is Open, Including in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers duck cultivation and breeding for meat, eggs, hatching eggs and stock, with PMA open nationally and not blocked by Bali's moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01465 is a production-centered activity for the cultivation and breeding of ducks. The Indonesian scope is clear: it covers budi daya itik dan bebek to produce meat ducks, laying ducks, consumption eggs and other outputs, and it also covers breeding activity that produces hatching eggs and duck stock. In plain English, this is the activity of raising ducks and running duck-breeding operations, with the economic object sitting in the birds, the eggs, and the breeding material described in the record.

The scale position is unusually broad because the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That means the same activity can be registered across the listed business scales, so long as the registered business activity remains the cultivation and breeding described in the scope. A small operator focused on duck cultivation and a larger enterprise producing meat ducks, laying ducks, consumption eggs, hatching eggs or duck stock are both within the scale language supplied. The important editorial point is not to narrow the code artificially: the record itself names the scale range and the productive outputs.

Nationally, the PMA reading is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling in the record is 100%. There is no capped foreign stake to explain here. For a foreign investor, the practical reading is unusually clean: this activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership and, in Bali, it is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium.

Bali is where the record needs to be read carefully, because the province's moratorium blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. This activity is not on the blocked side of that rule in the supplied record. editorial.headline: Quail Farming With a Clear Foreign-Ownership Lane
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01466 covers quail farming and breeding for meat birds, laying birds, consumption eggs, breeding stock, and hatching eggs, open across all business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01466 is a compact but complete agricultural activity: the cultivation and breeding of quail. Its scope is not merely keeping birds; it covers the production of quail for meat, quail kept for laying, eggs for consumption, breeding stock, and hatching eggs. In practical terms, this is the code for an operator whose business is built around the quail production cycle, from raising birds to producing the next generation of livestock.

The activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine this activity to a single size of operator. A small farm and a larger poultry operation can both sit within the same activity description, provided the actual work remains inside the stated scope: quail cultivation, quail breeding, meat birds, laying birds, consumption eggs, breeding stock, and hatching eggs.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership stated in the record is 100%. There is no partial ceiling to explain here: the record gives a full foreign-ownership lane. That does not turn the activity into a catch-all poultry category, and it does not add permissions that are not written in the scope. It simply means that, for this specific quail-farming and quail-breeding activity, the national investment status is open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling.

The Bali picture is also unusually clean. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this record is not blocked. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance: for this code, the record shows a nationally open PMA activity, open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, with no Bali moratorium block recorded.

editorial.headline: Pigeon Breeding at Commercial Scale, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers pigeon farming and breeding for meat, other production purposes, breeding stock, and hatching eggs, with access across all business scales.
editorial.body:
Pigeon breeding under this activity is a farming and propagation business. Its core is the cultivation of pigeons to produce birds for meat or other productive uses, alongside breeding work that produces livestock seed stock and hatching eggs. The scope is narrow but complete: it is not a broad animal-trading category, and it is not merely a hobby aviary. It is the registered activity for operators whose business substance is raising pigeons and reproducing them as a controlled livestock line.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification can serve anything from a very small farm to a large commercial setup. That matters because the registered KBLI should describe the actual operating activity, not just the legal vehicle around it. A small breeder, a mid-sized production farm, and a larger integrated operation may all sit inside the same activity description if their business is genuinely the cultivation and breeding of pigeons for the outputs stated in the scope.

For foreign ownership, the national position is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain English, a PMA structure is nationally open for this activity, and the slim record does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership. The source given for that national investment position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the record supports adding extra capital thresholds, licence promises, tax treatment, or processing timelines, so the editorial conclusion should stay disciplined: nationally open means open as recorded, not open with invented conditions.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province on a permanent basis, yet this activity is not marked as blocked. The recorded reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. That does not turn the activity into a casual registration; it simply means the specific Bali moratorium barrier shown in the record does not close the door. The honest reading is therefore: a foreign-owned setup may use this activity nationally, can reach 100% foreign ownership under the recorded ceiling, and is not currently blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium rule stated here.

editorial.headline: Purebred Chicken Breeding With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01468 covers breeding activity for broiler and layer stock, nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01468 is a narrow but important agricultural production category: the breeding of purebred broiler and layer chickens. Its scope is not ordinary poultry keeping or downstream retail. The record defines it around breeding activity that produces hatching eggs, breeding chicks known as *kuri*, and related outputs. In practical terms, this is the upstream genetic and reproductive layer of a chicken operation, where the business is structured around supplying the next generation of productive birds rather than simply raising chickens for sale.

The activity is open across the full scale range recorded for this code: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the category is not reserved only for very large operators in the record, nor is it limited to smallholder form. A founder reading this code should understand it as a registration lane that can sit at different business sizes, provided the actual registered activity remains within the breeding scope described: purebred broiler and layer breeding, hatching eggs, breeding chicks, and related results.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The slim record marks the code as TERBUKA and gives a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the recorded source. There is no foreign share cap to soften here: the record allows full foreign ownership. The editorial conclusion at national level is therefore straightforward, not cautious by default. For a foreign-owned company, this code is open nationally according to the fields provided.

Bali is also not a hidden stop sign for this record. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis, but this code is not marked as blocked. The recorded Bali reason is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That makes the honest national-vs-Bali picture unusually aligned. A foreign investor can read KBLI 01468 as nationally open, open up to 100% foreign ownership, and not currently blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium rule captured in this record.
editorial.pullQuote: For KBLI 01468, the national rule and the Bali moratorium record point in the same direction: open, including for 100% foreign ownership.
