editorial.headline: Other Poultry Breeding, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01469 covers the cultivation and breeding of turkeys, geese, guinea fowl and other poultry, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01469 is about other poultry as a productive activity, not a label for every animal-related venture.** Its scope covers the cultivation of poultry such as turkey, goose and guinea fowl, with outputs that include meat birds, laying birds and eggs for consumption. The same scope also includes breeding activity for those poultry, where the output is breeding stock or hatching eggs. The record therefore places two linked functions inside one activity: raising these birds for production, and maintaining the breeding line that produces the next flock.

That breadth matters for registration. The code is open across the stated business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical classification terms, the decisive question is not whether the operator is small or large, but whether the declared activity is genuinely the cultivation or breeding of the other poultry described in the scope. A smaller producer of consumption eggs and a larger operation producing meat birds can both sit within the same activity frame if the underlying activity remains inside this record. The scale field is broad, but the activity boundary is still specific.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100. Read plainly, this is not a capped line: the national data supplied here allows PMA participation up to full foreign ownership. There is no basis in the slim record to add a hidden stake limit, minimum capital figure, extra test or timing condition. Beyond the fields supplied, the editorial discipline is to stop where the record stops.

Bali needs its own reading because the provincial moratorium is not the same as the national PMA status. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently. For this activity, however, l4_bali_blocked is false. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. For this record, the honest national-vs-Bali picture is aligned: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and in Bali not blocked by the moratorium described here.

editorial.headline: Ostrich Farming With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: A concise reading of KBLI 01491: ostrich cultivation and breeding, open across business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01491 is a narrow but concrete agricultural activity: the cultivation of ostriches for consumption, including the production of slaughter-ready birds, eggs and related outputs, together with breeding activity that produces ostrich livestock seedlings or hatching eggs. Its scope is not a broad poultry umbrella or a general livestock label. The centre of gravity is the ostrich itself, treated both as a consumable farm output and as a breeding line for future stock.

For founders, that precision matters. A business registering this activity is saying that ostrich cultivation or ostrich breeding is the operating activity, not merely a side description in a wider food, retail or trading plan. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved only for large operators. It can sit at different business sizes, provided the registered activity remains within the actual scope: raising ostriches for consumption outputs, or breeding them for livestock seedlings and hatching eggs.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under the cited investment sources. That means the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no basis here to invent a minimum capital rule, a special livestock licence, a processing threshold, or a timeline. The editorial conclusion has to stay disciplined: nationally, for PMA structuring, this activity is open and the recorded ceiling is 100%.

Bali is also unusually clear on this record. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, permanently, but this activity is not recorded as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest Bali reading is therefore not a warning disguised as analysis: a foreign-owned registration is not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the facts provided. The right caution is narrower and more professional: keep the registered activity faithful to ostrich cultivation and breeding, and do not read permissions, obligations or adjacent activities into a record that does not contain them.

editorial.headline: Silkworm Cocoons Are Nationally Open, but Bali Blocks PMA Registration
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers silkworm cultivation and breeding for cocoons, with all business scales open nationally but PMA registration blocked in Bali under the moratorium.
editorial.body:
Silkworm cultivation is a narrow, physical activity in this record: the breeding and raising of silkworms to produce cocoons. The Indonesian scope is not written as a broad textile, trading, or processing category. Its centre of gravity is the biological production stage, where the business activity is the cultivation and breeding of the worm itself and the output is the cocoon or pupal casing. For founders, that distinction matters because the code describes the activity being registered, not a romantic idea of the silk industry around it.

Nationally, the record is straightforward. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**. The scale field is equally broad: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar** are all open. Read plainly, that means this activity is not reserved only for a single size of operator in the national record, and it is not capped below full foreign ownership under the PMA ceiling shown here. A small silkworm-breeding operation and a larger cultivation setup both sit inside the listed scale range, as long as the registered activity remains the cultivation and breeding of silkworms for cocoons.

The Bali position is the harder part, and it should be read without smoothing it over. Even though the national PMA status is open, the record marks Bali as **Blocked (risk class)** and sets **l4_bali_blocked** to true. The reason given is specific: OSS risk at scale **Besar** is **Rendah/Menengah-Rendah** on every scope, and that places it inside the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. So the honest lede is simple: a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today, even though the same activity is nationally foreign-open.

That tension is the practical editorial point of this code. On paper, the activity is accessible across all listed business scales and allows full foreign ownership under the cited national framework, **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In Bali, however, the provincial filter overrides the practical outcome for PMA registration because the activity falls into the blocked risk class under the moratorium source, **Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP**. This is not a warning about permits, capital, taxes, or timing beyond what the record says. It is a registration reality: nationally open does not mean Bali-open when the local moratorium blocks the risk class.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open does not mean Bali-open when the local moratorium blocks the risk class.

editorial.headline: Bee Cultivation and Breeding for Honey, Wax, Propolis and Honeycomb
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01493 covers bee cultivation and breeding, open across all business scales and fully open to foreign ownership, including in Bali under the stated risk picture.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01493 is a practical agricultural activity code for businesses built around bees themselves: cultivating and breeding bees to produce honey, beeswax, propolis and honeycomb, as well as the activity of bee breeding. The centre of the code is not retail, processing, packaging, or a wellness concept wrapped around honey. It is the underlying beekeeping and breeding operation that creates those bee-derived products.

That makes the code relevant for founders whose business model begins at the production layer. A micro beekeeper, a small farm-linked honey producer, a medium operator building a more formal supply base, or a large-scale venture can all sit within the scale range recorded for this activity. The record opens the code to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar, so the question is not whether the activity is reserved for a particular enterprise size. It is how the founder’s actual operation, capital structure and registration scale match the activity being declared.

For foreign-owned companies, the national position is clean: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national investment list does not cap foreign shareholding below full ownership for this activity. A PMA company can therefore use this code nationally, provided the registered business genuinely corresponds to bee cultivation and breeding rather than a neighbouring commercial activity not described in the record.

The Bali position is also important because many foreign founders assume that an activity open nationally is automatically blocked on the island if agriculture is involved. The record does not support that conclusion here. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, but this record states that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is straightforward: this KBLI is nationally foreign-open up to 100%, and the Bali status in the record is not a PMA registration block today. The caveat is narrow but real: the code should be used for the beekeeping and bee-breeding activity it actually describes, not stretched to cover downstream ideas that are not in the scope.

Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. editorial.headline: Deer Breeding as a Fully Open National Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01494 covers deer and muntjac breeding for stock, meat, hides, and related outputs, with full national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01494 is a focused agricultural activity: the cultivation and breeding of deer or muntjac for breeding stock, meat, hides, and other resulting products. Its scope is not a general wildlife business, a tourism concept, or a broad livestock category. The record points to a productive breeding activity, where the commercial substance is the raising and propagation of rusa or kijang and the outputs that come from that husbandry.

That makes the registration logic relatively clean. The activity is open across the full business-scale spectrum recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, this is not reserved only for a small local operator, nor only for a large agricultural investor. The same activity can sit at different operating scales, and the record explicitly recognises all four. A founder reading this code should understand it as a scale-flexible breeding and cultivation activity, not as a narrowly carved exception.

At the national level, the stance on foreign investment is just as unambiguous. TERBUKA is the PMA status, with the record setting the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%. There is no partial cap to soften or explain away: on the national reading supplied here, foreign ownership can reach the full ceiling stated in the record. The source given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and nothing in the slim record adds a separate threshold, minimum capital rule, licence condition, or timing requirement. The honest national picture is therefore that KBLI 01494 is foreign-open up to 100%, subject only to what is actually stated here.

The Bali reading is where many KBLI pages need caution, but this one does not turn into a block. The record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and that l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is specific: OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. That moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali on a permanent island-wide basis, but the supplied Bali assessment for this activity does not place it inside that blocked bucket. So the practical editorial conclusion is measured but clear: KBLI 01494 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali moratorium record supplied here does not block PMA registration for it.

editorial.headline: Rabbit Breeding and Farming with a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01495 covers rabbit cultivation and breeding for meat, skins, and other outputs, open nationally to all business scales and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01495 is a compact but specific agricultural activity: the cultivation and breeding of rabbits to produce meat, skins, and other outputs. Its Indonesian scope is direct and practical, centred on both pembibitan kelinci and budidaya kelinci, so the code belongs to operators whose business activity is not merely trading rabbits or processing downstream products, but raising and breeding the animals themselves. The commercial substance is animal husbandry: maintaining rabbit stock, developing breeding activity, and producing the outputs named in the record.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, which means the same KBLI can describe a small rabbit-breeding operation, a mid-sized cultivation business, or a larger agricultural enterprise. That breadth matters because the activity is not confined to a single class of operator. A founder reading this code should see a production activity with room for different operating sizes, provided the registered business is genuinely within rabbit cultivation and breeding as described by the scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with foreign ownership up to 100% under the cited Perpres source. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, so the national reading is straightforward rather than conditional. For a foreign-owned company, the central point is that the activity itself is open at the national level, and the record gives a full foreign-ownership ceiling rather than a minority or joint-venture limit.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. The record does include Bali's island-wide moratorium rule, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. Here, however, the Bali status is not blocked: the record states that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not blocked by the moratorium. In plain English, KBLI 01495 is not one of the Bali-blocked PMA activities in this record. The honest reading is therefore aligned: nationally open, fully foreign-open, open across Mikro through Besar scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated Bali note.

editorial.headline: Worm Cultivation With a Clear Bali PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers worm cultivation and breeding for seed stock, meat, and other outputs, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
Worm cultivation and breeding sits in a plain but important corner of the primary-production economy. The scope is not ornamental or advisory: it is the activity of cultivating and breeding worms to produce seed stock, meat, and other outputs. In practical terms, the code is about the controlled raising and propagation of worms as a productive activity, not a vague environmental service or a downstream trading label.

The record opens this activity across the full business-size spectrum: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved in the slim record for only one end of the market. A small operator can read it as an activity category for a modest cultivation setup, while a larger operator can also see a pathway within the same code, provided the registered activity is still the cultivation and breeding described in the scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean. The activity carries TERBUKA status, and its foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no foreign-share cap to qualify or dilute in the record; the ceiling is complete foreign ownership. The source field points to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, but the practical reading for founders is simpler: on the national investment list, this activity is open to PMA at the stated ceiling.

The Bali picture is also unusually direct. The record does not block this code for PMA registration in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by the province’s moratorium. That moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, island-wide and permanently, but this record says the activity is not blocked on that basis. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as caution: for this slim record, a foreign-owned setup can treat the code as nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium.

editorial.headline: Swiftlet Breeding Is Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01497 covers the cultivation and breeding of swiftlets for birds and nests, open across all scales with full foreign ownership and no Bali PMA block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01497 is a narrow but commercially distinctive agricultural activity: the cultivation and breeding of swiftlets, including the supporting activity needed to produce swiftlet birds and swiftlet nests. The center of gravity is production at the farm or breeding-house level. It is about raising and propagating the birds and generating nests as an output of that cultivation process, not about turning those nests into a processed product. Washing, processing, or finishing the nest sits outside the activity described in this record.

That distinction matters because the code is not written as a general edible-nest business. It is written around the upstream biological activity: maintaining the conditions, stock, and breeding cycle that produce birds and nests. A founder using this code should therefore be describing an operation whose primary registered activity is swiftlet cultivation and breeding. The scale field is broad: the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, the record does not reserve the activity for only small local operators or only large commercial players; it allows the full ladder of enterprise scale stated in the record.

Nationally, the foreign investment signal is clean. TERBUKA is the PMA status, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The source field points to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, but the practical editorial reading is simpler: for this activity, the national investment field is open, and the maximum foreign stake shown in the record is complete ownership. There is no basis in the slim record to add a minimum capital figure, a special licence, a tax treatment, or a registration timeline.

The Bali picture is also not a hidden prohibition. The province-wide moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record marks KBLI 01497 as not blocked in Bali. The reason given is specific: at Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the moratorium does not block it. That does not turn the code into a casual, low-risk footnote; it means the Bali field should be read with precision. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest answer is that this swiftlet cultivation and breeding activity is nationally open, carries a 100% foreign ownership ceiling, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium status recorded here.

editorial.headline: Wildlife Breeding, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali With Care
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01498 covers conservation-oriented captive breeding of wild animals, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01498 is a conservation-centred activity code for the captive breeding, rearing and propagation of wildlife. Its scope covers mammals, reptiles other than crocodiles and alligators, birds, insects and other wild animal types, with the purpose framed around preservation rather than ordinary livestock production. The record also refers to breeding of wild plant and animal species, but the core title is clear: this is the business classification for wildlife captivity and propagation.

The code is available across the full business-size spectrum recorded in OSS: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the activity is not presented as a narrow large-company category only; it can sit at every registered scale listed in the record. At the same time, the substance of the activity is specialised. A founder using this code is not simply registering a general animal business. The registered activity is tied to the controlled breeding or raising of wild species for conservation purposes, so the wording should be treated with discipline when describing the company’s actual operations.

Nationally, the investment position is unusually clean. The slim record marks PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. In plain English, the activity is open to foreign investment at the national level, and the record does not impose a reduced foreign-share cap. A foreign-owned company can therefore read the national PMA position as fully open, based on the fields provided here.

The Bali picture is also workable, but it should be stated precisely. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration across the province, permanently, under the listed governor-letter source. This code is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the recorded reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is not that Bali adds no friction; it is that the Bali moratorium, as captured in this record, does not close the door to PMA registration for this activity today.

editorial.headline: Other Animal Breeding With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01499 covers the breeding and cultivation of animals such as guinea pigs, dogs, cats, worms, and crickets, with PMA access open nationally and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01499 is for the cultivation and breeding of other animals: a deliberately practical category for activities that do not sit inside the more familiar livestock boxes. The slim record names guinea pigs, dogs, cats, worms, and crickets as examples, and it frames the business purpose broadly: producing breeding stock, meat, skins, and other outputs. In plain English, this is an animal-rearing and breeding activity where the commercial product may be the animal itself, its offspring, or material derived from the animal.

The code is open across the full business-size spectrum. A founder can read the scale field cleanly: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as eligible scales. That matters because this is not only a backyard or smallholder classification; the record also accommodates larger operators. The scope is still bounded by the activity itself: breeding and cultivating the listed kinds of animals, or comparable “other animals,” for the outputs stated in the record.

At the national level, the position on foreign investment is unambiguous. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the editorial reading is not “open but limited”; it is nationally open to full foreign ownership as recorded. That does not create any extra licence, tax, capital, or timeline rule here. It only states the investment-access position provided by the record.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this record is not blocked for Bali. Its L4 Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms: a foreign investor looking at this activity is not facing a Bali PMA registration block under the moratorium described in the record.

editorial.headline: Land Preparation Services That Stay Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01611 covers fee-based or contract land preparation for farms and plantations, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01611 is for the practical work that happens before planting: preparing agricultural land on a fee or contract basis. Its scope is not the cultivation itself, nor the sale of crops, but the service of getting land ready for planting. The record covers both rice-field land and non-rice-field land, including dry land, and it applies to preparation work for food-crop agriculture as well as plantation agriculture. In plain English, this is the code for a business hired to process, work, or prepare agricultural plots so another planting activity can begin.

The scale position is broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the code is not framed in the record as a narrow category reserved for only one size of business. A small local operator preparing fields under contract and a larger structured service provider can both sit within the same activity description, provided the actual business remains inside the recorded scope: land preparation for agricultural planting, performed for a fee or under contract.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. At the national level, PMA status remains TERBUKA, with recorded maximum foreign ownership at 100%. That is the central investment fact: the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. For a foreign-owned setup, the relevant reading is therefore straightforward at national level: this activity is open, and the foreign ownership ceiling is full according to the record’s stated PMA source.

Bali does not change that answer into a prohibition. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and explains that, at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest Bali picture is therefore not a hidden closure: KBLI 01611 is nationally open to PMA and, on the record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali. The precision matters because the Bali rule is real, but here it does not close the door.

editorial.headline: Fertilisation Services With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01612 covers contract-based farm fertilisation and related field services, open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01612 is a practical field-service classification: fertilising agricultural land on a fee or contract basis. Its scope is not limited to applying fertiliser. The record also places seed or seedling planting, pest and disease control, and weed control inside the same activity when those services are performed for food crops, horticulture, or plantation crops under a service arrangement. In plain English, this is the code for an operator paid to carry out hands-on agricultural support work on someone’s land, rather than a code defined by the sale of an input or the ownership of the harvest.

That distinction matters because the code is built around service delivery. A business under this activity is registering the operational work of improving and protecting agricultural land and crops: fertilising, planting, and controlling pests, diseases, and plant competitors. The common thread is contract performance. The slim record does not create separate sub-rules for crop type beyond naming food crops, horticulture, and plantations, so the editorial reading should stay broad but disciplined: this is an agricultural support service for cultivated land, not a platform for inventing downstream trading, processing, or licensing consequences.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar business scales. That means the classification is not framed only for a large operator; it can also describe smaller service providers, provided the registered activity remains within the scope above. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. In founder terms, the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, so there is no partial foreign-share cap to explain here. The cited source for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is better than the cautionary pattern that often surrounds local PMA registration. The Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently. But this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that the OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: for KBLI 01612, a foreign investor is looking at a nationally open activity with a 100% ceiling, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: For KBLI 01612, the honest conclusion is clean: it is nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Harvesting as a Contracted Agricultural Service
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01613 is for businesses paid or contracted to harvest crops and collect the crop yield at agreed locations, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01613 covers a practical but commercially important slice of agriculture: crop harvesting carried out for a fee or under contract. The activity is not the farming of the crop itself, and it is not framed as trading the harvest. Its centre of gravity is the service work at the point of harvest: taking crops from the field or agreed site, gathering the resulting yield, and doing so because another party has engaged the business to perform that work.

That makes the code relevant for operators whose business model is built around harvest execution rather than land ownership or crop production. A company under this activity may be paid on a service basis, or contracted around an agreed harvesting job and collection point. The scope is narrow enough to be clear: it is about harvesting plants and collecting the harvested output at the location agreed with the client. It does not need decorative language, because the commercial substance is already there: a specialised agricultural service delivered where the harvest happens.

The scale picture is broad. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it is not confined to one size of Indonesian enterprise. A small local operator can sit naturally inside the same activity definition as a larger service provider, provided the registered business is genuinely performing harvesting and harvest collection for compensation or under contract. For founders, that scale range matters because it describes the legal room in which the activity can be registered; it does not, by itself, add permits, capital thresholds, or operating promises that are not in the record.

The foreign-investment picture is also unusually clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the listed foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling. Bali does not reverse that conclusion in the record: the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is precise: at Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the Bali moratorium does not block it. That moratorium is still important context because Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently. But for this activity, the recorded outcome is not a Bali block. The honest reading is therefore direct: a foreign investor can treat KBLI 01613 as nationally open, with no Bali PMA moratorium block recorded for this code.

editorial.body:
Aerial spraying and pollination is a narrow, operationally specific activity. The record describes work carried out through the air, using special aircraft, when particular conditions require it. In plain English, this is not general agriculture, not general aviation, and not a broad land-service category. Its centre of gravity is the act itself: spraying or pollinating from the air by aircraft built or assigned for that kind of task.

That precision matters for founders because the activity is defined by method as much as by sector. The work is not simply “support for farming”; it is support delivered through aerial application. A business registering this activity is therefore presenting itself around specialised aircraft-based field service: the aircraft, the aerial route, and the condition-specific nature of the work are all part of the scope. The Indonesian title makes the same point compactly: jasa penyemprotan dan penyerbukan melalui udara.

The national investment picture is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling in the record is 100%. That means the national entry position is fully open to foreign ownership under the cited source, rather than open only to a capped minority stake. It is also open across the listed enterprise scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. The scale range is unusually broad in practical terms, but the record does not turn that into a licence rule, capital rule, or timing rule; it simply says the activity is available at those scales.

Bali is also usable on the record supplied. The province’s moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration island-wide, permanently, but this activity is not blocked by that rule. The Bali reason is explicit: at Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it falls outside the moratorium block. That creates an honest reading: a foreign-owned company can treat this activity as nationally open and not Bali-blocked today, while recognising that the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a low-risk pass.

editorial.body:
This activity is about agricultural field services performed for a fee or under contract, with a clear emphasis on protecting crops from the things that reduce yield and quality. The Indonesian scope covers pest control, plant disease control, and weed control on cultivated land. It also reaches supporting work that sits close to that protection function: fertilising agricultural land and planting seedlings or seeds. In plain English, this is not the ownership of a farm or plantation as such; it is the service business that comes onto agricultural land to help establish, maintain, and defend crops.

The scope is broad across the kinds of crops it can serve. It expressly includes food crops, horticulture, and plantation crops, so the commercial setting can range from routine field maintenance to more specialised crop-protection work. The constant is the basis of the work: it is carried out for compensation or by contract. That matters because the activity is defined by the service relationship. A business under this code is selling agricultural support and plant-protection capability, not merely managing its own internal planting activity.

Registration is open across the full scale ladder recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That gives the activity an unusually wide formal span, from small local service operators to larger agricultural contractors. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no partial cap in the supplied record, so the national reading is straightforward: a foreign-owned company can use this activity code at full foreign ownership, provided the registration stays within the activity actually described.

The Bali position is equally important, because Bali applies a province-wide PMA moratorium to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This record, however, is not blocked for Bali PMA registration. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as optimism: for this specific activity, the national regime is open, the foreign ceiling is 100%, and the Bali moratorium does not block PMA registration on the record provided.

editorial.headline: Seed-Planting Services for Contracted Agricultural Work
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01616 covers paid or contract-based seed planting, fertilising, and crop-protection work across agriculture, horticulture, and plantations.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01616 is a practical service category for agricultural work performed for a fee or under contract. Its core is seed or seedling planting for agricultural commodities, but the scope is broader than planting alone: it also includes fertilising farmland and controlling pests, plant diseases, and weeds. The activity sits on the service side of farming rather than the ownership of the crop itself. A business under this code is being engaged to carry out field operations for another party, whether the crop is food agriculture, horticulture, or plantation-based.

That distinction matters because the code describes a hired agricultural operator: someone providing the labour, know-how, and field service required to prepare and maintain cultivation. The Indonesian scope points to work done “atas dasar balas jasa atau kontrak”, which is the centre of gravity here. It is not framed as trading produce, processing harvests, or owning a plantation business. It is the contracted service layer around planting and crop maintenance.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code can describe a small local operator as well as a larger service company. Foreign investment is also nationally open: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading, that means a foreign-owned company may register this activity without a foreign-share cap in the record.

The Bali reading is more precise, and it is not a hidden block. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this record marks KBLI 01616 as not blocked because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than moratorium-blocked. For a founder, the honest conclusion is clean: nationally this activity is open to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali the record does not mark it as blocked by the PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: This code is best understood as the contracted service layer around planting and crop maintenance, not the ownership of the crop itself.

editorial.headline: KBLI 01619: The Operating Layer Behind Farm Support
editorial.standfirst: A foreign-owned company may register this broad agricultural support activity nationally and in Bali, across all business scales, when the operator-led service model fits the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01619 is a practical code for the working layer around agriculture: services that help farming activity happen, but are not the farming activity itself. The record frames it as other agricultural support services, especially irrigation or watering arrangements, the provision of agricultural equipment together with its operator, and the maintenance or care of agricultural equipment when performed for a fee or under contract. In plain English, this is not a passive ownership code for land or a vague rural-services label. It is about operational support supplied to agricultural users, where the service, the equipment, the operator, and the contractual basis matter.

That makes the code naturally relevant to businesses built around farm-service delivery rather than crop production. A company might sit between agricultural clients and the machinery, people, and maintenance needed to keep field operations moving. The slim record is also careful about the shape of the service: it points to equipment supplied with an operator and to maintenance and care of agricultural tools on a fee or contract basis. That distinction keeps the activity anchored in support work, not in bare equipment rental or in an invented advisory, financing, or trading business that the record does not describe.

On scale, the record is unusually clear. KBLI 01619 is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not reserved only for large operators, nor is it limited to small local service providers. A micro business, a small or medium operator, and a larger service company can all fit the scale field if the registered activity matches the scope. For foreign investment, the national position is also clean: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership figure is 100%. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the supplied record, so the correct reading is that a foreign-owned setup can be nationally open at the full stated ceiling.

The Bali picture is honest but not negative. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record marks KBLI 01619 as not blocked. The reason given is specific: at Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The Bali status is therefore not a soft warning that the code is unavailable; it is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For a foreign investor, the important conclusion is straightforward: nationally, this activity is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali it is not blocked under the stated moratorium logic. The discipline is to keep the registration tied to the actual support services described here, rather than stretching the code into activities the record never gives it.

editorial.headline: Livestock Breeding Services With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01621 covers contracted livestock mating work, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01621 is a technical services classification for livestock reproduction work performed for a fee or under contract. Its scope is not the ownership of the animals, nor a broad livestock-trading activity; it is the service layer around breeding. The record names artificial insemination, embryo transfer, pregnancy examination, and bull master activity as examples of what sits inside the code. In plain English, this is the professional handling of livestock mating and reproductive support when another party pays for that work as a service.

That service character matters because it defines who would normally use the classification. A business registering under this code is positioning itself as a provider of livestock breeding services rather than as a general farm, dealer, or feed operation. The code is open across the full scale range in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes the classification structurally available from small local service operators through to larger organized providers, provided the registered activity remains within the scope described in the record.

The national foreign-investment position is unambiguous. With its TERBUKA PMA status, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the national reading is that a foreign investor may hold the full interest in a PMA company using this activity code. The legal source given for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special licence threshold, capital threshold, timeline, tax treatment, or extra permit condition, so the editorial reading should stay narrow: nationally, this is open, including to full foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province on a permanent island-wide basis. For this code, however, the Bali field says it is not blocked: the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by that moratorium. The result is an unusually clean conclusion for a foreign-owned setup in Bali: this activity is nationally open and, on the record provided, not blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium today.

editorial.headline: Egg Hatching as a Contract Service
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01622 covers paid or contract-based egg hatching, open across all business scales and fully foreign-open nationally, with Bali not blocking PMA registration under the stated moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01622 is narrow by design. It covers **jasa penetasan telur**: egg hatching carried out on a fee basis or under contract. The important word is service. The record does not describe a broad livestock business, a trading line, or a full farming operation; it describes the activity of hatching eggs for payment or by agreement with another party. That makes the classification useful for operators whose commercial centre is the hatching process itself, not a wider chain of activities that the record does not name.

The scale position is unusually clean. The slim record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** businesses, so the classification is not reserved for only small operators or only larger enterprises. A founder reading the code should understand it as available across the registered scale spectrum listed in the record. That does not create any extra entitlement beyond the record, and it does not say anything about technical approvals, locations, facilities, or operating procedures. It simply tells us that the activity can be registered at every listed scale.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is also direct. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with **pma_max_asing** set at 100. In plain English, the record treats this KBLI as fully open to foreign ownership at the national level, with the ceiling rendered as **100%**. The cited source for that position is **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. There is no capped foreign stake to explain here: the record does not impose a 67%, 49%, or minority ceiling. For a foreign-owned setup, the national reading is therefore straightforward: this activity is open, and the ownership ceiling reaches 100%.

The Bali reading is where many founders expect a hidden trap, but this record does not mark one. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks **all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA**, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. For this activity, however, **l4_bali_blocked** is false and the Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. The stated reason is precise: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium**. The honest conclusion is not that Bali is automatically difficult, nor that a foreigner is blocked. On the record given, KBLI 01622 is nationally open to PMA and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium rule stated here.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Infrastructure Behind Animal Care
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01629 covers contracted support work around livestock and animal care, nationally open to PMA and not blocked for Bali registration under the stated moratorium check.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01629 is not the farm itself, but the practical support layer around animal husbandry. Its scope covers livestock-support services carried out for a fee or under contract: shearing, attaching or giving livestock identity, cleaning animal enclosures, grass-finding services, animal maintenance and care, and herding. It also includes farrier work and animal castration. In plain English, this is the operational labour and specialist handling that keeps livestock-related activity functioning without necessarily being the primary owner of the animals or the farm.

That makes the code relevant for businesses built around service provision rather than production. A company registering under this activity would be positioning itself as a contracted provider of animal-support work: cleaning, care, grooming or handling services, field assistance, or technical tasks such as shoeing horses. The slim record states that the activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the registered form is not limited in the record to one narrow business size. The key is that the commercial activity remains service-based and traceable to the listed forms of support.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is clear-cut. Its PMA status is TERBUKA, while the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling, with the cited basis being Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the slim record, so none should be invented. For a foreign-owned setup, the national reading is therefore clean: this is an open activity at the recorded ceiling, across the listed scales.

The Bali picture is also clear, and importantly it does not overturn the national position in this record. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is marked l4_bali_blocked: false. The reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms, KBLI 01629 should be read as nationally foreign-open and, on the slim record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali. The honest conclusion is not a warning disguised as analysis: this activity is open, including in Bali under the stated moratorium check.

editorial.headline: Post-Harvest Services With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: A contract-based activity for preparing agricultural outputs for primary markets, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01630 covers the practical work that happens after cultivation but before agricultural goods enter the primary market. Its centre of gravity is service: post-harvest activity carried out for a fee or under contract, rather than the farmer’s own preparation of the crop. In plain English, this is the business of making agricultural outputs sale-ready without turning them into a different industrial product. The record names cleaning, sorting, grading, peeling, sun drying, and disinfection as core examples, alongside more specific work such as separating cotton seed, preparing tobacco leaves by sun drying, peeling cocoa beans, waxing fruit, and naturally drying fruit, vegetables, spices, and medicinal herbs.

The scope is broader than a single commodity line. It can include sorting, cleaning, and cutting medicinal herbs; retting textile fibre plants such as jute, flax, or coir where that work is not part of the cultivation activity itself; and artificial ripening of fruit as a service, with banana ripening given as the example. That range matters because the classification is not defined by one product, but by the role the operator performs in the agricultural chain: a post-harvest contractor preparing goods for sale at the primary-market stage. The boundary is also clear from the record. It is not ordinary preparation done by the farmer, not seed-quality improvement, not commission or cooperative marketing, not wholesale trade, not oil production from grains, and not research into new seed forms.

For registration scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification can describe anything from a small contracted sorting operation to a larger service facility handling multiple agricultural outputs, as long as the work remains within the post-harvest service scope set out above. Nationally, the foreign-investment status is also clear: it is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the national reading is not a restricted-foreign-stake reading; it is a fully open PMA reading at the level stated in the record.

The Bali picture is equally important, because many otherwise open activities fail at the provincial gate. Here, however, the record does not show a Bali block. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record is severe: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently. But this activity, on the record supplied, does not fall into the blocked side of that rule. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: nationally it is open to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali it is not blocked by the stated PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Seed Selection for Propagation, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers post-harvest seed processing for stronger propagation, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block shown in the record.
editorial.body:
Seed selection for propagation is the quiet industrial layer between harvested seed and market-ready planting material. Its scope is not farming itself, and not research into new seed forms; it is the post-harvest handling that improves seed quality before the seed is sold. The work includes removing non-seed material, taking out seed that is too small, mechanically damaged, insect-damaged, or immature, and reducing moisture so the seed can be stored safely.

In practice, this is the discipline of making a seed lot more reliable. Drying, cleaning, grading, sorting, and related preparation sit at the centre of the activity, continuing up to the point where seed reaches the market. The record also places maintenance of modified seed inside this activity. That gives the code a practical breadth: it can serve operators whose value is not in planting crops, but in preparing propagation material so it is cleaner, better sorted, more stable in storage, and more suitable for commercial circulation.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not framed as a single-size business lane. A small seed-handling operation and a larger processing setup both sit within the recorded scale range, provided the actual activity remains within the defined seed-selection and processing scope. For founders, that matters because the code describes a specific technical function rather than a broad agricultural trade identity.

The national-vs-Bali reading is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, so the record indicates full foreign openness at the national level. Bali does have a province-wide moratorium rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record does not mark the activity as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as caution: for this activity, the record shows a nationally open PMA lane and no Bali PMA moratorium block today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Hunting and Wild Capture, Open Nationally and Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01700 covers commercial hunting, trapping, and related capture work, with full foreign ownership nationally and a high-risk Bali status that still survives the PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01700 is a narrow but serious activity: commercial hunting, trapping, and the capture of wild animals, whether dead or alive, for defined practical purposes. The scope includes capture for food, fur or skin, population control, research use, zoo placement, or keeping as pets. It also covers the production of fur skins, reptile skins, bird skins, mammal horns, reptile organs, and other animal organs when those products come from hunting or capture activity itself. The record is explicit enough to make this more than a generic wildlife label: it reaches frogs and toads taken from the wild, wild snail collection, land-based capture of marine mammals such as dugongs, sea lions, and seals, and protective hunting of foxes, weasels, and wolves where livestock protection is the purpose.

That breadth should not be mistaken for unlimited scope. This activity is built around wild capture and hunting, not farm production, slaughterhouse by-products, agricultural pest services, whale catching, sport or recreational hunting, or organizational support for hunting and capture. In practical registration terms, the centre of gravity is commercial extraction or control from the wild, plus services closely tied to that activity. A founder using this classification should be able to explain the actual animal source, the commercial purpose, and whether the work is capture, trapping, population control, research supply, zoo supply, pet supply, or production of specified animal-derived materials from the hunting or capture process.

Nationally, the investment message is clear: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the national table does not impose a foreign share cap below full ownership for this activity. The record also states that the activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. So the classification is not only available to large operators; it is framed as scale-open across the listed business sizes, while still requiring the operator to stay inside the exact activity boundary described above.

The Bali position is more nuanced, but not negative. The Bali status is Open in Bali (high-risk track), and the record says this code is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali. The reason is specific: nationally it is TERBUKA, and the Besar scale is treated as Menengah Tinggi, so it survives Bali’s moratorium, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. The honest reading is therefore not that Bali is closed, but that this is a registrable PT PMA activity in Bali with a high-risk status. For a foreign founder, the decisive point is simple: KBLI 01700 is nationally open at 100% foreign ownership and, on this record, remains registrable in Bali today.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Planting, replanting, and conservation of forests. Critically, this code now includes Natural Carbon Sequestration and the sale of Carbon Credits.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: **Medium-High Risk**. For PT PMA, it requires a certified expert in Seed Management and specific infrastructure for seed protection.
intel_2026.baliContext: Focus on West Bali (Jembrana) and Central Highlands for carbon projects. Governor Koster’s sustainability drive makes this a strategic code for "Green PMA" structures. Coordination with the Dinas Kehutanan is mandatory.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct match from 2020, but with new 2025 protocols for carbon inventory recording.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into carbon sequestration or forest management in Bali? Let me guide you through the latest 2025 carbon credit regulations and licensing.

editorial.headline: Forest Management, Carbon Stewardship, and the Bali PMA Reality
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 02101 covers forest management, replanting, conservation, and natural carbon sequestration, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 02101 is a forestry activity code for the active management of forests and timber land. Its scope is not limited to keeping land untouched. The record describes planting, replanting, conservation of forests and wooded land, and the management of forest areas for natural carbon sequestration. It also includes the sale of carbon credits or emission-reduction certificates when those outputs arise from the forest-management activity itself. In practical terms, this is the code for operators whose business is the stewardship of forest assets, including natural, semi-natural, and plantation forests, where the environmental outcome is part of the managed activity.

The same scope draws an important boundary. This code does not cover third-party inventorying or recording of forest carbon sequestration. That exclusion matters because the commercial substance here is management, not merely measurement. The record also places within the scope the use of areas in protected forest and the use of environmental services in protected forest. So the center of gravity is land and forest management: planting, restoring, conserving, and turning recognised forest-management outcomes into carbon-credit or emission-reduction-certificate value where the underlying activity produces them.

For scale, the code is unusually broad. The slim record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity is not described only as a large-company domain; the classification itself recognises participation across the full registered scale ladder. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear: the status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no partial foreign-share cap in the record. A foreign-owned company reading the national line would therefore see this as open, not capped below full foreign ownership, subject only to the facts actually stated in the record.

The Bali position is the point that needs precision. The province-wide moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this record does not mark KBLI 02101 as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is therefore neither alarmist nor casual: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and in Bali this record does not show a moratorium block, because the relevant risk position sits above the Low and Medium-Low category that Bali blocks.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is neither alarmist nor casual: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and this record does not show a Bali moratorium block.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

persyaratan: Dokumen sertifikat sumber benih atau Dokumen surat penunjukan sebagai pengelola dari pemilik sumber benih atau perjanjian Kerjasama pengelolaan sumber benih bersertifikat

Memiliki sarana dan prasarana perbenihan berupa: a. Pengunduhan Benih, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan detail rincian spesifikasi alat pengun- . Penangab. nan dibuktika n dengan foto proses penanganan benih berikut penjelasa n metode (tata cara, alat dan bahan) C. Penyimpanan Benih, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan disain penyimpanan benih dalam kaitannya dengan perlindungan benih (seed protection)
Memiliki tenaga ahli atau tenaga terampil di Bidang Pengelolaan Benih, dengan dibuktikan sertifikat pelatihan dan/atau ijazah akademik
Memiliki Stok Benih Bersertifikat, yang dibuktikan dengan laporan stok benih bersertifikat
Bukti Bayar PNBP atau Retribusi Daerah atas : a. Sertifikasi Sumber benih atau b. Sertifikasi Mutu Benih dan/atau c. Pengunduhan atau pengumpulan anakan alam dari kawasan hutan
Dokumen sertifikat sumber benih atau Dokumen pengelola dari pemilik sumber benih atau perjanjian Kerjasama pengelolaan sumber benih bersertifikat
Dalam hal lokasi kegiatan (persemaian) berada dalam area kerja badan usaha milik negara bidang kehutanan, dilengkapi pertimbangan teknis dari badan usaha milik negara bidang kehutanan
Memiliki Sistem irigasi dan penyiraman, yang dibuktikan dengan foto berikut dengan disainnya

Memiliki sarana dan prasarana pembibitan/ persemaian berupa: a. Penyimpanan benih, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan disain penyimpanan benih dalam kaitannya dengan perlindungan benih (seed protection) b. Penaburan benih, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan metode penaburan (tata cara, alat dan bahan) c. Pertumbuhan stek, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan metode pertumbuhan stek (tata cara, alat dan bahan) d. Penyapihan, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan metode penyapihan (tata cara, alat dan bahan) e. Pembesaran bibit, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan metode pembesaran bibit (tata cara, alat dan bahan) dan f. Fasilitas pengangkut bibit, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan spesifikasi alat pengangku tan bibit
Memiliki tenaga ahli atau tenaga terampil di bidang pembibitan, dengan dibuktikan sertifikat pelatihan dan/atau ijazah akademik
Memiliki stok bibit yang bersertifikat, yang dibuktikan dengan laporan stok bibit bersertifikat
Terdapat aktivitas pembuatan bibit, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan laporan kegiatan produksi bibit

Bukti bayar PNBP atau Retribusi Daerah atas: a. Sertifikasi sumber benih atau b. Sertifikasi mutu benih atau c. Sertifikasi mutu bibit sumber benih atau pengelola dari pemilik perjanjian Kerjasama pengelolaan sumber benih bersertifikat

Lokasi kegiatan: a. Jika pelaku usaha adalah Perum Perhutani, dan lokasi berada di luar area hutani maka dilengkapi Pertimbangan Teknis dari Gubernur b. Jika adalah pelaku usaha lain, dan lokasi usaha berada di area kerja Perum Perhutani, maka dilengkapi Pertimbangan Teknis dari Perum Perhutani
Memiliki Sistem irigasi dan penyiraman, yang dibuktikan dengan foto berikut dengan disainnya

Memiliki sarana dan prasarana perbenihan dan pembibitan/ persemaian berupa: a. Pengunduhan benih, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan detail rincian spesifikasi alat pengunduhan b. Penanganan benih, yang dibuktikan dengan foto proses penanganan benih berikut penjelasan metode (tata cara, alat dan bahan) c. Penyimpanan benih yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan disain penyimpanan benih dalam kaitannya dengan perlindungan benih (seed protection) d. Penaburan benih yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan metode penaburan (tata cara, alat dan bahan) e. Pertumbuhan stek, yang dibuktikan dengan pembesaran bibit (tata cara, alat dan bahan) dan h. Fasilitas pengangkut bibit, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan spesifikasi alat pengangkutan bibit
Memiliki tenaga ahli atau tenaga terampil di bidang pengelolaan benih dan pembibitan, dengan dibuktikan sertifikat pelatihan dan/atau ijazah akademik
Memiliki stok benih dan bibit yang bersertifikat, yang dibuktikan dengan laporan stok benih dan bibit bersertifikat
Terdapat aktivitas pembuatan bibit, yang dibuktikan dengan foto dan laporan kegiatan produksi bibit
Bukti bayar PNBP atau Retribusi Daerah atas: a. Sertifikasi sumber benih atau b. Sertifikasi mutu benih atau c. Sertifikasi mutu bibit

Memiliki salah satu sertifikat standar terverifikasi dari jenis perizinan berusaha di bidang perbenihan tanaman hutan, yaitu: a. Pengadaan dan pengedaran benih atau b. Pengadaan dan pengedaran bibit atau c. Pengadaan dan pengedaran benih dan bibit disesuaikan dengan komoditi (benih dan/atau bibit) yang akan dimasukkan dari luar negeri

Memiliki dokumen Surat Persyaratan Karantina Tumbuhan dari Badan Karantina Indonesia dan Dokumen Surat Hasil Analisa Resiko Jenis Tumbuhan Asing Invasif pre border dari Badan Riset dan Inovasi Nasional (BRIN)
Surat pernyataan dari produsen benih dan/atau bibit tanaman hutan negara asal yang menerangkan bahwa benih dan/atau bibit tanaman hutan yang dimasukkan ke Indonesia bukan Produk Rekayasa Genetik
Surat Keterangan tentang asalusul (certificate of origin), dokumen kualitas (certificate of quality) dari instansi yang berwenang di negara asal

Apabila benih dan/atau bibit yang dimasukkan ke dalam wilayah NKRI bukan berasal dari negara asal benih dan/atau bibit, maka wajib memiliki Sertifikat Kesehatan Tumbuhan (certificate of phytosanitary) dari NPPO (National Plant Protection Organisation) Negara asal dari benih dan/atau bibit serta Sertifikat Kesehatan Tumbuhan (certificate of phytosanitary) untuk Reekspor (certificate of phytosanitary for re-export) dari NPPO negara yang melakukan kegiatan pemasukan benih dan/atau bibit ke wilayah NKRI

Bukti bayar PNBP atas Perizinan Berusaha Pemasukan benih dan/atau bibit tanaman hutan dari luar negeri setelah mendapatkan kepastian persetujuan dari Menteri namun sebelum Sertifikat Standar diterbitkan oleh Sistem OSS
Bukti bayar PNBP atau Retribusi Daerah atas pengujian mutu benih dan/atau bibit untuk pelaku usaha yang menjual kembali benih dan/atau bibit secara langsung

Memiliki salah satu sertifikat standar terverifikasi dari jenis perizinan berusaha di bidang perbenihan tanaman hutan, yaitu: a. Pengadaan dan pengedaran benih atau b. Pengadaan dan pengedaran bibit atau c. Pengadaan dan pengedaran benih dan bibit disesuaikan dengan komoditi (benih dan/atau bibit) yang akan dikeluarkan ke luar negeri
Surat Keterangan tentang asalusul (certificate of origin), dokumen kualitas (certificate of quality) dari instansi berwenang

Bukti bayar PNBP atas Perizinan Berusaha Pengeluaran benih dan/atau bibit tanaman hutan ke luar negeri setelah mendapatkan kepastian persetujuan dari Menteri namun sebelum Sertifikat Standar diterbitkan oleh Sistem OSS
kewajiban: Melakukan sertifikasi mutu benih bagi benih yang akan diedarkan

Membuat laporan kegiatan usaha setiap 6 (enam) bulan sekali

Membuat laporan kegiatan usaha setiap 6 (enam) bulan sekali

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pengelolaan kayu di dalam hutan, mulai dari penanaman sampai penebangan dengan hasil produksi berupa kayu bulat. Kegiatan ini dapat dilakukan di dalam hutan alam, hutan semialami, maupun hutan tanaman.

per_skala.scope_uraian: Pemanfaatan hasil hutan kayu hutan tanaman di hutan produksi
persyaratan: Persetujuan Komitmen PBPH
Berita Acara Koordinat Geografis
Bukti pelunasan iuran PBPH
kewajiban: Menyusun dokumen rencana kerja usaha pemanfaatan hutan untuk 10 (sepuluh) tahun dengan memperhatikan rencana pengelolaan hutan jangka panjang KPH paling lambat 1 tahun setelah perizinan berusaha diberikan
Menyusun Rencana Kerja Tahunan (RKT) berdasarkan RKUPH sejak sejak RKU disahkan
Melaksanakan kegiatan nyata di lapangan paling lambat 1 tahun setelah perizinan berusaha diterbitkan
Melaksanakan penataan batas areal kerja 2 (dua) tahun sejak diberikan
Melaksanakan perlindungan hutan di areal kerjanya
Melakukan upaya pencegahan kebakaran hutan di areal kerjanya
Bertanggungjawab atas terjadinya kebakaran hutan di areal kerjanya
Melakukan pemulihan lingkungan terhadap kerusakan lingkungan di areal kerjanya
Melaksanakan penanaman paling sedikit 50% dari target yang telah ditentukan
Merealisasikan produksi paling sedikit 50% dari target yang direncanakan
Menatausahakan keuangan kegiatan usahanya
Mempekerjakan tenaga profesional bidang kehutanan dan tenaga lain yang memenuhi persyaratan sesuai kebutuhan
Membayar PNBP sesuai peraturan perundang undangan
Melaksanakan pemanfaatan hasil hutan dengan sistem silvikultur sesuai dengan kondisi setempat
Melaksanakan pemanenan hasil hutan kayu dengan menerapkan teknik pembalakan berdampak rendah/ Reduce Impact Logging (RIL)
Melakukan penatausahaan hasil hutan
Melakukan pengukuran atau pengujian hasil hutan sesuai ketentuan
Menyampaikan laporan kinerja secara periodik kepada Menteri LHK
Melaksanakan kewajiban lainnya sesuai ketentuan

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers managing timber inside forests end-to-end — from planting through felling — with round logs (kayu bulat) as the output. It applies in natural, semi-natural and plantation forests.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: **High Risk** under OSS — expect full licensing rather than automatic issuance. 100% open to foreign ownership (verified against Perpres 10/2021: the code sits outside all three lampiran, open by default), with a partnership condition (kemitraan) with local communities attached.
intel_2026.baliContext: Commercial timber harvesting is a minor activity on Bali itself — Indonesia's production forests are concentrated in Kalimantan, Sumatra and Papua. Bali-based investors typically structure forestry operations in those provinces, with the local-community partnership condition (kemitraan) shaping the operating design.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Renumbered and consolidated in KBLI 2025 — this code merges the KBLI 2020 timber-utilization codes 02111, 02112, 02113, 02119, 02121 and 02122.

editorial.headline: Forest Timber: Open to PMA, Conditional in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 02102 covers timber management in forests; it is 100% foreign-open nationally, while Bali attaches a local-community partnership condition.
editorial.body:
## Forest Timber, Managed at Its Source

KBLI 02102 covers timber management within forests, from planting through felling, with roundwood as the production output. Its stated scope includes timber forest products from plantation forests and natural forests in production forests. The activity may take place in natural, semi-natural, or planted forests. The defining thread is management of the timber within the forest itself, through the stages the record names. Planting and felling are the named ends of that continuum, rather than side notes to it. The scope describes timber as a forest product managed through those stages and produced as roundwood. It identifies natural forests, semi-natural forests, and plantation forests, and specifically includes timber forest products from both plantation and natural forests in production forests.

The record opens this activity to every listed business scale: micro, small, medium, and large. That breadth does not alter the classification’s subject matter. At each of those scales, the activity remains forest-based timber management with roundwood as its output, across the forest settings set out in the scope. The scale field answers who may register it; the scope field answers what is being registered. The record lists each of these scales as open to the activity; it states no exclusion among them.

Nationally, the position is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, foreign investment may own 100% of this activity at the national level. Bali adds a condition rather than a closure. The Bali record marks the activity TERBATAS, but not blocked for PMA registration, and requires a partnership with local communities. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI; this record does not mark this activity as blocked.

The honest Bali reading is therefore exact. Forest timber management under this classification is not closed to PMA in Bali, but its 100% national opening sits alongside the stated local-community partnership condition. That condition belongs in the registration picture from the start. For founders, the classification is neither a generic timber label nor a Bali prohibition: it is a defined forest-management activity, open across the listed scales and subject in Bali to the condition the record expressly sets out.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, the national 100% opening sits alongside a local-community partnership condition.

l4_bali.reason: PMA 100% open (Perpres 10/2021 open-default — code outside all three lampiran; pma_cap_verified) with kemitraan-with-local-communities condition. Not closed — this 2025 code merges KBLI 2020 codes 02111, 02112, 02113, 02119, 02121 and 02122.
