Membayar IPERA

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

Bentuk Perizinan Izin Pertambangan Rakyat (IPR)

  1. Orang perseorangan:
    1. Surat permohonan;
    2. Nomor Induk Berusaha;
    3. Salinan kartu tanda penduduk;
    4. Surat keterangan dari kelurahan/desa setempat yang menyatakan pemohon merupakan penduduk setempat;
    5. Surat pernyataan untuk mematuhi ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang lingkungan hidup serta keselamatan pertambangan; dan
    6. Surat keterangan fiskal sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perpajakan.
  2. Koperasi:
    1. Surat permohonan;
    2. Nomor induk berusaha;
    3. Salinan kartu tanda penduduk pengurus koperasi;
    4. Surat keterangan dari kelurahan/desa setempat yang menyatakan seluruh pengurus koperasi merupakan penduduk setempat;
    5. Surat pernyataan kesanggupan pengelolaan lingkungan serta keselamatan pertambangan; dan
    6. Surat keterangan fiskal sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perpajakan.

  2. Lingkungan: Surat pernyataan kesanggupan untuk mematuhi ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perlindungan dan pengelolaan lingkungan hidup.
  3. Finansial:
    1. Bukti penempatan jaminan kesungguhan pelaksanaan kegiatan Eksplorasi;
    2. Bukti pembayaran biaya pencadangan wilayah dan pembayaran pencetakan peta WIUP Mineral bukan logam atau WIUP batuan atas permohonan wilayah; dan
    3. Surat keterangan fiskal sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perpajakan.

kewajiban:
Pemegang SIPB:

  1. Menyusun dokumen perencanaan Penambangan untuk mendapatkan persetujuan Menteri, yang terdiri:
    1. Dokumen teknis yang memuat:
      • Informasi cadangan; dan
      • Rencana Penambangan; dan
    2. Dokumen lingkungan hidup sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.
  2. Menerapkan kaidah Pertambangan yang baik;
  3. Menyelesaikan hak atas tanah dengan pemegang hak sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang- undangan;
  4. Menyampaikan laporan pelaksanaan kegiatan SIPB kepada Menteri; dan
  5. Membayar pendapatan negara atas komoditas yang ditambang.

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

Pemegang IUP:

  1. Menempatkan jaminan kesungguhan Eksplorasi;
  2. Membayar pendapatan negara dan pendapatan daerah, termasuk kewajiban iuran tetap dan iuran produksi;
  3. Menyusun dan menyerahkan rencana Reklamasi dan/atau rencana Pascatambang;
  4. Menyediakan dan menempatkan dana jaminan Reklamasi dan/atau dana jaminan Pascatambang;
  5. Melaksanakan Reklamasi dan Pascatambang;
  6. Menyusun dokumen lingkungan;
  7. Melaksanakan pengembangan dan pemberdayaan masyarakat di sekitar WIUP; 
  8. Menggunakan jalan Pertambangan;
  9. Melaksanakan penerapan kaidah teknik Pertambangan yang baik, yaitu:
    1. Ketentuan keselamatan Pertambangan;
    2. Pengelolaan dan pemantauan lingkungan Pertambangan, termasuk kegiatan Reklamasi dan/atau Pascatambang;
    3. Upaya konservasi Mineral dan Batubara;
    4. Pengelolaan sisa tambang dari suatu kegiatan Usaha Pertambangan dalam bentuk padat, cair, atau gas sampai memenuhi standar baku mutu lingkungan sebelum dilepas ke media lingkungan.
  10. Memenuhi ketentuan penetapan jumlah produksi dan penjualan nasional;
  11. Mengutamakan pemanfaatan tenaga kerja setempat, barang, dan jasa dalam negeri sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
  12. Melakukan divestasi saham bagi PMA sesuai ketentuan perundang-undangan;
  13. Pada tahap kegiatan Operasi Produksi wajib menyediakan dana ketahanan cadangan Mineral dan Batubara;
  14. menggunakan perusahaan Jasa Pertambangan lokal dan/atau nasional;
  15. Menyelesaikan hak atas tanah;

Dokumen Nomor Induk Berusaha (NIB)
Salinan Kartu Tanda Penduduk (KTP) untuk orang perseorangan atau salinan Kartu Tanda Penduduk (KTP) seluruh pengurus beserta susunan pengurus untuk koperasi

editorial.headline: Soil and Clay Extraction With a Clear Bali PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the extraction and basic processing of soil and clay, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is for the practical business of taking soil and clay out of the ground, then preparing those materials through forming, crushing, or grinding. Its scope is not a vague construction catch-all. It is anchored in excavation and in the first physical handling of soil and clay materials after extraction. The record names the output universe clearly: kaolin or china clay, ball clay or firing clay, abu bumi, shale, and fill soil. That makes the activity relevant to operators dealing in raw or prepared earth materials, rather than businesses further downstream in finished goods.

The registration window is broad. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the same classification can serve a small local operator as well as a larger excavation business. The record also notes Permohonan IPR Koperasi and Permohonan SIPB, which signals that the activity sits close to formal resource-use administration. Those items should be read exactly as stated: they appear in the activity scope, but the record does not give thresholds, timelines, issuing procedures, or documentary requirements. A founder should therefore treat them as part of the activity’s regulatory context, not as permission to infer a complete licensing checklist.

Seen from Jakarta's rulebook, foreign investment in this activity raises no flags. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership shown in the record is 100%. In plain English, the activity is open to foreign ownership at the national level, with no foreign-share cap shown in this slim record. The source given for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company assessing whether the activity can sit inside an Indonesian investment structure, that is the central national answer: the classification itself is not closed to PMA, and the record gives a full foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali is often where the nuance appears, but here the record does not show a moratorium block. The province’s rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. This activity, however, is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest Bali reading is therefore not “nationally open but locally blocked.” It is nationally open, and on this record it remains available for PMA registration in Bali, while still carrying the higher-risk administrative character indicated by the Bali status note.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali reading is therefore not “nationally open but locally blocked.”

  1. Mematuhi ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan dibidang lingkungan hidup serta keselamatan pertambangan. (untuk badan usaha Perseorangan), atau;

editorial.headline: Gypsum Extraction With Full Foreign Ownership Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers gypsum excavation and finishing work, open nationally to all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
Gypsum extraction is a narrow but economically serious mining activity: the record defines it as the excavation of gypsum, including the cleaning and smoothing work that prepares the material after it is taken from the ground. That scope matters because it keeps the activity anchored in mineral extraction, not trading, manufacturing, construction, or general materials supply. The Indonesian title is concise, but the operational picture is clear: this is about taking gypsum from its source and carrying out the immediate preparation work attached to that extraction.

The slim record also names two regulatory phrases inside the scope: *Permohonan IPR Koperasi* and *IUP Tahap Operasi Produksi Mineral Bukan Logam*. Those phrases should be read exactly as the record gives them: they sit within the official description of the activity and point to the mining-administration character of the code. They do not expand the scope beyond gypsum, and they should not be treated as a licence checklist here. For editorial purposes, the practical boundary is simple: if the proposed business is genuinely about gypsum excavation, with cleaning and smoothing as part of that extraction activity, this is the relevant activity described by the record.

On business scale, the code is unusually broad. The record says it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not reserved only for large industrial operators, nor limited only to small local activity. The same activity label can sit across the full scale spectrum stated in the record, from micro through large. For a founder, that makes the classification question less about whether the scale exists in the record and more about whether the planned activity is truly the extraction of gypsum and its immediate preparation, rather than an adjacent commercial activity that the record does not describe.

The national-vs-Bali picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In Bali, the record does not mark this activity as blocked: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently, but this activity is not recorded as falling into that blocked category. The honest reading is therefore neither evasive nor inflated: for this slim record, gypsum excavation is foreign-open nationally up to 100%, and it is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity

persyaratan: Surat Permohonan
Dokumen Nomor Induk Berusaha (NIB)
Salinan Kartu Tanda Penduduk (KTP) untuk orang perseorangan atau salinan Kartu Tanda Penduduk (KTP) seluruh pengurus beserta susunan pengurus untuk koperasi
Surat keterangan dari kelurahan/desa setempat yang menyatakan seluruh pengurus koperasi atau orang perseorangan pemohon beserta seluruh pekerjanya merupakan penduduk setempat

Surat pernyataan yang menyatakan:
  1. Mematuhi ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan dibidang lingkungan hidup serta keselamatan pertambangan. (untuk badan usaha Perseorangan), atau;
  2. Kesanggupan pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan (untuk badan usaha Koperasi)
Surat keterangan fiskal sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perpajakan
Titik koordinat IPR
Dokumen tambahan berupa persetujuan / rekomendasi dari Instansi yang berwenang dalam hal lokasi IPR berada wilayah sungai/kawasan hutan.
Luas Wilayah Pertambangan
Titik koordinat IPR
Dokumen tambahan berupa persetujuan / rekomendasi dari Instansi yang berwenang dalam hal lokasi IPR berada wilayah sungai/kawasan hutan.

Membayar IPERA

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

editorial.headline: Tras Quarrying With a Nationally Open PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08107 covers tras excavation and cleaning, with all business scales open and Bali not applying its PMA moratorium block on the record given.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08107 is about the excavation of *tras*: volcanic rock that has undergone chemical change through weathering and groundwater conditions. The slim record keeps the activity narrow. It is not a broad construction-material category, and it is not a catch-all for every quarrying operation. Its stated scope is the digging of this altered volcanic material, including the cleaning activities that belong to that extraction work.

The record also places the activity inside a rock-mining administrative frame by naming *IUP Tahap Eksplorasi Batuan* and *Peningkatan IUP Tahap Operasi Produksi Batuan*. In plain English, the activity sits where exploration-stage and upgraded production-operation stages for rock materials become relevant, but the record does not give timelines, procedures, fees, or technical thresholds. For founders, that distinction matters: the commercial description is simple, but the registration context is not a casual retail activity. It is an extractive activity tied to a defined mineral-material scope.

On business scale, the entry is unusually broad. The record says it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity is not presented here as reserved only for large operators, nor limited to a single enterprise size. A founder reading this should treat scale as part of the registration profile, not as an afterthought: the same code can appear across the full range of scales listed in the record. The foreign-investment picture is also clear at the national level. PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On this slim record, there is no partial cap to explain; the national ceiling is full foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is the decisive practical nuance. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, permanently. But this entry is marked as not blocked: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, with the reason stating that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. That does not turn the code into a frictionless approval story, and the record’s Bali status remains `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, not a promise of simplicity. But it does give a clean conclusion from the data supplied: nationally, KBLI 08107 is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked by the stated PMA moratorium rule.

  1. Mematuhi ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan dibidang lingkungan hidup serta keselamatan pertambangan. (untuk badan usaha Perseorangan), atau;

Dokumen tambahan berupa persetujuan / rekomendasi dari Instansi yang berwenang dalam hal lokasi IPR berada wilayah sungai/kawasan hutan.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Penggalian Batu Apung (08108)? This is classified as High risk with PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through the requirements.
intel_2026.baliContext: Quarrying in Bali is limited to sand, stone, and marble extraction, primarily in Karangasem and parts of Gianyar. Environmental permits (AMDAL/UKL-UPL) are strictly enforced due to Bali's protected landscape status.

editorial.headline: Pumice Quarrying, Open Nationally and Not Bali-Blocked
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08108 covers pumice excavation and cleaning, open across business scales with full foreign ownership nationally and no PMA moratorium block in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08108 is a mining-and-quarrying activity with a very specific material at its centre: batu apung, or pumice. The record defines it as a light-coloured rock containing froth formed from glass-walled bubbles, commonly understood as a volcanic silicate glass rock. In plain terms, this code is for the extraction of that material from the ground, and it also includes the cleaning work attached to the quarrying activity. It is not a general stone-trading code and it is not an all-purpose construction-material category; the scope is anchored to pumice excavation and its immediate cleaning process.

The record also places the activity in the language of rock mining administration. It names IUP Tahap Eksplorasi Batuan and Perpanjangan IUP Tahap Operasi Produksi Batuan in the slim scope, so the activity sits within the rock exploration and production-operation vocabulary used for this kind of quarrying. That matters editorially because the code is not merely describing a commercial product; it is describing an extractive activity whose regulatory identity is tied to the quarry itself. The available business scales are broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open to this code, which means the classification is not reserved only for large operators in the record.

Across Indonesia, the foreign-investment path is clear. With PMA status marked TERBUKA, foreign ownership may reach 100%. On the record provided, there is no partial foreign-stake cap to soften or explain away: this is nationally open to full foreign ownership, with the cited source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, the important point is precision. The opening is national, it applies to this activity as recorded, and the permitted foreign percentage is the full ceiling stated in the data.

Bali does not reverse that result on this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The moratorium rule itself is still severe: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this record says KBLI 08108 is not caught by that block. The honest reading is therefore clean: a foreign investor can treat this code as nationally open and, on the Bali moratorium field supplied here, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

editorial.headline: The open quarrying code Bali can still register
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08109 covers residual stone, sand, and clay extraction, with national foreign ownership open up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block at large scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08109 is the residual home for extraction businesses working with stone, sand, and clay that sit outside the more narrowly named extraction buckets. In practical terms, it reaches quarrying and digging for materials such as diorite, basalt, and breccia, as well as dredging sedimentary material from the sea. The scope is not limited to taking material from the ground or seabed: it also includes the immediate handling that makes the material commercially usable, such as breaking, crushing, separating, screening, and smoothing.

That makes this a production-facing activity rather than a purely trading or brokerage label. A founder using it should be describing an operation connected to physical extraction and first-stage processing of these materials. The slim record also ties the activity to exploration-stage mining business licences for certain non-metal minerals and for rocks. Those references matter because they signal the sectoral character of the code: this is an extractive activity with mineral and rock licensing context, not a general construction-supply category dressed up as one.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the code to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can serve anything from a very small domestic operation to a large-scale enterprise, provided the registered activity is genuinely within the extraction and processing scope. Nationally, it is also marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. Put plainly, the national investment list does not cap foreign ownership below full control for this activity.

The Bali reading is the important point. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, permanently, but this record is not blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali is closed to this foreign-owned quarrying activity today. On this slim record, a PMA can register it in Bali, while still needing to treat the activity as a higher-risk extractive operation rather than a light administrative registration.

editorial.headline: Sulphur Mining Sits Open Nationally and Passes Bali’s PMA Filter
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08911 covers sulphur ore mining, crushing, and cleaning, with full foreign ownership available across every business scale listed in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08911 is a mining activity, not a trading label or a downstream chemical business. Its Indonesian scope is tightly drawn around **pertambangan bijih belerang**: the extraction of sulphur ore, together with the crushing and cleaning of sulphur minerals. That gives the code a clear industrial centre of gravity. It is about taking sulphur-bearing mineral material from the ground and preparing it at the mineral stage, before any further industrial transformation.

The record also places the activity inside the non-metallic mineral licensing universe by naming **IUP Tahap Eksplorasi Mineral Bukan Logam** and **Perpanjangan IUP Tahap Operasi Produksi Mineral Bukan Logam**. Editorially, that matters because it signals a real extractive-sector registration profile: this is the kind of code chosen by operators whose business activity is mineral exploration or the continuation of production operations for a non-metallic mineral. It is not a light service activity that happens to mention sulphur in passing. The activity being registered is the mining and physical preparation of sulphur minerals themselves.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. KBLI 08911 is open to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar**. That means the record does not reserve the activity only for one enterprise size. A founder reading this should understand the code as scale-inclusive on the face of the slim record: micro and small businesses appear alongside medium and large operators. The editorial caution is not about scale availability; it is about correctly matching the registered activity to the actual work. If the business is not mining sulphur ore, or crushing and cleaning sulphur minerals, this code should not be stretched to fit a merely adjacent idea.

The foreign-investment picture is clean. Nationally, the code is marked **TERBUKA**, with a **100%** foreign-ownership ceiling under the cited presidential-regulation sources. Bali does not reverse that outcome in this record. The provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, but the Bali status here is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and the stated reason is that OSS risk at large scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: for this slim record, sulphur mining is foreign-open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

editorial.headline: Phosphate Mining With a Clear Bali Door
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08912 covers phosphate extraction and basic mineral upgrading, with national PMA access open and no Bali moratorium block recorded for this activity.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08912 is the classification for phosphate mining. Its scope is not just the act of extracting phosphate-bearing material from the ground; it also includes the immediate handling that makes the mined material usable at the early processing stage. The record expressly names sorting, crushing, cleaning, and upgrading the grade of phosphate mineral material. In plain English, this is the business of taking phosphate deposits from raw mineral form toward a more prepared mineral product, while staying within the mining and basic beneficiation frame described for the code.

The slim record also places this activity inside the mineral-regulatory vocabulary attached to non-metallic minerals of a specified type. It names an exploration-stage IUP for certain non-metallic minerals and an SIPB application. Those labels matter because they show that the activity is treated as a formal mining activity, not as a generic trading or processing category. The editorial point is narrow but important: a founder registering this code is not describing a downstream retail activity or a broad industrial service; they are describing phosphate mineral extraction with the listed preparation steps.

On business scale, the code is unusually broad. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the record recognises the activity at every listed scale, from the smallest business scale through large enterprise registration. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap to explain here: based on this record, the national foreign-investment position is open up to full foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clean, but it should still be stated with precision. The province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this record does not mark KBLI 08912 as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is therefore not a warning that foreigners cannot register it in Bali today. It is the opposite: for this record, the national PMA opening and the Bali moratorium position point in the same direction. Phosphate mining remains a formal, risk-sensitive mining activity, but the Bali moratorium field does not close the door recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: For this record, the national PMA opening and the Bali moratorium position point in the same direction.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices
moratorium.virtual_office: requested in letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP; application not confirmed

editorial.headline: Nitrate Mining, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08913 covers nitrate mineral extraction and basic processing, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA block under the recorded risk reading.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08913 is a mining classification for nitrate mineral materials. Its scope is direct and industrial: extracting nitrate-bearing minerals, then carrying out the practical handling that makes the material usable in a mining chain, including cleaning, breaking, and sorting by other methods. This is not a trading or consultancy category dressed in mining language; the activity sits at the mineral-extraction level, with the record also placing it in the frame of non-metal mineral exploration and SIPB application language.

That matters because the registration audience is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale operators, so the code is not reserved only for large corporate mines. A smaller operator and a larger investor may both find themselves under the same activity description if the substance is nitrate mineral mining and the associated preparation of that material. The scale choice should therefore follow the real operating footprint, not the prestige of the project or the ambition of the investor.

For foreign ownership, the national picture is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a recorded foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain English, the record does not cap the foreign stake below full ownership. A PMA structure can therefore read this code as nationally foreign-open, subject only to the facts actually stated in the record. The source cited for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and there is no separate foreign-equity reduction shown here.

Bali is unusually clear as well, although the explanation is different. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning that Bali is closed to this PMA activity today; based on this record, nitrate mining stands as foreign-open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is that nitrate mining is foreign-open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

editorial.headline: Iodine Extraction With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08914 covers iodine-bearing groundwater extraction and distillation, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08914 is a narrowly drawn mining activity: the extraction of groundwater that contains iodine, including the distillation activity attached to that mineral extraction. In plain English, this is not a broad trading, processing, or general water-business category. Its centre of gravity is the mineral-bearing groundwater itself and the extraction-to-distillation chain described in the record.

The record places this activity across every business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed only for a large corporate operator, even though the Bali risk note specifically refers to scale Besar. The slim record also carries the Indonesian labels “IUP Tahap Eksplorasi Mineral Bukan Logam” and “Permohonan SIPB”; those should be read as part of the activity’s regulatory context as recorded, not as an invitation to invent extra thresholds, timelines, or conditions beyond the text.

For foreign investment, the national position is uncomplicated. The record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA and sets the maximum foreign ownership figure at 100%. That national position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder or investor reading the code, the clean national conclusion is therefore that KBLI 08914 is open to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling, with no lower cap appearing in the slim record.

Bali does not overturn that reading in this record. For Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK while l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, sourced to Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. But for this code, the record’s own Bali-side conclusion is not blocked. The honest reading is simple: KBLI 08914 is nationally open, carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, is open across all listed scales, and is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium logic supplied here.

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Pertambangan Potash (Kalium Karbonat) (08915)? This is classified as High risk with PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through the requirements.
intel_2026.baliContext: Quarrying in Bali is limited to sand, stone, and marble extraction, primarily in Karangasem and parts of Gianyar. Environmental permits (AMDAL/UKL-UPL) are strictly enforced due to Bali's protected landscape status.

editorial.headline: Potash Mining With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08915 covers potash mineral extraction and processing, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08915 is a mining classification for potash, or potassium carbonate-related mineral activity. Its scope is not just the act of extracting potassium oxide or potash from the ground; it also covers the mineral forms named in the record, including salt, feldspar, leucite, and analcite/analeum. The classification also reaches the crushing and cleaning of those minerals, so the activity should be understood as a focused upstream mineral operation rather than a general trading or industrial-processing category.

That scope matters because this is a code for operators handling the mineral itself. The record also references applications for SIPB and extensions of an IUP production-operation stage for non-metal minerals, which places the activity inside a regulated mining-administration frame. A founder reading this code should therefore treat it as a classification for mineral extraction and immediate mineral handling, not as a loose business label that can be stretched into unrelated potassium, construction, or commodity activity.

On scale, the national record is broad. This activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, and the PMA status is TERBUKA. The foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, so the national classification does not impose a reduced foreign shareholding cap in the slim record. In plain terms, a foreign-owned company can read the national line as open, with full foreign ownership allowed under the cited presidential-regulation source.

In Bali, the picture is equally clear, although the basis for that clarity is not what many founders expect. Bali’s provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, yet this record says the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and that the activity is not blocked. The reason given is specific: at Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is outside the moratorium’s blocked Low and Medium-Low band. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: nationally, KBLI 08915 is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked by the PMA moratorium according to this record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is straightforward: KBLI 08915 is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked by the PMA moratorium.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices
moratorium.virtual_office: requested in letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP; application not confirmed

data.judul: Pertambangan Mineral, Bahan Kimia, dan Bahan Pupuk Lainnya
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pertambangan mineral bahan kimia dan bahan pupuk lainnya yang belum tercakup dalam kelompok 08911 s.d. 08915, misalnya pertambangan barium sulfat alam dan karbonat (barite dan witherit), borat alam, magnesium sulfat alam (kiserit), pertambangan pigmen alami/earth colour, fluorspar, bentonit, dolomit, magnesit, pirofilit, tawas, diatomea, dan mineral lain yang utamanya sebagai bahan kimia; serta pertambangan guano (bahan pupuk dari kotoran burung atau kelelawar), termasuk kegiatan pembersihan, pemisahan, dan sortasi mineral tersebut.

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan;

    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;

    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

editorial.headline: Chemical and Fertiliser Minerals With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08919 covers specialised mineral extraction for chemical and fertiliser inputs, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08919 is the classification for mining mineral materials whose main use is chemical or fertiliser-related, where the activity is not better captured by a more specific mineral category in the record. In practical English, this is a broad home for specialised extraction: natural barium sulphate and carbonate such as barite and witherite, natural borates, natural magnesium sulphate, natural pigments or earth colours, fluorspar, bentonite, dolomite, magnesite, pyrophyllite, alum, diatomite, and other minerals primarily used as chemical materials. It also includes guano mining, where the fertiliser material comes from bird or bat droppings.

The scope is not limited to digging the material from the ground. The record expressly includes cleaning, separating, and sorting these minerals, which matters because this code is about a mining activity with basic preparation steps attached to the extracted material. It also carries references to extension of IUP Production Operation stage for rock mining and for certain types of non-metal mineral mining. Those lines do not turn the editorial into a licensing manual, but they signal that this is a serious extractive classification, not a light trading or distribution activity.

For business registration, the scale picture is unusually broad. Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all permitted scales under the record. That means the classification is not reserved only for large operators in the slim record; it is available across the listed business scales. The substance, however, remains industrial: founders should read the activity as extraction and preparation of chemical or fertiliser minerals, not as retail sale, laboratory formulation, commodity brokerage, or general fertiliser commerce.

The foreign-investment position is clean. Nationally, the status is TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In Bali, the record does not block PMA registration: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the province’s moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: this activity is foreign-open nationally, and the Bali screen in this record does not close the door today.

editorial.headline: Peat Extraction Is Open to Foreign Capital, Including in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08920 covers the extraction, preparation, and handling of peat as a raw material, with national PMA access and a Bali status that remains open but high-risk.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08920 is the classification for peat extraction: the physical taking of peat from the ground, followed by the industrial handling needed to make it usable, movable, and storable. Its scope is not just digging. The record includes excavation, crushing, washing, screening, collection, agglomeration, and preparation to improve quality or ease transport and storage. In plain English, this is the upstream peat activity: removing peat and conditioning it before it moves further along a supply chain.

That makes it a code for operators dealing directly with the material itself, not a broad downstream category. A business registering here is saying that its core activity is the extraction and preparation of peat, with the operational footprint that comes from working at the resource level. The scale access is unusually broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open in the record. So the code is not reserved only for large industrial players. It can be used across business sizes, provided the actual activity remains within this extraction-and-preparation scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. Under the national record, the PMA status is TERBUKA with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign-owned company, that means the record does not impose a foreign-shareholding cap below full ownership. The legal source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record supports adding a minimum capital figure, a special licence timeline, or a tax condition, so those should not be read into the classification. The clean national reading is simple: this activity is open to PMA, including up to full foreign ownership.

The Bali position is also open, but it has to be read carefully. Bali's province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, permanently, according to the recorded moratorium rule and source. This code is not marked as blocked in Bali. The reason is specific: nationally it is TERBUKA, and the Besar scale is classified as Tinggi, so it survives the Bali moratorium. The Bali status is therefore not a quiet prohibition; it is Open in Bali (high-risk track). A PT PMA can register this in Bali today on the record provided, but the editorial point is precision: it is open because it sits outside the moratorium's blocked risk band, not because the moratorium has disappeared.

editorial.headline: Salt Extraction Under the KBLI 2025 Lens
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the extraction and primary preparation of table salt, with national PMA access open and Bali not blocking it under the current moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08930 is about salt at its source. Its centre of gravity is extraction and primary production: drawing table salt from underground deposits, including through dissolving and pumping; producing table salt by evaporating seawater or other brine, such as in ponds; and the crushing, separation, and refining of table salt by salt farmers. The activity is therefore not a general food-manufacturing category. It sits at the earlier, resource-facing stage where salt is obtained and prepared before any separate downstream processing.

That boundary matters. The record keeps this activity focused on extraction and farmer-level preparation, while excluding the later transformation of salt into processed table salt such as iodized salt. It also excludes the production of drinking water by evaporating brine. In practical editorial terms, the code is for operators whose business is the obtaining and basic preparation of salt itself, not for businesses whose real activity is packaged, fortified, or drinking-water output.

The registration picture is broad at the national level. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**, and opens it across **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales. That means the code is not reserved only for a single business size, and the national PMA position is clean: foreign investment is open up to full ownership, according to the cited presidential-regulation source in the record.

The Bali position is more nuanced, but not negative. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This record, however, states that the OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so the activity is **not blocked by the moratorium**. The honest reading is therefore that Bali remains open to foreign registration for this code today. It is that the code is nationally foreign-open, and in Bali it falls outside the moratorium block as recorded, though the Bali status is still labelled **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** rather than a simple low-risk clearance.

editorial.headline: Gemstone Mining Is Open Nationally, and Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08991 covers gemstone mining and quarrying, including sorting and cleaning, with full foreign ownership allowed nationally and a Bali status that is not blocked by the PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08991 is a mining classification for precious stones and gemstones. Its Indonesian scope is direct: it covers the mining and quarrying of batu mulia and batu permata, including diamonds, and it includes separation, sorting and cleaning carried out by other methods on those stones. The centre of gravity is extraction and the immediate handling of mined gemstones. The scope text also names extensions of IUP operation-production stages for rock and for certain non-metal minerals, so the classification should be read as sitting inside a mining-administration context, not as a lifestyle label for a gem business.

Who uses it is defined more by the activity than by a narrow company size. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, which means the scale field does not reserve this classification only for large operators. A smaller registered activity and a large-scale mining operation are both within the scale range shown, so the practical question is not whether the scale label itself is closed. The practical question is whether the planned activity truly falls within gemstone mining, quarrying, separation, sorting or cleaning as described in the scope.

Nationally, the PMA reading is straightforward. The status is TERBUKA, the listed foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and the cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. For a foreign-owned setup, that matters: the national investment line is open rather than restricted, and the ownership ceiling in the data reaches all the way to 100%. There is no basis in this record for adding a minimum capital figure, timeline or special threshold beyond those fields.

The Bali position is the important nuance. Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island on a permanent basis, but this record does not mark 08991 as blocked. The record assigns it the Bali status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. That does not turn the classification into a casual green light for every project; it simply means the Bali moratorium, as captured in this record, is not the barrier. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership, open across the listed scales, and in Bali not blocked by the PMA moratorium.

Pemegang IPR:

  1. Melakukan kegiatan Penambangan dalam jangka waktu paling lambat 3 (tiga) bulan setelah IPR diterbitkan;
  2. Menyusun rencana Penambangan berdasarkan dokumen pengelolaan WPR yang disusun oleh Menteri, yang meliputi: metode penambangan, peralatan dan perlengkapan yang digunakan, jadwal kerja, kebutuhan personil, dan biaya atau permodalan; 
  3. Mematuhi persyaratan teknis pertambangan, antara lain:
    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;
    2. Tidak menggunakan bahan berbahaya beracun yang dilarang sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

    1. Tidak menggunakan bahan peledak;

    3. Tidak melakukan kegiatan penambangan dengan menggunakan metode penambangan bawah tanah bagi orang perseorangan; dan
    4. Menerapkan kaidah teknis pertambangan yang baik khususnya pengelolaan lingkungan dan keselamatan pertambangan

editorial.headline: Feldspar and Calcite Quarrying With Room for Foreign Capital
editorial.standfirst: A mineral-quarrying activity open across business scales, with Bali not blocking PMA registration under the record’s risk reading.
editorial.body:
This activity is about the quarrying of feldspar and calcite, with slate also brought inside the same operational scope. The record is practical rather than decorative: it includes extraction, then the physical handling that makes the material usable, namely breaking, crushing, screening, and smoothing. In other words, it is not only the act of taking mineral material from the ground; it also covers the immediate processing steps that shape quarried material into a more workable form.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to micro, small, medium, and large businesses, so the classification is not reserved only for heavy industrial operators. A smaller quarrying operation and a larger mineral operation can both sit inside the same activity description, provided the registered activity remains the one described here. The slim record also names SIPB applications and extensions of IUP operation-production stage for non-metal minerals, which signals that the administrative surface is tied to formal mineral business registration rather than informal material handling.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean: the activity is marked open, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. That means the record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The source given for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the editorial point should stay exactly there: open nationally, with the ceiling stated as the record states it. There is no basis in the slim record to add a minimum capital number, a separate sectoral licence threshold, a tax consequence, or a processing deadline.

Bali is where many open activities become more complicated, but this record does not show a block. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all low and medium-low risk activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. Here, however, the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at large scale is medium-high/high, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore narrow and useful: a foreign-owned company can look at this activity nationally as open, and the Bali record supplied here does not mark it as blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Natural Asphalt Mining With a Clear PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08993 covers natural asphalt, asphalt-bearing stone, and solid natural bitumen, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08993 is a mining classification, not a trading or construction label. Its Indonesian scope is focused on the extraction of natural asphalt, asphalt-bearing stone, and solid natural bitumen. The record also includes separation and pouring activities for those minerals, so the centre of gravity is the mineral activity itself: taking the material from its natural source and handling the mineral in the forms named by the scope.

That makes this a specialised code for businesses whose registered activity is tied to natural asphalt and bitumen as minerals. The slim record opens the code across all listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. It also carries the licensing language shown in the source field, namely IUPK Exploration and extension of IUP at the Production Operation stage. Those references should be read exactly as they appear in the record: they signal the mining character of the activity, without adding any separate threshold, timeline, or capital rule beyond the slim data.

At the national level, the PMA position is uncomplicated. This record marks PMA as TERBUKA and sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%. In plain terms, the national investment list source named here treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling recorded for this code. There is no partial foreign cap to explain for this record, and no basis here to introduce a special ownership restriction beyond the stated maximum.

The Bali reading is also unusually clean, because the record does not show a provincial PMA block. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this record says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and therefore it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is that KBLI 08993 is nationally open for PMA and, on this slim record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated Bali moratorium rule.

editorial.headline: Asbestos Excavation With a Clear Bali Registration Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08994 covers asbestos digging, cleaning, and separation, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08994 is a narrow mining activity: the excavation of asbestos, whether the material is in fibrous form or not. The scope also includes the cleaning and separation work that belongs to that extraction process. In practical classification terms, this is not a general construction-material trade, not a downstream manufacturing line, and not a broad mineral services bucket. It is the activity of taking asbestos from the ground and preparing it through the immediate cleaning and separation steps named in the record.

The slim record also places the activity inside the Indonesian administrative vocabulary for mineral operations. It refers to **Permohonan SIPB** and **Perpanjangan IUP Tahap Operasi Produksi Mineral Bukan Logam**. Those phrases matter because they show the classification sits in a regulated mining context, but the record does not give further conditions, thresholds, processing timelines, or capital rules. A responsible reading stops there: this KBLI is about asbestos excavation and the directly attached preparation work, with those two administrative references attached to its scope.

For business-size access, the record is unusually broad. It is open across **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales. Nationally, the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**. That means the national record presents this activity as open to foreign investment without a minority cap in the data provided. There is no basis here to invent a lower foreign-share limit, a special minimum capital figure, or an extra licensing hurdle beyond the phrases already present in the scope.

The Bali reading is also clear, and it should not be made more dramatic than the record allows. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the province, but this activity is **not blocked** in the slim record. The reason given is specific: at **Besar** scale, the OSS risk is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not caught by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: nationally this KBLI is foreign-open up to 100%, and for Bali the record does not show a PMA registration block under the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Quartz and Silica Sand Extraction, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers quartz, quartz sand and silica sand extraction, with processing steps included and PMA access open across every recorded business scale.
editorial.body:
Quartz and silica sand sit in a practical, industrial part of the mineral economy: not an abstract trading category, but the physical extraction and preparation of a defined material. The recorded scope covers the digging of quartz, quartz sand and silica sand, and it also includes the immediate processing activities that make the material usable: breaking, crushing, screening and refining. In plain English, this is a quarrying and preparation activity for quartz-based sand materials, not merely brokerage or distribution.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar operators, which means the classification is not reserved only for one size of enterprise. A small local operator and a larger industrial setup may sit under the same activity description if their work is genuinely the extraction and preparation of quartz or silica sand as described. The scope also names two administrative touchpoints: Permohonan SIPB and Perpanjangan IUP Tahap Operasi Produksi Mineral Bukan Logam Jenis Tertentu. Those phrases should be read exactly as recorded, without adding extra assumptions about procedure, timing or eligibility.

For foreign-owned companies, the national reading is straightforward: PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership recorded at 100%. That makes this one of the cleaner cases nationally, because the record does not impose a partial foreign-share ceiling. The investor still has to respect the activity’s actual substance: extraction and included processing of quartz, quartz sand or silica sand. A company that is only adjacent to that work should not stretch the classification beyond the field that the record actually describes.

A different factor makes the Bali position unusually clear as well. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali reason states that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms, this is not a hidden Bali closure: nationally it is foreign-open, and the Bali note does not convert it into a PMA block. The honest conclusion is therefore disciplined rather than dramatic: quartz and silica sand extraction is open to PMA nationally, up to full foreign ownership, and the Bali moratorium record does not block it where the stated risk position applies.

editorial.headline: Rare Earth Mining Is Open, Including in Bali, but Only on the Higher-Risk Track
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08996 covers rare earth metal ore mining, open to PMA up to 100% and not caught by Bali’s low-risk moratorium because its large-scale OSS risk is higher.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08996 is a mineral-mining classification for rare earth metal ore and rare earth metal alloys. Its scope is unusually explicit: it covers the mining of rare earth metals and alloys associated with lanthanum, cerium, praseodymium, neodymium, promethium, samarium, europium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, holmium, erbium, thulium, ytterbium, lutetium, plus scandium and yttrium. In plain English, this is not a general trading or processing label. It is the activity lane for extracting the rare earth mineral base itself.

The record also places the activity inside an IUP sequence. It names an Exploration Stage IUP for rare earth metal minerals and an upgrade to a Production Operation Stage IUP for the same mineral group. That wording matters editorially because it frames the code as a mining activity that moves from exploration into production operation, rather than a broad umbrella for downstream commercial uses. The classification is available across **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so it is not reserved only for one enterprise size in the slim record.

For foreign investors, the national position is clean: the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with a stated foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. There is no partial cap in the record, so the correct reading is full foreign ownership at the national classification level. That does not remove the need to respect the exact mining pathway named in the scope, but it does mean the KBLI itself is nationally open to foreign capital and is not capped below full ownership.

The Bali reading is also unusually straightforward. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record is marked **l4_bali_blocked: false**. The reason given is that OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In honest terms: a foreign-owned setup is not barred from registering this KBLI in Bali by the low-risk moratorium described in the record. The classification remains a higher-risk mining lane, but the Bali-specific status is not a prohibition.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign-owned setup is not barred from registering this KBLI in Bali by the low-risk moratorium described in the record.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity

data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup pertambangan dan penggalian lainnya yang belum termasuk dalam golongan manapun, termasuk kegiatan pemisahan/sortasi, dan pembersihan dengan cara lain terhadap bahan tambang/galian tersebut,seperti pertambangan dan penggalian mika, leusit, jarosit, zeolit, batu penggosok, grafit alam, steatit (talk), tepung fosil siliceous, oker, dan toseki.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup ekstraksi berbagai macam mineral dan material (seperti litium, uranium, dan torium) dari air asin, kecuali garam meja.

editorial.headline: Other Mining and Quarrying, Treated as a Serious Mineral Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08999 covers residual mining and quarrying activities, including sorting and cleaning of specified minerals and extraction from brine, with national PMA access open.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08999 is the residual home for mining and quarrying activities that are not already placed in another group. The record describes it in practical terms: mining, quarrying, separation, sorting, and cleaning of certain extracted materials. The examples matter because they show the character of the activity: mica, leucite, jarosite, zeolite, polishing stone, natural graphite, steatite or talc, siliceous fossil flour, ochre, and toseki. It also includes extraction of various minerals and materials from brine, such as lithium, uranium, and thorium, while expressly excluding table salt. This is not a general trading or advisory category. It is an extractive activity, with physical materials, mineral classification, and processing steps inside the scope.

The registration field is unusually broad on business scale. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not reserved only for large projects in the classification data. That said, the wording of the scope still keeps the activity anchored in mining and quarrying. The record also names two IUP-related phrases: exploration-stage IUP for certain non-metal minerals, and upgrade to operation-production stage IUP for non-metal minerals. Those phrases are part of the record’s description of the activity; they should not be expanded into extra assumptions about timing, thresholds, or procedural steps beyond what is written here.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder reading the category, that means the national classification does not itself impose a reduced foreign-share cap in this record. The activity may be registered across all listed scales, and the PMA field is not half-open or ambiguous: it is open, with the maximum foreign stake rendered at the full percentage shown in the data.

The Bali reading is also important because it is not the usual blocked-moratorium case in this record. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this code is not marked as blocked. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. That does not create a separate Bali ownership cap, a local partnership requirement, or a special Bali percentage. It simply means that, on the record provided, KBLI 08999 is nationally foreign-open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 08999 is nationally foreign-open and, on this record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: The Contract Backbone of Oil and Gas Field Work
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 09100 covers specialist oil-and-gas support services performed for a fee or under contract, and the record treats it as nationally open to PMA.
editorial.body:
KBLI 09100 is not the business of owning or operating an oil or gas field. It is the contracted support layer around extraction: the technical services that make exploration, drilling, well work, field logistics, and emergency response possible. The record describes services performed for a fee or under contract, from geological observation in prospective mining areas to drilling and re-drilling, installing drilling equipment on site, cementing oil and gas wells, making well channels, plugging and closing wells, and carrying out trial drilling connected with petroleum and gas refining.

Its scope is practical and field-facing. The activity also includes pumping and mine-distribution services carried out on a fee or contract basis, plus natural-gas liquefaction and regasification when done at the mining site for transport needs. The record expressly includes oil-and-gas field firefighting services, which gives the code a broader support character than routine drilling assistance alone. In plain English, this is the KBLI for companies hired to support oil-and-gas exploration and exploitation operations, rather than companies registering as the field operator itself.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar** scales, so the code is not reserved only for large corporate vehicles. A registrant still has to match its real activity to the technical scope: the business should be providing oil-and-gas mining support services for remuneration or contract, not general equipment repair, off-site gas transport processing, platform installation work, or geophysical survey work outside this stated scope. The editorial point is simple: the registered activity must sit inside the service perimeter described by the record, because this code is defined by what is done at or around the oil-and-gas mining operation.

For foreign investment, the national reading is clear. The record marks PMA status as **TERBUKA** and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**, with the source listed as **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. Bali does not change that into a separate percentage or quota in this record. The Bali-side status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the stated reason is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. That matters because the moratorium rule in the record blocks low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali; this activity is not marked as blocked. On the record provided, KBLI 09100 is nationally open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

editorial.headline: Mining Support Work That Stops Short of Operating the Mine
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 09900 covers contracted support services around mining and quarrying, nationally open to foreign investment and not marked as Bali-moratorium blocked.
editorial.body:
KBLI 09900 is for the work that surrounds a mine or quarry without becoming the mine or quarry operator itself. The record defines it as support services supplied for a fee or under contract, needed in mining and quarrying activity. In practical English, this is the technical and operational help around extraction: exploration support, traditional ore sampling, geological observation at prospective mine locations, pumping and drying mined output, trial excavation, trial drilling of wells or mining fields, and other site-side support tasks.

The scope is deliberately industrial and hands-on. It also includes third-party agglomeration and concentration of iron ore, securing mine shafts and tunnels, and demolishing structures or dismantling components and equipment inside underground mining facilities. That makes the code broad, but not unlimited. The record draws a boundary around it: it does not cover operating a mine or quarry under contract, specialist repair of mining machinery, or geophysical survey services supplied under contract. The centre of gravity is support, preparation, handling, safety, and dismantling around mining infrastructure, not taking over the extraction business itself.

On the registration side, the scale picture is unusually complete. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also plain: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is 100%. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no smaller national ceiling in the record, so the editorial point should not be softened into uncertainty: as recorded here, this activity is nationally open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling.

The Bali reading is more specific, and it matters because the Bali moratorium is not a general mood but a rule applied through the record’s risk logic. The moratorium text says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. KBLI 09900, however, is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is clean: this is a nationally open PMA activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and the Bali-side record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Where Ruminant Slaughter Becomes a Registered Industrial Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10111 covers ruminant slaughterhouse work, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for Bali PMA registration under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10111 is the registration lane for ruminant slaughterhouse activity.** In plain English, the record describes a facility handling animals such as cattle, buffalo, goats, and sheep, with the activity extending beyond the moment of slaughter itself. Its scope includes slaughtering, skinning, cleaning, and packing meat, which makes this a code for an operational processing site rather than a narrow trading label.

The same scope also reaches into the practical byproducts of slaughterhouse work. The record includes handling side outputs such as hides and skins from slaughterhouses and livestock operations, drying bones, processing animal remnants or waste, sorting wool, and cleaning fat. That breadth matters editorially: this is not just a meat-cutting description, but a classification for the controlled conversion of ruminant livestock into meat and associated materials.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the activity can be registered across the full range of business sizes named in the data. That does not turn the code into a casual category; it simply means the record does not reserve it for one scale of operator. A small slaughterhouse and a larger industrial facility are both contemplated by the same scale field, provided the activity being registered is the slaughterhouse work described in the scope.

The national-versus-Bali picture is clean rather than contradictory. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` recorded at 100, so the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100% according to the supplied record and its cited source. Bali is also not marked as blocked: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The record’s reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That means the Bali moratorium rule exists in the record, but this activity is not blocked by it on the supplied facts. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: KBLI 10111 is nationally open to PMA, carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling in the record, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali field provided.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.
