editorial.headline: Frozen Fruit and Vegetable Processing With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10304 covers fruit, vegetable, and tuber freezing, nationally open to foreign ownership and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10304 is about preservation by freezing. The slim record describes the activity as freezing fruits and vegetables into products that can be consumed directly or used as inputs for later production. Its practical field is concrete rather than abstract: frozen mango, frozen strawberries, and frozen potatoes sit inside the scope, as do frozen tubers such as cassava and porang. The common thread is not retailing, farming, or cold storage as a generic service; it is the processing step that turns fresh produce into a frozen food product or a frozen production input.

That makes this code relevant for founders building a food-processing operation around Indonesian produce, especially where the business model depends on stabilising perishables and making them usable beyond the immediate harvest window. A company registering this activity is not simply handling fruit and vegetables; it is preserving them through freezing. The record is also unusually broad on business scale. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the activity is not confined to one enterprise size in the slim record. A small processor and a large industrial operation can both sit within the same code if the registered activity is the freezing of the covered produce.

The national investment picture is clean. The record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA and sets maximum foreign ownership at 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to a fully foreign-owned setup. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign stake, special threshold, or additional capital figure in the record, so none should be read into the code. For a founder comparing structure options, the important point is simple: nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling in the slim record is full ownership.

The Bali-side reading is also clear, but for a different reason. The record does not mark this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the slim record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this code is not marked as caught by that block. The honest conclusion is therefore not a hidden Bali cap or a separate Bali percentage. It is that KBLI 10304 is nationally foreign-open, and the supplied Bali record does not block it under the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Canning Fruit and Vegetables as a Preservation Business
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10305 covers airtight canning with retort or pasteurisation, open across all business scales and nationally open to full foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10305 is for the industrial preservation of fruit and vegetables through airtight packaging or canning, with a retort or pasteurisation process as part of the activity. In plain English, this is not a code for simply putting produce into containers. The record defines it as processing and preserving fruit and vegetables so the finished product can stand as a canned food product: canned pineapple, canned rambutan, canned beans, canned mushrooms, and canned carrots are all examples named in the scope.

That distinction matters because the centre of the activity is preservation. The can, jar, or airtight pack is not merely a retail wrapper; it is part of the method by which the food is treated and made stable. A founder using this code should therefore be describing a production activity that changes the condition of the fruit or vegetable through canning, retort, or pasteurisation. The language of the record is broad enough to cover both fruit and vegetable lines, but it stays anchored in this specific processing method.

The registration scale is unusually wide. The slim record marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the code can be used from a very small production setup through to a large operation, provided the registered activity remains within the canning and preservation scope. For a foreign-owned company, the national investment picture is also direct: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali reading is not the same as a hidden local cap. The record does not give Bali its own foreign-ownership percentage, partnership formula, quota, or special capital condition. It marks Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule itself blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this record says KBLI 10305 is not blocked by that rule. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: nationally, this activity is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, this slim record does not mark it as blocked by the provincial moratorium.

editorial.headline: Fruit and Vegetable Juice Processing, Without the Bali Detour
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10306 covers the industrial work of turning fruit and vegetables into juices, concentrates, nectars, powders, and derivative juice products.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10306 is about transformation rather than retail display. The activity in the record is the processing and preservation of fruit and vegetables into juice products: fruit and vegetable juices, juice powders, fruit-juice concentrates, vegetable-juice concentrates, and fruit or vegetable nectars. It also reaches the processing of those juices into derivative products. In practical terms, this is the code for a business whose core work is taking agricultural inputs and making shelf-ready or further-processable juice-based outputs, not simply selling produce or serving drinks across a counter.

The boundaries matter because the record is precise about what sits inside this activity. It is not a catch-all label for every fruit-themed beverage. The scope points to real fruit and vegetable juice processing, preservation, concentration, powdering, nectar production, and downstream juice derivatives. It also draws a line away from artificial concentrates and fruit-flavoured drinks. That distinction gives the code its editorial centre: this is a food-processing activity anchored in the substance of fruit and vegetable juice, not a broader beverage-marketing category.

For registration scale, the record is unusually open: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as available scales. That means the activity can describe a small processing operation as well as a larger industrial setup, provided the business being registered genuinely matches the processing scope above. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the stated maximum foreign ownership is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial ceiling in this record; on the national reading, the activity is foreign-open up to full ownership.

The Bali reading is where the code avoids the common trap. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That does not create a separate Bali percentage, condition, quota, or partnership requirement. It simply means the record does not treat this code as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium logic. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest conclusion is therefore clean: nationally open, 100% foreign-owned, and not blocked in Bali on the facts provided here.

editorial.headline: Soybean Tempe Production Is Reserved for Koperasi and UMKM — Closed to PT PMA Nationwide
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10307 covers the making of tempe from soybeans; Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II allocates it to Indonesian cooperatives and MSMEs, so a foreign-owned company cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia.
editorial.body:
**This KBLI activity is deliberately narrow: it covers the making of tempe from soybeans.** The record does not frame it as a broad fermented-food category, a general protein-manufacturing activity, or a catch-all for every product called tempe. Its scope is the production activity itself, anchored in one raw material: kedelai, or soybeans. That precision matters because the commercial identity of the product may feel familiar, even domestic, but the registration question is still technical. The code is about what is being made, from what input, and under which registered industrial activity.

For operators, the scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. In practical registration language, that means the activity is not reserved only for cottage producers or only for large industry; it can sit across the full scale ladder recorded here. A founder setting up a small production unit, a growing local processor, or a larger manufacturing operation would all read the same scale field before moving on to the ownership and location question.

The ownership position is set by Perpres 10/2021, as amended by Perpres 49/2021, Lampiran II: soybean tempe manufacturing is allocated to Koperasi and UMKM (p.2, entry 4, sub-row "Industri tempe kedelai", ex-KBLI 2020 10391). A foreign investor can be neither a cooperative nor a UMKM, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded for tempe making is 0% and a PT PMA cannot register this code anywhere in Indonesia. Bali's provincial overlay does not change that answer: the record lists 10307 outside the 18 business fields Bali closed to new PMA licensing in 2026, but the national reservation already decides the PMA question.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity involves preserving fruits and vegetables by means other than those in certain pre-defined groups. It includes making foods where fruits or vegetables are the main ingredient (except frozen or canned ready meals), producing perishable items like fruit or vegetable salads, processing and preserving soybeans and legumes into products such as natto, yuba, fu zhu, douchi, and varieties of tempeh other than standard tofu and tempeh, and roasting nuts and legumes like peas, salted peanuts, coated peanuts, cashew nuts, and peanut-based snacks. The manufacture of processed vegetable foods is excluded and falls under a separate classification.

editorial.headline: A Versatile Code for Fruit, Vegetable, and Nut Processing
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10309 covers preservation and processing work where produce and legumes become prepared foods, short-life products, soy-based items, or roasted nuts.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10309 is a broad but still clearly bounded activity code for businesses that process and preserve fruit, vegetables, soybeans, legumes, and nuts in forms that sit outside the more narrowly defined preservation lanes. In plain English, it is for the workshop or factory where produce is turned into food products: fruit- or vegetable-based preparations, short-life salads made from fruit or vegetables, selected soybean and legume products such as natto, yuba, fu zhu, douchi, tempe gembus, and tempe bongkrek, and the roasting of nuts such as peas, salted nuts, egg-coated nuts, bogor nuts, atom nuts, cashews, and enting-enting.

That makes the code useful for founders whose real business is not farming or retailing, but transformation: taking perishable or raw ingredients and giving them a processed food identity. The record also draws the boundary by exclusion: processed foods from vegetables are not inside this activity when they fall under the separate subcategory named in the source record. For this code, the editorial point is not romance about food manufacturing; it is classification discipline. The activity is about preservation, preparation, soybean and legume processing, and nut roasting, not every possible food product that happens to include fruit or vegetables.

On registration scale, the code is unusually open. The slim record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as open scales, so the same activity can describe a small local operator or a larger processing business, provided the registered activity still matches the scope. Nationally, the PMA position is also clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial foreign cap in the record, so the national reading is straightforward: for foreign investment purposes, this activity is open up to full foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clear, and it is important not to overcomplicate it. The record does include the province-wide moratorium rule: Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” In practical editorial terms, the honest conclusion is that KBLI 10309 is nationally open and, on the provided Bali record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

editorial.headline: Crude Vegetable Oils Before the Refinery Stage
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers non-coconut, non-palm vegetable oils made as crude inputs, with national foreign ownership open and no Bali PMA moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
This activity is about the first industrial step in turning plant materials into crude vegetable oil. The record describes the processing of non-coconut and non-palm vegetable inputs into crude oil, including olive oil, soybean oil, peanut oil, sunflower-seed oil, cottonseed oil, castor oil, mustard-seed oil, and linseed oil. The important word is **crude**: these are oils that still need further processing, and the record frames them as products normally used as inputs in other activities rather than as finished consumer goods.

That makes the code useful for founders whose planned business sits at the raw-processing end of the vegetable-oil chain. It is not described as retailing, branding, distribution, food service, or final packaged oil. Its center of gravity is industrial conversion: taking specified vegetable materials and producing crude oil or fat that another activity may later refine, formulate, package, or otherwise transform. A clean registration should therefore match that upstream scope, because the record gives this activity its identity through processing, input use, and the fact that the product remains unfinished.

On business scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar**, so the activity is not limited in the record to one size of operator. Nationally, the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is recorded as **100%**. Put plainly, the national record treats this activity as foreign-open up to full foreign ownership. There is no smaller ownership cap in the slim record, and there is no basis here to invent one.

The Bali reading is also clear, but it should be stated carefully. The Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the record says: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The honest national-vs-Bali picture, then, is not a contradiction: nationally it is foreign-open, and in Bali the record does not apply the PMA moratorium block. For a foreign-owned setup, the strength of this code is that its permitted reading stays aligned across the national ownership field and the Bali moratorium field.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Margarin Manufacturing Is Nationally Open and Bali-Registerable
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10412 covers the making of margarine from edible vegetable oil, open nationally to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10412 is a narrow industrial code: it covers the manufacturing of margarine from edible vegetable oil. That is the full commercial centre of gravity in the record. It is not a trading category, not a restaurant category, and not a broad food-processing basket. The activity is the making of margarine itself, with the raw material described as plant-based edible oil. For a founder, that matters because the code reads like a production activity rather than a general food business label.

The scale picture is unusually clean. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not framed only for one size of operator. A small producer and a larger industrial player sit in the same activity definition, provided their registered business is still the manufacture of margarine from edible vegetable oil. The record does not add extra thresholds, production volumes, facilities, or minimum-capital figures, so none should be read into it.

Nationally, the PMA signal is direct: the code is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. In practical editorial terms, that means the national record treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and there is no special national caveat supplied here that would reduce that headline position.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. The code is not marked as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The record’s reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not caught by that block on the supplied record. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali creates a separate ownership cap or partnership condition. It does not, at least not in this record. The honest conclusion is that KBLI 10412 is nationally foreign-open and, on the Bali moratorium data provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Crude Animal Fats, Clearly Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10413 covers the industrial processing of non-fish animal material into crude, inedible fats and oils, with full-scale access and a clean Bali reading.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10413 is a narrow industrial classification, and its precision matters. The activity is the processing of animal materials other than fish into crude oils and inedible animal fats. The record’s examples are tallow and oil from marine mammals, which gives the code its practical shape: this is not a finished-food category, and it is not a general trading label. It is a production activity for crude, non-edible animal fat outputs, defined by the source material and by the fact that the resulting fats and oils are not for eating.

That makes the registration logic unusually clean. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale operators, so the slim record does not confine it to a particular business size. A founder reading this code should understand it as an industrial processing lane that can be registered across the full scale ladder, from micro through large. The classification should still be used with discipline: the scope points to processing, not every downstream use of animal fat, and not fish-based oil activity. The strongest reading is the plain one: non-fish animal inputs, crude oil or inedible fat outputs.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also direct. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` at 100 and the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In business English, that means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no separate national caveat in the slim record, and no lower foreign-share ceiling to explain. The right conclusion is therefore not cautious by habit, but factual: on the national PMA field, this code is open.

Bali does not add a hidden percentage or a separate ownership ceiling in this record. Its status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, and `l4_bali_blocked` is false. The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That is the honest Bali-side substance. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this code is not blocked by that rule on the record provided. For KBLI 10413, the national and Bali readings align: foreign registration is open nationally, and the Bali moratorium does not block it.
editorial.pullQuote: For KBLI 10413, the national and Bali readings align: foreign registration is open nationally, and the Bali moratorium does not block it.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Fish Oil Manufacturing, Read as a Real Production Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10414 covers the making of fish oil from fatty fish or fish organs, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10414 is not a broad seafood label. The record defines it as an industrial activity: making oil from fish with high fat content, such as lemuru, or from fish body organs, such as shark liver. The center of gravity is therefore production, not trading, harvesting, retailing, or general marine processing. Its scope is anchored in the conversion of fish-based raw material into fish oil, and the record also keeps a clear boundary around pharmaceutical or cosmetic ingredient processing.

That matters for founders because the activity is open across every business scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical classification terms, this means the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators; it can be used by smaller registered businesses as well as larger manufacturers, provided the real business activity is the manufacture of fish oil described in the scope. The record gives no licence threshold, capital rule, tax treatment, operating timeline, or facility condition, so none should be read into it. The classification tells us what the activity is and which scales are open, not the full operating compliance map.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. Under the record, PMA is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That is the plain national reading under the cited source, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021: a foreign-owned company can treat this activity as open at the national level, with no ownership cap below full foreign ownership stated in the record. This is one of those cases where the headline conclusion should not be made more cautious than the data allows.

Bali needs to be read separately, but not pessimistically. The record marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says it is not blocked. The reason given is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record does not place KBLI 10414 inside that blocked category. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.

Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing of cooking and edible oils from sources other than coconut and palm oil—like sesame, rice bran, lard, or poultry fat—producing niche vegetable and animal-based oils for culinary use.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business is open for 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Minyak Goreng dan Minyak Makan Bukan Minyak Kelapa dan Minyak Kelapa Sawit (10415)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur wanting to produce specialty edible oils (sesame, rice bran, or animal fat-based) for niche culinary or health markets, but currently unable to set up in Bali due to the PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Edible Oils Beyond Coconut and Palm
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers cooking and edible oils made from other raw materials, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10415 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label.** Its scope is the making of cooking oil and edible oil from materials other than coconut oil and palm oil. The record names sesame oil, rice-bran oil, pig cooking oil, and poultry cooking oil as examples. That gives the code a clear industrial centre of gravity: it is about processing edible-oil inputs into finished cooking or eating oils, where the defining boundary is what the oil is made from and the fact that coconut and palm oil sit outside this activity.

The registration profile is unusually broad on business scale. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the code is not framed only for industrial groups with large plants. A small producer and a larger manufacturer can both sit within the scale range if the registered activity is the production of these non-coconut, non-palm edible oils. The practical reading is simple: scale does not change the identity of the activity; it changes the business footprint around the same core manufacturing scope.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The record, drawing on Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, classifies the activity as TERBUKA and sets pma_max_asing at 100. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling in this record is 100%. There is no lower national cap stated here, and nothing in the slim record adds a special capital threshold, licence condition, tax treatment, or timeline. The only defensible national statement is that this activity is foreign-open up to the stated ceiling.

The Bali reading is also clear, but for a different reason. Under the record’s Bali moratorium, PMA is permanently barred throughout the province for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The record’s reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is not a warning about a hidden Bali cap. It is that the activity is nationally open to the stated foreign-ownership ceiling, and the slim record does not show a Bali moratorium block for PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is that this activity is foreign-open nationally and not marked as blocked by Bali’s moratorium in the record.

Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. editorial.headline: The Residual Oils and Fats Code With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10419 covers specialised processing of non-coconut and non-palm crude oils and fats, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10419 sits in a precise manufacturing corner: the processing of crude oils and fats from plant and animal sources outside the named coconut and palm-oil lanes. The slim record describes work such as making shortening from various vegetable oils, including coconut and palm oil inputs, producing cotton linter, and handling oilcake, pulp, and other residues from oil production and refining from fish and marine mammals. In plain English, this is not retail trading, farming, or a generic food-service activity. It is industrial processing around oils, fats, and the by-products left after extraction or refining.

The registration profile is unusually broad on scale. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the code is not framed only for large industrial capital. A small processor and a larger manufacturing operation can both fall within the scale language, provided the actual activity remains within the recorded scope. That breadth matters because the economic substance of the code can vary: one business may focus on a specialised fat product such as shortening, while another may be organised around residues from marine oil refining. What ties them together is the processing character, not a single finished consumer product.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. For a foreign-owned setup, the central point is therefore straightforward: the code is nationally open, and the national maximum foreign ownership value in the record is 100%.

Bali does not add a separate percentage or ownership ceiling in this record. Its local status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali-blocked flag is false. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule itself is broad, blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this record does not place KBLI 10419 inside that block. The honest national-vs-Bali picture is therefore not a contradiction: nationally open, and, on this slim record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the listed moratorium.

editorial.headline: Copra Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the drying of coconut into copra for coconut-oil production, with full national foreign ownership but no PMA registration path in Bali.
editorial.body:
Copra manufacturing is a narrow but important industrial activity: the making of copra from coconuts that are sun-dried and dried for use in coconut-oil production. The record is not describing coconut farming, retail trading, or a general food business. It is focused on the transformation step, where coconut becomes dried copra as an input for oil making. That gives the activity a practical industrial character, even when the operation itself may be simple in equipment and process.

The national scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar undertakings, so it is not reserved only for large factories or only for cottage-scale producers. A small producer preparing dried copra and a larger operator serving coconut-oil production both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the activity remains the manufacture of copra from dried coconut. For founders, the useful point is that the registration frame follows the activity itself, not a lifestyle label or a marketing description.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clear. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the stated maximum foreign ownership is 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is therefore an activity a foreign-owned company can hold in full. There is no lower foreign-stake ceiling in the record, and there is no extra capital, licensing, or timeline condition stated here. The national rule is open, and the ownership number should be read exactly as written.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks this activity as blocked for Bali PMA registration, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” In plain terms, a foreign investor should not treat the national 100% opening as a Bali registration route today. The Bali moratorium rule in the record says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, with the source identified as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest reading is split: nationally open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is split: nationally open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the industrial processing of coconuts into crude coconut oil (crude oil), including the production of copra pellets as a by-product from the oil extraction process. Basically, it's the first stage of turning dried coconut meat into raw coconut oil.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Minyak Mentah Kelapa (10422)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to build a large-scale coconut oil extraction facility with export ambitions, but who are flexible on location or timing if targeting Bali.

editorial.headline: Crude Coconut Oil Processing, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the industrial processing of coconuts into crude oil, with copra pellets as a by-product, and is open across every business scale in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10422 is a production-side activity, not a trading label or a general coconut business category. The slim record defines it as the processing of coconut into crude oil, including the production of copra pellets that arise as a by-product of making coconut oil. That gives the code a fairly clear industrial character: its center of gravity is transformation, where coconut is processed into a raw oil output, with the copra pellet stream sitting inside the same manufacturing process rather than as a separate commercial story.

The registration profile is unusually broad in scale terms. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the code is not confined to a single company size. A smaller producer and a larger industrial operator may both sit within the same activity description, provided the registered activity remains the processing of coconut into crude oil as described. The editorial point is precision: the code is about the activity being registered, not about every possible downstream use, retail channel, or agricultural supply arrangement around coconuts.

At the national level, the position on foreign investment is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%. In plain English, the national field treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. The source field attached to that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special capital figure, operating threshold, licence timeline, or tax condition, so none should be read into the registration analysis.

The Bali-side picture is also clear, but for a different reason. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not marked as blocked for Bali PMA registration. The reason given is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the record also states the moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. Here, the record’s own Bali assessment says the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest reading is therefore clean: nationally open, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali moratorium fields provided.

In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.

editorial.headline: Coconut Cooking Oil Refining, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10423 covers the further processing of crude coconut oil into cooking oil, with PMA access open nationally and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10423 is a manufacturing activity with a narrow, practical centre of gravity: it covers the further processing of crude coconut oil into coconut cooking oil. The record describes the work as refining, bleaching, and removing unwanted odours. In plain English, this is not the cultivation of coconuts and not the broad trade of edible oils; it is the industrial step that takes crude coconut oil and prepares it as cooking oil through additional processing.

That specificity matters because it tells founders what kind of business should sit under this code. A company registering this activity is positioning itself as an oil-processing operator, not merely a distributor. The record opens the activity across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not framed only for large plants or only for small producers; it can describe operations at any of the stated scales, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope of further processing crude coconut oil into cooking oil.

The national PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership value of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that is the core national reading: the activity is open, and the record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The correct way to read that is cleanly and without embellishment: nationally, KBLI 10423 is available for PMA registration up to 100% foreign ownership.

Bali does not change that into a separate percentage or a local quota in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali reason says: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest Bali-side conclusion is equally direct: the slim record does not block PMA registration in Bali for this code under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 10423 is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali record does not mark it as blocked.

data.judul: Industri Minyak Mentah Kelapa Sawit (Crude Palm Oil)
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pengolahan daging buah kelapa sawit menjadi minyak mentah/crude palm oil (CPO) yang masih perlu diolah lebih lanjut dan biasanya digunakan sebagai input dalam kegiatan lain.

persyaratan: Memiliki dokumen: a. legalitas penguasaan kebun buah kelapa sawit, berupa: 1) Sertifikat Hak Milik atau 2) legalitas pemanfaatan kebun buah kelapa sawit dengan masa penguasaan lahan minimal 25 (dua puluh lima) tahun, berupa i. Sertifikat Hak Guna Usaha ii. Sertifikat Hak Pakai atau iii.Sertifikat Hak Pengelo-laan, yang membuktikan adanya jaminan pasokan bahan baku berupa buah kelapa sawit dari sumber yang sah, dan kesesuaian luas lahan kebun dengan kemampuan pemenuhan minimal 20 (dua puluh) persen kebutuhan bahan baku berupa buah kelapa sawit atau b. Perjanjian jual beli tandan buah segar/buah kelapa sawit dengan jangka waktu kerjasama pasokan minimal 1 (satu) tahun yang dilakukan dengan pihak penjual, yaitu: 1) Petani plasma 2) Perusahaan perkebunan 3) Badan usaha tani (koperasi, kelompok tani, gabungan kelompok tani) /atau 4) perusahaan perdagangan besar hasil pertanian yang membuktikan adanya kontinuitas dan jaminan pasokan bahan baku berupa buah kelapa sawit dari sumber yang sah.

Memiliki dokumen: a. Bagi pelaku usaha dengan penguasaan kebun kelapa sawit: 1) Rencana kebutuhan bahan baku tandan buah segar/ buah kelapa sawit dalam siklus produksi 1 (satu) tahun pertama 2) Rencana pasokan pada periode usaha minimum 2 (dua) tahun setelah 1 (satu) siklus produksi 3) Rencana kebutuhan energi dan air baku dalam 1 (satu) siklus produksi atau selama lamanya 6 (enam) bulan ke depan. b. Bagi pelaku usaha dengan perjanjian jual beli tandan buah segar/buah kelapa sawit dengan jangka waktu kerjasama pasokan minimal 1 (satu) tahun: 1) Rencana pasokan bahan baku tandan buah segar/ buah kelapa sawit dalam siklus produksi 1 (satu) tahun pertama 2) Rencana kebutuhan energi dan air baku dalam 1 (satu) siklus produksi atau selama lamanya 6 (enam) bulan ke depan.

editorial.headline: Crude Palm Oil as an Industrial Input
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10431 covers the first industrial transformation of oil-palm fruit into crude palm oil, open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10431 is about the processing of oil-palm fruit flesh into crude palm oil, or CPO. The record frames this as an upstream industrial activity: the output is still crude, still requiring further processing, and usually used as an input for other activities. That distinction matters. This is not presented as a finished consumer product category, but as the production of a raw industrial oil that sits inside a wider manufacturing chain.

The code is open across every business scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration terms, that means the activity is not confined to one size of operator in the data supplied here. A small local processor and a large industrial operator may both sit within the same activity description, so long as the registered business is genuinely processing oil-palm fruit flesh into crude palm oil that remains subject to further processing.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives 100% as the maximum foreign ownership figure. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is identified as the source for that national position. There is no partial ceiling to interpret and no separate condition to infer from the slim record. On the national reading alone, this is a foreign-open industrial activity.

The Bali picture is also unusually clean. The record does include Bali’s island-wide moratorium rule, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. But this activity is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali adds a hidden percentage cap, quota, or local-partner condition; the record says no such thing. For this code, the national openness and the Bali-side status point in the same direction: foreign-owned registration is not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the facts supplied.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Crude Palm Kernel Oil as an Industrial Input
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10432 covers the first-stage processing of palm kernel seeds into CPKO, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10432 is a manufacturing activity with a narrow, industrial meaning: it covers the processing of palm kernel seeds into crude palm kernel oil, or CPKO. The record is clear that this is not a finished consumer product category. The oil produced under this activity still needs further processing and is usually used as an input in other activities. That makes the code best understood as an upstream or intermediate processing line, where the registered business is producing a crude material for later industrial use rather than presenting a final retail-ready oil.

The scale position is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators. A small producer and a larger processing facility can both sit inside the same formal activity description, provided the real activity is the processing of palm kernel seeds into crude palm kernel oil. The practical editorial point is precision: the registration should follow the actual process and output. This code is about CPKO that remains a crude input, not a broader palm-oil business, a trading activity, or a downstream product line not described in the record.

At the national level, the rules on foreign investment are clear. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership as 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to full foreign participation. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and there is no additional national condition supplied here that can be turned into a hidden obligation, licensing threshold, or capital rule. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is cited as the source for this national position.

Bali does not change that conclusion into a local prohibition on the facts given. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is also specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The honest national-versus-Bali reading is therefore clean: nationally open, up to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium assessment supplied in this record.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Crude Palm Fractionation With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10433 covers the first split of crude palm and palm-kernel oil into olein and stearin, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10433 is an industrial code for fractionating crude palm oil and crude palm-kernel oil before those materials move into later processing. The activity is not the finished-food or consumer-product end of the chain. Its core is the separation of a crude oil stream into two physical fractions: a liquid fraction, olein, and a solid fraction, stearin. The same logic is stated for crude palm oil and for crude palm-kernel oil: crude palm olein and crude palm stearin on one side, crude palm-kernel olein and crude palm-kernel stearin on the other. The record is explicit that these outputs still need further processing, which matters because it places the code in a technical, upstream industrial position rather than in a final retail category.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not written only for a single size of operator. In practical classification terms, that means the same defined activity can be registered across the scale spectrum, provided the registered business is genuinely doing the fractionation described in the scope: separating crude palm or crude palm-kernel oil into olein and stearin fractions. The editorial discipline here is important. The code is not a general palm-oil trading label, not a catch-all plantation activity, and not a finished processing claim. It is the specific industrial separation step described in the Indonesian scope.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clear. According to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record lists the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is 100%, so the record does not impose a lower foreign-stake cap for this activity at the national level. That is the first half of the founder’s reading: for foreign investment classification, this is nationally open according to the fields provided.

The Bali reading is also clear, but for a different reason. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This record, however, does not mark KBLI 10433 as blocked in Bali. For Bali, the record assigns OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, explaining it as follows: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That does not create a separate Bali foreign-ownership percentage, and it does not add a local quota or partnership condition. It simply means that, on this record, the activity is nationally open to PMA and is not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The record treats KBLI 10433 as a technical upstream fractionation activity: nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium.

The canonical pp28_sources=['10433','10490'] on 10433 therefore associates 10490 with the WRONG child code — the THIRD contaminated 'clean' control found that session (after 52101 and 46100), all on the crosswalk-metadata layer. Its per_skala (4 rows) is HEALTHY OSS-native licensing, unaffected by this crosswalk-pointer defect, and is NOT detached by this cure ('action':'metadata_only' — per_skala stays completely untouched regardless of its non-empty state). pp28_sources corrected to ['10433'] — 10490 REMOVED (it is recorded here as belonging to 10419, never re-added to 10433). status_mapping ('MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE') and intel_2026.whatChanged are left UNCHANGED by this cure: a single-element pp28_sources under a 'MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE' status_mapping is an already-precedented dataset convention (47771, 52101, 60101, 60103 all carry the same shape — pp28_sources tracks the PP28-licensing-basis pointer only, separate from the full BPS crosswalk-ancestor narrative, which lives in prose), so no inconsistency is introduced; whether the merge-aware status_mapping label itself needs re-adjudication (given the 'aggregation' this code originally cited turns out, per this same finding, to have been built on a false co-parent) is flagged here as a known follow-up, not silently left undocumented — the scope of this cure is the pp28_sources removal only, per the task that authored it. This is the FIRST use of the pp28_sources_correction compiler capability, added in this same PR (scripts/kbli_filiera/cure_canonical_collisions.py), mirroring the status_mapping_correction/whatChanged_correction pattern shipped for 47771 in PR #2761. RESIDUAL FIX (2026-07-19, M5 lane, field-vs-note contradiction closure, conductor comment on PR #2777): the 'known follow-up' flagged above ('whether the merge-aware status_mapping label itself needs re-adjudication') is now resolved — status_mapping corrected from 'MATCH_CON_AGGREGAZIONE' to 'MATCH_LANGSUNG' and whatChanged corrected to a clean 1:1 narrative, since 10490 (the co-parent this code's aggregation status depended on) belongs to 10419, not 10433: 2025-10433 is a genuine 1:1 continuation of 2020-10433 alone. pp28_sources is UNCHANGED by this residual fix (already correct at ['10433'] from #2777). aggregation_note (currently 'Dati da 10433 + 1 codici figli PP28', now stale — it describes a 2-source merge that no longer exists) is intentionally left untouched by this residual fix — cure_canonical_collisions.py's metadata_only action does not write that field; flagged here, not silently left undocumented, as a possible follow-up for a future pass.
data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial refining of crude palm oil (CPO) into refined, bleached, deodorized palm oil (RBDPO) and crude palm kernel oil into refined, bleached, deodorized palm kernel oil (RBDPKO). The output is a semi-finished product still requiring further processing before becoming consumer goods.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Pemurnian Minyak Mentah Kelapa Sawit dan Minyak Mentah Inti Kelapa Sawit (10434)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign palm oil millers or traders planning to refine crude oils into traded intermediate products; they should be aware that Bali is currently off-limits, but other Indonesian regions are fully open.

editorial.headline: Palm Oil Refining With A Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10434 covers the refining step that turns crude palm and palm-kernel oils into further-processable refined oils.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10434 is a manufacturing code for a precise industrial step: refining crude palm oil into refined bleached deodorized palm oil, and refining crude palm-kernel oil into refined bleached deodorized palm-kernel oil. The record is clear that these refined oils are still not necessarily end products; they remain materials that need further processing. In practical terms, this is the activity of improving crude palm-based oils into cleaner, more stable refined forms within the palm-oil value chain.

The code is open across the full scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not framed only as a large industrial category in the slim record. A registrant can read the scale field as deliberately broad, while still treating the underlying activity as manufacturing rather than trading, farming, or final-product retail. The business description should therefore stay close to the refining operation itself: crude palm oil or crude palm-kernel oil in, refined bleached deodorized palm or palm-kernel oil out, with further processing still expected.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the code as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, which means the national foreign-ownership ceiling should be rendered as 100%. The source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in this record adds a special national licence, minimum capital number, production threshold, or tax condition, so none should be inferred. The clean reading is that the activity is nationally open to foreign investment up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali does not change that conclusion in this record. The province-wide moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this code is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the recorded reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest Bali reading is not a hidden cap or a local quota; it is that the record treats this activity as not blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali reading is not a hidden cap or a local quota; it is that the record treats this activity as not blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Palm Oil Fractionation With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the separation of refined palm oil into olein and stearin, open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali by the record.
editorial.body:
This activity is about a precise industrial step: separating refined palm oil into its solid and liquid fractions. The record describes the solid fraction as stearin and the liquid fraction as olein, with the resulting products named as refined bleached deodorized palm olein and refined bleached deodorized palm stearin. In plain English, this is not a broad palm-oil category. It is the fractionation stage that turns refined palm oil into two defined refined outputs.

That narrowness matters. A founder reading this code should see a manufacturing activity with a clear process boundary: the separation of fractions from refined palm oil, not an open-ended permission to cover every adjacent activity in the palm-oil chain. The Indonesian scope is technical, but the commercial signal is simple enough: register it when the declared business activity is the fractionation of refined palm oil into olein and stearin as described in the record.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses. That means the classification itself is not reserved only for one business size in the slim record. A smaller operator and a large industrial registrant may both find the scale door open here, provided the registered activity remains this specific separation or fractionation activity. The editorial point is discipline: the scale permission is broad, while the activity scope stays narrow.

The foreign-ownership reading is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded at 100. Rendered plainly, the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For Bali, the record does not mark this activity as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA in Bali, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not caught by that block according to the supplied Bali reason. So the honest national-versus-Bali picture is not a hidden restriction story: on this record, it is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and Bali is not blocking it under the cited moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Palm Kernel Oil Fractionation With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the industrial split of refined palm kernel oil into olein and stearin, and the record treats it as foreign-open nationally and not moratorium-blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10436 is a focused industrial activity: the separation, or fractionation, of refined palm kernel oil into two product streams. The slim record describes the split between the solid fraction, stearin, and the liquid fraction, olein. In practical editorial terms, this is not general trading, plantation work, or a broad food-processing umbrella. It is the manufacturing activity that turns refined palm kernel oil into refined, bleached, deodorized palm kernel olein and refined, bleached, deodorized palm kernel stearin.

That narrowness matters because the activity is open across the full scale range shown in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small operator and a large industrial operator may both appear in the scale field, but the nature of the activity remains the same: fractionating refined palm kernel oil into its liquid and solid fractions. The record does not add a special threshold, local-content rule, production volume, or capital figure, so the editorial reading should stay disciplined. What it gives is the business classification, the open scales, and the investment-status signal.

Nationally, the signal is straightforward. For PMA, the status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is the cleanest national reading available from this record: foreign investment is open, and the maximum foreign stake is stated as a full 100%. The source field points to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, which is the record’s stated basis for that national PMA position. Nothing in the slim record suggests a lower national cap, a special partner requirement, or a separate numerical condition.

The Bali reading is also clean, but for a different reason: the record does not mark the activity as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false. The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, the record’s own Bali-side conclusion is that the activity is not caught by that block. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally, the activity is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record marks it as not blocked by the moratorium, because the relevant large-scale OSS risk reading is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is simple: nationally this activity is foreign-open up to 100%, and the record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial refinement of crude palm oil (CPO) into ready-to-use cooking oil. It includes purification, bleaching, deodorization, and may involve producing red palm oil or adding substances to improve quality or nutritional value.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Foreign ownership is fully allowed nationally, and in Bali the activity is not blocked by the local moratorium. However, it is classified as medium-high to high risk, meaning you will need to secure a proper industrial-zoned commercial address and be prepared for a more rigorous permitting process, including environmental and operational permits.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur aiming to establish a large-scale palm oil refinery or a branded cooking oil production facility, particularly for export or the Indonesian consumer market.

editorial.headline: Palm Oil Cooking Oil Refining, Without the Bali Dead End
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10437 covers the further processing of crude palm oil into consumer-ready cooking oil, and the record treats it as nationally open to foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10437 is not the cultivation of palm fruit or the broad trading of edible oils. On this record, its subject is the industrial further processing of crude palm oil into palm cooking oil ready for consumption. The work named in the scope is practical and technical: refining, bleaching, and removing unwanted odours from crude palm oil, so that the input becomes a finished cooking oil product. The scope also expressly includes red palm oil processing and the addition of certain substances to improve quality or added value.

That makes this a processing code with a clear manufacturing character. A founder using it is describing an operation that takes crude palm oil as a feedstock and performs the downstream steps that turn it into a consumable oil product. The record is also broad on business scale: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain terms, the activity is not confined in the record to only a small producer or only an industrial-scale plant; the scale field allows the whole ladder of registered business sizes.

The national PMA position is equally direct. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%. That is the national picture: a foreign-owned company can read this slim record as allowing full foreign participation, with the cited PMA source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no separate minimum-capital figure, licence threshold, tax rule, or operating timetable in the record, so none should be inferred from it.

The Bali reading is important because it does not create a contradiction. The record does include Bali’s moratorium rule, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. But for this code the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, the Bali blocked flag is false, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest conclusion is measured rather than dramatic: nationally, the code is open to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, this record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.
