editorial.headline: Fresh Milk and Cream, Open Nationally and Clear for Bali PMA
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10501 covers the processing of fresh liquid milk, UHT milk, and cream, with access across all business scales and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10501 is a processing code for milk in its liquid and semi-liquid form. The record defines the activity around fresh liquid milk, pasteurised milk, sterilised milk, homogenised milk, and ultra-high temperature milk, with cream-making included when it is made from fresh, pasteurised, sterilised, or homogenised liquid milk. In plain English, this is not a retail dairy label or a farm gate description. It is the industrial activity of turning milk into market-ready liquid milk and cream products.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the code can describe a small processing business as well as a larger industrial plant, provided the registered activity remains within the processing scope described above. That breadth matters because the same activity can sit at very different operational sizes: a compact local producer handling pasteurised milk is not the same business footprint as a large UHT facility, but both are within the same activity family when the substance of the work is milk and cream processing.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is 100%. There is no lower cap, shareholder formula, licence threshold, or minimum-capital figure in the record, so none should be read into the code from this editorial. The most precise conclusion is simply that the activity is nationally open to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali does not change that conclusion in this record. The province’s moratorium rule is serious: it blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this code is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The honest Bali-side reading is therefore straightforward: this activity is not recorded as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium. For founders, that is the important distinction. KBLI 10501 is nationally open, and the Bali record does not impose a moratorium block on it.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali-side reading is straightforward: this activity is not recorded as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Powdered and Condensed Milk Manufacturing, With Bali Open at Scale
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10502 covers processed milk in powder, condensed, evaporated, and solid forms, open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10502 is a manufacturing activity for milk that has been processed into shelf-stable or concentrated forms. The record describes powdered milk, condensed milk or thick creamer, evaporated milk, and milk or cream processed into solid form, whether sweetened or unsweetened. In plain English, this is not the sale of milk as a retail category, and it is not a broad food-and-beverage catch-all. Its center of gravity is the industrial processing of milk and cream into powder, condensed, evaporated, or solid products.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not written only for large plants or only for small producers. A founder reading the code should understand it as a formal manufacturing classification that can sit across the full size ladder shown in the record. What changes with a real business will be the concrete operation, capacity, and risk handling inside OSS, but those details are not supplied here; the editorial point is simply that the slim record does not reserve the activity for one scale band.

Nationally, the investment position is also clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here is 100%. The national position cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as its source. That means the national reading of the record is foreign-open, not capped below full foreign ownership. There is no separate local-shareholder condition, no minimum capital figure, and no extra numerical threshold in the record, so none should be inferred.

Bali is where many KBLI readings become less simple, but this one remains open on the facts provided. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says it is not blocked. The stated reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently, but this activity is marked outside that blocked lane because of the stated OSS risk position at Besar scale. The honest conclusion is therefore direct: for this record, a foreign-owned setup is nationally open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Ice Cream Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: A concise editorial reading of KBLI 10503: dairy-based ice cream and premix manufacturing, open across business scales and nationally available to foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10503 is about the industrial making of ice cream whose principal material is milk. The record places both finished ice cream and ice-cream premix inside the same activity, whether that premix is prepared as a powder or as a liquid. In practical terms, this is the manufacturing home for operators whose commercial product is built around dairy-based frozen dessert production, including the upstream preparation of a ready base for that production.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can accommodate anything from a small formal producer to a larger manufacturing operation. That range matters because the code is not written only for artisanal retail identity or only for industrial plants; it is broad enough to hold the business activity itself, provided the activity remains within the dairy-based ice cream and premix manufacturing scope described in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded at 100. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling stated in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no basis in this slim record to add a separate licensing threshold, capital figure, phased timeline, or special operating condition; the useful point is simpler and stronger: at the national level, the record treats this activity as open to full foreign ownership.

The Bali reading is honest but not negative. The Bali moratorium rule in the record says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its l4_bali_status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the editorial conclusion is clean: for this record, the national PMA position is open, and the Bali-side moratorium does not block registration on the information provided.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Edible Ice and Dessert Ice With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers non-dairy edible ices, from sorbet to flavored ice premix, and the record treats it as nationally open and not moratorium-blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
This KBLI activity is about edible ice whose main ingredient is not milk. In practical terms, the record points to a broad family of frozen sweet products: sorbet, es lilin, ice drop, flavored ice variants, es mambo, es puter, and flavored ice premix. The emphasis is on food-grade frozen dessert ice, not the industrial or utility side of ice. That boundary is important because the record expressly leaves out dry ice, ice cubes, and block ice.

For founders, the commercial shape is therefore quite clear. This is the registration lane for businesses making edible frozen products where flavor, format, and consumer use define the activity. It can fit a very small producer as much as a scaled manufacturer, because the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That matters: the code is not reserved only for large factories, and it is not limited to a cottage-scale interpretation. The same activity can sit across the full size range listed in the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is straightforward. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to full foreign ownership. There is no reduced foreign stake in the slim record, and no extra percentage to calculate. The only ownership number available is the national ceiling, so the responsible reading is simple: nationally, this is foreign-open up to 100%.

Bali does not add a separate foreign-ownership percentage here. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali reason says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest Bali conclusion is not a warning dressed up as nuance: on this record, a foreign-owned registration is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: The Broad Dairy Code for Butter, Yoghurt, Cheese and Fermented Milk
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10509 covers the wider dairy-processing shelf, nationally open to PMA ownership and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10509 is the classification for other dairy-product manufacturing: the processing of butter, yoghurt, cheese and curd, whey water, casein or lactose, fermented milk, whey, and milk kefir. It also reaches into the more patient end of dairy work, including cheese purification and ageing. In plain English, this is not raw milk collection and not a generic food-trading bucket. It is the manufacturing space where milk is transformed into finished or intermediate dairy products with distinct texture, acidity, fermentation, separation, or maturation.

That scope matters because the code is broad but not shapeless. A founder using it would be describing a dairy-processing activity, not simply a retail concept or a restaurant menu. The record’s examples point to production: churned, cultured, curdled, fermented, separated, refined, or aged dairy outputs. The boundaries are also visible from what the record leaves outside the group: it does not turn every frozen milk-based product or every kefir variant into this activity. The centre of gravity remains dairy processing, especially products derived from milk through fermentation, coagulation, separation, or further refinement.

On scale, the record is unusually open. It lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as scales open to the activity, so this is not reserved only for a large industrial plant. A small yoghurt producer, a medium cheese processor, or a larger dairy manufacturer can all sit inside the same formal activity description, provided the registered business activity remains within the record’s dairy-processing scope. That breadth is useful, but it also makes precision important: the registration should follow the actual manufacturing activity, not the commercial story around the brand.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership as 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali-side result is a status label: OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That means the record does not treat this activity as blocked in Bali by the island-wide moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally, this dairy-processing code is open up to full foreign ownership; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally, this dairy-processing code is open up to full foreign ownership; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Wheat and Cereal Milling Beyond the Everyday Staples
editorial.standfirst: A focused industrial code for milling wheat and other cereals into flour and pellets, open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity sits in the practical middle of Indonesia’s food-processing chain: the milling of wheat and other cereals into flour and pellets. The record names sorghum, rye, and oat as examples, and the title makes the boundary equally clear: this is not ordinary wheat-flour milling, and it does not take in rice or corn. Its commercial centre is transformation, not trading: raw cereal inputs are ground, processed, and shaped into usable industrial or food ingredients.

That makes the code relevant to operators who are building a production business around cereal processing rather than a retail food concept. The registration field is broad. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it can describe a small milling operation as well as a larger industrial facility. What matters is the activity itself: milling wheat and cereals such as sorghum, rye, and oat into flour and pellets. Anything beyond that should not be read into the code unless it appears in the underlying business scope.

At the national level, the position on foreign investment is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. In plain English, the national framework allows a foreign-owned PMA to hold the full foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here. The cited source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no smaller cap in the slim record, and there is no additional national percentage to infer. For a foreign founder reading this code at national level, the investment message is clean: the activity is open up to 100% foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also clean, but for a different reason than many low-risk activities. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This code is not marked as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest conclusion is not that Bali imposes a separate ownership cap, partnership rule, or quota. The record gives none. The conclusion is that this activity remains available for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied, with the important note that the Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a moratorium closure.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is not that Bali imposes a separate ownership cap, partnership rule, or quota.

editorial.headline: Bean-Flour Milling With a Clear National Lane
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10612 covers the milling of bean and legume flours, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10612 is a manufacturing classification for businesses that make flour from assorted beans and legume crops through a milling process. The slim record names examples such as mung bean flour, soybean flour, peanut flour, and red bean flour. The centre of the activity is not trading the beans or serving the finished food; it is the industrial act of grinding those raw materials into flour products.

The registration profile is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the classification can describe a compact producer as well as a larger milling operation. What matters editorially is the production character: a business entering this code is defining itself around the manufacture of milled bean-based flour, not around a neighbouring food category or a downstream retail use.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. With PMA status classified as TERBUKA, the foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%. That means the national record presents this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling stated in the data. The source named for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, but the practical reading should stay disciplined: the record gives openness and the ownership ceiling; it does not add a separate capital threshold, licence timeline, tax treatment, or operational permit condition.

Bali does not introduce a block here. For Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, while l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This activity is therefore not caught by that PMA block on the record provided. The honest conclusion is simple: for KBLI 10612, the national lane is foreign-open, and the Bali-side record does not mark it as blocked.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: A KBLI for Milling Root, Rhizome, and Vegetable Flours
editorial.standfirst: Code 10613 covers the industrial making of flour from tubers, rhizome plants, and vegetables, open across business scales and not marked as Bali-blocked in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10613 is a manufacturing classification for turning varied tubers, rhizome plants, and vegetables into flour through milling. The Indonesian scope names the activity plainly: making flour from cassava gaplek, sweet potato, taro, irut, ginger, temulawak, turmeric, cardamom, and vegetables. Its centre of gravity is not retail, farming, or food service; it is the processing step where plant material is milled into a flour product.

That makes the code useful for founders who need a clear industrial home for a flour-making operation built around these agricultural inputs. The record opens the activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical classification terms, that breadth matters because the code is not reserved only for large factories or only for small local producers. The same activity description can accommodate a modest milling operation and a larger industrial setup, provided the actual business remains within the recorded scope.

The national foreign-investment picture is straightforward. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership as 100%. That is the only ownership percentage in the record, and it is national. There is no separate Bali percentage, quota, partnership condition, capital threshold, or special local formula stated here. The cited PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the editorial conclusion must stay inside that boundary: nationally, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not marked as blocked for this code in the slim record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium text still matters as context because it says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. But for this record, the stated Bali-side conclusion is that the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest reading is therefore clean: KBLI 10613 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali fields do not mark it as blocked today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Premix Flour and Batter Manufacturing, Clearly Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the industrial making of mixed flours and prepared batters for breads, cakes, biscuits, pancakes, coatings, seasonings, and cereal-based dessert premixes.
editorial.body:
This activity is about the quiet infrastructure behind a great deal of everyday food production: flour that has already been mixed, seasoned, blended, or prepared so that another business can turn it into bread, cakes, biscuits, pancakes, coatings, or dessert bases. The record describes a manufacturing activity, not a cafe, bakery counter, or trading operation. Its centre of gravity is the making of mixed flour and ready batter products: flour for doughs, flour used to coat fish or chicken, seasoned flour, bakwan flour, bakso flour, cereal-based dessert premixes, and egg-free custard starch or flour. In plain English, this is where dry formulation becomes a repeatable food-manufacturing product.

That distinction matters because the code is broad enough for small producers but industrial enough for larger plants. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it can describe anything from a compact local premix operation to a larger factory supplying food-service, retail, or downstream food manufacturers. What unifies those businesses is not the size of the premises but the act of producing the prepared flour or batter itself. The finished product may support many kinds of cooking, baking, coating, or dessert preparation, but the registered activity is the manufacture of those flour mixtures and batter preparations.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. Recorded nationally as TERBUKA for PMA, this activity carries a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the slim record does not show a national foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. It also does not contain any additional licensing threshold, minimum-capital figure, tax treatment, timeline, or special approval condition, so none should be read into the code. For a foreign-owned structure, the reliable national takeaway is simple: the activity is marked open, with the maximum foreign ownership recorded as 100%, under the listed national source.

Bali does not add a separate percentage, quota, partnership rule, or local ownership condition in this record. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not blocked. The reason is stated as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not caught by that block on the information supplied. The honest editorial reading is therefore not a warning disguised as openness, but openness with proper boundaries: nationally open to PMA, recorded at a 100% ceiling, available across all listed business scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the slim record provided.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest editorial reading is therefore not a warning disguised as openness, but openness with proper boundaries.

editorial.headline: Cereal Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers ready-to-eat, instant, and hot cereal products, with all business scales open and no Bali moratorium block recorded for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10615 is a manufacturing classification for cereal foods. The record frames it around the making of ready-to-eat cereals, instant cereals, and hot cereal products, including rolled cereal, granola-style cereal, instant oatmeal, corn flakes, puffed grain, and muesli. It also includes cereal products made from soybeans and cereal-flour products made through extrusion. In plain English, this is the industrial home for businesses that turn grains, soy, or cereal flour into finished cereal foods rather than merely trading or packaging them.

The scale picture is broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the record does not reserve it for one size of company. A small producer making a focused cereal line and a larger manufacturer operating at industrial scale both sit inside the same activity description, provided the actual activity remains the manufacture of cereal foods described in the scope. That breadth matters because the code is not written as a niche craft category; it is an industrial food-processing category that can accommodate different operating scales.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The slim record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to the full stated ceiling. There is no separate minimum capital, licence timeline, tax treatment, or operational threshold in the record, so none should be assumed from this classification note alone.

The Bali picture is also clear, but it has to be stated carefully. In Bali, the activity is not recorded as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, while its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not caught by that block according to the record supplied. For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest reading is therefore not a hidden Bali percentage or a local quota; it is simply that this cereal-manufacturing activity is nationally open and is not recorded here as blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not a hidden Bali percentage or a local quota; it is that this cereal-manufacturing activity is nationally open and not recorded as blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Wheat Flour Milling With a Clean National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10616 covers wheat milling into wheat flour, open across all business scales and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10616 is narrowly and practically defined: it covers the milling of wheat that produces wheat flour. That is the centre of the code. The record does not treat it as a broad food category, a trading activity, or a catch-all for downstream processing; its scope is the grinding of wheat into flour. For founders, that narrowness matters because the registration should follow the actual productive activity, not the commercial possibilities that may sit around it.

The activity is open across the full scale ladder shown in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators in the national classification data supplied here. A smaller operator and a larger operator are both within the scale vocabulary of the record, provided the registered activity remains the milling of wheat into wheat flour. The editorial point is simple: this is a production code with a clear activity boundary and a broad scale range.

At the national level, the outlook for foreign investment is clear. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the national maximum foreign ownership value is 100%. In plain English, the record presents this activity as foreign-open at the national level, with no lower foreign-ownership ceiling stated in the supplied data. The source field for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special capital threshold, extra licence, timeline, or tax condition, so none should be read into the code from this editorial.

The Bali side is also unusually clear. The record does not mark this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the supplied moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this record says KBLI 10616 is not caught by that block. The honest national-vs-Bali picture, then, is not a contradiction: nationally foreign-open, and on this record not blocked in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally foreign-open, and on this record not blocked in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Cassava Starch Industry With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers cassava starch production, nationally open to PMA and not blocked for Bali under the record’s moratorium logic.
editorial.body:
Cassava starch is a plain industrial phrase, but this activity is more exact than it first appears. The record defines it as the making of starch from cassava, with tapioca flour and modified cassava starch named as examples. That gives the code a focused centre: not cassava trading, not a broad food catalogue, but the transformation of cassava into starch-based outputs. Its commercial identity sits in that manufacturing step, where cassava becomes a processed ingredient rather than an agricultural raw material.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the activity is not framed only for large industrial operators. A small producer, a medium processor, and a larger plant all sit inside the same scale envelope, provided the registered activity remains the making of cassava starch products described in the scope. For founders, that matters because the code does not force the business story into one size of operation; it recognises the same activity across the full scale range listed in the record.

The national investment position is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Stated simply, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling shown. There is no lower cap in the slim record, and there is no extra threshold, licence condition, timeline, tax point, or capital rule supplied here. The only national number that can be used is the 100% PMA maximum stated in the record.

The Bali reading is also clear, but for a different reason. For Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, while l4_bali_blocked remains false. The record’s reason says: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That places the activity outside the moratorium described in the record, which blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally the activity is open to PMA, and in Bali the record does not mark it as blocked. The conclusion is therefore straightforward: for this activity, the record supports a genuinely open PMA reading, with Bali not adding a separate percentage cap or quantified local restriction.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally the activity is open to PMA, and in Bali the record does not mark it as blocked.

editorial.headline: Palm Starch Manufacturing With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10622 covers palm-based starch production, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10622 is a manufacturing activity for starch made from palm-family plants. In plain English, the record points to factories or production operations that turn various palm sources into starch products, including sago starch, pearl starch, aren palm starch, and modified palm starch. Its scope is industrial and material-specific: the defining feature is not a trading channel, a food-service format, or an agricultural estate, but the making of palm-derived starch itself.

The activity is open across the business scales listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed as a narrow large-industry lane only, nor as a micro-business lane only. A registrant reading this record can see the full scale range named explicitly, while still needing to keep the activity anchored to the stated scope: palm starch production, including modified palm starch where the product remains within that description.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, so the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower ownership cap in the slim record, and no added threshold, licence, capital rule, or special condition is stated here. The honest national reading is therefore clean: for this activity code, the record presents full foreign ownership as available at the national level.

Bali does not change that into a separate percentage. The Bali-side field is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, and the record says it is not blocked: `OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium`. That sentence is the operative Bali distinction. The moratorium rule supplied here blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this record says KBLI 10622 is not caught by that block because the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. So the final reading is neither evasive nor alarmist: nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, open across all listed scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the supplied record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is clean: KBLI 10622 is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the supplied record.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it’s not blocked by the current moratorium, but it’s flagged as medium-high to high risk—meaning you can register a PMA, yet location and permits will face extra scrutiny. Always verify your intended address with a local advisor before committing.

editorial.headline: Glucose Manufacturing Is Nationally Open and Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers industrial glucose and similar sugar production, with all business scales open and full foreign ownership allowed under the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10623 is about the industrial making of glucose and closely related sugars.** The record frames it as manufacturing glucose and similar sweeteners outside the rice-and-corn category, including fructose, maltose, sucrose, glucose syrup, and comparable syrups. In practical terms, this is not a retail food activity or a general trading label; it is a production classification for businesses whose core operation is making these sugar products themselves.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification is not reserved only for large factories. A small producer and a larger industrial undertaking can both sit inside the same activity description if the registered business is genuinely making the products described in the scope. The important discipline is fit: the business should be registered here because its real activity is glucose or similar sugar manufacturing, not because the label sounds adjacent to food, commodities, or distribution.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The PMA status is marked **TERBUKA**, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. That means the national record does not impose a foreign-shareholding cap for this activity. If a foreign-owned company is being assessed at the national level, the plain reading is that the code is open to full foreign ownership, subject only to facts and rules that actually appear in the record.

Bali does not add a separate ownership percentage here. The Bali-side status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the record says it is **not blocked**. The reason is specific: **“OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.”** The moratorium rule still matters as background because Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, under the cited governor letter. But for this code, the record’s own conclusion is that the Bali moratorium does not block PMA registration today.
editorial.pullQuote: For this code, the honest reading is simple: nationally it is fully foreign-open, and Bali does not mark it as moratorium-blocked.

editorial.headline: Starch Processing with Room for Full Foreign Ownership
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10629 covers extracted and modified starch products, with all business scales open and no Bali PMA block recorded for this activity.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10629 is the industrial category for making starch and related starch products through extraction. The record frames it broadly: potato starch, bengkuang starch, temulawak starch, arrowroot starch, mango-seed starch, and modified starch all sit inside this activity. It also includes the production of inulin and gluten. In plain English, this is not a trading or packaging category; it is a manufacturing activity where raw agricultural or plant-based inputs are processed into starch-based materials and adjacent products.

That scope matters because the code is not limited to one commodity. It can fit a small producer extracting a specific local starch, a medium manufacturer making modified starch for downstream use, or a larger industrial operation working across several starch products. The scale field is unusually clear: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open. That means the record does not confine this activity to either small domestic operators or large industrial investors; it recognises the activity across the full business-size ladder.

Nationally, the investment picture is straightforward. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership field is 100%. The source given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading, then, a foreign-owned company is not being asked by this record to stop below full ownership. The correct editorial conclusion is simple: for this KBLI, the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is full ownership.

Bali does not change that conclusion into a block. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false. The reason is explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium." The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, but this activity is not marked as blocked under that rule. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a hidden contradiction: KBLI 10629 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali-side record does not mark it as blocked.

editorial.headline: Rice Milling as a Full-Scale Industrial Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10631 covers the conversion of paddy into saleable rice, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10631 is about the industrial step that turns harvested paddy into rice for sale. The slim record defines the activity as **penggilingan padi menjadi beras**, including **penyosohan beras**: the milling of paddy into rice, together with rice polishing. It also makes clear that polishing may be part of the same rice-milling business or handled as a separate polishing activity connected to rice milling. In plain English, this is not a broad food-trading category and not a general agricultural field activity. It is the processing point where paddy becomes marketable rice.

That scope matters because the record treats the activity as available across the full business-size spectrum. The scales open to it are **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar**. A small local milling operation and a larger industrial processing setup both sit within the same recorded scale range, provided the business activity being registered is still the milling of paddy into rice, including the relevant polishing activity. The editorial distinction is practical: the code follows the processing function, not the eventual buyer, channel, or commercial story around the rice.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as **TERBUKA**, with **pma_max_asing** at **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. On the national foreign-ownership point, there is no capped percentage below full foreign ownership in this slim record. A foreign investor reading only this record would therefore understand the national position as open, with the foreign-ownership ceiling stated at 100%.

The Bali layer is more nuanced, but it is not a hidden prohibition here. The record says **l4_bali_blocked** is **false** and gives the reason: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The broader moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked under that rule. The honest reading is therefore clean: KBLI 10631 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not block it under the listed moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is clean: KBLI 10631 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not block it under the listed moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Corn Shelling as a Full-Scale Processing Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10632 covers the drying, shelling, milling, and cleaning of corn, with full national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10632 is a processing code, not a trading label. The activity begins with wet corn and turns it into dried shelled corn. The record also brings the surrounding industrial work into view: milling, cleaning, and handling all parts of the corn plant within the same activity scope. In practical terms, the code describes the post-harvest step where corn is prepared into a cleaner, drier, more usable industrial form.

That scope matters because it is broad enough to cover both the central transformation and the supporting handling around it, but still specific in its object: corn. A business registering under this code is not merely identifying with agriculture in general. It is placing itself in the processing of corn after harvest, where moisture, shelling, cleaning, and milling define the work. The Indonesian scope is compact, but its commercial meaning is clear: this is a corn-processing activity built around making pipilan kering from jagung basah.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. That means the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators, nor is it limited to small production. It can describe a modest processing business as well as a larger operation, provided the registered activity remains within the recorded scope. The same code can therefore sit across the full scale ladder without needing to imply a different business activity.

The national PMA position is also clean. The record marks the code as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Stated plainly, the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Its local status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The Bali moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this record says this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. For this code, the honest reading is therefore open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the recorded moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Rice and Corn Flour With a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10633 covers the manufacture of rice flour, corn flour, and corn grits, with national foreign ownership open and no Bali PMA block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10633 is a compact but important food-processing activity: the manufacture of rice flour and corn flour, including corn grits. The record does not stretch the category into trading, farming, packaged food retail, or broader grain services. Its center is production: turning rice and corn into flour or grits as an industrial activity. That narrowness matters, because the code is not defined by a brand story or a downstream menu. It is defined by the making of these flour products.

The activity is open across the full business-size ladder in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not reserved only for one scale of operator. A small producer, a mid-sized processing venture, or a large industrial manufacturer can all sit within the same formal activity classification, provided the business being registered is actually the manufacture of rice flour, corn flour, or corn grits. For founders, this is the practical reading: the code follows the activity first, and the scale field tells you the registered size bands that the record opens.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is unusually straightforward. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For that national position, the record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the record, no special minimum-capital figure, and no extra ownership condition to add. The honest national conclusion is therefore simple: at the national level, this activity is foreign-open up to the full percentage shown in the record.

The Bali reading is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. This code, however, is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. So the careful conclusion is not that Bali has a separate foreign-ownership percentage, because the record gives no Bali-side percentage. The careful conclusion is that KBLI 10633 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and, on the Bali field supplied here, not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The careful conclusion is that KBLI 10633 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and, on the Bali field supplied here, not blocked by the Bali moratorium.

editorial.headline: Rice and Corn Starch, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of rice starch and corn starch, including modified forms, with PMA access open nationally and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10634 is a manufacturing activity with a narrow, practical scope:** the making of rice starch and corn starch, including maizena, and including modified rice and corn starch. The record does not expand this into trading, farming, distribution, or food-service activity. Its centre of gravity is production: taking rice or corn into a starch product, including a modified starch product, under the activity title *Industri Pati Beras dan Jagung*.

That clarity matters because this is not a code that belongs only to large industrial players. The scale field opens it across the full ladder recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, the activity can be registered from micro scale through large scale, so the distinction is not whether the activity exists only for one size of operator. The more important distinction is the registration and investment posture attached to the chosen setup, especially where a foreign-owned company is involved.

Nationally, the record is straightforward. PMA status is marked TERBUKA, while the foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-cap percentage in the record, and no additional national threshold, licence, timeline, or minimum-capital figure is stated here. The editorial picture should therefore stay clean: for this activity, the national PMA position is open, and the recorded ceiling is complete foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also important, but it should not be exaggerated into a separate cap or local condition. The record marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with `l4_bali_blocked` set to false. Its reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not blocked by that rule in the supplied record. So the honest reading is restrained and positive: KBLI 10634 is open nationally to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali layer shown here does not block PMA registration under the recorded moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Rice and Corn Sweeteners With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10635 covers the making of rice- and corn-based sweeteners, with all business scales open and the record marking both national PMA access and Bali registration as open.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10635 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label. Its scope is the making of sweeteners from rice and corn, with the record naming fructose, glucose, maltose, sucrose, and dextrose as examples. The useful way to read it is therefore quite concrete: this is about producing sweetening ingredients from those two agricultural bases, rather than merely distributing finished sweetener products or operating a general food business.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the classification is not reserved only for industrial-scale operators. editorial.headline: Rice and Corn Oil Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10636 covers the manufacture of oil from rice and corn, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10636 is a narrow industrial classification: the manufacture of oil from rice and corn. Its scope is not farming, trading, food retail, or a broad grain-processing label. It is the production activity itself, turning rice and corn into oil. That precision matters because the code’s strength is also its boundary: a founder using it should be describing a manufacturing operation centred on those two raw materials, not a wider packaged-food venture or a general commodities business.

The record opens this activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration language, that means the activity is not reserved in this record for only a large industrial operator, nor confined to small enterprise classifications. A micro producer, a small workshop, a mid-sized processor, and a large manufacturer all sit inside the scale range stated here, provided the registered activity remains the making of oil from rice and corn.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is the only ownership percentage in the record, and it is national, not Bali-specific. The cited source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Read plainly, this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity at national level, with no lower foreign-share cap supplied in the slim record.

The Bali side is also relatively clear, but for a different reason. The record does include Bali’s island-wide moratorium rule: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. Here, however, `l4_bali_blocked` is false and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. In other words, this record does not create a separate Bali ownership cap, partnership condition, or quota. It says the activity is nationally foreign-open, and it says Bali does not block it under the supplied moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The record says this is nationally foreign-open, and Bali does not block it under the supplied moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: The Industrial Bakery Code Behind Bread, Pastry, and Frozen Bake Goods
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10710 covers bakery manufacturing at every registered business scale, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali PMA moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10710 is the manufacturing home for bakery products, not the counter where a warm croissant is handed over.** The record places here the making of fresh, frozen, and dry bakery goods: sliced bread and rolls, pastries, cakes, pies, tarts, toast, biscuits, dry bread products, preserved pastry and cake products, sweet or salty snacks such as cookies, crackers, and pretzels, tortillas, and frozen bakery items including pancakes, waffles, and rolls. In plain English, this is the code for producing baked goods as products, whether they leave the facility fresh, shelf-stable, preserved, or frozen.

That breadth matters because the code is not confined to a boutique bakery format or a single industrial profile. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the registered operator may be a small maker or a larger food-manufacturing business, provided the declared activity is the making of bakery products described in the scope. The exclusions in the record also help define the boundary without needing to look elsewhere: this is not about making flour mixes or dough preparations, not pasta, not potato-based snacks, and not simply heating bakery products for immediate consumption. Its center of gravity is production.

Nationally, the investment picture is straightforward. The record marks KBLI 10710 as TERBUKA for PMA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national foreign-ownership ceiling in this record is 100%. There is no lower cap in the slim record, and there is no separate percentage attached to Bali. The clean national reading is therefore that foreign ownership is open up to the full stated ceiling.

The Bali reading is also unusually clean. The province-wide moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this code is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record’s reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". So the honest conclusion is not a hidden Bali cap or a special local percentage. On this slim record, KBLI 10710 is nationally open to foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium.

editorial.headline: Crystal Sugar Manufacturing, Read Through the Bali Lens
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of granulated sugar from cane, beet, or other materials, with national PMA openness and a Bali record not blocked by the island moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10721 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label or a broad food category. Its recorded scope is the making of sugar in crystal or granulated form, using sugarcane, beet, or other materials as the main input. The practical centre of gravity is therefore production: taking an agricultural or other qualifying raw material and turning it into the familiar crystalline sugar described by the Indonesian title, *Industri Gula Pasir*.

The scale profile is unusually straightforward in the slim record. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification is not reserved only for heavy industrial players. A small producer, a mid-sized processor, or a large manufacturing operation can all sit within the registered scale range, provided the activity being registered remains the manufacturing of crystal sugar described in the scope. The record does not add a separate licence, threshold, land rule, or capital number, so none should be read into the classification itself.

Nationally, the PMA picture is also direct. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown here is 100%. That does not make the activity automatically simple in every local context, but it does mean the national investment list in this record does not impose a lower foreign-share cap for this activity.

The Bali reading is the important nuance. The record does not mark KBLI 10721 as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. That matters because the moratorium rule in the same record says Bali province blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. Here, the Bali-side conclusion is not a separate percentage, quota, or partnership condition. It is simply that the record does not block this activity under that moratorium logic. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest reading is therefore clean: nationally open up to 100%, and in Bali not blocked by the recorded moratorium rule.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers making pure palm sugar from the sap of palm trees like sugar palm, coconut, or sugarcane—whether as molded blocks, granules, or syrup. It’s traditional, small-scale food processing without refinement or blending.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible. So despite being legally open on paper, a foreign-owned setup can’t get the needed license here right now.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Gula Merah (10722)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Indonesian-owned palm-sugar producers. The activity is reserved to cooperatives and Indonesian MSMEs by Perpres 49/2021, so foreign shareholding is 0% and a PT PMA cannot register it anywhere in Indonesia — the reservation is national, and moving the company to another province does not lift it. A foreign buyer can contract with a domestic producer for supply or private-label output; it cannot own the production company.

editorial.headline: Brown Sugar Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10722 covers pure brown sugar production from cane or palm sap. It is allocated to Koperasi and UMKM, so foreign ownership is 0% — and Bali's moratorium not catching the activity does not create a route for a PT PMA.
editorial.body:
KBLI 10722 is a manufacturing code for **pure brown sugar**. The record defines it through the making of gula merah from sap as the raw material, whether the sap comes from sugarcane or from palm plants such as aren, coconut, and similar sources. The finished product can take several forms: moulded blocks, powder or granules, or liquid sugar. That makes the code less about retailing a sweetener and more about the production activity itself: transforming nira into a brown sugar product that remains within this defined manufacturing scope.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** operators, so it can describe a small producer formalising a traditional process as well as a larger industrial operation. The important point is that the code is organised around the activity and its raw material, not around a particular brand position, distribution model, or market segment. A business registering under this code should therefore be able to connect its declared operation back to the making of pure brown sugar from cane or palm sap, in one of the product forms named in the scope.

Nationally, the position is closed to foreign ownership. The record allocates this bidang usaha to Koperasi and UMKM under Perpres 10/2021 as amended by 49/2021 (Lampiran II, the *dialokasikan* column), which sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 0%. A PT PMA cannot hold this activity anywhere in Indonesia, at any business scale.

Bali does not add a second restriction here, and that is worth stating plainly because it is easy to misread as good news. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali, and the reason it gives is precise: OSS risk at the large-business scale is medium-high or high — so the province's moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk activities does not catch it. That is true, and it changes nothing for a foreign investor: the national allocation already closes the activity to a PT PMA everywhere, so there is no Bali route left to unblock.
editorial.pullQuote: The national allocation to Koperasi and UMKM closes this activity to a PT PMA; Bali's moratorium not catching it changes nothing.
