editorial.headline: Tire Cord Fabric Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 13994 covers tire fabric made from high-strength synthetic yarns, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the supplied record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 13994 is a narrow industrial classification with a very specific material logic: it covers the manufacturing of tire fabric from high-strength synthetic yarns. The record names nylon tire fabric and polyester tire fabric as examples, which makes the activity closer to technical textile production than to general clothmaking. Its subject is not finished tires, retail distribution, or broad textile trading; it is the production of the reinforced fabric layer used in tire construction, where strength, consistency, and industrial processing matter.

For founders, the practical point is that this code is open across every business scale listed in the record: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar**. That breadth matters because the same activity can describe a small producer, a mid-sized technical textile workshop, or a large industrial plant, as long as the registered activity remains within the stated scope. The classification is therefore not limited to a single operational size. It gives room for registration at the scale that matches the actual manufacturing setup, while keeping the description anchored to tire fabric made from synthetic high-strength yarn.

The national PMA picture is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown here is full foreign ownership. That does not create any extra licence, timeline, capital rule, or technical approval in this editorial; none is stated in the supplied record. It simply means that, for the national foreign-investment field provided, this manufacturing activity is not shown as closed or capped below full ownership.

The Bali reading is also important, because many activities that look nationally open can face a provincial moratorium issue. Here, however, the supplied Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and `l4_bali_blocked` is **false**. The reason is stated as: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not marked as blocked under that rule. editorial.headline: Kapok Processing, Nationally Open but Stopped in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 13995 covers kapok processing: open across business scales nationally, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 13995 is a narrow industrial activity: the processing of kapok. The slim record gives no wider commodity chain, no downstream product family, and no special operating condition beyond that scope. Its useful precision is exactly there. This is not a general textile category or a catch-all agricultural code; it is the industrial handling and processing of kapok as an activity in its own right. For founders, that matters because the code should be read from the scope outward, not from assumptions about what kapok might later become.

On the national investment reading, the code is marked **TERBUKA**. The foreign-ownership ceiling given in the record is **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. The scale field is also broad: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar** are all listed as open. Taken only at national level, the classification therefore presents as a fully foreign-open activity, available across the full scale range recorded here. Nothing in the slim record adds a special national cap below 100%, a reserved scale, or a separate sector condition.

The Bali position is different, and it is the decisive point for a PMA setup on the island. The record marks this activity as **l4_bali_blocked: true** with the status **Blocked (risk class)**. Its stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record is broader still: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” That means the honest reading is not that Bali applies a lower percentage, a partnership condition, or a local quota. The record gives no Bali-side ownership percentage at all. It says the activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali because of the risk-class moratorium.

So the practical editorial conclusion is simple but important: nationally, KBLI 13995 is open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity today under the record supplied. This is exactly the kind of code where the national investment table alone would be misleading if read without the Bali layer. The activity itself is modest and specific, but the registration outcome turns on geography: Indonesia-level openness does not override the Bali moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 13995 is open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, the record says it is blocked for PMA registration.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This group covers the manufacture of tulle, embroidered fabrics, vitrage and window furnishings made from lace, as well as other net fabrics. The manufacture of fishing nets is classified under group 13942.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is NOT blocked by the 13 May 2026 moratorium — its OSS risk class at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale is medium-high or high, which the moratorium leaves open. A PT PMA can pursue this code in Bali, subject to the standard licensing for its risk class.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kain Tule, Kain Jaring, dan Kain Bordir (13996)? Here is the honest national-vs-Bali picture before you plan a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who can meet the higher-risk licensing requirements — one of the doors that stays open in Bali.

editorial.headline: Tulle, Lace and Net Fabric Manufacturing Under KBLI 13996
editorial.standfirst: A textile-manufacturing code for tulle, embroidery, lace-window fabrics and other net fabrics, open nationally to all business scales and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 13996 is a manufacturing code for a precise corner of the textile industry: the making of tulle fabric, embroidered fabric, vitrage and window accessories using lace fabric, and other net fabrics. Its scope is not a retail category, a garment label, or a general textile-trading description. It is concerned with production: the industrial act of making these fabrics and related window-fabric materials.

That matters because the activity sits where design, material processing and textile output meet. Tulle and lace-based fabrics can be delicate, decorative and technically specific, but the KBLI record keeps the definition sober: this is about the manufacture of those fabric types, including embroidered cloth and net fabrics. The code therefore gives founders a relatively clean classification when the business substance is the making of these materials rather than the sale, installation or downstream use of them.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar operators, so the classification can fit a small production business as well as a larger manufacturing setup. The important point is not the aesthetic character of the product, but the registered activity: if the business is manufacturing the covered fabric types, this code is built to carry that activity across the full scale range listed in the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is also clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a recorded maximum foreign ownership of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate ownership percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali-side question is whether the moratorium blocks PMA registration. Here, the record says it does not: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali reason is “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters as background because Bali blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record marks KBLI 13996 as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked. The honest conclusion is therefore direct: nationally open, fully foreign-open on the recorded ceiling, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the supplied Bali status.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is direct: nationally open, fully foreign-open on the recorded ceiling, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: The Open Field of Miscellaneous Textile Manufacturing
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 13999 covers textile manufacturing that sits outside named categories, with national foreign ownership open and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 13999 is the classification for textile manufacturing that the record treats as residual but not minor. Its Indonesian scope covers the making of textile products not already captured elsewhere: rubber thread, metal thread, shoelaces, decorative ornaments such as braids, tassels and pompons, and badges. In practical terms, this is the code for a producer whose work is still textile manufacturing, but whose output does not fit a narrower named activity in the record.

That residual character matters. This is not a trading label, a design service, or a general fashion business in the slim record; it is about making physical textile items. The examples are small in format but specific in production logic: threads, cords, shoe fastenings, trims, ornaments and badges. A founder using this classification would need the registered activity to match that manufacturing scope, because the code’s own description is the only ground available here.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so it is not framed as a classification reserved only for one size of operator. A small workshop making shoelaces or decorative textile ornaments and a larger manufacturer producing the same type of listed goods both sit within the scale range stated in the record. What the record does not do is add thresholds, investment figures, licensing steps or production-capacity tests, so none should be read into the code from outside.

The ownership and Bali reading are unusually clean. Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali also does not close it in this record: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not caught by that block on the record provided. The honest conclusion is therefore simple: for this code, the national foreign-ownership position is open, and the Bali moratorium field does not block PMA registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup
- kegiatan pembuatan pakaian jadi (konfeksi) dari tekstil/kain (tenun, rajutan, atau nirtenun) dengan cara memotong dan menjahit sehingga siap pakai, seperti kemeja, celana, kebaya, blus, rok, pakaian bayi, pakaian tari, gaun tidur, gaun ganti, piyama, dan pakaian olahraga, termasuk juga usaha pembuatan pakaian jadi sekali pakai dari tekstil dan bagian dari bra, seperti tali dan mangkok bra (cup bra);
- kegiatan pembuatan pakaian jadi (konfeksi) dari kain bordir dan kain perca.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegaitan pembuatan pakaian untuk hewan (lihat kelompok 15122).

editorial.headline: Textile Garment Manufacturing, From Cut Cloth to Ready-to-Wear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 14111 covers textile-based ready-made clothing production, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record provided.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14111 is the industrial home for making ready-to-wear garments from textile fabric. The record describes a practical manufacturing activity: cloth is cut and sewn until it becomes clothing ready for use. Its examples are broad but still tightly tied to textile konfeksi: shirts, trousers, kebaya, blouses, skirts, baby clothing, dance clothing, nightgowns, dressing gowns, pyjamas, and sportswear. It also includes disposable ready-made garments made from textiles, as well as textile parts of bras, including straps and cups.

The scope is not limited to plain fabric. It also reaches garments made from embroidered cloth and patchwork fabric, which matters because the defining activity is still the textile-garment process: turning woven, knitted, or non-woven fabric into wearable apparel through cutting and sewing. This is manufacturing, not retail branding in disguise. A company registering this activity should be describing an operation that produces finished textile clothing, whether the output is everyday apparel, ceremonial clothing, sportswear, sleepwear, or specific textile components identified in the record.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity can describe anything from a very small konfeksi workshop to a larger garment manufacturing operation, provided the registered business actually matches the production scope. The scale choice is not cosmetic: it should follow the real size and operating profile of the business. But the record itself does not narrow this KBLI to one business size. It places the activity across the full scale ladder named in the data.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For Bali, the same record does not create a separate foreign-ownership percentage, cap, quota, or partnership condition. It marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest reading is straightforward: nationally open, up to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.

editorial.headline: Leather and Imitation-Leather Garments, Ready to Wear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 14112 covers cut-and-sewn apparel from leather or imitation leather, nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14112 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label. Its center of gravity is the making of ready-to-wear garments from leather or imitation leather: material is cut, stitched, and finished into clothing that can be worn as a completed product. The record names jackets, coats, vests, trousers, skirts, and sportswear, and it also brings in leather clothing accessories such as a welder’s leather apron. That gives the code a clear industrial character: it is about confection-style garment production using leather or leather substitute as the principal material.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses, so it can describe anything from a small garment workshop to a larger manufacturing operation, provided the activity remains within the stated scope. The common thread is not the size of the operator but the nature of the work: cutting and sewing leather or imitation leather into finished apparel and related clothing equipment. A founder registering this code should therefore read it through the production process first, and only then through the commercial model around it.

Nationally, the investment position is clear. The slim record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, this record treats the activity as open nationally to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. There is no lower cap in the data, and no separate threshold, permit, minimum capital figure, or timeline stated here. The responsible reading is narrow but useful: for the national PMA question, the record says open, with a 100% ceiling.

The Bali side is also explicit, and it matters because Bali applies a moratorium rule that can block PMA for certain low-risk and medium-low-risk KBLI. For this activity, however, the record does not mark a Bali block. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is stated directly: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That means the honest national-versus-Bali picture is not a hidden contradiction. On this record, the activity is nationally open to PMA, and Bali’s moratorium does not block it.
editorial.pullQuote: On this record, the activity is nationally open to PMA, and Bali’s moratorium does not block it.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the custom tailoring and making of garments (not factory-made clothing) for individual clients, including cutting and sewing items such as suits, jackets, pants, kebaya, shirts, and dancewear. It includes both home-based tailors and boutique or atelier operations, but excludes garment repair services.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open for foreign-owned (PMA) companies. However, in Bali it is currently blocked for PMA registration because it falls under a low/medium-low risk class that is subject to a local moratorium (regulation 13 May 2026), meaning a foreign PT PMA cannot obtain this business activity in Bali.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Penjahitan dan Pembuatan (Bukan Konfeksi) Pakaian Sesuai Pesanan/Kustomisasi (14120)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who specialize in bespoke tailoring, custom-made clothing design, or high-end boutique apparel services.

editorial.headline: Custom Tailoring Is Nationally Open, But PMA Is Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A made-to-order clothing activity that spans home tailors and boutique studios is nationally open to foreign capital, yet Bali blocks PMA registration under its risk moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14120 is the code for made-to-order clothing work: cutting and sewing garments to a customer’s specification until they are ready to wear. The record is clear that this is not mass confection production. It is the craft and service side of apparel, covering custom pieces such as coats, suits, ensembles, jackets, trousers, skirts, baby clothing, sportswear, pyjamas, nightgowns, kebaya, shirts, and dance costumes, including the making of parts of those items. Its natural operators are the businesses that work directly from an order: home tailors, tailoring studios, and boutique-style makers serving the general public.

That scope matters because it places the activity in a practical, human-scale category, even though the record opens it across every business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small home-based tailor and a larger custom apparel operation can both sit inside the same activity description, provided the activity remains made-to-order and custom sewing rather than general ready-made clothing production. The centre of gravity is not retail display or industrial volume; it is the transformation of a client’s requested garment into a finished wearable item.

Nationally, the investment picture looks simple. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the national record treats this activity as open to PMA, with the foreign-ownership ceiling rendered as 100%. Nothing in the slim record adds a separate licence condition, capital threshold, operating timeline, or tax rule, so none should be inferred. The national signal is openness, and the recorded scale coverage is broad.

Bali is where the answer changes. The record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the status Blocked (risk class). Its reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanent, with the source listed as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest reading is this: although KBLI 14120 is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan perlengkapan pakaian jadi dari tekstil/kain(kain tenun, rajut, maupun nirtenun) dengan cara memotong dan menjahit sehingga siap pakai, seperti topi, peci, ikat kepala, dasi, sarung, sarung tangan, mukena, selendang, kerudung, ikat pinggang, syal, bando, dasi tuksedo, dan jaring rambut. termasuk pembuatan alas kaki tanpa pengaplikasian sol, seperti sandal kamar/slippers dan bagian-bagian dari produk yang disebutkan sebelumnya. Kelompok ini juga mencakup kegiatan pembuatan topi dari anyaman dan pembuatan perlengkapan pakaian jadi dari kain perca dan bordir.

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices
moratorium.virtual_office: requested in letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP; application not confirmed

l4_bali.rule: per-scala-Besar (OSS risk at scale Besar; PMA is Besar by law)

editorial.headline: Textile Accessories Manufacturing With Room for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A manufacturing code for sewn textile accessories, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity is about making finished clothing accessories from textile or fabric, not about general garment production in the broadest sense. The record describes a workshop or factory that cuts and sews woven, knitted, or nonwoven material into ready-to-use accessory products. Its examples are practical and specific: hats, peci, head coverings, ties, sarongs, gloves, mukena, shawls, kerudung, belts, scarves, hair bands, tuxedo ties, and hair nets. The scope also reaches modest textile footwear without an applied sole, such as bedroom slippers, together with parts of the products named in the record.

The texture of the category matters. It covers accessories made from fabric remnants and embroidery, as well as woven hats, so the activity can fit both small craft-led production and more formal industrial manufacturing. The defining idea is the transformation of textile material into finished wearable accessories through cutting and sewing, with the finished item ready for use. That makes the code relevant to businesses whose core output is accessory manufacturing rather than retailing, importing, branding, or merely trading someone else’s stock.

On scale, the record is unusually broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open to this activity. A founder reading this should treat scale as part of the registration picture, not as a decorative label. The same KBLI can be used by a micro-scale producer making embroidered accessories and by a larger manufacturer producing textile accessories at industrial scale, provided the actual business activity remains inside the recorded scope.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, meaning the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100% at the national level. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali-side status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium text in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not blocked under the record supplied here. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open, fully open to foreign ownership as recorded, and not presently blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium logic stated in the record.

editorial.headline: Leather Accessory Making, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 14132 covers cut-and-sewn leather or imitation-leather accessories, open across every business scale and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14132 is a manufacturing code for finished clothing accessories made from leather or imitation leather. Its scope is practical and workshop-based: the activity is the cutting and sewing of materials into ready-to-use accessories, including hats, gloves, belts, headbands, hairnets, furred-leather head coverings, and parts of those products. The emphasis is not on raw leather processing or general apparel; it is on the making of accessory items that are already shaped, stitched, and prepared for use.

That makes the code relevant for businesses whose core production sits in the accessory layer of fashion and personal goods. A founder registering under this activity should be able to recognise the work in the verbs of the scope: cutting, sewing, and finishing leather or imitation-leather items into usable products. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it can describe anything from a small specialised maker to a larger manufacturing operation, provided the registered activity remains within the stated accessory scope.

The national PMA position is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. In plain English, the national classification does not itself impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The source named in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the relevant number is straightforward: 100% is the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here.

The Bali reading is also clean, and it matters because Bali applies a province-level moratorium rule to PMA registration for low and medium-low risk KBLI. For this code, however, the record does not mark a block. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. That means the honest conclusion is not a hidden Bali prohibition, nor a separate Bali percentage. Based on this record, KBLI 14132 is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium for PMA registration today.
editorial.pullQuote: Based on this record, KBLI 14132 is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium for PMA registration today.

editorial.headline: KBLI 14200: Finished Goods from Fur-Bearing Leather
editorial.standfirst: A narrow manufacturing code for finished fur-bearing leather goods, nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14200 is a manufacturing activity for finished goods made from fur-bearing leather. The record points to a concrete, material-led scope: ready-made clothing and clothing accessories such as fur coats; assembled fur-bearing leather forms such as dropped fur, plates, mats, doormats, and strips; and other finished articles including rugs, unfilled pouffes, and industrial glossy cloth. Its center of gravity is not trading, farming, or raw material production. It is the making of finished articles after the material has already become fur-bearing leather.

That distinction matters because the record also draws the edges of the activity. It excludes raw fur-bearing skin production, raw leather and hide production, imitation fur made through weaving or knitting, fur hats, tanning and dyeing of fur-bearing leather, and boots or shoes with fur-containing parts. Read plainly, this is a code for businesses whose output is a finished fur-bearing leather product or assembly, not the upstream capture of the skin, the chemical finishing stage, or footwear and headwear activities that sit outside this record’s scope.

On scale, the record is unusually broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open. That means the activity is not framed here as belonging only to industrial-scale operators; it can cover a small workshop making specific finished articles as well as a larger manufacturer producing fur-bearing leather assemblies or goods. The same scope still governs each scale. A business should be able to point to the finished article it makes and show that the activity remains within the material and product boundary described by the record.

The national-vs-Bali picture is clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate foreign-ownership cap in this record. Its Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest reading is that this activity is nationally foreign-open, and the Bali moratorium record does not block it for PMA registration today. The caveat is not a hidden Bali percentage or partnership condition; it is simply the record’s own risk-based note.
editorial.pullQuote: So the honest reading is that this activity is nationally foreign-open, and the Bali moratorium record does not block it for PMA registration today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Knitted Apparel Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity is for making finished garments and accessories from knitted or crocheted materials, open across business scales and not marked as blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the industrial making of ready-to-wear clothing and related accessories from knitted or crocheted materials. In plain English, it is about turning knit or crochet fabric into finished apparel: sweaters, cardigans, jerseys, shirts, T-shirts, blouses, vests, coats, sleepwear, underwear, baby clothing, professional or individual-use sports clothing, sportswear, and swimwear. It also extends to similar clothing accessories made by knitting or crochet, including hats and gloves. The record draws one boundary clearly: sock manufacturing is outside this activity.

That scope matters because this is not framed as retail, branding, or design consultancy. It is a production activity. The common thread is the material method and the finished-garment outcome: clothing and clothing accessories made from knitted or crocheted inputs. A founder choosing this activity is therefore describing a manufacturing operation, whether the output is everyday apparel, professional-use sports garments, babywear, underwear, or knitted accessories. The wording is broad enough to hold a wide apparel mix, but it remains disciplined around knitted and crocheted finished goods.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so the classification can fit anything from a very small production setup to a large-scale manufacturing operation. Nationally, the foreign-investment position is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. That means the national record treats it as open to full foreign ownership. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is identified as the source for that national position.

The Bali reading does not add a hidden ownership cap or a local percentage rule. According to the record, l4_bali_blocked is false, while the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium text in the record says Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked here. So the honest conclusion is clean: on this record, a foreign-owned company can use this activity nationally, and it is not currently marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The Bali reading does not add a hidden ownership cap or a local percentage rule.

editorial.headline: Hosiery Manufacturing Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 14302 covers knitted and crocheted hosiery, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 14302 is a manufacturing code for hosiery made by knitting or crochet. In practical terms, the record describes the production of socks, tights, stockings, pantyhose, medical stockings, other medical hosiery, and knitted or crocheted footwear without soles. Its centre of gravity is not fashion retail, distribution, or medical services; it is the making of legwear and foot-covering products where the textile process is knitted or crocheted.

The scale position is broad. The slim record opens the activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scale operators, so the code is not framed only for industrial-scale factories or only for small workshops. A founder reading it should treat the scope as a production activity that can sit across the registered business scales named in the record, provided the actual business remains inside the described manufacturing field: hosiery, medical hosiery, and knitted or crocheted soleless footwear.

Nationally, the investment signal is clear. The record marks the PMA status as **TERBUKA** and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. That means the national field is open to foreign ownership up to the full percentage stated in the record. There is no smaller foreign cap in the slim record, and there is no extra capital threshold, licence condition, tax rule, or timeline stated here to add to the analysis.

Bali does not change that picture into a separate percentage. The Bali-side status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, with `l4_bali_blocked` marked false. The reason given is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this code is not marked as blocked. The honest reading is therefore simple: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and on the Bali layer the record does not show a moratorium block for PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and on the Bali layer the record does not show a moratorium block for PMA registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the preservation of raw animal hides and skins through methods like drying, salting, or pickling. It applies to large animal skins (cow, buffalo), small animal skins (sheep, goat), reptile skins (crocodile, snake, monitor lizard), fish skins (stingray, shark, snapper, eel), and other animal hides.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.

editorial.headline: Preserving Hides Before the Leather Trade Begins
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15111 covers the preservation of animal skins by drying, salting, or pickling, and is nationally open to foreign ownership across all listed business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15111 is a narrow but consequential industrial activity: the preservation of hides and skins before they move further into processing or trade. The record defines the work in practical terms. It covers preservation by drying, salting, or acid pickling, and it spans a wide range of raw animal skins, including large animals such as cattle and buffalo, smaller animals such as sheep and goats, reptiles such as crocodile, snake, and monitor lizard, fish such as stingray, shark, snapper, and eel, and other animal skins. In plain English, this is not the making of finished leather goods. It is the stabilising stage that keeps raw skins from deteriorating.

That scope matters because it gives the code its shape. A founder registering this activity is describing a preservation operation: receiving animal skins and applying one of the stated preservation methods so the material can remain usable. The record does not add a location rule, a production threshold, or a technical licence condition, so none should be read into it. What can be said is simpler and stronger: the activity is open in the record to Micro, Small, Medium, and Large scales, meaning the classification is not confined to a single business size in the data provided.

The national foreign-investment position is also clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. Rendered as an ownership ceiling, that is 100% foreign ownership at the national level, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company assessing the code nationally, the signal is therefore direct: the slim record treats this activity as foreign-open, not capped below full ownership.

Bali is not blocked on the facts supplied here, but the reason should be stated carefully. The record’s Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. Its explanation is that OSS risk at Large scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. This activity, on the supplied record, is therefore not one of the blocked Bali cases. The honest conclusion is clean: nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali by this record.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the tanning of animal hides and skins—after pre-tanning—using synthetic agents (like chromium) or vegetable-based methods to produce finished leathers such as wet blue, crust, suede, patent leather, laminated leather, and specialty skins like chamois or hair-on hides.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open (100% foreign ownership). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.

editorial.headline: Leather Tanning With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15112 covers the tanning of pre-tanned hides into finished and semi-finished leathers, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15112 is about the industrial transformation of leather after it has already passed through pre-tanning. The record describes tanning carried out with synthetic materials, including chromium, or with vegetable materials, turning the material into tanned leather. Its scope is not a retail category or a broad fashion trade description; it is the production activity that changes prepared hides into recognised leather outputs.

The examples in the record give the practical shape of the activity: wet blue, wet white, crust, sole leather, vache raam, box leather, velvet-like leather, glace leather, decorative leather, furred leather, laminated leather, patent leather, jacket leather, glove leather, and chamois. In plain English, this is the workshop or factory activity behind leather as an industrial input and finished material, where the defining act is the tanning process itself rather than the later sale or assembly of leather goods.

On business scale, the record is broad. KBLI 15112 is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not confined in the record to either small craft production or large industrial operation. A founder reading it should see a scale ladder that spans the full set listed in the data, while still keeping the activity anchored to the same core function: tanning pre-tanned leather into the forms named in the scope.

The national investment picture is also direct. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For Bali, the honest point is that the record does not mark this code as blocked: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium text in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently; this record places KBLI 15112 outside that block on the stated Bali reasoning.
editorial.pullQuote: The record’s practical message is that leather tanning under KBLI 15112 is nationally open to PMA and not marked as blocked by Bali’s moratorium.

editorial.headline: Dyeing Fur-Bearing Leather for Finished Goods
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15113 covers the colouring of fur-bearing leather used in finished leather goods, open across all business scales and nationally open to PMA ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15113 is a narrow, production-facing activity: the colouring or dyeing of fur-bearing leather that will be used in finished leather goods. Its centre of gravity is not general leather trading, not broad garment manufacturing, and not a catch-all craft category. The record points to a specific treatment step applied to a particular material before it appears in a finished leather product. In plain English, this is the business of giving colour to leather that retains a furry or hair-on surface, where that material is destined for finished leather goods.

That specificity matters because the code is open across the full registered scale spectrum in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small workshop may understand the activity as a finishing process inside a compact production chain; a larger operator may treat it as one stage in an industrial leather-goods supply operation. The record does not impose a narrower scale gate. It simply says that the activity can sit at any of those four scales, so the registration question is less about whether the code belongs only to one class of business size and more about whether the declared activity is truly the colouring of fur-bearing leather for finished leather goods.

The national PMA position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown here is 100%, not a partial cap. The source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and there is no additional national threshold, licence condition, capital figure, or timeline in the slim record. A careful reading should therefore stay disciplined: nationally, the code is foreign-open according to the fields provided, and the only ownership number available is the national 100% ceiling.

Bali does not change that into a hidden percentage or a separate foreign-share formula. For Bali, the status remains OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, while l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is exact and practical: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, but this record’s own Bali-side conclusion is that KBLI 15113 is not blocked by that rule. So the honest national-versus-Bali picture is straightforward: nationally open to PMA at 100%, and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium logic recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity encompasses the production of composition leather by recycling animal leather scraps or shreds and bonding them back together. Imitation leather made with textile as the primary material is classified under group 13992, while imitation leather based on rubber falls under sub-class 2219 and plastic-based imitation leather falls under sub-class 2229.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is NOT blocked by the 13 May 2026 moratorium — its OSS risk class at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale is medium-high or high, which the moratorium leaves open. A PT PMA can pursue this code in Bali, subject to the standard licensing for its risk class.

editorial.headline: Composition Leather, Read as Manufacturing Rather Than Imitation
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15114 covers bonded composition leather made from animal-leather fragments, open nationally to PMA ownership and not blocked for Bali registration in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15114 is a narrow manufacturing classification: the making of composition leather from pieces or crumbs of animal leather that are bonded back together. The important word is **composition**. This is not a general label for every material that looks like leather. The record draws the activity around animal-leather remnants and the industrial process of reconstituting them into a usable leather-based material.

That boundary matters because the classification is material-led. A founder using this code should be describing an operation whose main input is animal-leather offcut, fragment, or remnant, and whose output is composition leather. The slim record separates that from imitation leather whose main material is textile, rubber, or plastic. In plain English, this is a manufacturing code for bonded leather composition, not a catch-all for synthetic leather goods or downstream fashion production.

The registration profile is broad on business scale. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scale operators, so it is not reserved only for large factories. At the national PMA level, the code is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the stated PMA source. That means the national reading is clean: the record does not place a reduced foreign-share cap on this activity.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. The record includes the province-wide moratorium rule: Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this activity is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason is explicit: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali has a separate ownership cap, quota, or local-partner condition. The record says the national PMA ceiling is 100%, and for Bali it says this code is not blocked by the moratorium because the relevant risk status sits above the blocked Low and Medium-Low band.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is not that Bali has a separate ownership cap, quota, or local-partner condition.

data.judul: Industri Koper, Tas Tangan, dan Sejenisnya
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan tas koper, tas tangan, ransel dan lain-lain dari kulit, kulit komposisi atau bahan lain dengan menggunakan teknologi yang sama yang digunakan pada kulit, termasuk tas untuk membawa hewan/pet carrier. Kelompok ini juga mencakup pembuatan tali jam yang bukan metalik dan pembuatan tali sepatu dari kulit serta barang lainnya seperti dompet, kotak rias, sarung senjata, dan tempat kaca mata.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup pembuatan keranjang, wadah, tas dari anyaman (bambu, rotan, jerami, jerami kertas, plastik, dan sebagainya), lihat kelompok 16291 dan 16292.

editorial.headline: Leather-Technology Bags, Travel Goods, and Everyday Carriers
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15121 covers the making of luggage, handbags, backpacks, pet carriers, straps, wallets, and related goods using leather-type production methods.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15121 is a manufacturing activity, not a retail label or a fashion concept. Its centre of gravity is the making of luggage, handbags, backpacks, and similar carriers from leather, composition leather, or other materials when the production technology follows the methods used for leather. The record also brings pet carriers into the same industrial frame, which matters because the classification is shaped by how the object is made, not only by how it is marketed.

The scope then widens into the small but commercially important accessories around that same production logic: non-metal watch straps, leather shoelaces, wallets, cosmetic cases, weapon cases, eyeglass cases, and other comparable goods. Read carefully, this is a code for producers of finished personal and travel goods whose material handling, cutting, stitching, assembly, and finishing belong to the leather-goods manufacturing family. It is broad enough for a serious workshop, a scaled factory, or a specialized line of compact accessories, but it remains anchored to making the goods themselves.

The registration picture is unusually straightforward in the record. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the size of the operation does not narrow the listed scale access. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the record describes this activity as nationally open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling; there is no lower percentage, threshold, or extra capital condition in the record to add.

The Bali reading is also clean. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis, but this record is not blocked for Bali. For Bali, the record lists the status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; its stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a hidden contradiction: nationally open, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the information given here.

editorial.headline: Animal Saddlery And Harness Manufacturing, Read Without Drama
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of animal saddles, harnesses, collars, bags, shoes, clothing, and related goods from leather or other materials.
editorial.body:
This code is for a practical manufacturing activity: making goods for animals from leather or other materials. The record is broad. It includes animal collars, harnesses, saddles, muzzles, whips, animal shoes, animal bags, and clothing for animals. The final word in the scope is “Seluruh”, so the activity should be read as covering the full manufacturing scope described there, not only a luxury or equestrian niche.

For founders, the useful point is that this is not a service label or a retail description. It is an industrial activity: the making of physical animal-use goods. A business using this classification would be registering the production side of those items, whether the output is a harness, a saddle, a pet bag, a muzzle, or clothing made for animals. The material base is also deliberately wide: leather is named, but the scope also allows other materials. That makes the classification more about the object and its use than about a single material tradition.

The scale picture is unusually clean. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, it is available across the full business-size spectrum shown in the record, from micro activity through large-scale activity. The national foreign-investment position is also clean: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership recorded is 100%. There is no partial ceiling in the record to soften or interpret. Nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to the recorded full ceiling.

The Bali reading is where the classification has to be handled carefully, because the island moratorium is real but not triggered here in the record. The moratorium rule says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This code, however, is marked with Bali status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with `l4_bali_blocked` set to false. The record’s reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali imposes a separate ownership cap, and not that Bali blocks this activity. The conclusion is narrower and stronger: nationally it is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers making various leather and composition-leather goods not classified elsewhere—such as upholstery, decorative crafts (shadow puppets, lampshades), and machine parts like van belts and gaskets.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign artisan or manufacturer looking to produce niche leather goods for machinery or handicraft markets, though currently PMA registration is unavailable in Bali.

editorial.headline: KBLI 15129 Covers the Specialist Edge of Leather Goods Manufacturing
editorial.standfirst: A precise home for leather and composition-leather products that fall outside the standard product lanes, from crafted decorative work to machine-use components.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15129 is for the making of other goods from leather and composition leather: the specialist, less standardised end of leather manufacturing. The record points to products made for uses not otherwise captured in the narrower leather-goods categories, including seats, decorative carved-and-painted craft work such as ornaments, puppets, and lampshades, as well as leather or composition-leather items made for machinery, including vanbelts and packing components.

That range matters because this is not framed as retail, repair, design, or trading. It is manufacturing. A founder using this activity should be describing a production operation: taking leather or composition leather and turning it into finished goods for practical, decorative, craft, or machine-related use. The record is broad, but not vague; it gives the code its shape through material, process, and end use. The common thread is the manufacture of leather-based goods that do not sit inside the more ordinary product boxes.

The scale position is unusually straightforward. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can cover anything from a small workshop making carved decorative pieces to a larger production setup manufacturing leather components for machinery. Nothing in the record adds a special threshold, minimum capital figure, permit condition, timeline, or tax rule, so those should not be implied. The clean reading is simply that the activity is available across all listed business scales.

For foreign ownership, the national picture is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` recorded as 100. In plain English, the record treats this activity as nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate percentage, quota, partnership requirement, or foreign-share ceiling in this record. Its Bali-side status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, and `l4_bali_blocked` is false. The reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters as context because it says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, but this record does not mark KBLI 15129 as blocked. The honest conclusion is therefore simple: nationally foreign-open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.

editorial.headline: Everyday Footwear Manufacturing, Open Across Scales
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of daily-use footwear and its component parts, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**This activity is the industrial making of footwear for ordinary daily use.** The record describes shoes and sandals made from leather and imitation leather, rubber, textiles, plastic, and wood: daily shoes, casual shoes, sandal-shoes, wooden sandals, slippers, and similar products. It also reaches into the manufacture of the parts that make those products usable and finished: uppers, insoles, outer soles, front, middle, and rear reinforcements, linings, and accessories made from the same stated materials.

That scope matters because this is not framed as a narrow retail activity or a design-only business. It is manufacturing. A founder reading the category should see a production activity: cutting, forming, assembling, finishing, or otherwise making the footwear or the listed components that belong to it. The record is broad in materials and practical in product type, but it remains anchored to everyday footwear rather than specialised or ceremonial use. Its commercial centre is the ordinary object people wear daily, produced at industrial or workshop scale depending on the registered business size.

The scale position is clean. The record marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration language, that means the slim record does not reserve the activity to one size band; it can sit with very small operators, small and medium businesses, or larger manufacturing companies. The national PMA position is also straightforward: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no basis in the record to invent an additional national condition, capital threshold, licence timeline, or special manufacturing test. The available fact is simply that, nationally, foreign ownership is open up to the stated ceiling.

Bali is not presented as a hidden obstacle here. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The record gives its Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The honest reading is therefore balanced but clear: nationally, it is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium. For this activity, the national openness and the Bali-side status point in the same direction rather than pulling founders into a contradiction.

editorial.headline: Sports-Footwear Manufacturing With a Clean Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15202 covers the making of purpose-built sports shoes and their parts, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15202 is the manufacturing code for sports footwear: shoes specifically designed for athletic use, made from leather or imitation leather, rubber, plastic, and textiles. In practical terms, the record points to football shoes, basketball shoes, tennis shoes, athletic shoes, gymnastics shoes, jogging and running shoes, hiking shoes, ballet shoes, and the manufacture of parts for those shoes. The centre of gravity is not general fashion retail or a broad footwear label; it is production activity, defined by the making of shoes built for sport and physical movement.

The code is available across the full scale ladder recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not framed as a narrow preserve of only large factories or only small workshops. A small producer making specialised sports-footwear components and a larger manufacturing operation both sit inside the same activity description, provided the activity remains within the stated sports-footwear manufacturing scope. The record’s wording is especially useful because it includes both complete shoes and parts, giving the code room for manufacturers whose business model is component production rather than finished pairs alone.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The activity appears as TERBUKA in the record, which lists a pma_max_asing of 100 and cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, that means the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no separate national cap in the slim record below that number, and there is no recorded minimum capital figure, licence timeline, tax treatment, or operational threshold to add. The editorial conclusion should therefore stay disciplined: this is a nationally open PMA activity at the foreign-ownership ceiling stated in the record.

Bali does not change that into a hidden local percentage or partnership formula. The Bali field is not a second ownership table; it is a status and moratorium screen. Here, l4_bali_blocked is false and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not blocked on the record supplied. The honest national-vs-Bali reading is therefore unusually clean: foreign ownership is open nationally up to 100%, and the Bali moratorium screen does not block PMA registration for this activity on the supplied data.

editorial.headline: Industrial Footwear Built for Real Worksites
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 15203 covers the making of specialist field and industrial shoes, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 15203 is a manufacturing activity, but a very specific one: the production of footwear made for technical field use and industrial needs. The record points to shoes designed for demanding settings rather than ordinary retail footwear. It includes the making of the shoes themselves and the making of their parts, with materials ranging across leather, imitation leather, rubber, textile, and plastic. The examples in the scope are practical and physical: chemical-resistant shoes, heat-resistant shoes, and safety shoes.

That scope matters because this is not a broad fashion category dressed up in industrial language. The activity is anchored in protective and functional footwear: shoes built around exposure, durability, and workplace risk. A founder using this code would be registering a production activity for specialist footwear and components, not merely trading finished goods or operating a general shoe brand. The natural centre of gravity is manufacture: turning specified materials into shoes or shoe parts for field, safety, or industrial purposes.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, which means it is not reserved only for large factories. A small workshop, a growing mid-sized producer, or a large industrial manufacturer can all sit within the registered scale range, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope. That breadth is important for founders because the code can describe both early production capacity and more formal industrial expansion without changing the essential nature of the activity.

The national-versus-Bali reading is clean. Nationally, the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate foreign-ownership percentage in this record, and it is not marked as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule still matters as background, because Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this record’s own Bali reading does not place KBLI 15203 inside that block. In plain terms, this is a nationally foreign-open industrial footwear manufacturing code, and the slim record does not block it for PMA registration in Bali.
