data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Producing inorganic acids like hydrochloric and carbonic acid; bases such as sodium hydroxide (caustic soda), potassium hydroxide, lithium hydroxide; and salts formed from acid-base reactions, including sodium chloride, sodium carbonate (soda ash), and potassium chloride. This excludes edible salt production.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: This activity is open to foreign investment through a PMA company. The risk classification and permits shown here earlier came from a source that cannot reliably be applied to this KBLI-2025 code, so they have been removed from this page; a correct risk tier and licensing are not yet reliably defined. Before registering or investing, confirm the current requirements with the Bali Zero team.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Unchanged from KBLI 2020 — direct match.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Planning an inorganic chemical plant in Bali? Let me help you with the licensing requirements for producing acids, bases, and salts.

editorial.headline: Inorganic Acids, Bases and Salts, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20111 covers basic inorganic chemical manufacturing, nationally open to PMA up to full foreign ownership; whether Bali's moratorium applies is not yet classifiable pending re-derivation of the true risk tier.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20111 is a basic inorganic chemical manufacturing activity. The record places it in the production of inorganic acids, inorganic bases, and inorganic salts formed from acid-base reactions. In practical terms, this is the industrial making of materials such as hydrochloric acid and carbonic acid; sodium hydroxide, potassium hydroxide, and lithium hydroxide; and salts such as sodium chloride, sodium carbonate, and potassium chloride. It also includes acid oxides, base oxides, and salt oxides, provided those oxides are not used as pigments.

The boundary matters because this is not a catch-all chemical code. The record leaves outside this activity the production of iodized consumption salt and food-industry salt, pharmaceutical salt, and ammonia. It also carries two important process exclusions: new investment, expansion, and development are not allowed for chlor-alkali basic inorganic chemical activity using a mercury process, and mercury-industry activity itself is likewise prohibited for new investment, expansion, and development. Those limits sit inside the scope record and should be treated as part of the activity’s definition, not as a separate commercial afterthought.

For registration scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar business scales, so the activity is not framed only as a large industrial category even though many of its examples are heavy chemical inputs. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling recorded at 100%. That is the clean national answer: a foreign-owned company may use this activity nationally up to full foreign ownership, according to the source cited in the record.

Whether Bali's moratorium rule applies to KBLI 20111 cannot be determined until its risk tier is established: the earlier reading was based on a risk classification carried over from a different activity (code-number collision) and has been removed. Nationally, the activity remains open to foreign investment through a PMA company, a separate and unaffected fact. Confirm the current risk tier with the Bali Zero team before planning a Bali setup.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not a Bali-specific ownership cap: nationally this activity is open to foreign investment through a PMA company; whether Bali's moratorium applies is not yet classifiable pending re-derivation of the true risk tier.

l4_bali.reason: Bali moratorium applicability not classifiable: the risk tier this verdict depended on was carried over from a different activity (code-number collision) and has been detached. Pending re-derivation from the true risk tier (GARUDA-FILIERA). Previous status: OK_or_HIGHER_RISK.

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

data._data_note: KBLI 2025 code 20111 is a MANY-TO-ONE MERGE target, image-verified on BPS lampiran5 p.140-141: three KBLI-2020 codes converge into it — old-20111 (Khlor-Alkali), old-20114 (Anorganik Lainnya), old-20118 (Organik->Bahan Kimia Khusus). The served per_skala reflected a single-source inheritance (aggregation_note 'Dati da 20111'), not the aggregation across all three feeders that a MERGE requires. Detached pending a proper multi-source licensing extraction; a single-feeder block is neither complete nor certifiable for the merged code. BPS Vol.2 sha 29f17b3b. OSS RBA 2025 ruang-lingkup (fetched 2026-09-22) confirms 20111's own merged 3-scope licensing basis; the single-feeder PP28 block stays as the disputed audit trail.

- pembuatan gas amonia, lihat kelompok 20121.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Producing industrial gases like hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, and dry ice; as well as noble gases such as helium, neon, and argon. This excludes radon gas production (see 20114) and ammonia production (see 20121).
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**Small / Medium scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued within 7 working days.

**Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued within 7 working days.

**Small / Medium scale**: Medium-Low risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued automatically.

editorial.headline: Industrial Gas Manufacturing with a Clear National PMA Lane
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20112 covers the making of core industrial gases, and the record marks it as nationally open to foreign-owned registration across all listed business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20112 is the industrial-gas manufacturing activity: the making of basic chemicals that produce gases used across industrial systems. The record names hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, dry ice, and noble gases such as helium, neon, and argon. In plain English, this is not a trading or distribution classification; it is a production classification for the manufacture of industrial gases as basic chemical outputs.

That scope matters because the business profile implied by the record is broad in scale. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification is not reserved only for large plants in the national dataset. A small specialist producer and a larger industrial facility sit inside the same registered activity when the real work is manufacturing these gases. The editorial point is simple: the code is about what is being made, not the size of the company doing it.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, with the cited source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the slim record does not contain a national foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no basis here to invent extra capital thresholds, special licences, or operating timelines; the record gives only the openness status, the ceiling, the source, and the business scales.

Bali does not change that into a local blockage on this record. For Bali, the record assigns the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and sets l4_bali_blocked to false. The reason is stated directly: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked under that rule. So the honest national-vs-Bali reading is not a warning dressed up as opportunity: nationally it is open, and for Bali the record does not mark it as blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 20112 is nationally open to PMA and, on this record, not blocked for Bali registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Kimia Dasar Zat Warna dan Pigmen
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan produk kimia dasar berupa zat warna dan pigmen, seperti red lead; chrome yellow, zinc yellow, barium sulfat, pigmen serbuk aluminium, oker, pigmen dengan dasar titanium, termasuk hasil antara siklisnya seperti hasil antara fenol dan turunannya, serta zat warna tekstil dan zat warna untuk makanan dan obat-obatan.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan pembuatan sediaan zat warna dan pigmen dengan formulasi khusus, lihat subgolongan 2022.

editorial.headline: Basic Dye and Pigment Chemicals, Open Nationally but Scope-Sensitive in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20113 covers the manufacture of basic dye and pigment chemicals, with national PMA openness and a Bali registration picture that depends on declared scope and risk.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20113 is a manufacturing code for basic chemical products in the form of dyes and pigments. The record frames it around substances such as red lead, chrome yellow, zinc yellow, barium sulfate, aluminium powder pigments, ochre, titanium-based pigments, and cyclic intermediates including phenol intermediates and derivatives. It also reaches into textile dyes and dyes used for food and medicines. In plain English, this is not a general trading label or a light formulation category; it is an industrial manufacturing classification for the chemical base materials that give colour, opacity, or pigment function to other products.

The scope also draws a boundary. It does not cover the manufacture of specially formulated dye and pigment preparations, and the record separately carves out a long set of named dye-industry activities, including reactive, disperse, acid, basic, naphthol, mordant, vat, soluble vat, sulfur, oxidation, intermediate, pigment dye, Metanil Yellow, and Rhodamin B industries. That matters because the code should be read as a precise industrial manufacturing home for the covered basic dye and pigment chemicals, not as a catch-all for every colourant-related operation. A founder using it should be able to describe the activity in terms of manufacturing the covered chemical substances, intermediates, or dyes, rather than merely handling finished colourant products.

On scale, the record is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open to this activity. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The clean national reading is therefore straightforward: the code is foreign-open, and the record does not impose a lower national foreign-share cap. For a foreign-owned company, that is the strong part of the picture: the national investment field treats this activity as open, across all listed business scales.

Bali needs a more careful sentence. The record does not mark this code as fully blocked in Bali: `l4_bali_blocked` is false. But it also does not give a simple green light. The Bali status is `Blocked (scope-dependent)`, with the reason stated as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity". That sits beside the province rule that Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest conclusion is: nationally this code is open to PMA up to 100%, but in Bali the registration result depends on the exact declared activity and its live OSS risk treatment, especially at Besar scale. There is no separate Bali percentage in the record; the Bali question is not a foreign-share cap, but whether the declared scope can pass the provincial low-risk moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this code is open to PMA up to 100%, but in Bali the registration result depends on the exact declared activity and its live OSS risk treatment.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices
moratorium.virtual_office: requested in letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP; application not confirmed

l4_bali.rule: per-scala-Besar (OSS risk at scale Besar; PMA is Besar by law)

editorial.headline: Radioactive Basic Chemicals, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20114 covers the industrial making of radioactive basic chemicals, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20114 is a narrow, high-consequence industrial classification: the manufacture of basic chemical products that are radioactive in nature. The record names uranium, radium, thorium, and radon as examples, and it also brings within the scope the enrichment of uranium and thorium ores and the making of radioisotopes from radioactive substances. In plain English, this is not general chemical production. It is the industrial handling and transformation of radioactive basic chemical materials, where the defining feature is the radioactive character of the product or input.

The activity is open across the recorded business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the classification is not reserved in the slim record for only one size of operator. A small registered enterprise and a large industrial company are both within the scale range shown here, although the nature of the activity itself makes the scope much more specialised than the scale list might suggest. The description also marks boundaries around the activity by excluding ammonia and named hydrogen or ammonia variants, so the editorial reading should stay with the radioactive-basic-chemical lane rather than stretching it into broader industrial chemistry.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean: the record marks the code as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. Rendered as an ownership ceiling, that means 100% foreign ownership is recorded nationally. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the record, so there is no basis for implying a required Indonesian shareholding, a staged ownership structure, or a lower foreign ceiling. The honest national reading is that this activity is foreign-open at the maximum percentage stated in the data.

The Bali picture is also specific, and it should not be overcomplicated. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false and l4_bali_status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The record’s specific rationale reads: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this code is not captured as blocked under that rule in the supplied data. So the national-vs-Bali conclusion is unusually straightforward: open nationally, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium record provided.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali reading is unusually straightforward: open nationally, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium record provided.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

persyaratan: Memiliki dokumen rencana penggunaan jenis, spesifikasi, jumlah, dan asal dari bahan baku, serta sumber dan jumlah/ besaran dari energi dan air baku, yang dibutuhkan untuk menjalankan kegiatan usaha industri dalam 1 (satu) siklus produksi atau selamalamanya 6 (enam) bulan ke depan

Memiliki dokumen berupa: a. Spesifikasi mesin dan/atau daftar peralatan b. Foto mesin/ peralatan c. Perjanjian jual beli/sewa yang membuktikan penguasaan (kepemilikan/sewa) mesin untuk menghasilkan produk industri kimia serta peralatan pengujian kualitas produk

Memiliki dokumen pencegahan dan penanggulangan keadaan darurat bahan kimia yang terdiri atas: a. Penilaian risiko terhadap alur proses produksi dan pengelolaan daftar bahan kimia dalam rangka pencegahan dan penanggulangan keadaan darurat bahan kimia dalam kegiatan usaha industri kimia yang disusun secara mandiri (self assesment) b. Prosedur pencegahan dan penanggulangan keadaan darurat bahan kimia meliputi: 1) Personil tanggap darurat jumlah personil paling sedikit terdiri dari: i. Koordinator 1 orang i. Komandan 1 orang ii. Petugas 1 orang 2) Sistem komunikasi tanggap darurat 3) Pedoman teknis operasi tanggap darurat 4) Peralatan dan perlengkapan tanggap darurat 5) Perencanaan latihan tanggap darurat
Memiliki dokumen bagan alur: a. Pengadaan, penerimaan, penyimpanan bahan baku b. Proses produksi c. Proses quality control d. Pengemasan, penyimpanan, pengangkutan dan distribusi hasil produksi

Memiliki dokumen perencanaan tata letak Fasilitas pabrik/plant layout facilities sesuai dengan bagan alur proses dan membuktikan tersedianya: a. Tempat Penampung Sementara (TPS) B3 apabila menggunakan bahan kimia yang tergolong dalam Bahan Berbahaya dan Beracun (B3)
Sarana IPAL (Instalasi Pengolahan Air Limbah) untuk menampung dan menetrali-sir limbah cairan dari hasil sisa kegiatan produksi
Melampirkan Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi merkuri sesuai dengan Minamata Convention on Mercury
kewajiban: Memiliki bukti penyampaian wajib Data Industri tervalidasi setiap 6 (enam) bulan sekali sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan di bidang perindustrian
Menjamin keamanan dan keselamatan alat, proses, hasil produksi, penyimpanan, serta pengangkutan, sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan

Menjamin kegiatan usaha yang dijalankan tidak menghasilkan produk merkuri

Memiliki dokumen berupa: a. Spesifikasi mesin dan/atau daftar peralatan b. Foto mesin/ peralatan c. Perjanjian jual beli/sewa yang membuktikan penguasaan (kepemilikan/sewa) mesin untuk menghasilkan produk industri kimia serta peralatan pengujian kualitas produk

Memiliki dokumen pencegahan dan penanggulangan keadaan darurat bahan kimia yang terdiri atas: a. Penilaian risiko terhadap alur proses produksi dan pengelolaan daftar bahan kimia dalam rangka pencegahan dan penanggulangan keadaan darurat bahan kimia dalam kegiatan usaha industri kimia yang disusun secara mandiri (self assesment) b. Prosedur pencegahan dan penanggulangan keadaan darurat bahan kimia meliputi: 1) Personil tanggap darurat jumlah personil paling sedikit terdiri dari: i. Koordinator 1 orang ii. Komandan 1 orang iii. Petugas 1 orang 1) Sistem komunikasi tanggap darurat 2) Pedoman teknis operasi tanggap darurat 3) Peralatan dan perlengkapan tanggap darurat 4) Perencanaan latihan tanggap darurat
Memiliki dokumen bagan alur: a. Pengadaan, penerimaan, penyimpan an bahan baku b. Proses produksi c. Proses quality control d. Pengemasan, penyimpanan, pengangkutan dan distribusi hasil produksi

Memiliki dokumen perencanaan tata letak Fasilitas pabrik/plant layout facilities sesuai dengan bagan alur proses dan membuktikan tersedianya: a. Tempat Penampung Sementara (TPS) B3 apabila menggunakan bahan kimia yang tergolong dalam Bahan Berbahaya dan Beracun (B3) b. Sarana IPAL (Instalasi Pengolahan Air Limbah) untuk menampung dan menetralisir limbah cairan dari hasil sisa kegiatan produksi
Melampirkan Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi merkuri sesuai dengan Minamata Convention on Mercury

Menjamin keamanan dan keselamatan alat, proses, hasil produksi, penyimpanan, serta pengangkutan, sesuai peraturan perundang-undangan

Memiliki dokumen berupa SOP evakuasi bencana, termasuk penataan rambu keselamatan kerja
Menjamin kegiatan usaha yang dijalankan tidak menghasilkan produk merkuri

editorial.headline: Organic Basic Chemicals from Indonesia’s Living Resource Base
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20115 covers bio-based organic chemical manufacturing, nationally open to foreign investment and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20115 is for the manufacture of basic organic chemical products derived from biological natural resources. In plain English, this is the industrial conversion of agricultural, fishery, plant, animal, wood, resin, biomass, and essential-oil inputs into organic chemical materials. The record includes bio-benzene, bio-toluene, and bio-xylene made through biomass pyrolysis; carboxylic acids from animal or plant sources such as fatty acid, acetic acid, and citric acid; alcohols and esters such as bioethanol from sugarcane, corn, or similar fermentation; fatty alcohol, furfural, and sorbitol; charcoal, coconut-shell charcoal, coconut-shell briquettes, and other biomass charcoal; wood-distillation and natural-resin products such as gondorukem and turpentine; and separated compounds from essential oils, including caryophyllene, eugenol, vanillin, geraniol, and citronellaldehyde.

The scope is broad, but it is not unlimited. The slim record expressly excludes liquid biofuel manufacturing and plastic polymer manufacturing. It also names a long set of activities outside this group, beginning with ethanol, acetic anhydride, phenylacetic acid and its salts, lysergic acid and its salts, isosafrole, piperonal, safrole, anthranilic acid and its salts, diethyl ether, ephedrine and its salts, and several related chemical substances. That boundary matters because this code is not a generic label for any chemical plant using biological inputs. It is a defined manufacturing lane for basic organic chemicals from biological natural resources, with certain sensitive or separately classified chemical industries kept outside its perimeter.

For company planning, the registration picture is unusually straightforward. The activity is marked **TERBUKA** nationally, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited PMA source. The record also shows the activity open across all listed business scales: **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar**. That means the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators in the slim record; it can appear across the stated scale spectrum, while the exact business model should still fit the manufacturing scope rather than drift into excluded products.

The Bali reading is also clean. The record gives the Bali status as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and says: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The provincial moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is marked as not blocked. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and for Bali the record does not show a PMA moratorium block. For a foreign-owned setup, the important conclusion is precise rather than dramatic: this code stands as foreign-open nationally and Bali-open on the moratorium screen provided in the record.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of basic organic chemicals derived entirely from crude oil, natural gas, or coal. It includes producing cyclic hydrocarbons like benzene and xylene, acyclic hydrocarbons such as ethylene and propylene, and functional compounds made through processes like oxidation or alkylation, as well as distilling coal tar.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kimia Dasar dari Minyak Bumi, Gas Alam, dan Batu Bara (20116)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: This is for large-scale industrial foreign entrepreneurs in petrochemical processing or organic chemical synthesis who are scouting production bases—but not in Bali right now.

editorial.headline: Basic Petrochemical Chemistry With a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20116 covers core organic chemical manufacturing from petroleum, natural gas, or coal, and the record treats it as nationally foreign-open and not Bali-blocked.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20116 is an industrial chemistry code, not a trading or service label. Its scope is the manufacture of basic organic chemicals whose raw materials come from petroleum, natural gas, or coal. In practical terms, the record places this activity in the upstream chemical layer that produces cyclic hydrocarbons such as benzene, toluene, xylene, ethylbenzene, and styrene; acyclic hydrocarbons made through processes including pyrolysis, such as ethylene, propylene, butadiene, methanol, and synthetic ethanol; and functional compounds produced through oxidation, alkylation, halogenation, hydration, or hydrogenation, including ethylene dichloride, ethylene oxide, cyclohexane, terephthalic acid, synthetic glycerol, and caprolactam. It also includes coal-tar distillation.

The record is equally important for what it excludes. The scope text names many specific chemical industries as excluded from this grouping, which means KBLI 20116 should be read as a defined basic-chemical manufacturing bucket, not a catch-all for every named petrochemical product. The safe editorial reading is therefore narrow and technical: this code is for factories making basic organic chemical substances from fossil raw materials, with process chemistry at the centre of the activity. It is not a downstream brand, a retail channel, or a general chemical business description.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the registration surface is not limited in the slim record to one business size. That does not create any extra permission, capital, tax, or operating conclusion; it simply says the activity is recorded as available across those scales. A founder or adviser reading the code should therefore separate the scale field from the operational reality of the activity. The KBLI scope describes heavy basic chemical manufacturing, but the record’s scale field still lists every scale category as open.

The national-vs-Bali picture is clear. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% under the stated source. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not marked as blocked. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That matters because the record also states the Bali moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently. For this code, however, the record’s own Bali reading is not blocked, so the honest conclusion is simple: KBLI 20116 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the slim record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is simple: KBLI 20116 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the slim record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: A Closed Door for Other Inorganic Basic Chemicals
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers residual inorganic basic chemical manufacturing, but the record closes it to foreign ownership nationally and marks Bali as closed as well.
editorial.body:
For KBLI 20119, the activity is the manufacture of other inorganic basic chemical products that are not already covered elsewhere in the classification. In practical terms, the record points to production involving phosphorus and its derivatives, sulphur and its derivatives, nitrogen and other derivatives, metallic elements, other oxide compounds, raw materials for explosives, and products used as fluorescent whitening agents or luminophores. It is a technical industrial category, not a retail or service activity, and its scope is defined by what it makes: base inorganic chemical inputs and specialist chemical products.

The record also carries two important exclusions inside the scope itself. It states that inorganic basic chemical industry involving chlorine and alkali using a mercury process is prohibited for new investment, business expansion, and development. It separately states that the mercury industry is prohibited for new investment, business expansion, and development. Those notes matter because they narrow the practical reading of the activity: even inside an already technical manufacturing field, mercury-related routes are not treated as available business territory in the record.

On business scale, the category is broad. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the activity is not confined to large industrial players in the scale field. A domestic registration reading would therefore look first at whether the intended operation fits the stated manufacturing scope and avoids the prohibited mercury-related descriptions. The scale line is inclusive, but the investment line is not: for foreign-owned company formation, the record is unambiguous.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERTUTUP, with `pma_max_asing` at 0. That means the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 0%, not a partial cap. Bali does not reopen the door. The Bali status is also TERTUTUP, and `l4_bali_blocked` is true, so the honest reading for a foreign founder is simple: this activity cannot be registered as a PMA in Bali today. The Bali reason should be read carefully, because it says: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, but this entry’s own Bali note says the block is not the moratorium trigger at Besar scale. The closing fact remains the national PMA closure and Bali’s TERTUTUP status.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the industrial production of single‑nutrient fertilizers like nitrogen, phosphate, or potassium fertilizers (including urea, natural rock phosphate, and natural potassium salts), as well as products such as ZA, TSP, and DSP. It also includes manufacturing related nitrogen compounds—for example, nitric acid, ammonia, ammonium chloride, and potassium nitrates.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.

editorial.headline: Nitrogen Fertiliser Manufacturing, With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20121 covers core nitrogen, phosphate, and potassium fertiliser production, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20121 is an industrial code for making the chemistry that sits at the base of agricultural input supply: single fertilisers based on nitrogen, phosphate, or potassium, including urea, natural phosphate, natural potassium salts, ZA, TSP, and DSP. The record also places related nitrogen compounds inside the same frame, such as nitric and sulfonitric acids, nitrous acid, ammonia-derived salts, and potassium nitrites and nitrates. In plain English, this is not retail fertiliser trading or farm advisory work. It is manufacturing: the production of fertiliser materials and associated nitrogen chemistry.

The scope is broad, but it is not limitless. The record separates this activity from ammonia industry, green hydrogen industry, blue ammonia industry, and green ammonia industry. That boundary matters because a founder should read this code as a defined manufacturing activity, not as a general licence to describe every upstream chemical, hydrogen, or ammonia venture under the same heading. The editorial interpretation is therefore disciplined: KBLI 20121 is about producing the named fertilisers and related nitrogen compounds listed in the record, with the excluded activities left outside the frame.

On business scale, the code is unusually wide. The record marks it open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the classification is not reserved only for the largest industrial players in the way some heavy manufacturing categories might appear to be from the outside. A registrant can read the scale line as covering the full stated range, from micro through large enterprise. What the record does not provide is a factory-size threshold, capital minimum, production capacity, environmental approval detail, or operational timeline, so none should be inferred from the scale language alone.

The national-versus-Bali picture is straightforward here. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded as 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record, and the Bali side should not be read as a local equity cap. Instead, the record marks l4_bali_blocked as false and gives the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule still matters as background because Bali blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, but this record’s Bali conclusion is that KBLI 20121 is not blocked by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: This is a manufacturing code with a clear national opening and, on the Bali record provided, no PMA moratorium block.

editorial.headline: Compound Fertiliser Production With a Bali Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers macro-nutrient fertiliser manufacturing that is nationally foreign-open, while Bali depends on the exact OSS risk scope declared.
editorial.body:
This KBLI activity is for producers making fertiliser built around primary macro nutrients, especially products that contain at least two of those nutrients. The record describes two manufacturing routes. One is chemical reaction, with examples such as monoammonium phosphate, potassium ammonium chloride, potassium metaphosphate, and ammonium potassium phosphate. The other is physical blending, where fertilisers are mixed without changing the original chemical nature or fertiliser properties. The scope also reaches secondary macro-nutrient fertilisers containing calcium, magnesium, and sulphur, including examples such as kieserite and magnesium oxide.

In practical terms, this is not a trading label or a broad agriculture catch-all. It is a manufacturing classification for businesses whose activity is the making of compound or secondary macro-nutrient fertiliser products. The scale field is unusually broad: the record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators. That means the activity can be registered across the full enterprise-size spectrum shown in the record, from micro through large-scale businesses, provided the declared activity remains inside the manufacturing scope described above.

The national investment picture is clear. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nationally, then, this is a foreign-open activity at the full ceiling stated in the record. There is no lower percentage to infer, no special capital number to add, and no hidden licence condition supplied here. The honest reading is simply that the national field allows foreign ownership up to 100% for this activity.

Bali is more careful. The record does not mark the code as fully blocked; l4_bali_blocked is false. But the Bali status is Blocked (scope-dependent), and the stated reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity.” The moratorium rule also matters because the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. So the editorial conclusion is narrow but important: this activity is nationally open to PMA, yet in Bali the registration outcome depends on the exact declared OSS activity and risk scope. A founder should not treat the national 100% ceiling as automatic Bali registrability; the live OSS declaration must carry the higher-risk scope needed for Bali, if the exact activity supports it.
editorial.pullQuote: A founder should not treat the national 100% ceiling as automatic Bali registrability; the live OSS declaration must carry the higher-risk scope needed for Bali, if the exact activity supports it.

editorial.headline: Micro-Nutrient Fertiliser Looks Open Nationally, but Bali Blocks PMA
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of micro-nutrient and beneficial-element fertilisers, with national PMA openness but a Bali registration block under the record’s risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 20123 is a manufacturing code for a very specific corner of the fertiliser industry: products built around trace nutrients rather than broad commodity fertiliser categories.** The record describes activity that includes making fertilisers containing micro-nutrients such as zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron and molybdenum. It also includes single fertilisers containing beneficial nutrients such as cobalt, silicon, sodium, iodine, titanium and selenium. In plain English, this is the industrial production of specialised plant-nutrition inputs where small elements matter because the product is defined by targeted nutrient content.

**On the national record, the code is open.** Its PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the listed foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The same slim record shows the code open across the full scale spectrum: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters editorially because the activity is not framed only as large industrial manufacturing; the record explicitly names every operating scale. A founder reading this nationally would see a code that can accommodate foreign ownership up to the listed ceiling and can be registered at multiple business sizes, provided the registration question is treated at the national level.

**Bali is where the answer changes.** The record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true and gives the reason as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026”. It also states the moratorium rule in broader terms: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)”. That is the honest national-vs-Bali picture for this code. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA up to 100%. In Bali, the record says PMA registration is blocked because the relevant OSS risk pattern falls inside the provincial moratorium. There is no separate Bali percentage in the record, and the Bali restriction should not be translated into a shareholding cap; it is a registration block under the stated Bali rule.

**For a foreign-owned setup, the practical reading is therefore precise but uncomfortable: this code is nationally open, yet not available for PMA registration in Bali today according to the slim record.** That does not change what the activity is: manufacturing fertilisers containing micro-nutrients and beneficial elements. It changes where the registration logic lands. The code can look straightforward on national openness, scale coverage and foreign-ownership percentage, but the Bali-side status is not a footnote. It is the controlling local conclusion in this record: Blocked (risk class).
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, the activity is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, the record says PMA registration is blocked.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the production of organic fertilizers, biofertilizers with live microorganisms, growing media (such as peat-based potting mixes, soil blends with sand or clay), and soil amendment products like agricultural lime, dolomite, zeolite, and organic enhancers.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this is 100% open for foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs manufacturing eco-friendly fertilizers, biofertilizers, professional growing media, or soil-improvement products for local and export agricultural markets.

editorial.headline: Organic Fertilizer and Growing Media, with a Bali Scope Check
editorial.standfirst: This code covers soil-focused manufacturing that is nationally open to foreign ownership, but Bali registration depends on the exact activity declared in OSS.
editorial.body:
For KBLI 20124, the activity is the industrial making of inputs that improve soil, feed plants, or form the medium in which plants are grown. The record defines it around three practical families: fertilizers containing microorganisms or formulas made from industrial by-products where micronutrients are the main component; growing media built around fertile soil or peat, including mixtures of natural soil, sand, clay, and minerals; and ameliorant materials used to correct or improve soil, such as agricultural lime, phosphate lime, dolomite, zeolite, and organic-bearing soil improvers.

That makes this a manufacturing code, not a general trading label and not a broad agriculture service category. Its center of gravity is formulation and production: turning biological, mineral, or soil-based inputs into products used to support cultivation. A founder using it should be able to connect the registered activity to the making of organic fertilizer, biological fertilizer, growing media, or soil-improvement materials as described in the scope. The language is technical, but the commercial shape is clear: this is for businesses that produce the physical inputs behind healthier planting media and amended soils.

Nationally, the record is straightforward. At the national level, PMA is classified as TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. The code is also open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. In plain English, the national record does not present this as a closed activity for foreign investment, and it does not impose a partial foreign-equity cap in the data supplied here. The relevant source named in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, but no additional licence, tax, timeline, capital threshold, or operational condition appears in the slim record, so none should be inferred from it.

The Bali reading is more careful. The record does not mark the activity as automatically blocked in Bali, but it gives the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent) and says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity". It also states the moratorium rule: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". The honest conclusion is therefore conditional rather than binary: nationally this code is open up to 100% foreign ownership, but for Bali PMA use the exact declared scope and OSS risk treatment matter. A founder should not treat the national openness as the final Bali answer until the precise activity has been checked live in OSS.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is clear, but in Bali the decisive question is the exact scope declared in OSS.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of biostimulants—natural substances like seaweed extracts or microbial blends that boost plant growth, resilience, and nutrient uptake without being fertilizers themselves. It includes production of plant growth promoters for agriculture, horticulture, or forestry use.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Biostimulan (20125)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur with a scalable, export-oriented biostimulant production idea who may need to initially base manufacturing outside Bali or partner with an existing local producer.

editorial.headline: Biostimulants Sit Squarely Inside Industrial Manufacturing
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20125 covers the making of biostimulants, including seaweed-based products and plant-growth promoters, with a clean national and Bali registration picture.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20125 is a manufacturing activity, not a loose agricultural service or a trading label. The slim record defines it as the making of biostimulants, including biostimulants made from seaweed, and it explicitly includes the making of plant-growth promoters. That is the core commercial substance of the code: the activity is about production. A founder using this classification should therefore understand it as a factory-side or processing-side category for products intended to stimulate plant growth, with seaweed named as one example of the underlying material.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, which means the classification is not reserved only for large industrial operators. It can describe a small producer as well as a bigger manufacturing platform, provided the registered activity remains the making of biostimulants within the stated scope. The important editorial point is not that every scale has the same operational reality, but that the record itself recognises the activity across the full scale ladder.

Nationally, the PMA position is clear. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, and the stated maximum foreign ownership is **100%**. In plain English, the national record treats this code as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling. There is no separate cap in the record below that figure, and there is no basis here to add a hidden ownership condition, capital threshold, licensing timeline, or special local-shareholding rule. The source field given for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and that is as far as the record goes.

The Bali layer is also clear, but it needs to be read precisely. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks **all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA**, island-wide and permanently. This code, however, is not marked as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason is stated directly: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction. Nationally, KBLI 20125 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium because the stated Besar-scale OSS risk sits above the Low and Medium-Low band that Bali blocks.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 20125 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Damar Buatan (Resin Sintetis) dan Bahan Baku Plastik
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan damar buatan dan bahan baku plastik (biji plastik murni), seperti alkid, poliester, amino, poliamida, epoksi, silikon, poliuretana, polietilena (PE), polipropilena (PP), polistirena, polivinil klorida, selulosa asetat, selulosa nitrat, dan biopolimer, termasuk asam alginat. Pengolahan lanjutan dari damar buatan dan bahan plastik yang dibeli untuk menghasilkan barang dari bahan baku tersebut, seperti barang plastik, film dan lembaran film yang belum peka terhadap sinar dimasukkan dalam kelompok 26800.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the production of synthetic resins and pure plastic raw materials (plastic pellets), such as polyester, epoxy, polyethylene, PVC, and biopolymers like alginic acid. It does not include turning those materials into finished plastic goods.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Damar Buatan (Resin Sintetis) dan Bahan Baku Plastik (20131)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign chemical or plastics manufacturers looking to produce raw synthetic resins and plastic pellets, but they must set up outside Bali.

editorial.headline: Synthetic Resin and Virgin Plastic Feedstock, Without the Bali Trap
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20131 covers the making of synthetic resins and virgin plastic raw materials, open nationally to PMA and not blocked for Bali in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20131 is a manufacturing classification for the upstream chemistry of plastics: the making of synthetic resin and virgin plastic raw material. The record describes **damar buatan** and **bahan baku plastik**, including pure plastic pellets, with examples such as alkyd, polyester, amino resin, polyamide, epoxy, silicone, polyurethane, PE, PP, polystyrene, PVC, cellulose acetate, cellulose nitrate, biopolymers, and alginic acid. In plain English, this is not a retail or trading category and not a generic plastic-products label. It is for the industrial production of resin and primary plastic feedstock before those materials are turned into articles.

The boundary matters because the scope is about producing the material itself. The slim record separates this activity from later processing of purchased synthetic resin or purchased plastic material into finished goods, plastic articles, film, or light-insensitive film sheets. That distinction gives the code its character: it is a base-material activity, concerned with resin chemistry and plastic raw material, not the downstream shaping of already-bought inputs into consumer or industrial plastic products. The record also carries a long set of named chemical industries outside this activity, which reinforces that the classification is specific rather than a catch-all for every chemical or plastic-related operation.

For registration, the scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so the classification is not reserved only for a large enterprise on its face. The investment picture is also straightforward nationally: PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is **100%** under the stated source. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national entry point in the slim record is open rather than capped below full foreign ownership.

The Bali reading is equally important because this is where many activities become less simple. Here, the record does **not** mark the activity as blocked for Bali. Its Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not blocked in the record because of the risk position stated there. The honest conclusion is clean: KBLI 20131 is foreign-open nationally, and the slim record does not show a Bali PMA moratorium block for it today.

editorial.headline: Synthetic Rubber Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20132 covers the manufacture of synthetic rubber families, from SBR to silicone rubber, with full national PMA openness and no Bali PMA block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20132 is a manufacturing classification for synthetic rubber. The record describes an industrial activity centered on making artificial rubber materials, including styrene butadiene rubber, polychloroprene or neoprene, acrylonitrile butadiene rubber or nitrile rubber, silicone rubber or polysiloxane, and isoprene rubber. In plain English, this is not trading rubber, processing a finished rubber item, or providing a rubber-related service. It is the production of the synthetic rubber compounds themselves.

That scope matters because the classification sits at the material-manufacturing layer of the supply chain. A company using this activity code is registering the making of the rubber base materials named in the record: SBR, neoprene, nitrile rubber, silicone rubber, and isoprene rubber. The range is chemically diverse, but the common thread is clear enough: these are engineered rubber materials, produced as industrial inputs rather than described here as retail products or downstream goods. The slim record gives no separate sub-condition, permit threshold, output volume, or facility rule, so the clean reading stays with the stated production scope.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not framed, in the record, as only a large-industrial category or only a small-enterprise activity. The same KBLI code can be relevant across the listed business scales, from micro through large, so the practical registration question is not whether the code exists only for one size of operator. The record says all four scales are open.

The national-vs-Bali picture is also straightforward. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%, sourced to the presidential-regulation reference in the record. Bali is not marked as blocked: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The reason given is specific: `OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium`. That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, the record’s Bali-side conclusion is not a separate Bali ownership cap, quota, or partnership condition. It is simply that this activity is not blocked by that moratorium under the stated reason.
editorial.pullQuote: The record’s Bali-side conclusion is not a separate ownership cap, but a clear finding that this activity is not blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial production of active chemical compounds that form the core of pesticides – such as glyphosate, carbofuran, arsenic trioxide, and copper sulphate. It’s the manufacturing of the raw active ingredients, not the final formulated pesticide product you buy off the shelf.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bahan Baku Pemberantas Hama (Bahan Aktif) (20211)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign chemical manufacturers or agritech groups that want to produce key pesticide active ingredients in Indonesia to supply domestic agriculture or export markets – but Bali is currently off-limits for PMA setup in this sector.

editorial.headline: The Active-Ingredient Layer Behind Pest-Control Manufacturing
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20211 is for manufacturing pesticide raw materials: nationally foreign-open, and not blocked for PMA in Bali under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20211 sits at the upstream end of pest-control manufacturing. It is not framed as retail, distribution, application service, or farm advisory work; the record defines it as the making of raw materials for pesticides, the active substances that sit behind finished pest-control products. The scope names examples such as buthyl phenyl methyl carbamate (BPMC), methyl isopropyl carbamate (MIPC), diazinon, carbofuran, glyphosate, monocrotophos, arsenic trioxide, and copper sulphate. In plain English, this is a manufacturing classification for chemical active ingredients used in pesticide production.

That makes the code narrower, and more industrial, than the title alone may suggest. A founder choosing it should be looking at the production of active pesticide inputs themselves, not merely at trading, packaging, consulting, or using pest-control goods. The Indonesian scope is chemical and ingredient-led: it points to specific compounds, not to a general business story around agriculture or pest management. The useful reading is therefore precise: this code is for the factory-side making of pesticide raw materials, with the named substances serving as the guide to its technical centre of gravity.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It lists **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** as open, so the classification is not confined in the record to only a large industrial operator. That does not turn every small chemical activity into this code; it simply means the scale field itself is open across the full set shown. The decisive question remains whether the registered activity is genuinely the manufacture of pesticide raw materials as described in the scope, rather than a downstream or adjacent commercial activity.

The national foreign-investment position is clean: PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. On the Bali side, the supplied record does not mark it as blocked. Its Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason given is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this code is not blocked under that supplied Bali assessment. The honest read is therefore direct: nationally, the activity is open to up to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali the record does not block PMA registration for it.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Pest-Control Formulation With a Clean National and Bali Read
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20212 covers the formulation of ready-to-use pest-control products, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 20212 is about formulation, not vague chemical trading.** The activity described in the record is the processing of active ingredients into ready-to-use pest-control products. Its practical center is the finished formulation: insecticides, fungicides, rodenticides, herbicides, nematicides, molluscicides and acaricides are all named in the scope, as are disinfectants for agriculture and other uses. In plain English, this is the industrial step that turns active substances into products designed for actual pest-control use.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses, so it is not framed only as a large industrial category. A small producer and a larger manufacturer may both sit within the same activity code if the real business is the formulation of those ready-to-use pest-control or disinfectant products. That breadth matters because the code is defined by the activity itself, not by a single factory size, sales channel or product brand.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The record classifies PMA as TERBUKA, while placing the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%. That means the national entry in this slim record does not cap the foreign stake below full ownership. For that national position, the record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the record adds a separate minimum capital figure, licence threshold, tax treatment or approval timeline, so none should be read into it.

Bali also reads as open on this record, but for a specific reason. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The record explains the reason directly: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That matters because the stated Bali moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. Here, the record does not mark the activity as blocked. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: KBLI 20212 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, and this slim record does not block PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Growth-Regulator Manufacturing With a Bali Stop Sign
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20213 covers chemical processing into growth regulators, nationally foreign-open but currently blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20213 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label or a broad agricultural catch-all. The slim record defines it as the processing of chemical materials into growth-regulating substances: atonik, ethrel, cepha, dekamon, mixtalol, hidrasil, and sitozim are the examples named in the scope. In plain English, this is the industrial making of chemical products used to regulate plant growth. The emphasis is on the processing activity itself, and the record gives no further permissions, technical thresholds, product registrations, or operational conditions beyond that scope.

The registration profile is unusually broad on business scale. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the category is not framed only for large factories. A small operator and a large operator sit inside the same activity description if the activity is genuinely the processing of chemical materials into these growth-regulating substances. That scale openness matters because it tells a founder where the KBLI can sit structurally in OSS-style business classification terms; it does not, by itself, create any additional licence, timeline, facility standard, or capital requirement not written in the record.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.
