editorial.headline: Paint Manufacturing With National PMA Room and Bali Clearance
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20221 covers the making of paints for walls, wood, metal, ships, epoxy uses, primers, and enamel, with full scale access and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20221 is the manufacturing lane for paint. The record defines it through the making of many kinds of paint: primer, metal paint, wood paint, wall paint, ship paint, epoxy paint, and enamel. That scope is broad, but it is still specific. It is not a general trading category, not a construction service, and not a design or finishing activity. Its center of gravity is production: the making of paint products themselves, across the listed surfaces and uses.

The registration profile is unusually clear. The activity is open across every business scale stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators in the slim record. A small producer and a larger manufacturer are both inside the stated scale range, provided the registered activity remains within the described making of paints such as primers, metal paints, wood paints, wall paints, ship paints, epoxy paints, and enamel.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here is 100%. The source given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the record, and there is no special national carve-out described beyond that maximum foreign-ownership value. For a founder reading the code, the honest national message is therefore simple: this activity is foreign-open at the national level, up to the stated ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion in this record. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The record gives this basis: at scale Besar, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule itself says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this code is not recorded as blocked by that rule. So the honest national-vs-Bali reading is not a contradiction: KBLI 20221 is nationally open to PMA, and the Bali-side record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali reading is not a contradiction: KBLI 20221 is nationally open to PMA, and the Bali-side record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Varnish Manufacturing Is Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20222 covers the making of lacquer, varnish-related products, thinners, removers, and mastic, with national PMA openness up to full foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20222 is a manufacturing activity, not a retail or contracting category. The record defines it around the making of lacquer and various kinds of varnish, including organic composite solvents, thinners, paint or varnish removers, and mastic. In practical terms, this is the industrial side of surface-coating materials: the controlled production of substances used to finish, dilute, remove, or prepare coating systems. The code is therefore about production activity itself, as described in the Indonesian scope, rather than downstream trading, application, or construction work.

The registration picture is broad on scale. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, which means it is not framed only as a large industrial undertaking. A small producer and a larger factory both sit within the same activity description if their registered business is the making of these varnish and lacquer-related materials. That breadth matters because the code's scope is defined by what is being made, not by a single plant size or a single market position.

Nationally, the PMA signal is clean. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is recorded as 100%. That is the plain national reading: for a foreign-owned company structure, the record does not show a foreign-equity cap below full ownership. The supporting PMA source is listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and there is no separate threshold, licence condition, minimum capital figure, or operational timeline in the slim record. Those absent facts should stay absent from the analysis.

Bali is also not marked as blocked for PMA registration in this record. The province's moratorium rule is important because it blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. But this activity is not caught by that block here: the Bali reason states, verbatim, “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest national-vs-Bali picture is therefore unusually direct: this is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali field does not convert that openness into a local registration block.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali picture is unusually direct: this activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali field does not convert that openness into a local registration block.

editorial.headline: Putty and Surface Fillers, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20223 covers the making of putty, plamuur, non-refractory fillers, and similar surface-covering materials, with full national foreign ownership available.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20223 is a compact industrial category, but its commercial meaning is clear: it covers the manufacture of putty, plamuur, non-refractory putty, and similar materials used to close, smooth, or prepare surfaces. The record describes a production activity, not a trading desk or installation service. Its centre of gravity is the making of surface-covering materials themselves: the substances that fill gaps, even out imperfections, and prepare a substrate before finishing.

That matters for founders because the code is open across the full business-scale spectrum recorded here. Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as scales open to this activity. In practical registration language, the record does not confine this manufacturing line to one narrow size of operator. A small producer and a larger industrial setup are both inside the scale map, provided the registered activity remains the manufacture of the listed filler and surface-covering materials.

On foreign investment, the national position is unequivocal. This record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA and sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%. The stated national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no basis in this slim record to add a special licence, threshold, timeline, tax treatment, capital condition, or side obligation. The honest reading is simply that, at national level, this activity is open to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion in this record. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is explicit: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the editorial bottom line is clean: KBLI 20223 is nationally open, available across the listed scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record supplied.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 20223 is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Industrial Colour, Ink and Coating Preparations, Kept Open
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20229 covers the making of pigment, dye, ink and coating preparations, with national foreign ownership open and no Bali PMA block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20229 is an industrial manufacturing code for prepared colour and surface materials. The Indonesian scope places it around the making of pigment preparations and dye materials, colourants and opacifiers where the maker is not otherwise specified, polishing enamels and coating preparations, printing ink, artists' paints and other coating materials. In practical terms, this is not the retail sale of paint or the application of coatings on a building; it is the production side of formulated colour, ink and coating preparations themselves.

The record opens this activity across the full scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved only for a narrow industrial tier in the slim record. A small manufacturer preparing specialised coating materials and a larger producer working at industrial scale are both inside the scale envelope, provided the activity being registered remains the making of these preparations. The scope is broad, but it is still disciplined: pigment preparations, dye materials, opacifiers, enamels, printing inks, artists' paints and other coatings are the centre of gravity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership recorded is 100%. There is no partial cap to interpret, no lower foreign ceiling to explain, and no extra percentage hidden in the text. The national source given for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the face of this slim record, a foreign-owned company can treat the activity as nationally open rather than nationally restricted.

Bali does not change that conclusion into a block. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the activity is not blocked for PMA in Bali. The reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA in Bali, island-wide and permanently; this record says KBLI 20229 does not fall into that blocked outcome. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open, foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for Bali PMA registration in the slim record.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of a wide range of cleaning and care products, from bar soaps and liquid dish soap to laundry detergents, fabric softeners, surface polishes, air fresheners, and pre-moistened wipes. It also includes related processing of crude glycerol and blending of surfactants into powders or liquids.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bahan dan Produk Pembersih (20231)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs ready to manufacture cleaning products, waxes, or air care items at scale could use this KBLI elsewhere in Indonesia — and Bali is not off the table: this KBLI's large-scale risk class sits above the moratorium's Low/Medium-Low band, so a PMA can still register it here.

editorial.headline: Cleaning Products Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Conditional in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers household cleaning, detergent, polishing, antiseptic, and disinfectant products, with national PMA openness but a scope-sensitive Bali registration picture.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20231 is the manufacturing activity behind a broad shelf of cleaning and care products: cream soap, dishwashing soap, detergents, other household cleaning materials, wet wipes and similar materials coated with soap or detergent, crude glycerol, surfactant preparations, laundry powder or liquid, dishwashing preparations, and fabric softeners. It also reaches into household polish and finishing products, including room fragrance and deodorising products, processed wax, leather cream, wood polish, glass and metal polish, scouring paste and powder, and household antiseptic and disinfectant products.

That breadth matters because this is not a narrow retail description; it is an industrial manufacturing classification. A founder using it is describing production, not simply the sale of finished goods. The record opens the activity across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which means the classification is not framed only for large factories. It can also describe smaller production setups, provided the declared activity remains within the recorded manufacturing scope. The important editorial point is precision: the registered activity should match the actual product line, because the Bali position is explicitly tied to exact scope and risk.

Nationally, the record is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national line says this activity is open to foreign investment, with no lower foreign-share ceiling shown in the record. That national openness should not be softened into doubt, but neither should it be mistaken for an automatic Bali answer. The national investment status and the Bali registration filter are two different layers in this record.

For Bali, the honest reading is conditional rather than simply open or closed. The record does not mark this activity as fully blocked today, but it gives the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent) and explains why: "OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity". It also states the moratorium rule: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the practical message for a foreign-owned Bali setup is careful and exact: the code is nationally foreign-open, but Bali registration depends on the precise declared activity and its live OSS risk treatment, not on the headline title alone.
editorial.pullQuote: The national line is open, but the Bali answer depends on the exact activity declared in OSS, not on the title alone.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Industrial Backbone of Beauty and Contact-Lens Care
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of human cosmetics and contact-lens liquid, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record.
editorial.body:
This activity is not retail beauty, salon service, or brand storytelling. It is the industrial side of personal care: the making of cosmetics for human use and contact-lens liquid. The record places inside it a broad manufacturing field, from shampoo and hair curling or straightening products to nail-care goods for manicure and pedicure, skin-care creams or lotions for sun exposure, body-hygiene products, shaving products, decorative cosmetics, toothpaste and oral-hygiene goods, cosmetic teeth-whitening products, fragrances, hair dye, and liquid for contact lenses.

That breadth matters because the common thread is production. A business registering this activity is positioning itself as a maker of regulated consumer-care goods, not merely a seller of finished items. The scope reaches across daily hygiene, grooming, beauty, fragrance, oral care, and eye-care support products, which gives the code a practical industrial character: it can cover a focused manufacturer making one product family, or a larger operation producing several categories under the same personal-care umbrella. The record also makes the scale picture unusually clear. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the activity is not confined to a single size of operator.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, with its PMA source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the national classification presented here is foreign-open up to full ownership. There is no lower ownership cap in the slim record, and no additional capital, licensing, tax, timeline, or threshold detail is stated here, so none should be inferred from this activity note.

The Bali side is also explicit, but it needs to be read carefully. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is stated as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali province, but this activity is not caught by that block on the facts provided. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally, it is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium reason.

editorial.headline: Animal Cosmetics Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20233 covers the making of animal cosmetics, a nationally open activity that the Bali record blocks for PMA registration under its risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20233 is a manufacturing activity for cosmetics made for animals. The record describes its scope as the production of animal-use cosmetic goods, including perfume, shampoo, soap, powder, cream, lotion, and similar products. In plain English, this is not retailing, grooming, veterinary treatment, or pet-care services; it is the factory-side activity of making cosmetic products intended for animals. The emphasis is on production: turning formulas, ingredients, packaging, and manufacturing process into finished animal cosmetic goods.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not confined to one size of enterprise. A small producer and a larger industrial manufacturer can both sit inside the same activity description, provided what they do is the making of animal cosmetics. That matters because the KBLI question is not whether the business feels boutique or industrial in branding terms, but whether the registered activity matches the manufacturing scope in the record.

Nationally, the investment position is straightforward: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading, therefore, this is a foreign-open activity, not a closed one, and the maximum foreign stake shown in the record is the full percentage. Nothing in the slim record adds a licence condition, tax threshold, capital threshold, operational deadline, or special permit narrative beyond that national status, so the clean national conclusion is simply that KBLI 20233 is open to foreign ownership up to 100%.

Bali is the decisive exception. The record marks Bali as Blocked (risk class) and says l4_bali_blocked is true. Its reason is explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is also explicit: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". The honest reading is therefore not that Bali has a different foreign-ownership percentage, but that PMA registration for this activity is blocked in Bali under the recorded moratorium. A foreign-owned company may see a nationally open 100% figure, but for Bali today the practical answer in this record is no registration.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign-owned company may see a nationally open 100% figure, but for Bali today the practical answer in this record is no registration.

editorial.headline: Dental Adhesive Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20234 covers dental adhesive manufacturing, open nationally across all business scales with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20234 is a narrow industrial classification: the manufacture of dental adhesive products. The record does not expand the category into clinical services, dental practice, retail distribution, or medical-device trading. Its center of gravity is production. That makes the activity easier to read than many broader manufacturing labels: it is about making adhesive products used in dentistry, not about operating the professional dental setting in which those products may later be used.

At the national level, the record is open. Its PMA status is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. The business scales open to the activity are also broad: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar**. In plain English, the national line says that this activity can be registered across the full scale spectrum recorded here, and that a foreign-owned company is not capped below full ownership by the national figure supplied in the record.

Bali changes the practical answer completely. The Bali-side status is **Blocked (risk class)**, and the record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true. The reason is explicit: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026**. The moratorium rule attached to the record is equally direct: **Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)**. So the honest reading is not “open with a Bali caveat”; it is open nationally, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali moratorium information provided.

That distinction matters because the record contains two different regulatory pictures, not one blended answer. Nationally, KBLI 20234 reads as a foreign-open manufacturing activity with a 100% ceiling. Locally, for Bali, the same activity is stopped for PMA registration because of the recorded risk-class moratorium. A founder reading this code should therefore keep the two conclusions separate: the national ownership field is permissive, while the Bali registration outcome is blocked by the province-level rule stated in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is open nationally, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali moratorium information provided.

editorial.headline: Custom Perfume Blending Is Nationally Open and Bali-Clear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20235 covers made-to-order perfume production, including refill perfume, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20235 is a narrow but commercially recognisable manufacturing activity: making fragrances or perfumes that are specially blended to a customer’s order and chosen scent. The record’s Indonesian scope points to a bespoke formulation model rather than mass-market perfume branding in the abstract. Its clearest example is refill perfume production, where the business activity is the preparation of fragrance according to a customer’s selected aroma.

That makes this code relevant for operators whose core activity is production, mixing, or preparation of custom perfume, not merely retail display or general cosmetics trading. The registration picture is broad on scale: the record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. In plain terms, the activity is not confined to a small artisanal setup, nor reserved only for larger industrial players. A modest refill-perfume operation and a larger custom-fragrance manufacturer can both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the registered activity is genuinely the made-to-order perfume production described here.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is 100%. That is the only ownership percentage the record gives, and it means the national classification does not impose a foreign-shareholding cap below full foreign ownership. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, so the national reading is not a soft assumption or a practical shortcut; it is the record’s stated investment-status position.

The Bali position is also clear, but for a different reason: this record does not mark the activity as blocked in Bali. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the stated reason that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, therefore not blocked by the moratorium. That matters because the moratorium rule recorded here blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali province. For this activity, the record does not apply that block. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: KBLI 20235 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, open across all listed business scales, and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium information provided.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of glues and adhesives from plant, animal, or plastic sources—including starch glues, bone glue, cellulose-based adhesives, and synthetic resins like phenol, urea, melamine formaldehyde, and epoxy. The products are intended for both industrial applications and household tools.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Perekat/Lem (20291)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers of industrial or household adhesives who can consider locating outside Bali where PMA registration is still fully permitted.

editorial.headline: Adhesive Manufacturing With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20291 covers the making of industrial and household glues, and the record leaves it nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20291 is the industrial home for making adhesives and glues. The record defines the activity around production for industrial uses and household tools, with materials that may come from plants, animals, or plastics. Its examples are deliberately broad: starch-based adhesives, bone-derived glues, cellulose esters and ethers, phenol formaldehyde, urea formaldehyde, melamine formaldehyde, and epoxy adhesives. In plain English, this is not retailing glue, applying glue, or using adhesive inside another manufacturing process. It is the manufacture of the adhesive product itself.

That scope matters because the code can be registered across the full scale range in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small domestic producer and a larger industrial adhesive manufacturer are therefore both within the scale map shown here, provided the registered activity remains the making of adhesive or glue as described. The record does not add product thresholds, plant-size rules, technical standards, licensing timelines, tax treatment, or minimum-capital figures, so those should not be inferred from the classification note. The clean reading is narrower and stronger: this code identifies the activity, the examples of adhesive chemistry and origin that fit inside it, and the business scales open to it.

Nationally, the investment signal is straightforward. Nationally, the PMA status remains TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the record treats the activity as open at the national level, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial foreign cap in the slim record, and no special national caveat attached to the 100% figure. The honest sentence is therefore simple: on the national classification and investment fields supplied here, adhesive and glue manufacturing is open to full foreign ownership.

The Bali reading is also clean, and it should not be made more complicated than the record allows. Bali is not marked as blocked for this activity: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium itself is still relevant context because the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. But this activity is not caught by that block in the supplied record. The result is a rare clean alignment: nationally open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

It is a highly regulated industrial activity, typically involving significant safety and security protocols.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the local moratorium, but it carries a medium-high/high risk classification, meaning the location and business address will be strictly verified—expect extra scrutiny from spatial planning, safety, and security authorities.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bahan Peledak (20292)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: This fits a foreign entrepreneur with a proven background in industrial explosives or pyrotechnics who is ready to navigate Bali's heightened safety and zoning requirements for a high-risk manufacturing setup.

editorial.headline: Explosives Manufacturing, Nationally Open and Bali-Clear at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20292 covers the making of explosives and related propellant goods, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20292 is an industrial manufacturing activity, not a trading or service classification. The record defines it through the making of explosive goods: gunpowder, dynamite, detonators, fireworks, firecrackers, mercury fulminate, and rocket propellants. That scope is broad enough to cover both recognisable consumer-facing items, such as fireworks and firecrackers, and more specialised explosive and propellant materials. The common thread is production: this code is about manufacturing the goods themselves.

The scale profile is unusually wide in the record. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved only for a large-scale industrial operator. A founder reading the code should still keep the interpretation disciplined: the record says which business scales are open, but it does not add operational conditions, facility requirements, thresholds, or licensing steps. Those cannot be inferred here. What can be said is that the code is structurally available across the listed scale bands.

Nationally, the investment picture is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling. There is no lower foreign-stake cap in the slim record, and none should be invented. For a foreign-owned setup, the national reading is therefore not ambiguous: this is a foreign-open activity at the recorded maximum.

The Bali reading is also important, because this is where many nationally open activities become unusable for PMA registration on the island. Here, however, the record does not mark the activity as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. This code is therefore not blocked by that moratorium in the record. The honest conclusion is narrow but useful: nationally, KBLI 20292 is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, the slim record does not show a PMA moratorium block.

editorial.headline: Ink Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20293 covers the making of writing inks and specialised inks, with registration open across all business scales and no Bali moratorium block recorded for PMA.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20293 is a manufacturing code for ink. Its scope is direct: the activity is the making of various inks, including writing ink and specialised ink. That makes this a production activity rather than a trading label, a design service, or a general office-supply category. The record does not divide the field into subtypes beyond those examples, so the clean reading is that the code sits around the industrial act of producing ink in its different forms.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not reserved only for larger factories or only for small producers. A small ink producer and a larger manufacturing setup both sit within the same registration frame, provided the activity being registered is still the making of ink as described in the scope. That breadth matters because it keeps the code anchored in the activity itself, not in a single business size.

Nationally, the PMA position is also clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown here is 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-share cap in the record, and there is no special threshold or capital figure supplied, so none should be read into it. For a foreign-owned structure, the national signal is therefore open rather than capped.

The Bali picture does not reverse that conclusion. The record says l4_bali_blocked is false and gives the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not marked as blocked by that rule. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: KBLI 20293 is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and the Bali-side record does not show a PMA moratorium block.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Upstream Essential Oils, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20294 covers the making of essential oils from spices, flowers, leaves, roots, bark, resin, fruit, seeds, and other plant materials.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20294 is the upstream essential-oil manufacturing activity. In practical terms, it is where raw aromatic plant material becomes oil: ginger, cinnamon, coriander, clove, cardamom, nutmeg, jasmine, ylang-ylang, vetiver root, citronella, lemongrass, patchouli, sandalwood, agarwood, eucalyptus, peppermint, spice oils, and oils drawn from resin, bark, roots, leaves, fruit, seeds, and flowers that are not otherwise placed elsewhere. The centre of gravity is production, not retail presentation: the record points to the making of the oil itself, from plant inputs into an essential-oil output.

The activity is broadly usable across business sizes. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which means the same activity classification can describe a small producer as well as a larger industrial operator, provided the registered activity is still the making of upstream essential oils. That range matters because the activity is not framed only for artisanal production or only for large factories; the scale depends on the registrant, while the defining scope remains the same manufacturing activity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%, with the cited source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-stake ceiling in the slim record, and no extra national condition is stated here, so the editorial picture should stay disciplined: the national PMA reading is open at the recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not shown as blocked in this record. For Bali, the status reads OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not caught by that block on the record supplied. So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is simple: nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for Bali PMA registration on the supplied Bali moratorium check.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is simple: nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for Bali PMA registration on the supplied Bali moratorium check.

editorial.headline: Match Manufacturing With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of stick matches, open across business scales and nationally open to foreign ownership under the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20295 is a narrow industrial classification: the manufacture of matches in stick form. Its precision matters. The record is not describing a broad household-goods activity, a general fire-starting category, or a mixed manufacturing line. It is about the production of matches as batangan, the familiar matchstick form, and the editorial centre of gravity should stay there: a specific manufacturing activity with a defined product and an industrial character.

For registration scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not framed as a scale-exclusive classification. A small producer and a larger industrial operator are both inside the recorded scale envelope, provided the registered activity remains the manufacture of stick matches. That scale openness does not add extra facts, thresholds, or conditions; it simply means the record recognises this activity across the full listed scale range.

The national foreign-investment picture is also clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no partial ceiling in the slim record, no stated minimum capital, and no additional licensing threshold to infer. The correct reading is direct: nationally, this code is foreign-open at the recorded ceiling.

Bali does not overturn that picture in this record. In Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false. The reason given is exact and important: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The province’s moratorium rule is still part of the context, because the record states that Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this activity is not marked as blocked here. The honest national-versus-Bali conclusion is therefore simple: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and in Bali the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is direct: nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not mark it as blocked.

editorial.headline: Midstream Essential Oils for Flavour, Fragrance, and Bioadditives
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20296 covers further processing of essential oils into downstream inputs, with full national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20296 is not about the simple trading of essential oils, nor about a generic aromatic product line. Its centre of gravity is **further processing**: taking essential oils and turning them into downstream industrial products used as inputs for flavour production, fragrance production, and other chemical materials based on essential-oil processing. The slim record points to concrete examples: mixtures of essential oils and natural aromatic substances, odor preparations for flavour and fragrance use, essential-oil-based fuel bioadditives, and extracted oleoresin. In plain English, this is the activity code for the middle stretch of the essential-oil value chain, where botanical aromatics become usable industrial ingredients.

That matters because the code is framed as manufacturing, not merely branding or retail. A founder registering under this activity is describing a processing business: one that transforms essential-oil material into products with downstream application in taste, scent, fuel additives, or related chemical production. The activity is open across the full scale ladder shown in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That range is unusually broad in practical terms because the record does not confine the activity to either cottage-scale processors or larger industrial operators. The same classification can sit under a small specialist producer or a larger facility, as long as the registered activity remains within the described processing scope.

The national PMA picture is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company, the direct reading is that the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no lower cap in the slim record, and no separate national threshold, timeline, tax, or permit condition is provided here. The responsible editorial treatment is therefore simple: nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to full foreign ownership, according to the fields supplied.

Bali does not change that into a block in this record. The Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, and `l4_bali_blocked` is false. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule itself says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked by that rule. So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is not a warning disguised as nuance: KBLI 20296 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 20296 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Liquid Biofuel, Nationally Open and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This liquid biofuel activity covers biomass-based fuels and BBN trade across every scale, with a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling and no Bali PMA block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20297, in this record, is the liquid biofuel industry: the making of plant-based liquid fuel from biomass feedstock, including biodiesel, bioethanol, aviation biofuel, and biohydrocarbons such as plant-based diesel, plant-based gasoline, and plant-based jet fuel. The scope is broader than factory production alone. It also covers Bahan Bakar Nabati, or BBN, trade: processing, purchasing, selling, export and import, transport, storage, and marketing of liquid biofuel products meant for fuel use. The clean reading is industrial and commercial, but tightly anchored to liquid renewable fuel.

Who registers it is also clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses, so it can fit a smaller registered operator dealing in BBN products as well as a large manufacturing or trading company, provided the actual activity remains inside this liquid biofuel scope. That matters because the record is not a general energy label. A founder should read the title through the operational verbs in the scope: make, process, buy, sell, export, import, transport, store, and market liquid biofuel products.

Nationally, the position is clean: PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The record therefore treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to full ownership, with its national source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The only ownership ceiling in this slim record is national. Bali has no separate foreign-ownership percentage here, so the Bali analysis should not be turned into a second cap, quota, or implied local condition.

Bali is the decisive cross-check, and here the record stays open rather than closing the door. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, the Bali block flag is false, and the stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium." The moratorium rule still matters: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk PMA activity island-wide and permanently. But this record places the Besar-scale OSS risk above that blocked band. The honest conclusion is narrow but useful: based only on this slim record, a foreign-owned company can treat this liquid biofuel activity as nationally open and not blocked in Bali.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of e‑liquid for electronic cigarettes, both with and without nicotine. It includes formulating, mixing, and packaging liquids for closed systems (disposable pods, cartridges) and open refillable systems using raw materials like nicotine, flavourings, propylene glycol, and vegetable glycerin.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally the sector is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali it is registrable but classified as a medium‑high to high‑risk activity; it is not blocked by the current moratorium, so PMA is possible, though site‑specific verification and additional regulatory permits per address will be required.

editorial.headline: Electric Cigarette Liquids as a Standalone Manufacturing Activity
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the formulation, mixing and packaging of e-cigarette liquids, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20298 is a manufacturing code for electric cigarette liquids. Its scope is not retail, distribution, branding, or the operation of a smoking product outlet. The record describes the making of liquids for electric cigarettes, both with nicotine and without nicotine, and both for closed systems such as disposable pods and cartridges, and for open systems that can be refilled. In practical terms, the activity sits where raw ingredients become a finished liquid product: nicotine, flavouring substances, propylene glycol, vegetable glycerine, and other additives are formulated, mixed, and packaged.

That manufacturing emphasis matters because it gives the code a clear industrial character. The centre of gravity is the controlled production process: taking inputs, creating a liquid formulation, and preparing it in packaged form for the relevant device system. The scope is broad enough to include nicotine and non-nicotine variants, and it recognises both closed and refillable product formats. But it remains bounded by the record: this is about the manufacture of the liquid itself, not a wider tobacco, retail, logistics, or consumer-service business.

The scale profile is unusually inclusive. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it can describe anything from a small-scale producer to a larger industrial operation, provided the registered activity is the making of electric cigarette liquid as set out in the scope. For founders, that means the code is not reserved in the record for one size of enterprise. The same activity can be registered across the full scale ladder listed in the slim record, with the substance of the classification staying anchored in formulation, mixing, and packaging.

The national-vs-Bali picture is clean here. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the Bali side, the record does not mark the activity as blocked for PMA registration. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not blocked under that rule as recorded. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: this is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not add a moratorium block.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers manufacturing of miscellaneous chemical products not classified elsewhere, such as gelatin, peptones, modified animal/vegetable oils and fats, non-plastic/non-rubber insulating materials, and polishes.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Barang Kimia Lainnya YTDL (20299)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to produce specialty chemicals like gelatin, processed oils, or industrial polishes, but need to locate outside Bali under current restrictions.

editorial.headline: Specialty Chemical Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20299 covers the making of miscellaneous chemical materials and industrial chemical products not classified elsewhere, open across all business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20299 is a broad industrial category for chemical manufacturing that sits outside the named, narrower chemical groups. Its scope is not retail, trading, consulting, or laboratory service work; it is the making of chemical materials and chemical products. The record points to a wide field: gelatin, peptones and other protein substances, chemically modified animal, vegetable, or microbial fats and oils, non-plastic and non-rubber thermal insulation materials, polishes, lubricant additives, light-sensitive film, photographic paper, textile and leather treatment materials, brazing and welding powders or pastes, substances used for metals, formulated cement additives, formulated rubber accelerators, catalysts, anti-knock preparations, antifreeze preparations, composite diagnostic or laboratory reagents, brake fluid, and other chemical products for industrial use.

That breadth matters because this code is for manufacturers whose output is chemical in character but not captured by a more specific heading in the record. A company registering here should be able to describe a real production activity: transforming inputs into chemical substances, formulations, preparations, additives, reagents, fluids, or industrial-use chemical products. The common thread is not a single product family, but the fact that the activity is chemical manufacturing and the record expressly treats it as not classified elsewhere.

On business scale, the code is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes it available across the full scale ladder shown in the record, from small domestic-style operations through larger industrial establishments. Nationally, the PMA position is also clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. In plain English, the national record allows foreign ownership up to 100% for this activity, subject only to the facts stated in the record and without importing any separate licence, threshold, or capital rule that is not written here.

The Bali picture is unusually straightforward. The record does not mark this code as blocked in Bali; l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not blocked on the Bali-side fields supplied here. The honest reading is therefore that KBLI 20299 is foreign-open nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of synthetic or artificial filament fibers and strips, produced in tow form from materials like polyamide, polyester, acrylic, rayon, and cellulose acetate, for further industrial processing.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: While nationally 100% foreign ownership is permitted, in Bali this activity is classified as medium-high to high risk. It is not blocked by the current moratorium, but actual registration depends on your specific location and may require additional environmental or technical permits—verify the exact address’s zoning before proceeding.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Serat Filamen dan Strip Buatan (20301)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers scaling upstream synthetic fiber production, especially those supplying technical textiles or specialized composite material chains.

editorial.headline: Filament Fiber Manufacturing With a Clean PMA Line
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20301 covers synthetic and artificial filament fiber or strip made in tow rolls for further processing, open nationally to PMA at 100% and not blocked in Bali by the moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20301 is a manufacturing classification for synthetic and artificial filament fiber or strip, specifically in tow-roll form, made for further processing. The record names the base materials clearly: polyamide, polyester, polypropylene, acrylic, rayon, cellulose acetate, and similar inputs. In plain English, this is not the retail end of a product story. It is the making of the man-made fiber or strip that another operation will later process into something else.

That scope matters because the registration profile is broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the record does not reserve it for one size of operator. A small manufacturer and a large industrial operator are both within the scale language given here. The discipline is to keep the classification narrow: the activity is the making of those filament fibers or strips in tow rolls, not a wider promise about every downstream use of those materials.

Nationally, the PMA picture is direct. The status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source line given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company reading the code nationally, that means the record does not impose a lower foreign-equity cap. There is no need to soften the point: on the national fields supplied here, this activity is open to full foreign ownership.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion in this record. The moratorium rule stated here blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently. But KBLI 20301 is not marked as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The record's reason is precise: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". So the honest national-vs-Bali reading is clean: nationally open at 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium field supplied.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of short, synthetic or artificial staple fibers from materials like polyester, rayon, acrylic, nylon, and cellulose acetate (excluding glass and optical fiber). The output is a bulk industrial intermediate used in spinning, non-woven, and composite products.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the local investment moratorium, but it is classified as a medium-high to high risk activity, meaning your chosen location will face extra scrutiny for zoning and environmental compliance—address selection is critical.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign industrial manufacturer or textile-group investor looking to set up a chemical fiber production plant, where the product is an intermediate material rather than finished consumer goods.

editorial.headline: Artificial Staple Fibre Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20302 covers short synthetic and artificial fibres for further processing, nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20302 is a manufacturing classification for artificial staple fibre: short-length synthetic or artificial fibres made from materials such as polyamide, polyester, rayon, acrylic, cellulose acetate, and similar inputs. The record is explicit that the output is intended for further processing, and it also draws the boundary around what this activity is not: glass fibre and optical fibre are outside this scope. In practical terms, this is not a retail or trading category. It is an upstream industrial activity concerned with making short fibres that can become inputs for later production chains.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not reserved only for large industrial players. A founder reading this should still keep the nature of the activity in view: the scope describes manufacturing, materials, and downstream processing, so the business substance has to match the production of artificial or synthetic staple fibre rather than a looser textile-related idea. The title is concise, but the Indonesian scope gives the real editorial meaning: making short artificial staple fibres from named chemical or cellulose-based materials, for further processing.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The record marks the code as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100 and the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to a full 100% ceiling. There is no lower cap in the supplied data, and no additional national condition should be inferred from the classification alone. For a foreign investor, the important point is the simplicity of the national field: open status, 100% maximum foreign ownership, and a cited presidential-regulation source.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. KBLI 20302 is not marked as blocked in Bali. For Bali, the record gives it status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That does not create a separate Bali ownership percentage; it simply means this record does not place the activity inside Bali’s PMA moratorium block. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium data supplied here.

data.judul: Industri Bahan Baku Farmasi untuk Manusia
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan dan pengolahan bahan obat, bahan pembantu untuk manusia, yang berasal dari bahan kimia, bahan alam, hewan dan tumbuh-tumbuhan termasuk yang berasal dari hasil biologis, seperti bahan obat-obatan, seperti antisera dan fraksi darah lainnya, vaksin dan preparat homeopatik, substansi aktif obat (antibiotik, vitamin, salisilik dan asam o-asetilsalsilik dan lain-lain) untuk bahan farmakologi dalam industri obat-obatan, pengolahan darah, gula murni kimia, garam farmasi, pengolahan kelenjar dan pembuatan ekstraksi kelenjar.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup pembuatan monosodium glutamat (MSG), lihat kelompok 10779.

Area Penerimaan dan Pengiriman Barang 1) Area penerimaan barang dilengkapi dengan area pengambilan contoh/ sampel bahan baku dan/atau kemas b. Area Penyimpanan 1) Area penyimpanan terdiri dari area penyimpanan bahan baku dan/atau kemas, dan area penyimpanan produk yang saling terpisah satu sama lain 2) Setiap Area Penyimpanan sebagaimana dimaksud pada poin 1 huruf a memiliki area karantina sebelum bahan dan/atau produk dinyatakan lulus uji, dan area penolakan untuk bahan dan/atau produk yang dinyatakan tidak lulus uji c. intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing and processing of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and excipients for human medicines. It includes substances derived from chemicals, natural sources, animals, and plants—such as antibiotics, vitamins, vaccines, blood fractions, and glandular extracts—used in the production of pharmaceutical drugs. The scope spans everything from biologically sourced antisera to chemically pure sugars and pharmaceutical-grade salts.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Foreign-owned companies (PMA) are allowed 100% ownership for this KBLI nationally, and it is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium on certain businesses. However, due to its medium-high to high risk classification, successful company registration in Bali is not automatic and will depend on verifying the specific location address—you may face additional scrutiny or require permits tied to the chosen premises.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bahan Baku Farmasi untuk Manusia (21011)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: This suits foreign pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturers, biotech firms developing vaccines or blood-derived products, or natural-extract processors looking to set up a production base in Bali.

editorial.headline: KBLI 21011: Pharmaceutical Raw Materials for Human Medicine
editorial.standfirst: A precise classification for making and processing human pharmaceutical ingredients, nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 21011 covers the upstream industrial work behind human medicines: the making and processing of active drug materials and supporting pharmaceutical ingredients for human use. The scope reaches across chemical, natural, animal, plant, and biological origins, including medicinal substances, antisera and other blood fractions, vaccines, homeopathic preparations, antibiotic and vitamin actives, salicylic substances, pharmacological inputs for the medicines industry, processed blood, chemically pure sugar, pharmaceutical salts, gland processing, and gland extracts.

This is therefore not a retail, clinic, or distribution label. It is an industrial activity code for businesses whose substance is production or processing of pharmaceutical raw materials. The record opens the activity across the full scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not confined to one size of operator in the slim record; the decisive question is whether the registered activity really sits inside the described manufacturing and processing scope.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the PMA source. In plain English: on the national investment list supplied here, this code is open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. There is no lower cap, special minimum capital figure, or additional ownership condition in the slim record, so none should be read into it.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this code is not marked as blocked. The honest read is therefore simple: KBLI 21011 is nationally foreign-open, and the Bali moratorium data supplied here does not block PMA registration for it.

Memiliki bangunan, Fasilitas dan sarana pendukung yang dibuktikan dengan dokumen denah/layout pabrik yang berisi rincian daftar ruangan/area, fungsi, dan foto, paling sedikit meliputi: a. Area Penerimaan dan Pengiriman Barang 1) Area penerimaan barang dilengkapi dengan area pengambilan contoh/ sampel bahan baku dan/atau kemas b. Area Penyimpanan 1) Area penyimpanan terdiri dari area penyimpanan bahan baku dan/atau kemas, dan area penyimpanan produk yang saling terpisah satu sama lain 2) Setiap Area Penyimpanan sebagaimana dimaksud pada poin 1 huruf a memiliki area karantina sebelum bahan dan/atau produk dinyatakan lulus uji, dan area penolakan untuk bahan dan/atau produk yang dinyatakan tidak lulus uji c. Area Penimbangan 1) Area Penimbangan terpisah dan didesain khusus untuk kegiatan penimbangan 2) Area Penimbangan dapat menjadi bagian dari Area Penyimpanan atau area produksi d. Area Produksi 1) Tata letak ruang produksi dirancang sedemikian rupa untuk memungkinkan kegiatan produksi dilakukan di area yang saling berhubungan mengikuti urutan tahap produksi 2) Area produksi harus diberikan ventilasi secara efektif dengan menggunakan Fasilitas pengendali udara termasuk filter udara dengan tingkat efisiensi yang dapat mencegah kontaminasi dan kontaminasi silang, pengendali suhu, dan bila perlu, pengendali kelembaban udara sesuai kebutuhan produk yang diproses dan kegiatan yang dilakukan di dalam ruangan dan dampaknya terhadap lingkungan luar pabrik e. Area Pengawasan Mutu 1) Laboratorium pengawasan mutu harus terpisah dari area produksi 2) Area pengujian kimia, biologi, mikrobiologi, dan/atau radioisotop harus terpisah satu dengan yang lain 3) Laboratorium pengawasan mutu didesain sesuai dengan kegiatan yang dilakukan, memadai untuk mencegah kontaminasi silang, memiliki tempat penyimpanan untuk sampel, baku pembanding, pelarut, pereaksi, dan catatan, termasuk area khusus untuk barang berbahaya dan/atau beracun f. Sarana Pendukung 1) Ruang istirahat, ruang kantor, ruang rapat, dan kantin dipisahkan dari area produksi dan laboratorium pengawasan mutu 2) Toilet tidak boleh berhubungan langsung dengan area produksi atau area penyimpanan 3) Ruang ganti pakaian untuk area produksi harus berada di area produksi, namun terpisah dari ruang produksi 4) Bengkel perbaikan dan pemeliharaan peralatan sedapat mungkin terpisah dari area produksi 5) Sarana pemeliharaan hewan harus diisolasi dengan baik terhadap area lain dan dilengkapi pintu masuk terpisah (akses hewan) serta Fasilitas pengendali udara yang terpisah, bila ada 6) Sarana dan Fasilitas penanganan kecelakaan kerja, dan 7) Sarana pendukung lainnya yang diperlukan

editorial.headline: Human Pharmaceuticals as a Broad, Foreign-Open Manufacturing Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 21012 covers finished medicines, supplements, quasi-drugs, radiopharmaceuticals, and biotechnology pharmaceuticals for human use.
editorial.body:
KBLI 21012 is the manufacturing home for human pharmaceutical products. Its scope is broad but still specific: the making and processing of medicines, health or food supplements, and finished quasi-drug preparations for human use. The record names familiar finished forms such as tablets, capsules, ointments, powders, solutions, parenteral solutions, and suspensions. It also includes hormonal contraceptive medicines, radiopharmaceutical production, and biotechnology pharmaceutical production. In plain English, this is not a trading or advisory activity; it is the industrial production and processing of finished pharmaceutical products for people.

The scale picture is unusually wide. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not reserved only for large industrial applicants. A small producer and a larger manufacturer may be looking at the same activity code, provided their real business activity matches this manufacturing scope. That breadth matters editorially because the code is defined by what is made and processed, not by a single company size.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling should be read as 100% for this record. There is no lower cap in the supplied data, and no separate condition, licence, capital number, or ownership qualifier is stated here. The responsible reading is therefore direct: at national level, this activity is foreign-open up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali does not change that into a hidden percentage or a separate local cap. For Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and l4_bali_blocked is false. The record’s reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule supplied here says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, under the cited governor letter. For this activity, the supplied Bali reason says it is not caught by that block. The honest national-vs-Bali picture is therefore aligned rather than contradictory: foreign-open nationally, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali picture is aligned: foreign-open nationally, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium described in the record.

editorial.headline: Veterinary Pharma Is Nationally Open, but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers finished pharmaceutical products for animals, open nationally to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 21013 is about the industrial making, processing, and repackaging of finished pharmaceutical preparations for animals. The record’s scope is broad: powders, tablets, capsules, ointments, solutions, suspensions, and aerosols are all within view when they are prepared as animal medicines. It also brings in animal-specific medical and pharmaceutical support products, including surgical thread, medical diagnostic tools, radioisotopes for radiopharmaceuticals, biotechnology pharmacy, medical dressings, bandages, and similar products dedicated to animals.

That breadth matters because this is not a retail or advisory activity. It is a manufacturing classification for finished animal-health products and related animal-specific medical materials. A founder reading the code should see a production activity: formulation, processing, and repackaging sit at the centre of the scope. The Indonesian title points to veterinary pharmaceutical products, and the scope confirms that the activity reaches across conventional dosage forms and specialised medical-pharmaceutical goods, as long as they are dedicated to animals.

On scale, the national record is inclusive. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators. Nationally, the PMA position is also clean: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%, under the stated presidential regulation source. In national terms, therefore, this is not a code where the record itself imposes a foreign-share cap below full ownership. A foreign-owned structure can read the national line as open, subject only to facts that are actually present in the record.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks the Bali side as blocked, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is equally direct: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” The honest conclusion is therefore narrow but important: nationally, KBLI 21013 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it as PMA today because the Bali record blocks it under the province-wide moratorium rule.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 21013 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it as PMA today.
