data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing and processing active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and excipients for veterinary medicines. It includes substances from chemicals, natural sources, plants, animals, and biological processes—such as vaccines, antisera, antibiotics, vitamins, and purified biochemicals used as raw materials for animal drugs.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, it is not blocked by the general moratorium, but it is classified as medium-high risk; registration is possible but requires verification per specific business address and may involve additional compliance checks due to the risk level.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bahan Baku Farmasi untuk Hewan (21014)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs with expertise in pharmaceutical or biotech manufacturing who want to produce high-value animal health ingredients, targeting export or regional markets from a Bali-based facility.

editorial.headline: Veterinary Pharma Ingredients, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A precise industrial category for makers of raw and auxiliary pharmaceutical materials for animal medicine, nationally open to PMA and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 21014 covers the industrial base behind veterinary pharmaceuticals:** the manufacture and processing of active and supporting drug materials for animals. The record defines a broad technical field: materials derived from chemicals, natural inputs, animals, and plants, including biological products. In practical terms, this is not the retail or clinical face of animal health. It is the upstream activity that produces the substances and preparations later used in veterinary pharmacology, from antisera, blood fractions, vaccines, and homeopathic preparations to antibiotics, vitamins, salicylic and o-acetylsalicylic acid, pharmaceutical salts, chemically pure sugar, processed blood, gland processing, and gland extraction.

That breadth matters because the code is framed around manufacturing and processing rather than a single product line. A company using this classification is positioning itself as a producer of raw pharmaceutical ingredients or auxiliary materials for animal medicines. The Indonesian scope also ends with “Seluruh,” indicating that the activity is described as covering the whole of that stated field. It therefore belongs to businesses that make or process the inputs themselves, not merely those that trade finished veterinary products or provide animal-health services.

On business scale, the record is unusually clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the classification is not confined to large industrial players in the source record; it can describe a manufacturer across the listed scale spectrum, provided the business activity truly matches the defined scope. The important editorial distinction is still the nature of the work: this is a manufacturing KBLI for veterinary pharmaceutical raw materials and supporting ingredients, not a general animal-care category.

The national PMA picture is also straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling should be read as 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record, and none should be inferred. Instead, Bali is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The Bali moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, but this record says this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest reading is therefore clean: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and, on the Bali status given here, not presently blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Medical Diagnostics and Health-Support Manufacturing, Fully Open Nationally
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 21015 covers the manufacture of selected medical diagnostic tools, dressings, cotton products and related health-support goods, with full PMA ownership available nationally.
editorial.body:
KBLI 21015 is a manufacturing code for a very specific part of the health-products economy: the making and processing of medical diagnostic devices and related products within its stated industrial sub-group. In plain English, it covers factories producing externally used contraceptive products, medical diagnostic tools such as pregnancy tests and blood-glucose tests, medical cotton, beauty cotton, cotton buds, bandages, medical gauze, plasters, nasal wash, and personal lubricant. The record frames this as production and processing, not retailing, clinical service, distribution, or medical practice.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the code can fit both smaller manufacturing operations and larger industrial setups, provided the actual activity remains inside the recorded scope. That breadth matters because the products listed range from simple consumables such as cotton, bandages, gauze, and plasters to diagnostic items such as pregnancy and blood-glucose tests. The unifying point is not the sophistication of the product, but the fact that the business is making these health-support goods.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. For a PMA reading, that means the national field is fully open to foreign ownership, according to the source stated in the record: Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lesser foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and there is no separate national caveat to add. The correct editorial conclusion is therefore straightforward: at the national level, KBLI 21015 is foreign-open up to 100%.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. For Bali, the record shows no block on this activity: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. It states the following specific reason: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the stated Bali moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently. This activity is not caught by that block on the record provided. The honest reading is therefore not a hidden Bali restriction, not a separate Bali ownership cap, and not a local-partnership condition; it is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium analysis.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not a hidden Bali restriction; it is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium analysis.

Memiliki bangunan, Fasilitas dan sarana pendukung yang dibuktikan dengan dokumen denah/layout pabrik yang berisi rincian daftar ruangan/area, fungsi, dan foto, paling sedikit meliputi: a. Area Penerimaan dan Pengiriman Barang 1) Area penerimaan barang dilengkapi dengan area pengambilan contoh/ sampel bahan baku dan/atau kemas b. Area Penyimpanan 1) Area penyimpanan terdiri dari area penyimpanan bahan baku dan/atau kemas, dan area penyimpanan produk yang saling terpisah satu sama lain 2) Setiap Area Penyimpanan sebagaimana dimaksud pada poin 1 huruf a memiliki area karantina sebelum bahan dan/atau produk dinyatakan lulus uji, dan area penolakan untuk bahan dan/atau produk yang dinyatakan tidak lulus uji c. Area Penimbangan 1) Area Penimbangan terpisah dan didesain khusus untuk kegiatan penimbangan 2) Area Penimbangan dapat menjadi bagian dari Area Penyimpanan atau area produksi d. Area Produksi 1) Tata letak ruang produksi dirancang sedemikian rupa untuk memungkinkan kegiatan produksi dilakukan di area yang saling berhubungan mengikuti urutan tahap produksi 2) Area produksi harus diberikan ventilasi secara efektif dengan menggunakan Fasilitas pengendali udara termasuk filter udara dengan tingkat efisiensi yang dapat mencegah kontaminasi dan kontaminasi silang, pengendali suhu, dan bila perlu, pengendali kelembaban udara sesuai kebutuhan produk yang diproses dan kegiatan yang dilakukan di dalam ruangan dan dampaknya terhadap lingkungan luar pabrik e. Area Pengawasan Mutu 1) Laboratorium pengawasan mutu harus terpisah dari area produksi 2) Area pengujian kimia, biologi, mikrobiologi, dan/atau radioisotop harus terpisah satu dengan yang lain 3) Laboratorium pengawasan mutu didesain sesuai dengan kegiatan yang dilakukan, memadai untuk mencegah kontaminasi silang, memiliki tempat penyimpanan untuk sampel, baku pembanding, pelarut, pereaksi, dan catatan, termasuk area khusus untuk barang berbahaya dan/atau beracun f. editorial.headline: Natural-Medicine Raw Materials, Reserved for Domestic Capital Nationwide
editorial.standfirst: A precise KBLI for processing extracts, simplisia, galenic preparations, additives, and other inputs used in natural-medicine production for humans.
editorial.body:
This activity sits upstream in the natural-medicine chain. The record describes an industry for processing many kinds of extracts and simplisia, galenic preparations, additives, and other materials used in making natural medicines for humans. Some of those materials may have active properties and some may not; some may be transformed in processing and some may remain substantially unchanged. The important point is functional: these are inputs used in the processing of natural-medicine products, even where not every original ingredient remains visible in the bulk product.

That makes the code useful for founders whose business is not the retail face of wellness, nor the branding of finished consumer products, but the industrial preparation of the materials behind them. It is a production-side classification: a way to place extraction, preparation, and ingredient handling inside the formal KBLI map without overstating the activity as finished-medicine manufacturing. A company using this code should be able to describe its work in the language of the record: processing extracts, simplisia, galenic preparations, additives, or other materials for use in natural-medicine production for humans.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it can describe a small operation as well as a larger industrial setup, provided the actual business remains within this scope. At the national level, PMA is classified as TERBATAS, with the foreign-ownership ceiling at 0% — Perpres 10/2021 as amended by 49/2021 reserves this bidang usaha for domestic capital (Lampiran III entry #5). That restriction is presumed to carry over from the KBLI 2020 code this one renamed (UU 17/2023 Pasal 1; Peraturan BPOM 25/2023; no contrary OSS/BKPM guidance found), and it should not be diluted into a vague caveat: a PT PMA cannot hold this activity.

The Bali picture does not change that national answer. The record marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium — so this is not a Bali-specific block layered on top of an otherwise-open national position. The honest reading is the reverse of what an older version of this page said: nationally this activity is closed to foreign capital, and Bali's risk classification is a separate, secondary fact about licensing authority, not about ownership.

Area Penimbangan 1) Area Penimbangan terpisah dan didesain khusus untuk kegiatan penimbangan 2) Area Penimbangan dapat menjadi bagian dari Area Penyimpanan atau area produksi d. Area Produksi 1) Tata letak ruang produksi dirancang sedemikian rupa untuk memungkinkan kegiatan produksi dilakukan di area yang saling berhubungan mengikuti urutan tahap produksi 2) Area produksi harus diberikan ventilasi secara efektif dengan menggunakan Fasilitas pengendali udara termasuk filter udara dengan tingkat efisiensi yang dapat mencegah kontaminasi dan kontaminasi silang, pengendali suhu, dan bila perlu, pengendali kelembaban udara sesuai kebutuhan produk yang diproses dan kegiatan yang dilakukan di dalam ruangan dan dampaknya terhadap lingkungan luar pabrik e. Area Pengawasan Mutu 1) Laboratorium pengawasan mutu harus terpisah dari area produksi 2) Area pengujian kimia, biologi, mikrobiologi, dan/atau radioisotop harus terpisah satu dengan yang lain 3) Laboratorium pengawasan mutu didesain sesuai dengan kegiatan yang dilakukan, memadai untuk mencegah kontaminasi silang, memiliki tempat penyimpanan untuk sampel, baku pembanding, pelarut, pereaksi, dan catatan, termasuk area khusus untuk barang berbahaya dan/atau beracun f. Sarana Pendukung 1) Ruang istirahat, ruang kantor, ruang rapat, dan kantin dipisahkan dari area produksi dan laboratorium pengawasan mutu 2) Toilet tidak boleh berhubungan langsung dengan area produksi atau area penyimpanan 3) Ruang ganti pakaian untuk area produksi harus berada di area produksi, namun terpisah dari ruang produksi 4) Bengkel perbaikan dan pemeliharaan peralatan sedapat mungkin terpisah dari area produksi 5) Sarana pemeliharaan hewan harus diisolasi dengan baik terhadap area lain dan dilengkapi pintu masuk terpisah (akses hewan) serta Fasilitas pengendali udara yang terpisah, bila ada 6) Sarana dan Fasilitas penanganan kecelakaan kerja, dan 7) Sarana pendukung lainnya yang diperlukan

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 0% — Perpres 10/2021 as amended by 49/2021 reserves this activity for domestic capital (Lampiran III entry #6), presumed to carry over from the KBLI 2020 code this one renamed (UU 17/2023; no contrary OSS/BKPM guidance found). editorial.headline: Natural-Medicine Manufacturing — Reserved for Domestic Capital, No PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 21022 covers human natural-medicine product manufacturing. The national record reserves it for domestic capital — a PT PMA cannot register this activity, in Bali or anywhere else in Indonesia.
editorial.body:
KBLI 21022 is about the industrial processing of natural-medicine products for human use. Its scope is broad, but specific: it covers products made from natural resources in raw form, or not yet through further processing, drawn from plants, animals, microorganisms, minerals, or mixtures of those materials. In practical terms, the record points to an unusually wide range of final forms: powders and instant powders, sliced preparations, pills, dodol or jenang, pilis, tapel, pastilles, tablets, capsules, liquids, solutions, emulsions and suspensions, effervescent products, films, strips, gummy chewables, ointments, lotions, creams and gels, external-use medicinal aerosols, plasters, and suppositories. It also includes the making of jamu drinks and health or food supplements that are not pharmaceutical products.

That scope matters because the activity is not framed as a narrow retail or service category. It is a manufacturing code: the defining act is the processing of natural inputs into finished natural-medicine or related non-pharmaceutical health products for people. The record does not add separate permit conditions, product thresholds, capital figures, or approval timelines, so none should be read into the category here. What can be said, with confidence, is that this code sits on the production side of the natural-health economy, covering both traditional formats and more contemporary delivery forms when they are within the listed natural-medicine and non-pharmaceutical supplement scope.

For registration scale, the record is clean. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not described here as belonging only to large factories or only to small producers; the record makes it available across the full scale range it lists. Nationally, the PMA status is also clear, but in the other direction: it is marked TERBATAS, with a pma_max_asing value of 0. Put plainly, Perpres 10/2021 as amended by 49/2021 reserves this activity for domestic capital (Lampiran III entry #6) — a restriction presumed to carry over from the KBLI 2020 code this one renamed (UU 17/2023 Pasal 1; Peraturan BPOM 25/2023; no contrary OSS/BKPM guidance found).

The Bali picture is a separate, secondary fact — it does not reopen what the national record closes. For Bali, the record assigns the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; its reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That means Bali's own moratorium rule is not the thing standing in a PT PMA's way here — the national ownership cap is. Based only on this record, KBLI 21022 is reserved for domestic capital nationwide, and no Bali-specific reasoning changes that.
editorial.pullQuote: Based only on this record, KBLI 21022 is reserved for domestic capital nationwide — the PT PMA route is unavailable, in Bali and everywhere else in Indonesia.

It includes manufacturing remedies from plant, animal, mineral, or galenical ingredients into forms like powders, tablets, capsules, liquids, creams, gels, and suppositories. editorial.headline: Natural-Medicine Manufacturing for Animals, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers processed natural-medicine products for animals, across all business scales, with a clear national opening and a decisive Bali PMA block.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 21023 is a manufacturing activity for natural-medicine products made for animals.** The record describes the processing of products whose ingredients may come from plants, animal materials, mineral materials, galenic preparations, or mixtures of those sources. It also gives the physical range with useful specificity: powders, sliced or chopped preparations, pills, dodol or jenang forms, pastilles, tablets, capsules, liquids, solutions, emulsions and suspensions, ointments, creams and gels, and suppositories. In plain English, this is not a general animal-care label. It is the industrial preparation of natural-origin medicinal products for animals, covering both traditional solid formats and more modern pharmaceutical-style presentations.

The registration picture is broad on business scale. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the code is not reserved only for large factories. A small producer and a larger industrial manufacturer sit within the same recorded scale spectrum, provided the activity itself remains the processing of the listed natural-medicine products for animals. That matters because the scope is defined by the product and manufacturing activity, not by a single facility size, packaging style, or sales channel. The useful boundary is the one the record gives: ingredients from the listed natural sources, processed into the listed forms, for animals.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership recorded is 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, that is a clean foreign-open result: the record does not show a lower cap, staged threshold, special percentage split, or scale-specific foreign ceiling. A founder reading the national column would therefore see this as a fully open PMA activity at the national level.

Bali changes the practical conclusion. The record marks the Bali side as blocked, with the reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and that is blocked by the Bali moratorium from May 2026. The moratorium rule is even plainer: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest lede is not that this is merely complicated in Bali. It is that a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today, even though the same record shows it as nationally open with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.
editorial.pullQuote: A founder reading only the national column would see a fully open PMA activity, but the Bali record turns that opening into a registration block.

editorial.headline: Natural-Medicine Inputs for Animal Remedies, With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 21024 covers the making of raw and supporting materials used in natural medicines for animals, open nationally to PMA and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 21024 sits in a precise part of the animal-health supply chain: not the retail counter, and not a general veterinary service, but the industrial preparation of materials used to make natural medicines for animals. The record describes the activity as processing many kinds of extracts and *simplisia*, galenic preparations, additives, and other materials. Some may carry an active benefit, some may not. Some may be transformed in processing, while others may remain essentially unchanged. What matters is their destination: they are used in the processing of natural medicines for animals, including by producers of traditional animal medicines.

That makes this code a manufacturing classification for upstream substance preparation. A founder using it should be able to explain the business as the handling and preparation of inputs for animal natural-medicine products, rather than stretching the activity into unrelated animal-care, trading, or clinical territory. The Indonesian scope is broad enough to include extracts, prepared botanical or natural-material inputs, galenic forms, and supporting materials; it is also disciplined by its stated use, which is the processing of natural medicine for animals. The editorial line is therefore simple: this is an industrial raw-material and preparation code for animal natural-medicine production.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. That matters because the classification is not confined to one size of operator in the slim record: small producers and larger industrial setups are both within the scale language provided. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the record, and no special national caveat supplied here. For a foreign-owned company, the national reading is therefore direct: the classification is open, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is full ownership.

The Bali picture is equally important, because this Navigator is not only asking whether the code is open in Indonesia generally. Bali’s moratorium rule, as recorded, blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently. This record, however, does not mark KBLI 21024 as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest conclusion is not that Bali adds a separate percentage, quota, or partnership condition; none appears in the record. The conclusion is narrower and stronger: nationally, this code is open to PMA up to 100%, and in Bali the record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is narrower and stronger: nationally, this code is open to PMA up to 100%, and in Bali the record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Tire Manufacturing That Stays Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22111 covers the making of outer and inner tires from natural or synthetic rubber, with foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22111 is a manufacturing code with a concrete industrial meaning: the making of outer tires and inner tubes, using natural rubber or synthetic rubber as the main material. Its scope reaches across tires for motor vehicles, bicycles, other transport vehicles, and equipment that uses tires. In plain English, this is the production side of the tire business, not retailing, servicing, importing, or general rubber trading. The record points to fabrication of the tire itself: the outer tire, the inner tube, and the rubber-based manufacturing activity behind them.

That breadth matters because the code is not written around one vehicle segment. It is framed around tire use wherever the listed vehicle and equipment categories apply. A founder reading this code should see an industrial activity defined by process and product: making rubber tires and tubes for transport and equipment applications. The slim record does not add technical subcategories, special product thresholds, or extra operating conditions, so the editorial picture should remain exactly that narrow and exact: rubber-based tire and tube manufacturing under a single activity code.

On business scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the code is not confined to a single operating size in the available data. That does not mean every project has the same practical footprint; a small workshop and a large tire plant would plainly be different kinds of undertakings. But the registration scale field itself is inclusive. For this code, the source record allows the full ladder of scale labels, from micro through large, without introducing a separate scale exclusion.

The national foreign-investment position is also clean: the code is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100%. That is the national figure in the record. The Bali side does not create a separate ownership percentage, and it should not be rewritten as one. Instead, Bali is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason given as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. Here, however, l4_bali_blocked is false. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: nationally, foreign ownership is open up to 100%, and in Bali the record does not mark this activity as blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is straightforward: nationally, foreign ownership is open up to 100%, and in Bali the record does not mark this activity as blocked by the moratorium.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business line is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Pembentukan Kembali Ban dan Vulkanisasi Ban (22112)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs with expertise in industrial tyre retreading and remanufacturing, though currently a Bali-based PMA cannot be established for this activity.

editorial.headline: Retreading and Vulcanising Tyres as a Reuse Industry
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22112 covers the repair of used tyres into usable, near-new tyres, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22112 is a practical industrial category: the remaking of used tyres so they can return to use in a condition described by the record as like new. Its scope is not general vehicle repair, and it is not a broad recycling label. It is specifically about tyre repair through retreading and vulcanisation, applied to tyres that have already been used and are then made usable again for motor vehicles, bicycles, other transport vehicles, and equipment that uses tyres.

That gives the activity a clear commercial character. It sits at the point where transport demand, equipment maintenance, and material reuse meet. A business registering this activity is not merely trading tyres; it is carrying out an industrial process on used tyres. The slim record opens the activity across the full scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain terms, the classification can fit a small operator as well as a larger industrial setup, provided the registered activity remains inside the recorded scope of reshaping used tyres into reusable tyres.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown in this record is 100%. There is no basis in the record to add a special shareholding condition, minimum capital figure, tax threshold, operating licence, or timing requirement. The only national ownership number here is the 100% ceiling, and it should be read exactly as that: this activity is nationally open to foreign ownership up to the recorded limit.

The Bali picture is also direct, but it needs to be stated carefully. In the record, Bali does not classify this activity as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, while the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not caught by that block according to the recorded reason. So the honest reading is neither alarmist nor casual: KBLI 22112 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and, on this slim record, it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 22112 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and, on this slim record, it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Smoked Rubber Sheet Manufacturing, Without the Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22121 covers the smoking of rubber into ribbed smoked sheet and smoked rubber sheets, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22121 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label or a broad plantation category. The record defines it as the processing of rubber by smoking, producing products such as smoked rubber or ribbed smoked sheet (RSS), including smoked rubber sheets. In plain English, this is the industrial step where rubber is transformed through a smoking process into sheet-form output. The commercial centre of the code is therefore the making of smoked rubber sheet itself: the process, the finished sheet, and the RSS-style product named in the scope.

The scale profile is unusually broad in the record. This activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, which means the code is not framed only for large industrial operators. A smaller processor and a larger manufacturing plant can both sit inside the registered scale range, provided the business being registered is genuinely the smoking-based rubber-processing activity described above. The code should not be stretched into activities outside that scope; its editorial meaning comes from the specific act of smoking rubber into sheet products, not from every possible rubber-related business.

Nationally, the position is closed to foreign ownership. The record allocates this bidang usaha to Koperasi and UMKM under Perpres 10/2021 as amended by 49/2021 (Lampiran II, the *dialokasikan* column), which sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 0%. A PT PMA cannot hold this activity anywhere in Indonesia, at any business scale.

Bali does not add a second restriction here, and that is worth stating plainly because it is easy to misread as good news. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali, and the reason it gives is precise: OSS risk at the large-business scale is medium-high or high — so the province's moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk activities does not catch it. That is true, and it changes nothing for a foreign investor: the national allocation already closes the activity to a PT PMA everywhere, so there is no Bali route left to unblock.
editorial.pullQuote: In practical editorial terms, KBLI 22121 reads as a foreign-open rubber-sheet manufacturing code nationally, and as not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium information provided here.

editorial.headline: Rubber Sheet and Crepe Rubber Manufacturing, With Bali Still Open
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22122 covers the milling of rubber into smooth sheets and crepe rubber, open nationally to PMA and not blocked for Bali registration under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22122 is a manufacturing activity with a narrow industrial center of gravity: rubber is processed by milling until it becomes sheet-form rubber. The record names two examples inside that frame: smooth rubber sheet and crepe rubber, the wrinkled sheet form created through that same processing logic. This is not a trading classification or a broad plantation label; it is about the transformation step where rubber becomes a sheet product.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification can describe anything from a small rubber-processing setup to a larger industrial operation, provided the real business activity is still the milling of rubber into the sheet forms described in the scope. That matters because the KBLI should follow the actual operating activity, not the founder’s preferred label or the company’s eventual commercial ambition.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. Nationwide, the ceiling for foreign ownership is 100%. The source given for that national reading is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the record, and no separate minimum-capital, licence, tax, or timeline detail to add here. The honest reading is that, at national level, a foreign-owned company can use this code without a foreign-shareholding reduction being stated in the supplied data.

Bali does not change that into a blockage on this record. The Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule still matters as background because Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not caught as blocked in the supplied record. So the practical editorial conclusion is simple: KBLI 22122 is nationally open to 100% PMA, and the Bali-side record supplied does not block PMA registration for it.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 22122 is nationally open to 100% PMA, and the Bali-side record supplied does not block PMA registration for it.

editorial.headline: Crumb Rubber Manufacturing Stands Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22123 covers rubber processing that produces crumb rubber, with access across all recorded business scales and no Bali PMA block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22123 is a focused manufacturing classification: the processing of rubber to produce crumb rubber. The record does not widen the activity beyond that point. Its centre of gravity is industrial transformation, not trading, plantation work, or downstream product claims. For a founder, that makes the code relatively clean to read: it is about the factory-side activity that turns rubber into crumb rubber, and the registration should be judged on that precise scope.

The scale position is unusually broad in the supplied record. The activity is marked open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the code is not confined to a single size of operator. A small processor and a larger industrial setup are both visible within the scale field, although the record itself does not add any threshold, facility requirement, production volume, or capital figure. Those details would have to come from another verified source before they could be treated as compliance facts.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clear. Nationally, PMA status is TERBUKA, with the maximum foreign ownership recorded at 100%. In plain terms, the national record treats this crumb rubber manufacturing activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling shown here. The source attached to that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special national licence condition, ownership partner requirement, or reduced foreign stake, so none should be inferred.

The Bali reading is also important because this is where many open national classifications become practically unavailable for PMA registration. For Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That means the Bali moratorium is relevant context, but not a block for this record. The moratorium rule says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently; this code, as recorded here, is not caught by that block. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: KBLI 22123 is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali record supplied here does not block PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is straightforward: KBLI 22123 is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, and this Bali record does not block it.

editorial.headline: Semi-Finished Rubber for Liquid and Concentrated Forms
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22129 covers natural-rubber processing into other semi-finished products, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22129 is a specialised industrial classification for natural rubber before it becomes a finished rubber product. The record defines it as the processing of natural rubber into other semi-finished rubber products, with examples including concentrated latex and liquid rubber, specifically depolymerised rubber. That makes the activity industrial and intermediate in character: it is not about retailing rubber goods, branding finished products, or running a broad plantation operation. Its centre of gravity is the transformation stage, where natural rubber is processed into forms that can be used further down a production chain.

The code is open across the full business-size ladder recorded for it: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration terms, this means the classification is not reserved in the record for one narrow scale only. A small operator and a large industrial actor are both within the stated scale field, provided the registered activity remains this specific processing of natural rubber into semi-finished products such as concentrated latex or depolymerised liquid rubber. The important discipline is scope: the code should be read from its described activity, not stretched into adjacent rubber businesses that are not named in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is unusually clean. With PMA status recorded as TERBUKA, the classification permits foreign ownership up to its 100% ceiling. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full recorded ceiling. There is no smaller foreign-share cap in the slim record, and there is no extra threshold, permit, local-partner condition, or minimum-capital detail stated here. The source field for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, but the operational conclusion for this editorial is deliberately narrower: for this code, the national PMA line is open, and the recorded ceiling is complete foreign ownership.

Bali does not add a hidden percentage cap in this record. Its local status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali block flag is false. The stated rationale is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is not treated here as blocked by that rule. So the honest reading is not national openness with a Bali prohibition; it is national openness with Bali also not blocking PMA registration under the recorded moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not national openness with a Bali prohibition; it is national openness with Bali also not blocking PMA registration under the recorded moratorium logic.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan barang-barang dari karet untuk keperluan rumah tangga, seperti karpet karet, selang karet, tabung, pipa atau selang air, benang dan tali karet, benang rajut atau tenun dan kain berlapis karet, penutup bingkai penggulung dari karet, matras karet yang bisa dipompa, balon yang bisa dipompa, karet spons/busa, sikat dari karet, dan matras kasur air/waterbed dari karet. Kelompok ini juga mencakup kegiatan pembuatan keset, tali timba, dan pot bunga dari karet.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing household articles from rubber, such as rubber carpets, hoses, tubes, rubber thread, coated fabrics, inflatable mattresses and balloons, sponge rubber, rubber brushes, waterbed mattresses, doormats, bucket ropes, and flower pots.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business line is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Barang dari Karet untuk Keperluan Rumah Tangga (22191)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to produce everyday rubber household goods on a manufacturing scale, who would need to consider locations outside Bali due to current restrictions.

editorial.headline: Rubber Household Goods, With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: A manufacturing code for everyday rubber goods, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
This activity is the manufacturing of rubber goods intended for household use. In practical terms, it covers the making of rubber carpets and mats, rubber hoses, tubes, pipes and water hoses, rubber thread and cord, knitted or woven thread, rubber-coated fabric, rubber covers for roller frames, inflatable rubber mattresses and balloons, sponge or foam rubber, rubber brushes, and rubber waterbed mattresses. The scope also includes rubber doormats, bucket ropes, and flower pots. It is a broad but coherent manufacturing lane: household-use objects where rubber is the defining material, not a decorative or incidental input.

The record opens this activity to every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not presented as a narrow large-industry category only, nor as a protected small-enterprise lane. A small producer making rubber household items and a larger factory producing the same class of goods both sit within the stated scale range, provided the actual activity remains inside the scope described above. The scale field does not add a licence or a threshold; it simply says which sizes of business the record recognises as open for this activity.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national field supplied here treats the activity as open to foreign investment up to the full stated ceiling. There is no partial cap in the record, and no additional national condition is supplied, so the clean reading is that the national position is open rather than restricted.

Bali is also not blocked on this record, but the reason is important. The moratorium text says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. This activity is not caught by that block because the Bali reason states: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest Bali reading is neither a hidden local percentage nor a separate foreign-share cap. The record marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false, because the supplied risk reasoning keeps it outside the moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: The clean reading is that this rubber household-goods activity is nationally foreign-open and, on the supplied Bali record, not blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Barang dari Karet untuk Keperluan Industri
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup usaha pembuatan barang-barang dari karet untuk keperluan industri, seperti konveyour sabuk; fan belt; engine mounting; lining dari karet, pelat karet, lembaran karet, potongan karet, batangan karet, dan bentuk profil karet yang sudah ditambahkan zat aditif; perkakas, cincin dan segel dari karet; batang pipa untuk uap panas dari karet keras dan bahan repair dari karet; termasuk kelengkapan motor penggerak dari karet, transmisi, body, frame, suspensi, steering, dan aksel/axle terbuat dari karet.

editorial.headline: Industrial Rubber Goods That Stay Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22192 covers rubber components for industrial use, from belts and seals to vehicle and machinery parts, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22192 is a manufacturing category for rubber goods made for industrial purposes. Its scope is not general retail or raw rubber trading; it is the production of functional rubber components used inside machinery, industrial systems, and vehicle-related assemblies. The record names conveyor belts, fan belts, engine mountings, rubber linings, rubber plates, sheets, cuts, bars, and profiled rubber forms that have already been treated with additives. It also includes rubber tools, rings, seals, hard-rubber pipe rods for hot steam, rubber repair materials, and rubber parts connected to drive motors, transmissions, bodies, frames, suspensions, steering, and axles.

That makes this code most natural for manufacturers whose product is a working industrial component rather than a finished consumer object. A business registering here is describing a factory activity: shaping, forming, treating, or producing rubber goods that become part of equipment, infrastructure, or mobility systems. The scale range in the record is broad. Micro, small, medium, and large enterprises are all open to this activity, so the code is not limited to one size of operator. The important point is that the registered business must match the activity described in the scope: industrial-use rubber goods, including the listed belts, mountings, linings, seals, profiles, repair materials, and rubber vehicle or machinery components.

Nationally, the investment signal is clean. At the national level, the record lists PMA status as TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. There is no smaller foreign cap in the slim record, and no separate threshold or condition is stated here. The source listed for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, so the editorial reading should stay disciplined: open nationally, with the stated ceiling, and no extra licensing story added beyond the record.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear, because the record does not mark this code as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the record says this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. So the honest conclusion is not a warning dressed as advice: for this code, the national PMA opening and the Bali-side status point in the same direction.
editorial.pullQuote: For this code, the national PMA opening and the Bali-side status point in the same direction.

editorial.headline: Rubber Infrastructure Products, Built for Public Works Use
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22193 covers the manufacturing of rubber compounds and finished rubber goods for infrastructure, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22193 is an industrial manufacturing classification for rubber products made for infrastructure use. Its scope is not general rubber trading or a loose catch-all for rubber goods; the record points to production: rubber compounds and rubber-based items used in roads, ports, bridges, rail, canals, traffic management, and related civil works. The examples are practical and physical: rubber asphalt compound, activated natural rubber powder, dock fenders, seismic bearings, bridge bearings, rubber dams, rubber road bumps, rail pads, rail guards, canal blocking, and traffic cones.

That makes this code a home for operators whose business is built around making infrastructure-grade rubber components, not merely installing them or reselling them. The activity can sit at every scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain founder terms, the classification is not reserved only for large factories, although the products themselves can serve heavy-duty public or industrial environments. A small producer of qualifying rubber infrastructure goods and a larger manufacturer serving transport or civil-work demand both belong within the same scope, provided the real activity is manufacturing the goods described by the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. For PMA, the record lists its status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That means the national entry shown here is foreign-open, without a reduced foreign stake in the slim record. The source attached to that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the record adds a special minimum capital figure, extra threshold, sector licence, or operational timeline, so none should be read into it. The strongest national conclusion is simply this: for this activity, the record treats PMA participation as open up to 100%.

Bali is also not blocked in this record, but the reason matters. The province’s moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That is not a separate Bali ownership percentage, and it is not a new cap. It is a moratorium reading: because the record places the relevant large-scale risk above the blocked Low and Medium-Low band, KBLI 22193 is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is foreign-open up to 100%, and the Bali record does not mark this activity as blocked by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Medical Rubber Manufacturing with a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22194 covers rubber goods for health support, open nationally to foreign capital and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22194 is a manufacturing classification for rubber goods made to support health needs. The record names contraceptive sheaths, baby teats, compression tools, medical rubber gloves, and urinary or Folley catheters as examples of the activity. In plain English, this is not general rubber trading or a broad health-service category; it is the industrial making of specific rubber-based products used in health, care, and medical-support contexts.

The registration picture is broad on business scale. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification is not reserved in the record for only one size of enterprise. A smaller local manufacturer and a larger industrial setup are both inside the stated scale envelope, provided the activity they register is truly the making of these rubber health-support goods. The editorial point is scope discipline: the code follows the manufactured article, not the later user of the article.

Nationally, the foreign-investment line is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record supplied here does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. There is no basis in the record to add a licensing threshold, a minimum capital figure, a special permit, or a timing condition; those facts are simply not present in the supplied data.

The Bali reading is also clean, but it must be stated carefully. The record does not block this code for PMA registration in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is given in the record as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the moratorium rule supplied here says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This activity is therefore not presented as a Bali-blocked code in the record. The honest national-vs-Bali picture is aligned rather than contradictory: foreign-open nationally, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium data supplied.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Barang Lainnya dari Karet YTDL
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan barang lainnya dari karet, seperti pembuatan barang dari ban bekas dan sisa macam-macam barang dari karet, antara lain sarung tangan karet selain untuk keperluan medis; barang-barang karet untuk pakaian (jika hanya disatukan bersama, bukan dijahit), seperti sisir, jepit rambut, rol rambut dan sejenisnya dari karet keras; kain tekstil yang diresapi, dilapisi atau dilaminasi dengan karet, dengan karet sebagai bahan pokok; topi dan baju mandi dari karet; jas hujan dan pakaian selam dari karet; dan alat-alat seks dari karet.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This group includes the manufacture of other rubber products, such as items made from used tires and various rubber scraps. It covers non-medical rubber gloves; rubber accessories for clothing that are only bonded together, not sewn, like combs, hair clips, and rollers made of hard rubber; textile fabrics impregnated, coated, or laminated with rubber where rubber is the chief material; rubber bathing caps and swimwear; rubber raincoats and diving suits; and rubber sex aids.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is NOT blocked by the 13 May 2026 moratorium — its OSS risk class at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale is medium-high or high, which the moratorium leaves open. A PT PMA can pursue this code in Bali, subject to the standard licensing for its risk class.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Barang Lainnya dari Karet YTDL (22199)? Here is the honest national-vs-Bali picture before you plan a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who can meet the higher-risk licensing requirements — one of the doors that stays open in Bali.

editorial.headline: Rubber Goods Beyond the Standard Catalogue
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22199 is open nationally to foreign ownership and, on this record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22199 covers a practical manufacturing category: other rubber goods not separately defined elsewhere in the record. Its scope is broad, but not vague. It points to the making of rubber articles from used tyres and assorted rubber remnants, alongside non-medical rubber gloves, hard-rubber personal items such as combs, hair clips and hair rollers, rubber-based coated or laminated textile fabrics, rubber hats and bathing garments, rubber raincoats and diving suits, and rubber sex products. The connective tissue is material and process: these are finished goods where rubber is the defining substance, not merely a decorative or incidental component.

For founders, that breadth matters because the code can sit behind very different operating models. A small workshop making accessories from hard rubber, a producer working with tyre-derived material, and a larger factory producing rubber apparel or laminated textile goods can all fall within the same stated scope if the activity remains inside the record’s description. The scale field is unusually open: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed. That means the record does not reserve the activity for one business size; it recognises the same activity across micro, small, medium, and large registrations.

The national foreign-ownership position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. In plain English, this is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, based on the listed PMA source. There is no foreign-stake cap below full ownership in the slim record, and there is no separate operational threshold, minimum capital figure, licence timeline, or special permit detail supplied here. The safe reading is therefore narrow and useful: nationally, KBLI 22199 is open for PMA ownership at the ceiling shown in the record.

The Bali-side reading is also direct. The record does not block this activity for Bali PMA registration: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the record also states the Bali moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the Bali reason says the activity is not caught by that moratorium logic at the large scale. The honest conclusion is not a hidden Bali percentage or a special local quota; it is simply that the slim record shows no Bali moratorium block for this code today.

data.judul: Industri Barang dari Plastik untuk Bangunan
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan barang dari plastik untuk bangunan, seperti pintu, jendela, kusen, daun penutup jendela, kerai, skirting boards dari plastik; tangki, tandon air dari plastik; penutup lantai, dinding, dan langit-langit plastik dalam bentuk gulungan atau lembaran; serta peralatan kebersihan dari plastik, seperti gorden plastik, shower, wastafel, lavatory pan, dan bak penyiram (flushing).

editorial.headline: Building Plastics Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22201 covers plastic building products, from frames and tanks to flooring sheets and sanitary fittings, with national PMA ownership open up to 100%.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 22201 is the manufacturing lane for plastic goods used in buildings.** Its scope is practical and material: plastic doors, windows, frames, window shutters, blinds, and skirting boards; plastic tanks and water reservoirs; plastic floor, wall, and ceiling coverings in rolls or sheets; and plastic sanitary equipment such as curtains, showers, sinks, lavatory pans, and flushing tanks. In plain English, this is not trading in construction supplies. It is the making of plastic building components and related fixtures.

The record opens the activity across every business scale listed: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed only for a large factory profile. A smaller producer making a narrower range of plastic building items and a larger industrial operator making a broader product line both sit within the same activity description, so long as the work remains manufacturing goods of this kind. The centre of gravity is the product and the production activity, not the customer segment or the construction project where the goods may later be installed.

Nationally, the PMA signal is clear. The record marks the code as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower percentage in the record, and no special national qualification is stated here beyond that open status and the listed maximum foreign ownership. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest national reading is therefore simple: this activity is open, and the record allows foreign ownership up to the full 100% ceiling.

Bali does not change that into a separate percentage or a hidden local cap. The Bali-side status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked marked false. The record gives a precise basis: “At scale Besar, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this record is not caught by that block on the stated reason. So the balanced conclusion is that KBLI 22201 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not turn this code into a hidden percentage cap: the record marks it as not blocked by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Plastic and Bioplastic Packaging, Open Nationally and Clear for Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22202 covers the making of plastic and bioplastic packaging, with access across all business scales and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22202 is a manufacturing code for packaging made from plastic and bioplastic. Its scope is practical and broad: bags and plastic pouches, sacks, cosmetic packaging, film packaging, medicine packaging, food packaging, and other plastic packaging forms such as containers, bottles, boxes, cases, racks, and similar items. In plain English, this is the industrial home for businesses that turn plastic or bioplastic into packaging products, whether the final format is flexible, rigid, consumer-facing, or part of a product supply chain.

The record opens the activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because this is not framed only as a large-factory category. A small packaging producer and a larger industrial operation both sit inside the same activity description, provided the business is actually making the packaging products described in the scope. The code is therefore less about a single product shape and more about the function of the output: packaging made from plastic or bioplastic, including packaging for food, cosmetics, medicines, film, and general storage or presentation.

Viewed nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling. There is no basis in the slim record to add a separate capital threshold, special licence, local partnership condition, or narrower operational test. The clean reading is that a foreign-owned setup may use this code nationally, up to the 100% foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record.

Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is aligned rather than contradictory: nationally foreign-open, and in Bali not blocked by the moratorium according to the fields provided. The practical conclusion is narrow but useful: for this record, KBLI 22202 can be read as a plastic and bioplastic packaging manufacturing activity that remains available across all listed scales, with a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.pullQuote: For this record, the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and Bali is not marked as blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.
