intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of plastic pipes, hoses, and tubes—along with related fittings—typically from PVC, PE, or PP. It includes everything from simple water pipes to industrial tubing and joint components.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Pipa Plastik dan Perlengkapannya (22203)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: This suits a foreign manufacturer with existing plastic extrusion or piping expertise who wants to serve the Indonesian market, but for a Bali location would need to explore a domestic nominee structure or wait for the moratorium to lift.

editorial.headline: Plastic Pipe Manufacturing With a Clean Bali Position
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22203 covers the making of plastic pipes, hoses, tubes, and fittings, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22203 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading or installation category. The record defines it around the making of pipes and hoses from plastic, including plastic tubes and pipe fittings. It also identifies the permitted material families in plain industrial terms: polyvinyl chloride, polyethylene, and polypropylene. That gives the code a clear production character: it is about turning plastic materials into pipe, hose, tube, and fitting products.

The registration picture is unusually broad on business scale. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not framed only for large factories. A smaller producer and a larger industrial operator sit within the same recorded scale range, provided the activity being registered remains the manufacture of the plastic pipe, hose, tube, or fitting goods described in the scope. The editorial boundary matters here: the record supports manufacturing those goods; it does not add separate claims about distribution, installation, certification, or downstream permits.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing value of 100, which means the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The cited PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is therefore not a capped foreign-shareholding activity in the record; it is foreign-open up to the full percentage stated there.

Bali does not add a separate percentage, quota, or local-partner condition in the record. In Bali, the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, while l4_bali_blocked remains false. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters as context because the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But for this code, the recorded Bali result is not a block. The honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is clean: nationally it is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Plastic Sheet Manufacturing Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22204 covers sheet-form plastics, from PE and PP sheets to PVC, imitation leather, formica, plastic glass, film, foil, and cut plastic pieces.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22204 is a manufacturing classification for plastic sheet products. The record describes a broad industrial activity: making plastic sheets of various kinds, including polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC), as well as imitation leather, formica, and plastic glass. It also reaches plate plastic, plastic sheets, plastic blocks, film, foil, and cut plastic pieces, whether adhesive or non-adhesive. In plain English, this is the code for producing plastic material in flat or sheet-based forms rather than for a retail, trading, or installation activity.

The scale picture is unusually wide. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe a small production operation as well as a larger industrial plant. That range matters because the activity itself is defined by what is made, not by a single factory size. A founder reading this code should focus on whether the proposed business is genuinely manufacturing these plastic sheet, film, foil, plate, block, or cut-piece products. If the activity is only downstream use of such materials, the record here does not say that; this code is about making them.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` set at 100, and the source given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and there is no recorded national condition here beyond that stated PMA ceiling and source.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The reason is stated directly: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently; this activity is not caught by that block on the record provided. The honest reading is therefore simple: nationally foreign-open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.

editorial.headline: Plastic Household Goods Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22205 covers plastic household equipment, from mats and buckets to kitchenware, toilet goods, and durable floor coverings.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22205 is a manufacturing classification for household equipment and fittings made from plastic, excluding furniture. Its scope is practical and domestic: mats, carpets, buckets, vases, toothbrushes, plastic baby bottles, tableware, kitchen equipment, plastic toilet goods, and durable floor coverings such as vinyl and linoleum. In plain English, this is the code for making plastic household goods that end up in bathrooms, kitchens, floors, and everyday home use.

The record opens this activity across the full business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed only for a narrow factory profile. A small producer making plastic household fittings and a larger industrial operation making durable floor coverings can both sit within the same activity description, provided the actual registered business is manufacturing the goods described in the scope. The scope is not retail, distribution, furniture, or a general plastics category; its center of gravity is the making of household-use plastic equipment and supporting goods.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national classification is not the obstacle: the activity is open, and the stated ceiling reaches full foreign ownership. There is no lower ownership cap in the record, and no separate national condition, licence, threshold, capital rule, or timeline is stated here.

The Bali picture is also relatively clear, but for a different reason. For Bali, the record shows no block: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not caught by that block on the record supplied. So the honest reading is straightforward: KBLI 22205 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not block it under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is straightforward: KBLI 22205 is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and the Bali record does not block it under the stated moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. editorial.headline: Industrial Plastic Parts With a Clear PMA Route in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22206 covers technical and industrial plastic goods, from machine components to conveyor belts, and is nationally open to full foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22206 is the industrial end of plastic manufacturing: not household packaging as a general idea, but plastic goods and equipment made for technical or industrial use. The record’s scope points to plastic machine parts, motor-drive components, transmission parts, body and frame elements, suspension and steering components, axles, industrial bottles, pipes, plastic cabinets, and conveyor belts. In plain English, this is the code for plastic fabrication where the finished output serves machinery, production systems, vehicles, or industrial infrastructure.

That breadth matters because the activity is open across every business scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small workshop producing specialised plastic fittings and a larger manufacturer supplying plastic technical components can both sit within the same activity description, provided the actual business is still the manufacture of plastic goods and equipment for technical or industrial purposes. The code is therefore not defined by company size; it is defined by what is being made and the industrial function those products serve.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%. That means the national classification, on this record, does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. It is still important to keep that sentence narrow: the record gives the PMA status, the maximum foreign share, the legal source, and the eligible scales; it does not create any separate licence, capital threshold, operating permit, or tax conclusion beyond those fields.

The Bali reading is also unusually clean. The record does not mark this code as blocked for PMA registration in Bali. For Bali, it carries the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That sits against the moratorium rule recorded here, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali. For this activity, the supplied record’s conclusion is that the moratorium does not block it. The honest planning takeaway is therefore not a hidden Bali ceiling or a local-partner condition; it is that this industrial plastic manufacturing code is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and, on the Bali fields provided, not blocked by the island-wide PMA moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». editorial.headline: Plastic Manufacturing at the Edge of the Standard Catalogue
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 22209 is the home for specialised plastic goods that do not sit neatly elsewhere, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 22209 covers the manufacture of other plastic goods: the useful, specific, often highly engineered objects that fall outside the more obvious plastic-product categories. The record points to office and educational equipment, plastic health and laboratory equipment such as infusion bags and tubes, cellophane film or sheets, artificial stone made from plastic, non-electric plastic signs, and a long tail of finished goods. It also reaches into items as varied as head coverings, insulation equipment, lighting-equipment parts, certain sealed or joined plastic garments, furniture fittings, statues, plastic adhesive tape, plastic wall coverings, durable plastic shoes, plastic cigar and cigarette holders, combs, plastic hair curlers, and distinctive plastic objects.

That breadth matters. This is not a casual trading label for anything made of plastic; it is a manufacturing classification for producers whose output is plastic goods not otherwise captured in the record’s main list. The same scope also includes processing and finishing activities for plastic goods, including coating with metal or other coating substances and painting. The record draws one boundary inside that finishing language: it excludes such work where it concerns special plastic parts and accessories for motor vehicles. In practical editorial terms, this code is best understood as a home for diversified plastic fabrication and finishing, especially where the product is specific, functional, or niche rather than part of a more narrowly defined line.

The scale position is broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the record does not reserve it only for large industrial operators or only for domestic small enterprise. At the national level, PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a clean national signal: a foreign-owned company can use this classification at full foreign ownership where the activity and scale match the record. The source for that national investment position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, which is the only national source named here.

Bali adds an important but favourable local reading. The province’s moratorium blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across the island on a permanent basis, according to the record’s moratorium rule. This activity, however, is not blocked in Bali: the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is medium-high or high, so it is not caught by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning that Bali shuts the door, but a narrower one: the national position is fully foreign-open, and the Bali-side record does not block PMA registration under the moratorium stated here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Sheet Glass Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23111 covers the making, shaping, and processing of sheet glass, with national PMA access up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23111 is a manufacturing code for sheet glass: the industrial making of flat glass in several finished or semi-finished forms. Its scope covers clear colourless sheet glass, clear coloured sheet glass, coloured opaque sheet glass, stained glass, engraved glass, and mirror glass. It also reaches beyond the initial making of the sheet itself, because the record includes the forming and processing of sheet glass within the same activity. In plain terms, this is not a general retail or installation category; it is about producing and working sheet glass as an industrial material and finished surface.

That scope matters because the code can fit businesses operating at very different sizes. The record opens it to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so the activity is not reserved only for large industrial plants. A smaller workshop focused on processed or shaped sheet glass can sit within the same activity logic as a larger manufacturer producing clear, coloured, opaque, stained, engraved, or mirror glass, provided the registered activity remains the making, forming, or processing of sheet glass. The scale range is broad, but the commercial identity stays specific: sheet glass is the centre of the registration.

Nationally, the investment signal is straightforward. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is **100%** under the cited source. For a foreign-owned company, that means the national record does not impose a lower foreign-share cap for this activity. The important discipline is to read that exactly as far as the record goes: it confirms openness and the foreign-ownership ceiling, but it does not by itself add any extra licence, permit, capital threshold, tax treatment, or operating timeline.

The Bali picture is also unusually clear. Bali’s moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the province, but this record is not blocked. The reason given is that at **Besar** scale the OSS risk is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it does not fall into the moratorium’s blocked Low or Medium-Low risk band. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning against Bali registration, but a distinction: nationally this activity is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is recorded as not blocked by the moratorium, with the Bali status marked **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning against Bali registration, but a distinction: nationally this activity is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali it is recorded as not blocked by the moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of safety glass types such as tempered, laminated, and insulated glass used in construction, automotive, or protective applications. It involves industrial-scale production, not simple glass cutting or installation.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership, but Bali treats it as a medium-high/high-risk activity. It is not blocked by the general moratorium; however, your chosen address will face closer environmental and zoning verification before permits are issued.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kaca Pengaman (23112)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign glass manufacturers targeting Bali’s construction or automotive safety glass market and ready to set up a compliant industrial facility.

editorial.headline: Safety Glass Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23112 covers the manufacture of tempered, laminated, insulating and other safety glass, open nationally to PMA and not blocked in Bali under the stated risk reading.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23112 is the manufacturing home for safety glass: glass made to perform beyond ordinary sheet glass in strength, protection, layering, insulation or a comparable safety function. The record names tempered safety glass, laminated safety glass, insulating safety glass and other safety glass within the same activity. In plain terms, this is not a trading or installation category; it is about making the glass product itself, where the defining feature is that the finished material is engineered as safety glass.

The registration profile is broad. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the same KBLI can describe a small producer as well as a large industrial operation, provided the registered activity remains the manufacture of safety glass. Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward: the code is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. For founders reading the code from a foreign-investment angle, that means the national record does not impose a reduced foreign-share cap for this activity.

The Bali reading is equally important because it does not simply mirror the national headline. Bali’s moratorium rule, as stated in the record, blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the province on a permanent, island-wide basis. That is the gate a founder has to test before treating a nationally open activity as available in Bali. Here, the record says the activity is not blocked: at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it outside the blocked Low and Medium-Low band described by the moratorium.

So the honest picture is open nationally and not blocked in Bali on the record provided. That does not turn the category into a casual checkbox; it simply means the Bali-side moratorium is not the barrier identified for this KBLI. The decisive facts are narrow and concrete: this is safety-glass manufacturing, it is open to every listed scale, it is nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and Bali’s listed status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because the stated risk position keeps it outside the moratorium block.

editorial.headline: Other Glass Manufacturing with a Clear Bali PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: For glass tubes, rods, pipe glass, glass bars and flat-glass processing, this code is nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23119 is the registration home for a focused part of glass manufacturing: the making of assorted glass products such as tubes, rods, glass bars and glass pipes, together with the forming and processing of flat glass. Its centre of gravity is not branding, distribution or installation, but the industrial act of making and shaping glass articles that sit outside the narrower named glass-manufacturing categories in the source record. For founders, that makes the scope relatively practical: if the commercial activity is built around producing or processing these glass forms, this is the code that frames the business activity.

The scale access is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar operators, so it can sit under a small production undertaking as well as a larger industrial setup. That matters because KBLI choice is not only a label on a company deed; it is the operating perimeter that follows the business into OSS classification, risk treatment and later conversations with banks, landlords, partners and government systems. A founder using this code should be able to explain the activity in plain operational language: what glass is being made, what form it takes, and whether the business is manufacturing, forming or processing flat glass rather than merely trading finished items.

At the national level, foreign-investment treatment is unambiguous. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a PMA maximum foreign ownership figure of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In clean terms, the national ceiling allows full foreign ownership. There is no reduced foreign-stake cap in the slim record, and no capital threshold, licence timeline or special permit condition is stated here. The editorial conclusion should therefore stay disciplined: for national foreign-ownership purposes, this activity is open, and the recorded ceiling is complete foreign ownership.

Bali adds the question that founders most often get wrong: whether the province-level moratorium blocks PMA registration even where the national list is open. Here, the answer is favourable. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the activity is not blocked because the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, while Bali’s moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island. So the honest Bali reading is not “nationally open but locally closed”; it is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the facts supplied. That does not create extra obligations beyond the record, but it does give a founder the key directional answer: this is a glass-manufacturing code that can be considered for PMA registration in Bali today under the stated classification.
editorial.pullQuote: This is not a case of a nationally open activity being shut down by the Bali moratorium; on the supplied record, it remains open and not blocked.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Perlengkapan dan Peralatan Rumah Tangga dari Kaca
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan berbagai macam perlengkapan rumah tangga dari kaca, seperti cangkir, gelas minum, piring, mangkuk, teko, stoples, asbak dan botol susu bayi, termasuk juga kegiatan pembuatan barang-barang pajangan dari kaca, seperti patung atau arca dari kaca, vas, lampu kristal, semprong lampu tekan, dan semprong lampu tempel. Kelompok ini juga mencakup pembuatan berbagai macam wadah atau kemasan dari kaca dan kristal, seperti botol dan guci, termasuk kaca berongga.

editorial.headline: Glassware Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23121 covers household glassware, display pieces, and glass or crystal containers, with foreign ownership open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23121 is the industrial home for making glass objects that sit close to daily life: cups, drinking glasses, plates, bowls, teapots, jars, ashtrays, and baby milk bottles. Its scope also reaches beyond utility into display and decorative glass, including glass statues or figures, vases, crystal lamps, pressure-lamp chimneys, and wall-lamp chimneys. The same activity group includes the making of glass and crystal containers or packaging, such as bottles and jars, including hollow glass. In practical terms, this is not retailing glassware or merely trading finished stock; it is the manufacturing activity behind household, decorative, and container glass products.

The scale profile is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification can serve anything from a small workshop producing household glass items to a larger industrial operation making containers or display pieces. That breadth matters because the same KBLI title carries both everyday domestic objects and more formal glass or crystal packaging. A founder using this code should read it through the manufacturing acts named in the scope: making the items, shaping the output category, and staying within household glassware, decorative glass objects, and glass or crystal containers.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, so the national reading is not a partial opening. For a foreign-owned setup, the central point is that KBLI 23121 is recorded as open to PMA at up to full foreign ownership. Nothing in the record adds a minimum capital figure, operating threshold, special deadline, or separate licence condition, so none should be assumed from the classification alone.

Bali does not change that outcome into a closure. The province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record marks KBLI 23121 as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says its OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That is the honest national-versus-Bali picture: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and in Bali not blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic. The classification still needs to be kept close to the activity itself: manufacturing household glassware, decorative glass pieces, and glass or crystal containers, not a broader glass business by implication.
editorial.pullQuote: That is the honest national-versus-Bali picture: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and in Bali not blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Peralatan Laboratorium dan Kesehatan dari Kaca
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan berbagai macam peralatan laboratorium dan kesehatan dari kaca, termasuk alat laboratorium klinis yang pada umumnya untuk keperluan diagnosis seperti tabung uji untuk sampel biologis (darah, urin, dan saliva), serta alat laboratorium nonklinis dan kesehatan seperti botol serum/infus, ampul, tabung uji, tabung ukur, kaca sorong mikroskop, kuvet, dan desikator.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup peralatan laboratorium dari kaca yang tahan api pada suhu sangat tinggi, seperti labu distilasi, lihat kelompok 23919.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of glass laboratory and health equipment, such as test tubes for biological samples (blood, urine, saliva), serum bottles, ampoules, volumetric tubes, microscope slides, cuvettes, and desiccators. It includes both clinical diagnostic tools and general laboratory glassware, but excludes high-temperature-resistant glass equipment like distillation flasks (covered elsewhere).
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Laboratorium dan Kesehatan dari Kaca (23122)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur looking to manufacture specialized glass medical or lab equipment, but they must currently set up outside Bali because of the ongoing moratorium.

editorial.headline: Glassware for Clinics and Laboratories, Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the manufacture of glass laboratory and health equipment, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23122 is a manufacturing code for glass equipment used in laboratory and health settings. Its center of gravity is practical, clinical, and technical: the making of glass items used in diagnosis and routine laboratory work, including clinical laboratory tools for biological samples such as blood, urine, and saliva. The scope also reaches nonclinical laboratory and health glassware, including serum or infusion bottles, ampoules, test tubes, measuring tubes, microscope slides, cuvettes, and desiccators.

That makes this a code for producers, not traders or service operators. A company registering here is positioning itself as a manufacturer of defined glass instruments and containers for laboratory and health use. The record also draws a boundary around the activity: it does not cover fire-resistant glass laboratory equipment designed for very high temperatures, such as distillation flasks. For founders, that boundary matters because the commercial label “laboratory glassware” can sound broader than the registered activity actually is.

The scale position is unusually broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code can accommodate anything from a very small manufacturing setup to a large industrial operation, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope. It is not framed as a niche reserved for one enterprise size. The relevant question is therefore less whether the scale is available, and more whether the actual production line matches the glass laboratory and health equipment described in the record.

The national PMA position is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows full foreign ownership. Bali does not add a registration block on this record. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but the Bali reason here states that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest picture is therefore straightforward: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and in Bali not blocked by the PMA moratorium on the information provided.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing of miscellaneous glass products not classified elsewhere—such as fiberglass, glass wool insulation, nonwoven glass, glass bricks, tiles, roofing, paving, aquariums, watch glasses, optical elements (non-optical working), imitation jewellery glass, prayer beads, and enamelware. Essentially, it is the catch-all for glass fabrication beyond the more specific glass industry codes.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open (100% foreign ownership) for PMA companies. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible. A PMA can therefore not be established in Bali under this code at present.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Produk Lainnya dari Kaca (23129)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign manufacturer planning to produce specialised glass products for construction, craft, or industrial supply chains.

editorial.headline: A Broad Glass-Manufacturing Code With National PMA Access
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23129 covers specialist glass and crystal products, open to all business scales nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23129 is the broad manufacturing home for glass products that do not sit inside the narrower named glass-product categories. Its practical range is wide: devotional beads such as tasbih and rosaries, glass beads, enameled glassware, aquariums, fiberglass, glass wool and nonwoven glass products, watch and wall-clock glass, non-working optical glass and elements, glass used in imitation jewelry, insulating glass and glass insulation fittings, and other glass or crystal products. It also reaches construction-facing glass materials such as glass bricks, tiles, roof tiles, paving blocks, and wall partitions.

That breadth matters because this is not a retail or trading classification. The center of gravity is production: shaping, forming, or manufacturing glass into finished or semi-finished goods for consumer, decorative, technical, insulation, or building-material use. A founder using this code should be describing an industrial activity, not merely the sale, installation, or distribution of glass items. The record supports registration across the full size spectrum: micro, small, medium, and large enterprises are all listed as open scales.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. In plain terms, the national rule shown in the record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. There is no lower national cap in the slim record, so none should be implied. The editorial caution is therefore not about a national shareholding limit, but about reading the Bali position separately from the national PMA status.

For Bali, the same record gives a more specific and still usable answer. Bali’s island-wide moratorium blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The reason given is that OSS risk at large scale is medium-high or high, so it is not caught by the moratorium. That means the honest Bali read is not “blocked despite being nationally open.” It is nationally open to PMA, and in Bali it is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked. The practical conclusion is narrow but important: based only on this record, a foreign-owned setup can treat KBLI 23129 as available nationally and not blocked by the Bali moratorium, while still respecting that the record’s Bali comfort rests on the risk profile at large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: The caution is not a national foreign-ownership cap, but the need to read Bali’s moratorium status separately from the national PMA rule.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Refractory Building Materials with a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of refractory bricks, mortar, cement, concrete, and similar composites, open nationally to PMA and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 23911 is a manufacturing category for materials built to withstand fire and high heat.** Its scope is not ordinary brickmaking or general cement trade; it is specifically the production of refractory bricks, refractory mortar, refractory cement, refractory concrete, and similar refractory composites. The record names alumina, silica, and basic or alkaline materials as examples, which places the activity in a technical industrial lane: products whose defining feature is resistance to fire, rather than decorative finish, structural form, or retail use.

The registration profile is unusually broad across business scale. The activity is open to micro, small, medium, and large operators, so the same code can describe a small producer making refractory mortar as well as a larger industrial operation producing refractory concrete or composite materials. That breadth matters editorially because the code is defined by the nature of the product, not by the size of the enterprise. A founder reading it should focus first on whether the planned output is genuinely refractory brick, mortar, cement, concrete, or a similar heat-resistant composite, because that is the substance of the classification.

At the national level, the stance on foreign investment is clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this as open to PMA without a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The national position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no basis in the slim record to add a minimum capital figure, extra licensing condition, special tax point, or operational threshold, so those questions sit outside this editorial. What the record does say is enough: as a national PMA classification, this activity is open at the recorded ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that position. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis, but this record states that KBLI 23911 is not blocked. The reason is specific: at large scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by that moratorium. That does not turn the category into a casual administrative choice; it simply means the Bali-side status is not a PMA registration block under the stated moratorium rule. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: for foreign-owned setups, this refractory-materials manufacturing activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership and, on the record provided, remains registrable in Bali rather than barred by the provincial PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For foreign-owned setups, this refractory-materials activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership and remains registrable in Bali under the record provided.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Refractory Manufacturing Beyond the Standard Firebrick
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers specialised heat-resistant products, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is for manufacturers making refractory products beyond ordinary fire bricks: heat-resistant tiles, blocks, tubes, pipes, filters, melting vessels, distillation flasks and similar industrial components built to withstand intense heat. Its scope also reaches refractory intermediate products made from mined or quarried non-metallic minerals such as gravel, stone or clay, including goods containing magnesite, dolomite or chromite. In plain terms, this is not decorative ceramics or general construction material; it is industrial material for environments where heat, chemical exposure and durability matter.

The record opens the activity across the full scale ladder: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the code is not reserved only for heavy industrial players, even though the product category naturally points toward technical manufacturing. A founder may be entering through a narrow product line, a specialised component, or a larger refractory-material operation; the scale field says the activity is available at every listed business size. The defining question is therefore not whether the applicant is large enough to fit the classification, but whether the business is genuinely making the refractory goods described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The activity is marked open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no ownership cap to soften or interpret in the national field: a PMA company may hold the full foreign stake under the record’s stated source. For founders, that makes the national reading unusually direct. The classification describes a manufacturing activity, the scale access is broad, and the ownership field does not impose a partial-foreign structure.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The island-wide moratorium in the record blocks low and medium-low risk activities for PMA, but this activity is not blocked because its OSS risk at large scale is medium-high/high. The Bali status is therefore an open-but-watchful one rather than a prohibition: not blocked by the moratorium, yet carrying the record’s higher-risk signal at large scale. The honest reading is simple. data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Clay Brick Manufacturing Is Nationally Open and Bali-Clear
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23921 covers clay and ceramic brick production, open across all business scales and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23921 is a manufacturing code for the production of clay or ceramic bricks. Its scope is not limited to one brick format: it covers pressed bricks, hollow bricks, decorative bricks, non-pressed bricks, and perforated bricks. The same activity description also includes the making of red cement and clay gravel. In practical terms, this is the industrial home for operators whose core business is transforming clay or ceramic material into building inputs, whether the output is structural, decorative, or granular.

The code is open at every listed business scale: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar**. That breadth matters because the activity is not framed only as a large-plant category. A small producer and a larger industrial manufacturer are both within the record’s scale range, provided the registered activity remains the making of the covered brick, red-cement, or clay-gravel products. The editorial point is simple but important: this is a production code, not a trading label or a construction-services label. The registered business should be anchored in making the materials described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the maximum foreign ownership shown in the record is **100%**. There is no foreign-equity cap below full ownership in the slim record, so none should be invented. For a foreign-owned setup looking at this activity at the national level, the record supports a straightforward reading: KBLI 23921 is open to PMA, including up to full foreign ownership.

Bali does not change that conclusion on the data provided. The province’s moratorium blocks low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, but this record says the Bali-side status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and that the OSS risk at **Besar** scale is medium-high or high, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That is the honest national-versus-Bali picture: this activity is nationally open, and the Bali flag in the record does not close it for PMA registration. The right caution is not to add imaginary conditions; the record gives an open national ceiling, all four scales, and a Bali reason that points away from the moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-versus-Bali picture is that this activity is nationally open, and the Bali flag in the record does not close it for PMA registration.

editorial.headline: Clay and Ceramic Roof Tiles, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23922 covers the making of clay or ceramic roof tiles, with access across all business scales and a clear foreign-ownership ceiling nationally.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23922 is a manufacturing classification for roof tiles made from clay or ceramic. Its scope is practical and material-specific: pressed tiles, ordinary tiles, kodok-style tiles, and glazed tiles all sit inside the activity. The record is not describing retail trade, installation work, building contracting, or a broader ceramics business. It is about making the tiles themselves, from clay or ceramic inputs into finished roofing products.

That makes the code relevant for founders whose Indonesian company will operate a production activity rather than merely distribute building materials. The eligible business scales are broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open in the record. In plain terms, the classification is not reserved only for a small workshop or only for a large industrial plant. The same activity description can support a registered operation across the full scale spectrum, provided the actual business remains within the stated roof-tile manufacturing scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. For a foreign-owned setup, that is the key national reading: the record treats the activity as open to PMA and does not state a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a separate minimum capital number, special licence, operating threshold, or staged timeline, so those should not be inferred from this classification note.

Bali needs its own reading because the province applies a moratorium rule that blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI island-wide. For this activity, however, the Bali field is not blocked. The reason is that at Besar scale, the OSS risk level is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by the moratorium described in the record. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: a foreign investor can read KBLI 23922 as nationally open, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration on the moratorium ground. The caution is simply editorial discipline: keep the registered activity tightly aligned with clay or ceramic roof-tile manufacturing, because the favourable reading belongs to this specific activity and its stated scope.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can read KBLI 23922 as nationally open, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration on the moratorium ground.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Bahan Bangunan Lainnya dari Tanah Liat atau Keramik
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan produk dari tanah liat atau keramik untuk keperluan bahan bangunan bukan batu bata dan genteng, seperti saluran air, ubin, lubang angin, dan buis (cincin untuk sumur), termasuk tungku keramik atau ubin dinding nonrefraktori, kubus mosaik dan sebagainya, paving atau ubin keramik nonrefraktori, ubin untuk atap, cerobong asap, pipa, saluran keramik dan sebagainya, dan balok lantai dari tanah liat yang dibakar.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan pembuatan peralatan sanitasi dari tanah liat atau porselen, lihat kelompok 23934 dan 23935.

It explicitly excludes ceramic sanitary ware like sinks or toilets.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.

editorial.headline: Clay and Ceramic Building Materials With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23929 covers non-brick clay and ceramic building materials, open to all business scales and nationally open to foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23929 sits in a practical corner of building-materials manufacturing: fired clay and ceramic products made for construction, but not ordinary bricks or roof tiles. Its scope includes drainage channels, floor and wall tiles, ventilation blocks, well rings, ceramic furnaces, mosaic cubes, paving and non-refractory ceramic tiles, chimney elements, pipes, ceramic conduits, roof tiles, and fired-clay floor blocks. In plain English, this is the industrial category for shaped clay or ceramic components that become part of buildings, infrastructure, and site works.

The activity is not limited to a single business scale. The record opens it to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** operators, which matters because this line can range from smaller specialist production to heavier manufacturing. The common thread is not the size of the factory but the nature of the product: clay or ceramic building materials made as construction inputs. A founder reading this code should therefore focus less on a generic “ceramics” label and more on whether the output is a building-material component within the listed scope.

Nationally, the picture is straightforward. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited national source. That means the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. There is no basis in the slim record to add a special capital figure, local partner requirement, licensing timeline, or other threshold; the defensible statement is simply that the national foreign-ownership position is open up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not a hidden stop sign here. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA across the island, but the Bali reason for this record says the OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. That does not turn the code into a blank cheque for matters outside the record, but it gives the key registration signal: for this activity, the national openness and the Bali-side moratorium screen point in the same usable direction.
editorial.pullQuote: For this activity, the national openness and the Bali-side moratorium screen point in the same usable direction.

data.judul: Industri Perlengkapan Rumah Tangga dari Porselen
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan berbagai macam perlengkapan rumah tangga dari porselen, seperti piring, tatakan, cangkir, mangkuk, teko, kendi, sendok, asbak, barang toilet, serta stoples dan produk sejenis yang digunakan untuk pengangkutan atau pengemasan barang, termasuk juga kegiatan pembuatan barang pajangan dari porselen, seperti arca atau patung dan produk keramik ornamental lainnya, tempat bunga, kotak rokok, dan guci.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup pembuatan berbagai macam produk perlengkapan sanitasi dari porselen, lihat kelompok 23934.

editorial.headline: Porcelain Household Ware With Room for Full-Scale Investment
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23931 covers porcelain tableware, containers, display pieces, and ornamental ceramics, with national PMA access open across all business scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23931 sits in the practical, material world of porcelain household goods. Its scope is not merely dinner plates and cups, although those are central examples. It also reaches the wider domestic porcelain cabinet: saucers, bowls, teapots, pitchers, spoons, ashtrays, toilet articles, jars, and similar products used for carrying or packaging goods. The same activity also covers porcelain display and ornamental ceramic goods, including figures, statues, flower vases, cigarette boxes, urns, and comparable decorative pieces. In plain terms, this is the manufacturing code for porcelain objects that move between household utility, packaging use, and interior display.

The boundary matters because this is still a manufacturing activity, not a broad licence for every porcelain object a factory might imagine. The record expressly leaves porcelain sanitary fittings outside the activity, so the centre of gravity here is household equipment, containers, and decorative porcelain. A founder choosing this classification should therefore be able to describe production in terms of porcelain ware for domestic, packaging, or ornamental use, rather than drifting into adjacent building or sanitary product lines. The phrase “seluruh” in the slim record also signals that the activity is being treated inclusively within its own described scope, but only within that scope.

On scale, the code is unusually straightforward: it is open to micro, small, medium, and large enterprises. That means the classification can serve a modest workshop making ornamental porcelain pieces as well as a larger manufacturing operation producing household tableware or porcelain containers. The scale choice does not change the basic character of the activity; it changes the business size at which the activity is registered. For a founder, the editorial point is simple but important: the code is not reserved only for industrial-scale producers, nor is it confined to cottage production. It is written to accommodate the full span of Indonesian business scales listed in the record.

The national-versus-Bali picture is also clear. Nationally, the PMA status is open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, based on the cited presidential regulation source in the record. Bali does not block PMA registration for this activity under the moratorium rule because the Bali-side risk note says that at large scale the OSS risk is medium-high or high, and therefore it is not caught by the provincial block on low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA. The honest conclusion is that this is genuinely available for foreign-owned registration in Bali on the facts provided: nationally open, no foreign-equity reduction shown, and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium rationale.

editorial.headline: Ceramic Household Ware with a Real Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers clay and ceramic household, decorative, technical and packaging goods, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
This activity is the manufacturing home of everyday clay and ceramic objects: plates, cups, bowls, pitchers, teapots, cooking pots, jars and similar household ware. Its scope also reaches display and decorative pieces such as statues, flower vases, betel containers, cigarette boxes and piggy banks. The record is not limited to ornamental craft; it also includes technical ceramic products such as insulators, insulating fittings and permanent magnets, as well as jars and similar products used to transport or package goods.

That breadth matters because it describes a production activity rather than a retail label or a purely artistic category. A founder registering under this code is placing the business in the making of clay or ceramic goods for use, display, technical application, transport or packaging. The same activity can therefore sit behind a small workshop producing tableware, a decorative ceramics operation, or a larger facility making more functional ceramic components, provided the activity remains within the stated manufacturing scope.

The scale position is unusually straightforward in the slim record: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical editorial terms, that means the code is not reserved in the record for only one size of operator. It can describe a micro producer, a small or medium manufacturer, or a large-scale industrial setup. The record gives no extra thresholds, capital figures, local licences, tax treatment or timing requirements, so none should be read into it. Its core message is scope and access: clay and ceramic household, decorative, technical and packaging goods, open across all listed business scales.

The national foreign-investment picture is also clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It includes items like mortars and pestles, chemical tubes and beakers, fuse holders, high- and low-voltage insulators, ferrite magnets, and other ceramic products used in labs, chemical processes, and industrial settings.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA).
