editorial.headline: Metal Cutlery Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers metal cutlery for the kitchen and table, with national PMA openness and a Bali record that is not blocked by the province-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25933 is the industrial home for making metal cutlery: the everyday metal implements that move between kitchen work and the dining table. The slim record names spoons, forks, soup ladles, dinner knives, butter knives, sugar tongs, chopsticks, straws, and similar tools as the core scope. Its boundary matters just as much as its centre. Dinnerware, flat tableware, and cookware sit outside this activity, so the code should be read as a manufacturing category for metal eating, serving, and closely related utensils, not as a broad kitchen-goods basket.

The registration scale is wide. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, which means the same code can frame a modest formal workshop or a larger manufacturing operation, provided the output remains within the described scope. A founder should therefore start with the object being made. If the business is producing the metal tools listed in the record, the fit is direct. If the business concept drifts into dinnerware, flat tableware, or cookware, the record itself draws a boundary and this activity no longer carries the whole description.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the supplied data treats this as open to foreign ownership at the national level, with no lower foreign-stake ceiling stated in the record. That clarity should not be diluted with invented conditions. The source field supports the national reading, but the editorial point is simple: for this activity, the national foreign-ownership line is open.

Bali needs a separate reading, because the province-side status is not a separate ownership percentage. The record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA under an island-wide, permanent moratorium, yet this activity is not marked as blocked. The stated reason is precise: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. Bali’s record is not a hidden equity cap; it is a clear not-blocked reading under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s record is not a hidden equity cap; it is a clear not-blocked reading under the stated moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: General Metal Hardware, Open Nationally and Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25934 covers the making of everyday metal hardware, with national PMA openness and a Bali record that does not block it under the moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25934 is a practical manufacturing category: the making of general metal equipment that sits inside buildings, furniture, and everyday fitted objects. The slim record names keys, padlocks, door locks, hinges, bolts, and similar metal fittings as examples. In plain English, this is not a broad lifestyle or retail activity; it is the production side of common metal hardware, the kind of component manufacturing that supports construction, interiors, furniture, security, and related uses.

The activity is open across the full scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the category is not framed only for one size of operator. A small workshop making hinges and locks can sit inside the same activity description as a larger industrial setup, provided the business is genuinely manufacturing this kind of general metal equipment. The editorial discipline is important: the record gives the product scope and the eligible scales, but it does not add special permits, technical thresholds, timelines, tax treatment, or capital rules. Those cannot be inferred from the title alone.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, meaning the foreign-ownership ceiling should be rendered as 100%. The cited source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned structure, the national reading is therefore not a partial opening or a closed lane: on the record provided, this activity is foreign-open up to the stated ceiling. That conclusion comes directly from the PMA fields, not from any neighbouring classification or assumed industry pattern.

Bali is the more important check, because the island-wide moratorium can block PMA registration for activities that are otherwise open nationally. Here, the record does not mark KBLI 25934 as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not caught by that block on the provided Bali assessment. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium record supplied.

editorial.headline: Metal Containers for the Business Behind the Package
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25940 covers the making of metal cans, drums, buckets, jerrycans, boxes, and metal closures, with national PMA access open up to 100%.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25940 is the industrial code for making the metal vessels that sit behind a large part of everyday commerce: food and drink cans, paint and chemical cans, barrels, drums, buckets, boxes, jerrycans, and the components used in metal cans. It also includes metal closures, including metal bottle caps such as crown corks and lug caps. The scope is practical rather than decorative: this is about containers, closures, and the metal packaging hardware that allows goods to be filled, sealed, stored, moved, and sold.

The activity is open across the full scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not framed only as a large-factory category, even though the examples clearly include industrial packaging outputs. A small operator making specific metal containers sits inside the same recorded scale ladder as a larger manufacturer producing cans, drums, or closure components at higher volume. The code therefore reads as a manufacturing classification with room for different operating sizes, while staying tightly focused on metal containers and related closures.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward. The national record lists the activity as TERBUKA and sets pma_max_asing at 100, citing Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded for this activity is 100%. There is no lower foreign-equity limit in the slim record, and no separate condition, threshold, permit, tax, timeline, or capital figure is stated here. The honest national reading is therefore clean: for foreign investment classification purposes, this activity is open nationally up to full foreign ownership.

The Bali-side reading is also unusually clear because the record does not mark the activity blocked. Bali’s moratorium rule in this dataset blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but KBLI 25940 is recorded with l4_bali_blocked as false and l4_bali_status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That is the key operational distinction. This is not a case where national openness is neutralised by a Bali PMA block. Based on this record alone, a foreign-owned registration in Bali is not blocked by the moratorium for this activity, while the national ownership ceiling remains 100%.
editorial.pullQuote: This is not a case where national openness is neutralised by a Bali PMA block.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Barang dari Kawat Logam Bukan Kabel
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan berbagai macam barang dari kawat logam bukan kabel, termasuk tali kawat logam, seperti kawat berduri, pagar kawat, kasa kawat, jaring kawat, dan alat pemanggang (grill). intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing metal wire products like barbed wire, fences, mesh, grills, springs (except watch springs), and chains (but not power transmission chains). It does not include making electrical transmission cables or wires.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign-owned (PMA) companies. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Barang dari Kawat Logam Bukan Kabel (25951)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who want to produce wire goods, springs, or chains, but cannot set up a PMA in Bali while the moratorium applies.

editorial.headline: Metal Wire Goods Without the Cable Confusion
editorial.standfirst: This KBLI covers the practical factory work of turning metal wire into fences, mesh, springs, chains, grills, and related non-cable products.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25951 is a manufacturing code for metal-wire goods that are not cable. Its centre of gravity is the workshop or factory floor where wire becomes a finished industrial or household object: barbed wire, wire fencing, wire mesh, wire nets, metal wire rope, and grill products. The same scope also reaches into spring production, including leaf springs, helical springs, torsion bar springs, and spring sheets, while explicitly keeping clock springs outside the boundary. It also covers chain manufacturing, except for power-transmission chains. The practical reading is simple: this is not a trading code and not a general metalworking bucket. It is for making tangible goods from metal wire, provided the product is not an electrical-transmission cable and not one of the excluded spring or chain categories.

The scale position is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so the code can describe anything from a small producer making wire fencing or grills to a larger plant manufacturing mesh, springs, wire rope, or chains. That matters because this activity is not defined only by industrial size; it is defined by the nature of the manufactured object. A smaller producer and a larger factory can both sit inside the same activity when the work is still the making of non-cable metal-wire goods. For founders, the editorial point is that the code follows the product and process, not the ambition of the company.

Nationally, the investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. There is no lower cap in the slim record, no special threshold, and no minimum-capital detail beyond the foreign-ownership ceiling itself. The cited national source is carried in the record, but the operative conclusion is the status and ceiling: open, with a 100% PMA maximum.

Bali does not add a separate ownership percentage here. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That is the important local distinction. The province’s moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this record is not marked as blocked in Bali. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally open, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium in this record. The caveat is only the one the record actually gives: the Bali status is framed through risk status, not through a separate Bali foreign-ownership cap.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction: nationally open, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium in this record.

editorial.headline: Metal Fasteners With a Clean National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25952 covers the manufacture of nails, nuts, bolts, rivets, tacks, and similar threaded metal goods, open nationally and not blocked for Bali PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25952 is a manufacturing classification for the small metal pieces that hold larger systems together: nails, nuts, bolts, and similar threaded goods made from iron, steel, copper, aluminium, and other metals. Its scope also reaches plug nails or rivets and thumbtacks. In plain English, this is not a trading code and not a broad machinery category; it is the industrial making of metal fastening components themselves.

The record opens this activity across the full scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved in the slim record for only one business size. A founder reading it should understand the category as available from smaller production setups through larger industrial operations, while still staying within the activity described: manufacturing the named metal fasteners and closely similar threaded goods.

The national PMA picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower cap in the slim record, so the editorial answer should be direct: nationally, this activity is open to foreign investment up to the stated ceiling. No extra capital rule, permit sequence, licence name, or operational threshold is added here because the slim record does not provide one.

Bali does not change that into a prohibition on the facts provided. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says it is not blocked. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That sits against the moratorium rule in the record, which blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali province. For this code, the honest national-vs-Bali picture is therefore clean: foreign ownership is nationally open up to 100%, and Bali is not marked as blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: For this code, the honest picture is clean: nationally open up to 100%, and not marked as blocked for Bali PMA registration.

editorial.headline: Metal Safes and Office Security Built for Every Scale
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25991 covers the manufacture of metal office security goods, nationally open to PMA ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25991 is a manufacturing code for metal office equipment where security and storage are the point. The record places safes, filing cabinets, strongboxes, armoured doors, and similar metal products inside the activity. It also draws one important boundary: this is not the manufacture of metal furniture. The centre of the code is therefore not general furnishing, but the production of office-use metal goods designed to hold, protect, organise, or secure.

That scope gives the code a practical industrial character. A business registering this activity is not simply trading in finished security goods; it is making them. The slim record describes fabrication of metal office items, including safes and filing cabinets, and extends the field to strongboxes, armoured doors, and other similar products. The word “Seluruh” in the scope reinforces that the activity is treated broadly within that described manufacturing field, while still staying inside the stated boundary and outside metal furniture.

The registration scale is unusually straightforward. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain terms, the record does not reserve this manufacturing line for only large industrial players, nor does it describe it as available only to small operators. It can sit at any of the listed business scales, from micro through large, provided the registration follows the activity as defined: metal office security and storage products, not neighbouring activities and not a broader furniture business.

The ownership picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded as 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the Bali side, the record does not mark the code as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. For this code, the record’s conclusion is that the moratorium does not block PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: For this code, the record’s conclusion is that the moratorium does not block PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Metal Kitchenware Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25992 covers the making of metal kitchen and table equipment, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25992 is a manufacturing code for the objects that sit closest to daily use: metal kitchenware and metal table equipment. Its scope covers production of kitchen tools made from aluminium and from other metals, including eating utensils, plates, shallow plates, bowls, teapots, pots, pans, kettles, cooking pots, steamers, food carriers, basins, trays, containers, and similar goods. The record also brings in other non-electric equipment used at the table or in the kitchen, small hand-operated kitchen tools and their accessories, and metal scouring tools.

That makes the code practical rather than decorative. It is not simply about finished consumer goods in a showroom; it is about the industrial making of household and kitchen objects from metal. A founder using this code should be describing a business whose core activity is fabrication or manufacture: shaping, producing, and supplying these kitchen and table items as metal goods. The record does not add separate permit names, technical standards, capital thresholds, or production-volume conditions, so the editorial picture stays deliberately within the activity definition and ownership fields provided.

The registration scale is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe anything from a small producer of hand-operated kitchen tools to a larger factory making pans, kettles, trays, or related metalware. That does not mean every business model is identical; it means the KBLI record itself does not reserve the activity to only one scale. The important test is whether the actual registered activity remains the manufacture of the metal kitchen and table equipment named in the scope.

The national-vs-Bali picture is clean. Nationally, the PMA status is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded at 100, so the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this code is not blocked on the provided Bali logic. For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, that is the central conclusion: this activity is nationally open and, on this slim record, not blocked by the Bali moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the central conclusion is that this activity is nationally open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium.

editorial.headline: Metal Household Goods With a Clear PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25993 covers non-kitchen metal household products, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25993 is a manufacturing category for household goods made from metal, outside the narrower world of kitchenware and table equipment. The record describes the activity as the production of other household-use tools and fixtures, made from aluminium or non-aluminium metals, including clothes-drying racks, ladders, bathtubs, dishwashing tubs, washbasins, and similar equipment. In plain English, this is the metal-fabrication lane for practical domestic products: the everyday objects that sit between light construction fittings and finished home utility goods.

The scope is industrial rather than retail-facing. A founder using this activity code is registering the making of the products, not merely selling them, importing them, or installing them as a service. The examples in the record matter because they give the code its texture: not ornamental metalwork, not kitchen utensils, not dining equipment, but household fixtures and tools that are useful, durable, and commonly formed from aluminium or other metals. The final word in the Indonesian scope, “Seluruh,” also indicates that the record treats the activity as covering the whole described scope rather than carving out a narrower subset.

On business scale, the registration path is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means it can describe anything from a small fabrication outfit producing simple household metal goods to a larger manufacturer running more formal production. That scale range is important for founders because the same activity definition can sit beneath very different operating models, provided the registered business is still genuinely engaged in making the household metal products described in the scope.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership as 100%, with the cited source shown as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate foreign-ownership percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali question is whether the province-side moratorium blocks PMA registration for this activity. Here, it does not: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters as background because the record says Bali blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; but for this code, the record’s conclusion is that the activity is not blocked by that rule. For a foreign founder looking at Bali, the honest reading is therefore straightforward: this activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and, on the record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign founder looking at Bali, the honest reading is straightforward: this activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the industrial manufacturing of welded steel profiles such as H-beams and I-beams, used mainly in heavy construction and structural frameworks.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Profil Logam (25994)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs looking to produce large-scale welded steel sections for the construction, infrastructure, or industrial sectors.

editorial.headline: Welded steel profiles, open nationally and not blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25994 covers welded steel profile manufacturing, from H-Beams to I-Beams, with national PMA openness and a Bali status that is not moratorium-blocked.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25994 is a manufacturing code for **Industri Profil Logam**: the making of steel profiles by welding. The slim record gives the practical shape of the activity clearly: H profiles, I profiles, H-Beams, I-Beams, and similar welded steel forms. This is not a vague metalworking category. It is about producing structural-looking profile shapes through a welding process, with the scope text keeping the emphasis on the profile itself rather than on downstream installation, trading, or construction services.

The record also draws a boundary around the activity. It states an exclusion for the manufacture of welded profiles for heavy construction, and repeats that exclusion in the source text. That matters because the code should be read as a defined industrial manufacturing activity, not as a licence to absorb every possible heavy-construction steel profile operation. A founder reading this code should treat the Indonesian scope as the controlling description: welded steel profiles such as H-Beam, I-Beam, and similar products are inside the frame; the excluded heavy-construction profile manufacturing language sits outside it.

On registration scale, the code is broad. The record marks it as open to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so the classification is not reserved only for large industrial operators. In editorial terms, that says the KBLI can describe a small metal-profile operation as well as a larger manufacturing setup, provided the real activity remains within the stated scope. The scale list should not be overread as a promise about facilities, permits, capital, or operating conditions; it simply records the scales that are open in the slim record.

The national-vs-Bali picture is unusually clean here. Nationally, the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` recorded as **100**, so the foreign-ownership ceiling is properly rendered as **100%**. For Bali, the record does not create a separate foreign-ownership percentage and does not impose a Bali-side cap. Instead, it gives the Bali status as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and says: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this code is not marked as blocked. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: for this record, KBLI 25994 is foreign-open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali by the cited provincial moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is straightforward: KBLI 25994 is foreign-open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali by the cited provincial moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership. editorial.headline: Metal Lighting Manufacturing, Without the Bali Moratorium Trap
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25995 covers metal-based lamps and components, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25995 is a manufacturing classification for lamps whose main material is metal. The Indonesian scope is compact but clear: it covers the making of various metal lamps, including lighthouse lamps, pressure lamps, hanging lamps, and their components. This is not a retail or installation activity in the record; its centre of gravity is production, with the object being the metal lamp itself and the parts that belong to it.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not framed only for a large factory or only for a small workshop. A business using this code could sit anywhere on that stated scale ladder, provided the registered activity remains within the recorded manufacturing scope: metal-based lamps and components. That scale openness matters because it tells the founder that the code is not inherently confined to one size of enterprise.

Nationally, the investment reading is direct. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling supplied in the record is 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. That conclusion should not be stretched into claims about permits, capital, operating timelines, taxes, or technical standards, because none of those details appear in the supplied record. The authoritative investment facts here are the status, the ceiling, the source, and the registered scale range.

The Bali picture is also clean, and it is important not to overcomplicate it. The record does not mark this KBLI as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently, but this record’s Bali-side assessment does not place the activity inside that blocked result. So the honest conclusion is that KBLI 25995 is nationally foreign-open and, on the supplied Bali record, not blocked by the Bali moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan berbagai macam produk dari logam lainnya yang tidak diklasifikasikan di tempat lain, seperti jepitan rambut, peniti, staples, klip kertas; jarum (selain jarum untuk mesin jahit), seperti jarum jahit, jarum rajut, dan jarum bordir; kepala gesper; rantai logam; bel; bingkai (lis) gambar; papan nama logam, dan berbagai barang logam yang kecil, termasuk pembuatan baling-baling, rantai kapal, jangkar kapal, lonceng, perlengkapan tetap (fixture) rel kereta api yang terpasang, kabel logam yang dijalin pembalut sejenisnya, kabel logam yang tidak terisolasi atau kabel logam terisolasi yang tidak dapat digunakan sebagai konduktor listrik, cincin penutup, dan barang-barang tidak berulir yang sejenis, screw machine product, kantong berbahan foil, magnet logam permanen, botol atau kendi logam hampa udara, tanda logam (bukan listrik), lencana logam dan lencana militer logam, pengeriting rambut dan sisir logam, serta kerangka dan pegangan payung. Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan pembuatan jarum untuk mesin jahit, lihat kelompok 28261.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacture of a wide range of miscellaneous metal products not classified elsewhere, such as small hardware items (paper clips, staples, safety pins, sewing needles), metal chains, bells, picture frames, nameplates, propellers, ship anchors, and other fabricated metal goods.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Produk Logam Lainnya YTDL (25999)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who want to manufacture niche metal goods or hardware items but must either wait for the Bali moratorium to end or choose a location outside Bali to start immediately.

editorial.headline: Metal Objects at the Edge of the Catalogue
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 25999 covers the miscellaneous metal products that do not sit neatly in a narrower manufacturing class, with full national foreign ownership but a scope-sensitive Bali pathway.
editorial.body:
KBLI 25999 is the workshop of remaining metal goods: the activity code for making metal products that are real, manufactured, and commercially specific, but not classified elsewhere in a narrower group. The record points to small everyday articles such as hair clips, safety pins, staples, paper clips, sewing, knitting, and embroidery needles, buckle heads, metal chains, bells, picture frames, metal nameplates, non-electric metal signs, badges, metal hair curlers and combs, and umbrella frames or handles. It also reaches into heavier or more technical products: propellers, ship chains, ship anchors, installed railway fixtures, woven metal cable coverings, certain non-conductor metal cables, sealing rings, screw-machine products, foil pouches, permanent metal magnets, and vacuum metal bottles or jugs.

That range is the point of the code. It is not a prestige label for one product line, and it is not a catch-all for anything vaguely metallic. It is for manufacturers whose output is a finished or semi-finished metal article within this residual metal-products field. A founder using this classification should be able to describe the actual item being made with care, because the record itself is broad: a paper clip, an anchor, a metal badge, and a vacuum metal jug all sit inside the same recorded scope. The boundary also matters: the record expressly leaves sewing-machine needles outside this activity.

On business scale, the national record is expansive. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale operators, so it is not reserved in the record for only cottage production or only large industrial plants. At the national level, PMA status remains TERBUKA, while foreign ownership may reach 100%. In plain terms, the national investment line treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali is more delicate. The record does not mark this code as automatically blocked, but it does mark the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent). The reason given is precise: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on some scopes but higher on others, and PMA registration in Bali is registrable only by declaring the higher-risk scope; the exact activity must be verified live in OSS. This sits under the recorded Bali moratorium rule that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. The honest reading is therefore not that KBLI 25999 is simply closed in Bali, and not that it is casually open either. Nationally it is fully open; in Bali, the registrability of a PMA filing depends on the exact declared metal-product activity and its OSS risk treatment.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers industrial manufacturing of solar cells, photovoltaic panels, and photovoltaic inverters—the core building blocks of solar electricity systems. It does not include installation, solar-powered lamps, or solar heating equipment.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, the activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the local moratorium, but it is classified as a higher-risk activity. While a PMA can be registered, expect additional requirements like an industrial-zoned address, environmental impact assessment, and local permit verification before the business licence is issued.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Sel Surya, Panel Surya, dan Inverter Fotovoltaik (26110)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign industrialists or clean-tech investors who plan to set up a solar cell, panel, or inverter manufacturing facility in Bali—provided they can secure a compliant industrial location.

editorial.headline: Solar Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26110 covers the factory side of photovoltaic hardware, and the record treats it as nationally open while not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26110 is the industrial code for making the core hardware of photovoltaic power: solar cells, solar panels, and photovoltaic inverters. The scope is manufacturing, not installation and not a general renewable-energy umbrella. Its center of gravity is the physical production of cells, modules, panels, and inverters, the components that turn sunlight into usable electrical architecture. In plain English, this is the factory code for photovoltaic equipment, from the cell level through finished panel assemblies and the inverter layer that makes the system workable.

That manufacturing character matters because the record opens the activity across the full business-scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small workshop, a growing component maker, a mid-sized industrial producer, and a large factory all sit inside the scale language of the record. The code is therefore not framed only for large industrial capital, even though the product category naturally points toward equipment, production control, and supply-chain discipline. The editorial point is simple: the activity is defined by what is made, not by a single assumed company size.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That is the strongest form of openness available in the slim record: a PMA is not being pushed into a lower ownership cap by the fields provided here. The stated source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the record adds a special licence condition, minimum capital figure, tax treatment, timeline, or operational threshold, so none should be read into the code.

The Bali reading is also unusually direct. The record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. That moratorium is still relevant background because the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. But for this activity, the record’s own conclusion is that the moratorium does not block PMA registration in Bali today. The honest result is therefore not a hidden restriction: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership ceiling, and not blocked by the Bali rule recorded here.

It’s the physical production of these electronic components, not retail or repair.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: While nationally the business is 100% open to foreign ownership, Bali classifies it as a higher-risk (medium-high) activity. It is not blocked by local moratoriums, but you’ll need to verify the business address meets industrial zoning and be prepared for stricter licensing due to the risk level.

editorial.headline: Electronic Tubes and Connectors as a Manufacturing Code
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26191 covers the factory production of electronic tubes, valves, connectors, and common device cables, with full national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26191 is a manufacturing classification for the physical production of electronic tube and connector components. The record describes a scope that includes television picture tubes, television camera tubes, amplifier and receiver tubes and valves, electronic tubes, electronic connectors, printer cables, monitor cables, USB cables, other connectors, electronic valves, and lamp tubes. In plain English, this is not a retail or repair activity. It is a factory-side code for making the componentry and connection hardware that sits inside, between, or alongside electronic devices.

The code is open across every business scale named in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not reserved only for large industrial operators in the classification data provided here. A small producer of connector assemblies, a mid-sized cable manufacturer, or a larger electronics-component plant all sit within the scale language of the record, provided the actual registered activity remains inside this manufacturing scope.

Indonesia's national framework treats foreign investment in this code plainly. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` recorded as 100. That means the national record treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%, with the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap in the slim record, and no additional national threshold or special condition is stated here, so the editorial point should stay clean: at the national level, this activity is foreign-open.

For Bali, the position is equally clear, though for a reason that often surprises founders. The Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and `l4_bali_blocked` is false. The reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this code is not marked as blocked by that rule. So the honest reading is that KBLI 26191 is nationally open to PMA, and the Bali-side record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Komponen dan Papan Elektronik Lainnya YTDL
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan komponen dan papan elektronik lainnya yang tidak diklasifikasikan di tempat lain, seperti transistor dan peralatan semikonduktor yang sejenis, sirkuit terpadu (integrated circuits), printed circuits, induktor, resistor, kapasitor, dan berbagai komponen elektronik lainnya, termasuk pembuatan mikroprosesor, mikrokontroler, induktor jenis komponen elektronik (misalnya choke, kumparan, dan trafo), kristal elektronik dan crystal assemblies, solenoid, switch dan transducer untuk aplikasi elektronik, kartu antarmuka atau interface cards (misalnya kartu suara, kartu video, kontroler, kartu jaringan, dan modem), komponen layar (misalnya plasma, polimer, dan LCD), dioda pemancar cahaya atau light emitting diodes (LED), sirkuit terpadu atau integrated circuit (IC) (baik analog, digital, maupun hibrid), dan dioda.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup pembuatan cip, wafer, dice, dan programmable logic controller (PLC).

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the production of electronic components and boards not classified elsewhere — think transistors, integrated circuits, printed circuit boards, resistors, capacitors, microprocessors, microcontrollers, crystals, solenoids, switches, transducers, and interface cards like sound or video cards.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Komponen dan Papan Elektronik Lainnya YTDL (26199)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to manufacture electronic components or circuit boards, typically for export or high‑tech industrial supply chains.

editorial.headline: Electronic Components Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26199 covers specialised electronic components and boards, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 26199 is a manufacturing code for the less easily named parts of the electronics economy: components and electronic boards that sit inside larger devices rather than appear as finished consumer products.** Its scope is broad but still technical. The record places here the making of transistors and similar semiconductor equipment, integrated circuits, printed circuits, inductors, resistors, capacitors, microprocessors, microcontrollers, electronic crystals and assemblies, solenoids, electronic switches, transducers, interface cards, display components, LEDs, diodes, chips, wafers, dice, and programmable logic controllers. In plain English, this is the industrial layer where electronic intelligence, control, signal handling, and connectivity are manufactured as components.

That breadth matters because this is not a narrow workshop description. It reaches from familiar board-level parts to semiconductor-adjacent items and control components used in electronic applications. A company using this code should be able to recognise itself in the act of making the component, board, chip, wafer, diode, interface card, or control unit described in the scope. The editorial point is simple: the code is about production of electronic components and boards, not the retailing, installation, or general trading of electronics.

On scale, the record is unusually clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not framed only for large industrial plants, even though its subject matter can easily sound capital-intensive. The registration scale still has to match the actual business, but the slim record itself keeps all four scale categories available. For founders, that is the useful operational signal: this classification can describe anything from a small component-making setup to a larger manufacturing operation, provided the real activity remains inside the stated manufacturing scope.

The national-vs-Bali picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. So the record supports saying that foreign ownership is open up to 100% at national level. Bali does not add a separate percentage, quota, partnership requirement, or local ceiling in this record. The Bali-side status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province; this activity is not marked as blocked by that rule. The honest reading is therefore not a warning disguised as nuance: for this record, KBLI 26199 is nationally foreign-open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the Bali moratorium field.

editorial.headline: Computer Assembly With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26210 covers the making and assembly of computers, from laptops and servers to interactive terminals, and is nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26210 is the industrial home for computer manufacturing and computer assembly. In plain English, it covers businesses that make or put together computing devices: mainframes, desktop computers, laptops, computer servers, handheld computers, tablets, and interactive computers such as digital signage, smartboards, and self-service interactive devices. The record also places computer assembly inside the scope, together with computer terminals such as ATMs and point-of-sale terminals, provided they are not mechanically operated.

The scope is broad because the activity is defined by the computer as a programmable machine, not by one retail format or one narrow device category. The record describes digital computers as systems that can store processing programs or the data needed to execute them, be programmed according to user needs, carry out arithmetic operations requested by the user, and run processing programs without human intervention while modifying execution through logical decisions. It also recognises analog computers that simulate mathematical models and include at least analog control and programming elements. That definition gives the code room for ordinary PCs as well as more specialised equipment.

For registration scale, the code is open across the full business-size ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because a workshop-style assembler and a larger industrial manufacturer are not treated as different activities merely because their scale differs. The activity can include desktop production, laptop production, server production, tablet production, terminal production, and special-purpose computers for cybersecurity functions such as firewalls or network detection and response systems. The centre of gravity is still manufacturing or assembly: the business is making the computing hardware, not merely selling it, servicing it, or advising on its use.

The national foreign-investment picture is unusually clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, so the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record, and it should not be read as having one. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this code is not blocked on the record provided. For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership allowed, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium as recorded.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest reading is straightforward: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership allowed, and not blocked by the Bali moratorium as recorded.

editorial.headline: Computer Peripherals Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26220 covers the factory side of computer peripherals: nationally open to foreign ownership, but not registerable as PMA in Bali under the record’s moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26220 is the manufacturing code for the physical equipment that sits around a computer and makes it usable: storage devices, input devices, output devices, display hardware, scanning equipment, and immersive-media peripherals. In plain English, this is not software, consulting, retail, repair, or online trading. It is the industrial production of computer peripherals themselves: magnetic disk drives, flash drives and other storage equipment; optical disk drives for computers; printers; monitors; keyboards; mice, joysticks and trackball accessories; scanners, including barcode scanners; smart card readers; computer projectors; and immersive-media equipment such as virtual reality helmets and augmented reality glasses. The record also brings in multifunction office equipment that can print, copy and fax, which places this activity firmly in the machinery-and-device manufacturing world rather than the services layer around it.

The scale position is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not confined to one size of operator. A small workshop-like manufacturer and a larger industrial producer both belong inside the same activity frame if the work is the making of these computer peripheral products. That breadth matters because the code describes the object of production, not a single commercial format. What unifies the category is the act of manufacturing peripheral computer equipment: devices that store, display, input, output, scan, project, or extend computer interaction into immersive media.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is simple and generous. The record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA, while its maximum foreign ownership figure remains 100%. On the national reading, therefore, a foreign-owned company can hold the full foreign stake allowed by the record for this activity. For that national position, the named source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial ceiling in the record, no special ownership split, and no extra national condition stated here. The editorial conclusion at national level is clean: as a KBLI activity, computer peripherals manufacturing is foreign-open up to 100% according to the slim record.

Bali is the decisive complication. The record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets `l4_bali_blocked` to true. Its reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source identified as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. That means the honest operating sentence is not “open in Bali with conditions.” It is sharper: a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today, even though the same code is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today, even though the same code is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership.

editorial.headline: Telephone and Fax Equipment Manufacturing, With Bali Still Open
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26310 covers the making of telephone, fax and related communication-transmission equipment, and the record leaves it nationally open to PMA at every scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26310 is a manufacturing activity, not a retail, installation or telecom-service category. Its recorded scope is the making of communication-transmission equipment: telephone apparatus, fax machines, answering machines and similar equipment. The practical centre of the code is therefore the factory or production operation behind the device, where the business is producing the equipment itself rather than merely using, selling or servicing it.

The registration picture is unusually broad on scale. The slim record opens the activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar** operators, so the code is not reserved in the record for one size of enterprise. A small producer and a large industrial operation sit inside the same stated scale range, provided the registered business is genuinely doing the manufacturing described in the scope. That breadth matters because the scale field is one of the few concrete operational facts the record gives; it should be read plainly, without adding extra thresholds or conditions that are not written here.

Nationally, the code is marked **TERBUKA** for PMA, with `pma_max_asing` recorded as **100**. In founder language, that means the national record allows a fully foreign-owned PMA structure for this activity. The source named for that national position is **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. There is no lower foreign-ownership ceiling in the slim record, so the clean reading is that the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, not a capped minority or joint arrangement.

Bali is where many codes become more complicated, but this record does not block the activity. The Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and `l4_bali_blocked` is **false**. The reason is specific: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this activity is not caught by that block on the facts given here. The honest conclusion is therefore simple: for this record, KBLI 26310 is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, and it is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This industry covers the manufacturing of wireless communication transmission equipment—such as pagers, cordless phones, mobile phones, mobile tablets, and other mobile communication devices. Essentially, you’re making the physical gadgets that connect people without cables.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this is open 100% to foreign ownership. In Bali, the status is not fully blocked, but it is classified as higher-risk; the moratorium doesn’t stop it, yet regulators will verify your business address and location closely. You can establish a PMA here, but expect extra scrutiny and compliance steps during licensing.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Komunikasi Tanpa Kabel (Wireless) (26320)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur aiming to manufacture wireless communication hardware, whether for local sales or export, who is comfortable with a higher-risk classification and location-specific approval processes in Bali.

editorial.headline: Wireless Communication Equipment, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of wireless transmission equipment, with national PMA openness and a Bali record that is not blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26320 is a manufacturing classification for wireless communication equipment. The slim record defines the scope around the making of wireless communication transmission equipment, including pagers, cordless phones, mobile phones, cellular tablets, and mobile communication equipment. In plain English, this is not a retail, repair, software, or service category; it is the industrial activity of producing the physical equipment used for wireless and mobile communication.

The record opens this activity across the full scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the classification is not presented as a narrow large-industry-only lane. A founder reading it should understand the basic registration picture first: the activity itself can be registered at each of those listed scales, while the operational reality of the business would still need to match the manufacturing scope described in the record. The definition is anchored in equipment production, so the center of gravity is the making of wireless transmission devices and mobile communication hardware.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling recorded as 100%. The cited national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That is the clean national picture: the record does not show a partial foreign cap, and it does not create a smaller national ownership band. For a foreign-owned setup, the national reading is therefore straightforward: this activity is open, and the recorded ceiling is 100%.

The Bali side is also clear, but for a different reason. The record marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says it is not blocked. Its reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA in Bali, island-wide and permanent, but this activity is not caught by that block on the record provided. The honest conclusion is simple: KBLI 26320 is foreign-open nationally and, on this slim record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan kartu cerdas (smart card), seperti perencanaan desain cip (chip) design (house design), perencanaan tata letak sirkuit kartu cerdas, pembuatan chip foundry, pembuatan chip module packaging, pembuatan firmware dan perangkat lunak/software yang berkaitan langsung dengan kartu cerdas, serta chip packaging. Kartu cerdas dapat berupa beberapa produk, seperti simcard, komunikasi medan dekat atau near field communications (NFC), dengan teknologi 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G dan sebagainya, kartu perbankan, kartu akses, kartu micro dan macro payment, kartu kredit, dan semua kartu yang menggunakan pengaman data dan atau komunikasi.

editorial.headline: Smart Card Manufacturing Meets Bali’s PMA Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26391 covers the smart-card industry, from chip design and packaging to firmware, software, SIM cards, NFC products, banking cards and secure access cards.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26391 is a manufacturing classification for smart cards. Its recorded scope is broad and technical: chip design planning, smart-card circuit layout planning, chip foundry work, chip module packaging, chip packaging, and the firmware or software directly connected to smart cards. The activity is not limited to one consumer-facing format. The record includes SIM cards, near-field communication products, cards using 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G and related technologies, banking cards, access cards, micro and macro payment cards, credit cards, and cards that use data security or communication features.

That makes this a code for businesses operating inside the physical and embedded-technology layer of card infrastructure. A company under this activity is not merely reselling cards or providing a generic software service; the record points to production and directly related technical work around the smart-card object itself. It covers both the electronic component side and the associated firmware or software where that software is directly tied to the card. On the business-scale question, the record is unusually inclusive: the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales.

Nationally, the investment picture is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In national terms, then, this is a foreign-open activity at the stated ceiling. A foreign investor reading only the national line would see an activity that can be owned up to 100% by foreign shareholders, subject only to the facts actually stated in this slim record.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks this activity as blocked for Bali PMA registration: l4_bali_blocked is true, and the Bali status is Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, with the cited source Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The honest conclusion is therefore precise: nationally, KBLI 26391 is open to foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today because the record marks it as blocked by the Bali moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 26391 is open to foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it as PMA today.
