intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers manufacturing of communication transmission equipment not classified elsewhere—think PBX systems, routers and gateways, cable TV and studio gear, broadcast transmitters, infrared remote controls, and radio/TV antennas and receivers. It’s about building the hardware that moves data, voice, and video signals across networks and airwaves.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible. You would need to operate through a local nominee structure, set up outside Bali, or wait for the policy to change.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Komunikasi Lainnya (26399)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A specialized hardware manufacturer or deep-tech entrepreneur producing communication devices — and Bali is not off the table: this KBLI's large-scale risk class sits above the moratorium's Low/Medium-Low band, so a PMA can still register it here.

editorial.headline: The Communications Equipment Code Behind Broadcast, Data, and IoT Hardware
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26399 covers the manufacture of specialised communications equipment, from broadcast studio systems to routers, smart watches, IoT modules, set top boxes, EDC devices, and CCTV.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26399 is a manufacturing classification for communications equipment that sits beyond the most familiar consumer-device categories. The slim record describes it as the making of other communications transmission equipment: private branch exchange equipment, data-communication devices such as bridges, routers and gateways, cable-television equipment, transmitting and receiving antennas, television and radio studio equipment, broadcast equipment including television cameras, carrier modems, radio and television transmitters, and equipment using infrared signals such as remote controls. In plain English, this is the code for businesses that manufacture the hardware through which signals are transmitted, routed, received, recorded, or converted.

The scope is deliberately broad, but it is not vague. It includes broadcast-studio machinery such as reproduction equipment used in broadcasting, commercial video cameras, transmitting and receiving antennas, and studio systems for television and radio. It also reaches into the connected-device layer: smart watches, Bluetooth transmission equipment or modules, radio-frequency modules, GSM modules, and other connectivity equipment used in the internet of things. The same record includes terrestrial and satellite set top boxes, closed-circuit television cameras, and electronic data capture equipment. What unifies the category is not the final user, but the industrial act: manufacturing communications equipment and related transmission, receiving, studio, connectivity, or data-capture hardware.

The record opens this activity across all listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification can be relevant both to small manufacturers and to larger industrial operators, provided the activity being registered matches the manufacturing scope described in the record. The foreign-investment position is equally direct at the national level. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, with the national source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In practical editorial terms, the national file presents this as fully open to foreign ownership, not merely conditionally open or capped below full ownership.

The Bali picture is important because this Navigator is not just a national taxonomy; it is read by founders who need to know whether a national opening survives local registration reality. Here, the record does not mark Bali as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, with the cited source being Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For KBLI 26399, however, the record’s conclusion is clean: the activity is nationally open up to 100 percent foreign ownership, and the Bali-side status recorded here is not blocked by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For KBLI 26399, the record’s conclusion is clean: the activity is nationally open up to 100 percent foreign ownership, and the Bali-side status recorded here is not blocked by that moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing and assembly of television sets, including TV receivers, monitors, and large-scale display panels like videotron screens. It's a factory-based activity that involves building the actual hardware from components.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Televisi, Monitor Televisi, dan Displai (26410)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign electronics manufacturer planning to produce TV sets or large-format displays inside Indonesia, though not on the island of Bali for now.

editorial.headline: KBLI 26410 and the Industrial Side of Screens
editorial.standfirst: Television, monitor, and display manufacturing is nationally open to foreign investment and, on this record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26410 sits in the physical economy behind the screens people usually treat as finished objects. The record defines it as the manufacturing and assembly of televisions, television receivers and combinations, television monitors, and display products such as videotron. In plain English, this is not broadcasting, content, software, installation, or retail. It is the industrial activity of making and assembling the viewing hardware itself: the television set, the monitor, and the larger display format that turns electronics into a visible surface.

That distinction matters because the activity is open across the full business-scale ladder listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A very small assembler and a large industrial operation are therefore both inside the scale universe for this code, as long as the registered activity remains the making and assembling of the products described. The scope is broad enough to cover conventional television units and modern display formats, but still disciplined: the anchor is manufacturing and assembly, not the commercial life that may come before or after the object leaves the factory.

The national investment position is unusually clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign-owned company reading this record, the national answer is therefore not a partial opening or a negotiated carve-out; the record states that the activity is open and allows full foreign ownership. The source attached to that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. No additional capital threshold, licence name, tax treatment, timetable, or technical permit appears in the slim record, so none should be inferred from the national opening alone.

Bali adds the practical second reading. The province’s moratorium rule is severe in its wording: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this particular record is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward. Nationally, KBLI 26410 is foreign-open up to 100%. On the Bali side, this record does not mark it as closed by the PMA moratorium. The caveat is not a hidden Bali percentage or a local quota; the only Bali-side fact in the record is that its higher-risk reading keeps it outside the moratorium block described here.

editorial.headline: Audio and Video Equipment Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26420 covers non-television audio and video equipment manufacturing for home entertainment, households, and motor vehicles, with full national PMA openness.
editorial.body:
KBLI **26420** is an industrial manufacturing classification for electronic audio and video equipment that is not television. In plain English, it is the code for making home-entertainment hardware used in households and motor vehicles: equipment that records, receives, plays, duplicates, or projects audio and video content. The record places within this scope video recording and duplicating equipment, audio recorders and duplicators, CD and VCD/DVD players, radio receivers and combination devices, stereo equipment, optical media players, computer projectors, TV projectors, household video cameras such as tape recorders and video recorders, and jukeboxes.

The shape of the activity matters. This is not a retail, rental, content, broadcasting, or service category; it is the making of the equipment itself. A founder using this code is presenting an industrial activity around the production of electronic consumer audio-video devices. The range is broad, but it is still bounded by the record: home entertainment equipment for households and vehicles, excluding television. That makes the classification useful for manufacturers whose product line sits around playback, recording, duplication, projection, radio reception, stereo systems, optical media, household video cameras, or jukebox-style equipment.

The scale position is straightforward. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so it is not reserved only for large industrial operators. A small workshop-like manufacturer and a larger production operation may both find themselves inside the same activity description, provided the registered business activity is still the manufacture of the listed audio and video equipment. The practical editorial point is that scale does not narrow the doorway in this slim record: all four stated scales appear as open.

The national PMA picture is also clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA** and gives a **100%** foreign-ownership ceiling, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. For a foreign-owned company, that means the national record does not impose a reduced foreign-share cap for this activity. Bali does not change that with a local percentage in this record. The Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the activity is not blocked: the reason given is **“OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.”** The moratorium text still matters as context because Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this record’s Bali-side conclusion is not a block.
editorial.pullQuote: For KBLI 26420, the honest reading is unusually direct: nationally open to full foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the record supplied.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This group covers the manufacture of other household electronic equipment, including public address systems and amplifiers for musical instruments. It also includes making microphones, speakers and loudspeakers, headphones for devices like radios and computers, karaoke machines, video game consoles, personal audio/video gear such as VR headsets, and home theater equipment.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is NOT blocked by the 13 May 2026 moratorium — its OSS risk class at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale is medium-high or high, which the moratorium leaves open. A PT PMA can pursue this code in Bali, subject to the standard licensing for its risk class.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Audio dan Video Elektronik Lainnya (26490)? Here is the honest national-vs-Bali picture before you plan a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who can meet the higher-risk licensing requirements — one of the doors that stays open in Bali.

editorial.headline: Audio-Video Electronics Manufacturing With a Clean Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: A manufacturing code for speakers, microphones, amplifiers, karaoke machines, consoles, VR headsets, and home-theater equipment, open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26490 covers the making of other electronic audio and video equipment for household, personal, and entertainment use. In practical terms, the record points to products such as loudspeakers for conveying information, amplifiers for musical instruments, microphones, speakers and loudspeakers, headphones for radio, stereo, and computer use, karaoke machines, video game consoles, personal audio-video devices such as VR headsets, and home-theater equipment. The center of gravity is clear: this is a manufacturing activity, not a retail description, service activity, or content business.

That matters because the scope is broad but still technical. A founder using this code should be describing a production setup for physical electronic equipment: assembling, manufacturing, or otherwise making the devices named in the record. The examples range from practical sound systems to consumer entertainment hardware, which gives the code a useful spread across audio, gaming, immersive devices, and domestic video systems. The editorial reading is not that every electronics idea belongs here; it is that the products listed share a manufacturing logic around audio and video equipment intended for use by individuals, households, performers, or entertainment spaces.

On scale, the record is unusually open. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the KBLI can describe anything from a small production operation to a large industrial setup, provided the real activity remains inside the recorded scope. Nationally, the investment position is also clean: the PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded as 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, the national record does not impose a foreign-ownership cap below full ownership for this activity.

The Bali reading is where many KBLI notes become less straightforward, but this record is comparatively direct. Bali is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. Its stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not treated as blocked on the supplied Bali field. The honest conclusion is therefore not a warning disguised as advice: for this slim record, a foreign-owned registration is nationally open and not marked as blocked in Bali today.
editorial.pullQuote: For this slim record, a foreign-owned registration is nationally open and not marked as blocked in Bali today.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing manual mechanical measuring, checking, and testing instruments—like thermometers, barometers, compasses, precision scales, tape measures, water and gas meters, land surveying tools, and their accessories. It includes both scientific and non-scientific devices that rely on mechanical operation.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Alat Ukur dan Alat Uji Manual (26511)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who build and sell precision mechanical measurement instruments—such as thermometers, compasses, scales, or surveying gear—would typically use this classification.

editorial.headline: Manual Instruments, Precision Work, and a Bali Registration Caveat
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26511 covers manual measuring and testing instruments, nationally open to foreign investment but requiring careful Bali risk-scope verification.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26511 is a manufacturing classification for manual measuring, checking, and testing equipment. Its scope is mechanical and practical: instruments used to measure, inspect, test, weigh, orient, meter, or support land measurement. The record includes examples such as measuring apparatus, thermometers, barometers, compasses, precision scales, mechanical therapy equipment, tape measures, water and gas meters, and land-measuring instruments. It also includes equipment accessories, which matters because the activity is not limited to a finished instrument alone; it reaches the supporting fittings that belong to that manual measurement and testing ecosystem.

For founders, the commercial signal is broad rather than niche. This is not framed as a scientific research service, a retail trade activity, or a digital platform category. It is the making of manual instruments and related equipment. The eligible business scales are also broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as open. That means the classification can be used across a spectrum of operating sizes, from a small workshop-style manufacturing operation to a larger industrial producer, provided the declared activity stays inside the record’s stated manufacturing scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national table treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling shown in the record. There is no lower national cap in the slim record, and there is no additional national threshold, licence, timeline, or capital figure supplied here, so none should be read into the classification.

Bali is the more careful part of the reading. The record does not say this activity is simply blocked in Bali; `l4_bali_blocked` is false. But it does mark the Bali status as `Blocked (scope-dependent)`, and the reason is exacting: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity.” The moratorium rule supplied in the record is also blunt: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest conclusion is therefore not that Bali has a separate ownership percentage. It does not, in this record. The conclusion is that a PMA founder looking at Bali must verify the live OSS risk treatment for the exact declared activity, because the Bali issue turns on risk scope under the moratorium, not on a separate Bali foreign-share cap.
editorial.pullQuote: The Bali question is not a separate foreign-share percentage; it is whether the exact declared activity survives the province’s Low and Medium-Low risk moratorium in live OSS.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing electrical instruments that measure, test, detect, or monitor electricity, including simple current meters, sensors, and smart IoT-enabled control modules. It spans both basic industrial devices and advanced communication-capable monitoring equipment.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open for 100% foreign-owned PMA companies. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Alat Ukur dan Alat Uji Elektrik (26512)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers of electrical meters, sensors, or IoT-connected monitoring devices looking to establish a wholly owned production facility.

editorial.headline: Electric Testing Instruments, Open Nationally but Scope-Sensitive in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26512 covers the manufacture of electrical measuring, testing, detection, monitoring, and connected control equipment, with a national PMA ceiling of 100%.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26512 is a manufacturing classification for electrical measuring and testing equipment. Its scope is technical but broad: instruments for measurement, inspection, testing, detection, and monitoring of electrical or electric systems, whether or not the equipment is connected to scientific investigation. The record names current meters, electric sensors, measuring-device modules, and electrical monitoring or control equipment with communication capability, including Internet of Things functions. Accessories for those instruments also sit inside the scope.

In practical terms, this is not a retail, consulting, or installation category. It is about making the devices themselves: the meters, sensors, modules, monitoring units, and control equipment that allow electrical conditions to be measured, checked, detected, watched, or communicated. A founder reading this code should therefore treat the manufacturing activity as the anchor. The activity can be registered across the full scale range shown in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar.

Nationally, the investment picture is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. That means the national record does not impose a lower foreign-share cap for this activity. If the question is only whether KBLI 26512 is nationally open to foreign ownership, the answer from the slim record is yes, up to 100%.

Bali is less simple, and this is where the record asks for care rather than a shortcut. The Bali status is Blocked (scope-dependent), while `l4_bali_blocked` is false. The governing Bali note says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor letter. For this code, the Bali reason says OSS risk at scale Besar is low on some scopes but higher on others, and that PMA registration in Bali is only registrable by declaring the higher-risk scope, with live OSS verification required for the exact activity. So the honest reading is not that Bali adds a separate ownership percentage, and not that this code is cleanly blocked in every case. It is nationally open, but Bali registration depends on the exact declared scope and its OSS risk treatment.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacture of electronic measuring, testing, monitoring, and control instruments. It includes lab equipment like analytical instruments, scales, balances, and incubators, as well as electronic devices such as speedometers, radar, radio controls, sensors, and radiation detectors.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership, but in Bali it is currently blocked due to a moratorium on low and medium-low risk activities. As of 13 May 2026, no new PMA can be registered for this business in Bali, regardless of national policy.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Alat Ukur dan Alat Uji Elektronik (26513)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur producing precision electronic testing or lab equipment, and who is willing to base operations outside Bali until restrictions lift.

editorial.headline: Electronic Measuring Instruments, Nationally Open, Bali Scope-Dependent
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26513 covers factories making electronic measurement, testing, monitoring, control, and sensing equipment; nationally it is open to PMA up to 100%, while Bali depends on OSS risk by exact scope.
editorial.body:
This is the manufacturing code for electronic instruments that sense, measure, test, monitor, and control. The record's scope reaches laboratory analytical instruments, scales, balances, incubators, and other lab equipment used for measurement and testing. It also includes electronic measuring and inspection devices, whether tied to scientific investigation or not: automatic electronic controllers, speedometers, argometers, cathode-ray electronics, radar and radar equipment, radio control, electronic sensors, radiation detectors, and GPS.

The same scope continues into navigation, meteorology, geophysics, hydrology, and spectrophotometer instruments, plus digital measuring tools such as thermometers, barometers, and digital scales. It also covers proton and electron microscopes, except optical microscopes, and electronic monitoring and control modules with communication capability: IoT devices, embedded systems, data loggers, real-time monitoring units, early warning systems, including fire and theft alarms that send signals to a control station. The editorial point is not consumer electronics in general; it is instrumentation that turns physical conditions, movement, position, warning signals, and laboratory variables into measurable electronic information.

The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That matters because the code can hold anything from digital measuring tools to laboratory instruments, radar equipment, sensors, and electronic monitoring systems, provided the declared activity remains manufacturing inside this scope. The shared denominator is production, not a loose technology label. A registrant should treat the exact activity declaration as material, because the Bali field turns on OSS risk at scale Besar.

Nationally, the record is clean: pma_status is TERBUKA, pma_max_asing is 100, and the source named is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Plainly stated, the national record allows full foreign ownership for PMA registration. Bali is not as clean. l4_bali_blocked is false, but l4_bali_status is Blocked (scope-dependent). The reason is precise: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on some scopes but higher on others, so PMA registrability in Bali depends on declaring the higher-risk exact activity and checking live OSS for that activity. The standing Bali rule in this record is that the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So this is not a Bali no; it is a Bali yes only when the declared scope survives the OSS risk test.

editorial.headline: Precision Equipment Manufacturing With a Bali Scope Check
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers makers of measuring, testing, navigation and control equipment, nationally open to foreign ownership but sensitive to exact Bali scope.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 26519 is a manufacturing code for precision instruments.** The record describes it as the production of various measuring, testing, navigation and control equipment, including instruments used inside industrial processes. In plain English, this is the activity behind devices that measure heat, pressure, viscosity and the properties of goods. It is not a general trading category, and it should not be stretched into services or distribution simply because the finished products may later be sold.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar operators, which means the category can describe anything from a small specialist workshop to a larger industrial manufacturer, provided the declared business activity is still the making of these instruments. That breadth matters editorially: the same KBLI label can cover different operational realities, but the record keeps the common thread clear — equipment is being manufactured, and the equipment is for measurement, testing, navigation or control.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national record treats this activity as open up to 100% foreign ownership. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and there is no extra capital, licence, timeline or operational condition stated here. The honest national reading is therefore straightforward: as a national KBLI classification, this activity is foreign-open.

Bali requires more care. The Bali status is not a simple block; it is marked Blocked (scope-dependent), and l4_bali_blocked is false. The record’s own reason is precise and should be kept precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity.” The standing Bali moratorium rule says that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source listed as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the practical Bali conclusion is conditional, not decorative: this activity may be nationally open, but PMA registration in Bali depends on the exact declared scope and live OSS risk reading, especially at Besar scale.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this activity is foreign-open, but in Bali the decisive question is the exact scope declared in OSS.

editorial.headline: Timekeeping Manufacture Is Nationally Open, but Bali Blocks PMA Registration
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26520 covers the making of watches, clocks, time-recording devices, and their parts; nationally it is open to PMA, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
For a foreign-owned company looking at KBLI 26520, the decisive fact is not the national ceiling. Nationally, the activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with foreign ownership permitted up to **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In Bali, however, the record is explicit: this activity is blocked for PMA registration today. The reason given is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026**.

The business activity itself is the manufacture of time-measuring equipment. In plain English, this means making watches and clocks of many kinds: wristwatches, pocket watches, necklace watches, wall clocks, alarm clocks, bells, clock-panel devices, and clocks that contain radioactive substances. The scope also reaches deep into the industrial anatomy of timekeeping: movement parts, jewels, dials, plates, hands, bridges, springs, clock faces, watch cases, including cases made from precious metal, and protective outer covers made from different materials.

This is not only a consumer-watch category. The record also brings in equipment that measures, records, or displays intervals of time using a watch or clock mechanism or a synchronous motor. That includes alarms for watches, panel-clock instruments, chronometers, stopwatches, parking time recorders, employee attendance time recorders, time and date stamps, process-time recorders, and time switches or time locks. The common thread is precise mechanical or motor-driven time measurement, whether the product sits on a wall, a wrist, a factory panel, a parking system, or an administrative timekeeping desk.

On scale, the national record is broad: **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar** are all listed as open. That matters because it shows the activity is not confined to one size of enterprise in the national classification. But for a PMA structure in Bali, the scale openness does not rescue the filing. The Bali-side rule in the record says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the clean conclusion is this: KBLI 26520 can be understood as a nationally foreign-open timekeeping-manufacturing activity, but it cannot be registered by a foreign-owned company in Bali under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 26520 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but in Bali the record blocks PMA registration outright under the risk-class moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Peralatan Iradiasi, Perlengkapan, dan Sejenisnya
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan peralatan dan tabung iradiasi (penyinaran) yang didasarkan pada penggunaan radiasi sinar-X, sinar alfa, beta, gamma, atau radiasi pengion lainnya, yang digunakan untuk keperluan industri, diagnosis medis, terapi medis, penelitian, dan ilmu pengetahuan. Kelompok ini juga mencakup pembuatan peralatan sumber radiasi pengion untuk uji tak rusak, pengukuran (gauging), pengeboran (well logging), iradiasi (iradiator), pemindai barang, analisis, termasuk perlengkapan pembangkit radiasi pengion yang terkait keselamatan radiasi dan mutu citra, seperti kontrol panel dan screen (reseptor citra).
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup alat pembaca film sinar-X (X-ray film viewer), lihat kelompok 26602.

editorial.headline: Precision Radiation Equipment, Open Nationally and Clear for Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26601 covers the manufacture of irradiation and ionising-radiation equipment for industry, medicine, research, and scientific use.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26601 sits in a technically demanding corner of manufacturing: equipment built around ionising radiation. The record describes the making of irradiation equipment and tubes based on X-ray, alpha, beta, gamma, or other ionising radiation. Its uses are not narrow. The same activity can serve industrial applications, medical diagnosis, medical therapy, research, and scientific work. In plain English, this is the code for businesses that manufacture the physical equipment through which controlled radiation becomes a working industrial or medical tool.

The scope is broader than a single machine type. It includes equipment for ionising-radiation sources used in non-destructive testing, gauging, well logging, irradiation, goods scanning, and analysis. It also includes related radiation-generating accessories tied to radiation safety and image quality, including control panels and screens or image receptors. The record also names decommissioning and operation of Category III irradiator facilities using radioactive sources, which gives the activity a facility-side dimension as well as a manufacturing one. The common thread is not the customer segment, but the technical basis: equipment and facilities organised around ionising radiation.

For registration scale, the record is unusually wide. It is open to small, medium, and large businesses: **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar**. That matters because the activity is not framed in the record as only a large industrial category, even though its subject matter is specialised. A founder reading this code should understand it as a manufacturing and facility activity whose formal scale availability spans the full recorded range. The scale labels are the only scale facts in the record; they do not themselves add capital thresholds, licensing steps, or operating timelines.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with a recorded maximum foreign ownership of **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. Bali does not change that into a separate percentage or ownership cap in this record. Its Bali-side status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason given is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is not marked as blocked. So the honest reading is direct: nationally, KBLI 26601 is fully foreign-open; in Bali, the record does not block PMA registration under the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is direct: nationally, KBLI 26601 is fully foreign-open; in Bali, the record does not block PMA registration under the moratorium.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan peralatan dan perlengkapan elektromedik dan elektroterapi, seperti peralatan elektrokardiograf (EKG), peralatan tes mata (termasuk reflektor, endoskopi, dan lain-lain), peralatan terapi ozon, peralatan terapi oksigen, penangkap citra (scanner) untuk diagnostik medis, peralatan magnetic resonce imaging (MRI), peralatan ultrasonografi (USG), peralatan endoskopi elektromedik, peralatan laser medis, alat bantu dengar, alat bantu dan terapi pernapasan, alat pacu jantung, alat pijat medis elektrik, alat pembaca film sinar-X (X-ray film viewer), dan ventilator elektromedik. Kelompok ini juga mencakup pembuatan peralatan atau perangkat elektromedik dan elektroterapi yang dilengkapi dengan fitur internet of things (IoT).

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this is open to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali it is currently not blocked by the local PMA moratorium. editorial.headline: Electromedical Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26602 covers the making of serious medical devices, from ECG and MRI equipment to ventilators, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26602 is a manufacturing code for electromedical and electrotherapy equipment. In plain English, it covers the production of medical devices that use electrical, imaging, therapeutic, or connected functions: electrocardiograph equipment, eye-testing equipment, ozone and oxygen therapy equipment, diagnostic medical scanners, MRI equipment, ultrasonography equipment, electromedical endoscopy equipment, medical lasers, hearing aids, respiratory assistance and therapy devices, pacemakers, electric medical massage equipment, X-ray film viewers, and electromedical ventilators. The record also brings internet-of-things features inside the same activity, where the electromedical or electrotherapy device is made with connected functionality.

That scope is broad, but it is not vague. The centre of gravity is the making of equipment and supplies, not a general healthcare service description. A founder registering under this activity is describing a production business around electromedical or electrotherapy devices. The examples in the record range from diagnostic equipment to therapy equipment and assistive devices, which is why the activity reads as a serious industrial code rather than a narrow product label.

The scale picture is unusually straightforward in the slim record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as open. That matters because the activity is not reserved in the record for only one size of operator. A small founder, a mid-sized manufacturer, or a larger industrial setup can all read the scale line without needing to invent a missing category. The record does not add any extra licence, capital, threshold, tax, or operating timeline, so none should be assumed from the editorial layer.

The foreign-ownership picture is also clear. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 named as the source. Bali does not change that into a hidden percentage. The Bali-side field is not a separate ownership cap; it says OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this code is marked as not blocked. The honest reading, therefore, is simple: nationally open, foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the slim record provided.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial-scale manufacturing of photographic equipment: all types of cameras (film, instant, digital, underwater, forensic, aerial survey, microfilm) and accessories like light meters and flash apparatus. It’s the ‘making’ side, not retail or repair.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, 100% foreign ownership is permitted. In Bali, this activity is not blocked by the general moratorium, but it is classified as medium-high risk at every business scale, from micro to large—meaning location-specific approval (zoning, environmental checks) is required, and not every address will automatically qualify.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Fotografi (26701)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign manufacturer or industrial investor wanting to set up camera/photo-equipment production in Indonesia, whether for the local market or export.

editorial.headline: Photographic Equipment Manufacturing, With Bali Open on the Record
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26701 covers the manufacture of cameras and photographic equipment, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26701 is the industrial code for making photographic equipment. In plain English, it covers the manufacture of cameras and closely related photographic apparatus: ordinary still cameras, instant-print cameras, microfilm cameras, digital cameras, cameras fitted with mini projectors, underwater cameras, still-picture cameras, aerial-research cameras, forensic or criminology comparison cameras, and other photographic cameras. The scope also reaches the equipment around the camera itself, including photographic light meters, photographic flash apparatus, and flash bulbs other than tube lamps.

That makes this a manufacturing classification, not a retail, studio, or media-service activity. The record is concerned with the production of the physical photographic devices and equipment named in the scope. A founder using this code should therefore be describing an industrial activity centered on making cameras or photographic instruments, rather than selling cameras, operating photography services, or producing visual content. The language of the scope is broad inside that manufacturing lane, but it remains anchored to photographic equipment.

The scale picture is unusually clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the record does not reserve it only for large manufacturers or only for small domestic operators. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here is 100%. In practical editorial terms, the national record treats this as a foreign-open manufacturing activity, with no lower foreign cap shown in the slim record.

The Bali question is the point to read carefully. The Bali moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But this code is not marked as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason given is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a hidden Bali closure. On this record, KBLI 26701 is nationally open, carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and is not blocked by the Bali PMA moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of cinematographic cameras and projectors, with or without built-in sound recording and playback, plus related accessories like camera frames, casings, and film holders.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the local moratorium on low-risk sectors, but it falls under medium-high risk at every business scale, from micro to large—so a PMA can be established, provided you secure a business address zoned for industrial manufacturing and obtain the required environmental, safety, or operational permits.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Sinematografi (26702)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur setting up a manufacturing base in Bali to produce professional cinema equipment and accessories for the film industry, either for the domestic market or export.

editorial.headline: Cinematography Equipment Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 26702 covers the manufacture of cinematography cameras, projectors, and related accessories, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26702 is a manufacturing activity, not a production-house, studio, rental, or media-service category. The slim record defines it around the making of cinematography equipment: various kinds of cinematography cameras and projectors, whether or not they are fitted with sound recording and reproduction apparatus. It also reaches the making of cinematography accessories, including camera frames, camera casings, and film holders. In plain English, this is the industrial side of cinema hardware: the physical devices and fittings that allow moving images to be captured, projected, housed, or handled.

That scope matters because the record places the activity inside manufacturing, and it is open across the listed operating scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A founder reading this code should therefore see it as suitable where the registered business is making the equipment itself or its cinematography-specific accessories. The record does not add separate language on retail, distribution, repair, content creation, venue operation, or film services, so those ideas should not be smuggled into the interpretation. The editorial centre of gravity remains narrow: cameras, projectors, sound-capable or not, and the accessory hardware named in the scope.

Nationally, the investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded for this activity is 100%, not a lower capped stake. The source field for that PMA reading is `Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021`. Nothing in the slim record adds a minimum capital figure, special licensing threshold, tax treatment, registration timeline, or operational condition, so the correct reading is limited but useful: this activity is nationally open to foreign investment at the full percentage shown in the record.

The Bali picture is also important, because many KBLI choices that look viable nationally can fail at the Bali registration layer. Here, the slim record does **not** mark the activity as blocked in Bali: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently; this code is not caught by that block on the facts provided. So the honest conclusion is restrained but positive: KBLI 26702 is nationally foreign-open, and the Bali moratorium data supplied here does not block PMA registration for it today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Optical Lenses Beyond Eyewear: KBLI 26703 in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This is a precision manufacturing code for non-eyeglass optical lenses, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26703 covers the manufacture of optical lenses that are not eyeglass lenses. Its field is specialised and technical: lenses for photography, cinematography, medicine, industry, and scientific work. The record names camera lenses, projector lenses, microscope lenses, telescope lenses, spectrometer lenses, and similar optical products. It also includes objective lenses for cameras and projectors, camera zoom lenses, and coated lenses that have been ground.

The practical identity of the code is therefore not retail eyewear, lens fitting, or general optical trade. It is manufacturing: the production of optical components used inside instruments, imaging systems, projection systems, laboratory tools, and industrial or medical equipment. A founder using this code should be describing a business that makes these lenses, not merely imports, sells, repairs, or installs them. The scope is narrow in the useful sense: it tells the market, OSS, and counterparties that the business is operating in the industrial production of non-eyeglass optical lenses.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not reserved only for large manufacturers; it can describe a smaller optical production activity as well as a larger industrial operation, provided the actual activity remains within the manufacturing scope described above. The code can therefore fit a workshop-scale producer of specialised optical lenses, a mid-sized manufacturer making camera or projection lens components, or a larger facility serving scientific, medical, industrial, or imaging applications.

The national foreign-ownership position is clean: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows full foreign ownership. The Bali picture is also unusually clear: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The recorded reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA in Bali, island-wide and permanently, but this code is not marked as blocked under that rule. So the honest conclusion is straightforward: nationally, KBLI 26703 is foreign-open, and on this record it is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Peralatan Fotografi dan Instrumen Optik Bukan Kacamata Lainnya
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan peralatan fotografi dan instrumen optik bukan kacamata lainnya, termasuk bagian-bagiannya yang belum diklasifikasikan di tempat lain yang digunakan untuk ilmu pengetahuan dan percetakan, seperti teropong monokular, teropong astronomi, elbow telescope, periskop, optik, spektroskop, dan spektrografi, termasuk mikroskop optik, teleskop binokular, cermin optik, peralatan kaca pembesar optik, peralatan presisi optik untuk keperluan mekanik, komparator optik, peralatan pembidik senjata optik, peralatan positioning optik, serta peralatan dan instrumen pengukuran dan pemeriksaan optik (misalnya peralatan pengontrol api atau fire control equipment, pengukur jarak). Kelompok ini juga mencakup pembuatan motion picture dan slide projector, overhead transparancy projector, peralatan laser, pita magnetik audio dan video unrecorded, dan cakram optik unrecorded.

editorial.headline: Precision Optics Manufacturing with a Clear Bali Reading
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers specialist photographic, laser, projection, and optical-instrument manufacturing, nationally open to PMA up to 100% and not blocked for Bali registration under the record's risk note.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26709 belongs to the manufacturing side of precision seeing, projecting, measuring, and unrecorded media. The record describes the making of photographic equipment and optical instruments other than eyeglasses, including parts that are not classified elsewhere in its scope language. Its center of gravity is technical hardware: monocular and astronomical telescopes, elbow telescopes, periscopes, optical components, spectroscopes and spectrographic equipment, optical microscopes, binocular telescopes, optical mirrors, magnifying equipment, and precision optical apparatus for mechanical use. It also includes optical comparators, optical weapon-sighting equipment, positioning instruments, and optical measuring or inspection equipment such as fire-control equipment and rangefinders.

The scope then widens from instruments to image and light-output equipment. Motion picture and slide projectors, overhead transparency projectors, laser equipment, unrecorded audio and video magnetic tape, and unrecorded optical discs all sit inside the same activity description. Read plainly, this is a production code for enterprises that manufacture precision optical, projection, laser, photographic, or unrecorded-media products. It is not written as a service activity; the operative verb throughout the record is manufacture, and the examples stay close to physical equipment, instruments, parts, and media.

On scale, the record is broad rather than selective. Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open, so the activity can be read across the full scale ladder given in the slim record: from small makers of defined optical equipment to larger manufacturers of the same category of goods. That breadth does not loosen the scope. The clean registration narrative stays close to the named products and parts: optical instruments, photographic equipment, laser equipment, projectors, measurement and inspection optics, and unrecorded media. The more the business description drifts away from making those goods, the less it resembles the activity captured here.

The national PMA position is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100; in investor language, the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%. Bali does not add a second percentage in this record. Its l4_bali_status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the reason is `OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium`. The moratorium rule still matters because the record says Bali province blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But for this activity, the Bali line is not a stop sign. The honest reading is straightforward: nationally open, fully foreign-ownable up to the record's ceiling, and not blocked in Bali under the risk note provided.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is straightforward: nationally open, fully foreign-ownable up to the record's ceiling, and not blocked in Bali under the risk note provided.

editorial.headline: Blank Media Manufacturing Is Nationally Open, But Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the making of blank magnetic and optical recording media, nationally open to foreign ownership but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26800 is a manufacturing code for blank recording media: the physical carriers that can hold sound, images, or data before any content is placed on them. The record places audio and video magnetic tape, blank audio and video cassettes, blank vinyl records, unexposed film, data-recording tape, blank disks and diskettes, and blank optical discs inside the same industrial frame. Its center of gravity is not publishing, recording, duplication, or computer services; it is the making of the empty medium itself.

That distinction matters because this is a production activity, not a content activity. A company using this code is registering the industrial manufacture of carriers for future recording, storage, or distribution. The slim record opens the activity across the full business-size spectrum: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical registration language, the code is not reserved only for large factories in the national classification; the record says every listed scale is open to it.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position leaves no ambiguity. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national layer alone, that means a foreign-owned company can treat the activity as open, with no lower foreign-share ceiling stated in the slim record. Nothing in the record adds a special national threshold, licence, timeline, capital rule, or operational condition, so none should be implied.

Bali changes the answer completely. The record marks this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali, with the Bali status Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, and the cited source is Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest reading is narrow but decisive: KBLI 26800 is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, yet a foreign investor cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali today under the Bali-side moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 26800 is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, yet a foreign investor cannot register it as a PMA activity in Bali today.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of electric motors and their key components, including AC and DC motors, armatures, stators, rotors, brushes, and commutators. It is focused on building electric drive units rather than the starter motors used in combustion engines.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership, but in Bali it is currently blocked for PMA companies. A moratorium since 13 May 2026 suspends new foreign registrations for low and medium-low risk businesses, which includes this sector.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Motor Listrik (27111)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers or clean-tech entrepreneurs in electric vehicle drivetrains or industrial motor production looking to establish local assembly or component fabrication.

editorial.headline: Electric Motor Manufacturing Is Nationally Open, but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27111 covers the making of electric motors and core components, with a clear national PMA opening and a firm Bali registration block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27111 is the industrial code for making electric motors and the parts that make those motors work. The slim record defines the activity around electric motor production and its components or parts, including alternating-current motors, direct-current motors, dynamo armatures, stators, rotors, brushes, and commutators. It expressly excludes internal combustion engines used to start motors. In plain English, this is a manufacturing classification for the physical production of electric motor systems and their essential electromechanical components, not a general trading, repair, or combustion-engine category.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to micro, small, medium, and large businesses, so the code is not reserved only for heavy industrial operators. A small workshop making components and a larger manufacturing operation can both sit within the same activity description, provided the real business activity is the manufacture of the electric motors or listed parts themselves. That matters because the code is defined by what is being made: AC motors, DC motors, armatures, stators, rotors, brushes, commutators, and related components or parts.

Nationally, the foreign-investment reading is straightforward. The PMA status is marked as TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. On the national rule set alone, this is therefore a foreign-open manufacturing activity with no lower foreign-ownership ceiling stated in the slim record. For founders reading the code from Jakarta or from the national investment list, the key takeaway is simple: the record treats KBLI 27111 as open to full foreign ownership at the national level.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. The stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a soft caveat. A foreign investor may see a nationally open, 100% PMA-eligible activity, but cannot register this PMA activity in Bali today under the Bali moratorium recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

That means a foreign investor cannot set up a PMA in Bali for this activity right now—other Indonesian regions without such restrictions remain an option.

editorial.headline: Generator Manufacturing Is Open Nationally, But Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27112 covers generator manufacturing across every business scale, yet the record blocks PMA registration in Bali under the province’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27112 is the manufacturing code for electric generators and their parts. Its scope is industrial rather than retail-facing: it covers the making of AC generators, DC generators, generator sets, stators, rotors, commutators, and rotary converters. The record also includes power generators, motor-generator devices, and generator units with a prime mover, while carving out battery-charging alternators for internal combustion engines and turbine generator devices. In plain English, this is the code for businesses that manufacture the machinery and core components that turn mechanical input into electrical output.

The code is broad in business scale. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can describe anything from a very small producer of generator components to a large-scale manufacturer assembling complete generator systems. That breadth matters because the activity is not limited to one size of enterprise in the national classification record. A founder reading this code should therefore focus less on whether the activity sounds “big” and more on whether the actual business is manufacturing generators, generator parts, or covered generator devices.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership shown in the record is 100%. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national layer alone, this is not presented as a closed or capped activity for foreign ownership. For a foreign-owned setup, that would normally be the clean headline: the classification is open, the ceiling is 100%, and every business scale is listed as open in the record.

Bali changes the practical answer completely. The record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true and gives the reason as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” It also states the province rule directly: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” So the honest reading is this: KBLI 27112 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here. The source named for that Bali rule is Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 27112 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
