data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Transformers Open Nationally, Blocked for Foreign Setup in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers transformer and rectifier manufacturing, open to all business scales nationally but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s moratorium flag.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27113 is an industrial manufacturing activity: the making of transformers, current converters, rectifiers, and their components or parts. In practical terms, the record places here the equipment that changes, distributes, regulates, or converts electrical power: distribution transformers, power transformers, special transformers, AC-to-DC current converters, radiators, commutators, electrical distribution transformers, arc-welding transformers, fluorescent or lighting ballasts, substation transformers for power distribution, and devices that regulate electrical transmission and distribution voltage.

That scope is broad but still coherent. It is not a general electrical-trading activity, and it is not merely installation or repair. The center of gravity is fabrication: producing the physical devices and parts that sit inside electricity networks, workshops, lighting systems, substations, and voltage-control environments. A founder reading this record should understand the activity as manufacturing for the electrical conversion and distribution chain, with both finished equipment and component-level production included in the field described by the Indonesian scope.

The scale position is unusually wide. The record marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it is not reserved only for a large industrial investor in the national classification data supplied here. A smaller manufacturer making components, a medium-sized production operation, and a larger transformer or rectifier factory all sit within the stated scale envelope, provided the actual registered activity remains inside the manufacturing scope described above. Nationally, the PMA line is also clear: the activity is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded as 100 and the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows a fully foreign-owned PMA structure for this activity.

Bali is where the answer changes. The same record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the Bali status as Blocked (risk class). The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule supplied in the record is equally direct: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source identified as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is this: the activity is open to foreign ownership nationally, but a foreign investor cannot register this KBLI as a PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this transformer and rectifier manufacturing activity is foreign-open; in Bali, the record says it is blocked for PMA registration today.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing electrical control and distribution hardware: voltage regulators, circuit breakers, surge suppressors, automatic control panels, switchgear, relays, electrical piping for switchboards, fuses and related components.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign PMA. In Bali, however, it is blocked for new foreign-owned companies because of a regional moratorium on low/medium-low risk business classes in force since 13 May 2026—so you cannot currently register a PMA for this activity on the island.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Pengontrol dan Pendistribusian Listrik (27120)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign manufacturer of electrical distribution and control equipment aiming to produce locally—who must wait until the Bali moratorium lifts or consider another Indonesian province.

editorial.headline: Electrical Control Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27120 covers the industrial manufacture of electrical control and distribution equipment, with full national PMA openness but a Bali registration block for PMA.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27120 is a manufacturing code for the hardware that controls, protects, switches, and distributes electrical power. Its scope includes voltage regulators, circuit breakers, surge suppressors for distribution-voltage systems, control panels for power distribution, switchgear and its components, automatic control panels, lighting distribution boards, control desks, electrical relays, switchboard conduits or channels, fuses, power-switching equipment, electrical power switches, and kWh meters.

In practical terms, this is not a trading or installation activity. It is the factory-side production of the apparatus that sits inside electrical distribution systems: the boards, relays, breakers, regulators, switches, fuses, and metering equipment that make power controllable and interruptible. The record also draws the boundary by exclusion, keeping this activity focused on control and distribution equipment rather than other electrical, process-control, generator, soldering, converter, or combustion-engine starter equipment.

The national investment picture is straightforward. Citing Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record lists the activity as TERBUKA and sets pma_max_asing at 100. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The activity is also open across all listed operating scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. For a founder reading the code nationally, the signal is broad: this is an industrial manufacturing activity that can be registered at any of those scales, and the national PMA line is open up to full foreign ownership.

Bali changes the answer. The same slim record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and therefore the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium from May 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is categorical: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is this: nationally, KBLI 27120 is foreign-open; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it for PMA today under the Bali-side block described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 27120 is foreign-open; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it for PMA today.

Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan berbagai macam batu baterai, seperti sel dan baterai listrik primer, baterai alkali, baterai merkuri, serta pembuatan baterai dan sel-sel turunannya, termasuk di dalamnya pembuatan sel yang menggunakan mangan dioksida, merkuri dioksida, atau perak oksida; serta pembuatan baterai asam timbal/lead acid, baterai nikel-kadmium (NiCad), baterai hidrida logam nikel/nickel-metal hydride (NiMH), baterai litium, baterai sel kering, dan baterai sel basah (termasuk baterai untuk ponsel dan laptop).

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of all types of batteries, from primary cells (like alkaline, mercury, and silver oxide) to rechargeable batteries such as lead-acid, NiCad, NiMH, and lithium-ion batteries (including those for phones and laptops), as well as associated energy storage systems.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, this activity is not blocked by the investment moratorium, but it is classified as medium-high risk. You will need a suitable industrial-zone address and must pass additional verification during registration; it’s allowed but not a simple process.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Batu Baterai (27201)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign industrialists planning a genuine battery manufacturing plant in Bali, not a virtual office or small workshop.

editorial.headline: Battery Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27201 covers battery and portable energy-storage manufacturing, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27201 is the industrial home for making batteries, cells, and battery-based portable energy-storage products. Its scope is broad but still specific: primary electric cells and batteries, alkaline batteries, mercury batteries, and derivative cells made with materials such as manganese dioxide, mercury dioxide, or silver oxide. It also covers lead-acid batteries, nickel-cadmium batteries, nickel-metal hydride batteries, lithium batteries, dry cells, and wet cells, including batteries for phones and laptops.

The record also brings newer portable storage into the same activity. Manufacturing battery energy storage systems for portable devices, including power banks for phones, tablets, and similar devices, belongs here. So does making batteries that use cathodes produced by the manufacturer itself. In plain English, this is not merely retail packaging or trading of battery products; it is the industrial activity of producing the battery, cell, or portable battery-storage system itself.

Registration is open across the stated business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not framed as only a large-factory category in the record, even though large-scale operations are part of the pathway. A founder reading this should treat scale as a registration dimension, not as a change in the underlying activity. The same code is anchored in manufacturing batteries and related cells, while the business scale determines how the setup is positioned inside OSS.

The foreign-investment picture is unusually clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate ownership ceiling in this record. Instead, the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and l4_bali_blocked is false. The reason given is direct: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters in the background because Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this record does not mark KBLI 27201 as blocked in Bali. For this activity, the honest reading is therefore straightforward: a foreign-owned company may use this battery-manufacturing code nationally, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is straightforward: the record marks battery manufacturing as nationally foreign-open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Electric Accumulator Manufacturing: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of electric accumulators and their components, with full-scale national openness but a clear Bali PMA block.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 27202 is about manufacturing electric accumulators, not merely trading or installing them.** The record describes the activity as the making of various electric accumulators and their components, including 6 V or 12 V batteries with power of 200 A or less. It also reaches into the physical parts that make the accumulator work: battery plates, separators, containers, covers or wrapping, poles, and toothed battery clamps. In plain English, this is the industrial code for producing the battery unit and its core components, from the casing to the conductive and connecting parts.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not framed only as a large-factory category. A small producer, a medium industrial operator, or a larger manufacturing company can all sit within the formal scale range described by the record, provided the registered activity is the manufacture of electric accumulators and the listed components. That breadth matters because the code’s scope is technical but not narrow: it covers the finished accumulator and the parts that define its industrial production chain.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. That means the national record treats this activity as open to full foreign ownership. There is no lower national ceiling in the slim record, and there is no additional national condition supplied here. The honest national reading is therefore straightforward: for Indonesia as a whole, this activity is foreign-open up to the full percentage stated in the record.

Bali is the decisive exception. The same record marks the Bali status as **Blocked (risk class)** and sets `l4_bali_blocked` to true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, which is blocked by the Bali moratorium in May 2026. The moratorium rule is even broader in wording: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source given as **Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP**. So the practical editorial lede is not the national openness; it is the Bali block. A foreign-owned company may see a 100% national ceiling in the record, but for Bali PMA registration today this activity is marked as blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign-owned company may see a 100% national ceiling in the record, but for Bali PMA registration today this activity is marked as blocked.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Electric-Vehicle Battery Manufacturing, Open at National and Bali Level
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27203 covers the manufacture of electric-vehicle batteries, including BESS for EVs, and is open to PMA registration across all recorded scales.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27203 is a manufacturing activity for batteries used in electric vehicles and electric bicycles. The record also brings battery-based energy storage systems into scope when they are made for electric vehicles, and it includes electric-vehicle batteries made with cathodes produced by the same operator. In plain English, this is not a trading or repair category: its centre of gravity is production, with the activity defined around making the battery product itself.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The slim record marks the activity as open to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** operators, so the registration frame is not limited to one business size. That matters because the code can cover a small manufacturing setup as well as a larger industrial operator, provided the activity being registered remains inside the recorded scope: making batteries for electric vehicles or electric bicycles, including BESS for electric vehicles, and including battery production using self-produced cathodes.

Nationally, the PMA reading is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100**. Rendered commercially, that means the national foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**. There is no lower foreign-share cap in the slim record, and no additional national condition is stated here beyond the recorded PMA status, ceiling, and source. The responsible editorial reading is therefore direct: for a foreign-owned setup at national level, this activity is recorded as open up to full foreign ownership.

The Bali picture is also open on this record, but for a specific reason. The province-wide moratorium rule in the record blocks **Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA**, island-wide and permanently. KBLI 27203 is not marked as blocked in Bali: `l4_bali_blocked` is **false**, and the Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. The recorded reason is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. So the honest national-versus-Bali conclusion is not a warning about a Bali ban, nor a hidden local percentage. It is simpler: this code is nationally foreign-open, carries a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-versus-Bali conclusion is not a hidden local percentage: this code is foreign-open nationally and not blocked in Bali by the recorded moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This KBLI covers the manufacturing of fiber optic cables used for direct data or image transmission, with or without connectors. It does not include the production of raw glass fibers, separate connector manufacturing, or installation of cables.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the local moratorium, but it falls under a medium-high risk classification, meaning you must verify that your specific business address meets zoning and other local requirements before registration.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kabel Serat Optik (27310)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs looking to set up a fiber optic cable factory rather than just trading or installing cables, provided they can secure a compliant location in Bali.

editorial.headline: Fiber-Optic Cable Manufacturing as Infrastructure Industry
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27310 covers the factory production of fiber-optic cables for data or image transmission, nationally open to PMA and not blocked in Bali under this record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 27310 is a manufacturing code, not an installation code.** Its center of gravity is the production of fiber-optic cable used to carry data or images directly. The record makes the line quite specific: the cable may be supplied with connectors or without them, but the activity remains the making of the cable itself. It is not the making of glass fiber as a material, not the separate production of connectors, bundles, or cable connectors, and not the field work of installing fiber-optic or other cables. In practical terms, this is the industrial side of digital infrastructure: the plant, process, and output behind the cable before it is deployed into a network.

For registration, the code is open across all stated business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine the activity to a narrow industrial class or reserve it only for large operators. A small manufacturer, a mid-sized supplier, or a larger industrial facility can all sit within the stated scale range, provided the registered activity is genuinely the manufacture of fiber-optic cable described in the scope. The editorial caution is therefore about activity fit, not about stretching the code: a company using this code should be making the cable product, rather than importing, trading, installing, or separately producing adjacent components.

The national foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling. There is no extra threshold, licence, capital floor, or timing condition in the slim record, so none should be read into the code. The source attached to that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, which is the only source stated here for the PMA opening.

The Bali picture is also relatively straightforward, but it needs to be said precisely. Bali’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across the province. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked in Bali. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. So the honest reading is not that Bali has a separate foreign-ownership cap, quota, or local partnership requirement; the record gives none. It says the activity is nationally open to PMA, and on the Bali side it is not blocked by the moratorium because of the recorded risk position at large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that this is a nationally open PMA manufacturing activity and, on this record, not blocked for Bali registration.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity involves the manufacture of insulated electrical and telecommunication cables and wires made from steel, copper, or aluminium, as well as computer, printer, and USB cables produced without connectors attached. It excludes drawing bare metal wire, making ready-to-use cable assemblies with connectors, and automotive wiring sets.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, this KBLI is not blocked by the moratorium but is flagged as medium-high/high risk. A foreign-owned company can be established, yet you must verify that your specific business address meets local zoning and risk-assessment requirements, and expect additional licensing steps.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kabel dan Kawat Listrik dan Elektronik Lainnya (27320)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to produce bulk insulated cable and wire for industrial or telecom supply chains in Bali.

editorial.headline: Insulated Cable Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27320 covers the making of insulated electrical, telecom, computer, printer, and USB cabling, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27320 is a manufacturing classification for the physical production of insulated or sheathed cable and wire. Its centre of gravity is material transformation: steel, copper, or aluminium becomes protected cable stock for electrical and electronic use. The scope includes electric cable and telecommunication cable, and it also reaches computer, printer, and USB cables when those cables are made without connectors. That connector point matters editorially because the record draws the activity around cable and wire production itself, not finished connector-equipped cable assemblies.

The record also keeps the boundary clean. This activity does not cover bare wire drawing where metal is made into wire without insulation, and it does not cover electrical cable that already carries insulated wire and connectors. It also leaves out automotive cable assemblies. In practical registration language, a founder choosing this code should be describing a production operation that makes insulated or sheathed cable and wire, not a broader electronics assembly business and not a raw metal-wire operation. The business story is industrial, process-led, and product-specific.

On scale, the record is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are open. That means the classification is not reserved only for large plants in the record; it can describe activity from smaller manufacturing setups through larger industrial operations, provided the declared activity remains within the recorded scope. The PMA picture is equally direct at national level. The status is TERBUKA, the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and the source given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as foreign-open, with full foreign ownership allowed by the recorded ceiling.

The Bali reading is not a hidden contradiction. The record says l4_bali_blocked is false and gives the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its reason is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not marked as blocked by that rule. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is clean: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and not recorded as blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium logic.

editorial.headline: Cable-Accessory Manufacturing With a Clean PMA Reading
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27330 covers the making of electrical cable fittings and related hardware, with the record marking it nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali's PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27330 sits in the practical hardware layer of electrical infrastructure. Its scope is the making of current-carrying and non-current-carrying wire equipment for electrical circuits, across all materials. In plain English, this is the manufacturing of the components that let electrical systems connect, switch, protect, mount, and carry current: conductor bars, electrical conductors outside switchgear type, fittings, switches, sockets, GFCI units, lamp holders, lightning rods, coils, plugs, connectors, electrical boxes, conduit and its fittings, transmission poles, line hardware, and plastic non-current-carrying parts such as junction boxes, face plates, pole-line equipment, and plastic switch covers.

The business identity here is manufacturing, not trading, installation, or a general electrical-services label. A company choosing this code is saying that its activity is to make these cable accessories and wiring-equipment components. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale, so the classification is not confined to a single business size. What matters is that the registered activity remains within the product scope: electrical cable equipment and related hardware, including both conductive parts and non-conductive supporting parts. Ceramic insulators are outside the stated scope.

For a foreign-owned PMA reading, the national position is unusually direct. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling recorded here is 100%, not a partial cap. The cited source is the presidential-regulation source named in the record, and there is no separate national limitation stated in the slim record. For a founder checking the classification itself, the national answer is therefore open.

The Bali side does not reverse that answer. Bali's moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not marked as blocked. The Bali reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The honest reading is not national yes and Bali no; it is national yes, and Bali not blocked by the moratorium on this record. Do not add a Bali percentage, partnership condition, quota, or local-side cap: the record gives none.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is not national yes and Bali no; it is national yes, and Bali not blocked by the moratorium on this record.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Incandescent, Stage, UV and Medical Lighting Manufacturing in One Code
editorial.standfirst: A nationally foreign-open lighting manufacturing activity that spans every business scale, but is blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27401 is a manufacturing code for a specific corner of the lighting industry: the making of incandescent lamps and related specialist lamps. The record describes ordinary lighting bulbs, while excluding fittings and accessories. It also reaches into photographic flash bulbs, stage and spotlight lamps, ultraviolet lamps, infrared lamps, flashlight lamps, and lighting used in medical equipment. In practical terms, this is not a retail lighting code and not a broad electrical-goods label; it is about producing the lamps themselves, from familiar bulbs to more technical illumination products used in photography, performance, portable lighting, and medical devices.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe a small production operation as well as a larger industrial manufacturer. That breadth matters editorially because the activity is not reserved in the record for only one business size. A founder reading the classification should see it as a manufacturing scope that can sit at different operational scales, provided the business being registered is genuinely making the kinds of lamps named in the scope rather than trading them or producing separate lighting accessories.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the source listed for that national position. On the national reading alone, this is therefore not a restricted foreign-ownership activity in the slim record. The honest interpretation is simple: as a national KBLI category, this lighting-manufacturing activity is open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling.

Bali changes the answer completely. The record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. Its reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is also explicit: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the practical Bali lede is not that the activity is nationally closed; it is the opposite. The code is nationally foreign-open, but a foreign-owned company cannot register this KBLI in Bali today because the Bali-side moratorium blocks it for PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: The code is nationally foreign-open, but a foreign-owned company cannot register this KBLI in Bali today because the Bali-side moratorium blocks it for PMA registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Gas and Discharge Lamps: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27402 covers the manufacture of gas and discharge lamps; nationally it is foreign-open, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27402 is a manufacturing classification for gas and discharge lamps. The record defines the activity as the making of various gas and discharge lamps, including neon, helium, argon, sodium, and mercury lamps, as well as electric lamps used for insect traps. Its center of gravity is therefore industrial production, not retailing, installation, or lighting consultancy. A company using this code should be able to point to the actual manufacture of these lamp types as the activity being registered.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so the classification is not reserved only for large factories. It can describe a small producer as well as a larger manufacturing operation, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope: making gas and discharge lamps and the included electric insect-trap lamps. That breadth matters because the KBLI code is about the nature of the activity first, while the business scale sits alongside it as a registration dimension.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clear. For national PMA, the entry records TERBUKA status with pma_max_asing set at 100, citing Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower foreign-share ceiling in the slim record, and no special national condition stated here beyond that open status and source reference.

Bali is the decisive exception. The same record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the reason as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". It also states the Bali moratorium rule: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the honest reading is not that KBLI 27402 is difficult, ambiguous, or merely capped in Bali. It is nationally open to PMA, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the Bali-side risk-class moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 27402 is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the recorded risk-class moratorium.

editorial.headline: Vehicle Lighting Manufacturing Is Open Nationally, but Bali Needs Scope Discipline
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27403 covers the making of vehicle lighting and its components, with national PMA openness but a Bali position that depends on exact OSS scope.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27403 is a manufacturing classification for the lighting equipment used on transport vehicles. The record places inside it the making of lighting for motorbikes, cars, aircraft, ships, and other transport equipment. Its examples are concrete rather than decorative: brake lights, turn-signal lamps, interior lamps, and related components and accessories. In plain English, this is the activity of producing the lighting systems and parts that allow vehicles to signal, illuminate, and operate visibly as transport equipment.

The scale position is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** business scales, so it is not framed only as a large industrial category. A smaller workshop producing components and a larger manufacturer assembling lighting equipment both sit within the recorded scale range, provided the declared activity remains inside the stated scope. The important editorial point is that the classification is about production, not retailing, importing, repair, or vehicle operation. The centre of gravity is the manufacture of vehicle-lighting equipment and its parts.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. That means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full stated ceiling. Nothing in the slim record adds a sector-specific licence, capital threshold, tax treatment, or special minimum investment rule, so those should not be inferred from the classification itself. For a founder reading the KBLI record, the national signal is clean: this is an open PMA activity at the recorded ceiling.

Bali is more delicate. The Bali status is **Blocked (scope-dependent)**, and the record does not mark the activity as automatically blocked; `l4_bali_blocked` is false. But the reason is explicit: **OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity**. That must be read together with the moratorium rule: **Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)**. So the honest Bali reading is not a separate percentage cap and not a blanket national contradiction. It is a scope-and-risk problem: this activity is nationally open, but PMA registration in Bali depends on the exact OSS activity being declared and verified against the Bali moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: The national record is open, but Bali turns this into a scope-and-risk question rather than a simple yes.

editorial.headline: LED Lamp Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers LED lamp production, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s risk note.
editorial.body:
**Industri Lampu LED** is a manufacturing activity, not a retail label or a general electronics catch-all. The record defines it as the making of LED lamps, whether the lamp is produced as a separate LED unit or assembled into a lamp for a particular use. The examples in scope are concrete: LED lamps used in flashlights, vehicles, or public lighting. That makes the center of gravity clear. This is about producing LED lighting goods, including use-specific assemblies, rather than merely trading, installing, or designing them.

The registration picture is broad on business scale. The slim record opens the activity to **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar** scales, so the code is not reserved only for a large industrial operator. A small producer and a larger manufacturing operation sit inside the same activity definition if their work is the making of LED lamps described in the scope. The editorial discipline here matters: the record says what the activity covers and which scales are open; it does not add capital thresholds, production volumes, factory-size tests, or technical licensing conditions. Those details should not be read into the code.

Nationally, the PMA signal is straightforward. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In plain English, the national field indicates that foreign ownership can reach 100% for this activity. That is the national position in the record, and it should be stated without hedging or embellishment. If a founder is comparing whether the activity is foreign-open at the Indonesia level, the answer from this slim record is yes.

Bali is also clear, but for a different reason. The record does not mark this activity as blocked for Bali PMA registration: `l4_bali_blocked` is **false** and the Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. The stated reason is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not blocked on the record’s own Bali-side test. The honest national-vs-Bali reading is therefore unusually clean: nationally foreign-open up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the supplied moratorium analysis.

editorial.headline: Other Lighting Equipment, Open Nationally and Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27409 covers the making of non-standard lighting equipment, from chandeliers and street-light fittings to solar lighting and electrical lamp components.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27409 is a manufacturing classification for lighting equipment that sits outside the basic, familiar idea of simply making lamps. The record describes ceiling- and wall-mounted lighting equipment, including chandeliers, table lamps, standing floor lamps, decorative chain lights, electric fireplace logs, lanterns using carbide, electricity, gas, petrol, or kerosene, street-lighting equipment other than traffic signs, and solar-powered lighting equipment. It also includes electrical lamp components such as starters, filaments, and reflectors, as well as lamps using or containing radioactive substances.

That breadth matters because this is not a retail classification and not a design-only activity. The centre of gravity is production: making the equipment itself and, where the record says so, making the components that allow electric lamps to function. The scope also draws one important boundary around ballast manufacturing, which is not included here. For founders, the practical reading is that this code belongs to businesses whose registered activity is the manufacture of these lighting products or components, not merely trading, installing, or advising on them.

On scale, the record is unusually clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not confined to a narrow enterprise size in the slim record: it can describe a small producer of decorative fittings, a medium manufacturer of street-light equipment, or a larger industrial lighting operation, provided the activity remains within the manufacturing scope described above. The foreign-investment position is also clean at national level. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali picture follows the same direction, with one precise caveat from the record rather than a hidden local percentage. Bali is not marked as blocked for this activity. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule itself blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this record says KBLI 27409 is not blocked by that rule. So the honest conclusion is straightforward: nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to 100%, and in Bali the record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial-scale manufacturing of common household electrical appliances—from major white goods like refrigerators, washing machines, and dishwashers to smaller kitchen gadgets (blenders, juicers, can openers) and personal care devices (electric toothbrushes, shavers). It's about setting up a production facility, not just trading or retailing these items.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this sector is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it's not blocked by the local moratorium, so a PMA can be registered here. However, due to its medium-high risk classification, expect a stricter licensing process that requires verifying the specific production address and likely additional operational permits.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Peralatan Listrik Rumah Tangga (27510)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign manufacturer looking to set up a home-appliance factory in Bali, rather than just an import-export or retail operation.

editorial.headline: Household electrical appliances, treated as real manufacturing
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27510 covers the making of domestic electrical appliances, nationally open to PMA and not blocked for Bali on this record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27510 is a manufacturing code for household electrical appliances: the factory work behind refrigerators, dishwashers, washing and drying machines, vacuum cleaners, floor polishers, electric bins, and the smaller powered tools that sit around a domestic kitchen or bathroom. The record also brings in food-preparation appliances such as grinders, blenders, can openers and juicers, together with electric toothbrushes, electric shavers, other electric body-care devices, electric knife sharpeners, and ventilation hoods. The centre of gravity is clear: these are electrical products made for household use, not a general code for every appliance-like machine or every installation job connected to them.

That distinction matters because this is not framed as retail, repair, installation, or commercial plant work. The activity is the making of the appliance itself. A business registering here should be able to describe a production activity around domestic electrical goods: assembling, manufacturing, or otherwise producing the kinds of household equipment named in the scope. The record explicitly leaves out commercial refrigeration and freezer equipment, air conditioners, permanent space heaters, commercial ventilation equipment, commercial cooking equipment, commercial laundry and dry-cleaning equipment, commercial vacuum cleaners, household or non-household sewing machines, and central vacuum-system installation. Those exclusions keep the code tightly focused on domestic electrical-appliance industry rather than broader machinery, building services, or commercial equipment.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the registration logic is not confined to one size of operator. A small domestic-appliance producer and a larger industrial manufacturer can both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the activity itself remains inside the household-electrical-appliance scope. That breadth should not be read as a licence condition, a capital threshold, or a production-volume rule; the slim record gives no such figures. It simply says the activity is open across those four named business scales.

The national-vs-Bali picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, which means the record treats this activity as foreign-open at the national level up to full foreign ownership. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali status is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule still matters as background because the record says Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this activity is not marked blocked here. The honest reading is therefore direct: for this code, the record shows national PMA openness and no Bali PMA block under the stated moratorium logic.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing of household electrothermal appliances — from electric ovens, microwaves, and water heaters to hair dryers, irons, toasters, coffee makers, and electric cookers. It includes any appliance that uses electric heating for domestic purposes.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it falls under a medium-high risk classification, so it is not blocked by the general moratorium, but you will need to verify eligibility per specific commercial address — local district requirements may apply.

editorial.headline: Household Heat Appliances With a Clear Bali PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27520 covers the manufacture of household electrothermal appliances, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27520 is the industrial home of household electrothermal equipment: appliances that turn electricity into domestic heat, cooking, drying, ironing, brewing, roasting, grilling, warming, or extraction. The record’s scope is concrete rather than abstract. It includes electric water-heating devices for cooking, electric blankets, hair-care appliances such as dryers, combs, brushes, and curlers, electric irons, room heaters, electric ovens, microwave ovens, cookers, hot plates, toasters, coffee and tea makers, fry pans, roasters, electric grills, kitchen hoods, and electric heating-resistor equipment. In plain English, this is not general electronics and not every appliance factory. It is the manufacturing category for household heat-based electrical products.

The boundary is equally important. The slim record excludes commercial refrigerators and freezers, air conditioners, attic fans, permanent room heaters, commercial ventilation fans or exhaust fans, commercial cooking equipment, commercial laundry and dry-cleaning equipment, commercial vacuum cleaners, and similar equipment for business or commercial use. That exclusion keeps the code focused on household electrothermal manufacturing, not the broader universe of commercial machinery or institutional equipment. For a founder, the useful test is whether the intended product is a domestic electrothermal appliance of the kind named in the scope, rather than a commercial-grade system or facility-oriented machine.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity is not framed only as a large industrial play in the slim record; it can sit across the full stated scale range. A small maker of household heating appliances and a larger manufacturer of electric ovens, hoods, or heating-resistor products are still dealing with the same activity description, provided the product remains inside the household electrothermal scope. The editorial point is not that every factory is simple to set up, but that the KBLI record itself does not narrow the registration scale to one class of operator.

The national-versus-Bali picture is clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced in the record to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali then adds the test that often changes the answer for foreign founders: the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the record does not mark the code as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest conclusion is therefore direct: this activity is foreign-open nationally and, on the slim record provided, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Peralatan Rumah Tangga Bukan Listrik
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup
- pembuatan peralatan masak dan pemanas rumah tangga yang tidak menggunakan listrik, seperti kompor masak, panggangan, pemanas air, penghangat makanan, dan penghangat piring;
- pembuatan pemanas ruangan yang tidak menggunakan listrik, seperti tungku atau perapian.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- pembuatan kulkas dan freezer komersial, pendingin ruangan, kipas angin loteng, pemanan ruangan permanen, kipas angin ventilasi komersial/exhaust fan, peralatan memasak komersial, peralatan penatu/laundry dan cuci kering komersial, penyedot debu komersial, dan sejenisnya untuk kepentingan niaga/komersial, lihat golongan pokok 28.

editorial.headline: Non-Electric Household Appliances With a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27530 covers the making of non-electric domestic cooking, heating, and warming equipment, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27530 is a manufacturing code for household equipment that works without electricity. The record places it around domestic cooking and heating appliances: cooking stoves, grills, water heaters, food warmers, plate warmers, and non-electric room heaters such as stoves or fireplaces. Its centre of gravity is practical household hardware, not commercial machinery or electrical appliances.

That boundary matters. The activity is about making products for household use where heat is generated or managed without an electrical system. It includes the familiar objects that sit between domestic utility and light industrial fabrication: a stove body, a grill unit, a warmer, a water-heating appliance, or a fireplace-style room heater. The record also draws a clear exclusion line around commercial equipment such as commercial refrigeration, air conditioning, attic fans, permanent room-heating systems, commercial ventilation or exhaust fans, commercial cooking appliances, laundry and dry-cleaning equipment, and commercial vacuum cleaners. In plain English, this code is not a catch-all for every appliance workshop; it is for non-electric household appliances within the described domestic scope.

The registration picture is broad on scale. The slim record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can describe anything from a small producer to a larger manufacturing setup, provided the business is still inside the stated activity. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. That means the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The legal source named in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the practical reading is simple: for a foreign-owned company, this code is nationally open.

The Bali side is also unusually clear. The record does contain the Bali moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But for this specific record, l4_bali_blocked is false. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is not a contradiction here. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium. The remaining discipline is editorial as much as legal: stay inside the household, non-electric manufacturing scope, and do not stretch the code into commercial appliance production that the record expressly excludes.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, the activity is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This business class comprises the manufacture of electrical equipment other than electric motors, generators, transformers, batteries and accumulators, wiring and cabling gear, lighting equipment, and household appliances. It covers the production of items such as battery chargers (including solid-state), electric door openers and closers, electric bells, extension cords made from purchased insulated wire, ultrasonic cleaning machines (except laboratory and dental), tanning beds, fuel cells (excluding motor vehicles), regulated and unregulated power supplies, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), surge suppressors (except for voltage-level distribution), equipment cords and insulated cable sets with connectors, carbon and graphite electrodes and contacts, particle accelerators, capacitors, resistors, electrical condensers, similar components, and electromagnets, including dynamos.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership. In Bali, however, it is currently blocked for a PT PMA under the 13 May 2026 moratorium, which suspends new foreign-owned registrations for business lines classified as low / medium-low risk at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale. A foreign-owned setup is viable outside Bali (e.g. Jakarta); inside Bali this code is on hold until the moratorium lifts.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.

editorial.headline: Other Electrical Equipment, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27900 covers a wide band of electrical equipment manufacturing, nationally open to PMA, but the Bali record blocks PMA registration under the moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27900 is the manufacturing home for electrical equipment that sits outside the better-known families of motors, generators, transformers, batteries, wiring, lighting equipment, and household appliances. In practical English, it is a broad industrial category for making specialised electrical devices and components: battery chargers, electric door openers and closers, bells, extension cables made from purchased insulated wire, ultrasonic cleaning machines outside laboratory and dental use, tanning beds, fuel cells outside motor vehicles, regulated and unregulated power supplies, UPS units, surge suppressors outside distribution-voltage level, appliance cords, electrical extension cords, carbon and graphite electrodes and contacts, particle accelerators, capacitors, resistors, condensers, electromagnets, sirens, scoreboards, electric advertising signs, traffic and pedestrian signalling equipment, and related electrical products named in the record.

That breadth matters because this is not a retail or service label. It is an industrial manufacturing classification for businesses that actually make the equipment or electrical product identified in the scope. The record opens the activity across all listed enterprise scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A founder reading the code should therefore treat scale as a registration dimension, not as a clue that the activity changes character. Whether the operation is small or large, the core activity remains the production of other electrical equipment within the scope stated above.

The national PMA picture is clean. According to the record, the activity is TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100 sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. There is no separate percentage to calculate, soften, or reinterpret. If the question is only whether the national classification is foreign-open, the answer from the record is yes.

Bali is the decisive constraint. The same record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the reason: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is equally direct: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the honest reading is national openness without Bali registrability for PMA today. A foreign investor can see a 100% national ceiling in the record, but that does not make this activity registerable as PMA in Bali under the Bali-side block recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Industrial Power Machinery With a Bali Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28111 covers the making of steam, turbine, wind, water, and gas or air power machinery, nationally open to foreign ownership but scope-sensitive in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28111 is a manufacturing activity for power-driving machinery that is not an internal-combustion engine. In plain English, the record places here the making of steam engines, turbines and their parts, steam turbines and similar turbines, hydraulic turbines, water wheels and their regulators, wind turbines, gas or air turbines, boiler-turbine sets, generator-turbine sets, and windmills. It also includes milling machinery, while the record expressly excludes turbojets or turboprops for aircraft. The activity is industrial and mechanical in character: it is about making the machines and assemblies that convert steam, water, wind, gas, or air into motive power.

The registration profile is broad. The record says this activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not framed only as a large-plant industrial category; the slim record keeps the door open across the scale ladder. A founder reading the code should therefore begin with the actual declared manufacturing scope, not with an assumption that turbine-related work automatically belongs only to a single scale or a single industrial format. The scope text is the anchor: the activity must stay inside the manufacturing of the machinery and parts described there.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the record gives a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-share cap in the slim record, so none should be added. The national reading is therefore that this KBLI can support a wholly foreign-owned PMA setup, provided the declared activity remains the activity described by the code. That is the simple national picture: open status, full foreign-ownership ceiling, and no invented capital, licensing, tax, or timing condition attached to the record.

Bali is more careful. The record does not mark this activity as outright blocked in Bali: `l4_bali_blocked` is false. But the Bali status is `Blocked (scope-dependent)`, and the reason says: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope — verify live OSS per exact activity.” The moratorium rule in the record is blunt: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest Bali reading is not a separate percentage cap, and not a blanket no. It is scope-dependent: national PMA openness exists, but Bali registration turns on the exact activity and the live OSS risk classification for that activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this is a fully foreign-open machinery manufacturing code, but in Bali the decisive question is the exact declared scope.
