editorial.headline: Industrial Combustion Engines, With a Bali Caveat
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28112 covers the manufacture of internal-combustion prime movers, nationally open to PMA but conditional in Bali by declared OSS scope.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28112 is the industrial engine code for makers of internal-combustion prime movers. In plain English, it covers the manufacture of engines that create motive power through combustion inside the engine itself: spark-ignition engines, compression-ignition engines such as diesel units, petrol engines, and engines using gas or alcohol fuels. The record also places industrial applications and piston internal-combustion engines inside the scope, including marine and railway engines, while keeping vehicle and aircraft engine manufacturing outside this activity. It also includes factory repair of ship and boat engines.

The scale profile is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not framed as a code reserved only for large manufacturers. That said, the activity itself is industrial in character: the useful reading is not merely “engine trade”, but production of engine machinery and related factory repair. A founder choosing this code should be able to point from the declared activity to that manufacturing scope, not to a neighboring automotive or aircraft-engine line that the record expressly excludes.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. Recorded as TERBUKA for PMA, the activity carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, with Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as its sources. On the national reading alone, this is therefore a foreign-open activity with no lower percentage cap stated in the slim record. Nothing in the record adds a separate national condition, minimum capital number, tax rule, or special licence threshold, so none should be inferred from the code description alone.

Bali is more careful. The record does not mark the code as outright blocked for Bali, but it does mark the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent). The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity.” That sits beside the moratorium rule that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest conclusion is that KBLI 28112 is nationally open, but in Bali it cannot be treated as automatically clean for every declared scope. The exact OSS activity and risk classification carry the decision.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28112 is nationally open to foreign ownership, but in Bali the declared OSS scope determines whether the registration path is actually usable.

editorial.headline: The Industrial Core of Engine and Turbine Components
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28113 covers the making of non-automotive engine and turbine parts, nationally open to PMA and not blocked for Bali registration under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28113 is a manufacturing code for the parts that sit inside, around, and immediately alongside prime-mover machinery: the components and spare parts of engines and turbines. In practical terms, the record points to industrial items such as engine blocks, pistons, piston rings, carburetors, cylinder heads, and comparable parts for internal-combustion and diesel engines, together with inlet valves and gas-release valves. The scope is deliberately mechanical and component-led. It is not a general trading activity, and it is not framed as vehicle manufacturing; the record expressly excludes motor-vehicle use.

That makes this a code for businesses whose real activity is fabrication, machining, assembly, or production of engine and turbine components rather than merely buying and reselling them. The scale profile is unusually broad: the record marks it open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small workshop producing defined spare parts and a larger industrial plant making higher-volume components can both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the activity remains inside the stated manufacturing scope. The editorial point is simple: the code is about making the working parts of machines, not branding the finished machine or operating the machine as a service.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with `pma_max_asing` at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is 100%. There is no lesser percentage, special threshold, capital number, licence timeline, or additional national condition in the slim record, so none should be read into it. The national answer is therefore clean: this activity is open to PMA at the ceiling stated in the record.

The Bali layer is also clean, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. This record, however, does not mark the activity as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, and the reason is: `OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium`. So the honest national-versus-Bali reading is not a contradiction. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA; in Bali, the supplied record does not block PMA registration under the moratorium because the relevant large-scale risk position is higher than the blocked Low and Medium-Low categories.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the activity is open to PMA, and the Bali record does not block it under the moratorium because its large-scale risk position is higher than the barred categories.

editorial.headline: Fluid Power Equipment Is Nationally Open, but Bali Blocks PMA
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28120 covers hydraulic and pneumatic power equipment manufacturing, open nationally to foreign ownership yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28120 is the manufacturing class for the machinery that turns liquid and gas pressure into controlled industrial motion. The record defines it around hydraulic and pneumatic machines and components: pumps, cylinders, valves, hydraulic and pneumatic motors, air-processing equipment used in pneumatic systems, fluid and gas power systems, hydraulic transmission equipment, electric linear actuators, and gas spring cylinders. In practical terms, this is not a general machinery catch-all. It is the industrial layer where pressure, flow, and actuation become equipment.

That precision matters because the activity sits inside a broad manufacturing economy, but its scope is quite specific. A company registering here is positioning itself as a maker of fluid-power equipment or its defined components, not merely as a trader, installer, repairer, or producer of adjacent rubber, plastic, compressor, pump, or mechanical transmission products that the record places outside the class. The eligible business scales are unusually wide: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open to the activity. That means the classification is not reserved only for large industrial producers; the record allows it across the full scale spectrum.

The national foreign-investment picture is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership recorded is 100%. For an investor reading the national rule alone, that is the clean signal: this activity is open to foreign capital, with the cited source being Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial national ceiling in the record, no special minimum-capital detail, and no extra licensing condition stated here beyond the classification and ownership fields supplied.

Bali changes the answer completely. The record marks this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali, with the reason stated as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026. The moratorium rule is broader still: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide, permanent. So the honest reading is national openness, local closure. KBLI 28120 may be 100% foreign-open nationally, but a foreign-owned company cannot register it in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Industrial Pumps, Compressors, Taps and Valves With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of core fluid and gas-handling equipment, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28130 is a manufacturing activity for the machinery that moves, compresses, controls, and releases air, gas, water, oil, fuel, and other liquids. In practical terms, it covers the making of air and gas compressors, compressors for refrigeration and air-conditioning systems, motor-vehicle compressors, laboratory pumps, water pumps, air pumps, vacuum pumps, and pumps for liquids whether or not they are fitted with measuring equipment. It also reaches pumps designed for internal-combustion engines, including fuel, oil, and water pumps for motor vehicles.

The scope is not limited to pumps and compressors alone. The record also places industrial valves and taps inside this activity: regulating valves, inlet pipe taps, sanitary taps and valves, heating taps and valves, and hand pumps. That gives the code a broad but still precise industrial character. It is about manufacturing functional components used in mechanical systems, fluid systems, vehicle systems, sanitation systems, and heating systems. The common thread is not retail, installation, repair, or trading; it is the production of the equipment itself.

On business scale, the record is unusually inclusive. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the activity can describe anything from a small specialist workshop making hand pumps or selected valve parts to a larger industrial manufacturer producing compressors, vehicle pumps, or fluid-control assemblies. That scale range matters because the code is not reserved only for heavy factories. The same activity definition can accommodate different production sizes, provided the registered business is genuinely manufacturing the covered goods.

The national foreign-investment position is also clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain English, the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. The Bali picture is similarly direct, but for a different reason: the record does not mark this activity as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium described in the record blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not caught by that block on the facts supplied here. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest reading is therefore simple: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership allowed, and not currently blocked for PMA registration in Bali according to this record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is simple: nationally open, 100% foreign ownership allowed, and not currently blocked for PMA registration in Bali according to this record.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacture of mechanical power-transmission parts: bearings (ball and roller), gears, gearboxes, clutches, pulleys, link chains, transmission chains, and related components like camshafts, crankshafts, bearing housings, and plain shaft bearings.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). However, in Bali it is currently blocked for new PMA companies because it falls under the low/medium-low risk classification, which is subject to a government moratorium on foreign registration since 13 May 2026. A local-penanam modal dalam negeri (PMDN) company may still be possible, but a foreign-owned entity cannot be licensed for this KBLI in Bali right now.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bearing, Roda Gigi, dan Elemen Penggerak Mesin (28140)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur in precision mechanical component manufacturing who wants to produce bearings, gears, or transmission elements—but must currently look outside Bali or wait until the moratorium lifts if set on a Bali location.

editorial.headline: Precision Machinery, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28140 covers the industrial making of bearings, gears, clutches and mechanical transmission components, with a clear national opening and a hard Bali stop for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28140 is a manufacturing code for the quiet hardware inside moving machines: ball and roller bearings, bearing rings and parts, gears, gearboxes, speed changers, clutches and clutch shafts, pulleys, linked chain elements, and power-transmission chains. It also reaches into the component layer of mechanical transmission equipment, including cam shafts, crank shafts, cranks, bearing frames, simple shaft bearings, bearing blocks, gear assemblies, clutches, pulleys and related mechanical drive parts. In plain English, this is not a general metalworking label. It is a code for businesses that make the parts that let industrial motion turn, carry, couple, reduce, transmit and repeat reliably.

That breadth matters because the record opens the activity across every stated business scale: micro, small, medium and large. A founder using this code is not merely describing trading or repair activity; the scope is anchored in production. The activity can fit a workshop making specific transmission parts, a more specialised component producer, or a larger factory manufacturing the bearing, gear and drive elements named in the scope. The common thread is mechanical transmission: parts that sit between power and movement, whether in the form of bearings, gears, shafts, chains, pulleys or coupling systems.

Nationally, the investment picture is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That means the national classification does not, in this slim record, impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The national position is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup outside the Bali constraint, the code reads as nationally open, with the full stated scale range available and no lower foreign-ownership percentage appearing in the record.

Bali is the decisive exception. The record marks this activity as blocked in Bali for PMA registration, with the status Blocked (risk class). The reason given is not a separate Bali percentage, quota or partnership rule; it is a risk-class moratorium: OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. So the honest reading is simple: KBLI 28140 may be nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the record supplied.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28140 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but the Bali record turns that opening into a hard local stop for PMA registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of non-electric industrial ovens, fireplaces, and combustion furnaces used to heat, bake, or melt ores, metals, and similar materials. It also includes central heating boilers, industrial and utility boilers, scrubbers, solar water heaters, and mechanical equipment like mechanical stokers, grates, and ash discharge systems.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, the KBLI is 100% open to foreign investment (TERBUKA 100%). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs planning to manufacture industrial-scale, non-electric heating equipment or boilers — and Bali is not off the table: this KBLI's large-scale risk class sits above the moratorium's Low/Medium-Low band, so a PMA can still register it here.

editorial.headline: Non-Electric Industrial Furnaces With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28151 covers the manufacture of non-electric furnaces, boilers, scrubbers, and related heat-processing equipment, open nationally and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28151 is about heavy heat equipment made without electric current as the operating basis: furnaces and similar apparatus used to heat, roast, or melt iron ore, metals, and related materials. The record also brings into the same activity the manufacture of burners, central-heating boilers, industrial processing boilers, utility boilers, scrubbers, and solar water heaters. Its scope is not decorative or household-oriented; it is the manufacturing side of thermal equipment used where heat, combustion, steam, ash handling, or industrial processing must be engineered into machinery.

The activity also reaches into mechanical components that make combustion systems work: coal-burning chambers for steam locomotives, mechanical stokers, roasters, mechanical grates, and mechanical ash discharges. Read in plain English, this code is for producers of non-electric furnace and boiler systems and their close mechanical ecosystem. It is the kind of registration a manufacturer would look at when the business is not merely trading equipment, installing it, or servicing it, but making the apparatus itself.

On scale, the record is broad. It marks the activity open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the code is not reserved in the record for only one class of operator: the slim record presents it as available across the full scale range. A small producer and a larger industrial manufacturer are not described as separate worlds here; the difference is scale, not the nature of the KBLI activity itself. The editorial discipline is to keep that distinction clean: this code describes manufacturing scope and open scales, not extra licensing thresholds or capital rules that the record does not state.

The national investment picture is equally direct. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with the foreign-ownership ceiling recorded at 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a separate foreign-share percentage in this record. Instead, Bali is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali block flag is false. The reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium." The moratorium rule still matters as background because Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently. But this record does not put KBLI 28151 inside that blocked result. The honest reading is therefore clean: nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 28151 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, this record does not block PMA registration under the stated moratorium logic.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Oven, Perapian dan Tungku Pembakar Sejenis yang Menggunakan Arus Listrik
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan tungku, oven, dan alat pemanas lainnya yang penggunaannya memerlukan arus listrik, misalnya peralatan induksi listrik untuk industri dan laboratorium, termasuk insinerator, tungku pembakar, pendingin dan peralatan ventilasi rumah tangga, dan tungku listrik untuk rumah tangga.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup:
- pembuatan alat pengatur panas untuk makanan, minuman dan tembakau, termasuk pula oven nonelektrik untuk pembuat roti, lihat kelompok 28250;
- pembuatan alat pengatur panas untuk bubur kertas/pulp, kertas, dan bahan industri lainnya, lihat kelompok 28292 dan 28299.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Oven, Perapian dan Tungku Pembakar Sejenis yang Menggunakan Arus Listrik (28152)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who manufactures electric heating appliances, like industrial furnaces or electric household ovens, and plans to set up in Indonesia — but must wait or choose another region if targeting Bali.

editorial.headline: Electric Furnaces and Ovens as a Serious Manufacturing Category
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28152 covers electric industrial and household heat equipment, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28152 is a manufacturing category for equipment that produces, manages, or channels heat through electric current. The record places it around the making of furnaces, ovens, and related heating apparatus whose use depends on electricity. In practical English, this is not a general kitchenware label or a catch-all for every kind of industrial heater. It is the production lane for electric heat equipment such as industrial and laboratory induction equipment, incinerators, combustion furnaces, household cooling and ventilation equipment, and electric furnaces for household use.

That breadth matters because the code sits across two different worlds: heavy, technical equipment for industrial or laboratory settings, and selected household equipment where electric heat or air movement is central to the product. A founder using this code should be able to describe a manufacturing activity, not merely trading, installing, or servicing finished machines. The scope also draws a boundary around what it does not cover, excluding certain food, beverage, tobacco, pulp, paper, and other industrial heat-control equipment. The editorial point is simple: the activity is defined by making electric-current-based heating or related apparatus, with the listed examples anchoring the interpretation.

On scale, the record is unusually open. Micro, small, medium, and large enterprises are all shown as open to this activity. That means the category is not framed only for large plant manufacturers; it can also hold smaller production setups, provided the business activity genuinely fits the manufacturing scope. The scale list should not be over-read as a licence, permit, or operational clearance. It is a registration-scale signal in the record, and it says that every named scale is open.

The national foreign-investment picture is also clean. The PMA status is marked **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. The Bali picture does not reverse that conclusion. The record marks Bali as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, says `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and gives the reason as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record is still important context: Bali blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. But for this activity, the record’s own Bali-side conclusion is that it is not blocked by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For this activity, the honest reading is that full foreign ownership is nationally open and Bali does not block PMA registration under the recorded moratorium check.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of lifting and moving equipment—everything from hand-operated hoists, pulleys, and jacks to industrial cranes, mobile lifting frames, work trucks, and specialized robotic manipulators used for loading, unloading, and transporting materials in factories or construction.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, a 100% foreign-owned PMA is allowed for this activity. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Alat Pengangkat dan Pemindah (28160)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who design or manufacture industrial lifting, material-handling, or robotic handling systems and intend to produce or assemble in Indonesia—though they would currently need to incorporate outside Bali.

editorial.headline: Heavy Lifting, Clear Access
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28160 covers the machinery behind industrial movement: lifting, loading, conveying, warehouse handling, elevators, escalators, and their suitable parts.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28160 is a manufacturing classification for the machines that move weight, position goods, and turn industrial space into a working system. The record frames it around lifting, handling, loading, and unloading equipment, whether operated by hand or by powered drive. That includes hoists, winches, anchor turns, jacks, derricks, cranes, mobile lifting frames, straddle carriers, factory work trucks, hand-handling equipment, hand carts, and mechanical manipulators or industrial robots designed specifically to lift, handle, load, or unload.

Its scope also reaches the more automated end of factory and warehouse movement. The record includes unmanned forklifts, robots and pallet loading or unloading equipment, conveyors and other goods-lifting or goods-transport devices, lifts, escalators, moving walkways, and automatic transport and lifting equipment for warehouses. It also includes parts suitable for transport and lifting equipment. The shape of the activity is therefore not general robotics or broad machinery; it is the manufacture of equipment whose purpose is the physical movement of people, goods, pallets, loads, or industrial materials.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the record does not confine it to large factories only. A small workshop making suitable components and a larger industrial manufacturer producing conveyor or lifting systems sit within the same activity logic, provided the work remains inside the described lifting, moving, loading, unloading, or handling scope. That breadth matters because the classification is defined by what is manufactured, not by a single factory size or one narrow product line.

The national foreign-investment position is clear: the record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**. For a PMA reading, that means the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali-side question is whether the provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for this activity. Here, the record marks Bali as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, with `l4_bali_blocked` set to false. The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” In plain terms, the moratorium described in the record blocks low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not blocked on the Bali record supplied here.
editorial.pullQuote: The national foreign-investment position is clear: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%.

data.judul: Industri Mesin Kantor dan Akuntansi Manual
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan macam-macam mesin kantor dan akuntansi secara manual, seperti mesin hitung manual, mesin tik manual, mesin stensil manual, mesin peruncing pensil, sempoa, alat timbang pos (postage meters), mesin pengelola surat (pengisi amplop, penyegel dan mesin pemberi alamat, membuka, mengurutkan, memindai), mesin stenografi, alat penjilid (penjilid plastik atau pita), mesin penghitung koin. penyortir koin, dan pembungkus koin, mesin staples, mesin pemungutan suara, mesin isolasi (tape dispencer) dan mesin pembuat lubang kertas dan sejenisnya, rermasuk pembuatan komponen dan suku cadangnya.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan jasa pemeliharaan dan perbaikan mesin dalam kelompok ini, lihat kelompok 33121.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity involves manufacturing manual office and accounting machines—everything from old-school mechanical typewriters and calculators to mail-sorting systems, coin counters/wrappers, staplers, binding equipment, pencil sharpeners, tape dispensers, and even manual voting machines. It also includes making components for these devices.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, however, foreign companies are currently blocked from registering this activity due to a moratorium that halts PMA licences for low and medium-low risk classes—effective from 13 May 2026. So right now, you cannot set up a foreign-owned company in Bali for this line of business.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.

editorial.headline: Manual Office Machines, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28171 covers the manufacture of manual office and accounting machines, with national PMA openness but a Bali-side registration block for foreign investors.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 28171 is an old-mechanics manufacturing category with a surprisingly precise scope.** It covers the making of manual office and accounting machines: manual calculators, typewriters, stencil machines, pencil sharpeners, abacuses, postage meters, mail-handling machines, stenography machines, binding tools, coin counters and sorters, staplers, voting machines, tape dispensers, paper punch machines, and similar equipment. The record also brings components and spare parts into the same industrial frame, so the activity is not limited to finished machines alone. Its centre of gravity is physical manufacture, not service work around the machines after they exist.

For registration purposes, the scale profile is broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, which means it can describe anything from a small workshop producing simple manual office tools to a larger manufacturing operation making a wider set of office or accounting equipment. That breadth matters because the activity is defined by what is made, not by a single product line. A company does not need to be making every item named in the scope; the scope reads as a family of manual office, accounting, mailing, binding, counting, fastening, and paper-handling machines, together with their parts.

The national PMA picture is clean: the record marks the activity **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100** and the source listed as **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to a 100% ceiling. There is no lower national cap in the slim record, and no extra national threshold, licence, capital figure, or timing rule is stated here. The only responsible reading is therefore narrow but clear: nationally, this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity at the full recorded ceiling.

Bali is the decisive complication. The same record says `l4_bali_blocked` is **true** and gives the reason as: **“OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.”** It also states the moratorium rule directly: **“Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).”** So the honest lede for a foreign-owned setup in Bali is not that the code is merely sensitive or partially open; it is that a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today, even though the national PMA line is open. That is the national-vs-Bali split founders need to see before building plans around the code.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity, but the Bali record blocks PMA registration today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Mesin Kantor dan Akuntansi Elektrik
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan macam-macam mesin kantor dan akuntansi elektrik, seperti mesin hitung elektrik, mesin tik elektrik, mesin stensil elektrik dan sejenisnya, kalkulator, alat timbang pos (postage meters), mesin pengelola surat (pengisi amplop, penyegel dan mesin pemberi alamat, membuka, mengurutkan, memindai), mesin stenografi, mesin fotokopi analog, alat penjilid (contoh penjilid plastik atau pita), mesin penghitung koin, penyortir koin, dan pembungkus koin, peruncing pensil, stapler, mesin pemungutan suara, mesin pembuat lubang kertas. Kelompok ini juga mencakup usaha pembuatan macam-macam mesin kantor dan akuntansi elektronik, seperti mesin hitung elektronik dan cash register.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- pembuatan subassembly dan komponen elektronik mesin komputasi, termasuk pembuatan komponen dan suku cadangnya, lihat kelompok 26199
- jasa pemeliharaan dan perbaikan mesin dalam kelompok ini, lihat kelompok 33121.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of electric office and accounting machines—like calculators, electric typewriters, stencil machines, postage meters, mail-handling machines, coin sorters, staplers, and binding devices. It’s the industrial production of office equipment, not retail or repair.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it's allowed but classified as medium-high risk, so registration isn't blocked by the general moratorium, but approval depends heavily on your specific business address and local zoning—expect extra scrutiny and local permits.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign manufacturer looking to set up an actual production facility for office or voting machines, not a simple trading or service operation.

editorial.headline: Electric Office Machinery With a Clear PMA Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28172 covers the manufacture of electric and electronic office and accounting machines, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the slim record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28172 is a manufacturing classification for the machines that sit behind office administration, accounting counters, mailrooms, copy desks, and document handling. The scope covers electric office and accounting machines, including electric calculators, electric typewriters, stencil machines, calculators, postage meters, mail-handling machines, stenography machines, analogue photocopiers, binding tools, coin-counting and coin-sorting machines, pencil sharpeners, staplers, voting machines, and paper punching machines. It also extends to electronic office and accounting machinery such as electronic calculating machines and cash registers.

The centre of gravity is production, not upkeep. The slim record draws the boundary around making these machines; it excludes the manufacture of electronic subassemblies and computing-machine components, and it excludes maintenance and repair services for the machines in this group. That distinction matters because KBLI 28172 is not a broad technology-services bucket. It is a factory-side code for finished office, accounting, document, coin, and related administrative machines.

The registration picture is unusually broad on scale. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can describe a small producer as well as a larger manufacturing setup. At the national level, PMA status is TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In plain English, the national record treats this as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling stated in the data, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

The Bali reading is also clear, and it should not be made more complicated than the record allows. Bali’s moratorium rule says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But for this activity, the Bali field is not marked blocked. The record’s reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest national-vs-Bali conclusion is that KBLI 28172 is nationally open to PMA and, on this slim record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan macam-macam mesin kantor dan akuntansi elektronik, seperti mesin hitung elektronik, mesin fotokopi digital, dan cash register.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan pembuatan subassembly dan komponen elektronik mesin komputasi, lihat kelompok 26199.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing of electronic office and accounting machines, like electronic calculators, digital photocopiers, and cash registers. It excludes manufacturing subassemblies or electronic components for computing machines, which is grouped elsewhere.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business line is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin Kantor dan Akuntansi Elektronik (28173)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who want to produce electronic office equipment (e.g., digital cash registers or calculators), but need to look outside Bali for registration due to local restrictions.

editorial.headline: Electronic Office Machinery With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28173 covers the manufacture of electronic office and accounting machines, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28173 is a manufacturing classification for electronic office and accounting machinery. The record defines it around the making of products such as electronic calculating machines, digital photocopiers, and cash registers. Its centre of gravity is not software, retail distribution, or generic electronics trading; it is the production of finished office and accounting machines with electronic functions. The scope also draws a boundary around what it is not: the manufacture of electronic subassemblies and components for computing machinery sits outside this activity.

The registration picture is broad. The slim record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so it can describe anything from a small manufacturing setup to a larger industrial operation, provided the actual activity remains inside the recorded scope. That breadth matters because the classification is not reserved only for large factories. What anchors it is the kind of manufacturing being performed: electronic office and accounting machines, including the examples named in the record.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position remains straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing recorded at 100, under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower ceiling, partner requirement, paid-up capital figure, licence timeline, or additional quantitative condition in the slim record, so none should be read into it.

The Bali picture is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. This activity is not marked as blocked in Bali. For Bali, it carries the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, because the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: based on this record, KBLI 28173 is nationally foreign-open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

editorial.headline: Office Equipment Manufacturing, Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28179 covers the manufacture of office equipment such as toner cartridges, writing boards, and dictation machines, and is nationally open to PMA ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28179 is a manufacturing classification for office equipment. The record describes it as covering the production of several kinds of office equipment, including toner cartridges, white boards and marker boards with writing and drawing surfaces, and dictation machines. In plain English, this is not a retail or office-services activity. It is the industrial making of physical office-use products: the consumables, presentation surfaces, and equipment that support daily administrative work. The scope is modest but concrete, and that matters because the code is defined by manufacture, not by distribution, installation, repair, or general office supply trading.

The activity is open across the full scale ladder recorded for the code: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not framed only for a large factory profile, even though industrial manufacturing can naturally reach that scale. A founder reading this code should first ask whether the planned business is truly making the products described in the scope. If the commercial plan is centred on producing toner cartridges, writing boards, marker boards, or dictation machines, the record supports this code as the relevant activity. If the business is doing something outside that manufacturing scope, the record gives no permission to stretch this code to cover it.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The code is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put plainly, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to 100% foreign ownership. There is no lower foreign-equity ceiling in the slim record, and there is no stated special threshold, minimum capital figure, licence condition, or timeline to add. For editorial purposes, the important national point is therefore simple: this code is foreign-open nationally, and the recorded ownership ceiling reaches the full 100%.

The Bali picture does not reverse that conclusion. For Bali, the entry sets l4_bali_blocked to false and assigns the status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. Its reason is specific: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The Bali moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this code is not recorded as blocked by that moratorium. So the honest national-versus-Bali reading is clean: KBLI 28179 is nationally open to PMA ownership at 100%, and the slim Bali record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is clean: KBLI 28179 is nationally open to PMA ownership at 100%, and the Bali record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Powered Hand-Tool Manufacturing: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers factories making powered hand tools, open nationally across all scales, but the record blocks PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium.
editorial.body:
Powered hand-tool manufacturing is a compact industrial category with a practical centre of gravity: the making of hand-held tools driven by power. The record describes tools moved by electric motors, non-electric motors, air pressure, or water pressure. Its examples are workshop and construction staples: circular and reciprocating saws, chainsaws, drills and hammer drills, hand-operated sand spreaders, pneumatic nailers, buffers, routers, grinders, staplers, nail guns, planers, shears and pliers, adjustable wrenches, and powder-actuated fastening tools.

In plain English, this is not general machinery manufacturing and it is not retail trading in tools. It is the factory-side activity of producing powered tools that workers can carry, guide, hold, or operate by hand. The record is broad enough to include electric, pneumatic, hydraulic, and other powered formats, but it remains anchored in the same industrial idea: making practical, hand-operated equipment for cutting, drilling, fastening, grinding, shaping, sanding, gripping, or driving fixings. A founder using this code would normally be describing a production business, not a showroom, service desk, or import-only operation.

On the national investment reading, the code is clearly foreign-open. The PMA status is marked **TERBUKA**, the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%**, and the cited basis is **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. The record also opens the activity to the full range of business scales: **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar**. That matters because the code is not written only for a large industrial plant; the slim record recognises it across all listed scales. Nationally, therefore, the basic signal is straightforward: a foreign-owned company can sit inside this activity, and the ownership ceiling shown in the record is complete foreign ownership.

Bali is the decisive caveat, and it changes the practical answer for PMA founders on the island. The Bali-side status is **Blocked (risk class)**, with `l4_bali_blocked` marked true. The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” Spelled out, the record says this activity may be open nationally, but it is blocked for PMA registration in Bali because the Bali province rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. For a foreign founder, the honest reading is not “open with a Bali nuance”; it is open nationally, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali today under the moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign founder, the honest reading is not “open with a Bali nuance”; it is open nationally, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali today under the moratorium recorded here.

editorial.headline: The Machinery Behind Bottles, Cans, Boxes and Labels
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28191 covers packaging, bottling and canning machinery that is nationally open to PMA, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28191 is not about the packaged goods themselves. It is the industrial activity behind the machines that prepare those goods for market: equipment for wrapping, bottling and canning, including machines that fill, close, seal, wrap and label bottles, cans and boxes. The record also brings in machinery for drying and cleaning beverage bottles, as well as machines that mix air into drinks and similar equipment. In plain English, this is a manufacturing code for the machinery that sits on or around a packaging line, turning containers and products into sealed, labelled, sale-ready units.

That makes the code broad in scale but specific in function. The slim record marks it as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar operators, so it is not reserved for one size of business. A small manufacturer of specialised packaging equipment and a larger industrial machinery producer both sit within the same activity frame, provided the business is making the machines described in the scope: packaging, bottling, canning, filling, closing, sealing, wrapping, labelling, bottle-cleaning, bottle-drying, carbonation-related machinery and similar equipment. The common thread is the machine, not the drink, can, box or bottle being processed.

Nationally, the PMA picture is simple. The record classifies the activity as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to a full 100% foreign shareholding. There is no lower national cap in the slim record, and there is no additional national condition stated here that should be inferred. On the national layer alone, KBLI 28191 reads as a straightforward foreign-open manufacturing activity.

Bali is the decisive exception. The same record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true and gives the Bali status as Blocked (risk class). Its reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and that this is blocked by the Bali moratorium dated May 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is blunt: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source listed as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest reading is this: KBLI 28191 may be nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreign investor cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side rule recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28191 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but the Bali record blocks PMA registration for this activity today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

You cannot register a foreign-owned company in Bali for this KBLI right now, even though it would be eligible elsewhere in Indonesia.

editorial.headline: Weighing-Machine Manufacturing Is Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28192 covers non-laboratory weighing machines and their components, with full national PMA openness but a clear Bali block for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
For KBLI 28192, the activity is the manufacture of weighing machines outside the laboratory setting. The record places the work in practical, commercial, and domestic territory: scales for shops, offices, and households; baby scales and body scales; weighing devices integrated with calculators; station scales; continuous weighing scales; weighbridges; and other weighing equipment. The scope also includes both mobile and fixed forms, along with the manufacture of components and accessories. In plain English, this is the industrial production of everyday and operational weighing systems, not laboratory measurement equipment.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so the classification is not reserved only for large factories. A small producer of scale components and a larger manufacturer of weighbridge systems both sit inside the same recorded activity, provided the work remains within the stated scope: non-laboratory weighing machinery and its supporting parts. That breadth matters because the code is about the activity itself, not one single product size, customer type, or production footprint.

Nationally, the PMA reading is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100 under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is full foreign ownership. There is no lower national cap in this slim record, and no additional threshold, licence, tax, timeline, or capital rule is stated here. The national note is therefore simple: for foreign ownership, the record presents KBLI 28192 as open up to 100%.

Bali is the hard stop. The same record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the status Blocked (risk class). Its stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule supplied in the record is also explicit: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)", with the source shown as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest reading is this: nationally, KBLI 28192 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today because the Bali-side block applies.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 28192 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today because the Bali-side block applies.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacture of commercial cooling and freezing equipment—including cold storage, display cases, vending dispensers, vehicle and building air conditioning, industrial/lab fans and exhaust hoods, gas liquefaction machines, and specialized coolers for biological products like vaccines and blood—as well as assembly of their main components.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin Pendingin (28193)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers of commercial refrigeration, HVAC, or specialized cooling systems (e.g., for medical or retail use) who want to build a production facility in Indonesia, though a new PMA cannot be registered in Bali for now.

editorial.headline: Commercial Cooling Machinery Is Nationally Open and Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28193 covers the industrial machinery behind commercial cold storage, air conditioning, laboratory ventilation, gas liquefaction, and biological-product cooling.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28193 is not a shopfront activity; it is the industrial manufacture of cooling and refrigeration machinery. The record describes a wide manufacturing field: commercial refrigeration and freezing machines, cold-storage equipment, and the assembly of their main components. It also reaches the making of display cases, dispense cases, air-conditioning machinery including for motor vehicles, industrial and laboratory fans and exhaust hoods, related components and accessories, machinery for liquefying air or gas, and cooling machines used for biological products such as vaccines and blood.

That scope matters because the activity is broader than ordinary appliance handling. It sits in the productive layer behind commercial cold chains, conditioned environments, industrial ventilation, and specialist biological cooling. A company registering this activity is presenting itself as a manufacturer or assembler of the machinery and principal equipment in that field, not merely as a distributor, installer, or service counter unless those activities are separately supported by the record. On the scale side, the slim record is unusually clean: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, the classification is not limited to one company size category in the data provided here.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also direct. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, which means the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100% at the national level. There is no lower national cap in the record, and no special percentage condition is supplied. The national source field is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, so the article should stay with that: open nationally, with a 100% ceiling, and no invented side condition.

The Bali reading is more nuanced, but still favourable on the facts given. Bali's moratorium rule in the record says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. This code, however, is not marked as blocked in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is false and the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". So the honest conclusion is that KBLI 28193 is nationally foreign-open and, on this slim record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan mesin umum lainnya, seperti fire sprinklers, mesin penyaring dan pembersih cairan dan gas, unit penyulingan cairan, peralatan untuk proyeksi, penyebaran atau penyemprotan cairan atau bubuk, seperti pistol semprot, pemadam api, mesin penyemprot pasir, mesin pembersih dengan uap air dan lain-lain, mesin penyulingan atau rektifikasi untuk kilang minyak, industri kimia, industri minuman, mesin penukar panas (heat exchanger) dan lain-lain, generator gas, mesin penggulung lainnya dan silindernya (kecuali untuk logam dan kaca) termasuk calendering machine (mesin pres), mesin sentrifugal (kecuali mesin pemisah krim dan pengering pakaian), mesin paking dan tali untuk isolasi dan sejenisnya yang terbuat dari kombinasi bahan atau lapisan bahan yang sama, mesin penjual barang otomatis, kipas ventilasi loteng (kipas gable/dinding, ventilasi atap dan lain-lain), meteran pita dan perkakas tangan sejenis, alat presisi masinis (bukan optik) dan peralatan patri dan solder bukan listrik, termasuk pembuatan komponen dan peralatannya.
