intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers manufacturing of general-purpose machinery not elsewhere classified, such as fire sprinklers, liquid/gas filtering and cleaning machines, distillation units, spraying or projecting equipment (spray guns, fire extinguishers, sandblasters, steam cleaners), heat exchangers, gas generators, and calenders or rolling machines (except for metal and glass).
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign investment (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin untuk Keperluan Umum Lainnya YTDL (28199)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers of industrial machinery components or specialized processing equipment who intend to sell to factories or set up assembly lines — and Bali is not off the table: this KBLI's large-scale risk class sits above the moratorium's Low/Medium-Low band, so a PMA can still register it here.

editorial.headline: The Broad Machinery Workshop Behind Indonesia’s Industrial Back Room
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28199 covers a wide field of general-purpose machinery, nationally open to full foreign ownership but requiring careful Bali scope checking.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28199 is the broad workshop category for general-purpose machinery that does not sit neatly elsewhere. Its Indonesian scope points to the manufacture of practical industrial equipment: fire sprinklers, machines that filter or clean liquids and gases, distillation units, heat exchangers, gas generators, centrifuges, spraying and sandblasting equipment, steam-cleaning machines, vending machines, attic ventilation fans, tape measures and similar hand tools, non-optical machinist precision tools, and non-electric brazing or soldering equipment. It also includes the manufacture of components and equipment for that machinery.

The common thread is not a single product but a manufacturing role: machinery that helps factories, buildings, workshops, refineries, chemical plants, beverage operations, and other industrial settings move, clean, press, distil, ventilate, dispense, measure, or apply materials. The record is deliberately wide. It reaches from fire extinguishers and spray guns to calendering presses, winding machines and their cylinders, and rectification machinery for oil refineries and chemical or beverage industries. A company registering this activity is therefore not describing ordinary trading or installation work; it is identifying itself as a maker of machinery and related equipment within this broad general-purpose field.

On scale, the record is unusually open. Micro, small, medium, and large businesses are all listed as eligible scales. Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also clear: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing value of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no separate lower ceiling in the slim record, and there is no basis here to add one.

Bali is the more careful reading. The record does not mark this activity as simply blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false. But its Bali status is Blocked (scope-dependent), and the reason is explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity". That warning sits beside the moratorium rule that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest conclusion is precise rather than dramatic: nationally, KBLI 28199 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, PMA registration depends on the exact declared activity and its live OSS risk treatment, because some scopes may fall into the Bali moratorium logic while others may be registrable only through the higher-risk declaration path described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 28199 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the decisive issue is the exact activity declared in OSS.

editorial.headline: KBLI 28210: Agricultural Machinery With a Bali Registration Wall
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture of farming and forestry machinery, nationally open to full foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28210 is the industrial code for making agricultural and forestry machinery: the heavy, functional equipment that prepares land, plants seed, distributes inputs, harvests crops, and supports farm-side processing. Its scope is broad but practical. It covers tractors for agriculture and forestry, walking single-axe tractors, ploughing and harrowing machines, seed and fertilizer spreaders, harvesters and cutting machines, rice threshers, corn shellers, milking machines, horticultural sprayers, handsprayers, and lawn mowers, including those used for home lawns. It also reaches more specialised equipment: self-unloading agricultural trailers and semi-trailers, poultry warming machines, beekeeping machinery, animal-feed preparation equipment, machines for cleaning and sorting eggs and fruit, machinery for vertical farming, and the components and accessories for agricultural machinery.

That makes the code relevant to manufacturers rather than ordinary farm operators. The registrant is not simply using a tractor or a sprayer; it is producing machinery, equipment, parts, or related fittings for agricultural and forestry use. The scale profile is unusually wide: the record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In plain English, the same activity family can be registered by micro, small, medium, or large-scale businesses, so the code is not reserved only for factory-sized manufacturers. Its commercial footprint can range from focused component-making to larger machinery production, provided the activity remains within the manufacturing scope described in the record.

Nationally, the signal is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For an investor reading only the national rule, this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity. There is no national foreign-share reduction in the record, no partial cap below full ownership, and no special percentage calculation to make. At the national level, KBLI 28210 reads as an industrial manufacturing code that can support full foreign ownership.

Bali is the hard exception. This record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets `l4_bali_blocked` to true. The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is also explicit: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest reading is therefore simple: a foreign investor may find the activity nationally open, but cannot register this PMA activity in Bali under the Bali-side record. This is not a Bali ownership ceiling; it is a Bali registration block.

editorial.headline: Machine Tools for Metal and Other Hard Materials
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28220 covers the manufacture of industrial machine tools, nationally open to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28220 is a manufacturing code for the machinery behind industrial fabrication: machine tools used to make or work metal and other hard materials such as wood, bone, stone, hard plastic, hard rubber and cold glass. Its scope is not limited to conventional cutting or forming equipment. The record includes machine tools using laser beams, electromagnetic waves, plasma sparks, magnetic vibration and similar technologies, placing this activity squarely in the industrial-production layer rather than in general trading or light workshop services.

The activity reaches across a broad workshop floor. It includes machines for turning, drilling, milling, forming, planing, grinding, pressing and stamping. It also covers punch presses, hydraulic presses, hydraulic brakes, hammers, forging machines, draw-benches, thread rollers and machinery for working cable. Stationary machines for nailing, stapling, gluing or assembling wood, cork, bone, hard rubber and plastic are within scope, as are drilling, filling, riveting and sheet-metal cutting machines. The record also includes particle-board pressing machines, electroplating machines, and parts or accessories integrated into machine tools, including work holders, dividing heads and other specialised components.

This is therefore a serious industrial-manufacturing registration, not merely a label for portable tools or consumables. The record expressly leaves out interchangeable tools for hand tools or machine tools, hand electric soldering equipment, and powered hand tools. For applicants, that distinction matters because the centre of gravity here is the manufacture of machine tools themselves and the specialised parts that become part of those machines. The code is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the record does not confine it to one enterprise size.

Nationally, the investment signal is clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the national source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali is the hard stop. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class), and the record says: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is also explicit: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest reading is that a foreign investor can treat this code as nationally open, but cannot register it as PMA in Bali under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the code is open to 100% foreign ownership, but Bali is the hard stop for PMA registration under the recorded moratorium.

editorial.headline: Metallurgical Machinery, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28230 covers machinery for hot metalworking, smelting, rolling, and related metallurgical or foundry equipment, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28230 is the manufacturing line for machinery used where metal is worked, melted, poured, or rolled. The record describes equipment for hot metalworking, including converters, steel ingot moulds, and ladling or pouring equipment used in metallurgy or metal casting. It also includes smelting machinery, metal rolling mills, rollers for similar mills, and machines for rolling metal in both hot and cold processes. In plain English, this is not the making of metal products themselves; it is the making of the machines that industrial metalworking depends on.

The activity is open across the full business-scale range recorded for this code: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the classification is not framed only for a large industrial actor in the record. A founder choosing this code would be describing the manufacture of metallurgical machinery and its equipment, whether the registered scale is small or large. The scope is technical, but it is also quite bounded: it is about machinery for hot metalworking, smelting, rolling, and metallurgical or foundry use, not every tool or mould connected with metal.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clean. The slim record marks the code as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In practical editorial terms, the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is therefore 100%. There is no basis here to add another threshold, licence condition, capital figure, or timing requirement. The national message is simply that the code is open to foreign investment up to the recorded ceiling.

The Bali picture is also unusually straightforward. The record does include the Bali moratorium rule: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this specific record is not blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. So the honest conclusion is not a hidden Bali cap or a local quota; it is that this code is nationally open, and the record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This class covers the manufacture of machinery and equipment for mining, quarrying, and construction. It includes continuous-action elevators and conveyors for underground use, drilling and cutting machines, mineral processing equipment for sorting, crushing, grinding or mixing solid minerals, and concrete and mortar mixers. Also covered are earth-moving machines like bulldozers, graders, scrapers, and excavators, as well as pile-drivers, asphalt spreaders, concrete surface finishers, off-road dump trucks, snow ploughs, and snow blowers.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is NOT blocked by the 13 May 2026 moratorium — its OSS risk class at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale is medium-high or high, which the moratorium leaves open. A PT PMA can pursue this code in Bali, subject to the standard licensing for its risk class.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin Penambangan, Penggalian dan Konstruksi (28240)? Here is the honest national-vs-Bali picture before you plan a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who can meet the higher-risk licensing requirements — one of the doors that stays open in Bali.

editorial.headline: Heavy Machinery Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28240 covers the making of mining, quarrying, and construction machinery, with all business scales open and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28240 is the industrial home for companies that manufacture the machines behind mining, quarrying, and construction work. Its scope is broad but concrete: underground continuous elevators and material carriers, drilling and tunnelling machines, mineral-processing equipment for washing, crushing, grinding, mixing, or kneading solid mineral materials, concrete and mortar mixers, earth-moving machinery such as bulldozers, graders, scrapers, levelers, shovels, and loaders, plus pile drivers, pile extractors, asphalt and mortar spreaders, concrete finishing machines, excavators, bulldozer blades, off-road dumping trucks, snow ploughs, and snow blowers.

In plain English, this is not a trading or contracting classification. It is for the factory-side activity of making the machinery itself: the equipment used to cut, drill, dig, lift, move, crush, mix, and finish materials in heavy industrial and construction settings. The record points to a manufacturing activity with a technical, capital-equipment character, where the product is the machine or machine component rather than the construction service performed with it.

The scale position is unusually clean. The record lists **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar** as open, so the activity is not framed only for large industrial operators. A small workshop making qualifying equipment and a larger plant manufacturing heavy construction machinery both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the actual activity remains within the manufacturing scope described above.

The national-versus-Bali picture is also clear. Nationally, the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**, so the record treats this as open to full foreign ownership at the national level. Bali does not add a recorded block here: `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. The reason given is precise: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This code is not marked as caught by that block. For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest reading is therefore straightforward: this activity is nationally open and, on this record, not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign-owned setup in Bali, the honest reading is straightforward: this activity is nationally open and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Food-Processing Machinery, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28250 covers the machinery behind food, drink, and tobacco processing, with a sharp split between national openness and Bali PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28250 is the manufacturing lane for machinery used to process food, beverages, and tobacco. Its scope is industrial rather than retail: machines that dry agricultural products, handle dairy production, clean and sort rice or grain, mill flour, press fruit for wine, cider, and juice, bake bread, form pasta, and process meat, poultry, fruit, nuts, vegetables, fish, shellfish, cocoa, chocolate, sugar, beer, and related food inputs. In plain English, this is the code for building the equipment that turns agricultural and marine products into processed food and drink at production scale.

The record makes the breadth of the activity clear. It includes cream separators, milk homogenizers, butter-making and cheese-making machinery; grain cleaners, sifters, separators, polishers, mills, flour sieves, fillers, blenders, rice-husk cleaners, rice mills, and pea splitters; presses and crushers used for fruit-based drinks; bakery ovens, mixers, dough makers, moulds, cutters, and bread-making machines; and other machinery for confectionery, cocoa, chocolate, sugar, brewing, meat, poultry, fruit, vegetable, nut, fish, shellfish, seafood, distillation, and refining processes. A company registering this activity is not simply trading finished machines. It is placing itself in the manufacturing of equipment for the production chain.

On the national record, the activity is open. The PMA status is marked **TERBUKA**, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. The scale field is also broad: **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar** are all listed as open. Taken nationally, then, the code reads as a permitted manufacturing activity across the listed business scales, including full foreign ownership according to the slim record.

Bali changes the practical answer. The Bali status is **Blocked (risk class)**, and the record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true. The stated reason is: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026**. The moratorium rule is also explicit: **Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)**. So the honest reading is direct: while KBLI 28250 is nationally open to PMA with a 100% ceiling, a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 28250 is open to full PMA ownership, but the Bali record turns that openness into a practical registration block.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Mesin Jahit, Mesin Cuci, dan Mesin Pengering untuk Keperluan Niaga
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan mesin jahit, kepala mesin jahit, jarum mesin jahit (baik untuk keperluan rumah tangga maupun untuk untuk keperluan niaga), termasuk pembuatan mesin obras, mesin bordir, mesin oversum dan mesin-mesin untuk penatu dan dry cleaning (mesin cuci dengan atau tanpa air, mesin pengering, mesin seterika dan lain-lain).
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- pembuatan mesin cuci, mesin pengering dan sejenisnya untuk keperluan rumah tangga. lihat kelompok 27510;
- pembuatan jarum jahit yang tidak melekat pada mesin jahit, lihat kelompok 25999.

editorial.headline: Commercial Sewing and Laundry Machinery, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28261 covers the manufacture of sewing, embroidery, laundry and dry-cleaning machinery, with a sharp Bali caveat for foreign-owned registrations.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28261 is an industrial manufacturing classification for the machines behind garment production, commercial laundry, and dry-cleaning operations. Its scope covers the making of sewing machines, sewing-machine heads, and sewing-machine needles for both household and commercial use, alongside overlock, embroidery, and oversum machines. It also reaches into laundry and dry-cleaning machinery: washing machines with or without water, dryers, ironing machines, and related equipment for penatu and dry-cleaning use.

That makes this a machinery-manufacturing code, not a retail, repair, or laundry-service classification. The centre of gravity is production: building the equipment itself. A founder using this code is describing an activity that manufactures the physical machines used by tailors, garment workshops, laundries, and dry cleaners. The record marks the code as open across the full business scale ladder: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. In practical classification terms, it is not confined to one company size; the same activity description can sit behind a small machine workshop or a larger industrial manufacturer, provided the registered activity is the manufacture described in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national table treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no lower foreign-equity cap in the record, and no additional national threshold, licence, or capital figure appears in the slim record. For a national reading of the KBLI alone, this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity.

Bali changes the answer. The Bali-side status is Blocked (risk class), and l4_bali_blocked is true. The record’s reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is also explicit: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is this: KBLI 28261 is nationally open to PMA, but a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today under the Bali moratorium described in the record. This is not a Bali percentage cap or a partial local-partner rule; the record gives no such figure. It is a Bali registration block tied to the risk-class moratorium, despite the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers building machines for textile production—spinning, weaving, knitting, garment finishing, and specialized attachments like automatic stop motions or jacquards—essentially any machine that turns fiber into fabric or finished goods.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this is 100% open to foreign ownership, but Bali applies a strict moratorium on all low and medium-low risk KBLI. Because of that, a PMA company cannot register this activity in Bali since 13 May 2026—it’s effectively blocked for now.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin Tekstil (28262)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign textile-machinery manufacturers aiming to serve Indonesia’s textile hubs, but who currently must set up their factory outside Bali.

editorial.headline: Textile-Machinery Manufacturing Is Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A precise manufacturing code for textile machinery is foreign-open at national level, but the record blocks PMA registration in Bali under the island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 28262 covers the manufacturing side of textile machinery.** The record describes a broad industrial scope: machines for preparing fibre, spinning, preparing weaving, weaving itself, textile printing, knitting, cloth inspection, finishing, and garment-making. It also reaches the auxiliary equipment that keeps textile machinery operating, including dobby and jacquard equipment, automatic stop-motion machines, shuttle-change machinery, spindles, and spindle flyers. In plain English, this is not a trading or showroom activity. It is the activity code for making the machines and attachments used inside textile production lines.

That scope matters because the code is open across every business scale listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small workshop making specialised textile-machine components and a larger industrial manufacturer would both sit inside the scale range shown here, provided the actual registered activity matches the manufacturing scope. The editorial point is narrow but important: the code is defined by the making of textile machinery and its related equipment, not by textile production itself, not by distribution, and not by a general engineering identity detached from the listed machines.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national record treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no smaller national cap in the slim record, no staged ownership rule, and no extra threshold stated here. For a founder reading only the national position, this looks like a straightforward foreign-open manufacturing activity.

**Bali is the decisive exception.** The record says `l4_bali_blocked` is true and gives the Bali status as `Blocked (risk class)`. Its reason is specific: OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, so the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium from May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. So the honest reading is this: a foreign investor may see a nationally open, 100% PMA-eligible code, but cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.

editorial.headline: Leather-Product Machinery, Open Nationally but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers machinery for preparing, tanning, working, making, and repairing leather products, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28263 is about the machinery behind leather production, not the leather goods themselves. The record describes an industrial activity for making machines used to prepare, tan, or work leather, and machines used to make or repair footwear and other products from large hides, small hides, and fur-bearing skins. In plain English, this is the manufacturing lane for the equipment that turns animal-derived leather materials into workable industrial inputs and finished leather-product processes.

That distinction matters because the activity sits upstream of the finished product. A company registering this code is not simply trading shoes or bags; it is positioning itself as a maker of the machines used in leather preparation, leather processing, and the production or repair of footwear and other leather goods. The slim record also marks the scope as "Seluruh", so the editorial reading has to stay broad: the activity covers the full stated scope of machinery for leather-product preparation and manufacture, rather than a narrowed sub-segment.

On scale, the record is unusually clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators. That means the code is not framed only for large industrial players; the registration window in the record spans the full scale ladder. Nationally, it is also marked TERBUKA for PMA, with pma_max_asing at 100 and the source given as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The national picture, therefore, is straightforward: the slim record treats foreign ownership as open up to 100%.

Bali is the hard qualification, and it changes the practical answer for a foreign-owned setup on the island. The record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the status as Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026". The moratorium rule is equally direct: "Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)". So the honest reading is not that Bali applies a different percentage, quota, or partnership formula. The record gives no Bali-side cap at all. It says this nationally open, 100% foreign-ownership activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali because of the Bali moratorium rule attached to the recorded risk classification.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that this nationally open, 100% foreign-ownership activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

It’s the industrial side of the printing world: you’re building the hardware that printers and binderies use.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. editorial.headline: Printing-Machine Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28291 covers the making of printing and binding machinery, with national PMA openness but a clear Bali block for foreign registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28291 is a manufacturing activity for the machinery behind print production. The record describes it as the making of printing machines, including simple press machines, cylinder presses, and rotary presses. Its scope also reaches the equipment that supports print finishing and binding: book-sewing machines, spiral-binding machines, and page-numbering machines. In plain English, this is not publishing, design, or print-shop operation. It is the industrial making of the machines and equipment used to print, bind, and number printed materials.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not reserved in the record for only one size of enterprise. A small producer of binding equipment and a larger manufacturer of press machinery both sit inside the same stated activity, provided the actual work remains within the recorded scope: making printing machinery, printing-equipment machinery, and binding machinery. That breadth matters because the scope is defined by the machine-making activity itself, not by the customer, the printed content, or a separate service model.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is a foreign-open manufacturing line with no ownership cap below full foreign ownership in the slim record. There is no basis here to add a minimum capital figure, a special licence, a tax condition, or a timing rule. The national facts are simply that the activity is open and the recorded ceiling is 100%.

Bali changes the practical answer. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class), and the record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, so the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA, island-wide and permanently. The honest reading is therefore direct: a foreigner may see KBLI 28291 as nationally open, but cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the record supplied.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreigner may see KBLI 28291 as nationally open, but cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the record supplied.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing of machinery for paper mills, including equipment for pulp processing, paper and cardboard production, drying, and finishing machines for paper products like envelopes, bags, and cutting tools.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this KBLI is 100% open to foreigners, but a Bali-specific moratorium on low and medium-low risk sectors (effective from 13 May 2026) blocks PMA registration. A foreign-owned company cannot obtain this license in Bali under current local policy.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin Pabrik Kertas (28292)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur planning to manufacture paper mill machinery, but they must incorporate outside Bali due to the local moratorium.

editorial.headline: Paper-Mill Machinery With a Closed Door in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the factory machinery behind pulp, paper, carton, paperboard, and paper-goods production, but Bali blocks PMA registration under its moratorium.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 28292 is an industrial machinery activity, not a paper-trading or paper-making activity.** The record places it around the manufacture of machines used inside paper plants: equipment for pulp processing, paper and carton production, paperboard making or finishing, drying machines for wood, pulp, and paper, and the machinery used to turn paper or paperboard into finished goods. That includes paper-cutting machines, envelope-making machines, paper-bag machines, and similar equipment. In plain English, this is the code for building the machines that make and finish paper-industry output.

That scope matters because it points to a manufacturing business with a technical production profile. The activity is open across the full recorded scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A small machine workshop and a larger industrial manufacturer are therefore both inside the scale language of the record, provided the actual registered activity remains the manufacture of the paper-plant and paper-goods machinery described above. The record does not add a licensing timetable, a capital floor, a tax treatment, or any operational threshold, so the clean editorial reading stops at the activity scope, the scale range, and the investment-access status it actually states.

Nationally, the picture is straightforward. At the national level, PMA status is TERBUKA, with the recorded maximum foreign ownership set at 100%. For a foreign-owned company looking only at the national investment line, this is therefore not a capped activity. The stated national source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national record alone, the activity reads as fully foreign-open across the manufacturing scope described in the slim record.

Bali is the decisive exception. The record marks this activity as blocked for PMA registration in Bali: l4_bali_blocked is true, and the Bali status is Blocked (risk class). The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, which brings it inside the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is blunt: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest conclusion is narrow but important: KBLI 28292 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet a foreigner cannot register it as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28292 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet a foreigner cannot register it as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Mesin Keperluan Khusus Lainnya YTDL
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup berbagai mesin-mesin keperluan khusus lainnya yang belum termasuk kelompok sebelumnya, seperti mesin untuk pengerjaan karet atau plastik lunak atau untuk pembuatan produk dari bahan tersebut, seperti mesin ekstrusi, pencetak, mesin pembuatan ban angin (pneumatik) atau ban vulkanisisasi, mesin lainnya untuk pembuatan produk dari plastik atau karet khusus, mesin cetak dan penjilidan buku dan mesin untuk pendukung pencetakan pada berbagai macam bahan, mesin cetak tiga dimensi (3D printing), mesin untuk memproduksi ubin, batu bata, perekat keramik potongan, pipa, grafit elektroda, kapur tulis, cetakan besi tuang dan lain-lain, mesin pabrik semikonduktor, robot industri yang menjalankan berbagai tugas untuk keperluan khusus, mesin untuk merakit lampu listrik dan lampu elektronik, tabung atau bola lampu, mesin untuk memproduksi atau pekerjaan panas dari kaca atau barang-barang dari kaca, serat kaca atau benang dan mesin atau peralatan untuk pemisahan isotopik, peralatan meluruskan dan menyeimbangkan ban (kecuali penyeimbang roda), mesin untuk memasang dan melepas ban (termasuk ban untuk alat berat dan alat pertahanan), sistem pelumasan pusat, persneling pesawat terbang (launching gear), pelontar pembawa pesawat terbang (carrier catapult) dan peralatan yang terkait, peralatan arena bowling otomatis (pin-setter), peralatan jalan berputar (roundabouts), ayunan, galeri menembak, gelanggang hiburan atau permainan lainnya, mesin pembuat briket dari produk pertanian, serta mesin industri aditif.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing of special-purpose machinery that doesn't fit neatly into other categories—think machines for processing rubber or soft plastics (extruders, moulders, tyre-building or vulcanizing equipment), 3D printers, bookbinding and printing support devices, and machinery for making tiles, bricks, ceramic adhesives, pipes, or graphite electrodes. It's essentially a catch-all for niche industrial equipment production.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership, but in Bali it is currently blocked for PMA companies. The province has placed an island-wide moratorium—effective from 13 May 2026—on new foreign registrations for low and medium-low risk classifications like this one, so you cannot set up a PMA in Bali to manufacture these machines right now.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Mesin Keperluan Khusus Lainnya YTDL (28299)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign manufacturers or industrial entrepreneurs looking to produce specialized machinery—such as plastic extruders, 3D printers, or ceramic tile lines—and who need a production base, though Bali is currently off-limits for a PMA setup.

editorial.headline: Special-Purpose Machinery Is Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28299 covers a broad industrial machinery class: nationally open to foreign ownership, but not registerable by PMA in Bali under the record’s risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28299 is a catch-all industrial machinery classification for special-purpose machines that do not sit in the earlier, more specific machinery groups. The record describes machinery for rubber and soft-plastic processing, including extrusion, moulding, pneumatic-tyre and vulcanisation equipment; machinery for printing, bookbinding and print support on many kinds of material; three-dimensional printing machines; equipment for producing tiles, bricks, ceramic adhesives, pipes, graphite electrodes, chalk, cast-iron moulds and other industrial products. It also reaches into semiconductor plant machinery, industrial robots assigned to special-purpose tasks, equipment for assembling electric and electronic lamps, machinery for hot-working glass and glass products, and isotope-separation equipment.

That breadth is the point. This is not a narrow retail or service activity; it is a manufacturing-machine category for producers of technical equipment used by other industries. The scope also includes tyre-straightening and balancing equipment, tyre-mounting and removal machines including those for heavy equipment and defence equipment, central lubrication systems, aircraft launching gear, carrier catapults and related equipment, automatic bowling pin-setters, amusement equipment such as roundabouts, swings, shooting galleries and other entertainment-park devices, agricultural briquette-making machines, and additive industrial machinery. In plain English, the code is for manufacturers of specialised production, processing, assembly, industrial, defence-adjacent, entertainment-equipment and additive-manufacturing machines that fall within this residual special-purpose machinery class.

On scale, the national record is broad: the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The foreign-investment position is also clear at the national level. The PMA status is marked TERBUKA, the maximum foreign ownership figure is 100, and the source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder reading the national line only, that means the activity is presented as fully foreign-open, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling in the record and no partial cap stated here.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true and gives the reason: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” It also states the moratorium rule as: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” So the honest reading is split: nationally, KBLI 28299 is open for PMA up to the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity today as PMA because the Bali-side record blocks it by risk class. The distinction matters: the block is not a separate Bali percentage, quota or local-partner formula. The only ownership percentage in the record is the national PMA figure; Bali’s status is a registration block under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 28299 is fully foreign-open in the record; in Bali, the same activity is blocked for PMA registration by risk class.

editorial.headline: Four-Wheel Motor Vehicle Manufacturing, Read at Factory Scale
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 29100 is the vehicle-making code for cars, buses, commercial vehicles, engines, and special-purpose four-wheel machinery, with national foreign ownership open up to 100%.
editorial.body:
KBLI 29100 is a manufacturing code for the making and remaking of motor vehicles with four wheels or more. Its scope is broad, but it is not vague: it covers electric vehicles, hybrid combustion vehicles, autonomous vehicles, passenger cars, buses, ambulances, station wagons, vans, lorries, road tractors for semitrailers, trolley buses, rail coaches, and special-purpose vehicles. The record also brings vehicle engines into the frame, including electric motors used for propulsion, and it extends to the remanufacture of motor-vehicle engines.

The practical centre of gravity is clear. This is a production code, not a showroom code and not a light trading category. It is for operators whose business activity is the industrial creation or rebuilding of complete vehicles, vehicle platforms, or propulsion systems within the stated scope. The examples range from ordinary passenger and commercial vehicles to fire trucks, road sweepers, armoured vehicles, tow trucks, all-terrain vehicles, go-carts, racing cars, golf cars, amphibious vehicles, snow cars, travelling-library vehicles, and rural multipurpose four-wheel mechanical equipment. A founder choosing this code is therefore describing a manufacturing activity with a serious technical footprint.

The scale position is unusually open in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as open. That matters because the code is not confined to one size of enterprise in the slim record. A small remanufacturing business and a large industrial manufacturer may both recognise themselves in the registered scope, provided the activity is genuinely within the making or remaking of the vehicles, engines, or special-purpose vehicle types described. The editorial caution is not to stretch the code beyond that factual centre. If the business is mainly producing unrelated components, bodies, agricultural machinery, forestry tractors, excavating machinery, or off-road dumping trucks, the record itself signals that those activities sit outside this scope.

The national-vs-Bali picture is clean rather than dramatic. Nationally, the record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Put simply, foreign ownership may reach 100% nationwide. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record, and the Bali status is not blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, with the reason stated as “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule still matters as context, because Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, permanently. But for this record, the conclusion is that KBLI 29100 is nationally foreign-open and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The national-vs-Bali picture is clean rather than dramatic.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This business group covers the manufacturing of motor vehicle bodies and related parts. Activities include producing bodywork for specialized vehicles like fire trucks, mobile libraries, armored cars, and concrete mixers; making equipment for all motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers; and building trailers, semi-trailers, tankers, caravans, and specially designed containers for multimodal transport. It also involves the repair and custom ordering of motor vehicles and the production of trailer chassis and frames.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this activity is open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is NOT blocked by the 13 May 2026 moratorium — its OSS risk class at the large-enterprise (Besar) scale is medium-high or high, which the moratorium leaves open. A PT PMA can pursue this code in Bali, subject to the standard licensing for its risk class.

editorial.headline: Bodies, Trailers, and Custom Vehicle Builds Under KBLI 29200
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 29200 covers the industrial work of building vehicle bodies, trailers, semitrailers, specialist containers, and made-to-order motor-vehicle customisation.
editorial.body:
KBLI 29200 is a manufacturing classification for the built form of road vehicles rather than the complete vehicle as a brand or consumer product. Its centre of gravity is the making of vehicle bodies and bodywork for four-wheeled-or-larger motor vehicles, including specialised bodies for fire engines, mobile libraries, armoured cars, and concrete mixer trucks. The record also brings in seating as part of vehicle-body production, equipment for motor vehicles, trailers, and semitrailers, and the fabrication of chassis or frames for trailers.

The activity is broader than a simple workshop label. It includes trailer and semitrailer manufacturing, with examples such as tankers, enclosed and open-body trailers, and caravans. It also includes custom repair and made-to-order customisation of motor vehicles, plus the manufacture of specially designed containers, including containers for liquid transport, when they are equipped for carriage by one or more modes of transport. In plain English, this is the code for businesses that turn steel, structure, and vehicle engineering into usable transport bodies and towed platforms.

On scale, the record is unusually wide: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification can describe anything from a small bodywork or customisation operation through to a larger industrial manufacturer, provided the registered activity remains inside the scope described here. But this record does not mark KBLI 29200 as blocked in Bali. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record provided.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the industrial manufacturing of components, spare parts, and accessories for four-wheeled or more motor vehicles—think suspension systems, exhausts, steering parts, body elements like doors and bumpers, car seats, and related electrical equipment.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open (100% PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Suku Cadang dan Aksesori Kendaraan Bermotor Roda Empat atau Lebih (29300)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs looking to manufacture automotive parts locally, but who must choose a location outside Bali while the Bali moratorium remains in place.

editorial.headline: Motor-Vehicle Components With Full National PMA Access
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 29300 covers the manufacturing base behind four-wheel vehicle parts, from chassis modules to electrical systems, and the record treats it as nationally open to foreign investment.
editorial.body:
KBLI 29300 is an industrial manufacturing code for the parts that make a four-wheel-or-larger motor vehicle work, fit together, and meet modern equipment expectations. Its scope is broad but still disciplined: mechanical components such as radiators, fuel tanks, mufflers, brakes, gearboxes, axles, wheels, shock absorbers, exhaust pipes, catalytic converters, clutches, steering wheels, steering columns, and steering boxes sit inside it. So do body-related parts and accessories, including seat belts, doors, bumpers, airbags, and car seats. The record also brings vehicle electrical equipment into the same frame: generators, alternators, spark plugs, ignition wiring harnesses and starters, automatic door and window systems, taximeters fitted into instrument panels, voltage regulators, and lights.

The code is not only about individual spare parts. It also covers chassis or frames without engines, inverter modules and fuel cells for four-wheel-or-larger vehicles, and plastic vehicle components such as car interiors, coolant reservoirs, mirror covers, and battery holders. The finishing of those plastic parts is also in scope when it involves metal coating, other coating substances, or painting. In practical terms, this is the classification for a manufacturer whose activity is centred on automotive components rather than complete vehicle assembly: the factory may be producing structural, mechanical, safety, electrical, interior, or finished plastic components, as long as the activity remains within the recorded scope.

The registration scale picture is unusually open across the business-size spectrum. The slim record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as open scales, so the code is not framed only for a large industrial operator. A small workshop-style component producer and a larger parts manufacturer are both within the recorded scale ladder, provided their actual activity matches the manufacturing scope. That breadth matters because KBLI selection is not a branding exercise; it should describe the real production activity, the material process, and the product family being manufactured.

On foreign ownership, the national picture is clear. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows foreign ownership up to 100% for this activity. The Bali position is also clear, but it is not a separate ownership cap. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently; this code is not marked as blocked. The honest reading is therefore simple: nationally open, not blocked for Bali PMA registration in this record, with the Bali conclusion resting on the recorded risk-and-moratorium reason rather than on any separate Bali percentage.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the building or assembly of manned ships and underwater vehicles that need a crew physically on board to handle navigation, propulsion, and safety. It includes everything from passenger ferries, cargo ships, and tankers to fishing boats, research vessels, and even military warships—as long as the crew operates the vessel in person.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kendaraan Air dan Bawah Air Berawak (30111)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign shipbuilders or marine engineering entrepreneurs who want to manufacture or assemble crewed commercial or specialist vessels, but for now they’ll need to look outside Bali.

editorial.headline: Crewed Shipbuilding Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the manufacture and assembly of crewed surface and underwater vessels, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 30111 is industrial shipbuilding for crewed vessels, not a loose maritime services category.** The record frames it around the making or assembly of water and underwater vehicles, military or civilian, whose core functions depend on a physically present crew. Navigation, propulsion, and safety are explicitly tied to crewed operation. In practical language, the activity includes passenger ships, ferries, cargo ships, tankers, tugboats, commercial sailing vessels, warships, research vessels, fishing vessels, and vessels used for fish processing or preserving fishery products when those vessels can operate only with crew physically on board.

That scope gives the code a manufacturing character. It is about building or assembling the vessel itself: industri perahu, industri kapal, and the wider set of crewed ships and underwater craft described in the record. A founder using this activity would be registering an industrial undertaking around vessel production or assembly, not merely operating a ferry route, providing logistics, or trading marine equipment. The defining question is whether the business is making or assembling crewed water or underwater vehicles that perform their main functions through an onboard crew.

The scale picture is broad. Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar may all pursue the activity under this record. That matters because it does not reserve the activity only for large industrial groups in the slim data; it recognises the activity across the full listed scale range. At the same time, the content of the scope remains heavy and specific: the activity is still ship and boat industry work, including commercial, research, fishing, cargo, tanker, tug, ferry, passenger, and military vessel examples given by the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. Put plainly, the national record treats it as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. Bali does not introduce a separate percentage in this record, and none should be inferred. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with l4_bali_blocked set to false. The reason is also explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this activity is not blocked by that moratorium in the slim record.
editorial.pullQuote: The national record treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and the Bali record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This industry covers the fabrication of offshore and floating structures—think drilling platforms, floating docks, barges, pontoon bridges, cranes, buoys, storage tanks, and non‑recreational hovercraft. Essentially, it’s large‑scale marine construction for industrial, commercial, or oil‑and‑gas support, not pleasure craft.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Bangunan Lepas Pantai Dan Bangunan Terapung (30112)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: This fits experienced offshore engineering firms, marine construction companies, or industrial shipbuilders who serve oil & gas, port infrastructure, or heavy coastal development projects.

editorial.headline: Offshore and Floating Structures With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30112 covers industrial construction of offshore and floating structures, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30112 is an industrial code for building offshore constructions and floating structures, together with their equipment and fittings. Its scope is deliberately heavy and marine-facing: platforms and floating or diving structures for drilling activity; floating docks, lifeboats and floating cranes; floating bridges, pontoons and coffer-dams; floating landing structures, living quarters, jackets, platforms and mooring buoys; buoys, floating tanks, barges, crane vessels and inflatable rafts that are not for recreation. The record also includes hovercraft manufacturing, while excluding recreational hovercraft.

That makes this a manufacturing and construction activity, not a general marine-service label. A company using this code should be anchored in the making of these offshore or floating assets: the physical structures, hull-like equipment, support buildings and marine industrial units named in the scope. The language of the record is broad, but it is not casual. It points to engineered objects built for work at sea, on water, around drilling activity or in floating infrastructure contexts.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar operators, so the registration pathway is not confined to one business size. A small workshop fabricating qualifying floating components and a larger industrial builder making platforms or floating cranes sit within the same scale logic, provided the registered activity remains the construction or manufacture described by the record. The important editorial point is that scale openness does not change the identity of the activity: the code is still about building offshore and floating structures, including their equipment and fittings.

The national foreign-ownership position is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali also does not block this code under the moratorium record supplied here. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That matters because the Bali moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. For this code, the supplied Bali-side result is not a percentage, quota or partnership condition; it is simply that the record does not mark PMA registration as blocked in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Kendaraan Air dan Bawah Air Tanpa Awak
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan atau perakitan kendaraan air tanpa awak (KATA)/unmanned surface vehicle (USV), kendaraan bawah air tanpa awak (KBATA) yang didesain untuk dapat dioperasikan dengan kendali jarak jauh oleh awak, misalnya remotely operated underwater vehicle (ROV), kendali otomatis berbasis kecerdasan artifisial, atau kendali campuran (dapat diawaki jika diperlukan), seperti KATA dan KBATA untuk survei batimetri, pemantauan dan pemetaan, inspeksi infrastruktur bawah air, penelitian kelautan, survei arkeologi bawah air, operasi penyelamatan, dan operasi militer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing or assembly of unmanned surface and underwater vehicles (USVs and UUVs) that can be operated remotely, autonomously via artificial intelligence, or with optional human control. They're used for tasks like bathymetric surveys, ocean monitoring, underwater infrastructure inspections, marine research, archaeological mapping, rescue missions, and military operations.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business field is 100% open for foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kendaraan Air dan Bawah Air Tanpa Awak (30113)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign marine robotics manufacturers or tech companies ready to produce unmanned water vehicles for commercial, scientific, or defence applications.

editorial.headline: Unmanned Marine Vehicles With a Clear National Opening
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30113 covers the making and assembly of unmanned water and underwater vehicles, with national PMA access open and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30113 is a manufacturing and assembly activity for unmanned marine vehicles: surface craft and underwater vehicles designed to operate without a conventional crew on board. The record names unmanned surface vehicles and unmanned underwater vehicles, including remotely operated underwater vehicles, and it also recognises systems that can run by remote crew control, automatic artificial-intelligence-based control, or mixed control where the vehicle can be crewed if needed. In plain English, this is the industrial code for building advanced marine platforms rather than merely using them.

The scope is deliberately practical. These vehicles are described for bathymetric surveys, monitoring and mapping, underwater infrastructure inspection, marine research, underwater archaeological survey, rescue operations, and military operations. That range matters because it shows the activity is not limited to one narrow research niche. It sits across marine technology, vessel manufacturing, survey infrastructure, and specialist underwater work, while the record also places it in the wider context of boat and ship industry.

For registration scale, the record is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open. That means the activity is not reserved in the record for only one size of operator. A founder reading this code should therefore focus first on whether the intended business is genuinely about making or assembling these vehicles, including their relevant control model and use case, rather than treating the code as a generic marine-services label.

The national foreign-investment position is clean. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali is also not marked as blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali-side reason says, “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule still matters as context because the record states that Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this record does not place KBLI 30113 inside that blocked outcome. The honest reading is therefore direct: nationally open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is direct: nationally open to foreign ownership up to the stated ceiling, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the record provided.
