intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of all kinds of pleasure and sports boats—yachts, motorboats, canoes, kayaks, jetskis, personal watercraft, and even hovercraft for recreation. It also includes factories that convert or refit existing vessels into leisure or sports craft. If you're building recreational boats, this is your category.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kapal dan Perahu Untuk Tujuan Wisata atau Rekreasi dan Olahraga (30120)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign boat builders and watercraft manufacturers who want to produce recreational vessels, though under present rules they must set up their factory outside Bali.

editorial.headline: Recreational Boatbuilding With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30120 covers the making and conversion of leisure, sport, and recreational craft, nationally open to foreign investment and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30120 is the manufacturing lane for boats and watercraft built for leisure, recreation, tourism, and sport. Its scope is broad, but still clearly industrial: it covers the making of inflatable rubber boats and rafts, sailing boats and yachts with or without motors, motorboats, recreational hovercraft, cruise vessels, personal watercraft, canoes, kayaks, jetskis, rowing boats, sampans, speedboats, racing sailboats, and other sport or pleasure craft. The record also includes factories that convert yachts and sport vessels, so the code is not only about new builds; it also reaches industrial conversion work where the end product remains a recreational or sport vessel.

That boundary matters. This is not a general marine-services code, and it is not a rental, repair, parts, engine, surfboard, or crewed-charter activity. The centre of gravity is production: a factory, workshop, or industrial operation whose output is a leisure or sport vessel. A founder choosing this code is therefore presenting the business as a maker or converter of recreational craft, not as an operator of tourism trips or a maintenance provider. That distinction keeps the activity anchored in manufacturing, even when the finished product belongs to the tourism, marina, or water-sports economy.

The scale profile is unusually inclusive. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, which means the code can describe a small specialist boatbuilder as well as a larger industrial operation. That range is useful for founders because the same activity family can cover modest production and more capital-intensive vessel manufacturing. It does not, however, change the nature of the code: whatever the business size, the registered activity should still be the making or conversion of boats and vessels for leisure, recreation, tourism, or sport.

The national investment picture is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, so the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The Bali picture is also not a hidden closure. The record says l4_bali_blocked is false and gives the reason: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium". The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not blocked by that rule on the record provided. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open, foreign ownership up to 100%, and not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Where Rail Manufacturing Sits in the PMA Map
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30200 covers the industrial making of locomotives, rail carriages, specialist parts, railway service vehicles, signalling equipment, mine rail units, and rail simulators.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30200 is an industrial manufacturing code for the railway system itself. Its scope begins with the making or assembly of electric, diesel, steam, and other railway locomotives, then extends across self-propelled rail carriages, electric train carriages, trams, vans, and trucks. It also covers maintenance and service vehicles for railways and electric trains, plus non-self-propelled rolling stock such as passenger carriages, freight wagons, tank wagons, workshop wagons, crane wagons, unloading wagons, trains, and carts. In plain English, this is the code for businesses that build the moving hardware of rail transport, not a general metalworking or transport-services activity.

The scope is also specific about the parts and systems that belong inside the activity. It includes special parts for railways, electric trains, and carriages: bogies, axles, axle boxes and wheels, brakes and brake parts, coupling and hook equipment, buffers and buffer parts, shock absorbers, locomotive and carriage frames, bodies, inter-corridor connectors, and similar components. The record further brings in mechanical and electromagnetic signal equipment, safety and control equipment for railway signs, electric trains, water traffic, roads, parking facilities, airfields, and other settings. Mine locomotives, mining rail carriages, and railway transport simulators are included as well. The boundary matters because the activity is not merely the assembly of a train; it is a rail-manufacturing ecosystem with specialised rolling stock, parts, safety systems, and simulation hardware.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. That means the classification is not reserved in the record for only one operating scale: it can be registered by very small, small, medium, and large-scale operators. The practical reading is that the activity can describe a wide range of businesses, from a focused specialist making components to a larger manufacturer assembling locomotives or rail carriages, so long as the registered activity remains within the record's stated scope.

The national foreign-investment position is clean: the record marks PMA status as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Rendered as ownership language, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the recorded reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule stated in the record is that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest reading is that this is not a low-risk Bali activity being stopped by the moratorium; it is marked as not blocked.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Industri Pesawat Udara Berawak dan Mesin Terkait
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembuatan atau perakitan pesawat udara untuk sipil dan militer dan perlengkapannya, pesawat udara untuk penumpang atau barang yang didesain untuk beroperasi hanya dengan kehadiran secara fisik penerbang dalam menjalankan fungsi utama pesawat udara, seperti pesawat udara bermesin jet, pesawat udara propeler, helikopter, balon udara dan pesawat layang. Kelompok ini juga mencakup kegiatan pembuatan pesawat terbang untuk olahraga atau tujuan lain, pesawat peluncur dan pesawat peluncur gantung, kapal seplin/balon berkemudi dan balon udara panas, suku cadang dan aksesori pesawat terbang, seperti rakitan utama seperti badan pesawat terbang, sayap, pintu, pengontrol permukaan, roda gigi untuk mendarat, tanki bahan bakar, nacelles dan lain-lain; baling-baling, pisau rotor helikopter dan rotor pendorong; berbagai macam motor dan mesin yang terdapat di pesawat terbang; dan suku cadang jet turbo dan pendorong turbo untuk pesawat terbang, pesawat terbang latih darat, termasuk pemeriksaan, pembangunan kembali, dan konversi pesawat atau mesin pesawat serta pembuatan tempat duduk pesawat terbang.

editorial.headline: Crewed Aircraft Manufacturing Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30301 covers the making, assembly, rebuilding, and conversion of crewed aircraft, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 30301 is an industrial manufacturing code, not an aviation service code.** Its scope is the making or assembly of crewed aircraft and related aircraft machinery for both civil and military use. The defining feature is physical pilot presence: the record describes aircraft for passengers or cargo that are designed to operate only when a pilot is physically present to carry out the aircraft's main functions. In practical language, this code reaches aircraft with jet engines, propeller aircraft, helicopters, air balloons, and gliders.

The scope is broad because it follows the aircraft into its principal hardware. It includes aircraft made for sport or other purposes, gliders and hang gliders, airships or steerable balloons, hot-air balloons, and aircraft parts and accessories. The record names major assemblies such as fuselages, wings, doors, surface controls, landing gear, fuel tanks, and nacelles, as well as propellers, helicopter rotor blades, pusher rotors, aircraft motors and engines, turbojet and turboprop-related parts, ground flight trainers, inspection, rebuilding, aircraft or aircraft-engine conversion, and the making of aircraft seats. That makes the code suitable for a business whose registered activity is the industrial production or assembly of the aircraft or aircraft-machine layer itself.

On scale, the record is unusually clean: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the registered activity is not confined in the record to one enterprise size band. A founder reading the code should still treat the registration choice as a matter of fit between the actual factory activity and the scale declared in OSS, because the record's Bali note refers specifically to risk at scale Besar. The editorial point is not that every small workshop is automatically equivalent to a major aircraft plant; it is that the slim record marks all four scales as open for this activity code.

The national foreign-investment position is also direct. Under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record lists the PMA status as TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling as 100%. Bali does not add a separate ownership percentage here. Instead, the Bali-side question is the moratorium screen. The record states `l4_bali_blocked: false` and gives the reason as: `OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium`. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali province, permanently; this code, on the record supplied, is not blocked by that rule. So the honest reading is simple: nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record marks it as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than moratorium-blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this activity is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the record marks it as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than moratorium-blocked.

editorial.headline: UAV Manufacturing With Room to Scale in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30302 covers the serious end of unmanned aircraft manufacturing, from assembly and modification to AI-enabled and remotely piloted systems.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30302 is a manufacturing classification for unmanned aircraft and their related machinery. In practical terms, it is the code for businesses that make, assemble, rebuild, or modify unmanned aerial vehicles designed for remote piloting, automatic control through artificial intelligence, or mixed-control operation where crewed use remains possible if needed. The scope is broad, but it is not vague: it points to purpose-built aircraft for agriculture, topographic survey, search and rescue, cargo delivery, reconnaissance and surveillance, combat support, mine destruction, and air defence.

That makes this a production-side activity rather than a simple trading or service label. A company using this code is placing itself in the industrial chain around UAV systems: fabrication, assembly, technical reconstruction, and modification. The record opens the activity across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the classification is not reserved only for large industrial operators. What matters is that the registered activity matches the substance of the work: making or technically altering unmanned aircraft and the machinery tied to them.

Nationally, the record is clear. PMA status is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100. For a foreign-owned setup, that means the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, under the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no partial cap in the slim record, and no additional national threshold is stated here. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: at national level, this activity is open to foreign investment up to the full recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not blocked on this record. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this entry is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason given as: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. That is the key operational distinction. This is not a case where a nationally open PMA activity is then stopped at the Bali registration layer. For KBLI 30302, the record shows a nationally foreign-open activity and a Bali status that does not trigger the moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: This is not a case where a nationally open PMA activity is then stopped at the Bali registration layer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the manufacturing or assembly of spacecraft for passengers or cargo, launch vehicles, satellite-carrying rockets, satellites, planetary exploration vehicles, orbital stations, and space shuttles.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business field is fully open (100%) to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.

editorial.headline: Spacecraft Manufacturing, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30303 covers the making or assembly of spacecraft and related machines, with national PMA ownership at 100% and Bali marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 30303** is a manufacturing and assembly classification for space vehicles and related machines. The scope names spacecraft for passengers or goods, space launch vehicles, rockets that orbit satellites, satellites, planetary exploration craft, orbital stations, and space shuttles. The record is unusually specific: it is concerned with the object being made or assembled, not with a general technology label. A business using this activity code should therefore be anchored in those space-vehicle and machine categories, because that is the entire scope the slim record gives.

The scale reading is broader than the activity may sound. The record opens the code to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar registrations. That does not add any hidden threshold, capital figure, tax treatment, or timeline; none appears in the slim record. It simply means the scale field itself is open across the listed categories. The disciplined reading is narrow: the classification can sit at those registration scales, while the record stays silent on everything outside its own activity scope, ownership field, scale field, and Bali-status field.

Nationally, the PMA signal is direct. The status is TERBUKA, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. No smaller foreign stake cap appears in this record. The result is a clean national reading for a foreign-owned setup: the activity is open under the PMA field, with the maximum foreign ownership rendered at the full recorded percentage. The source field for that national position is carried separately in the record, and no other national limitation is supplied here.

For Bali, the important distinction is that the record gives a status, not a local percentage: OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. It also sets l4_bali_blocked to false. The reason is stated as: "OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium." The moratorium rule in the same record blocks all Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent; this entry is not marked as caught by that block. For a foreign founder reading this record, the decisive point is simple: the national PMA door is open to the full 100%, and Bali is not marked as closed by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of military combat vehicles—tanks, armored personnel carriers, armored supply and recovery vehicles, amphibious military vehicles, remote-controlled tanks, and their armored hulls, turrets, doors, and protective plating.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Foreign shareholding in this activity is capped at 49%: without the Minister of Defence's approval, foreign shareholders can hold up to 49% of a PT PMA and the rest must be held by Indonesian shareholders. The cap is set by Perpres 49/2021, Lampiran III, entry #7, and the record notes a route above it — the approval of the Minister of Defence. Bali's moratorium does not block the activity: it reaches only low and medium-low risk lines, and this one sits above that band.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Kendaraan Tempur Militer (30400)? Nationally this carries PMA status: TERBATAS — capped at 49% foreign ownership, may exceed 49% with Menteri Pertahanan approval. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign defense contractor or heavy-industry entrepreneur with substantial capital and a clear connection to government or military supply chains, looking to establish a specialized manufacturing base with high-level approvals.

editorial.headline: Military Combat Vehicles, Treated as a National Industrial Activity
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30400 covers the manufacture and rebuilding of military combat vehicles — foreign shareholding is capped at 49%, and Bali's moratorium does not block registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30400 is a defence-manufacturing activity, not a general automotive line. The record defines it around the making of military war vehicles, whether already fitted with weapons or not, and around the parts that make those vehicles what they are: armoured bodies, turrets, doors, protective structures, armour plate identified as part of a military combat vehicle, and other military war vehicles. Its centre of gravity is the combat platform itself: tanks, armoured combat carriers for transporting people, armoured supply or recovery vehicles with cranes, armoured amphibious military vehicles, and remotely operated tanks.

The scope also reaches factory inspection and rebuilding of military war vehicles. That matters because this code is not limited to first manufacture from a blank production line; it includes industrial rebuilding activity at the factory level. At the same time, the record keeps the boundary tight. It is not the making of weapons and ammunition, not ordinary passenger cars or trucks with light or detachable armour, not military ships, not repair and maintenance of military combat vehicles, and not military drones. The editorial reading is therefore precise: this is the industrial manufacture and factory rebuilding of military combat vehicles and their identified vehicle parts.

On registration scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That does not make the business ordinary; it simply means the scale field does not reserve the activity for one size of enterprise. A founder reading this record should separate two ideas that are often blurred: the activity’s industrial seriousness comes from the scope, while the scale availability comes from the registration data. The code can be registered across all listed business scales, but the substance remains defence-vehicle manufacturing.

Foreign shareholding in this activity is capped at 49%. Perpres 49/2021, Lampiran III — the annex of business fields carrying specific requirements — lists it at entry #7, and the record notes a route above that ceiling: the approval of the Minister of Defence. Without that approval the 49% ceiling is the national position, and the remaining shares cannot be in foreign hands. Bali's moratorium does not block it. That moratorium suspends new PMA registration for activities assessed at low or medium-low risk, and this one is recorded above that band. What the record does limit is the foreign side of the shareholding — 49%, in Bali exactly as anywhere else in Indonesia — with the defence-ministry approval as the recorded route above it.
editorial.pullQuote: The constraint on this activity is not Bali's moratorium: it is a 49% ceiling on foreign shareholding, with the Minister of Defence's approval recorded as the route above it.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers the complete manufacturing and assembly of two- and three-wheeled motor vehicles—such as motorcycles, scooters, mopeds, electric bikes, and utility three-wheelers—using internal combustion or electric motors.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Foreign-owned (PMA) companies can register this high-risk activity in Bali, as it is not blocked by the moratorium. However, due to its medium-high risk classification, you must secure additional permits (environmental, location, and possibly industrial zoning) and your proposed business address will be strictly verified before approval.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Sepeda Motor Roda Dua dan Tiga (30911)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs planning to set up a motorcycle, scooter, or electric two/three-wheeler manufacturing facility in Indonesia.

editorial.headline: Two- and Three-Wheel Vehicle Manufacturing, Without a Bali Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30911 covers complete manufacturing and assembly of motorcycles, scooters, mopeds and similar two- or three-wheel vehicles, open nationally to full foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30911 is the industrial category for making and fully assembling two- and three-wheel motor vehicles. The record describes a broad manufacturing scope: motorcycles, mopeds, scooters, bemo, side-cars, skateboards and similar vehicles, whether driven by spark-ignition piston engines, rotary engines, or electric motors. It also includes the making and remaking of multipurpose two- and three-wheel motor vehicles. In plain English, this is not a retail, workshop, or distribution activity; it is the production-side category for building the vehicle itself.

The registration profile is unusually wide. The slim record opens this activity to every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the category is not framed only for a large industrial plant. A smaller domestic-scale manufacturer and a larger production operation both sit within the scale range stated in the record, provided the registered activity remains inside the manufacturing and complete-assembly scope described above.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership figure is 100%. There is no partial ceiling in this record, no local shareholder percentage stated, and no special ownership formula to infer. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the cited source for that national position. On the record provided, the correct national reading is therefore straightforward: KBLI 30911 is open for foreign-owned registration up to full foreign ownership.

The Bali reading is also cleaner than many founders expect. The record does include Bali’s moratorium rule: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” But this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, `l4_bali_blocked` is false, and the stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” So the honest national-vs-Bali picture is this: KBLI 30911 is nationally open to PMA, and the record does not block it for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium logic supplied. That is not a promise about site approvals, industrial suitability, or operational permits; it is simply the registration reading traceable to this slim record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 30911 is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

data.judul: Industri Komponen dan Perlengkapan Sepeda Motor Roda Dua dan Tiga
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan komponen dan suku cadang kendaraan bermotor roda dua dan tiga, seperti motor pembakaran dalam, suspensi, rem, kotak roda gigi, roda jalan, peredam suara, pipa knalpot, penutup spion, penutup bodi, dan sepatbor, termasuk inverter untuk kendaraan bermotor roda dua dan tiga.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup penyelesaian suku cadang dan komponen kendaraan bermotor roda dua dan roda tiga dari plastik, seperti pelapisan dengan logam atau zat pelapisan lainnya dan pengecatan.

editorial.headline: Motorcycle Component Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30912 covers the industrial making and finishing of parts for two- and three-wheeled motor vehicles, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked in Bali by the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30912 is a manufacturing code for the parts economy behind two- and three-wheeled motor vehicles. The record describes the making of components and spare parts such as internal combustion engines, suspension, brakes, gearboxes, road wheels, silencers, exhaust pipes, mirror covers, body covers, and fenders. It also expressly includes inverters for two- and three-wheeled motor vehicles, which places the activity not only in conventional motorcycle supply chains but also within the component base that can serve electric vehicle architecture.

The scope is not limited to forming or assembling hard mechanical parts. It also includes the finishing of plastic parts and components for two- and three-wheeled motor vehicles, including coating with metal or other coating substances and painting. That matters because the activity is broader than a narrow workshop label: it can cover component manufacturing and the surface treatment that turns parts into usable, finished inputs for vehicle production or replacement markets. The record’s own wording is industrial in character, but it is not confined to one material, one component, or one stage of finishing.

On scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, meaning the same activity can be registered across the full scale ladder recorded here. A small operator finishing plastic body covers sits inside the same activity description as a larger factory producing gearboxes, brakes, exhaust-related components, or inverters, provided the business remains within the component-and-spare-part scope stated in the record. The editorial point is simple: this code is about manufacturing and finishing motorcycle and three-wheeler components, not trading them, repairing them, or describing the finished vehicle itself.

The national foreign-investment picture is clean. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, so the foreign-ownership ceiling should be read as 100% at the national level. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, Bali is described by status and reason: l4_bali_status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, l4_bali_blocked is false, and the reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. For this code, however, the record does not mark Bali as blocked. The honest reading is therefore direct: nationally open, open up to 100% foreign ownership, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the data provided.

data.judul: Industri Sepeda dan Kursi Roda Termasuk Becak
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup pembuatan dan perakitan macam-macam sepeda dan becak, seperti sepeda tanpa motor, sepeda yang dilengkapi motor listrik dan sepeda lainnya, termasuk sepeda roda tiga (pengantar), tandem (sepeda gandeng), dan sepeda anak-anak baik roda dua maupun roda tiga, termasuk pembuatan kereta bayi, kendaraan difabel atau kursi roda untuk penyandang disabilitas baik bermotor maupun tidak, dan sepeda berbantuan listrik (yaitu, sepeda dengan motor bantu untuk bergerak). Kelompok ini juga mencakup sepeda multiguna tanpa motor.

editorial.headline: Bicycles, Wheelchairs and Becaks Are Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30921 covers the making and assembly of bicycles, becaks, baby carriages, wheelchairs and assisted electric bicycles, with a clear national opening but a Bali PMA block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30921 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label. The record places it around the making and assembly of bicycles and becaks: ordinary non-motor bicycles, electric-motor-equipped bicycles, other bicycles, delivery tricycles, tandem bicycles, and children's bicycles with either two or three wheels. It also includes baby carriages, multipurpose non-motor bicycles, disability vehicles and wheelchairs for people with disabilities, whether motorised or non-motorised, and electric-assisted bicycles, meaning bicycles that use an auxiliary motor to move.

That scope matters because it describes a practical, physical production category: workshops, factories or assembly operations that turn parts into mobility products. The activity is broad enough to cover everyday bicycles, family and child mobility products, disability-access vehicles, and becak-related production, but it remains anchored in making and assembling the items named in the record. A founder using this code would be positioning the business inside a defined industrial activity, rather than a general mobility, retail or transport concept.

At national level, the picture is straightforward. The record marks the PMA status as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. It is also open across the listed business scales: **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar**. In plain English, the national investment line says this activity is foreign-open, including full foreign ownership, and it is not confined in the record to a single scale band.

Bali is the hard turn. The same record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true and gives the Bali status as **Blocked (risk class)**. The reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is also explicit: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent).” So the honest reading is not that this activity is commercially impossible, or nationally closed, or subject to a different Bali ownership ceiling. It is nationally open for PMA up to 100%, but a foreign-owned registration in Bali is blocked by the Bali moratorium recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is that KBLI 30921 is nationally foreign-open up to 100%, but blocked for foreign-owned registration in Bali under the recorded moratorium.

editorial.headline: A Components Code That Bali Blocks for Foreign Registration
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30922 covers bicycle, wheelchair, baby-carriage, and becak equipment manufacturing, open nationally to all scales but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30922 is a manufacturing classification for the parts and accessories that make small mobility products work: bicycle frames, forks, rims, spokes, hubs, brakes, saddles, pedals, crank gears, and derailleur gears, alongside accessories for baby carriages, wheelchairs for persons with disabilities, and becak. Its practical centre is not the finished showroom object, but the component layer: the metal, mechanical, seating, braking, wheel, and valve-adjacent pieces that sit inside a wider mobility supply chain.

The record marks the activity as open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses, so it is not written as a scale-exclusive field. A small workshop making saddles or pedals, a mid-sized component supplier producing rims or spokes, and a larger industrial operator manufacturing wheel or braking assemblies all sit within the same basic activity description, provided the business remains inside the stated scope. The classification is therefore broad in scale, but still specific in substance: it is about making listed components and accessories for bicycles, baby carriages, wheelchairs, and becak.

Nationally, the investment signal is clear. The record gives PMA status as TERBUKA and sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is a foreign-open manufacturing code. A foreign investor looking only at the national PMA field would see no percentage cap below full ownership, and no scale closure in the scale field.

Bali changes the answer. The record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true, with the stated reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, so it is blocked by the Bali moratorium in May 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is wider still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest conclusion is therefore not that KBLI 30922 is nationally closed. It is nationally open, including up to 100% foreign ownership, but a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest answer is that KBLI 30922 is nationally foreign-open, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Small Transport Equipment, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 30990 covers makers of hand-propelled and animal-drawn transport equipment, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 30990 is a manufacturing classification for transport equipment that sits close to the ground, the workshop, and the everyday movement of goods or people. The record describes hand-propelled vehicles such as cargo trolleys, handcarts, sledges, shopping trolleys, strollers, wheelbarrows, carts, and other multipurpose equipment. It also includes animal-drawn vehicles: delman, lorries, racing carts, donkey-drawn carts, and hearses. In plain English, this is not about powered automotive manufacturing; it is about making the simpler physical vehicles used for pushing, pulling, carrying, and local movement.

The boundaries matter because the scope is practical but not unlimited. The record excludes work trucks used in industrial or factory settings, whether or not they carry lifting or transport equipment and whether or not they are self-propelled. It also excludes decorative restaurant carts, including dessert carts and food carts. That leaves KBLI 30990 with a clear identity: the fabrication of other transport equipment whose function is manual or animal-drawn movement, rather than factory handling equipment or hospitality furniture.

For registration scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification can describe anything from a small workshop producing handcarts or wheelbarrows to a larger manufacturer making a wider range of non-powered transport equipment. The business substance should still match the scope: the company should be able to show that its activity is manufacturing these forms of transport equipment, not merely trading them or using the code as a loose industrial label.

The national PMA picture is straightforward. According to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, the record classifies the activity as TERBUKA and sets a pma_max_asing of 100. For a foreign-owned setup, the honest reading is that the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Bali does not add a separate percentage in this record. Instead, the Bali field says OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; here, the record does not mark the code as blocked. So the conclusion is clean: nationally open, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium field provided.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Wood Furniture Manufacturing Is Nationally Open, but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 31011 covers wooden household and office furniture, open nationally to all business scales and full foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 31011 is the manufacturing category for furniture made from wood and wood-based panels. The record describes household and office furniture: tables, chairs, stools, beds, wardrobes, shelves, cabinets, room dividers, and similar items. The practical test is material-led. A piece belongs here when its frame is wood, or, where there is no frame, when wood is the largest component.

That makes this a production code rather than a retail or design label. It is for businesses that actually make the furniture, including items built from plywood, particle board, and other wood-panel materials named in the scope. The activity can serve domestic, office, and general furnishing demand, but the defining feature remains the manufacturing of the object itself: wooden furniture as a physical product.

On the national register, the picture is broad. The record marks the PMA status as **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. It is also open across every listed scale: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, Besar**. In plain English, the national classification does not reserve this activity only for local capital, nor does it limit the code to one business size. A foreign-owned company can read the national line as open.

Bali is the decisive exception. The same record marks **l4_bali_blocked** as true and gives the reason: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026**. The moratorium rule is broader still: **Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)**, with the source listed as **Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP**. So the honest reading is simple: nationally, this wood-furniture manufacturing code is foreign-open; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it as a PMA today. There is no separate Bali percentage in the record, and no Bali-side ownership cap to quote. The Bali issue is not a reduced ceiling. It is a registration block.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This KBLI covers the manufacturing of furniture made primarily from rattan and bamboo—think tables, chairs, beds, cabinets, shelves, and room dividers. It’s for workshops or artisans creating natural-fiber furniture, from simple pieces to more intricate designs.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership, meaning a PMA could normally be established anywhere in Indonesia. In Bali, however, a regional moratorium in place since 13 May 2026 blocks new PMA registrations for low and medium-low risk businesses, and rattan/bamboo furniture making falls into that blocked category. So, for now, a foreign-owned company cannot register for this activity in Bali.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Furnitur dari Rotan dan Bambu (31012)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign artisans, furniture designers, or eco-conscious brand owners who want to craft hand-made rattan and bamboo furniture, either for export or the local market—but they’ll need to wait out the Bali moratorium or set up in another part of Indonesia for the time being.

editorial.headline: Rattan and Bamboo Furniture, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers furniture made mainly from rattan and bamboo, open across all business scales nationally but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 31012 is a manufacturing classification for furniture whose main materials are rattan and bamboo. The record places tables, chairs, stools, beds, cupboards, racks, and room dividers inside its scope. In plain English, this is not a general furniture label and not a retail activity; it is the making of finished furniture where rattan and bamboo are the defining materials. That gives the code a clear industrial character: the activity is about production, shaping raw or semi-processed natural materials into domestic, hospitality, or workspace furniture.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can describe anything from a small workshop to a larger manufacturing operation. That breadth matters because rattan and bamboo furniture can sit at very different levels of formality and ambition: craft-led production, export-oriented manufacturing, or larger domestic supply. The code itself does not add extra thresholds, licences, capital figures, or timelines in the slim record. Its practical meaning must therefore stay close to the activity description and to the scale categories explicitly listed.

Nationally, the record marks the activity as **TERBUKA** for PMA and gives the foreign-ownership ceiling as **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. On the national reading alone, that is a clean foreign-investment signal: the code is open, and the recorded ceiling is full foreign ownership. But Bali is not a simple mirror of that national position. The Bali-side status is **Blocked (risk class)**, and the record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, which brings the activity under the Bali moratorium.

That is the honest national-vs-Bali picture. A foreign investor can read the national PMA line as open, but cannot treat Bali as available for this registration today under this record. The moratorium rule given here says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, and the cited source is Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the editorial conclusion is deliberately narrow: KBLI 31012 is a clearly defined rattan-and-bamboo furniture manufacturing activity, nationally open to PMA up to 100%, open across all listed business scales, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali because of the Bali risk-class moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this furniture activity is open to full foreign ownership, but the Bali record closes the registration route for PMA.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the manufacturing of furniture made primarily from plastic, including items like tables, chairs, shelving, benches, room dividers, cabinets, and beds. It’s light industrial production, not retail or wholesale of finished goods.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Industri Furnitur dari Plastik (31021)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur with production experience who wants to set up a plastic furniture factory in Indonesia, but currently must look outside Bali or wait for the moratorium to lift.

editorial.headline: Plastic Furniture Manufacturing With a Scope-Dependent Bali Gate
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers plastic-led furniture production, nationally open to PMA ownership, with Bali registration depending on the exact OSS risk scope declared.
editorial.body:
Plastic furniture manufacturing is a straightforward industrial activity, but the record gives it a sharper operational edge than the title alone suggests. Its scope is the making of furniture whose main material is plastic: tables, chairs, shelving, benches, room dividers, wardrobes, and beds. The emphasis is on production, not retailing, design consultancy, or a broad household-goods business. For a founder, the useful reading is therefore quite narrow: this code belongs to businesses that actually manufacture plastic-based furniture as their registered activity.

The registration picture is broad on business scale. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not framed only for large factories or only for small workshops. That matters because the same activity can plausibly describe a compact production setup as well as a larger industrial operation, provided the declared activity stays inside the recorded scope. The editorial discipline here is important: the record does not add special thresholds, equipment rules, location standards, tax treatment, or licence timelines, so none should be assumed from the title.

Nationally, the PMA signal is clean. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. If the business is being read only at the national investment-list level, there is no foreign-share cap in the slim record. The owner may still need to satisfy ordinary OSS and business-process requirements, but this record itself gives no extra numerical condition beyond the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali is the part that needs more care. The Bali status is recorded as Blocked (scope-dependent), and l4_bali_blocked is false, so this is not presented as an absolute island-wide rejection for every possible registration path. At the same time, the moratorium rule says Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source recorded as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The l4_bali_reason is therefore the decisive note: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity”. The honest conclusion is that national openness does not automatically make a Bali PMA registration routine; for this activity, the exact OSS-declared scope controls the practical answer.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this activity is fully foreign-open, but in Bali the decisive question is the exact OSS risk scope declared.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Metal Furniture Manufacturing, With a Bali Scope Check
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 31022 covers metal furniture production for homes and offices, nationally open to PMA but requiring careful Bali scope verification.
editorial.body:
KBLI 31022 is the industrial classification for making furniture whose main material is metal. The record describes household and office furniture: tables, chairs, racks, beds, cabinets, and room partitions. The useful word here is *manufacturing*. This is not a retail shelf label or a design-services description; it is the activity of producing metal furniture itself, with the finished articles ranging from domestic pieces to office fixtures.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** operators, so it is not framed only for a small workshop or only for a large factory. A founder reading this code should therefore think first about the actual activity being registered: whether the business is truly making metal furniture for home or office use, and whether the declared activity matches that production scope. The scope is compact, but it is not vague: the common thread is furniture, the main material is metal, and the end use includes both household and office settings.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with `pma_max_asing` at **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In plain English, the national record presents this activity as foreign-open, with a full foreign-ownership ceiling. There is no separate national cap, threshold, or capital condition in the slim record, and none should be read into it.

Bali is more delicate, but not because the record gives Bali its own percentage. It does not. The Bali field is **Blocked (scope-dependent)**, with `l4_bali_blocked` marked **false**. The reason says the OSS risk at scale **Besar** is low on some scopes but higher on others, and that PMA registration in Bali is possible only by declaring the higher-risk scope, with live OSS verification required for the exact activity. That sits beside the Bali moratorium rule: Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. So the honest conclusion is precise: this code is nationally open to PMA at 100%, but a Bali filing cannot be treated as automatic. For Bali, the declared scope and live OSS risk position carry the practical weight.
editorial.pullQuote: This code is nationally open at 100%, but a Bali filing cannot be treated as automatic.

editorial.headline: Other-Material Furniture, Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 31029 covers furniture made from materials outside the main named furniture categories, but Bali currently blocks PMA registration under its risk moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 31029 is for a particular corner of furniture manufacturing: furniture whose main material is not wood, rattan, bamboo, metal, plastic, or imitation goods. In practical terms, the record places tables, chairs, stools, beds, cupboards, shelving, and room partitions inside the field when they are made from these other materials. It also includes mattress and bedding-related production: mattress or bed complements, spring-filled or stuffed mattresses, mattresses filled with kapok or dacron, and uncoated plastic or rubber mattresses and similar goods.

The category is not limited to the familiar furniture showroom object. The scope also reaches furniture made from plant fibres, and even decorative restaurant carts such as dessert carts and food carts. That makes this a manufacturing code for makers working outside the dominant material families, rather than a general trade or retail description. The substance is production: making the furniture or mattress-type goods described in the record.

On the national investment reading, the code is open. The slim record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives the maximum foreign ownership figure as 100%, with the source stated as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It is also open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Taken nationally, that is a clean signal: the record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership, and it does not narrow the activity to only one business scale.

Bali is the harder part, and it changes the practical answer for a foreign-owned setup on the island. The record marks the Bali side as blocked, with the reason: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. So the honest conclusion is that KBLI 31029 may be nationally foreign-open, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side record provided here.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 31029 may be nationally foreign-open, but a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side record provided here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Gemstone Cutting, Polishing, and Colour Work Under KBLI 32111
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32111 covers the industrial craft of shaping, finishing, and altering gemstones, with full national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32111 is the classification for **Industri Permata**: the business of taking gemstones and similar materials through the physical processes that make them usable, saleable, or more refined. The record describes cutting, grinding, and smoothing gemstone materials, including jewellery diamonds, other jewellery-grade stones, batu aji or batu akik, and synthetic diamonds. It also includes the enhancement or alteration of gemstone colour through irradiation. In plain English, this is not retail jewellery, branding, or showroom activity; it is the industrial handling and transformation of precious or semi-precious stones themselves.

The scale profile is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** operators, so the classification can sit behind a small workshop as well as a larger manufacturing or processing operation. What matters editorially is the nature of the activity: precision work on stone, from basic finishing to more technical colour modification. A founder registering under this code should be able to explain the actual processing activity with that same clarity: what material is being worked on, what physical process is being performed, and whether the business is cutting, polishing, smoothing, or changing colour through the method named in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The PMA status is **TERBUKA**, and the maximum foreign ownership figure in the record is **100%**. There is no recorded national cap below full foreign ownership for this activity, and the source cited is **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. That makes the national reading straightforward: for a foreign-owned company, this activity is not closed on the face of the record, and the foreign stake is not capped below full ownership.

The Bali picture is also important, because the province applies a separate moratorium rule to PMA registrations: **Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)**. For this activity, however, the Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason given is exact: **OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium**. So the honest reading is not a hidden Bali percentage, partnership quota, or local ownership condition; none is in the record. The record simply marks this code as not blocked by the Bali moratorium, because at large scale its OSS risk position sits outside the Low and Medium-Low category that the moratorium blocks.
editorial.pullQuote: The Bali reading is not a hidden ownership cap; the record marks KBLI 32111 as not blocked by the moratorium because its large-scale OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi.

editorial.headline: Precious-Metal Jewellery Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the making of body-worn precious-metal jewellery, with national PMA openness set against a clear Bali registration block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32112 is about the manufacture of jewellery whose main material is precious metal: gold, platinum, and silver. The record describes articles worn on the body, on human clothing, or on pet animals, including rings, necklaces, bracelets, earrings, brooches, belts, buttons, and their parts and accessories. In plain English, this is the industrial activity behind precious-metal jewellery as a made product, not merely the trading or display of finished pieces.

The scope is specific enough to matter. The core test is the main material and the function of the article: precious metal, made into jewellery or related accessories. The record also draws one boundary around the activity by excluding imitation jewellery, so the editorial centre of this code remains genuine precious-metal manufacture rather than lookalike ornamentation. That distinction keeps the category anchored in production, material, and finished wearable form.

On business scale, the record is unusually broad. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it is not framed only as a large factory category or only as an artisan-sized activity. A small workshop making silver earrings and a larger operation producing gold rings both sit inside the same recorded scale envelope, as long as the activity remains within the described manufacture of precious-metal jewellery and its parts or accessories.

The national-versus-Bali picture is the decisive point. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But Bali is not nationally neutral here. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class), and the record marks it as blocked: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule is broader and clearer still: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is simple: this activity is foreign-open nationally, but a foreigner cannot register it as PMA in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.

editorial.headline: Precious Metal Objects Beyond Jewellery
editorial.standfirst: This KBLI covers precious-metal objects made for tables, offices, homes, awards, religious use, and related fittings, nationally open to PMA but blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 32113 is a manufacturing code for precious-metal goods that are valuable, material-led objects rather than jewellery.** The record describes articles whose main material is precious metal and that are not worn on the body, clothing, or pets. In practical terms, its scope runs through tableware and drinking ware, flat dishes, hollow containers, toiletry goods, household decorative objects, office or desk articles, trophies, medals, novelties, and religious-related goods, including their parts and accessories. The important boundary is not glamour or retail presentation; it is whether the business is making non-wearable precious-metal objects as industrial output.

That makes the code relevant to founders operating at very different production scales. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so the activity is not reserved only for large factories. A small workshop producing precious-metal desk pieces, a medium manufacturer making ceremonial objects, and a larger operation producing awards or table articles all sit inside the same stated scale range, as long as the activity remains the manufacture of these non-jewellery precious-metal goods. The word “Seluruh” in the scope reinforces that the described field is treated broadly within the listed activity rather than narrowed to one named product line.

Nationally, the PMA picture is straightforward: the record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100. For a foreign-owned company looking only at the national investment layer, that means the foreign-ownership ceiling shown in this record reaches 100%, with the source identified as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a special national licence, a capital threshold, a tax condition, or a timeline, so none should be read into the code. The national fact is simply that this activity is open to PMA at the stated ceiling.

Bali is the decisive exception. The Bali-side status is Blocked (risk class), and l4_bali_blocked is true, so the honest conclusion is that a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, which places it inside the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record is broader and firmer: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. That is not a separate Bali percentage, quota, or partnership formula; it is a registration block. So the code is nationally foreign-open, but for Bali PMA use, the record closes the door.
editorial.pullQuote: The code is nationally foreign-open, but for Bali PMA use, the record closes the door.

editorial.headline: Pearl Jewellery, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32114 covers pearl working and jewellery made from pearls as the main material; nationally it is open to PMA, but Bali’s record blocks PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32114 is a narrow, material-led activity: the working of pearls and the making of jewellery from pearls, or jewellery in which pearl is the main material. The record does not treat this as general accessories, fashion retail, or a broad jewellery trade. Its centre is the pearl itself: processing it, shaping it into jewellery, and producing pieces where pearl is the defining input. That gives the code a clear industrial character, even when the final object may feel delicate, decorative, or artisanal.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The activity is open across **Mikro**, **Kecil**, **Menengah**, and **Besar** scales, so the record can accommodate anything from a very small workshop to a larger manufacturing setup. That does not add extra facts about capital, facilities, staffing, or licensing; it simply means the slim record does not confine this activity to one size of operator. A founder reading this code should therefore focus first on the substance of the activity: pearl work and pearl-based jewellery production, not the commercial romance around the finished product.

Nationally, the PMA signal is clean. The record marks the activity as **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**, under **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. In plain English, the national field says this activity is foreign-open up to full foreign ownership. There is no lower percentage in the record, and no hidden national qualification is available to add. For a non-Indonesian investor looking only at the national PMA fields, the headline would be straightforward: pearl jewellery manufacturing under this code is open, and the foreign stake is not capped below full ownership.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks the Bali status as **Blocked (risk class)**, sets **l4_bali_blocked** to true, and explains that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, which is blocked by the Bali moratorium dated **May 13, 2026**. The moratorium rule in the record is blunt: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is not “open with a Bali percentage” or “open with a local partnership condition.” No Bali percentage exists in this record. The honest reading is sharper: nationally, KBLI 32114 is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today because the Bali-side record blocks it.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 32114 is open to PMA up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today because the Bali-side record blocks it.
