editorial.headline: Power Transmission And Distribution As Infrastructure Business
editorial.standfirst: This code is for operating the grids that move electricity from generation or storage into transmission, distribution, and final consumer supply.
editorial.body:
This activity is the business of moving electricity through the network, not merely trading it. Its center of gravity is the operation of transmission systems that carry power from generating facilities into distribution systems, or move electricity between systems through high-voltage and extra-high-voltage networks. The record defines those networks in concrete technical terms: high voltage from 35 kilovolts up to 245 kilovolts, and extra-high voltage above 245 kilovolts. It also includes the substations attached to those transmission systems, whether the electricity comes from the operator’s own production or from another producer.

The same code reaches downstream into distribution. It covers the operation of medium-voltage-and-below distribution systems, including lines, poles, meters, cables, and distribution substations, that deliver electricity received from generation facilities or transmission systems to final consumers. It also covers distribution through electricity networks, leasing or lending distribution networks, selling electricity to consumers where the operator owns the transmission or distribution assets, operating electricity capacity exchange and power transmission without intermediaries, and channeling stored electricity through the grid. In plain English, this is a network-asset activity: the company’s role is tied to the physical system that carries power.

For registration scale, the record is broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar business scales, so it is not framed only as a large-enterprise category in the slim record. That breadth should not be confused with a light operational profile. The scope itself describes infrastructure that may include high-voltage transmission, extra-high-voltage transmission, distribution equipment, substations, metering, and direct consumer supply using owned network assets. Founders should therefore read the scale availability as an OSS classification fact, not as a statement that every project under the code has the same practical footprint.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is straightforward: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a PMA foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not reverse that position in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is specific: at Besar scale, the OSS risk level is medium-high/high, so it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The moratorium described in the record blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently; this activity is outside that blocked category because of its recorded risk position. The honest reading is therefore clean: a foreign-owned company may register this activity nationally up to 100%, and the Bali-side note does not block PMA registration on the facts provided here.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is clean: this is a foreign-open electricity network activity, and the Bali-side note does not block PMA registration on the facts provided here.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.

editorial.headline: Electricity Storage With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35132 covers power storage, battery-swap infrastructure, and reconversion of stored energy, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35132 is the activity code for electricity storage in its practical, infrastructure-facing sense. Its scope is not simply warehousing batteries or trading equipment. The record describes the conversion of electrical energy into a form that can be stored, the storage of that energy, and the conversion back into electricity. In operational terms, that includes pump-storage facilities, compressed-air storage facilities, and battery storage facilities. It also expressly includes the operation of public electric-vehicle battery exchange stations, known as SPBKLU.

That makes the code relevant to founders working on the balancing layer of the power system: assets that absorb electricity, hold it, and return it when needed. It is also relevant to public EV battery-swap operators, because the activity is named directly inside the scope. The registration picture is broad by scale. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not framed only as a large-utility category. A small operator and a large infrastructure platform are both within the scale language of the record, provided the activity itself matches the storage, reconversion, or public battery-exchange scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain English, a foreign-owned company may register this activity nationally with full foreign ownership under the record’s cited investment framework. There is no lower national foreign-share cap in the slim record, and no additional capital threshold, licence, deadline, or operational condition is stated here. For this editorial, those unstated items stay unstated.

Bali is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all low and medium-low risk activities for PMA across the island, yet this record does not mark KBLI 35132 as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the Bali reason says that at Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, meaning medium-high to high risk, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: this is a nationally open, 100% foreign-ownership activity, and the Bali-side record does not close it to PMA registration. The caution is not a hidden Bali cap; it is the risk classification itself, which the record treats as the reason the moratorium does not apply.
editorial.pullQuote: This is a nationally open, 100% foreign-ownership activity, and the Bali-side record does not close it to PMA registration.

editorial.headline: Charging Infrastructure, Open Nationally and Viable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers standalone charging operations for electric mobility and everyday devices, with broad scale access and no Bali PMA moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35133 is the operating code for charging infrastructure rather than electricity generation itself. Its centre of gravity is practical: running facilities or stations where electric vehicles can recharge, including cars, motorcycles, scooters and electric bicycles, as well as public EV charging stations that are not integrated with a power plant. The scope also reaches smaller-format charging facilities for electrical equipment such as mobile phones and laptops. In plain terms, this is the business of making charging available and operational as a service point, without folding the activity into power-generation operations.

That distinction matters because the code is about the station or facility as an operating business. A founder using it should be looking at the day-to-day activity of keeping charging access available to users, whether the customer is an EV rider, a car owner, or someone charging portable equipment. The record does not add technical thresholds, licence names, site rules, grid requirements, tariff formulas or capital tests, so none should be read into it. The editorially useful point is narrower and clearer: this is a standalone charging-operation activity, and its official scope is broad enough to cover both vehicle charging and device-charging facilities.

On scale, the record is unusually open. Micro, small, medium and large enterprises are all listed as open to this activity, so the code is not reserved only for utility-scale or large-network operators. It can describe a modest facility as well as a bigger charging-station business, provided the registered activity remains within the stated scope. Nationally, the PMA status is open, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national reading in this record is clean: foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership.

The Bali position is also important, because the island applies a moratorium that blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA. This record, however, does not mark the activity as blocked in Bali. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at large scale is medium-high/high and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign founder, the honest conclusion is that this activity is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership and, on the Bali fields provided here, not blocked by the Bali moratorium today. Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembangkitan tenaga listrik, penyaluran tenaga listrik melalui jaringan transmisi dan/atau distribusi tenaga listrik, penyimpanan tenaga listrik, dan penjualan tenaga listrik kepada konsumen akhir yang dilaksanakan dalam satu kesatuan usaha.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup
- pengoperasian stasiun pengisian kendaraan listrik umum (SPKLU) yang terintegrasi dengan pembangkit.

editorial.headline: Integrated Electricity Supply With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35140 covers end-to-end electricity supply, from generation to final sale, and is nationally open to foreign ownership without a Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35140 is the integrated electricity-supply category: a single business framework for generating power, moving it through transmission and distribution networks, storing it, and selling it to final consumers. Its defining feature is unity of activity. The code is not merely about one isolated part of the electricity chain; it is about operating those linked functions as one business. The scope also expressly includes public electric-vehicle charging stations when they are integrated with generation, bringing charging infrastructure inside the same electricity-supply logic when the power source is part of the setup.

That breadth matters for founders because this is a serious operating category rather than a narrow service label. The record places it open across all business scales: micro, small, medium, and large. In practical editorial terms, the code can describe anything from a smaller integrated operation to a large-scale electricity business, provided the activity remains within the recorded scope of generation, network delivery, storage, and sale to end users. The scope text also names cross-border electricity network interconnection and cross-border electricity sales permits, so the category is written with both domestic integration and cross-border electricity activity in view.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clean. The activity is marked open, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no partial foreign cap in the national field: the record allows full foreign ownership at the national level. That is the first anchor for any PMA reading of this code, and it should not be softened into a vague “possibly open” conclusion.

Bali is also open for this code today under the record provided. The province’s moratorium blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide on a permanent basis, but KBLI 35140 is not blocked here: the Bali reason states that OSS risk at large scale is medium-high or high, so it is not caught by that moratorium. The honest national-versus-Bali picture is therefore unusually direct: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule. The Bali status still reads OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, which should be understood as an openness signal tied to a higher-risk OSS profile, not as a hidden ban.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest national-versus-Bali picture is unusually direct: nationally open to foreign ownership up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.

editorial.headline: Operating Indonesia’s Power Infrastructure, Without a Bali PMA Block
editorial.standfirst: This code covers third-party operation of electricity generation, transmission, and distribution facilities, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35151 is about the operation of electricity infrastructure by a party other than the facility owner. Its scope is operational, not ornamental: it covers facilities that generate electrical energy, the transmission system that carries power, and the distribution system that moves it onward. In plain English, this is the activity code for a business that runs electricity-supply installations across the generation, transmission, or distribution chain.

That makes the code relevant to operators whose work sits inside the practical machinery of power supply. The record does not describe construction, equipment sales, retail billing, or advisory work; it describes the **operation** of existing electricity-supply facilities and systems. That distinction matters because the code is framed around taking responsibility for running infrastructure: keeping a generating facility, transmission system, or distribution system in operation as the business activity being registered.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** businesses, so it is not confined to large enterprises in the national classification data provided here. A founder should read that as a scale eligibility statement only: the slim record says the code is open across those four scales, but it does not provide capital thresholds, licence procedures, technical prerequisites, or operating timelines. Those details cannot be inferred from the KBLI entry itself.

For foreign-owned company planning, the national position is clear. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a stated foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**, sourced to **Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021**. Bali does not reverse that position in this record. The province’s moratorium rule blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island, but this activity is marked **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** because the OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**. The practical conclusion is direct: on the data provided, KBLI 35151 is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: On the data provided, KBLI 35151 is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the moratorium.

editorial.headline: Operating Electrical Utilisation Installations, Without a Bali Moratorium Block
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers third-party operation of high-, medium-, and low-voltage electrical utilisation installations, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35152 is not about selling electricity or building a power project in the abstract. Its scope is narrower and more operational: the running of electrical utilisation installations by a party other than the facility owner or principal user. The record expressly covers high-voltage, medium-voltage, and low-voltage electrical utilisation installations, so the practical centre of gravity is the professional operation of systems that already sit on the consumption side of electricity use. In plain English, this is the activity of operating electrical facilities for another party, across the voltage bands named in the classification.

That makes the registration logic fairly broad, but still specific. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not reserved only for large operators. A small specialist operator and a larger technical services company can both sit within the scale language of the record, provided the registered activity remains the operation of electrical utilisation installations. The important editorial distinction is that scale openness does not expand the business scope: the code remains tied to operating those installations, not to every commercial activity connected to electricity.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clear. This activity holds TERBUKA PMA status, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so the clean national reading is that a foreign-owned company may register this activity up to full foreign ownership. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the consequence is not a mystery category or a restricted-equity setup; on the national investment list, this is an open activity with a full foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion under the moratorium data in this record. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, but this activity is marked l4_bali_blocked: false. The reason given is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. That is the honest Bali picture: this is not one of the foreign-owned registrations barred by the Bali moratorium in the supplied record. The right caution is therefore not to invent a local cap or hidden partnership condition, because none is stated here; the Bali-side signal is simply that the activity is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali picture is that this activity is not blocked by the moratorium in the supplied record.

editorial.headline: Electricity Support Services, Nationally Open but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35159 covers practical support work around electricity supply and use, yet Bali’s moratorium changes the PMA answer decisively.
editorial.body:
For a foreign-owned company looking at KBLI 35159, the first practical point is also the sharpest: this activity is nationally open, but it cannot be registered by PMA in Bali under the record provided. The national line is straightforward enough. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited presidential regulations. Bali, however, records the activity as blocked by risk class, because OSS treats the large-scale version as low or medium-low risk across every scope, bringing it inside the provincial moratorium.

Substantively, this code is about support services directly connected with the supply and use of electricity. The record points to work that sits around the electricity system rather than the generation or sale of power itself: electricity energy-conservation services, meter-reading services, billing services, and other directly related support activities. That makes it a practical code for operators whose business model is service-heavy: monitoring, conservation, usage administration, customer-facing utility support, and adjacent work tied to how electricity is consumed, measured, and managed.

The registration scale is broad. The record opens the activity to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** businesses, so the code is not reserved for only one size of operator. That breadth matters editorially because the Bali restriction is not framed as a narrow ownership cap or a company-size preference. It turns on the Bali moratorium rule in the record: Bali province blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. In the specific Bali reason, the decisive point is the large-scale OSS risk classification, not a separate Bali-side percentage or partnership condition.

The honest reading is therefore split, not ambiguous. Nationally, KBLI 35159 is open to foreign investment up to 100%, and the slim record gives no lower national cap. In Bali, the same activity is blocked for PMA registration because of the risk-class moratorium recorded from the Governor’s letter and the Bali reason dated May 13, 2026. A founder should read that as a location-specific stop sign: the national framework says foreign-open, but Bali’s PMA treatment for this activity is blocked under the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The national framework says foreign-open, but Bali’s PMA treatment for this activity is blocked under the record.

per_skala.scope_uraian: Kegiatan Usaha Pengolahan Minyak dan Gas Bumi untuk Komoditas Gas Bumi
persyaratan: Administrasi (Izin Usaha Sementara/ Tetap/Perpanjangan/ Penyesuaian) a. Surat Permohonan b. Daftar Penerima Manfaat c. Surat pernyataan tertulis diatas materai mengenai kesanggupan Badan Usaha

Teknis (Izin Usaha Sementara) a. Studi Kelayakan b. Kesepakatan Jual Beli Gas Bumi atau Kesepakatan kerjasama Pengolahan Gas Bumi dengan KKKS atau Badan Usaha Minyak dan Gas Bumi yang memiliki Izin Usaha sesuai peraturan perundang undangan yang berlaku c. Kesepakatan awal dengan pengguna akhir atau Badan Usaha Minyak dan Gas Bumi yang memiliki Izin Usaha sesuai peraturan perundang undangan yang berlaku d. Jaminan kecukupan pendanaan, yang dibuktikan dengan: 1) Laporan keuangan 3 (tiga) tahun terakhir 2) Dokumen kesepakatan dengan pihak lain untuk nominal tertentu atau 3) Surat keterangan dari bank umum yang berkedudukan di Indone-sia, yang menerangkan bahwa Badan Usaha memiliki kemampuan pendanaan dengan nominal tertentu e. Rencana pemanfaatan atau pembangunan sarana dan fasilitas Pengolahan Gas Bumi yang meliputi antara lain teknologi yang digu-nakan, dimensi, kapasitas, serta sarana dan fasilitas dan data titik koordinat berupa Data Georeference Standard Datum WGS84 f. SK Izin Usaha Sementara awal untuk permohonan perpanjangan Izin Usaha Sementara (apabila ada)

Teknis (Izin Usaha Tetap/ perpanjangan/ penyesuaian) a. Studi Kelayakan b. Dokumen pasokan berupa Penetapan alokasi gas bumi dari Menteri atau Perjanjian jual beli Gas Bumi (PJBG/ GSA) dengan Badan Usaha Niaga Minyak Gas Bumi atau Dokumen kerjasama Pengolahan gas bumi c. Dokumen kontrak jual beli dengan pengguna akhir atau Badan Usaha Niaga Gas Bumi/ LNG / LPG d. BA commisioning atau BA hasil pemeriksaan keselamatan instalasi dan peralatan yang ditandatangani oleh Petugas Direktorat Teknik dan Lingkungan Migas atau Persetujuan Layak Operasi (PLO) e. Badan Usaha yang melakukan kegiatan usaha pengolahan yang menghasilkan Bahan Bakar Minyak, Bahan Bakar Gas, dan/atau hasil olahan dapat memiliki laboratorium uji terakreditasi untuk melakukan pengujian terhadap mutu hasil olahan sesuai standar dan mutu yang ditetapkan Menteri atau dokumen kerjasama dengan Labotorium independent yang terakreditasi f. Bukti kepemilikan/ penguasaan atau kontrak sewa menyewa sarana dan fasilitas g. SK lzin Usaha Sementara dan/atau Izin Usaha/ Pe-nyesuaian/ Perpanjangannya (apabila ada)
kewajiban: Izin Usaha: a. Menjamin dan bertanggung jawab atas penggunaan peralatan, keakuratan, dan sistem alat ukur yang digunakan yang memenuhi standar sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan b. Menjamin mutu produk atau komoditas sesuai dengan standar yang ditetapkan oleh Direktur Jenderal c. Menjamin keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja, pengelolaan lingkungan hidup serta pengembangan masyarakat setempat d. Melaksanakan penugasan Menteri dalam rangka penyediaan cadangan bahan bakar binyak dan bahan bakar gas nasional e. Melaporkan dan/atau menyampaikan permohonan penyesuaian Izin Usaha apabila terdapat perubahan data administratif dan teknis f. Melaporkan kepada Menteri melalui Direktur Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi mengenai kegiatan usahanya setiap 1 (satu) bulan sekali atau sewaktu waktu apabila diperlukan g. Memenuhi perizinan yang ditetapkan oleh instansi terkait sesuai dengan ketentuan Peraturan perundang undangan h. Melaksanakan kewajiban yang tercantum dalam Izin Usaha

Rencana pemanfaatan atau pembangunan sarana dan fasilitas Pengolahan Gas Bumi yang meliputi antara lain teknologi yang digu-nakan, dimensi, kapasitas, serta sarana dan fasilitas dan data titik koordinat berupa Data Georeference Standard Datum WGS84 f. SK Izin Usaha Sementara awal untuk permohonan perpanjangan Izin Usaha Sementara (apabila ada)

Teknis (Izin Usaha Tetap/ perpanjangan/ penyesuaian) a. Studi Kelayakan b. Dokumen pasokan berupa Penetapan alokasi gas bumi dari Menteri atau Perjanjian jual beli Gas Bumi (PJBG/ GSA) dengan Badan Usaha Niaga Minyak Gas Bumi atau Dokumen kerjasama Pengolahan gas bumi c. Dokumen kontrak jual beli dengan pengguna akhir atau Badan Usaha Niaga Gas Bumi/ LNG / LPG d. BA commisioning atau BA hasil pemeriksaan keselamatan instalasi dan peralatan yang ditandatangani oleh Petugas Direktorat Teknik dan Lingkungan Migas atau Persetujuan Layak Operasi (PLO) e. Badan Usaha yang melakukan kegiatan usaha pengolahan yang menghasilkan Bahan Bakar Minyak, Bahan Bakar Gas, dan/atau hasil olahan dapat memiliki laboratorium uji terakreditasi untuk melakukan pengujian terhadap mutu hasil olahan sesuai standar dan mutu yang ditetapkan Menteri atau dokumen kerjasama dengan Labotorium independent yang terakreditasi f. Bukti kepemilikan/ penguasaan atau kontrak sewa menyewa sarana dan fasilitas g. SK lzin Usaha Sementara dan/atau Izin Usaha/ Pe-nyesuaian/ Perpanjangannya (apabila ada)
kewajiban: Izin Usaha: a. Menjamin dan bertanggung jawab atas penggunaan peralatan, keakuratan, dan sistem alat ukur yang digunakan yang memenuhi standar sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan b. Menjamin mutu produk atau komoditas sesuai dengan standar yang ditetapkan oleh Direktur Jenderal c. Menjamin keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja, pengelolaan lingkungan hidup serta pengembangan masyarakat setempat d. Melaksanakan penugasan Menteri dalam rangka penyediaan cadangan bahan bakar binyak dan bahan bakar gas nasional e. Melaporkan dan/atau menyampaikan permohonan penyesuaian Izin Usaha apabila terdapat perubahan data administratif dan teknis f. Penggunaan tenaga kerja asing dan tenaga kerja lokal f. editorial.headline: Gas Fuel Production, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35201 covers the making and upgrading of usable fuel gases, from natural gas and LPG to hydrogen and biogas, with full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35201 is a production code for fuel gas that can be used directly as fuel, with the processing work sitting at the centre of the definition. Its scope is not merely the holding or trading of gas. It covers the treatment and improvement of gas quality through purification, blending, and other processes, including gas derived from natural gas, liquid petroleum gas, coal carbonisation and gasification, and other gas sources. The record also places hydrogen fuel gas inside the same activity when it is produced through electrolysis, photolysis, thermochemical, biological, geological, or other methods, using either new and renewable energy sources or fossil energy sources.

The code also reaches into biogas where the fuel gas is generated from agricultural, plantation, livestock, or waste by-products, again with the important qualifier that the activity includes gas-quality improvement such as purification, blending, or other processing. In plain English, this is a code for businesses that make gas into a usable fuel product, whether the feedstock begins as natural gas, LPG-related gas, coal-derived gas, hydrogen pathways, or biogas from organic by-products and waste streams. The common thread is production and upgrading, not a loose association with the energy sector.

For registration scale, the record is unusually broad: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses. That means the activity is not framed only for industrial-scale operators in the slim record; it can also be selected by smaller businesses when the registered activity genuinely matches the production and processing scope. Founders should read that breadth carefully. The scale field tells you who may register the line, but it does not turn every energy-adjacent idea into this activity. The substance still has to be gas fuel production with the processing or quality-improvement character described in the scope.

The national foreign-investment position is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a block in the record. The province’s moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide, but the Bali reason here says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Medium-High/High, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest reading is therefore not a hidden closure story: nationally, this activity is fully foreign-open, and in Bali it is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked.

Menyampaikan laporan kepada Menteri energi dan sumber daya mineral melalui direktur jenderal minyak dan gas bumi mengenai pelaksanaan kegiatan usaha niaganya dan/atau terdapat perubahan terhadap data administrasi
Memenuhi dan mematuhi peraturan perundang undangan

persyaratan: Administrasi (Sementara/ Tetap/ Perpanjangan/ Penyesuaian) a. Surat Permohonan b. Daftar Penerima Manfaat/ Beneficial Ownership c. Persetujuan Kesesuaian Kegiatan Pemanfaatan Ruang atau Persetujuan Pemerintah/ instansi yang berwenang sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku atau pengelola kawasan yang berwenang mengenai lokasi untuk pembangunan fasilitas dan sarana Dalam hal fasilitas berupa floating Storage diperlukan Surat Persetujuan Penggunaan Permukaan Perairan untuk Lokasi Penyimpanan (penetapan Titik Koordinat) dari instansi yang berwenang d. Pernyataan tertulis di atas materai mengenai: 1) Kesanggupan memenuhi aspek keselamat-an, kesehatan kerja dan pengelolaan lingkungan hidup 2) Kesanggupan memenuhi kewajiban badan usaha 3) Kesediaan dilakukan audit kepatuhan terhadap ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan 4) Kesanggupan badan usaha menjamin dan bertanggung jawab bahwa sarana dan fasilitas yang dimiliki/ dikuasai layak beroperasi dan mampu dijalankan sesuai dengan kaidah keteknikan yang baik selama masa operasi 5) Badan usaha bebas dari konflik atau permasalahan hukum lainnya dengan pihak lain 6) Dokumen persyaratan dan ketera-ngan/ pernyataan yang diberikan adalah benar adanya dan apabila dikemudian hari terbukti tidak benar akan dicabut izin usahanya sesuai dengan peraturan perundang undangan 7) Kesanggupan menerima penunjukan dan penugasan dari Menteri untuk melaksanakan penyimpanan dalam rangka penyediaan cadangan penyangga energi dan pemenuhan kebutuhan minyak bumi di dalam negeri pada fasilitas dan sarana penyimpanan miliknya (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga minyak bumi) 8) Kesanggupan menerima penunjukan dan penugasan dari Menteri untuk melaksanakan penyimpanan dalam rangka penyediaan cadangan penyangga energi dan pemenuhan kebutuhan bahan bakar minyak di dalam negeri pada fasilitas dan sarana penyimpanan miliknya (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga bahan bakar minyak) 9) Surat pernyataan tertulis di atas materai mengenai kesanggupan badan usaha menerima penugasan dari Menteri untuk pemanfaatan secara bersama dengan pihak lain atas fasilitas yang dimiliki (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga gas bumi yang memiliki fasilitas jaringan distribusi) 10)Kesang-gupan badan usaha menerima penugasan dari Menteri untuk pemanfaatan secara bersama dengan pihak lain atas fasilitas penyimpanan dan/ atau pengangkutan LPG yang dimiliki dan/ atau dikuasai termasuk penyalurnya secara bersama dengan pihak lain (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga LPG) dan/ atau dikuasai termasuk penyalurnya secara bersama dengan pihak lain (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga LPG) 2 Teknis (Izin Usaha Sementara) a. Analisis kelayakan b. Kesepakatan jual beli Gas Bumi/ LNG/CNG dengan pemasok yang telah memiliki perizinan sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan c. Kesepakatan jual beli Gas Bumi dengan konsumen yang telah memiliki perizinan sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan d. Kesepakatan pengangkutan gas bumi dengan Badan Usaha yang telah mendapat Izin Usaha Pengangkutan Minyak dan Gas Bumi dan/atau Hak Khusus Ruas Transmisi dan/atau Wilayah Jaringan Distribusi, (jika ada) e. Salinan surat permohonan kepada Menteri mengenai usulan Pengembangan Jaringan Transmisi dan/atau Distribusi Gas Bumi untuk rencana pipa Gas Bumi yang akan dibangun pada wilayah yang belum ditetapkan sebagai Wilayah Jaringan Distribusi ke dalam Rencana Induk Gas Bumi Nasional beserta tanda terima f. Rencana pemanfaatan atau pembangunan sarana dan fasilitas Niaga Gas Bumi, yang meliputi antara lain teknologi yang digunakan, jalur, dimensi, kapasitas, right of way pipa serta sarana dan fasilitas selain pipa dan data titik koordinat berupa Data Georeference Standard Datum WGS84 g. Terhadap Pemegang Hak Khusus Wilayah Jaringan Distribusi, salinan dokumen penetapan pemenang lelang Hak Khusus Wilayah Jaringan Distribusi dari Badan Pengatur/ salinan dokumen penugasan Menteri untuk membangun dan mengoperasikan Wilayah Jaringan Distribusi dan/atau Wilayah Niaga Tertentu h. Analisis kelayakan usaha paling sedikit memuat: 1) Sumber pasokan dan calon konsumen 2) Neraca gas bumi 3) Spesifikasi gas bumi 4) Lokasi kegiatan usaha beserta data teknis sarana dan fasilitas beserta data titik koordinat berupa data georeference standard datum wgs84 (tamba-han baru belum ada di aplika-si) 5) Skema usaha dan rencana pengembangan usaha 6) Penggunaan tenaga kerja asing dan tenaga kerja lokal 7) Capaian tkdn dan 8) Harga beli gas bumi, komponen dan besaran harga jual gas bumi b. Dokumen pasokan berupa Penetapan alokasi gas bumi/LNG dari Menteri atau kontrak jual beli LNG/CNG dengan pemasok yang bukan kontraktor kontrak kerjasama hulu migas atau kontrak jual beli dengan BU Niaga gas bumi dengan skema interruptible sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku c. Kontrak jual beli Gas Bumi dengan konsumen akhir atau BU Pengolahan LNG atau BU niaga CNG atau BU niaga BBG atau BU niaga gas bumi dengan skema interruptible sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku d. Perjanjian pengangkutan gas bumi dengan badan usaha yang telah mendapat izin Usaha Pengangkutan dan/atau hak khusus ruas transmisi dan/atau wilayah jaringan distribusi, jika ada e. intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers transporting natural or artificial gas through pipeline networks—from high-pressure long-distance lines down to low-pressure local distribution—and selling it to end users. It also includes acting as a gas agent, operating commodity exchanges for gas, and managing transport capacity on behalf of other parties.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, however, the activity is classified as medium-high or high risk. The moratorium does not block it outright, but your application’s success will depend on the specific business address: local safety, spatial planning, and environmental requirements must be met, so a site-specific verification is essential.

editorial.headline: Gas Distribution Networks, Open Nationally and Workable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers networked gas distribution, trading through channels, and newer gas fuels, with full PMA ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
This activity is about gas moving through a network, not simply gas as a commodity sitting in a tank or traded on paper. Its scope reaches the distribution of natural and manufactured gas through extra-high-pressure networks above ten bar, high-pressure networks from four to ten bar, and medium-to-lower-pressure networks below four bar. The gas may come from the operator’s own production or from another producer, but the defining feature is delivery through a network to consumers or customers.

The scope is broader than utility-style delivery alone. It also covers the sale of gas to consumers through channels, gas agents trading through a distribution system operated by another party, and the operation of exchanges for gas-fuel commodities and transportation capacity. It is also written with newer fuel pathways in view: hydrogen fuel gas distributed through networks is included, whether produced by electrolysis, photolysis, thermochemical, biological, geological, or other methods, and whether the energy source is renewable, new energy, or fossil. Biogas and other gases distributed through networks also sit inside the frame. What falls outside is pipeline delivery carried out purely for a fee or compensation, where the business is carriage rather than this distribution activity.

For founders, the scale position is unusually broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, which means the classification is not reserved only for large infrastructure groups in the way a casual reading might suggest. A smaller operator, a mid-sized distributor, or a large network business may all find themselves inside this activity if the real business is distribution, trading through gas channels, agency trading through another operator’s system, or running the relevant exchange and capacity functions. The editorial discipline here is to follow the activity, not the ambition: the decisive question is whether the company is actually in networked gas distribution and the related trading or exchange functions described above.

The national foreign-investment position is clean. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a PMA ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity. Bali does not add a block on the record supplied here. The province’s moratorium blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, but this activity is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because, at Besar scale, OSS risk is medium-high or high; for that reason it is not blocked by the moratorium. The practical conclusion is direct: nationally it is foreign-open, and in Bali it is not marked as moratorium-blocked in this record.

editorial.headline: Steam, Hot Water and District Cooling Under KBLI 35301
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35301 is open to foreign ownership nationally and, on the record provided, is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35301 covers the production and distribution of steam, hot water and cold air. In practical terms, this is infrastructure for heat, energy and cooling: producing, collecting and distributing steam or hot water for heating, power generation and other uses, as well as producing and distributing chilled air. The scope also includes geothermal heat storage, which gives the code a clear place in thermal-energy systems rather than ordinary building services alone.

The record treats the activity as open across all listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity is not framed only as a large utility undertaking. A founder reading this code should understand it as covering the activity itself, whether the planned operation is modest or substantial, so long as it remains within the stated scope of producing, distributing or storing thermal energy in the forms described.

Nationally, the PMA position is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the slim record, and no extra capital figure, licence threshold or operating condition is supplied here. The national source identified for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, but the editorial point is simpler: on the record given, KBLI 35301 is foreign-open at the national level.

Bali does not add the usual moratorium problem on this record. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide on a permanent basis, but this activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason given is that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That classification means it is not blocked by the Bali moratorium in the record provided. The honest reading is therefore aligned nationally and in Bali: a foreign-owned company may register this activity, with the national ceiling recorded as 100%, and with Bali’s status recorded as not blocked rather than closed.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is aligned nationally and in Bali: KBLI 35301 is foreign-open and not blocked by the Bali moratorium on the record provided.

editorial.headline: Ice Production With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35302 covers ice and chilled-water production and distribution, nationally open to PMA and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35302 is a practical, infrastructure-facing activity: the production and distribution of cold water or ice water for cooling needs, together with the production of ice itself. In plain terms, it is the category for businesses making and moving cooling media and commercial ice products such as crystal ice, ice tubes, and ice cubes. The scope is not framed as a hospitality, retail, or food-service activity; its centre of gravity is production and distribution, with cooling demand as the underlying use case.

That distinction matters for founders because the registered activity should match the operating reality. A company producing ice at a dedicated facility, distributing ice water for cooling, or supplying formed ice products would read naturally within this scope. The record also makes the scale position unusually broad: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the code is not reserved only for large industrial operators; it can describe activity from smaller-scale production through to large-scale operations, provided the actual business remains inside the stated production-and-distribution scope.

Viewed nationally, there is nothing conditional about the foreign-investment stance. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a PMA structure, that means the national ceiling is 100% foreign ownership. There is no lower foreign-stake cap in the slim record, and none should be inferred. The clean national reading is therefore that this activity is foreign-open at the full stated ceiling.

Bali’s position is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali on a permanent, island-wide basis, according to the governor letter source in the record. This activity is not blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false, and the Bali reason says that at Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the moratorium does not catch it. The honest Bali conclusion is therefore not a hidden prohibition, but an open path under this record: KBLI 35302 is nationally open to PMA at 100%, and in Bali it is not blocked by the moratorium because the cited OSS risk position sits above the Low and Medium-Low band.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest Bali conclusion is therefore not a hidden prohibition, but an open path under this record.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers acting as a broker or sales agent for electricity that flows through a distribution system owned by others. It includes selling electricity tokens and negotiating capacity exchanges for transmission or distribution, but not generating or distributing power yourself.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, this activity is open to 100% foreign ownership in principle, as the national ban does not apply. However, it falls into a medium-high to high risk category, so registration is subject to stricter checks and your specific business address will be verified by local authorities before approval.

editorial.headline: Electricity Sales Intermediation Without Owning the Grid
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35401 is for electricity brokers and sales agents, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35401 sits in the commercial layer of the electricity market, not the physical one. Its subject is brokerage and agency work in electricity sales through a power distribution system operated by another party. In plain terms, this is the activity of selling, arranging, or intermediating electricity transactions where the registered business is not itself the operator of the distribution system. The record also brings electricity token sales into the same frame, which makes the code relevant to businesses working at the retail and agency end of electricity access rather than at the infrastructure-owning end.

The scope is broader than a simple point-of-sale activity. It also includes sales agency activity for electricity operations, and for the exchange of distribution and transmission capacity for electric power. That wording matters because it points to a market-facing intermediary role: the business may be involved in connecting demand, sales channels, operational rights, or capacity arrangements, while the underlying electricity system is operated by someone else. Just as important, the scope draws a boundary around what this is not. It does not cover storage, distribution, or the supply of electricity to users through a main system by a producer using its own system. The code is therefore best read as agency and brokerage around electricity sales, not ownership or operation of the core power supply chain.

The registration audience is unusually wide. The record states that the activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. It also expressly captures domestic electronic commerce operators and intermediary-service providers that are not exempt, as well as comparable operators based outside Indonesia's jurisdiction when they conduct electronic trading activity in Indonesia. The final scope line makes clear that the activity is not limited to those platform and intermediary categories, so a conventional non-platform sales agent can still sit within the same activity if its work matches the electricity brokerage or agency scope.

The national foreign-investment position is clean: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100 under the cited source, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the record gives no national foreign-share cap below full ownership. Bali is also workable on the information provided, but for a specific reason. The province's moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, yet this record says the OSS risk at Besar scale is Medium-High/High, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: a foreign investor is not barred from registering this activity in Bali by the Bali moratorium, while the national record treats the activity as fully open to foreign ownership.
editorial.pullQuote: This is the commercial agency layer of electricity sales, not ownership or operation of the power system itself.

data.judul: Aktivitas Broker dan Agen Penjualan Gas Alam
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan agen penjualan gas yang mengatur penjualan bahan bakar gas melalui sistem distribusi gas yang dioperasikan oleh pihak lain.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup
- kegiatan agen penjualan pertukaran kapasitas komoditas dan distribusi untuk bahan bakar gas.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- penyimpanan dan distribusi atau penyediaan gas alam kepada pengguna melalui sistem utama oleh produsen (milik sendiri), lihat golongan 352;
- aktivitas jasa intermediasi untuk pengangkutan bahan bakar gas, lihat subgolongan 5231.

editorial.headline: Natural Gas Sales Agency, Without Owning the Pipes
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 35402 covers gas-sales agents that arrange fuel-gas sales through distribution systems operated by other parties, with national PMA access and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 35402 is not a natural-gas producer, storage operator, pipeline owner, or direct supplier through a principal system. Its center of gravity is agency work: arranging the sale of gas fuel through a gas distribution system run by someone else. In practical terms, this is the commercial layer around distribution rather than the physical operation of the gas network itself. The scope also reaches agents involved in the sale of commodity-capacity exchange and distribution arrangements for gas fuel, which places the activity in the world of organized gas-market intermediation rather than infrastructure ownership.

That distinction matters because the registration is built around the broker or sales-agent role. The slim record also brings electronic commerce into the frame: domestic PPMSE and intermediary-platform operators that are not exempted, as well as foreign-domiciled PPMSE and intermediary-platform operators conducting PMSE business in Indonesia, are expressly mentioned. The wording then makes clear that the activity is not limited to those electronic-commerce operators. The code can sit with micro, small, medium, and large-scale businesses, so the scale door is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open categories in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment reading is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. That means the record does not impose a national foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the cited basis for that national position. For a foreign-owned setup, the clean national point is therefore not ambiguity but access: this activity is open to PMA at the recorded ceiling, subject only to facts actually stated in the slim record.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion on the facts provided. The province’s moratorium rule is severe in general: it blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, according to the listed governor letter source. But this particular record is marked as not blocked in Bali. The reason is specific: at Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, or Medium-High/High, so it is not caught by that moratorium block. The honest national-versus-Bali picture is therefore unusually clean: nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali not blocked by the stated PMA moratorium because the recorded risk position sits above the blocked Low and Medium-Low band.

editorial.headline: Drinking Water Systems, From Source to Customer
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 36001 covers the managed capture, treatment, and sale of drinking water through piped and non-piped distribution systems.
editorial.body:
KBLI 36001 is the business of turning raw water into drinking water and getting it to customers. Its scope begins at the source: surface water, groundwater, seawater, and similar inputs may be collected or drawn, then processed into drinking water. The activity does not stop at treatment. It also covers distribution, whether through a pipe network or through non-piped channels such as tank trucks, provided those trucks remain under the same administrative management as the drinking-water company.

The code is therefore broader than a simple utility label. It includes direct water intake from the sea, direct supply from a water terminal, and delivery by pipe or managed tank truck to paying customers. The customer base named in the record is wide: households, government institutions and bodies, social bodies, state-owned enterprises, and private businesses such as hotels, processing industries, and shops. What unifies these cases is not the type of buyer, but the controlled chain from capture or terminal supply through treatment and distribution for sale.

Registration is open across the full scale range stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because this activity can describe very different operating footprints, from a smaller local undertaking to a large-scale water provider. The scale does not change the core character of the code: it remains about managed drinking-water provision to consumers or subscribers. The record also makes clear that, nationally, the PMA position is open. With a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, a foreign-owned company is not capped below full ownership under the PMA field supplied here.

Bali’s position is also clear, and it is not a silent blocker. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the activity is not blocked by the island-wide moratorium because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, permanently, but this activity is marked outside that block. The honest reading is therefore straightforward: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the Bali-side reason supplied.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is straightforward: nationally open to PMA up to 100%, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the Bali-side reason supplied.

editorial.headline: Raw Water Supply With a Scope-Dependent Bali Gate
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers raw-water storage and delivery for industry, power generation, irrigation networks, and certain fixed marine-water uses, with Bali PMA registration depending on exact scope.
editorial.body:
KBLI 36002 is about raw water before it becomes a downstream service or another commercial product. Its core field is the provision of raw water for industrial use, power generation, and other non-domestic needs, including activity carried out inside forest areas. It also reaches the management of irrigation networks, so the category is not limited to pipes and tanks; it can include the organised control of water movement through a larger supply system.

The scope is deliberately specific about what belongs here and what does not. It includes the procurement and channeling of raw seawater where marine space is used on a fixed basis for at least thirty days, whether or not the water is processed, when the purpose is industry, power generation, or similar uses. It also includes storage and distribution of raw water from surface water other than seawater. But it does not cover irrigation services such as agricultural spraying, and it does not cover the use of raw water as an aquaculture medium when that use is part of an integrated fish-farming activity.

Nationally, the record is straightforward: this activity is marked open to PMA, with foreign ownership shown at 100%. The same record shows it open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which means the registration question is not confined to large infrastructure sponsors. A small operator, a medium-scale supplier, or a larger water-infrastructure company would all read the national position from the same baseline: the activity is open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling shown in the record is full foreign ownership.

Bali is where the reading becomes more exacting. The Bali status is scope-dependent rather than a flat block, and the record says it is not blocked outright. The reason is that, at Besar scale, OSS risk can be low for some scopes but higher for others. Bali’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently, so a foreign-owned registration in Bali depends on declaring an exact activity scope that carries the higher-risk pathway in OSS. In practical terms, the honest position is this: KBLI 36002 may be nationally open, but in Bali a PMA filing cannot be treated as automatically available across the whole description. It is registrable only if the declared scope places the activity outside the Low or Medium-Low risk route caught by the Bali moratorium, and that must be checked live in OSS against the exact activity being registered.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 36002 may be nationally open, but in Bali a PMA filing cannot be treated as automatically available across the whole description.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Infrastructure Behind Water Supply
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 36003 covers practical support work around water provision, from distribution-network use to billing and direct water distribution.
editorial.body:
KBLI 36003 is not the headline act of water production; it is the operational layer that keeps water provision functioning around the edges. The activity covers work directly connected with supplying water, including the rental or lending of water distribution networks, billing, and other support activities tied to the provision of water. Its scope also reaches a very practical end of the market: water distribution carried out by individuals, including sellers using shoulder poles, pushcarts, or tanker vehicles.

That breadth matters because this code sits across very different business realities. A company may be formalising support services around a distribution network or customer billing process. A smaller operator may be registering direct water distribution as a personal or micro-scale activity. The record opens the code across **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales, so it is not framed only for large infrastructure players. The common thread is proximity to water supply itself: the activity must be directly related to provision, rather than a detached administrative service.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. The code is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited presidential-regulation source. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to full foreign ownership. There is no partial cap in the slim record, so there is no basis here for inventing one. For founders, the national reading is therefore straightforward: the activity can be used for a PMA structure at the recorded ceiling, provided the business being registered genuinely fits the water-supply support scope described above.

Bali is also not blocked in this record, but the reason needs to be read carefully. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA registration island-wide on a permanent basis; this activity is recorded on the Bali side as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** because it is medium-high risk, and therefore not blocked by that moratorium. That is a meaningful green light, not a guarantee that every address or implementation detail will pass untouched. The record itself says to verify per address, so the honest conclusion is narrow but useful: KBLI 36003 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and in Bali it is not stopped by the stated PMA moratorium, subject to address-level verification.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 36003 is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and in Bali it is not stopped by the stated PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: Wastewater Collection With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the collection and transport of wastewater, and it remains nationally open to foreign ownership while not being blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
**37001 is the practical infrastructure activity behind wastewater collection.** It covers the collection and transport of wastewater from its source, including households and industrial units, through wastewater disposal networks, wastewater collectors, and other transport facilities such as waste or sewage vehicles. The scope also reaches the suction and cleaning of latrine wells, septic tanks, and waste pits, as well as wastewater collected from chemical toilets, including portable toilets and toilets on aircraft or trains.

The code is broad enough to include both non-hazardous domestic wastewater collection and transport, and hazardous domestic wastewater collection and transport. That breadth matters editorially: this is not a narrow maintenance label. It describes the operating layer that moves wastewater out of buildings, temporary sanitation systems, and industrial or domestic sources into the relevant collection and transport chain. The common thread is not the type of client, but the activity itself: collecting and carrying wastewater from defined sources through a waste-handling route.

For company formation, the scale position is unusually straightforward. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Nationally, it is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national record does not impose a foreign share cap below full ownership for this activity. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the record gives no separate capital threshold, special licence detail, or timing rule to add beyond that.

Bali is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, permanently, under the stated governor-letter source. This activity is not blocked in Bali because the record identifies the OSS risk at Besar scale as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside that moratorium block. The honest reading is therefore not a hidden prohibition, but a clean national-and-Bali alignment: foreign investors can read the national PMA position as open, and the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is therefore not a hidden prohibition, but a clean national-and-Bali alignment.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Wastewater Treatment That Stays Open in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 37002 covers wastewater and septage treatment facilities, nationally open to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 37002 is the practical infrastructure code for handling wastewater after it leaves homes, buildings, and service networks. Its scope covers the operation of wastewater treatment facilities, the treatment of wastewater through channels, and the cleaning of wastewater drains and their disposal channels. In plain English, this is not a general environmental-services label; it is about running the systems that receive, process, clean, and discharge wastewater safely through dedicated facilities and lines.

The record also brings two facility types into the frame. First, it includes domestic wastewater treatment plants, including their supporting facilities, with capacity serving up to 20,000 per day. Second, it includes septage sludge treatment plants, again with supporting facilities, where capacity is below 50 cubic metres per day. Those details matter because they keep the activity anchored in operational treatment infrastructure, rather than consultancy, trading, construction, or broad sanitation work.

For company formation, the scale picture is unusually broad. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the record does not reserve it only for a large operator. A smaller registered undertaking and a larger infrastructure operator can both sit within the same activity definition, provided the actual business is the operation, treatment, and cleaning work described in the scope. The key is fidelity to the activity: founders should read this as a code for wastewater-processing operations and their supporting facility context, not as a catch-all for every water or drainage-related business.

The national-versus-Bali position is also clear. Nationally, the code is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100% under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not block it under the province-wide moratorium described in the record. The reason is specific: at Besar scale, the OSS risk level is medium-high or high, so the Bali PMA moratorium that blocks low and medium-low risk activities does not apply here. The honest reading is therefore not a hidden prohibition, and not a Bali-only cap. For this slim record, KBLI 37002 is foreign-open nationally and remains available for PMA registration in Bali under the stated risk-based moratorium logic.

l4_bali.reason: No foreign-ownership reservation or cap for this activity was located in Perpres 10/2021 as amended by Perpres 49/2021 (Lampiran I, II, III) or in its closed list — so this is not a national 0% finding. OSS currently publishes licensing rows for this code only at Mikro, Kecil and Menengah scale, while a PT PMA is by law an Usaha Besar that must invest more than IDR 10 billion per KBLI per location (Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 7(1); Permen Investasi/BKPM 5/2025 Pasal 26(1)–(2)): whether OSS will license this code for a PT PMA must be confirmed in OSS; a scale missing from the licensing rules does not by itself restrict the activity (Permen Investasi/BKPM 5/2025 Pasal 8(6)). The only waste-sector Lampiran II row (38302) is a partnership (kemitraan) row, which does not bar a PT PMA. In Bali we flag this code as blocked as a precaution, not because a closure naming it was located. The Governor of Bali asked BKPM (letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, 28 Jan 2026) to close OSS to PT PMA in the Rendah and Menengah Rendah risk tiers, which include this code (Menengah Rendah). The provincial government reports that the closure applied from the third week of May 2026 covers 18 listed KBLI, and under the official BPS KBLI 2020→2025 crosswalk this code is not among them. Confirm the current OSS status in Bali before relying on this flag either way.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the collection and gathering of non-hazardous solid waste—from household trash, recyclable materials, used cooking oil, and animal/plant waste to construction and demolition debris. It’s the hands-on front end of waste recovery, often involving bins, containers, and public space clean-up, before any treatment or recycling.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, the Positive Investment List opens this KBLI to 100% foreign ownership, and no ownership restriction on non-hazardous waste collection was located in the investment annexes or in any sectoral instrument read — but a PT PMA still cannot register it at a Bali address today: the island-wide provincial moratorium in force since 13 May 2026 (Governor's letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP) blocks every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, and this activity is classified Medium-Low risk. Outside Bali the picture is different: nothing in the national rules bars a PT PMA from this KBLI, so the block follows the Bali address rather than the activity. In Bali the block is reinforced by the provincial moratorium on Low and Medium-Low-risk PMA registrations (effective from 13 May 2026).
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Pengumpulan Limbah atau Sampah Tidak Berbahaya (38110)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs building a scalable, eco-driven waste-collection and sorting business who are willing to launch outside Bali or wait until the moratorium is lifted.

editorial.headline: Non-Hazardous Waste Collection: Open Nationally, Blocked In Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers local collection of non-hazardous waste and recyclables, open nationally to foreign ownership yet blocked for PT PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 38110 is the business of collecting non-hazardous waste at the local level. Its centre of gravity is practical, municipal, and operational: household and business waste gathered through bins, containers, and similar systems; recyclable materials whether already separated or not; non-hazardous waste from animal or plant sources; used cooking oil and fats; rubbish from public places; construction and demolition waste; rubble and debris; factory waste; and the operation of transfer facilities for non-hazardous waste. The scope is collection and transfer, not wastewater, hazardous waste, permanent disposal or storage, or the operation of sorting facilities for recoverable materials.

The record also gives this activity a distinctly community-enterprise profile. It is open at Mikro, Kecil, and Menengah scales, and the Indonesian scope names Bank Sampah Induk, entrepreneurs, self-employed operators, and sociopreneurs as actors, including conventional businesses and digital-platform models. In plain English, this is the code for the front line of non-hazardous waste logistics: the people and systems that aggregate waste before later processing, disposal, or recovery happens elsewhere. It can be small, local, and service-led, but it can also sit inside a more organised platform or social-enterprise model, provided the activity remains within the collection scope.

Nationally, the investment signal is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national position shown here is open to foreign ownership up to the full recorded ceiling. There is no lower national cap in this slim record, and no separate national condition should be read into it. For a founder reading only the national line, this looks like a clean opening for a foreign-owned structure.

Bali changes the practical answer. The Bali status is closed to PMA, and the reason is provincial rather than sectoral: Bali's moratorium suspends PMA registration island-wide for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, and non-hazardous waste collection is classified Medium-Low risk. Nationally the activity stays foreign-open — what closes the door is the address, not the business. The Bali moratorium adds a second, broader barrier: Bali blocks Low and Medium-Low risk PMA registration island-wide on a permanent basis under the cited governor letter. So the honest reading is narrow but important: nationally this activity is foreign-open up to 100%, but a foreigner cannot register it as a PT PMA in Bali today.

data.judul: Pengumpulan Limbah Berbahaya Selain Limbah Radiokatif
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup pengumpulan limbah yang berbahaya serta sampah spesifik yang berbahaya nonradioaktif, yaitu bahan yang mudah meledak, bahan yang mudah teroksidasi, bahan yang mudah terbakar, bahan beracun, iritan, karsinogenik, korosif, bahan yang dapat menyebabkan infeksi, dan substansi dan preparat lainnya yang berbahaya untuk kesehatan manusia dan lingkungan. Kegiatan ini juga dapat mencakup identifikasi, penanganan, pengemasan dan pelabelan limbah berbahaya dan sampah spesifik yang berbahaya nonradioaktif untuk tujuan pengangkutan.
Kelompok ini mencakup
- pengumpulan limbah berbahaya dan sampah spesifik berbahaya, seperti minyak bekas pakai dari kapal atau bengkel, sampah biologis yang berbahaya (bio-hazardous), aki dan baterai bekas pakai, limbah berbahaya yang berasal dari hewan, obat-obatan yang sudah kedaluwarsa;
- pengoperasian fasilitas pemindahan limbah untuk limbah berbahaya nonradioaktif.

editorial.headline: Hazardous Waste Collection With a Bali Scope Test
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to foreign ownership, but Bali registration turns on the exact declared scope and OSS risk treatment.
editorial.body:
This activity is the organised collection of non-radioactive hazardous waste and specific hazardous waste. The record describes materials that may explode, oxidise, burn, poison, irritate, corrode, cause cancer, transmit infection, or otherwise endanger human health and the environment. Its practical field is not ordinary rubbish collection; it is the front end of a controlled waste chain, where the collection process may include identifying, handling, packaging, and labelling hazardous waste so it can be transported.

The examples in the scope make the activity concrete. It includes used oil from ships or workshops, bio-hazardous waste, used batteries and accumulators, hazardous waste from animals, and expired medicines. It also includes the operation of transfer facilities for non-radioactive hazardous waste. The record further names the collection of waste containing B3 and/or B3 waste from households at facilities for managing specific waste, as well as B3 waste collection. In plain English, this is the classification for businesses whose work begins where hazardous materials are gathered, secured, and prepared for movement rather than left unmanaged at the source.

At national level, the foreign-investment position is clear. The activity is marked open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The scale access is also broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all listed as open. That matters because the record does not reserve the activity to a single size of operator. A founder reading this nationally would see a hazardous-waste collection activity that can be registered across the full stated scale range, including by a foreign-owned company up to the stated ceiling.

Bali needs a more careful reading. The Bali status is Blocked (scope-dependent), while the blocked flag is false. That means the record does not treat this as categorically closed in Bali, but it also does not give a simple island-wide green light. The reason says OSS risk at Besar scale is low for some scopes and higher for others, and that PMA registration in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope, with live OSS verification required for the exact activity. The underlying Bali rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province on a permanent basis. So the honest position is this: nationally, the activity is open up to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, a PMA setup depends on the precise declared scope and its OSS risk treatment, not merely on the broad title of hazardous-waste collection.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, the activity is open up to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, a PMA setup depends on the precise declared scope and its OSS risk treatment.

It’s a tightly regulated environmental service for hazardous nuclear or medical byproducts.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: This 2025 code is specifically radioactive-waste collection, newly separated from generic hazardous-waste collection. editorial.headline: Radioactive Waste Collection Is Nationally Open, but Closed to Private and PMA Capital
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 38122 covers the controlled collection and transfer preparation of radioactive waste, yet a sectoral closure reserves it to the State (BUMN) and BAPETEN, closed to PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 38122 is a narrow, technical activity: the collection of radioactive waste. Its scope is not ordinary waste handling in a loose commercial sense. The activity may include identifying the radioactive waste, handling it, packaging it, and labelling it before it moves onward. It also includes transporting that waste to a waste manager. In practical registration language, this is the code for operators whose role begins at collection and controlled preparation, and extends to the movement of the material toward an authorised waste-management party.

Our records file KBLI 38122 as **TERBUKA** for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%**, across **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** scales — the baseline classification applied when the national investment list carries no specific entry for this code. That baseline is a default fill, not a recorded permission, and on its own it does not make the activity open to foreign capital. As the next section shows, a separate and more specific rule closes it outright.

That default classification does not survive contact with the rule that actually governs this activity. Radioactive-waste collection is a strategic sector reserved to the State through BUMN and BAPETEN, and closed to private capital and PMA capital. This is not a tourism moratorium or a soft local preference; it is a national sectoral closure, so the classification above never actually opens the door. The honest conclusion is therefore blunt: a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity anywhere in Indonesia today.

There is also a wider Bali rule in the record: the province blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, under the cited governor’s letter. For this activity, though, that rule is beside the point: the State reservation to BUMN and BAPETEN closes the activity to private and foreign capital regardless of risk scale, business size, or shareholding structure. For founders, the usable distinction is simple: this is a sector the State keeps for itself nationwide, not a Bali-specific restriction that a company might sidestep by registering elsewhere in Indonesia.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is real, but it does not override the sectoral closure recorded here.
