intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers support services for water transportation — everything from navigation and berthing assistance, lighthouse operations, and vessel cargo surveys to ship-to-ship cargo transfers, managing floating production/storage/offloading units, and maintaining waterway infrastructure. It’s the hands-on, behind-the-scenes work that keeps ports and waterways running, but excludes construction or dredging.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, however, the local risk classification is medium-high to high, so while the activity is not blocked by the general moratorium, you will face increased scrutiny. Expect a more rigorous check on your intended business address and possibly supplementary permits before your license can be issued.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Terkait Transportasi Perairan Lainnya (52229)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs providing maritime logistics, port support, floating storage/offloading operations, or waterway maintenance — typically those operating near a harbor or requiring direct water access.

editorial.headline: The Waterway Work That Keeps Maritime Routes Functioning
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans navigation, waterways and specialised vessel support, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA block under the recorded moratorium.
editorial.body:
Waterway support is the practical substance of this activity: services that enable vessels to navigate, sail and berth, rather than the movement of goods itself. Its field includes navigation and shipping services, lighthouse activity, the operation of waterways and related routes, and river-route information. It also reaches the transfer of cargo between large and small vessels, ship-cargo surveys, winter storage of vessels and maintenance work on waterway infrastructure. The scope further expressly includes operating floating production, storage and offloading vessels and floating storage and offloading vessels, rental of marine transport equipment or related-service equipment, and underwater work.

That breadth does not make every maritime undertaking part of the same activity. The stated perimeter excludes construction and dredging of waterways; construction of underwater cables or pipelines; cargo handling through loading and unloading; recreational or tourist marina-berth operations; and ship-crew recruitment services. The focus is instead on the operational services expressly named: keeping water routes functional, providing information and navigation-related support, conducting specified surveys and transfers, or carrying out the other listed work.

The code is open to registration at every listed enterprise scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. This is not a partial foreign-share arrangement. The recorded ceiling permits foreign investors to hold up to the entire stake nationally for this activity. That national position is tied to the stated source, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse this national position through the island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium recorded here. That measure blocks all activities classified Low or Medium-Low risk for PMA. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and its stated OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali result is direct: it is not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign-owned structure, the Bali picture is therefore not a concealed local prohibition but continued availability for PMA registration, with its higher-risk standing at the Besar scale explaining why the moratorium does not close it.

editorial.headline: Airport Operations Begin Where the Runway Meets the Terminal
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the infrastructure and services that make aircraft movements, passenger terminals, and airport safety functions work as one system.
editorial.body:
Airport operations are more than a terminal building or a stretch of runway. This activity covers services for aircraft and passengers: providing or developing facilities for landing, take-off, manoeuvring, parking and aircraft storage; aircraft hangars; and the infrastructure found on runways, taxiways and aprons. Its scope also includes aircraft accident handling and firefighting, alongside passenger-terminal facilities such as aviobridges and departure check-in counters. In practical terms, it is the operational fabric that supports both the movement of aircraft and the passage of passengers through an airport.

The activity is open to businesses at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. That breadth matters because the code describes a field with several distinct operational elements, from aircraft-side facilities to passenger-service infrastructure. What unifies them is not a particular building or piece of equipment, but the provision of airport services: the facilities and functions required for aircraft operations, safety response and terminal use.

At the national level, the activity remains open to foreign investment, allowing foreign ownership of up to 100%. The record therefore presents no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this code. Its stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the activity at national level, the essential point is straightforward: this is an open PMA activity under the stated foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali requires a more precise reading, but not a pessimistic one. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. That does not make the activity casual or automatic; it means the record does not place it inside Bali’s moratorium category. For an airport-services business considering Bali, the national openness remains meaningful, while the relevant Bali distinction is the activity’s higher risk position at Besar scale rather than a moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not place this activity inside its PMA moratorium category; its decisive distinction is the higher risk position at Besar scale.

editorial.headline: The Operating System of Air Navigation
editorial.standfirst: A clear reading of this aviation-navigation activity, its all-scale availability, and why Bali’s PMA moratorium does not block it—while address verification still matters.
editorial.body:
Flight navigation is the connective operating layer that keeps aircraft movements informed, coordinated and supported. This activity covers air traffic services: air traffic guidance, flight information and alerting; aeronautical telecommunications, including fixed and mobile aeronautical systems and aeronautical radio navigation; and aeronautical information services. Its defined information work includes aeronautical information and flight charts, publication and dissemination of notices to airmen (NOTAM), and airport aeronautical information. Aviation meteorological information and search-and-rescue information are part of the same scope, placing operational information alongside communications and navigation rather than treating any one of them in isolation.

The definition also reaches the physical and operational systems around air traffic. It includes the provision of operations and support for air traffic movements, including control towers and coordination relating to flight-traffic activity. It covers work connected with air-traffic services and aeronautical telecommunications, flight-navigation telecommunications construction, installation of flight-navigation equipment, and related flight information. It also includes operating facilities or equipment for flight navigation, aeronautical telecommunications, aeronautical information, aviation meteorology and search-and-rescue information. Supporting facilities and equipment can involve mechanical, electrical, electronic and information-technology systems. That breadth matters: the activity describes an integrated service and support environment for air navigation, from the control-tower setting to the systems that carry, publish and support aviation information.

A business may register this activity at every listed scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. Nationally, its PMA status is open, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a complete foreign-ownership ceiling, not a partial stake. Yet Bali must be read on its own terms. The province has a permanent, island-wide PMA block for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is identified as medium-high risk, so it does not fall within those blocked risk bands. For that reason, it is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium.

For a foreign investor looking at Bali, the honest conclusion is neither a ban nor an unconditional site-level assurance. The Bali position recorded here is OK-or-higher-risk, and the record says the activity is not blocked by the moratorium. It also says to verify the position per address. That last qualification deserves to remain visible: national openness allows up to 100% foreign ownership, while Bali’s moratorium does not exclude this activity, but the address-specific reading needs to be checked. The result is a clear national opening and a Bali route that remains outside the named moratorium, subject to that address verification.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness allows up to 100% foreign ownership, while Bali’s moratorium does not exclude this activity.

editorial.headline: The Ground Work That Keeps Air Travel Moving
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the airport services behind a safe, orderly aircraft turnaround—from passenger handling to cargo, post and ground technical support.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned company can register this activity in Bali today. It is nationally open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, and Bali does not block it under the provincial PMA moratorium. That matters because this is not a peripheral airport service: it is the operational work that connects an aircraft’s arrival, turnaround and departure to passengers, baggage, freight and post.

Its scope is broad but coherent. It includes technical and operational support for aircraft on the ground, including refuelling, water provision, waste handling and aircraft movement. It also covers the passenger-facing rhythm of an airport—check-in, boarding and transit—alongside loading and unloading baggage, cargo and post. Cargo work extends to inspections using ionising-radiation sources, whether radioactive materials or radiation-generating equipment. Documentation, weighing, security and the special handling of dangerous or high-value goods are part of the same operational field.

This activity may operate at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That range reflects the different layers of airport support contained within the scope: some work is administrative or handling-focused, while other functions sit directly inside the technical choreography of an aircraft’s ground operation. The defining feature is not a particular item of equipment or a single customer touchpoint, but responsibility for services that must work together when an aircraft is on the ground.

Bali’s position is clear in the record. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that rule: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The result is a clean alignment between national foreign-investment openness and Bali’s current treatment of the activity. For founders, the practical distinction is simple: the activity is available to PMA registration, while its actual scope remains firmly anchored in airport ground, passenger, baggage, cargo and post handling.
editorial.pullQuote: This is the operational work that connects an aircraft’s arrival, turnaround and departure to passengers, baggage, freight and post.

data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup aktivitas pemeriksaan danpengendalian keamanan penerbangan terhadap kargo atau pos yang akan diangkut menggunakan pesawat udara,termasuk pesawat udara tanpa awak (drone),untuk memenuhi standar keamanan penerbangan nasional dan internasional, sebagai bagian dari sistem keamanan rantai pasok udara. Aktivitas ini biasanya dilakukan entitas yang bergerak di bidang keagenan kargo atau pengiriman.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup
- aktivitas pemeriksaan keamanan kargo atau pos menggunakan metode yang telah disetujui seperti sumber radiasi pengion (zat radioaktif dan pembangkit radiasi pengion), explosive trace detection (ETD), atau prosedur keamanan internal lainnya, sebelum barang diserahkan ke maskapai;
- aktivitas pengendalian akses ke area terbatas, pengawasan terhadap pergerakan barang, pengendalian kendaraan pengangkut, serta pengawasan proses penyerahan barang kepada maskapai penerbangan.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- pemeriksaan dan pengendalian keamanan muatan penerbangan oleh penyedia penyimpanan dan pergudangan, lihat subgolongan 5210;
- pemeriksaan dan pengendalian keamanan muatan penerbangan oleh pos dan kurir, lihat golongan pokok 53.

editorial.headline: Aviation Cargo Security, From Screening to Airline Handover
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the security controls that clear air cargo and mail for carriage, including by drone, within the air-supply-chain system.
editorial.body:
Aviation cargo security is not a peripheral check performed at the edge of an airport operation. It is the work of examining and controlling cargo or mail before it is carried by aircraft—including unmanned aircraft or drones—to meet national and international aviation-security standards. The activity sits within the security of the air supply chain, where the condition of a consignment, its movement and its handover all matter before it reaches an airline.

Its practical scope is deliberately broad. It includes approved security-screening methods, from ionising-radiation sources and ionising-radiation generators to explosive trace detection (ETD) and internal security procedures. It also reaches beyond the point of inspection: controlling entry to restricted areas, monitoring the movement of goods, controlling transport vehicles and supervising the transfer of goods to an airline. The record identifies this work with the Regulated Agent/Known Consignor setting, and notes that it is usually undertaken by entities active in cargo agency or forwarding.

Registration is open at every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. At the national level, PMA is open, allowing foreign ownership up to the 100% ceiling. In other words, the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. That status is grounded in the cited presidential regulations, while the operating description remains focused on the security chain around cargo and mail destined for air transport.

Bali does not reverse that national position. Throughout the province, PMA registration is permanently blocked for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activity. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a prohibition. For a foreign-owned registration in Bali, the decisive point is straightforward: this activity can be registered there today, subject to its recorded higher-risk profile at the Large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, this activity is not caught by the permanent PMA moratorium because its Large-scale OSS risk is Medium-High/High.

editorial.headline: Air and Space Transport Services Beyond the Usual Categories
editorial.standfirst: Open to every listed business scale and up to 100% foreign ownership nationally, this air-and-space transport activity is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium, subject to address verification.
editorial.body:
“Other” should not be mistaken for vague. This activity covers services connected to air and space transport for passengers, animals or goods when those activities are not classified elsewhere. Its breadth comes from the transport subjects—people, live animals and cargo—and from the fact that it reaches both air and space transport. The practical reading must remain disciplined: the record defines the field by its connection to transport and by what has not been classified elsewhere; it does not offer a neat menu of named services. A registration should therefore be read against that boundary, rather than expanded with examples the classification does not supply.

The scale position is notably broad. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses, so the classification is not reserved for one stated size of enterprise. That does not turn the four scale labels into a description of operational complexity or a set of further conditions; the record supplies only the eligibility range. It does, however, establish a clear starting point for founders: this is an activity available across the full Micro-to-Large sequence recorded here, provided the business genuinely sits within the stated air-and-space transport-related scope.

At the national level, PMA is open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for PMA registration of this activity. The stated source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national openness is the relevant baseline, but it is not a reason to flatten the local reading. Bali has a separate status and a separate reason, and those fields matter because a national ownership ceiling and a provincial registration position can be different things.

For Bali, the record’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. More importantly, it describes the activity as medium-high risk and says it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium, with verification required for the address. The moratorium itself is recorded as permanent and island-wide, but this activity is expressly outside its block. So the honest Bali conclusion is narrow but useful: PMA registration is not barred by that moratorium today; the actual address still needs verification. That is neither a new ownership cap nor a condition invented around the activity—it is the specific local qualification the record gives.
editorial.pullQuote: PMA registration is not barred by that moratorium today; the actual address still needs verification.

editorial.headline: Cargo Work at the Point of Transfer
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers hands-on cargo and baggage handling across transport modes, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and a Bali position not blocked by the moratorium.
editorial.body:
Cargo handling is the practical work of loading and unloading goods and baggage, regardless of the transport mode involved. It includes the loading and unloading of ships and freight rail wagons, as well as the provision of operator-supplied lifting and handling equipment such as cargo lifts and cranes. It also covers moving loads at industrial sites, generally with transport equipment not suited to use on public roads. The centre of gravity is the physical handling of a load: receiving it, lifting it, placing it, or transferring it as part of an operational movement.

A business registering under this activity may operate at any of the stated enterprise scales: Micro, Small, Medium, or Large. That breadth reflects a classification concerned with the handling task itself, from the movement of baggage and goods to equipment-led lifting and industrial-site transfers. The defining work is hands-on and operational, whether the cargo is being loaded, unloaded, or repositioned with the appropriate handling equipment and an operator.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. Put simply, the national-level record allows 100% foreign ownership. This is a clear position rather than a partial opening: the stated ceiling does not require foreign ownership to stop below complete ownership. For a founder assessing the activity at the national level, the relevant facts are its open PMA status and that full foreign participation is permitted within the stated ceiling.

Bali requires a more exact reading, but it is not a prohibition in this record. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. This activity is explicitly not blocked by that moratorium. At the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High, which is the reason given for the Bali outcome. Its Bali status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: the activity is not caught by the stated moratorium, while the local assessment rests on the higher-risk classification at the Large scale. The national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the stated national position.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not block this activity through the stated moratorium because its Large-scale OSS risk is Medium-High/High.

editorial.headline: The Contract That Holds a Multimodal Freight Journey Together
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers freight moved under one multimodal contract, with national PMA ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block at the stated large-scale risk level.
editorial.body:
Multimodal freight transport is defined by continuity rather than by any one vehicle. It covers goods carried using at least two different transport modes under a single contract, documented as multimodal transport, from the point where the multimodal operator receives the goods to the designated point of delivery for their recipient. The commercial centre of gravity is that one contractual journey: the operator connects the handovers between modes into a single transport undertaking.

The stated scope also embraces the supporting work when it forms part of that multimodal operation: freight forwarding, warehousing, cargo consolidation, the provision of cargo space, and customs handling. That matters because these functions are presented here as elements of an integrated movement of goods, not as detached activities. The activity is open at **Menengah** and **Besar** scales, making it a registration category for businesses operating the through-transport arrangement at either of those stated scales.

Nationally, the PMA position is unambiguous. Its status is **TERBUKA**, with a maximum foreign ownership of **100%**. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity; there is no foreign-share cap below full ownership in the supplied record. That openness belongs to the activity as defined: transport carried through at least two modes, under one multimodal contract, with its included supporting services forming part of the same operation.

Bali requires a more specific reading, but not a pessimistic one. The record places the activity in an **OK or higher-risk** position and says that, at the **Besar** scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High or High. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities. This activity is expressly recorded as **not blocked** by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: a foreign investor may rely on the national 100% ownership ceiling, and this activity is not stopped by Bali’s PMA moratorium on the basis stated in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The commercial centre of gravity is that one contractual journey: the operator connects the handovers between modes into a single transport undertaking.

editorial.headline: Counting Cargo, With a Foreign-Ownership Limit
editorial.standfirst: Independent tally work records the facts of cargo movement for owners and carriers—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but capped at a 49% foreign stake for cargo/freight forwarding.
editorial.body:
Independent tally activity is the discipline of establishing the facts around cargo: counting it, measuring it, weighing it and making the corresponding records for the cargo owner and/or carrier. The scope expressly includes independent tally operations at ports. It is therefore a defined cargo-recording service, built around a clear account of the load rather than a generic label for commercial activity.

The registration record is open to businesses at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. That breadth matters because the activity is not reserved in the record for one class of enterprise. Whether the work is organised on a smaller footing or at a larger operating scale, the stated scope remains the same: measurement, count, weight and documentation concerning cargo for those with an interest in it.

The position, as recorded, is restricted rather than open. Status: TERBATAS. Within the cargo/freight-forwarding context that applies to this code, foreign nationals may hold no more than 49%. That is the material fact for a founder weighing this activity — a capped-ownership structure, not a fully open one.

The record also notes a permanent, island-wide Bali rule that blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity’s own entry is not marked as blocked; it is marked TERBATAS and states the 49% foreign-ownership limit. The slim record does not assign this activity a risk classification, so the precise reading is to keep those two facts distinct: the general moratorium applies to the risk categories named in the rule, while this activity’s recorded treatment is a restriction on foreign ownership, capped at 49%, rather than an outright block. For founders, that distinction is the essential one: this is a capped-ownership activity, not an open one.
editorial.pullQuote: Cargo and freight forwarding carries a 49% ceiling for foreign nationals — the limit attaches to the activity, and our source records no Bali-specific variation.

editorial.headline: The Transport Work That Happens Between the Journeys
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the organising, planning and in-transit handling work that keeps transport, storage and distribution operations moving.
editorial.body:
Transport is often understood through the visible journey: the train, road vehicle, vessel or aircraft in motion. This activity concerns much of the work around that journey instead. It covers arranging or organising transport operations across rail, road, sea and air, alongside logistics consultancy for transport, warehousing and distribution operations. Its scope also reaches the management of logistics for sports equipment and supplies, as well as practical cargo-handling work during transit.

That last distinction matters. The handling included here is specifically tied to moving goods: temporary protective packing while goods are in transit, unpacking, sampling and weighing. Taken together, the scope describes a broad operational layer of transport support—where planning, coordination and controlled handling meet. It is an activity for businesses whose role is to make transport and distribution systems function coherently, whether through advisory work, operational organisation or carefully bounded goods handling.

Registration is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The national position is TERBUKA to foreign investment, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. At the national level, the record therefore permits full foreign ownership. That position is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the important point is not to confuse a broad activity title with a narrow operational remit: the business description should remain anchored to transport-support operations, logistics consultancy and the specified transit-related handling tasks.

Bali does not place this activity within its island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The Bali record places it at medium-high risk and says it is not blocked by that moratorium. This is therefore not a case where a foreign investor is nationally open yet unable to register in Bali today. Still, the record calls for verification by address. That is the honest Bali position: no moratorium block is identified for this activity, but the proposed location should be checked before treating the national 100% ceiling as a completed Bali registration outcome.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Work of Moving Goods at Scale
editorial.standfirst: This activity code covers the coordination of large-volume goods shipments across rail, road, sea and air, with a nationally open foreign-ownership position and no Bali moratorium block at large scale.
editorial.body:
Goods do not move at scale through transport alone. They move through organisation: deciding how a consignment is sent, coordinating its passage by rail, road, sea or air, and arranging shipment on a client’s behalf. That is the centre of this activity. It covers the organisation of delivery or packing of goods in large volumes, as well as the arrangement and administration of consignments for clients, whether those consignments are grouped or individual.

The practical subject is therefore the management of the shipment rather than the physical act of carrying it. A business registered under this activity may organise the dispatch of goods across several transport modes and handle the associated arrangements in the client’s name. The scope is specific about a boundary, too: third-party packing performed for a fee or under contract is not part of this activity. Its focus remains on directing the movement and dispatch of goods, especially where volume and coordination matter.

The code is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses. At national level, it carries a TERBUKA PMA status and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. At the national level, this record allows foreign ownership in full. That position is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; it is not an inferred opening or a commercial reading of the activity’s transport role.

Bali requires the same clarity. The province’s standing moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For a founder assessing this code, the distinction matters. The national position is fully open to foreign ownership, while the Bali position is not a blanket prohibition; it remains outside the stated moratorium because of its recorded risk classification at large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is fully open to foreign ownership, while Bali does not impose a moratorium block on this activity at large scale.

editorial.headline: The Ship Agent’s Desk: KBLI 52312 at Sea and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 52312 covers the operational agency work behind vessel calls, port services, documentation and supplies—open nationally to foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, KBLI 52312 covers the agency work of managing a sea-transport vessel’s affairs. It includes reporting planned and actual arrivals and departures; arranging port services; appointing loading and unloading companies; and settling vessel documentation. The work also extends to cargo accounting and disbursement, issuing bills of lading for and on behalf of the shipowner, and handling bunkering of fuel and fresh water. Supplying equipment and provisions, alongside other agency services agreed between the shipowner or operator and the ship agent, sits within the same remit. The scope additionally includes intermediary operational handling for fishing vessels at sea.

A business undertaking those functions may register this activity at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth places the code around the practical administration of a vessel’s port call and ongoing requirements, from formal reporting and paperwork to cargo, fuel, water, equipment and provisions. The record gives no narrower scale distinction within the activity itself; those four listed scales are its complete stated position.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For this activity, there is no recorded national foreign-share cap below full ownership. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position is material because the code concerns the party responsible for coordinating a substantial set of vessel-facing services rather than a single isolated task.

Bali requires its own reading. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island. This activity, however, is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and is not recorded as blocked. The stated reason is specific: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is clear: the activity is foreign-open nationally and, on this Bali record, is currently not barred from PMA registration in the province.

editorial.headline: Cargo Air Representation: Open Nationally, Scope-Dependent in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A cargo-air representative activity with wide scale eligibility, foreign ownership open nationally, and a Bali outcome that turns on the precise scope declared and its OSS risk.
editorial.body:
This activity concerns the operational representation of specialised cargo air transport: the commercial work of selling and marketing air-transport services, including the full marketing function. Its practical territory runs from market research and promotion to distribution. The record expressly places this work in the context of marketing and selling for foreign air-transport companies. It also includes the stated activities of electronic-trade operators and intermediary-platform operators, whether established in Indonesia or operating from abroad while conducting electronic trade in Indonesia. The focus is on putting cargo air-transport services into the market, rather than selling passenger air tickets.

The scale position is notably broad. Registration is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises, allowing the activity to sit across the country’s recognised business-scale categories. That range fits the character of representative work: an enterprise may be responsible for market-facing activity, promotion and distribution without the description itself turning into a statement about operating aircraft or selling passenger tickets. The defining thread is commercial representation for cargo air transport and the surrounding marketing responsibilities.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company assessing the national position, the record therefore presents no foreign-equity reduction below that stated ceiling. The important distinction is that this is the national ownership position; it does not settle the separate Bali registration outcome.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The activity is not marked as automatically blocked, but its Bali status is scope-dependent. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is low for some scopes and higher for others. The record says PMA registration in Bali is possible only by declaring the higher-risk scope, with live OSS verification required for the precise activity. Alongside that, Bali permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island. The honest conclusion is conditional rather than blanket approval: the national 100% ceiling remains clear, while Bali registration depends on the exact declared scope and its live OSS risk assessment.
editorial.pullQuote: The national 100% ceiling remains clear, while Bali registration depends on the exact declared scope and its live OSS risk assessment.

editorial.headline: Freight Intermediation Is Not Freight Transport
editorial.standfirst: For freight intermediaries, the national picture is open; in Bali, PMA registration depends entirely on the declared scope and its live OSS risk.
editorial.body:
**This activity is about the work around a freight movement, not operating the vehicle, vessel or aircraft that makes it.** It covers intermediary services tied to the transport of goods where the business does not run its own transport equipment. In practice, that can mean reserving cargo capacity, preparing shipment paperwork, issuing or obtaining transport documents and freight charges, or acting as representative for a shipper, consignee or logistics operator. It also takes in sea-shipping and air-cargo agency activity, freight-transport service platforms, and customs-agency work representing clients in customs processes.

The field is broad enough for a company whose value lies in arranging access, paperwork, representation and the connective tissue of cargo movement. It is not a description of operating the transport itself: the record makes that distinction explicit. A prospective registrant should therefore treat the declared activity as a precise account of an intermediary role—whether centred on capacity booking, documentation, agency representation, a freight-services platform or client representation in customs—rather than as a catch-all label for moving goods. It is open to businesses at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales.

Nationally, the PMA position is clear: the activity is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali requires a more exact reading. The activity is not marked as outright blocked, but its local position depends on scope. Bali permanently blocks PMA registration for activity scopes assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk, island-wide. The record says that, at the Besar scale, some scopes may carry Low OSS risk while others carry higher risk. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope, and the exact activity must be verified live in OSS.

For a founder, the useful reading is practical rather than abstract. National openness answers the ownership question at the national level, while Bali’s treatment turns on the particular scope selected in the registration and the OSS risk attached to it. A business carrying out several of the listed intermediary functions should not assume that one general label settles the Bali outcome. The declared higher-risk scope—not the category in general—is what keeps PMA registration available there.
editorial.pullQuote: The declared higher-risk scope—not the category in general—is what keeps PMA registration available in Bali.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers acting as an intermediary selling tickets for flights, trains, buses, ships, or other passenger transport, whether through a physical office or an online booking platform. It includes operating a website for reservations but excludes ridesharing or taxi-hailing apps that don’t provide transport themselves.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, the KBLI is fully open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the activity isn’t blocked by the moratorium but is classified as medium-high to high risk—so while registrable, it requires address verification and may face extra local scrutiny.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: bps only.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Agen Penjualan Tiket Transportasi (52321)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign travel-tech founders, online travel agencies, or booking platform operators wanting to legally sell transport tickets in Bali.

editorial.headline: The Business of Getting Passengers Booked
editorial.standfirst: Ticketing intermediation is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership—and Bali does not block its PMA registration.
editorial.body:
Transport ticket sales agents occupy the booking layer of passenger travel. This activity covers intermediary services that help passengers buy tickets for road, rail, water and air transport, for journeys within Indonesia or abroad. It also encompasses online platforms used to book transport tickets and reservation services for passenger transport. Its subject is not merely the ticket itself but the organised path to it: the service that mediates a purchase, manages a reservation, or makes booking available online. The definition therefore brings passenger travel across several modes into one ticketing activity, whether the destination is domestic or international.

The register is not reserved for one company size. It is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The recorded business population includes non-exempt PPMSE and PSP operators established in Indonesia, and non-exempt PPMSE and PSP operators established outside Indonesia that conduct PMSE business in Indonesian jurisdiction. The scope further reaches businesses beyond those named e-commerce and intermediary-operator categories. This matters because the activity is defined by the ticketing and reservation function, not by a single organisational form: the record expressly accommodates both the platform operator and the passenger-ticket reservation service.

For foreign investment, the national reading is direct. The status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor may therefore hold the whole company nationally for this activity. Bali does not reverse that result. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk, island-wide; this activity is specifically recorded as not blocked. Its OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—medium-high/high—so it falls outside the moratorium’s blocked band. In Bali, a foreign investor can register this activity; the recorded status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, not a PMA prohibition.

That creates a clean, if precise, reading for a founder. National openness is not undone in Bali: foreign participation can reach the national 100% ceiling, and the activity is not blocked for PMA registration there. The Bali record’s point is narrower and important: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is medium-high/high. For this activity, that places it outside the province-wide rule aimed at Low and Medium-Low risk PMA registrations. The business remains what the scope says it is—an intermediary for passenger transport tickets and reservations, including an online booking platform.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is not undone in Bali: this activity is not blocked for PMA registration there.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers acting as an intermediary to obtain flight approvals on behalf of aircraft operators—handling overflight and landing permits, airport slot times, and other operational clearances from civil or military aviation authorities. It also includes administrative and representative support for those clearances.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: National regulations allow 100% foreign ownership (PMA) for this flight approval agent service, and Bali does not outright block it under the current moratorium. However, the activity is classified as higher risk in Bali, so registration likely requires extra scrutiny and is subject to address-specific verification—you may need a physical office that meets zoning and authority checks.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Work Behind Every Flight Approval
editorial.standfirst: A flight-approval agent handles the permissions, clearances and administrative representation that allow an operator’s planned flight to proceed.
editorial.body:
Flight approval is the unglamorous but consequential work that sits between an operator’s intended route and the authorities able to approve it. This activity covers intermediary services performed on an aviation operator’s behalf: arranging permission to cross airspace, securing landing permission, seeking airport time slots, and handling other operational clearances with the relevant civil or military aviation authorities. It also includes the related administrative and representative service. The activity is about obtaining approval, not operating an aircraft.

The record places this work within a digital-trade setting. It identifies electronic-trading-system providers and intermediary-platform providers that are not exempt, whether established inside Indonesia’s legal jurisdiction or established outside it while conducting electronic-trade business in Indonesia. The available business scales are broad: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the code describes a specialised aviation-facing intermediary role without reserving it, in the record, for one particular business size.

Nationally, the position is clear. Foreign investment is permitted, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits this activity to be wholly foreign-owned. Its stated basis is Presidential Regulation 10/2021 and 49/2021. That national openness should not be mistaken for a universal local registration outcome, however; the Bali treatment turns on the precise scope declared in the live OSS process.

Bali’s status is scope-dependent rather than categorically blocked. The province permanently blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA registration across the island. For this activity, the record says that some scope may be low risk at large scale while other scope is assessed more highly. PMA registration in Bali is therefore available only where the business declares the higher-risk scope, with the record giving PPMSE in platform-trade cases as an example. The practical conclusion is narrow but important: a foreign investor cannot rely on the national 100% ceiling alone; the exact activity declared must support the higher-risk route in live OSS.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor cannot rely on the national 100% ceiling alone; the exact activity declared must support the higher-risk route in live OSS.

editorial.headline: Passenger Air Representation Is Nationally Open, but Bali Depends on Scope
editorial.standfirst: For passenger-airline operational representatives, Indonesia permits full foreign ownership nationally; in Bali, the precise scope and OSS risk declaration determine whether PMA registration is available.
editorial.body:
This activity is the commercial representation of passenger air transport: selling and marketing air-transport services and handling the full marketing orbit around them. That orbit expressly reaches market research, promotion and distribution. In practice, it is the representative function that helps a passenger air service reach the market, rather than the separate act of selling air tickets. The record also identifies marketing and selling for foreign air-transport companies, bringing the same broad work—sales, marketing, research, promotion and distribution—within the activity. It further refers to non-exempt electronic-commerce organisers and intermediary-facility providers, whether established inside Indonesia’s jurisdiction or conducting Indonesian e-commerce business from outside it.

Registration is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. At the national level, the PMA status remains TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clear national permission for a foreign-invested registration: there is no stated foreign-equity cap below full ownership in this record. The significance is not simply that a company can market a passenger air service, but that its proposed operation must genuinely fit the representation, marketing and sales role described here. The activity encompasses all aspects of that marketing function, while direct passenger ticket sales are outside its stated scope.

Bali requires a more exact reading. Its status is scope-dependent, not an outright block, and the record says that some scopes at Besar scale are low risk while others are higher risk. Bali’s island-wide, permanent rule blocks every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration. Yet the record specifically says this activity can be registered as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope where the precise activity calls for it. No Bali-side ownership percentage is given; the decisive issue is the scope and risk declaration, not a separate equity figure. Before filing, the live OSS position must be verified against the exact activity.

That distinction is the central fact to keep in view. A 100% national ceiling does not by itself settle the Bali filing route, but neither does the provincial rule make the activity universally unavailable. For a foreign founder, the honest conclusion is narrow: the activity is nationally open, including at every listed business scale; in Bali, PMA registration turns on using the appropriate higher-risk scope declaration and confirming the exact activity in live OSS. The record provides no additional Bali condition beyond that scope-and-risk pathway.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national ceiling does not by itself settle the Bali filing route.

editorial.headline: Passenger Transport Intermediation, Without Running the Journey
editorial.standfirst: A business of booking, brokering and coordinating passenger movement—nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 52329 is for the business that makes passenger transport possible without operating the transport itself. Its centre of gravity is intermediation: an online platform for booking ride-sharing, brokering passenger seats on ships or aircraft, arranging carpools and vanpools, or coordinating non-emergency medical transport without providing social-assistance services. It also reaches taxi-call intermediation where the intermediary does not itself provide the ride, along with passenger reservations, travel-schedule management, travel-document handling and representation for passengers or transport operators. The activity is therefore about the connective tissue around a journey, rather than the physical act of carrying someone.

That distinction gives the code a broad commercial character. It suits businesses whose value lies in matching, reserving, organising, documenting or representing passenger transport arrangements. The record opens it at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. At the national level, its PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, the national record allows full foreign ownership for this activity; there is no stated minority-share requirement within the material provided.

Bali is where the reading needs care, because the province permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked. The Bali record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale as medium-high or high, and expressly says that it is not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign investor considering this particular activity in Bali, the record’s answer is therefore affirmative: PMA registration is not barred there today. That conclusion is specific to this activity and rests on the stated Bali risk position, not on a general exemption from the province’s rule.

The result is a code with a clear operational boundary and a comparatively direct ownership picture. It accommodates the businesses that organise access to passenger transport—digital or otherwise—while keeping the transport operation itself outside its defining role. At the national level, the ownership ceiling is complete; in Bali, the moratorium does not block the activity on the record supplied. For founders, the important discipline is to keep the registered activity aligned with that intermediary function: arranging the journey is the point of the code.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, the moratorium does not block an activity whose role is to arrange the journey rather than operate it.

Kelompok ini mencakup aktivitas layanan pos yang dijalankan berdasarkan kewajiban layanan universal oleh satu atau lebih penyedia layanan universal yang ditunjuk, yaitu pengiriman pos jenis tertentu yang wajib dijamin oleh pemerintah untuk menjangkau seluruh wilayah dalam negeri yang memungkinkan masyarakat mengirimkan dan/atau menerima kiriman dari satu tempat ke tempat lain di dunia. Kegiatan yang dilakukan meliputi penggunaan infrastruktur layanan universal, termasuk lokasi ritel, fasilitas penyortiran dan pengolahan, serta jalur pengiriman untuk mengambil dan mengantarkan surat. Pengiriman dapat mencakup surat pos, yaitu surat, kartu pos, dokumen cetak (koran, majalah, materi iklan, barang cetakan dalam kantong khusus, dan sebagainya), paket kecil, paket, sekogram, barang atau dokumen lainnya, termasuk juga jasa lain yang diperlukan untuk mendukung kewajiban layanan universal.
Kelompok ini mencakup
- pengambilan, penyortiran, pengangkutan, dan pengiriman (domestik atau internasional) dengan layanan pos yang beroperasi di bawah kewajiban pelayanan universal, yang meliputi surat, kartu pos, dokumen cetak, dan paket kecil (surat berisi barang), sekogram, barang cetakan yang dikirim dalam kantong khusus yang ditujukan untuk penerima dengan alamat yang sama, dan paket pos. satu atau lebih moda transportasi dapat digunakan, dan aktivitas ini dapat dilakukan dengan menggunakan transportasi milik sendiri (pribadi) atau transportasi umum;

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers universal postal services—collecting, sorting, transporting, and delivering mail and small parcels to any address, using retail outlets, processing centres, and delivery routes. Essentially, it’s the core public mail delivery function that a government-appointed operator guarantees nationwide.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, a foreigner can own 100% of a postal service company under this code. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct 1:1 match from KBLI 2020 — code and scope unchanged.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Pos (53100)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who wants to run a universal postal delivery network, typically as a designated operator serving the entire country or a region.

editorial.headline: Postal Activity: Nationally Open, Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This universal-service postal activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership and, at Besar scale, is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Postal activity here means the public-serving postal system operated under a universal-service obligation by one or more appointed universal-service providers. Its premise is reach: the government-guaranteed service must extend across the domestic territory, allowing people to send and/or receive consignments between locations in Indonesia and elsewhere in the world. This is an activity defined by that obligation and by the service network built to meet it. Its listed work joins physical infrastructure with the handoff of consignments across those routes.

That network is concrete. It uses universal-service infrastructure: retail locations, sorting and processing facilities, and delivery routes used to collect and deliver letters. The operational chain spans collection, sorting, transport and delivery, within Indonesia or internationally. It can employ one or more transport modes, using the operator’s own transport or public transport; movement is not confined to one method. Collection may start at public letter boxes or post offices. The consignments named in the record range from letters and postcards to printed documents—newspapers, magazines, advertising material and specially bagged printed matter—along with small packets, postal parcels, sekograms and other goods or documents. Supporting services necessary for the universal-service obligation are part of the activity as well.

Businesses may register at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. The scale designation runs from Mikro through Besar, rather than identifying a single business size. Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In practical ownership terms, the national record places no foreign-share cap below full foreign ownership. Its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

On Bali, the record does not mark the activity as blocked for PMA registration. It assigns the status **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK** and notes that, at Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That is why it is not blocked by Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The distinction matters: national openness and Bali’s result are both affirmative in this record, while Bali’s conclusion is expressly tied to the recorded Besar-scale risk treatment. No Bali-specific foreign-ownership ceiling or partnership condition is stated.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, it is open to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, it is not moratorium-blocked because of its recorded Besar-scale risk treatment.

editorial.headline: Courier Activity: The Full Delivery Chain
editorial.standfirst: From parcel pickup to doorstep delivery, this activity spans domestic and international courier work across every listed scale — foreign ownership is capped at 49%, with no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Courier activity concerns the organised journey of a consignment, from collection or pickup through sorting or processing, transport and final delivery. The materials expressly within scope are letters, documents, parcels, goods and packages. The service can operate domestically or internationally, with one or more transport modes, using either transport owned by the operator or public transport. Its line of definition is equally important: this is activity outside the universal-service obligation, with the operator’s work framed as collection, processing, carriage and delivery.

The food element is carefully limited but real. Door-to-door delivery is included, as is food delivery. The record also brings in non-prepared meals only when they are preserved or packed so they can undergo further processing and are not easily perishable during collection, processing, transport and distribution within a package service. Read plainly, this is a scope that follows the delivery chain rather than stopping at a single leg: pickup and preparation for dispatch are part of the picture alongside transport and the doorstep handover.

Registration is not reserved for one end of the enterprise spectrum. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale businesses—the complete range supplied in the record. Each scale belongs in the same listed range. That breadth gives the operational description room to serve a business from its smallest listed category through its largest, while remaining the same courier activity in the record.

Foreign ownership in courier activity is capped at 49%. The cap comes from Perpres 49/2021, Lampiran III — the annex of business fields carrying specific requirements — at entry #32, so foreign shareholders can hold up to 49% of a courier company set up as a PT PMA and the rest must be held by Indonesian shareholders. Bali does not add a second obstacle to that. The island-wide moratorium suspends new PMA registration only for low and medium-low risk lines, and the record puts courier work at high risk at every scale, so it is not caught. The essential distinction is straightforward: registration in Bali is available, and what limits the foreign side is the 49% ceiling, nationally.
editorial.pullQuote: Registration in Bali is available for courier work; the foreign side of the shareholding stops at 49%.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers operating a digital intermediary platform that connects customers with postal and courier services for booking, tracking, and payment—without performing any physical delivery. It also includes online platforms that let users order food delivery through aggregated providers.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Portal Intermediasi Pos dan Kurir (53301)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.

editorial.headline: A Digital Gateway to Indonesia’s Delivery Networks
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the online portals that connect customers with postal, courier and food-delivery ordering services—nationally open to full foreign ownership, but scope-sensitive in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 53301 concerns the digital layer between a customer and a postal or courier provider. It is an intermediary service: a platform or portal that enables customers to access delivery services offered by multiple postal and courier companies, rather than carrying goods or documents itself. Its practical terrain includes ordering, tracking and payment through an online portal. The scope also includes an online platform through which the public can order food delivery.

This is therefore an activity for the operator of the digital marketplace or portal, not the physical delivery provider. The recorded scope expressly reaches non-exempt PPMSE and PSP operators established within Indonesia’s jurisdiction, as well as non-exempt operators established outside it when they conduct electronic-trading activity within Indonesia. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, placing the platform model within every listed business scale rather than reserving it for a single size of enterprise.

At the national level, the position is straightforward: the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a full foreign-ownership ceiling, not a partial one. The legal source recorded for that national position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For an investor considering a portal that coordinates booking, tracking and payment across delivery providers—or enables food-delivery ordering—the national record supports a foreign-owned structure within that ceiling.

Bali requires more careful reading. The record does not mark the activity as categorically blocked, but gives it a scope-dependent status. At Besar scale, OSS risk may be Low for some declared scopes and higher for others. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA registration for activities assessed Low or Medium-Low risk. The recorded route to PMA registration in Bali is therefore conditional: the business must declare the higher-risk scope, such as the relevant PPMSE scope for platform-trade activity, and verify the live OSS position for the exact activity. The national 100% ceiling remains the national ceiling; it does not remove this Bali registration condition.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this platform activity becomes a question of exact declared scope in Bali.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This code covers acting as a middleman between people or businesses who need delivery services and third-party courier or postal providers. You don’t do the actual shipping yourself; instead, you connect customers with logistics companies and earn a fee or commission, which could come from either side. The matchmaking can happen through an app, website, or even offline methods like phone or door-to-door introductions.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership, so in most of Indonesia you could set up a PMA for a courier-booking platform. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Jasa Intermediasi Pos dan Kurir Lainnya (53309)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign founders looking to launch a logistics marketplace, a delivery-booking app, or a courier aggregator platform — and Bali is not off the table: this KBLI's large-scale risk class sits above the moratorium's Low/Medium-Low band, so a PMA can still register it here.

editorial.headline: The Business of Connecting Postal and Courier Services
editorial.standfirst: This activity is open to foreign investment nationally, but Bali registration depends on declaring the exact higher-risk scope in the live OSS system.
editorial.body:
Postal and courier intermediation is the business of making the connection, not performing the delivery. It brings clients together with postal or courier providers for a fee or commission, whether through a digital platform or through non-digital channels such as face-to-face contact, door-to-door service, telephone or mail. The intermediary may be paid by the client, the service provider, or through other income such as advertising.

Its practical scope is wider than a simple referral. It includes third-party intermediary services around postal and courier providers’ access points for both business clients and households. It also covers the collection and processing of goods within domestic or international activity where the business does not itself transport or deliver them. Work performed on assignment from a postal or courier operator can also sit within the activity, provided the intermediary is not operating in its own name or contracting directly with the public for the service.

At the national level, the activity is open to foreign investment and permits foreign ownership of up to 100%. Businesses can register at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That national position is clear, but it should not be mistaken for an automatic Bali outcome. Bali permanently blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration across the province under the stated moratorium rule.

For this activity, Bali does not impose a blanket PMA block. Its treatment depends on the precise scope declared: some Besar-scale scopes are low risk, while others carry a higher risk. PMA registration in Bali is available only where the higher-risk scope is declared, with the exact activity to be verified in the live OSS system. For a founder, that distinction is decisive: the proposed operating model must be described with enough precision for its actual scope and risk treatment, rather than relying on the national foreign-ownership ceiling alone.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness permits full foreign ownership, but Bali registration turns on the precise higher-risk scope declared in OSS.

persyaratan: Dokumen penilaian mandiri Kesiapan Penerapan Standar

Dokumen Penilaian Mandiri Kesiapan Penerapan Standar
Silakan kirim semua dokumen yang diminta dalam satu file.
1. Unduh dan lengkapi formulir Penilaian Mandiri.
2. Dokumentasi Standar Pelaksanaan Kegiatan Usaha.
Lampirkan 6 dokumen Sarana
  1. Petunjuk identitas/nama usaha dengan tulisan yang terbaca.
  2. Ruang kantor/area administrasi yang dilengkapi peralatan dan perlengkapan kerja.
  3. Peralatan Pertolongan Pertama pada Kecalakaan (P3K) dan Alat Pemadam Api Ringan (APAR) yang berfungsi dengan baik.
  4. Ketersediaan air bersih yang tidak berwarna, tidak berbau, tidak berasa, dan jernih.
  5. Ketersediaan gudang atau tempat penyimpanan barang yang aman.
  6. Status kepemilikan kantor/tempat usaha yang jelas.
Lampirkan 1 dokumen Sumber Daya Manusia
Perlindungan asuransi kesehatan dan/atau kecelakaan bagi karyawan tersedia dan berlaku.
Lampirkan 1 dokumen Ketentuan Produksi
Pelayanan kesehatan, seperti informasi tentang dokter, rumah sakit, atau klinik terdekat terdokumentasi.
Lampirkan 3 dokumen Sistem Manajemen Usaha
  1. Struktur organisasi dan uraian tugas setiap jabatan jalas dan terdokumentasi.
  2. rencana bisnis (business plan) masih berlaku dan terdokumentasi.
  3. S0P dan/atau petunjuk teknis pelaksanaan karja masih berlaku dan terdokumentasi.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Five-star hotels — the top tier of Indonesian hotel classification. Full-service luxury accommodation with daily or weekly stays in a dedicated building. Think Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, Bulgari-level operations. Rooms, suites, restaurants, pools, spas, concierge — the works.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**Small / Medium / Large**: Two licensing tiers exist.
- **Medium-Low risk path**: NIB + Standard Certificate, issued **automatically**. Self-Assessment document required covering facilities, organization, HR, and products/services. Health Feasibility Certificate needed.
- **Medium-High risk path** (higher tier): NIB + Standard Certificate within **14 working days**. Requires Self-Assessment plus LSPr-certified tourism business standard.

**Micro + Small + Medium**: Separate Medium-Low entry with periodic reporting and health cert.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership.
intel_2026.whatChanged: In KBLI 2020, ALL star-rated hotels were under a single code: KBLI 2020 code 55110. editorial.headline: Five-Star Hotels: Open Nationally, Conditional in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers short-stay five-star hotel accommodation, from furnished suites to direct on-site guest service, across small, medium and large business scales.
editorial.body:
Five-star hotel activity is, at its core, the provision of short-stay accommodation on a daily or weekly basis. It applies to establishments that meet five-star hotel requirements and use part or all of a building, whether the building area is at or below 6,000 square metres or above it. The description is not limited to a room key and a reception desk: it contemplates furnished living areas and suites, with the direct, on-site customer service that defines a full hotel operation.

The operational picture can be correspondingly broad. Daily cleaning and bed-making, food and beverage service, laundry, and conference or convention facilities may all sit within the activity. These are not separate promises or regulatory conditions; they are the additional services expressly contemplated within the stated hotel accommodation scope. The activity is open to businesses at small, medium and large scales, giving the classification room to describe both compact five-star properties and larger hotel operations.

At the national level, the activity is open to foreign investment, with its foreign-ownership ceiling set at 100%. Bali requires a more exact reading. Its status is conditional on scope rather than categorically blocked: some scope(s) assessed through OSS at the large-business scale are low risk, while others carry a higher risk assessment. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. For this hotel activity, PMA registration in Bali is therefore possible only where the declared activity falls under the higher-risk scope; the exact activity must be checked live in OSS.

That distinction matters because a national opening does not, by itself, settle the Bali registration outcome. The national position remains fully open to foreign ownership, while the Bali result turns on the risk classification attached to the precise scope declared in OSS. For an investor or operator, the practical task is to align the proposed hotel activity with its actual scope before treating Bali registration as available.

Perlindungan asuransi kesehatan dan/atau kecelakaan bagi karyawan tersedia dan berlaku.

Pelayanan kesehatan, seperti informasi tentang dokter, rumah sakit, atau klinik terdekat terdokumentasi.

  1. Struktur organisasi dan uraian tugas setiap jabatan jalas dan terdokumentasi.

editorial.headline: Four-Star Hotels: Nationally Open, Bali Scope-Dependent
editorial.standfirst: Four-star hotel activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a Bali PMA registration turns on the exact scope and risk declared in live OSS.
editorial.body:
This activity covers four-star hotels providing short-stay accommodation, ordinarily on a daily or weekly basis, in part or all of a building. The accommodation may include furnished living rooms and suites, with direct on-site customer service as a defining feature. It can also include the familiar operational fabric of a hotel stay: daily cleaning and bed-making, food and beverage service, laundry, and conference or convention facilities. The record recognises this activity both for buildings of up to 6,000 square metres and for those exceeding that area.

It is open to small, medium, and large businesses. Nationally, the position is clear: the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is an unusually clean national starting point for a founder considering a four-star hotel operation. The applicable source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires more care. The record does not mark this activity as categorically blocked for PMA registration in the province, but it does make the result dependent on the exact scope declared. Some scopes at the large-business scale are assessed as low risk in OSS, while others carry a higher risk. Bali’s permanent province-wide rule blocks PMA for every low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activity. For this activity, the record says PMA registration in Bali is possible only where the declared scope is the higher-risk one, and it directs founders to verify the live OSS result for the precise activity being registered.

The practical point is not that the national 100% ceiling disappears in Bali; it is that the Bali registration outcome is shaped by the risk classification attached to the declared scope. A four-star hotel proposal therefore needs its exact OSS scope checked before the ownership structure is treated as registrable in Bali. The national door is open, while Bali’s door remains conditional on the live classification of the activity declaration.

editorial.headline: A Three-Star Hotel Is More Than a Building
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers short-stay, three-star accommodation with direct on-site service—and a national PMA opening that requires care in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 55103 covers the provision of short-stay accommodation, generally offered by the day or week, in premises that meet the requirements of a three-star hotel. The activity may use part or all of a building, and its stated scope applies both to buildings of up to 6,000 square metres and those above that size. The defining proposition is accommodation for a short stay, delivered as a hotel rather than merely as space.

The guest experience described here is correspondingly fuller than a room alone. Accommodation may include furnished living rooms and suites, while additional services can include daily cleaning and bed-making, food and beverage service, laundry, and conference or convention facilities. Most importantly, the activity is generally marked by direct, on-site customer service. Those details give the classification its practical shape: it is an accommodation operation with a service relationship visibly present at the property.

Registration is open at small, medium, and large scale. Nationally, the PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is the national position set out in the record, and it should be read as exactly that: the activity is open to PMA nationally, without a lower stated foreign-share cap.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The provincial rule permanently blocks PMA for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI across the island. This activity is not recorded as categorically blocked, however; its Bali status depends on scope. At large scale, some declared scopes carry low OSS risk while others carry higher risk. PMA registration in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope, so the exact activity must be verified in live OSS. The honest conclusion is neither a blanket Bali prohibition nor an automatic national opening: the national 100% position remains clear, while Bali registration turns on the risk classification of the scope actually declared.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open at 100%, this activity still demands a scope-specific OSS reading before PMA registration in Bali.

This code descends from KBLI 2020 55110 (Hotel Bintang (<6.000 m²)) on that list (BPS KBLI 2020→2025 conversion table). The list limits it to buildings under 6,000 m².
