editorial.headline: Digital Television Broadcasting: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Digital television programming and broadcasting is open to foreign investment nationally, with Bali’s moratorium not blocking this activity.
editorial.body:
Digital television is treated here as an operating activity, not merely a programme idea. It covers running television programming and broadcasting services with digital signals from television-broadcast studios and transmission facilities. The intended recipients may be the public, affiliates or subscribers; delivery can run through terrestrial, cable or satellite channels. Live theatre broadcasts also sit within the activity. The code therefore concerns the business of putting a digital television service on air and carrying it to its audience, from programming through transmission.

The relevant registrant is a television operator with the studio and transmission function described in the record, whether working at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah or Besar scale. The scale range is broad, yet it does not dilute the nature of the activity: registration follows a digital television broadcasting and programming operation. The record also identifies a permit for a private digital television broadcasting operator. The practical focus is an organised broadcasting service, built around facilities, programming and a defined relationship with its audience.

For a foreign investor, the national picture is straightforward. The activity is TERBUKA, and its foreign ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, national treatment permits foreign investment up to full ownership within this activity’s stated scope. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That conclusion comes from the record’s stated maximum, rather than an assumption drawn from the general label of the business.

Bali’s conclusion is equally clear, but rests on a specific reason. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA only for activities assessed at Low or Medium-Low risk. This activity is not flagged as blocked. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—so the record says it is not blocked by the moratorium. Bali therefore presents an open PMA-registration position for this activity, marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, rather than a foreign-ownership prohibition. The record gives no separate Bali ownership percentage or partnership condition; its Bali explanation is the risk classification and moratorium outcome.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign investor, the national picture is straightforward: the activity is open up to a 100% ownership ceiling.

editorial.headline: The Business of Video on Demand
editorial.standfirst: A clear route for on-demand video services nationally, with Bali remaining outside the island-wide PMA moratorium block but subject to address-level verification.
editorial.body:
On-demand video distribution and streaming is the activity at the centre of this code: the operation of services that deliver video when viewers choose to watch it. Its scope includes programming video-on-demand channels, distributing such video through subscription or advertising models, and enabling downloads of digital video content. That content may belong to a third party or be original material produced by the operator. It also includes game-video streaming where the audience watches rather than plays.

The activity is open across the full business-scale range stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the definition is built around the service of distributing and streaming video, rather than a single commercial format. A business may operate an on-demand channel, distribute subscription video, offer advertising-supported viewing, make digital video available for download, or stream gameplay for viewing only. The common thread is the delivery of video content on demand.

Nationally, this is an open activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In practical terms, the record does not place the foreign stake below full ownership at the national level. The national position is therefore straightforward: the activity is TERBUKA, and its stated ceiling permits 100% foreign ownership. That clarity should not obscure the commercial breadth of the code, which can encompass both third-party content and content produced by the operator itself.

Bali presents a distinct but not prohibitive picture. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island on a permanent basis. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: the Bali record places it in an OK-or-higher-risk position and states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. The remaining qualification is specific and limited: the position should be verified for the relevant address. For a PMA applicant considering Bali, the accurate conclusion is neither a blanket refusal nor an invented guarantee; it is an activity that remains outside the moratorium block, with address-level verification still called for.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this is an open activity with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.

editorial.headline: Government News Offices: Public Information, Closed to PMA
editorial.standfirst: This government news activity spans the full public-information chain, but remains closed to foreign investment nationally and for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Government news-office activity is the public-information function of finding, gathering, processing and distributing news. It covers work undertaken by government through print or electronic media, publishers or broadcasters, with the explicit purpose of delivering information to the public. The definition is broad in process but clear in character: this is not simply the publication of material; it is the government-led handling of news from collection through dissemination.

The record places the activity across every business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Scale, however, should not be mistaken for an invitation to foreign participation. Nationally, the PMA position is **TERTUTUP**, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of **0%**. In practical terms, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as a PMA business in Indonesia. The activity may span the smallest to the largest operational scale, but its ownership position is closed at the national level.

Bali reaches the same practical conclusion for PMA registration: the local status is **TERTUTUP**, and the record marks the activity as blocked. A foreigner therefore cannot register this activity in Bali today as PMA. The Bali note is important for its precision. It identifies the activity as medium-high or high risk and says it is **not** blocked by Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The closure recorded for Bali should therefore not be casually attributed to that moratorium.

That distinction matters because it keeps the analysis honest. Bali’s record does not offer a substitute foreign-ownership route, a local-partnership condition or a Bali-side percentage. Instead, it records a closed PMA status while directing that the position be verified for the specific address. For founders, the central fact is uncomplicated: this is a government news activity, available across stated business scales, but closed to foreign ownership nationally and unavailable for PMA registration in Bali. The address-specific verification is a necessary check on the Bali record’s application, not evidence of an unrecorded exception.
editorial.pullQuote: This activity may span every business scale, but it is closed to foreign ownership nationally and unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: The Business of Taking News to the Public
editorial.standfirst: Private news-agency activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership; whether Bali's moratorium applies is not yet classifiable pending re-derivation of the true risk tier.
editorial.body:
Private news-agency activity is the business of turning events into public information. Its scope covers the private search for, collection, processing and distribution of news through print or electronic media, publishers or broadcasters, with the purpose of informing the public. That formulation matters. The activity is not confined to publishing a finished item, nor to operating a single channel: it follows the news process from finding material and preparing it through to making it available as information. The defining thread is private activity directed toward public information.

The record opens this activity to every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth makes the code usable across different operating footprints without changing its essential character. Across those scales, the scope remains the private handling and dissemination of news, using the stated routes of media, publishing or broadcasting. The scale entries establish access at each size; they do not turn the activity into something other than the search, collection, processing and distribution of news for public information.

Nationally, the investment position is open. The recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%, meaning there is no recorded national foreign-equity ceiling below full ownership for this activity. This is the clean national picture reflected in the cited presidential regulations. It should not, however, be treated as a substitute for the Bali assessment. The record deliberately distinguishes national openness from Bali's local position, making the practical question not whether national access exists, but how the activity is treated at the proposed Bali address.

In Bali, the result is not yet classifiable. Whether this activity is caught by the province-wide PMA moratorium cannot be determined until its risk tier is established: the earlier reading was based on a risk classification carried over from a source that cannot reliably be applied to this KBLI-2025 code, and has been removed. PMA registration remains open nationally, a separate and unaffected fact. Confirm with the Bali Zero team before planning a Bali setup.
editorial.pullQuote: PMA registration is open nationally, a separate and unaffected fact; whether Bali's moratorium applies to this activity is not yet classifiable pending re-derivation of the true risk tier.

editorial.standfirst: Indonesia permits full foreign ownership of this platform activity nationally, but Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for it today.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, registering this activity in Bali is not possible today. That is the practical starting point for KBLI 60390, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali blocks it because, at the large-business scale, its OSS risk classification is Low or Medium-Low across the activity’s scope, placing it inside the province-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for those risk categories.

The activity itself concerns the operation of social-networking sites and other platforms for distributing or sharing content and information. Its scope includes blog and wiki sites, online-game sites, and the provision of downloadable e-books where that provision is not connected to publishing activity. It also reaches intermediary services for the trade of digital goods used in video games when those services are not related to publishing: a platform or digital marketplace may facilitate the sale of vouchers, credits, in-game items, or premium access. The common thread is the platform’s role in distributing content, information, access, or digital game goods.

This is an activity open to businesses at every stated scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, that openness is clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the permitted foreign stake is 100%. A founder assessing the code at the national level can therefore read it as fully foreign-open, with the source recorded as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But that national position does not settle the Bali question. The provincial rule applies island-wide and permanently to PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities.

For Bali, the decisive fact is not a lower foreign-ownership percentage or a partnership condition. It is a registration block. The record identifies the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and ties it directly to the moratorium, dated May 2026, because the relevant OSS risk at the Besar scale is Low or Medium-Low throughout the scope. The result is stark but precise: full foreign ownership is available nationally for this activity, while PMA registration in Bali is blocked today. Founders should keep those two truths separate rather than treating a nationally open status as an automatic route to a Bali registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

per_skala.scope_uraian: Penyelenggaraan jaringan Tetap Tertutup Melalui Media Fiber Optik Teresterial
persyaratan:
Rencana penyelenggaraan jaringan telekomunikasi yang memuat:

  1. Jenis layanan sesuai dengan penyelenggaraan yang dimohonkan;
  2. Konfigurasi sistem dan teknologi jaringan yang akan dibangun;
  3. Diagram dan rute serta peta jaringan;
  4. Cakupan wilayah pembangunan dan layanan yang akan dibangun (roll out plan) yang merupakan komitmen untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  5. Komitmen kinerja layanan untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  6. Data teknis alat/perangkat, sarana dan/atau prasarana telekomunikasi yang akan dibangun;
  7. Bukti kepemilikan perangkat;
  8. Perjanjian kerja sama dengan penyelenggara telekomunikasi lainnya;
  9. Pusat kontak informasi berkaitan dengan layanan prajual dan purnajual; dan
  10. Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) terkait monitoring jaringan, penanganan gangguan, billing dan penagihan, aktivasi dan deaktivasi pengguna/pelanggan, dan pelayanan pengguna/pelanggan.

Pernyataan:

  1. Kesanggupan melaksanakan ketentuan penyelenggaraan jaringan; dan
  2. Menyampaikan data yang valid dan benar.
Tidak memiliki kewajiban Penerimaan Negara Bukan Pajak yang terhutang kepada kementerian yang menyelenggarakan urusan pemerintahan di bidang komunikasi dan informatika;
Memiliki konfirmasi status wajib pajak dari kementerian yang menyelenggarakan urusan pemerintahan di bidang keuangan; dan
Daftar susunan pengurus untuk membuktikan bahwa Direksi, Pengurus, dan/atau Badan Hukum Pelaku Usaha tidak ditetapkan dalam Daftar Hitam Penyelenggara.
Memperoleh penetapan penomoran telekomunikasi dalam hal Penyelenggaraan Jaringan Telekomunikasi menggunakan penomoran telekomunikasi;
Dalam hal Penyelenggaraan Jaringan Telekomunikasi menggunakan spektrum frekuensi radio, harus memperoleh izin penggunaan spektrum frekuensi radio sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
Memperoleh hak labuh dalam hal Penyelenggaraan Jaringan Telekomunikasi menggunakan satelit asing sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
Mengajukan permohonan pelaksanaan Uji Laik Operasi; dan
Memperoleh surat keterangan laik operasi berdasarkan pelaksanaan Uji Laik Operasi.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers operating and providing wired telecommunication networks – think fiber optic cables and other physical lines – to transmit voice, data, and video. It includes connecting homes, offices, cell towers, data centers, and even international submarine cable systems.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, foreign ownership is fully open (100% PMA). In Bali, the activity is flagged as medium-to-high risk, so it’s not blocked by the local moratorium, but you’ll face heightened scrutiny. You must verify that your specific address meets all zoning and licensing requirements, and expect stricter due diligence.

editorial.headline: The Wired Networks Behind Indonesia’s Everyday Connections
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 61101 is the operating business of wired telecommunications networks—open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 61101 is the business of running the wired networks that carry voice, data, text, audio and video. Its terrain is broad but coherent: cable infrastructure on land and beneath the sea; access and distribution networks reaching homes and offices; and connections spanning regions, islands and countries. It also reaches the quieter infrastructure links between buildings, telecommunications exchanges, cellular towers, data centres and core networks. An operator may provide access points for customers, build the connective tissue between networks, or lease cable-network capacity to other telecommunications-network and telecommunications-service operators. Cable installation by itself, without operating the facility, sits outside this activity.

The register is deliberately open in scale. Micro, small, medium and large businesses may undertake it, reflecting an activity that ranges from customer-facing access networks to substantial connective infrastructure. Nationally, it is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is the clear starting point for a foreign-owned operator: this classification concerns the active provision, maintenance and operation of a wired telecommunications network, not merely the presence of cable in the ground or under the sea.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The province’s standing moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low-risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the large-business scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High/High, which places it outside the moratorium’s blocked risk categories. The honest Bali reading is therefore straightforward: PMA registration for this wired-telecommunications activity is not shut out by the provincial moratorium. The Bali status is appropriately framed as open or higher risk—not as a low-risk exemption, and not as a prohibition. For founders, that distinction matters: national foreign openness remains intact, while Bali’s record identifies the activity’s higher-risk character at the large scale rather than closing the door to it.

  3. Diagram dan rute serta peta jaringan;
  4. Cakupan wilayah pembangunan dan layanan yang akan dibangun (roll out plan) yang merupakan komitmen untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  5. Komitmen kinerja layanan untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  6. Data teknis alat/perangkat, sarana dan/atau prasarana telekomunikasi yang akan dibangun;
  7. Bukti kepemilikan perangkat;
  8. Perjanjian kerja sama dengan penyelenggara telekomunikasi lainnya;
  9. Pusat kontak informasi berkaitan dengan layanan prajual dan purnajual; dan
  10. Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) terkait monitoring jaringan, penanganan gangguan, billing dan penagihan, aktivasi dan deaktivasi pengguna/pelanggan, dan pelayanan pengguna/pelanggan.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the operation, maintenance, and provision of wireless telecommunication networks using electromagnetic waves. It includes building infrastructure for fixed wireless services like broadband wireless access or microwave links, as well as mobile services such as cellular networks and radio trunking. You can also lease out wireless network capacity to other providers.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership, but in Bali it's classified as medium-high to high risk. It is not currently blocked by the local moratorium, meaning a PMA can be established, but approval is more cautious and requires verification of the specific business address. Expect extra scrutiny on location and operational plans.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Telekomunikasi dengan Nirkabel (61102)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Ideal for foreign telecom entrepreneurs building wireless broadband networks, mobile virtual network operators, or companies leasing wireless infrastructure in Bali.

editorial.headline: Wireless Networks: Open Nationally and Outside Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers terrestrial wireless network infrastructure and capacity, open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked by Bali’s risk-based PMA moratorium at large scale.
editorial.body:
Wireless Telecommunications Activities concerns the infrastructure behind wireless communication on the earth’s surface: operating, maintaining, or providing networks that use electromagnetic waves to transmit voice, data, text, audio, and video. It is an activity defined by the network itself, rather than by a single kind of message or customer. The work may involve the technical backbone through which communications travel wirelessly, from the infrastructure’s operation to its continuing upkeep.

Its scope spans infrastructure for both fixed and mobile services. Fixed networks may include fixed broadband, wireless broadband access, or microwave-link communication systems; mobile networks may include cellular service or radio-based systems such as radio trunking. It also includes leasing wireless network capacity to other telecommunications-network operators or telecommunications-service operators. In practical terms, this is an activity for businesses providing and running the wireless network layer, including the capacity on which other operators may rely.

The activity is open across the listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, and foreign ownership is permitted up to the 100% ceiling. That makes the national position unusually direct: foreign investment is open up to the stated ceiling, while the activity remains available at every listed scale. The relevant national reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a more careful reading, but not a more pessimistic one. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is stated as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it beyond the risk bands covered by the provincial prohibition. For an activity operating at large scale in Bali, the stated risk level puts it outside that moratorium’s blocked bands. The Bali position is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: open in the sense that the moratorium does not block it, while its large-scale risk classification remains central to the local picture.
editorial.pullQuote: For an activity operating at large scale in Bali, the stated risk level puts it outside that moratorium’s blocked bands.

  3. Diagram dan rute serta peta jaringan;
  4. Cakupan wilayah pembangunan dan layanan yang akan dibangun (roll out plan) yang merupakan komitmen untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  5. Komitmen kinerja layanan untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  6. Data teknis alat/perangkat, sarana dan/atau prasarana telekomunikasi yang akan dibangun;
  7. Bukti kepemilikan perangkat;
  8. Perjanjian kerja sama dengan penyelenggara telekomunikasi lainnya;
  9. Pusat kontak informasi berkaitan dengan layanan prajual dan purnajual; dan
  10. Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) terkait monitoring jaringan, penanganan gangguan, billing dan penagihan, aktivasi dan deaktivasi pengguna/pelanggan, dan pelayanan pengguna/pelanggan.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity involves building and running satellite-based telecommunication networks for public connectivity—from launching and controlling satellites (geostationary, MEO, LEO) to operating earth stations and gateways. It also covers providing fixed satellite services like VSAT-based cellular backhaul that link two points via satellite infrastructure.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the local PMA moratorium, but its medium-high/high risk status means you must verify the specific address—licensing is possible but subject to extra verification and likely higher regulatory attention.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Telekomunikasi dengan Satelit (61103)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign satellite operators, VSAT providers, or telecom infrastructure companies that want to deploy satellite connectivity solutions—especially for backhaul or remote-area networks—in the Indonesian market.

editorial.headline: Satellite Networks, and Bali’s Higher-Risk Route
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the infrastructure and network work that turns satellite systems into public connectivity—nationally open to full foreign ownership, with a higher-risk but unblocked position in Bali.
editorial.body:
Satellite telecommunications is the operation, maintenance and provision of telecommunications networks using satellite infrastructure for public connectivity. Its practical estate includes geostationary satellites, medium- and low-earth-orbit satellites, earth stations, satellite-control centres, gateway exchanges and the connecting networks that make those assets useful as a system. It includes satellite-based network services: fixed links between two points—mobile backhaul through VSAT is the example named—and mobile services, without defining them by a particular application. It also includes making satellite-network capacity available to other telecommunications-network and telecommunications-service operators.

The code is open at each stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Its registrant is therefore an enterprise with a distinctly operational role: one that operates, maintains or provides satellite-based network infrastructure; supplies connectivity over that infrastructure; or leases capacity to other operators. The stated scope also expressly names basic telephony through satellites that have Landing Right, alongside fixed-mobile satellite-network operations. Registering at any of those scales does not change the activity’s defining subject: it remains satellite telecommunications infrastructure and network services rather than an application-specific service.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. A foreign investor can therefore hold the full stake under the national figure given here. That openness applies to this defined satellite-network activity: the provision, operation or maintenance of satellite infrastructure, satellite-based network services and capacity leasing described above. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali needs the same attention to wording. The province’s stated moratorium permanently blocks PMA across the island for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. This code is not blocked under that rule. Rather, its Bali record says that at Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The essential distinction is the higher risk classification at large scale, not a moratorium bar. The provincial rule is framed around risk levels, and this activity sits outside the two levels it blocks.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the activity is open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, it is higher risk at large scale but not barred by the moratorium.

Adanya perjanjian kerja sama antara penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi dengan pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi, dengan ketentuan sebagai berikut: a. Pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi menggunakan merek dagang layanan penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi yang dijual kembali dan dapat menambahkan merek dagang pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi kepada pelanggan (end user) b. Seluruh pendapatan dari pelaksanaan jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi menjadi pendapatan dari dan dibukukan oleh penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi d. Penagihan (billing) mencantumkan merek dagang penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi e. Dalam hal jual kembali layanan jasa telekomunikasi berbasis protokol internet, pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi wajib menggunakan alamat protokol internet (Internet Protocol Address/ IP Address) publik dan nomor sistem otonom (Autonomous System Number) milik penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers operating as a full Internet Service Provider (ISP) that owns and runs its own physical or wireless infrastructure—fiber, radio towers, satellite links—to deliver internet directly to end users. It includes dedicated business connections, public Wi-Fi hotspots, and even connectivity on planes and other transport.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Akses Internet (Internet Service Provider) (61104)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur who intends to build and operate their own internet infrastructure (not just resell someone else's service) to provide ISP-grade connectivity in homes, businesses, or public venues.

editorial.headline: Internet Access, Built on Infrastructure You Operate
editorial.standfirst: For operators serving end users through their own network infrastructure, this activity remains fully foreign-open nationally and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Internet access is the service at the centre of this activity, but the defining feature is the operator’s control of the infrastructure behind it. It covers an internet service provider that owns and operates its own cable, wireless or satellite infrastructure and delivers access directly to end users. The scope is therefore practical and broad: internet access through telecommunications networks, dedicated connections, public-space hotspots, and on-board connectivity, including internet access during flights, all sit within the activity described here.

The record opens this activity across the full range of business scales: micro, small, medium and large. That matters because the activity is not framed as a large-network proposition alone. Its stated field reaches from end-user access through a telecommunications network to more specific settings where connectivity is part of the environment itself—whether a dedicated connection for a user, a hotspot in public space, or access provided during transport. What remains constant is the model: the operator owns and runs the infrastructure used to provide the service.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is classified as open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership under the national position recorded for this code. That openness applies alongside availability at every listed business scale, giving the activity a notably complete national profile without requiring the editorial to add conditions that the record does not state.

Bali’s position is also open, rather than a disguised exclusion. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities across the island, but this activity is expressly not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status is recorded as OK or higher risk. At the large-business scale, the OSS risk classification is medium-high or high; this is why the activity is not caught by the moratorium. For a foreign-owned operator considering Bali, the honest reading is uncomplicated: PMA registration for this activity is not blocked there today.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign-owned operator considering Bali, PMA registration for this activity is not blocked there today.

data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup aktivitas penyelenggaraan jasa telekomunikasi berupa penyediaan jasa komunikasi data berbasis protokol internet dan/atau selain protokol internet melalui jaringan telekomunikasi dan/atau satelit asing yang telah memperoleh hak labuh (landing right) untuk memenuhi berbagai kebutuhan tertentu, dengan jaminan ketersambungan, kualitas, dan keamanan.
Kelompok ini juga termasuk
- aktivitas penyediaan jenis komunikasi data dalam jasa sistem komunikasi data, seperti komunikasi point-to-point, komunikasi remote host, komunikasi server-to-client, komunikasi machine-to-machine, dan komunikasi Internet of Things (IoT);
- aktivitas penyediaan jasa sistem komunikasi data yang mendukung penginderaan jarak jauh, pengukuran jarak jauh, kontrol jarak jauh, dan layanan perkantoran jarak jauh.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers providing data communication system services—supplying internet-protocol or non-IP data links over telecom networks or foreign satellites that hold landing rights. It includes point-to-point, remote host, server-to-client, and machine-to-machine connections, with guarantees of connectivity, quality, and security.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the investment moratorium, but it falls into a higher-risk category (medium-high/high). A PMA can be registered, but each business address will be verified separately—expect additional location checks to ensure compliance with risk requirements.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Sistem Komunikasi Data (61105)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs building private data networks, IoT/M2M connectivity platforms, or satellite-based data link services that need secure, high-quality transmission infrastructure.

editorial.headline: Data Communications as a Connected Service
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers dependable, secure data communications delivered through telecom networks or eligible foreign satellites, from machine links to remote-office systems.
editorial.body:
Data communications is the service here—not merely the infrastructure behind it. The activity encompasses telecommunications services that provide data communication using internet protocols and/or other protocols, delivered through telecommunications networks and/or foreign satellites that hold landing rights. Its defining promise is practical: connectivity, quality and security for particular requirements. That can mean a point-to-point connection, a remote-host arrangement, server-to-client communication, machine-to-machine links, or Internet of Things communication. It can also support remote sensing, measurement, control and remote-office services.

The breadth matters because the category follows the function of the service. A business may be creating the communications layer that allows devices, systems and people to exchange data reliably across distance. It may support a technical operation that needs remote monitoring or control; it may provide the connective tissue for distributed systems and offices. The record frames these as types of data communication within a communications-system service, with connectivity, quality and security forming the common standard rather than incidental features.

Businesses at each listed scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—can register for this activity. At the national level, this activity is TERBUKA to PMA and allows a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In straightforward terms, foreign ownership can reach 100% under the national position recorded here. That is the national opening founders should begin from, rather than treating the category as narrowly reserved for a particular size of enterprise.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: an investor considering a Bali registration is not facing a recorded PMA block for this activity, while the large-scale risk classification remains part of the practical picture. The useful conclusion is clean: the activity is nationally open to PMA up to full foreign ownership, and Bali’s stated moratorium does not prohibit its PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: Data communications is the service here—not merely the infrastructure behind it.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers running an IPTV service—delivering TV, radio, video, and other content over internet protocol networks with guaranteed quality, security, and interactive two-way capability between you and your subscribers.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: At national level, this is 100% open for foreign ownership. In Bali, it’s not blocked by the general moratorium, but it falls under medium-high to high risk; expect extra scrutiny during licensing and you must verify the specific commercial address is permitted for this activity.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitias Jasa Televisi Protokol Internet (IPTV) (61106)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur building a legitimate IPTV platform with proper infrastructure and compliance, not a reseller of pirated streams.

editorial.headline: IPTV’s Full-Service Definition—and Bali’s Real Position
editorial.standfirst: This IPTV activity spans converged digital content over IP networks, is open across every stated business scale, and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity is an internet-protocol television service, but the record defines it more broadly than television delivered online. It covers a telecommunications service that brings together radio, television, video, audio, text, graphics and data over an IP-based network. The service is to be delivered with assured quality, security and reliability, while retaining two-way interactivity between provider and subscriber. That combination is the centre of the classification: converged content, carried through an IP network, with the service qualities and interactive capability expressly named in the scope.

The registration picture is deliberately broad in scale. The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar as open registration scales. It therefore accommodates the activity across the full stated scale range, without reducing the classification to a single kind of operator. What must remain constant is the activity described: an IPTV telecommunications service whose content convergence and technical attributes are integral to the definition. The scale list says who may register at the stated sizes; it does not add a new service or revise the underlying scope.

At national level, PMA status is TERBUKA, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. In plain terms, the national record allows the activity to be held entirely by foreign capital. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign cap contained in this record, so the national position should be read directly: the activity is open to PMA up to the stated 100% ceiling. That is the relevant national position for an IPTV operation structured with wholly foreign ownership.

Bali is not a hidden reversal of that national position. Its recorded status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities; this activity is recorded as not blocked by that moratorium. A foreign investor is therefore not prevented from registering this activity in Bali by that specific moratorium. The honest reading is straightforward: the national 100% ceiling stands, and Bali does not block this activity under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: The national 100% ceiling stands, and Bali does not block this activity under the stated moratorium.

data.judul: Aktivitas Jasa Gerbang Akses Internet (Network Access Point)
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup aktivitas penyelenggaraan jasa telekomunikasi yang menyediakan layanan penyaluran trafik internet dan routing bagi penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi lainnya agar dapat terhubung ke jaringan internet internasional (IP Transit), terhubung dengan sesama penyelenggara jasa Gerbang Akses Internet (NAP), dan menjadi titik penyebaran akses internet di dalam negeri (Internet Exchange), serta sebagai penyimpan sementara (caching) dan/atau pengatur penyaluran (distribusi) konten internet.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers running an Internet Gateway or Network Access Point service – you provide the critical infrastructure that lets other telecommunication operators connect to the global internet (IP Transit), exchange traffic locally (Internet Exchange), and distribute or cache content. It’s the backbone layer that enables ISPs and content providers to route data efficiently within a country and internationally.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. On Bali, it falls under a higher-risk classification (medium-high/high risk), which means it is not blocked by the current moratorium but requires careful address verification – local zoning, building permits, and potentially sector-specific approvals may be scrutinized more closely before your company can be registered.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Gerbang Akses Internet (Network Access Point) (61107)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign telecom infrastructure investor or tech group that wants to build and operate the physical peering and caching hubs that power Indonesia’s internet connectivity.

editorial.headline: Internet Gateways: Open Nationally, Still Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity operates the infrastructure that moves, exchanges, routes and temporarily holds internet traffic—open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
An Internet Access Point is not a consumer internet service; it is part of the infrastructure that lets networks meet, exchange traffic and reach beyond Indonesia. The activity covers telecommunications services that carry and route internet traffic for other telecommunications providers. It includes IP Transit to international internet networks, connections with other Internet Access Point providers, and domestic Internet Exchange functions. It also encompasses the temporary storage of internet content through caching and the distribution of that content.

That scope places the business in the connective tissue of the internet rather than at its visible edge. Its role is to make pathways available: between telecommunications providers, towards international networks, and within Indonesia through points of access and exchange. Routing, traffic delivery, caching and content distribution are all expressly within the activity’s stated scope. For a founder, the practical importance is precision: this is the registration category for operating those network-access and interconnection services, not a broad label for every business that happens to use the internet.

Registration is open across the full scale spectrum recorded for this activity: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, its investment status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. Put simply, it allows full foreign ownership nationally. That conclusion rests on the stated national source, Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and should be read as the national position for this specific activity.

Bali does not reverse that position through its permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is marked as not blocked by that moratorium. The reason recorded is specific: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk level is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low reach. Bali’s status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali, while recognising that the record identifies a Medium-High/High OSS risk position at the Besar scale.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali because it is not blocked by the province’s Low and Medium-Low risk PMA moratorium.

persyaratan:
Rencana penyelenggaraan jaringan telekomunikasi yang memuat:

  1. Jenis layanan sesuai dengan penyelenggaraan yang dimohonkan;
  2. Konfigurasi sistem dan teknologi jaringan yang akan dibangun;
  3. Diagram dan rute serta peta jaringan;
  4. Cakupan wilayah pembangunan dan layanan yang akan dibangun (roll out plan) yang merupakan komitmen untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  5. Komitmen kinerja layanan untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  6. Data teknis alat/perangkat, sarana dan/atau prasarana telekomunikasi yang akan dibangun;
  7. Bukti kepemilikan perangkat;
  8. Perjanjian kerja sama dengan penyelenggara telekomunikasi lainnya;
  9. Pusat kontak informasi berkaitan dengan layanan prajual dan purnajual; dan
  10. Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) terkait monitoring jaringan, penanganan gangguan, billing dan penagihan, aktivasi dan deaktivasi pengguna/pelanggan, dan pelayanan pengguna/pelanggan.

per_skala.scope_uraian: Penyelenggaraan jaringan Tetap Tertutup Melalui Media Fiber Optik Teresterial
persyaratan:
Rencana penyelenggaraan jaringan telekomunikasi yang memuat:

  1. Jenis layanan sesuai dengan penyelenggaraan yang dimohonkan;
  2. Konfigurasi sistem dan teknologi jaringan yang akan dibangun;
  3. Diagram dan rute serta peta jaringan;
  4. Cakupan wilayah pembangunan dan layanan yang akan dibangun (roll out plan) yang merupakan komitmen untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  5. Komitmen kinerja layanan untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  6. Data teknis alat/perangkat, sarana dan/atau prasarana telekomunikasi yang akan dibangun;
  7. Bukti kepemilikan perangkat;
  8. Perjanjian kerja sama dengan penyelenggara telekomunikasi lainnya;
  9. Pusat kontak informasi berkaitan dengan layanan prajual dan purnajual; dan
  10. Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) terkait monitoring jaringan, penanganan gangguan, billing dan penagihan, aktivasi dan deaktivasi pengguna/pelanggan, dan pelayanan pengguna/pelanggan.

Pernyataan:

  1. Kesanggupan melaksanakan ketentuan penyelenggaraan jaringan; dan
  2. Menyampaikan data yang valid dan benar.

Daftar susunan pengurus untuk membuktikan bahwa Direksi, Pengurus, dan/atau Badan Hukum Pelaku Usaha tidak ditetapkan dalam Daftar Hitam Penyelenggara.

per_skala.scope_uraian: Penyelenggaraan Jasa teleponi dasar melalui satelit yang telah memperoleh Hak Labuh (Landing Right)
persyaratan:
Rencana penyelenggaraan jaringan telekomunikasi yang memuat:

  1. Jenis layanan sesuai dengan penyelenggaraan yang dimohonkan;
  2. Konfigurasi sistem dan teknologi jaringan yang akan dibangun;
  3. Diagram dan rute serta peta jaringan;
  4. Cakupan wilayah pembangunan dan layanan yang akan dibangun (roll out plan) yang merupakan komitmen untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  5. Komitmen kinerja layanan untuk 5 (lima) tahun;
  6. Data teknis alat/perangkat, sarana dan/atau prasarana telekomunikasi yang akan dibangun;
  7. Bukti kepemilikan perangkat;
  8. Perjanjian kerja sama dengan penyelenggara telekomunikasi lainnya;
  9. Pusat kontak informasi berkaitan dengan layanan prajual dan purnajual; dan
  10. Standard Operation Procedure (SOP) terkait monitoring jaringan, penanganan gangguan, billing dan penagihan, aktivasi dan deaktivasi pengguna/pelanggan, dan pelayanan pengguna/pelanggan.

Daftar susunan pengurus untuk membuktikan bahwa Direksi, Pengurus, dan/atau Badan Hukum Pelaku Usaha tidak ditetapkan dalam Daftar Hitam Penyelenggara.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the operation of basic telephone services that deliver voice calls directly to end users, using traditional circuit-switched or modern technologies, via fixed lines, mobile networks, or satellites. It’s the core “phone company” activity of connecting people for voice communication.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: While nationally the KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership, in Bali it falls into a higher-risk classification that is not blocked by the current moratorium, but requires extra verification per business address. You can likely register a PMA here, though expect closer scrutiny and stricter licensing conditions compared to a low-risk activity.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Teleponi Dasar (61108)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign telecom operators or infrastructure investors looking to offer direct basic voice services to residential or business customers in Indonesia.

editorial.headline: Basic Telephony, With a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity delivers basic voice telephone services to end users and is open to 100% foreign ownership nationally, including PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 61108 covers the provision of basic telephony services directly to end users. In plain terms, it is the business of carrying fundamental voice communications for customers—not merely supporting a telecommunications operation in the background, but providing the telephone service itself. The service may run through circuit-switched technology or other technologies, and may be delivered over fixed networks, mobile networks or satellite. Its centre of gravity is basic voice communication supplied directly to the customer.

The scope also encompasses the operation of basic telephony services through telecommunications networks and a fixed international-connection network. That makes this a code for businesses operating at the service layer of voice connectivity: organisations whose offering reaches the end user and whose infrastructure can span more than one network form. The activity is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises, so the classification does not reserve the field for a single business scale. Its practical identity is defined by the direct provision of basic voice service, whatever the underlying network technology.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is classified as open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign-owned company may therefore hold the full permitted stake under the national position recorded here. That openness matters because basic telephony is often understood through infrastructure alone; this classification instead makes the end-user service the key point, while allowing the technology and network type to vary.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. For this activity, however, the recorded OSS risk at Large scale is Medium-High or High, placing it outside that moratorium rather than within it. The Bali status is therefore OK or Higher Risk, and the record expressly confirms that it is not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign investor considering Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: this activity can be registered for PMA there today, with the national foreign-ownership ceiling remaining 100%.

data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup aktivitas penjualan kembali jasa telekomunikasi yang diperoleh melalui kerja sama dengan Penyelenggara Jasa Telekomunikasi, termasuk aktivitas jual kembali jasa akses internet melalui jaringan antara pelanggan dan Penyedia Layanan Internet (ISP) yang tidak dimiliki atau dioperasikan oleh ISP tersebut, seperti akses Internet dial-up, dan sebagainya.
Aktivitas pada kelompok ini di dalam pelaksanaannya, Penyelenggara wajib menjamin keberlangsungan layanan, sementara pelaksana jual kembali menggunakan merek dagang Penyelenggara (dengan kemungkinan menambahkan mereknya sendiri), memenuhi standar kualitas layanan yang ditetapkan, serta seluruh pendapatan dibukukan sebagai pendapatan Penyelenggara. Penagihan (billing) dilakukan atas nama Penyelenggara Jasa Telekomunikasi. Untuk layanan berbasis protokol internet, pelaksana jual kembali wajib menggunakan alamat IP publik dan Nomor Sistem Otonom (Autonomous System Number) milik Penyelenggara Jasa Telekomunikasi.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- aktivitas penyelenggaraan jasa akses internet oleh operator telekomunikasi yang memiliki dan mengoperasikan infrastruktur jaringan sendiri, lihat kelompok 61104.

editorial.headline: Telecom Resale: Nationally Open, Scope-Dependent in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the resale of telecommunications services under a provider’s framework—open to full foreign ownership nationally, but dependent on the exact risk scope declared in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is a telecommunications-service resale activity. The business obtains services through cooperation with a Telecommunications Service Provider and sells them on again, including resold internet access delivered through a network that the relevant ISP does not own or operate. The commercial role is therefore defined by resale within a provider-led service arrangement, rather than by an independent service framework of its own.

That arrangement is deliberately structured. The Telecommunications Service Provider must ensure continuity of service; the reseller uses the provider’s trade mark, although it may add its own. The reseller must meet the prescribed service-quality standards, while all revenue is recorded as the provider’s revenue and billing is issued in the provider’s name. For internet-protocol-based services, the reseller must use the provider’s public IP addresses and Autonomous System Number. These details matter because they describe not merely a sales channel, but the operational boundaries of the activity itself.

The code is open nationally to businesses at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale. Its foreign-investment status is TERBUKA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In national terms, that is a clear opening: foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity. The applicable source cited in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The activity is not marked as absolutely blocked for PMA registration, but its Bali status is scope-dependent. Across Bali, PMA registration is permanently blocked for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activity. The record says that some scopes at Besar scale may carry low OSS risk while others carry higher risk; PMA registration in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope. The practical conclusion is precise rather than dramatic: national openness remains real, but a Bali registration depends on the exact activity scope and must be verified in live OSS before relying on it.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness remains real, but a Bali registration depends on the exact activity scope declared in live OSS.

editorial.headline: The Business of Making Telecom Capacity Reach the Market
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the resale, brokering and agency intermediation that connects telecom capacity, service packages and public access with users.
editorial.body:
This activity sits in the commercial layer of telecommunications: the businesses that resell services, arrange transactions, and represent operators rather than simply supplying the underlying network. Its scope includes buying and reselling cable, wireless and satellite telecommunications capacity; telecom brokering; and the resale of prepaid calling cards. It also reaches the intermediary work around those services, where an agency sells on behalf of an operator or helps place a service package with the customer.

That intermediary role is broad enough to include agencies for cable, wireless and satellite telecommunications, agents selling mobile-phone service packages, agents selling wireless telephone packages in the name of a wireless operator, and agencies serving mobile virtual network operators. The same activity also includes the provision of telephone and internet access in facilities open to the public, including telephone shops and internet cafés. In practical terms, the code describes a route-to-market business: reselling capacity, placing packages, acting as an agent, or providing public access.

At the national level, the activity permits foreign investment up to the full 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar business scales. That is the clean national position: a foreign investor may participate fully in an activity built around telecom resale and intermediation, provided the registered activity is the one actually being carried on.

Bali requires a more exact reading of the proposed scope. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis. For this activity, the record does not impose a blanket Bali block; instead, its PMA registrability depends on the declared scope. Some scopes at the Besar scale are low risk, while others carry a higher risk. PMA registration in Bali is available only when the higher-risk scope is declared, and the exact activity should be verified in live OSS. The national opening remains real, but in Bali the registration outcome turns on how the business’s actual telecom role is stated.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: While nationally a PMA can be 100% foreign-owned, in Bali this activity is classified as higher risk (medium-high/high) and therefore requires extra verification, especially of the physical commercial address. It is not blocked by the current moratorium, so registration is possible, but you should expect a more detailed review process.

editorial.headline: Premium Calls: Nationally Open, Clearly Read in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A premium-call operation is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not marked as blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Premium-call services under this code are defined by how the call is delivered. The activity is the operation of premium-tariff telephone calling services that use an intelligent-network (IN) premium-call access code to connect the caller with a premium-call agent and/or a recorded information service. Each part matters: it is a telephone calling service, the tariff is premium, and the connection uses the named intelligent-network access code. The agent and recorded-information routes are both within the stated scope: the and/or wording allows either connection as well as a combination of the two.

The scale field is equally direct. Micro, Small, Medium and Large are all listed as open to this activity, so the record does not confine premium-call service operations to one listed business size. The scale label sits beside a precise operational description: a registration at any of those stated sizes still concerns premium-tariff telephone calls, the IN access code, and a connection to a premium-call agent, recorded information, or both. It gives founders a clear account of who may register by scale without changing what the activity is.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The code is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. In ordinary terms, the national record permits a fully foreign-owned PMA registration for this activity. That is the full national ceiling stated for the code; it is not a partial foreign-share allowance. For a founder deciding whether this precise premium-call operation can sit in a foreign-owned company, the national answer in the record is yes, up to the stated 100% maximum.

Bali calls for a separate, equally plain reading. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This record, however, is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and its explanation says that, at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High—so it is not caught by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is not a workaround: this premium-call activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not moratorium-blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the supplied record. The Bali risk observation is expressly tied to the Large scale.

kewajiban: Memenuhi standar usaha aktivitas jasa jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi

Adanya perjanjian kerja sama antara penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi dengan pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi, dengan ketentuan sebagai berikut: a. Pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi menggunakan merek dagang layanan penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi yang dijual kembali dan dapat menambahkan merek dagang pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi kepada pelanggan (end user) b. Pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi memenuhi ketentuan standar kualitas pelayanan jasa telekomunikasi yang telah dikomitmenkan oleh penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi c. Seluruh pendapatan dari pelaksanaan jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi menjadi pendapatan dari dan dibukukan oleh penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi d. Penagihan (billing) mencantumkan merek dagang penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi e. Dalam hal jual kembali layanan jasa telekomunikasi berbasis protokol internet, pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi wajib menggunakan alamat protokol internet (Internet Protocol Address/ IP Address) publik dan nomor sistem otonom (Autonomous System Number) milik penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi

Penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi yang melakukan kerja sama jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi wajib menjamin keberlangsungan seluruh layanan telekomunikasi yang diselenggarakan nya

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers running a service that delivers paid content via SMS text messages on mobile networks, including premium SMS. Payment happens by deducting prepaid credit or adding to postpaid bills. The content can be text, audio, images, animation, or a mix — like polling, quizzes, ringback tones, subscription info, and other interactive features.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open for foreign ownership (PMA). In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Konten SMS Premium (61902)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs aiming to offer interactive mobile content services (like voting, quizzes, or personalised ringtones) directly to Indonesian consumers through telecom operator partnerships.

editorial.headline: Premium SMS Content Services: Open Nationally, Clear of Bali’s Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers paid content delivered by mobile SMS, from polls to interactive subscriptions, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Premium SMS Content Services covers the organisation and provision of content sent through mobile-network text messaging, including premium SMS. Its commercial mechanism is explicit: customers pay by a deduction from prepaid credit or through postpaid billing. The content may be written material, sound, images, animation, or a combination. Polls, quizzes, personalised ringback tones, subscription information and other interactive services are named examples. Taken together, these details define an activity built around paid content delivered in messages on a cellular mobile network, with both the message medium and the billing route forming part of the stated scope.

The registration is open at the micro, small, medium and large scales. That breadth is significant because the record does not confine the activity to one content form: a text offer, sound, imagery, animation or a combination can all sit within the described service when delivered through SMS. Nor is the scope limited to one interaction model; polling, quizzes, personalised ringback tones, subscription information and other interactive services all appear in its examples. The common thread is not a particular creative output but the provision of content over mobile SMS with the stated charging method.

Nationally, the status is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Put plainly, foreign ownership may reach full ownership for this activity at the national level; the record supplies no lower national ceiling. The PMA basis listed is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is the essential national position for a foreign-owned setup: the activity is recorded as open, rather than as an arrangement in which the foreign share is capped below 100%. That conclusion concerns ownership access; the activity itself remains defined by the provision of paid SMS content described above.

Bali requires a separate reading. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record gives a specific reason: at the large scale, the OSS risk is medium-high/high, so the moratorium does not block it; the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The Bali conclusion is therefore direct, but limited to what the record says: a foreign investor is not prevented from registering this activity in Bali by the stated moratorium. No local percentage or partnership condition is given here, so the national 100% ceiling remains the ownership figure stated for the activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Foreign ownership may reach full ownership for this activity at the national level; the record supplies no lower national ceiling.

Pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi menggunakan merek dagang layanan penyelenggara jasa telekomunikasi yang dijual kembali dan dapat menambahkan merek dagang pelaksana jual kembali jasa telekomunikasi kepada pelanggan (end user) b. intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers providing voice call services to the public using internet protocol (VoIP) – like long-distance and international calls – without needing to own the physical transmission network. It's essentially running a phone service over the internet for general use.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this code is 100% open for foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Jasa Internet Teleponi untuk Keperluan Publik (ITKP) (61903)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who want to launch internet-based telephony services for the public, like VoIP calling platforms or international direct-dial solutions.

editorial.headline: Internet Telephony in Bali: Open Nationally, Outside the Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers public internet-based voice calling without transmission infrastructure—and remains open to PMA registration in Bali under the record’s stated risk position.
editorial.body:
Internet Telephony Services for Public Use (ITKP) is about organising public call and voice-communication services over Internet Protocol, or VoIP. Its defining boundary is equally important: the provider does not own or operate the transmission facilities themselves. The scope also expressly includes long-distance direct-dial and international direct-dial telephony services delivered through internet networks. In other words, this is a service activity built around internet-based voice communications, rather than the operation of the underlying transmission infrastructure.

The code is open across every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth matters because the activity is not confined in the record to a particular size of operator. A business registering under it is providing the public-facing call or voice-communication service described in the scope, including the specified long-distance and international calling functions, while remaining outside the ownership and operation of transmission facilities.

Nationally, the PMA status is **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The record therefore supports a straightforward national reading: foreign ownership may reach 100% for this activity. Its stated PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no need to soften that position with invented thresholds or unlisted obligations; the national position in this record is an open one, expressed through a full foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that result today. The record marks the activity as not blocked for PMA registration in Bali, with the local status recorded as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. At the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High, which is why it is not caught by the provincial moratorium described here. That moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration across Bali for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity sits outside that stated restriction. For a founder, the distinction is clean: the national position is fully open to foreign ownership, and the Bali moratorium identified in the record does not block this code.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is fully open to foreign ownership, and the Bali moratorium identified in the record does not block this code.

editorial.headline: Calling Cards, With Control at Their Core
editorial.standfirst: Managed calling-card services are nationally open to full foreign ownership and may be registered by PMA in Bali, where their large-scale risk position sits outside the provincial moratorium.
editorial.body:
A managed calling-card service is best understood as a calling service built around controlled access, rather than as an unadorned act of making a call. Its stated features are user authentication or a call-management system, operated through a special access code. Those features serve two named purposes: controlling use and supporting billing that is prepaid or managed. The classification therefore describes a service in which the code, authentication, and management layer are integral to the offer. They are the mechanism through which users reach the calling service and through which use and charging are organised.

The activity is open to registration at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. The record does not reserve this description for one business tier; it recognises the smallest listed scale, the middle tiers, and the largest. A business registering the activity at any of those scales is still defined by the same core proposition: a calling service with an added authentication or call-management feature, using special access codes to organise controlled use and prepaid or managed billing. Scale identifies the range of registrations available, while the stated service features identify the activity being registered.

At the national level, the PMA position is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. This permits full foreign ownership for the activity nationally. It is a clear ownership answer, but it does not broaden the business description. The registration remains anchored to the managed calling service stated in the record: the extra authentication or call-management feature, the special access code, and the practical function of usage control and prepaid or managed billing. That focus keeps the ownership conclusion and the operational scope in their proper places: both are specific to this activity.

Bali carries no block on PMA registration for this activity. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registrations for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, across the island and permanently. This activity’s stated position is different: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and the record says it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest reading is straightforward: a foreign investor may register this activity in Bali today, and the stated reason is that the large-scale OSS risk position does not fall within the moratorium’s Low or Medium-Low reach. The record’s Bali conclusion is therefore about moratorium coverage; nationally, the 100% ceiling remains the stated ownership figure.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor may register this activity in Bali today, because its large-scale OSS risk position does not fall within the moratorium’s Low or Medium-Low reach.

editorial.headline: Satellite Special Telecoms: Nationally Open, Bali Address-Specific
editorial.standfirst: Satellite-specific communications operations—from tracking and earth stations to orbital systems—are nationally open to foreign ownership, while Bali requires an address-specific verification.
editorial.body:
Satellite special telecommunications is a deliberately bounded field: communications services using satellite technology and/or satellite networks for communications, navigation, monitoring and remote sensing. Its perimeter is defined as much by what it excludes as by what it includes: it is not the provision of general connectivity. The scope names specialised applications such as satellite tracking, communication telemetry and the operation of radar stations. These are distinct operational uses of satellite-enabled telecommunications, grouped around a particular function rather than a service offered as general connectivity. That distinction gives the activity its practical centre of gravity.

It also reaches from the ground to orbit. The record includes the operation of satellite terminal, or earth, stations and related facilities on the ground, when they are operationally connected with one or more terrestrial communications systems. Their function may be to transmit communications to a satellite or receive them from one. At the orbital end, the activity includes operating satellites for remote sensing, navigation and specialised telecommunications, with low-Earth-orbit telecommunications satellites given as an example. The resulting picture is of a defined operating activity across stations, related facilities and satellites, held together by specialised satellite communications rather than ordinary network access.

Registration remains open across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the PMA status is open, and the maximum foreign ownership is 100 percent under the stated Perpres basis. For a foreign-owned business, that is a direct national position: the record does not place the foreign stake below full ownership for this activity. The wide scale range is similarly explicit. It says the classification is available from Mikro through Besar, without narrowing the activity to a single listed business scale.

Bali needs a more local reading, but the record does not show a prohibition. Its Bali assessment is medium-high/high risk and expressly says it is not blocked by the moratorium, while also requiring verification for the particular address. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This activity is therefore not shown as caught by that blanket restriction. The distinction matters: national foreign investment may reach 100 percent; in Bali, the record's conclusion rests on the activity's recorded risk level and an address-specific check. National openness is clear here; Bali adds an address-specific verification rather than a moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is clear here; Bali adds an address-specific verification rather than a moratorium block.
