editorial.headline: When an Open Brokerage Meets Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: Securities and commodity-contract brokerage is open to foreign investment nationally, yet Bali’s PMA moratorium stops a registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor seeking PMA registration, the decisive fact is geographic: this activity cannot be registered at a Bali address today. It is nationally open to foreign investment, but Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The record identifies the Besar scale here as Medium-Low, placing the activity within that prohibition. The result is location-specific, not a revision of the activity’s national foreign-ownership position.

At its core, the activity is brokerage in securities and commodity contracts. It covers acting as broker in those transactions and conducting financial-market trades on another person’s behalf. Its defining feature is agency: the business brings a client’s instruction to market rather than buying or selling for its own account. The scope gives bullion trading on behalf of another party as an example of that brokerage role. In every case, the client is the person whose market interest the broker represents.

The distinction makes the category practical as well as technical. It is for a business that stands between a client and the market in an intermediary capacity, not one trading its own financial-market position. A firm may arrange or execute the specified transactions as broker, provided it is acting for someone else. Trading on the firm’s own account is expressly outside the stated scope. That boundary keeps the activity anchored to brokerage rather than turning it into a general label for participation in financial markets.

Nationally, the field is TERBUKA: foreign investors may hold up to 100%, and registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. In Bali, the relevant fact is whether a PMA registration can proceed at a Bali address. It cannot. Because the Besar scale is classified as Menengah Rendah, it falls inside the island-wide, permanent moratorium described in the record. The rule applies across the province and is tied to a Governor’s letter dated May 13, 2026. Put plainly: nationally this activity is fully foreign-open; for a PMA registration with a Bali address, it is blocked today.
editorial.pullQuote: Put plainly: nationally this activity is fully foreign-open; for a PMA registration with a Bali address, it is blocked today.

editorial.standfirst: This activity covers clearing and settlement across financial markets, with national foreign ownership open to 100% but PMA registration blocked for a Bali address.

This activity sits behind the completion of financial-market transactions: it covers clearing and settlement for securities, commodity contracts, money-market and foreign-exchange transactions, digital financial assets, and other financial-market dealings. In plain terms, its subject is the process by which those transactions are cleared and settled across the markets named in the record. That breadth matters. The activity is defined by this transaction-completion function, rather than by one asset class alone.

Registration is open at every scale recorded—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes scale an inclusive national entry point in the record, not a narrow label reserved for a single size of business. Yet the Bali assessment adds a crucial qualification within that same record: the Besar scale is classed as Menengah Rendah for the relevant local assessment. The label matters because it is the classification to which the Bali PMA restriction attaches.

Nationally, the position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor therefore has a nationally open route to this activity under the stated national basis, Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. Bali is different. The activity is marked Closed (Bali moratorium) and blocked for PMA registration at a Bali address. The record explains that the Bali PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI island-wide and permanently; for this activity, the recorded Menengah Rendah assessment brings that block into force.

That is the decision-critical reading for a founder considering a Bali address. The national 100% ceiling does not override the local result: today, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali. Nor does the availability of Mikro through Besar change the stated moratorium outcome. The record presents national openness and Bali closure as two separate facts that must be read together. The precise conclusion is simple: nationally open, yet unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the permanent island-wide moratorium recorded here.

editorial.headline: Financial Asset Custody: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This custody activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership across every enterprise scale, yet PMA registration at a Bali address is blocked by the province’s permanent moratorium.
editorial.body:
Financial asset custody is the quiet infrastructure behind market transactions: this activity covers safekeeping services for financial assets traded on financial markets. Its remit includes securities, assets connected with collective investment portfolios, commodity futures contracts, bullion financial assets and digital financial assets. The common thread is custody—holding assets and contracts within a financial-market context rather than creating or trading them. It brings both financial assets and commodity-futures contracts within one clearly custodial description.

At the national level, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The scale listing is equally broad: micro, small, medium and large enterprises may register it. For a founder considering a PMA structure, those two points set out a clear national position. The activity is not confined to one business size and, on this record, foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership. Its national PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali is where that national answer stops being decisive. A foreigner cannot register this activity through a PMA at a Bali address today. The Bali record marks it closed under the province’s PMA moratorium and identifies the large-scale classification as Medium-Low risk. The permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA for activities in the Low and Medium-Low risk bands. National openness is real, but it does not override Bali’s address-based PMA moratorium.

The distinction is practical. “Open” is the national status here, not a portable conclusion that overrides a location rule. Nationally, the record permits full foreign ownership and lists every enterprise scale. At a Bali address, the operative conclusion reverses: the PMA route is blocked by the moratorium. Read plainly, this is a custodial financial-services activity that is nationally open, including to a 100% foreign stake, while its registration outcome in Bali is closed to PMA. The difference lies in the Bali rule, not in ambiguity about its national status.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Infrastructure Behind Securities Ownership
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 66133 covers the contracted administration that records securities ownership and distributes the rights attached to those securities.
editorial.body:
KBLI 66133 is the administrative backbone of securities ownership. It covers the work of recording who owns securities and administering the distribution of rights connected to those securities and/or their issuers. The activity is performed under a contract with the issuer: a business is engaged by that issuer to maintain ownership records and handle the allocation of the associated rights. Its subject is therefore precise—ownership records and the rights that follow from them—rather than a broad claim over every activity connected with securities.

The code is available at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record does not reserve the activity for one size of enterprise. A prospective registrant should nevertheless keep the contractual centre of gravity in view. The work described here is carried out for an issuer, under contract, and consists of recording ownership and distributing related rights. A clear operating description should remain faithful to that relationship and to those two functions.

At the national level, PMA is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap in the record to soften or qualify: the national ceiling is the full 100%.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province-wide moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, but this code is not blocked by that moratorium. For the Besar scale, the OSS risk position is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than blocked. The practical picture is consequently direct: this activity is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali moratorium does not block its PMA registration on the stated risk basis.
editorial.pullQuote: This activity is nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali moratorium does not block its PMA registration on the stated risk basis.

editorial.headline: Payment Services: A Clear National and Bali Route for Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the customer-facing infrastructure of payments, from payment accounts and remittances to acquiring and payment gateways.
editorial.body:
Payment Services Provision is the front-end work of making a payment system usable for its end users. It covers the administration of payment funding sources, including the issuance of payment instruments or payment accounts; the transmission of fund-transfer instructions, including remittance services; and the transmission of payment-transaction data. In practice, its scope reaches the customer-facing functions around displaying funding-source information, initiating transactions, acquiring, electronic wallets, payment accounts, fund transfers and payment gateways.

It is a category for businesses that sit where a user meets the payment system: the point at which an account is issued, a transfer is sent onward, a transaction is initiated, or payment data is routed through an acquiring or gateway function. The definition is broad enough to encompass connected payment-service activities, yet precise about their position on the front end. It is not framed as a back-office abstraction; it describes services supplied directly to the end user of the payment system.

The registration picture is notably straightforward at national level. Foreign investment is permitted, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. It is also open across the full stated range of business scales: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. For a founder assessing market entry, that means the record does not place a lower ownership ceiling on a foreign investor nationally, nor reserve the activity to one business-size category.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. This code is not blocked for PMA registration under the province-wide moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The Bali record identifies Large-scale OSS risk as Medium-High/High, which is why the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today; nationally it is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali’s stated moratorium does not close that route for this code.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today, with national foreign ownership open up to 100%.

editorial.headline: Payment-System Infrastructure: Open Nationally, Viable in Bali at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the infrastructure behind payment transfers—from switching and clearing to final settlement—and is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
Payment-system infrastructure is the operational framework that allows payment-transfer transactions to move through clearing and settlement. Its remit includes acting as a principal, providing switching functions, and maintaining the records needed to identify parties involved in completing a payment transaction. It also covers infrastructure primarily used to facilitate transactions for Payment Service Providers, whether for the providers’ own purposes or for end users. In practical terms, this is the activity behind the systems that route, reconcile and complete payments rather than the payment transaction itself.

The activity is open across every recorded business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth matters because the scope is defined by the infrastructure function, not by a single size of operator. A business may be positioned around principal functions, switching, clearing, final settlement, or the administration of identities connected with transaction completion. Each sits within the same activity where it forms part of organising the payment-system infrastructure described in the record.

At the national level, this activity is open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In Bali, it is not blocked for PMA registration under the island-wide rule that blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The record’s reason is specific: at the Large scale, OSS risk is Medium-High or High, placing this activity outside that moratorium. The Bali picture is therefore not a hidden prohibition: it remains available for PMA registration, while its recorded risk position at the Large scale is higher.

That distinction is the useful one for a founder assessing the activity. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling establish the investment position; Bali’s result turns on the activity’s recorded risk classification at scale rather than on a separate foreign-ownership cap. The code should consequently be read as payment infrastructure with a nationally open investment route and a Bali position that is not caught by the permanent moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities.

editorial.headline: Payment-System Support Is Infrastructure, Not a Footnote
editorial.standfirst: From card personalisation and terminals to data centres and routing, this activity supports payment processing—and remains open to full foreign ownership nationally and unblocked in Bali by the stated moratorium.
editorial.body:
Payment systems are often noticed only at the moment a customer taps a card or an online transaction is approved. This activity concerns the enabling work that lets that moment be processed at all. It covers services supporting payment-service providers and payment-system infrastructure operators in processing payment transactions. In practical terms, that includes card printing, payment personalisation, data centres and disaster-recovery centres, terminals, security features for payment instruments or transactions, contactless-transaction technology, and routing data that supports transaction processing.

The definition marks out a broad supporting function. Its subject is the operational and technical layer around payment processing: the equipment, data pathways, resilience arrangements and security features that help payment systems function. The examples range from physical card production and terminals to data-centre provision, disaster recovery, contactless technology and routing. What joins them is their role in supporting the processing of payment transactions and the associated payment-system infrastructure.

The activity is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The national position is recorded under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder considering the activity across Indonesia, the essential point is clear: foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership. The stated scale range is equally significant, placing this supporting activity within the record from Mikro through Besar rather than confining it to one business scale.

Bali requires its own reading, but it does not reverse that national position. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration island-wide for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The recorded reason is specific: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low reach. For this activity, the Bali question turns not on a blanket ban but on how its risk position sits outside the provincial moratorium. In plain terms, foreign-owned registration is not blocked in Bali today on the moratorium ground recorded here.
editorial.pullQuote: For this activity, the Bali question turns not on a blanket ban but on how its risk position sits outside the provincial moratorium.

editorial.headline: The Business of Keeping Rupiah Moving
editorial.standfirst: A look at the businesses that keep rupiah circulating and cash machines supplied—and why a nationally open PMA activity is not blocked by Bali’s risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
Rupiah handling is infrastructure work, not simply the movement of cash from one counter to another. This activity covers the distribution of rupiah, its custody in cash vaults and its processing. It also embraces the practical cycle that keeps cash machines useful: putting cash into, taking cash from, and monitoring the adequacy of cash in ATMs, cash deposit machines, cash recycling machines and other cash-rupiah transaction machines. It extends to supplying and maintaining those machines, as well as cooperation connected with bringing foreign banknotes into and out of Indonesia’s customs territory.

That scope makes this an activity for enterprises that operate the machinery and systems behind cash availability: businesses handling physical rupiah, managing vault-based storage and processing, or maintaining the devices through which customers deposit, withdraw or recycle it. The record opens the activity to Micro, Small, Medium and Large businesses. This is broad in scale, but not in subject matter: the common thread is the operational handling of rupiah and the associated cash-machine estate.

Nationally, the PMA position is open, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. Put plainly, the record does not set a national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The cited basis is Presidential Regulations 10/2021 and 49/2021. That national reading should be kept separate from Bali’s local risk treatment: national openness does not erase the way Bali’s PMA moratorium is applied.

Bali’s stated rule permanently blocks PMA for all low and medium-low risk activities across the province. This activity is not marked as blocked. Instead, the Bali record says that at the Large scale its OSS risk is Medium-High/High, placing it outside the moratorium’s blocked category. Its Bali classification is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The distinction is precise: this is an activity open to PMA nationally and not blocked in Bali by the island-wide moratorium because its large-scale risk sits above the barred bands.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not erase the way Bali’s PMA moratorium is applied.

editorial.headline: Financial Transaction Clearing: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers financial transaction clearing and settlement outside payment systems and fund transfers—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but blocked for PMA registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
This activity is concerned with organising financial transactions and managing rupiah outside the financial markets, where the work is not otherwise classified. Its practical centre of gravity is the machinery of clearing and settlement: bringing transactions to completion after they have been made. The stated examples are deliberately narrow and useful—clearing and settling financial transactions other than those belonging to payment systems and fund transfers. It is an operational financial-services activity, defined by the orderly completion and administration of transactions rather than by participation in the financial markets themselves.

The activity is open to businesses at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale. At national level, this activity carries PMA status TERBUKA, and its foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. That is a clear national position: a foreign investor may hold the full permitted stake in a company registered for this activity. The applicable national reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the activity on an Indonesia-wide basis, there is no foreign-equity reduction stated in the record.

Bali produces a materially different answer. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA at a Bali address today. The record identifies the Besar scale as Menengah Rendah and states that it is blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium. That moratorium applies across the province and permanently blocks PMA registration for KBLI activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk. The restriction is therefore not a national foreign-ownership limit disguised as a local preference; it is a Bali-address registration block for PMA.

That distinction matters because the national and Bali positions can both be true at once. Nationally, this is a fully foreign-open activity, with 100% foreign ownership permitted. In Bali, however, the provincial PMA moratorium controls the immediate registration outcome for a Bali address. The sensible reading is not that foreign ownership has been reduced, but that the PMA route is unavailable there under the stated moratorium. Founders should treat the location of registration as central to the analysis: the national framework describes the ownership ceiling, while Bali’s rule determines whether PMA registration can proceed on the island.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Investment advisory services — providing professional advice to clients on investment decisions, portfolio allocation, and financial planning, whether for securities, real estate, or other asset classes. You advise, you don't manage or trade on behalf of clients.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**Micro / Small / Medium / Large scale**: Medium-Low risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued automatically.


**PMA:** Fully open to PMA — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Unchanged from KBLI 2020 — direct match.
intel_2026.baliContext: Investment advisory in the securities market requires OJK registration as a Penasihat Investasi (PI) under POJK 10/2018. Advisors who manage client portfolios cross into fund management territory (66301). The growing number of wealthy foreigners investing in Bali's property and business market creates demand for locally-based investment advisors. IFRS and Indonesian PSAK accounting standards knowledge is important for cross-border advisory.
intel_2026.youllAlsoNeed:
- OJK Penasihat Investasi license — if advising on securities
- 66301 — Investment management if you actively manage funds
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Investment advisory services in Bali? Let me explain OJK licensing and the scope of advice you can legally provide.

editorial.headline: Investment Advice, With a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: This is the paid business of advising clients on the sale or purchase of securities, open nationally to foreign investment and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Investment advisory activity is, at its core, the paid provision of advice on whether another party should sell or buy securities. It is not framed here as trading on a client’s behalf or as a general commercial consultation: the activity is specifically the giving of investment advice about securities transactions in return for a service fee. The scope is deliberately neutral about the client, the instrument beyond securities, and the form of advice; its defining feature is professional guidance on a purchase or sale decision.

Both individuals and companies may carry out the activity. An individual investment adviser gives that advice directly to another party for compensation; a company does the same through its business activity. The code is open across the full stated range of business scales: micro, small, medium, and large. That matters because the activity is not confined in the record to a particular size of operator. It can therefore describe a professional practice as well as an investment-advisory company operating at a larger scale.

The national foreign-investment position is straightforward. The PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record does not place a national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The national basis cited is the relevant presidential-regulation source, but the essential editorial point is simpler: investment advisory activity is nationally open to PMA at the stated ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that position through its island-wide PMA moratorium. The provincial rule blocks all low- and medium-low-risk activities from PMA registration. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the large scale, its OSS risk is recorded as medium-high or high, and its Bali status is recorded as OK or higher risk. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today without the moratorium being the obstacle. For founders, that is the distinction worth retaining: the national position is fully open, and Bali’s special restriction does not close this route.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today without the moratorium being the obstacle.

Surat pernyataan tertulis di atas materai mengenai:

  1. Kesanggupan memenuhi aspek keselamatan, kesehatan kerja dan pengelolaan lingkungan hidup;
  2. Kesanggupan memenuhi kewajiban badan usaha;
  3. Kesediaan dilakukan audit kepatuhan terhadap ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan;
  4. Kesanggupan badan usaha menjamin dan bertanggung jawab bahwa sarana dan fasilitas yang dimiliki/dikuasai layak beroperasi dan mampu dijalankan sesuai dengan kaidah keteknikan yang baik selama masa operasi;
  5. Badan usaha bebas dari konflik atau permasalahan hukum lainnya dengan pihak lain;
  6. Dokumen persyaratan dan keterangan/ pernyataan yang diberikan adalah benar adanya dan apabila dikemudian hari terbukti tidak benar akan dicabut izin usahanya sesuai dengan peraturan perundangan-undangan;
  7. Kesanggupan menerima penunjukan dan penugasan dari Menteri untuk melaksanakan penyimpanan dalam rangka penyediaan cadangan penyangga energi dan pemenuhan kebutuhan minyak bumi di dalam negeri pada fasilitas dan sarana penyimpanan miliknya (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga minyak bumi);
  8. Kesanggupan menerima penunjukan dan penugasan dari Menteri untuk melaksanakan penyimpanan dalam rangka penyediaan cadangan penyangga energi dan pemenuhan kebutuhan bahan bakar minyak di dalam negeri pada fasilitas dan sarana penyimpanan miliknya (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga bahan bakar minyak);
  9. Surat pernyataan tertulis di atas materai mengenai kesanggupan badan usaha menerima penugasan dari Menteri untuk pemanfaatan secara bersama dengan pihak lain atas fasilitas yang dimiliki (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga gas bumi yang memiliki fasilitas jaringan distribusi);
  10. Kesanggupan badan usaha menyediakan cadangan LPG minimum sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan yang besarnya dihitung dari rencana volume penjualan harian rata-rata (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga LPG);
  11. Kesanggupan badan usaha menerima penugasan dari Menteri untuk penyediaan dan pendistribusian LPG (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga LPG);
  12. Kesanggupan badan usaha menerima penugasan dari Menteri untuk pemanfaatan secara bersama dengan pihak lain atas fasilitas penyimpanan dan/atau pengangkutan LPG yang dimiliki dan/atau dikuasai termasuk penyalurnya secara bersama dengan pihak lain (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga LPG); dan/atau
  13. Kesanggupan badan usaha menyediakan cadangan operasional LPG sesuai ketentuan peraturan yang berlaku (untuk kegiatan usaha niaga LPG).

Jaminan kecukupan pendanaan, yang dibuktikan dengan:

  1. Dokumen jaminan kecukupan pendanaan sendiri yang dibuktikan dengan laporan keuangan 3 (tiga) tahun terakhir yang telah diaudit oleh akuntan publik yang terdaftar sesuai dengan Peraturan Perundang-undangan bagi Badan Usaha yang telah berdiri lebih dari 3 (tiga) tahun;
  2. Dokumen kesepakatan dengan pihak lain yang menyatakan jaminan kecukupan pendanaan yang dikeluarkan oleh pihak lain yang nilainya sesuai dengan rencana usaha dalam analisis kelayakan usaha; atau
  3. Surat keterangan dari bank umum yang berkedudukan di Indonesia, yang menerangkan bahwa Badan Usaha memiliki kemampuan pendanaan untuk melakukan kegiatan usahanya dengan nominal yang sesuai dengan rencana usaha dalam analisis kelayakan usaha

editorial.headline: Commodity Futures Advisory: Open Nationally, Clear of Bali’s PMA Block
editorial.standfirst: This code covers paid advice on trading commodities through futures and derivative contracts, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100% and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Commodity futures advisory is the business of giving paid advice to other parties on buying and selling commodities through futures contracts, sharia derivative contracts, and other derivative contracts. Its scope also includes those acting as futures-adviser representatives. The defining activity is advisory work: helping another party navigate transactions based on the contracts named in the classification, in return for compensation.

The activity is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises. That breadth matters because the code is not written as a large-company-only category: the same defined advisory activity can be registered across the full range of business scales stated in the record. The commercial focus, however, remains specific. It concerns advice on commodity trading conducted through futures and derivative instruments, rather than a general description of commodity business.

Nationally, the code is marked open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In plain terms, the record places no foreign-share cap below full ownership at the national level. The stated basis for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali’s position is also materially clear. This activity is not blocked for PMA registration by the province-wide rule that blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The record identifies the OSS risk at the Large scale as Medium-High/High, and expressly says that this keeps the activity outside that moratorium block. Bali’s status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: not a prohibition, but a classification that should be read alongside the activity’s stated risk position at the Large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: For this advisory activity, Bali does not apply its PMA moratorium block because the recorded Large-scale risk is Medium-High/High.

editorial.headline: Nationally Open, but Bali Blocks Sharia Capital-Market Advice
editorial.standfirst: This sharia advisory activity permits full foreign ownership nationally, yet PMA registration at a Bali address is blocked by the province’s permanent moratorium.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity through a PMA company at a Bali address today, even though it is nationally open. This activity concerns sharia advisory work for the capital market: advising on, and/or overseeing, the application of sharia principles in a company’s business activities; and/or issuing a statement that a sharia capital-market product or service conforms with those principles. It is work rooted in applied sharia knowledge and experience, directed at how those principles are put into practice and evidenced in the capital-market setting.

The activity may be undertaken by an individual who has sharia knowledge and experience, or by a business entity whose management and employees have that knowledge and experience. The record makes the activity available at micro, small, medium and large scales, so the form of registration can follow the scale of the enterprise. Its scope is deliberately specific: the advisory and oversight functions sit alongside the ability to give a sharia-conformity statement for products or services in the capital market. That makes the underlying expertise—not a generic corporate label—the centre of the activity described.

Nationally, the position is clear. The activity is open to PMA and permits a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For an investor reviewing the national framework alone, that is a fully foreign-owned route rather than a capped foreign stake. Bali requires a separate conclusion. The record classifies the large-scale route as Medium-Low risk, bringing it within Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The result is not a reduced Bali ownership percentage; it is a block on PMA registration for a Bali address. The provincial position is linked to a Governor’s letter issued in May 2026. National openness therefore remains real, but it does not create an available PMA registration path in Bali for this activity.

editorial.headline: Financial Market Advice: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This advisory activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
For a Bali address, the starting point is blunt: a foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. That conclusion sits beside, not against, the national setting. Nationally, Other Financial Market Advisory Activities is open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Bali’s status is closed under the PMA moratorium, so the national opening does not translate into a PMA registration route on the island.

The activity itself is a broad home for financial-support work not classified elsewhere. It includes financial consulting; mortgage advisory and brokerage; mortgage consulting; and other investment advisory services. The record specifically names robo-advisor services as an example. Taken together, the scope describes advice and advisory intermediation across financial and mortgage matters, including technology-enabled investment guidance, rather than a single narrow professional service. Its breadth matters: several advisory forms sit within one declared activity without being confined to one delivery model.

Registration is open across every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That broad scale availability is national context; it does not dissolve Bali’s local PMA position. The record identifies the Besar scale as Menengah Rendah. Under Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium, all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities are blocked where registration uses a Bali address. The decisive Bali fact is therefore not whether the advisory work is delivered conventionally or through a robo-advisor, but that its stated risk treatment brings it within the moratorium.

The record must be read in two layers. The national layer says the activity is TERBUKA and allows a foreign stake of up to 100%. The Bali layer says PMA registration is blocked for a Bali address because of the moratorium. Both statements are true at once; neither overrides the other. For a proposal centred on Bali, the address is the point at which the national permission stops being actionable. The code remains the description for the listed advisory activities, but it is not a current PMA-registration path in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not create a PMA registration path in Bali under the island-wide moratorium.

editorial.headline: The Conventional Fintech Behind a Direct Rupiah Loan Match
editorial.standfirst: A conventional fintech peer-to-peer lending service, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali's PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity is a conventional, technology-based lending-and-borrowing intermediary. It provides, manages and operates a financial-service offering that connects lenders with borrowers so they can enter conventional loan agreements. The activity is expressly built around direct rupiah loan agreements made through electronic systems using the internet. Its subject is the service that enables those agreements: bringing the lending and borrowing sides into a structured meeting point, then keeping the financial service available, managed and operating. The scope calls this conventional fintech peer-to-peer lending, but the definition stays concrete. It is the provision, management and operation of a digital financial service for matching lenders and borrowers according to the terms described in the record. Every part of that formulation matters: the service is financial in character, intermediary in function, conventional in the agreements it supports, and internet-based in the way those agreements are made.

That description identifies the registrant in functional terms: the business operating the intermediary service itself. Its task covers the provision, management and operation of the financial-service layer through which borrowers and lenders meet, agree and make the agreement directly in rupiah. The record makes no distinction among the available business scales. Registration is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar, allowing the same defined activity to be registered from the micro scale through the large scale. The breadth of those listed scales does not dilute the description; throughout, the legal-commercial centre remains a conventional loan agreement made directly between lender and borrower through an internet-connected electronic system. Across all four scales, the record preserves one operational description for the service.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and its maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain English, the national record allows the activity to be fully foreign owned. The Bali result is equally clear, though it turns on risk rather than a separate ownership figure. Bali assigns it the OK_or_HIGHER_RISK status. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which means the activity is not blocked by Bali's moratorium. The moratorium itself blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA across the island on a permanent basis. It does not block this activity. A foreign-owned business can therefore register this activity in Bali today, within the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.

editorial.headline: Sharia-Compliant Digital Lending Intermediation, Clearly Defined
editorial.standfirst: A technology-based Islamic financing platform may be foreign-owned nationally and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the provision, management and operation of a technology-based financial service that brings lenders and borrowers together under sharia principles. In practical terms, it is the operating layer for an Islamic peer-to-peer lending service: a digital system through which parties enter directly into rupiah-denominated financing agreements over the internet. Its defining feature is not merely the use of technology, but that the service is conducted entirely according to sharia principles.

The scope is therefore broader than a simple online marketplace. It encompasses the continuing work of making the service available, managing it and operating the financial-services platform that connects the two sides of a financing arrangement. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, giving the classification a deliberately wide commercial reach. The common thread at every scale is the same: the platform intermediates between a lender and a borrower for financing conducted electronically in rupiah.

Nationally, the activity is open to PMA with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a clear position: foreign investment is permitted without a stated national shareholding cap below full ownership. For founders, the relevant distinction is between the national investment position and the actual character of the service. The business remains an Islamic, technology-based lending-intermediation operation, rather than a generic digital-finance label applied after the fact.

Bali does not block PMA registration for this activity. The province’s standing is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record identifies the reason plainly: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so the activity is not caught by Bali’s moratorium. That moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. Here, the Bali picture is therefore aligned with the national opening: the activity can be registered for PMA in Bali, while its large-scale risk classification remains part of the regulatory context.
editorial.pullQuote: The Bali picture is aligned with the national opening: the activity can be registered for PMA in Bali.

editorial.headline: Financing the Securities Trade
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers OJK-licensed lending of funds or securities to brokers for securities transactions, open to PMA nationally and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is the financing infrastructure behind a securities trade. The activity provides brokers with lending facilities in the form of funds and/or securities so that the transaction can proceed. The stated examples—margin transactions, short selling and repos—show the practical terrain: financing is extended in direct support of securities transactions. The formal scope also draws a firm professional boundary around the activity. It covers parties that have obtained a business licence from the Financial Services Authority (OJK) to provide lending facilities of funds and/or securities for securities transactions. That licence status is part of the activity’s definition.

The registration canvas is broad across business scale. Under the record, enterprises at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales may all undertake this activity. It does not reserve the category for only the largest market participants; each of the four stated scales is included. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In plain terms, the national record does not place the foreign stake below full ownership for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder, those facts give the category its national shape: regulated transaction finance, available across the specified business scales, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.

Bali’s conclusion is clear, and it is not a prohibition: PMA registration is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. The Bali entry is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the recorded reason says that at the Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—so the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The moratorium itself permanently applies, island-wide, to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This activity’s recorded Bali position therefore remains open rather than barred: the risk assessment cited for the Besar scale places it outside that particular restriction. The honest reading is simply that Bali does not block PMA registration here under its moratorium, while the OJK licence boundary continues to define the business activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not block PMA registration here under its moratorium, while the OJK licence boundary continues to define the business activity.

editorial.headline: Trust Administration Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers fee- or contract-based custody and management under trust agreements for beneficiaries—open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet unavailable for PMA registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
PMA registration for this activity is unavailable to a foreign investor in Bali today. That local restriction sits beside a very different national position: the activity is nationally open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For founders, the distinction is not semantic. National openness describes the investment position for the activity; the Bali address triggers an island-wide PMA moratorium that closes the registration route there.

The activity itself is narrowly defined. It concerns the custody and management carried out under a trust agreement for the benefit of a beneficiary, performed in return for remuneration or under a contract. The centre of gravity is therefore the administration of an agreed trust arrangement: holding and managing on behalf of the beneficiary within the terms of that arrangement. It is not a catch-all label for financial activity, but a defined custodial and management service grounded in a trust agreement and directed to the beneficiary’s interest.

Registration is open across the stated business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That breadth does not dilute the Bali result for PMA. The record identifies the Besar scale for this activity as Menengah Rendah, or Medium-Low risk. Bali’s permanent, province-wide PMA moratorium blocks all Low- and Medium-Low-risk KBLI activities when the registered address is in Bali. The consequence is categorical for a foreign-owned registration in Bali: despite the national 100% foreign-ownership position, this activity is blocked there.

The practical reading is straightforward but must remain precise. A founder considering this activity should recognise both facts at once: nationally, full foreign ownership is permitted; in Bali, PMA registration is closed under the moratorium because of the activity’s Medium-Low-risk treatment at the stated scale. The Bali restriction is not a reduction of the national ownership ceiling. It is a location-specific bar on PMA registration for a Bali address, and it is the controlling fact for a foreign investor planning to establish this activity on the island.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not overcome Bali’s location-specific bar on PMA registration for this activity.

editorial.headline: The Discipline Behind a Securities Rating
editorial.standfirst: This activity turns assessments of repayment capacity into a defined rating system that gives investors a clearer basis for judging securities and rated entities.
editorial.body:
## A judgement system for investors

Securities rating is the business of translating financial judgement into an established rating system. It covers ratings for debt securities, sukuk, asset-backed securities and other securities capable of being rated, as well as ratings of entities themselves. Its remit also includes mutual funds and real-estate investment funds structured as collective investment contracts. The purpose is precise: to give investors information on a party’s ability to meet payment obligations fully and on time.

That purpose makes the activity more exacting than a broad financial commentary service. The rating is expressed through a predetermined system, and its value lies in making a view of payment capacity legible to the market. The registrant is the party undertaking those ratings: assessing the relevant securities or entity, then communicating that assessment through the stated rating framework. Registration is open across the full stated range of business scales, from Mikro and Kecil through Menengah and Besar.

At the national level, PMA participation is TERBUKA, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. In practical terms, the record does not set a foreign stake below full ownership for this activity at the national level. That openness applies to the rating activity itself: ratings of the specified securities, entities, mutual funds and qualifying real-estate investment funds are all within its stated scope.

Bali’s position is also clear, but it deserves to be read on its own terms. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks activities classified as Low or Medium-Low risk across the island. This activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record notes that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—therefore it is not blocked by the moratorium. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; the record identifies no separate Bali ownership ceiling or partnership condition.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today because it is not blocked by the province’s PMA moratorium.

editorial.headline: The Discipline Behind a Fair Market Price for Securities
editorial.standfirst: Securities price assessment is an OJK-licensed activity, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Price assessment for securities is the specialised work of determining a fair market price. The code covers the assessment itself: a defined pricing activity carried out to establish that market benchmark. Its centre of gravity is the conclusion the work is intended to produce—a fair market price for securities. In practical registration terms, the listed business activity is the formal assessment of securities prices undertaken to set that price. The record places this work with a party that has obtained a business licence from Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority (OJK) to perform it.

Who may register it is equally precise. The record opens the activity to micro, small, medium and large businesses, so it is not reserved in the stated scale field for one end of the enterprise spectrum. That does not dilute the nature of the work: at every listed scale, the activity remains securities price assessment for the establishment of fair market value. For a founder, the scale classification and the OJK-authorised function sit together: the scale identifies where the activity is open, while the licensed function identifies the work being registered.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is straightforward. The code is marked open, and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. A foreign-owned company can therefore register this activity nationally up to the full ownership ceiling, provided it has the stated OJK business licence to undertake the price-assessment work. The record cites Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 as the PMA source. This is a national ownership position, expressed without a lower foreign cap.

Bali calls for a separate read, because its standing rule permanently blocks PMA registration for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activity across the island. This record, however, marks the activity as not blocked for PMA registration. Its Bali assessment is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the stated reason that the OSS risk at the Large scale is Medium-High/High—outside the risks caught by the moratorium. Bali’s record says the activity is not blocked today, and it gives the risk rationale for that result.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s record says the activity is not blocked today, and it gives the risk rationale for that result.

editorial.headline: Investor Protection Fund Management, Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the authorised organisation and management of collective funds created to protect investors from asset loss, with a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling and no Bali PMA block.
editorial.body:
Investor protection funds are collective funds formed to protect investors from the loss of their assets. This activity is the organisation and management of that pool: it is concerned with running a fund created for investor protection, not merely invoking investor protection as a general aim. The record makes both elements inseparable. A protection fund is formed; the party undertaking the activity organises and manages it; and the fund’s stated function is to protect investors where their assets are lost. That chain of purpose and administration is the practical definition of the activity.

The record also identifies the kind of party that conducts this work. It is a party that has obtained business authorisation from Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) to organise and manage the collective investor-protection fund. This is therefore an activity tied to an authorised operator and to the management of a defined pooled fund. It is open at the Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. Those are the scales expressly available in the record; the activity is not presented as confined to only one of them. Across each stated scale, the described role remains the organisation and management of the protection fund.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits a foreign investor to hold the full ownership interest nationally. The point is unambiguous but should not be overread: it states the foreign-ownership setting for this activity at the national level. It sits alongside, rather than replaces, the record’s description of the activity as work undertaken by a party holding the relevant OJK business authorisation. The national answer is openness at a 100% ceiling.

Bali does not reverse that position in this record. The activity carries the Bali status `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK` and is not marked as blocked for PMA registration. The stated reason is specific: at the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High, so it is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium. The honest local conclusion is therefore clean: a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today, with the national ceiling of 100% and the OJK business authorisation described in the record.

editorial.headline: Underwriting, Corporate Action, and the Bali PMA Line
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers securities underwriting and corporate-action advice, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Securities underwriting is not simply a transaction at the moment securities are offered to the public. It is an activity spanning the preparation and support of an offering, alongside work connected to the corporate actions of companies preparing for, or already having made, a public offering. In practical terms, its scope includes underwriting securities issues and advising on their issuance, as well as on mergers, consolidations, acquisitions, and restructurings. It also encompasses other activities determined and/or approved by the Financial Services Authority.

The registration follows the activity itself: the party carrying out securities underwriting and the related corporate-action work. Its scope is therefore defined by a close relationship with companies at a public-offering stage, rather than by a single isolated service. The code is open across the full stated business-scale range—Micro, Small, Medium, and Large—so the formal scale classification does not narrow the underlying description of the work. What matters is that the registered business is undertaking the underwriting or the connected advisory and corporate-action activity described here.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is full foreign ownership, not a partial allowance framed as openness. The relevant national source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the activity at national level, the essential point is that the code does not impose a lower foreign-equity ceiling in the record.

Bali’s position is also clear, but for a different reason. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Large scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High/High, which is why the Bali assessment is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a prohibition. A foreign-owned business registering this activity in Bali is therefore not stopped by the stated Bali moratorium; the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the relevant ownership figure in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign-owned business registering this activity in Bali is not stopped by the stated Bali moratorium.

editorial.headline: Money-Market and FX Support: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This intermediary market activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet a permanent Bali PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
**For a foreign-owned company, this activity cannot be registered at a Bali address today.** Nationally, the activity is open to PMA and permits foreign ownership of up to 100%. Bali reaches a different result. Its island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium blocks every Low and Medium-Low risk activity for a Bali address. The Large-scale entry for this activity is classified as Medium-Low, bringing it inside that block. The restriction concerns PMA registration, not a recalculation of the national foreign-ownership ceiling. Bali’s address-based rule controls even though the national status remains open.

The underlying work is intermediary activity in the money and foreign-exchange markets. It encompasses intermediation connected with the issue and trading of instruments, together with execution of transactions in those markets, provided the activity is conducted other than through an exchange. Money-market and foreign-exchange markets are both named in the scope, as are both instrument-related work and transaction-related work. The scope brings the intermediary side of issuance and trading together with transaction execution. The exclusion of exchange-based execution marks the boundary set by the recorded scope.

Businesses undertaking that intermediary work may register it at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah or Besar scale under the national framework. The record expressly includes the activity across those four categories; it does not confine the stated scope to one business size. For a PMA applicant, however, scale is more than a descriptive label when the registered address is in Bali. The Bali record points to the Besar-scale classification in explaining why PMA registration is blocked. National scale coverage does not displace that Bali-specific rule.

That makes the national-versus-Bali picture clear. The national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, supported in the record by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali’s rule is a full PMA registration block for the Bali address. It is tied to Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, dated May 13, 2026, and is described as permanent. A founder can read the code as nationally open without mistaking that status for present PMA availability in Bali: for this activity, a Bali address remains blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a PMA registration route at a Bali address for this activity.

editorial.headline: Who Rates Indonesia’s Small Businesses and Cooperatives?
editorial.standfirst: A nationwide activity for independent rating services, with full foreign ownership nationally but a scope-dependent route in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 66198 covers the provision of rating services for micro, small and medium enterprises, as well as cooperatives. In practical terms, it is the business of assessing and classifying these organisations through a rating service. Its stated scope also includes MSME-rating activities and work carried out by independent cooperative-rating institutions. The focus is therefore specific: an evaluative service for the enterprises and cooperative bodies that sit at the smaller-business end of Indonesia’s economy.

The activity is open at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a clear national position: foreign investors may hold the full permitted stake in a company registered for this activity. The applicable national reference in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a more exact reading. This activity is not marked as categorically blocked for PMA registration there; its Bali status is scope-dependent. The record says that, at the Besar scale, OSS risk may be low for some scopes and higher for others. A PMA registration in Bali is possible only by declaring the higher-risk scope, with the precise activity to be checked live in OSS. This is not a cosmetic distinction. The declared scope determines whether the registration route is available.

The reason is Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. For this rating-services activity, national openness does not automatically translate into an uncomplicated Bali registration. The national ceiling remains 100%, but Bali eligibility turns on the exact scope declared and its live OSS risk treatment. For founders, the disciplined conclusion is simple: the business is nationally open and available at all listed scales, while a Bali PMA filing depends on selecting and verifying the higher-risk scope for the exact activity.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not automatically translate into an uncomplicated Bali registration.

editorial.headline: Financial Support Work Where Trust and Technology Meet
editorial.standfirst: This broad financial-services support activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
For foreign-owned businesses, the position is unusually direct: this activity is open nationally to 100% foreign ownership and is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium. In Bali, the relevant status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**. The reason is practical rather than promotional: at the large-business scale, the OSS risk classification is Medium-High or High, placing the activity outside the moratorium’s block on Low and Medium-Low risk PMA activities.

The activity is a home for financial-support work that does not sit elsewhere in the classification. Its scope ranges from fiduciary services performed for a fee or under contract, including trustee work, to agency or partnership activities for marketing securities and selling mutual-fund securities. It also includes digital-financial-asset tokenisation, including security token offerings and initial coin offerings; validation and mining of digital financial assets such as crypto assets regarded as financial assets; tax-receiving offices; branchless-banking activity; and paid or contracted collection and screening of financial-services information.

The category also reaches work undertaken by parties registered with the Financial Services Authority to approach prospective customers to become securities-broker clients, where commission is earned under a cooperation agreement. A distinct place is also made for businesses that market mutual-fund securities under a cooperation agreement with the investment manager responsible for the fund. The common thread is supporting, connecting, administering, marketing or processing financial activity rather than presenting a single, narrow operating model.

Businesses may register at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, under the cited Presidential Regulations. Bali does not add a separate foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition in this record. Its province-wide, permanent PMA moratorium applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities; this activity is expressly identified as outside that block at the Besar scale because its OSS risk is Medium-High or High. That distinction is the central Bali reading: open nationally, and not moratorium-blocked in Bali on the record provided.

editorial.headline: Insurance Risk Assessment: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This pre-insurance risk-assessment activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this insurance risk-assessment activity at a Bali address today. That is the practical Bali position for the activity, even though its national PMA status is open and the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The difference is central, not cosmetic: the national setting permits foreign capital at that ceiling, while Bali’s PMA moratorium prevents the registration route there. A founder reading only the national status would therefore miss the operative local outcome.

An insurance risk surveyor assesses risk or supplies an expert opinion on the object proposed for insurance. The work occurs before the insurance is concluded, which gives the activity a precise place in the insurance process. In clear commercial English, it is the business of examining the proposed insured object and bringing professional judgment to its risk before the insurance is finalised. The record ties both the assessment and the opinion to that object; it also makes the pre-conclusion timing explicit. That is the scope prospective registrants should use when deciding whether their intended activity belongs here.

Nationally, the activity is open at every scale listed in the record: Micro, Small, Medium, and Large. It is therefore not presented as an activity reserved for one size of undertaking. These are the business scales open to the registrant, with the record making no distinction among them in its list. The PMA position is also explicit: TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the cited source. In the national frame, then, a foreign investor may take the full permitted 100% stake in this activity.

Bali changes the answer decisively. Its recorded status is closed under the PMA moratorium. The stated reason is specific: at the Large scale, the activity is classified as Medium-Low risk, placing it within the provincial rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA. The moratorium applies island-wide and is permanent. The governing reference given in the record is the governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, issued in May 2026. The consequence is plain: national openness and a 100% national ceiling do not create a PMA registration option at a Bali address. The Bali position is a block, not a lower foreign-ownership limit.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and a 100% ceiling do not create a PMA registration option at a Bali address.

editorial.headline: Insurance Loss Assessment: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: For insurance claim assessment and consulting on insured objects, this activity is open to foreign investment nationally and is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Insurance claims call for a disciplined assessment of what has been claimed and, where needed, advice concerning the object insured. This activity is the business of assessing insurance claims and providing consulting services on insured objects. In the loss-adjuster role, the work is performed when a claim occurs. The scope is therefore precise: it centres on the claim assessment itself and/or consultation about the insured object. A company registering here is describing a practice built around those two stated functions, with loss adjustment attached to the moment of claim.

The registration is stated to be open at every scale named in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes scale an availability point, not a rewriting of the underlying activity: whether the business is registered as Mikro or Besar, the described work remains claim assessment and/or consulting on insured objects. The scope adds an important timing note for loss adjustment: it is undertaken when a claim has occurred. For founders, that keeps the reading grounded in the record, with the enterprise focused on assessment and consulting in the insurance-object context.

At the national level, this is a TERBUKA activity for foreign investment, and its maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In practical ownership terms, the record does not impose a national foreign-share ceiling below full ownership. Its PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. A foreign founder can therefore take the national position at face value: the activity is open to PMA, with the stated 100% maximum, and it is available across the four listed scales. That national reading is necessary, but it is not the entire local answer for a Bali-based registration.

The local answer is favourable as well: a foreign founder can register this activity in Bali today, because it is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. Bali marks the activity OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and gives the operative reason: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk activities; this activity is expressly recorded as outside that block. The honest conclusion is simple and exact: nationally the foreign-ownership maximum is 100%, and in Bali the moratorium does not bar PMA registration for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally the foreign-ownership maximum is 100%, and in Bali the moratorium does not bar PMA registration for this activity.

editorial.headline: Insurance Brokerage: Nationally Open, Not Barred by Bali’s Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: Insurance brokerage for policyholders, insured parties and participants is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 66222 covers the work of an insurance broker acting on behalf of the policyholder, insured party or participant. In practical terms, it brings together consulting services and/or intermediation in the closing of conventional insurance or sharia insurance, then carries that representative role through the handling of claim settlements. The record includes advisory services and/or brokerage, so the activity may be performed through advice, through intermediation, or through both. In every formulation, its defined position is clear: it acts for and in the name of the policyholder, insured party or participant. The scope states that formulation twice, reinforcing the representative relationship at the centre of the activity. This is therefore a precise description of a service joining insurance placement and claims handling for the represented party.

Registration is open across the listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The record places each of those scales within scope. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with maximum foreign ownership at 100%. Put plainly, the national record permits a foreign investor to hold the entire business under this activity. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national setting sits alongside the scale listing: the reference to business scale does not create an alternative foreign-ownership ceiling. The national position is consequently direct—this activity is open to PMA, with no recorded foreign-equity restriction below 100%.

Bali requires its own reading because the record includes an island-wide, permanent moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This activity is not blocked. The Bali assessment states that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and is therefore outside the moratorium’s block. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The distinction matters: the moratorium remains the stated provincial rule, but this activity’s recorded risk position means it is not caught by it. No Bali-specific foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition is recorded. On the evidence provided, the candid conclusion is straightforward: a foreign-owned insurance-brokerage business may be registered nationally with up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali’s stated moratorium does not bar its PMA registration there.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is direct: this activity is open to PMA, and Bali’s moratorium does not bar its registration.

editorial.headline: Reinsurance Brokerage: Open Nationally, Clear of Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers advice and brokerage for reinsurance placements and related claim settlement, with full foreign ownership permitted nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
**Reinsurance brokerage** is a specialist advisory and intermediary activity for placing reinsurance or sharia reinsurance, and for handling the settlement of related claims. The broker acts for and on behalf of an insurance company, sharia insurance company, guarantee company, sharia guarantee company, reinsurance company, or sharia reinsurance company making that placement. The scope is therefore defined by representation and placement: advising on, or intermediating in, reinsurance arrangements for the institutions that place them, while also handling the associated claim-settlement work.

The activity is open across the full scale spectrum recorded here: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth is significant because the code does not confine this work to one particular size of enterprise. A business registering this activity may be organised at any of those listed scales, while remaining within the same core description: consulting and/or acting as intermediary in reinsurance or sharia reinsurance placement, including the handling of claims settlement for the named insurance, guarantee and reinsurance businesses.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is listed as open, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits a foreign investor to hold the entire foreign-ownership ceiling in a PMA business registered for this activity. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower national foreign-ownership cap in the record to qualify that position.

Bali’s picture is also clear, though it turns on risk classification rather than a separate ownership percentage. Bali permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the province. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Large scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High/High. Bali therefore does not bar PMA registration for this activity under the province-wide moratorium. For a foreign founder considering Bali, the honest conclusion is that the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains relevant here, and the Bali moratorium does not shut the activity out.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali therefore does not bar PMA registration for this activity under the province-wide moratorium.

editorial.headline: Guarantee Agency Activity: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: An agency role marketing guarantee-business activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet PMA registration at a Bali address is blocked by the island-wide moratorium.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor seeking a Bali address, this activity cannot be registered today. That is the decisive local fact, even though its national record is open. KBLI 66224 covers agency activity in the guarantee sector: marketing the business activities of guarantee companies or sharia guarantee companies, for and on their behalf. It is a defined representative and market-facing role, not a catch-all description of commercial activity. The scope stays anchored to both the marketing function and the named guarantee businesses whose activity is being marketed. It does not merely name an industry; it specifies marketing undertaken for and on behalf of those businesses.

A national ceiling of 100% therefore does not create a route to a Bali address: for a foreign investor, the moratorium controls the registration outcome there.

The national entry describes an activity that is open to foreign ownership, while Bali’s rule bars a PMA registration for the same activity at a Bali address. Founders should read both statements together, beginning with the real activity—marketing undertaken for the named guarantee businesses—and then the listed scale. Only then does the apparent contradiction resolve: national openness and a Bali registration block can coexist.

editorial.headline: KBLI 66225: Acting for the Guaranteed Party
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers advisory and brokerage services for guarantees, including claim settlement handled on behalf of the guaranteed party.
editorial.body:
KBLI 66225 covers guarantee-broker activity: advisory and intermediary services in arranging guarantees, together with the handling of claim settlement. Its defining perspective is clear. The broker acts for and on behalf of the guaranteed party, not as a detached observer of the guarantee process. In practical terms, this is an activity built around representing that party’s interests while consulting on, or mediating, the provision of a guarantee and its claims.

The code is open across every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity is not framed as the preserve of one company size. The record places the same core work—consultation, intermediation and claim-settlement handling for the guaranteed party—within a classification available from micro through large enterprises.

At the national level, PMA is classified TERBUKA, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is an unambiguous national opening: foreign ownership is permitted up to the full ceiling recorded for this activity. The governing source cited is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the record suggests a lower national foreign-ownership limit, so the national picture should be read exactly as it stands: open, with a maximum foreign stake of 100%.

Bali requires a more precise reading, but not a pessimistic one. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record explains why: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low scope. Bali’s recorded status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For a foreign-owned registration, the honest conclusion is that this activity is not barred in Bali by the provincial PMA moratorium described in the record; the relevant distinction is its higher OSS risk position at the Besar scale, rather than any Bali-specific foreign-ownership cap.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not bar this activity under its PMA moratorium because its Besar-scale OSS risk position sits above the blocked categories.
