intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers the work of notaries (civil notaries) and land deed officials (PPAT) who prepare authentic documents—everything from general legal deeds, wills, and court-related tasks (bailiff, arbitrator) to specific sale-purchase contracts for land and buildings. It’s a regulated profession that gives legal certainty to agreements.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: On the national list this KBLI appears 100% open for foreign investment, but national law overrides that listing: the profession is personal and statutory, reserved exclusively for Indonesian citizens (WNI) under the Notary Law (UU 30/2004 as amended by UU 2/2014). Consequently, a foreign-owned company (PMA) cannot be registered to carry out this activity anywhere in Indonesia.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Unchanged from KBLI 2020 — direct match.
intel_2026.baliContext: Every property transaction in Bali — villa purchase, land lease, AJB (deed of sale), PPJB (binding agreement of sale and purchase) — requires a licensed Notaris/PPAT. Bali has many experienced bilingual notaries (Indonesian/English) in Seminyak, Denpasar, and Ubud who specialize in foreign investment structures. Note: foreigners cannot buy Hak Milik land — a Notaris/PPAT will advise on Hak Pakai, HGB, or PT PMA land ownership structures. The Notaris must be a licensed Indonesian citizen — this is not a PMA-eligible role.

editorial.headline: Notarial and Land-Deed Work: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA Nationwide
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans notarial work and land-and-building sale agreements, with a citizenship requirement under the Notary Law that bars PMA registration nationwide.
editorial.body:
This activity centres on the formal work of notaries and related legal officers: public and civil-law notarial functions, alongside the activities of bailiffs, arbitrators, examiners and *liperi*. It also includes work connected with agreements for the sale and purchase of land and buildings when handled by a land deed official. The record additionally identifies advocate offices within its stated scope. In practical terms, it is an activity rooted in the preparation, handling and formalisation of legally significant instruments and proceedings.

Our records carry a default marker for this activity — PMA status TERBUKA with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling — but that marker is a fallback applied whenever no specific closure is recorded, not a confirmed permission. The registration scope is not confined to one business size: Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises are all included. That breadth does not translate into a universal operating answer, however: the determining restriction here is not a matter of scale or province, but a nationwide citizenship rule that applies regardless of business size or location.

For a foreigner seeking to register this activity anywhere in Indonesia, the answer is clear: PMA registration is not available, in Bali or in any other province. The stated reason is substantive, not merely procedural: under UU 30/2004 (as amended by UU 2/2014), the notary and land-deed-official role is a personal public office reserved for Indonesian citizens, making PMA impossible nationwide. Bali separately records a permanent, island-wide provincial rule blocking PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, but that rule is not what closes this activity — the citizenship requirement alone closes it everywhere.

That contrast is the point founders need to hold onto — but it is not the contrast the record actually supports. There is no confirmed national ownership ceiling for this activity: the 100% figure some records display by default is a fallback, not a recorded permission. The real distinction is between business scale and citizenship: no scale category, and no province, changes the outcome. UU 30/2004 (as amended by UU 2/2014) assigns the notary and land-deed-official function a citizenship-based public-office character nationwide, and that is what makes a PT PMA impossible for this activity anywhere in Indonesia.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not erase the nationwide citizenship-based bar on PMA registration for this activity.

editorial.headline: Accounting Work, Fully Open Nationally, Carefully Limited for Public Accountants
editorial.standfirst: This activity reaches from routine books to financial-statement audit, with national foreign ownership open to 100% and a specific limit for public-accountant firms.
editorial.body:
At its centre, this activity is the business of making financial records reliable. It covers financial-accounting bookkeeping, payroll-accounting bookkeeping and other bookkeeping services; the preparation and analysis of financial statements; and the preparation or audit of those statements. The scope goes further, including the testing of reports and certification of their accuracy. That combination matters: it describes a field that can begin with the ordered record of transactions and extend to the examination and confirmation of financial reporting.

The registration field is broad in scale. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses, placing small operations and larger organisations within the same stated scope. Its work is defined by the services performed rather than by one narrow task: bookkeeping, report preparation, analysis, audit, examination, testing and accuracy certification are all expressly within it. The full sequence is important, from the books themselves to the financial statements built from them and the assessment of their accuracy.

Our records file the PMA entry for this activity as TERBUKA with a maximum foreign ownership of 100% — the baseline classification applied when the national investment list carries no specific entry for this code, not a recorded permission in its own right. A narrower, specific condition sits alongside that baseline: in a public-accountant firm, foreign nationals may make up no more than 20%. Our records mark this as a restriction rather than an outright block, and they do not say where it applies or does not apply. For founders, the useful discipline is to keep the 100% ownership-ceiling default separate from the 20% cap on foreign nationals in the firm, and to treat the cap, not the ceiling, as the operative limit on staffing.

One further rule appears in the record: the province permanently blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide, under the cited Governor's letter. The record does not assign a risk level to this activity, so that rule cannot itself be read as covering it. The condition that does apply here is the 20% cap on foreign nationals in a public-accountant firm, and it stands on its own: our records do not fold it into either the province-wide moratorium above or the default ownership-ceiling figure. For founders, the useful discipline is to keep the ownership-ceiling default separate from the 20% cap on foreign nationals in the firm, and not to treat either figure as telling you where the other one applies.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is not a substitute for reading the stated limitation on a public-accountant firm.

editorial.headline: Tax Consulting With a Clear Bali PMA Route
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers tax advice, return preparation and non-legal representation—and remains open to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
Tax Consulting Activities covers the practical work of helping business and individual clients navigate tax matters. Its stated scope includes preparing income-tax returns for businesses or individuals, providing tax-consulting services, and offering accounting-consulting services. It also includes advice and representation on a client’s behalf before tax officials or the tax court, provided that representation is not legal representation. The centre of gravity is therefore tax-facing professional support: preparation, advice, accounting consultation and non-legal client representation within the tax system.

The classification is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the activity is not confined in the record to one kind of enterprise size. A provider serving individual taxpayers through return preparation sits within the same recorded scope as one advising business clients, while the scope also accommodates work conducted before tax officials or the tax court on the client’s behalf. The boundary is explicit where representation is concerned: it is representation other than legal representation.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record presents this activity as open to foreign investment at the national level, without a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position should be read together with the Bali entry, rather than assumed to settle the provincial picture by itself.

For Bali, the recorded status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and the activity is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. For this activity, the record states that at the Besar scale its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is straightforward: a foreign investor can register this tax-consulting activity in Bali today under the recorded position. The national foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%; the Bali record adds no separate foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this tax-consulting activity in Bali today under the recorded position.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Head-Office Activity: Open Nationally, Blocked Pending Verification in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Head-office work is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but we hold no verified Bali licensing rows for this code — until that gap is closed, a PT PMA's registration here is blocked pending case-by-case verification.
editorial.body:
Our records do not currently let us confirm that a PT PMA can register this activity in Bali. That gap matters because the national position initially appears straightforward: head-office activity is open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In Bali, though, we hold no verified licensing rows for this code, so its registration path there is unresolved. The result is not a minor local qualification; for a PT PMA seeking to register this activity in Bali, the record is clear that registration is blocked pending verification.

In practical terms, this is the work of directing the centre of an enterprise rather than carrying out the trade, manufacturing, financing, or other work performed by its operating units. It covers supervising and managing other units within a company or group of companies; setting strategic or organisational plans; making decisions on company or enterprise policy; maintaining operational control; and managing the day-to-day operation of related units. The character of that head-office work remains the same regardless of what the managed units themselves do. Central administrative offices, incorporated offices, district or regional offices, and branch-management offices all sit within this scope.

The scale-and-risk picture is exactly where the record runs out: the licensing rows this code's classification once relied on could not be independently verified against our pinned sources, so they have been withdrawn rather than served as fact — no scale tier and no risk tier is currently established for this code. We located no foreign-ownership restriction on the activity itself — not in the Perpres annexes, not in the closed list, not in any sectoral instrument we read — but that is a separate question from whether a PT PMA can register it in Bali, and on that question we have no verified licensing rows to go on. It is therefore treated as blocked until verified case by case. Bali separately enforces an island-wide, permanent PMA block on Low- and Medium-Low-risk activities, but because this code's own risk tier is not currently verifiable, we cannot say whether that rule applies here; it is background context, not the reason this code is blocked.

For founders, the useful distinction is between what the activity is and where it can be registered in the intended corporate form. Nationally, the activity can accommodate 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, we cannot currently confirm a registration path for a PT PMA under this code — the position is unresolved and treated as blocked until it is verified case by case. The activity remains a defined category of enterprise coordination and control; what changes is the route available to a foreign-investment company on the island. Treating the national opening as a guarantee of Bali registration would miss the point entirely.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest answer here is not yes and not no: it is that we will not state a position we cannot evidence.

l4_bali.reason: No foreign-ownership restriction located in Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran I/II/III, the closed list, or any sectoral instrument read. The catalogue holds no licensing rows for this code, so its Bali risk tier is unknown and the Bali position cannot be stated — verify case by case. editorial.headline: Tourism Management Advice, Open Nationally but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Professional tourism consultancy is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity in Bali today.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned company cannot register this activity in Bali today. That is the practical starting point for **KBLI 70201**, despite its national PMA position being open. The activity covers professional tourism-consulting services: providing views, advice and studies on feasibility, planning, organisation, direction, coordination, supervision, reporting, budgeting and other management functions in the tourism field. It is an advisory and management discipline for tourism, not a catch-all label for operating a tourism business itself.

The code is available at the **Mikro**, **Kecil** and **Menengah** scales. Its subject matter is broad enough to follow a tourism project through the management questions that shape it: whether an idea is viable, how work should be planned and organised, how functions should be coordinated, and how oversight, reporting and budgets should be handled. The common thread is professional counsel applied to tourism management. The record therefore places the activity with providers delivering informed analysis and direction rather than merely supplying a discrete operational service.

Nationally, foreign ownership may reach **100%** under the cited PMA source. In Bali, however, the registration outcome is different. The Bali record marks the activity **Closed in Bali (2026 moratorium)** because the province-wide block covers every **Low and Medium-Low risk** KBLI, and tourism management consulting is classified Low risk. The provincial block covers the whole **Low risk** tier, so a PT PMA cannot register this activity there today. The issue is structural: national foreign-ownership openness does not create a Bali registration path where the applicable scale row is absent.

Bali also has a permanent, island-wide rule blocking PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities, recorded under the Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For this code, the immediate conclusion remains clear: national openness up to full foreign ownership is real, but Bali does not permit PMA registration today because the activity falls in the Low risk band that the provincial moratorium has blocked island-wide since 13 May 2026.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness up to full foreign ownership is real, but Bali does not permit PMA registration today.

editorial.headline: Industrial Management Advice, Nationally Open but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Industrial management consulting is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks its registration on the island.
editorial.body:
Nationally, this is an open activity for foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, however, the immediate answer is different: a foreign investor cannot register it as a PMA activity today. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island on a permanent basis, and this activity falls into that blocked class. The restriction is not a judgement on the value of management advice; it is the practical registration position created by Bali’s risk-based rule.

The underlying work is industrial management and business consulting. It covers advising, guiding, and supporting operations where an industrial enterprise faces organisational or management issues. The scope reaches industrial-service consulting on strategy and organisation; financial decisions; marketing aims and policies; human-resources planning, practices, and policies; and the planning, scheduling, and control of production. In plain terms, the activity is about helping industrial businesses decide how the company should be structured, directed, staffed, marketed, financed, and run.

It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the Bali outcome turns on the risk reading at scale Besar: OSS identifies Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope. Under Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium, that assessment closes the PMA-registration route in the province. It does not erase the national classification; it means that an activity nationally open to up to 100% foreign ownership is nevertheless blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

For an industrial consultant, the clean distinction is geographical and regulatory, not conceptual. The national position says the activity is TERBUKA, with full foreign ownership permitted within the stated ceiling. Bali’s position says that the same activity is blocked for PMA registration because of its risk class, under the moratorium recorded in the Governor’s letter. Any plan centred on Bali has to begin with that present registration reality, rather than treating the national opening as a local clearance.
editorial.pullQuote: An activity nationally open to up to 100% foreign ownership is nevertheless blocked for PMA registration in Bali.

editorial.headline: Marketing Consultancy, Nationally Open but Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers marketing strategy and brand-development consulting, open nationally to every business scale but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign-owned business cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local fact, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, it is classified as blocked by risk class: at the Large scale, every scope is assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk and falls within the Bali moratorium.

The activity is marketing and commercial-management consulting. Its work includes giving opinions, advice and studies on developing and analysing marketing strategies; building and developing brands; providing services that improve sales value; and supporting other management functions in marketing. In practical terms, this is the advisory side of marketing: the strategic work of shaping how a business understands its market, develops its brand and strengthens its commercial function.

Nationally, the activity is open across Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. The record sets the maximum foreign ownership at 100%, under the cited national investment framework. That national openness is clear, but it does not displace the Bali position. Bali’s province-wide, permanent rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA, and the Large-scale risk assessment for this activity brings it within that rule.

For founders, the distinction is not a technical footnote. The national investment position describes the ownership ceiling for the activity; Bali’s moratorium determines whether PMA registration is available on the island. Here, the national ceiling is fully open, while Bali blocks the activity for PMA registration because of its risk classification. Any reading of the code needs to hold both facts together.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers professional advisory services that help businesses improve strategy, organisation, finances, HR, and production processes. It includes anything from designing accounting methods to agricultural management consulting by agronomists and economists.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open (100%) to foreign-owned PMA companies. In Bali, however, a specific block has been in effect since 28 January 2026, meaning a PMA cannot be registered under this KBLI on the island.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Direct match from KBLI 2020 (unchanged). Note that some activities that were previously under KBLI 2020 code 70204 (other management consulting) were absorbed into 70201 during the 2025 revision. What remains in 70209 is the true 'everything else' category.
intel_2026.baliContext: This code is the Swiss Army knife for niche consultants in Bali. Environmental consultants advising on sustainable tourism? 70209. Security consultants working with villa complexes? 70209. Agricultural advisors helping with coffee or cacao operations in the highlands? 70209. It has the same favorable profile as 70203 (Low risk, automatic, 100% PMA) but with the added flexibility of covering areas that don't fit the general business consulting label. In practice, many Bali-based consultants choose between 70203 and 70209 — the difference is semantic rather than regulatory. Use 70209 if your specialty is genuinely niche and you want the code description to match what you actually do.

editorial.headline: Management Consultancy: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Broad management advice is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s recorded rule closes PMA registration for the activity.
editorial.body:
Management consultancy under KBLI 70209 is a broad operating-advice category: it covers helping a business work through strategy and organisation, finance-related decisions, planning goals and policies, human-resources practices, and production scheduling and control. Its centre of gravity is not simply recommendations on paper, but advice, guidance and practical operational assistance on management functions and organisational problems. The scope reaches specialist work as well: agriculture-related management advice, the design of accounting methods and procedures, cost-accounting programmes, budget-control procedures, management information, and assistance to businesses and public services on planning, organisation, efficiency and supervision.

The brief also expressly takes in occupational health and safety consultancy, including risk identification and documentation, along with infrastructure investment study services and port-security management consultancy. It also encompasses advice and assistance concerned with the planning, organising, efficiency and supervision of business and public-service activity. That range matters because the activity is defined by the business and management problem being addressed, rather than by a single industry setting. For a founder, the stated scope is the important boundary: it brings together connected management work across multiple functions while remaining advice, guidance and operational assistance.

Nationally, the classification is open to PMA and permits up to 100% foreign ownership. It is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the register itself does not reserve it to one size of enterprise. Those two points are important, but they are not the whole registration answer for someone choosing Bali. National openness does not translate into PMA registration availability in Bali for this activity.

Bali’s recorded status is Closed in Bali: management consultancy has been closed to PMA registration there since January 2026, as the first of seven announced sectoral closures. The provincial setting is stricter still: Bali applies an island-wide, permanent moratorium blocking PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities. For a foreign investor, the practical conclusion is plain: even though full foreign ownership is available nationally, this activity cannot be registered through PMA in Bali under the recorded Bali rule.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not translate into PMA registration availability in Bali for this activity.

l4_bali.reason: Closed to new PMA licensing in Bali: the Bali Provincial Government closed OSS to foreign-owned companies for 18 business fields from the third week of May 2026, until further policy, with the approval of the Minister of Investment/BKPM (press release, 24 Jul 2026). This code descends from KBLI 2020 70209 (Aktivitas Konsultasi Manajemen Lainnya) on that list (BPS KBLI 2020→2025 conversion table). This 2025 code also merges KBLI 2020 activities that are not on the list; the closure is applied to the whole code as a conservative reading.

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This is your code for running an architecture practice — building design, town planning, landscape architecture. It covers the full spectrum from concept sketches to construction documentation. Because buildings involve public safety, this sits at Medium-High risk across all business scales, which means real licensing requirements beyond just your NIB.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro through Besar): Medium-High Risk**

You need an NIB plus a Sertifikat Standar (Standard Certificate) with verification. The big requirement here is your SBU (Sertifikat Badan Usaha) issued by an accredited LSBU — this is your company-level construction services license. Your professional staff must hold SKA (Sertifikat Keahlian) or SKK (Sertifikat Kompetensi Kerja) certifications.

For PMA companies, you'll likely need to register as a BUJKA (Badan Usaha Jasa Konstruksi Asing) — the foreign construction services entity framework.

**PMA: 100% foreign ownership allowed.**

Foreign architects often partner with locally-licensed firms to navigate the permit landscape faster.

editorial.headline: Architecture Beyond the Drawing Board
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans architectural advice, design and planning—from buildings and landscapes to urban land use—with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Architectural activity here is not confined to producing drawings for a single building. It covers the full advisory and design terrain of architectural practice: early architectural studies, pre-design advice, architectural design and other architectural services, as well as assessments of a building’s maintenance and feasibility. Its reach extends from the individual building to the spaces around it—built environments, landscapes, regions and urban areas—and includes work on the use and development of space.

The scope is equally concerned with how the built environment is shaped over time. It includes designing buildings and their surroundings, planning the conservation of buildings and their environments, and preparing arrangements for buildings and their settings. It also includes technical planning documents and supervision of architectural aspects during construction. Urban planning, land-use planning, project management, construction management, community assistance and other construction-related work are expressly within the activity’s stated scope.

Its building-design remit is broad, covering objects classified across meeting and assembly, business, education, factories and industrial buildings, high-hazard buildings, institutional and government uses, commercial premises, homes, storage, utilities and miscellaneous buildings. The activity is open at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. Nationally, it is classified as open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. **For this activity, Bali does not turn a nationally open architectural practice into a barred foreign-investment registration.**

That Bali conclusion rests on the record’s stated risk position at the Large scale: the OSS risk is medium-high or high, so the activity is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. The moratorium itself blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA across the province on a permanent, island-wide basis. That rule does not produce a block here. The practical reading is therefore straightforward: the activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and its Bali status is not blocked by that moratorium, with the recorded Large-scale risk classification explaining why.
editorial.pullQuote: For this activity, Bali does not turn a nationally open architectural practice into a barred foreign-investment registration.

It's the heavier-duty sibling of general architecture, focused on industrial applications where safety stakes are highest.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**Mikro/Kecil/Menengah: Medium-High Risk**

Keep in mind Bali's environmental sensitivity means factory projects face extra scrutiny from local environmental agencies.

editorial.headline: Factory Technical Design Is Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This factory-focused consultancy and design activity is open to PMA at every listed business scale, with a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
**71102** covers professional technical consultancy and design focused on factories. Its work concerns the planning, construction, dismantling and relocation of factories, including machinery, equipment and other parts of a plant. The scope is deliberately wide in the considerations it may take in: economic, social, cultural, environmental, natural-resource and other aspects can all form part of the assignment. This is therefore an activity concerned with the technical planning and transition of factory operations, from their establishment through physical change or relocation.

The record also includes substantial geospatial services. These include terrestrial geospatial data acquisition, particularly three-dimensional positioning of geodetic control points and the measurement of angles, distance, area and height differences. It covers ground control-point surveys, horizontal and vertical control networks, detailed situation surveys, utility surveys, toponym surveys, boundary-affirmation surveys and gravity surveys. The activity further encompasses planning and supervision documents for geospatial data acquisition using terrestrial, photogrammetric, remote-sensing and hydrographic methods; aerial-photo and imagery processing; geospatial database design and construction; spatial and regional analysis; the presentation of geospatial information; and the management and dissemination of geospatial data and information.

The activity is open to businesses at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is a full foreign-ownership ceiling, not a partial stake. The record identifies Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the source for that national position. A business registering this activity should therefore be carrying out the stated factory consultancy, technical design or included geospatial services, at one of the four listed scales.

Bali does not reverse the national position. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities. For this activity, however, the Bali record states that the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Medium-High/High, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. Bali’s status is OK or Higher Risk rather than blocked. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today: the national 100% ceiling remains in place, and the Bali risk note explains why the moratorium does not prevent registration.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today: the permanent moratorium does not block it.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

persyaratan: Memenuhi Standar Perizinan Berusaha Jasa Konsultansi Dalam Bidang Instalasi Tenaga Listrik
kewajiban: Menyampaikan Laporan Berkala *Khusus kantor perwakilan jasa penunjang tenaga listrik asing juga harus memenuhi kewajiban sebagai berikut:

Membentuk kerja sama operasi dengan badan usaha jasa penunjang tenaga listrik dalam negeri berkualifikasi besar yang memiliki perizinan berusaha dalam setiap kegiatan usaha jasa penunjang tenaga listrik di Indonesia dengan ketentuan paling rendah 50% (lima puluh persen) dari nilai biaya pekerjaan dikerjakan dengan badan usaha jasa penunjang tenaga listrik dalam negeri
Mempekerjakan lebih banyak tenaga kerja Indonesia daripada tenaga kerja asing
Menempatkan warga negara Indonesia sebagai penanggung jawab badan usaha kantor perwakilan asing
Mengutamakan penggunaan material dalam negeri
Memiliki teknologi tinggi, mutakhir, efisien, berwawasan lingkungan, serta memperhatikan kearifan lokal dan
Melaksanakan proses alih teknologi

persyaratan: Pemilik Manfaat (Beneficial Ownership)
Berita Acara Klarifikasi Rencana Pelaksanaan Survei Umum
Batas wilayah dan lintasan Survei Umum yang dilengkapi dengan koordinat geografis dalam proyeksi Longitude dan Latitude
Tata waktu dan rencana kerja
Peralatan dan parameter survei
Parameter dan tahapan pengolahan data
Rencana pembiayaan perolehan data Survei Umum
Rencana pemasyarakat an data

Jaminan kecukupan pendanaan yang dibuktikan dengan: a. Bagi Badan Usaha yang telah berdiri lebih dari 3 tahun menyampai kan laporan keuangan 3 (tiga) tahun terakhir yang telah diaudit oleh akuntan publik yang terdaftar dari Badan Usaha atau yang dilakukan bersamaan dengan perusahaan induknya b. Bagi Badan Usaha yang berdiri kurang dari 3 (tiga) tahun: 1) laporan keuangan tahunan yang ada 2) laporan keuangan perusahaan induknya yang telah diaudit oleh akuntan publik bagi badan usaha yang merupakan anak perusahaan 3) jaminan kecukupan pendanaan yang dikeluarkan oleh perusahaan induk yang nilainya sesuai dengan rencana usaha dalam Studi Kelayakan dan/atau 4) Surat keterangan dari bank utama (prime bank) yang berkedud ukan di Indonesia, yang menerang kan bahwa Badan Usaha memiliki kemampu an pendanaan untuk melakukan kegiatan usahanya

Apabila melintasi Wilayah Kerja maksimal 30% dari seluruh luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum, wajib menyertakan: a. Surat keterangan tidak keberatan dari Kontraktor yang Wilayah Kerjanya dilintasi b. Dokumen/ peta yang menggamb arkan luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum termasuk pada area Wilayah Kerja yang dilintasi
Surat Pernyataan Kesanggupan untuk menandatangani Confidentiality Agreement (CA) apabila pengolahan data survei dilakukan di luar negeri
kewajiban: Setelah diterbitkannya Izin Survei Umum, pemegang izin wajib mengadakan kontrak kerja sama dengan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM mengenai penyimpanan, pemeliharaan, dan pemasyarakatan data dengan ketentuan dan mekanisme sebagai berikut: a. Apabila sampai pada akhir masa berlakunya Izin Survei Umum, pemegang Izin tidak memiliki kontrak kerja sama, Izin Survei Umum dinyatakan tidak berlaku dan seluruh data hasil kegiatan Survei Umum wajib diserahkan kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM b. Dalam hal Survei Umum melintasi Wilayah Kerja, Izin Survei Umum yang terdiri dari area di Wilayah Terbuka dan area di Wilayah Kerja yang dilintasi akan dituangkan pada 1 (satu) kontrak kerja sama terkait penyimpanan, pemeliharaan, dan pemasyara katan data antara Pemegang Izin Survei Umum dan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM c. Kontrak kerja sama dengan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM dapat dilakukan setelah Izin Survei Umum diterbitkan, dengan tanggal efektif kontrak yaitu sejak memenuhi realisasi luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum minimal 51% (lima puluh satu persen) di Wilayah Terbuka berdasark an hasil pemantauan pelaksanaan Survei Umum oleh Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi d. Apabila realisasi luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum lebih kecil dari yang tertuang dalam Izin Survei Umum, termasuk perubahan izinnya apabila ada, akan mengurangi secara proporsional jangka waktu kontrak kerja sama terkait penyimpanan, pemeliharaan, dan pemasyarakatan data

Dalam hal terjadi perubahan, baik luasan area, panjang lintasan, jumlah titik dan/atau lokasi survei di luar wilayah yang tercakup dalam Izin Survei Umum, pemegang Izin wajib: a.Mempertahankan realisasi pelaksanaan minimal 70% {tujuh puluh persen) di Wilayah Terbuka dalam hal Survei Umum melintasi Wilayah Kerja b. Melaporkan pelaksanaan Survei Umum kepada Direktur Jenderal Minyak dan Gas bumi

Dalam hal terdapat perubahan luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum yang melebihi 20% (dua puluh persen) dari total luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum yang tertuang dalam Izin Survei Umum, pemegang izin terlebih dahulu wajib menyampaikan surat permohonan perubahan izin kepada Kepala Badan Koordinasi Penanaman Modal setelah melakukan presentasi ke Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi. Setelah terbitnya perubahan izin, kontrak kerja sama dengan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM wajib dilakukan amandemen

Apabila pemegang Izin Survei Umum tidak melaksanakan kewajiban sebagaimana dimaksud pada angka 2 dan angka 3, data tambahan yang dihasilkan dari perubahan luasan area, panjang lintasan, jumlah titik dan/atau lokasi survei wajib diserahkan kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM setelah dievaluasi oleh Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi serta data menjadi milik negara dan pemegang izin tidak memiliki hak pemasyarakatan atas data tambahan

Dalam hal Survei Umum melintasi Wilayah Kerja, luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik hasil survei umum yang dapat dimasukkan dalam kontrak kerja sama dengan Pusat Data Teknologi dan Informasi ESDM wajib memenuhi minimal 70% (tujuh puluh persen) dari realisasi pelaksanaan Survei Umum di Wilayah Terbuka. Data hasil Survei Umum yang tidak masuk dalam lingkup kontrak kerja sama wajib diserahkan kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM setelah dievaluasi oleh Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi serta data menjadi milik negara dan pelaku usaha tidak memiliki hak pemasyarakatan atas data

Pemegang Izin Survei Umum menyampaikan dokumen perjanjian dengan pihak ketiga kepada Pusat Data Teknologi dan Informasi ESDM antara lain terkait dengan pelaksanaan Survei Umum dan penyimpanan, pemeliharaan, dan pemasyarakatan data hasil kegiatan Survei Umum
Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib melaporkan perkembangan pelaksanaan Survei Umum kepada Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi
Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib bertanggung jawab sepenuhnya terhadap penguasaan di dalam kegiatan penyimpanan, pengelolaan dan kegiatan pemasyarakatan data hasil kegiatan survei umum

Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib menyerahkan Snapshot perekaman seluruh data Survei Umum yang diperoleh termasuk daftar seluruh datanya kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM melalui Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi serta mempresentasikan hasil Survei Umum kepada Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi

per_skala.scope_uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup jasa konsultasi kegiatan survei geofisika, survei geologi, survei seismik dan survei geokimia
persyaratan: Rencana pemasyarakatan data
Pemilik Manfaat (Beneficial Ownership)
Berita Acara Klarifikasi Rencana Pelaksanaan Survei Umum
Batas wilayah dan lintasan Survei Umum yang dilengkapi dengan koordinat geografis dalam proyeksi Longitude dan Latitude
Tata waktu dan rencana kerja
Peralatan dan parameter survei
Parameter dan tahapan pengolahan data
Rencana pembiayaan perolehan data Survei Umum

Jaminan kecukupan pendanaan yang dibuktikan dengan: a. Bagi Badan Usaha yang telah berdiri lebih dari 3 tahun menyampaikan laporan keuangan 3 (tiga) tahun terakhir yang telah diaudit oleh akuntan publik yang terdaftar dari Badan Usaha atau yang dilakukan bersamaan dengan perusahaan induknya b. Bagi Badan Usaha yang berdiri kurang dari 3 (tiga) tahun: 1) laporan keuangan tahunan yang ada 2) laporan keuangan perusahaan induknya yang telah diaudit oleh akuntan publik bagi badan usaha yang merupakan anak perusahaan 3) jaminan kecukupan pendanaan yang dikeluarkan oleh perusahaan induk yang nilainya sesuai dengan rencana usaha dalam Studi Kelayakan Dan/atau 4) Surat keterangan dari bank utama (prime bank) yang berkedudukan di Indonesia, yang menerangkan bahwa Badan Usaha memiliki kemampuan pendanaan untuk melakukan kegiatan usahanya

Apabila melintasi Wilayah Kerja maksimal 30% dari seluruh luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum, wajib menyertakan: a. Surat keterangan tidak keberatan dari Kontraktor yang Wilayah Kerjanya dilintasi b. Dokumen/peta yang menggambarkan luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum termasuk pada area Wilayah Kerja yang dilintasi
Surat Pernyataan Kesanggupan untuk menandatangani Confidentiality Agreement (CA) apabila pengolahan data survei dilakukan di luar negeri
Bukti bayar PNBP
kewajiban: Setelah diterbitkannya Izin Survei Umum, pemegang izin wajib mengadakan kontrak kerjasama dengan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM mengenai penyimpanan, pemeliharaan, dan pemasyarakatan data dengan ketentuan dan mekanisme sebagai berikut: a. Apabila sampai pada akhir masa berlakunya Izin Survei Umum, pemegang Izin tidak memiliki kontrak kerjasama, Izin Survei Umum dinyatakan tidak berlaku dan seluruh data hasil kegiatan Survei Umum wajib diserahkan kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM b. Dalam hal Survei Umum melintasi Wilayah Kerja, Izin Survei Umum yang terdiri dari area di Wilayah Terbuka dan area di Wilayah Kerja yang dilintasi akan dituangkan pada 1 (satu) kontrak kerjasama terkait Penyimpanan, pemeliha-raan, dan pemasyarakatan data antara Pemegang Izin Survei Umum dan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM c. Kontrak kerjasama dengan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM dapat dilakukan setelah Izin Survei Umum diterbit-kan, dengan tanggal efektif kontrak yaitu sejak memenuhi realisasi luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum minimal 51% (lima puluh satu persen) di Wilayah Terbuka berdasarkan hasil pemantauan pelaksanaan Survei Umum oleh Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi d. Apabila realisasi luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum lebih kecil dari yang tertuang dalam Izin Survei Umum, termasuk perubahan izinnya apabila ada, akan mengurangi secara proporsional jangka waktu kontrak kerjasama terkait Penyimpanan, pemeliha-raan, dan pemasyarakatan data

Dalam hal terjadi perubahan, baik luasan area, panjang lintasan, jumlah titik dan/atau lokasi survei di luar wilayah yang tercakup dalam Izin Survei Umum, pemegang Izin wajib: a.Memperta-hankan realisasi pelaksanaan minimal 70% (tujuh puluh persen) di Wilayah Terbuka dalam hal Survei Umum melintasi Wilayah Kerja b. Melaporkan pelaksanaan Survei Umum kepada Direktur Jenderal Minyak dan Gas bumi

Dalam hal terdapat perubahan luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum yang melebihi 20% (dua puluh persen) dari total luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik Survei Umum yang tertuang dalam Izin Survei Umum, pemegang izin terlebih dahulu wajib menyampaikan surat permohonan perubahan izin kepada Kepala Badan Koordinasi Penanaman Modal setelah melakukan presentasi ke Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi. Setelah terbitnya perubahan izin, kontrak kerjasama dengan Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM wajib dilakukan amandemen

Apabila pemegang Izin Survei Umum tidak melaksanakan kewajiban sebagaimana dimaksud pada angka 2 dan angka 3, data tambahan yang dihasilkan dari perubahan luasan area, panjang lintasan, jumlah titik dan/atau lokasi survei wajib diserahkan kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM setelah dievaluasi oleh Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi serta data menjadi milik negara dan pemegang izin tidak memiliki hak pemasyarakatan atas data tambahan

Dalam hal Survei Umum melintasi Wilayah Kerja, luasan area, panjang lintasan, atau jumlah titik hasil survei umum yang dapat dimasukkan dalam kontrak kerjasama dengan Pusat Data Teknologi dan Informasi ESDM wajib memenuhi minimal 70% (tujuh puluh persen) dari realisasi pelaksanaan Survei Umum di Wilayah Terbuka. Data hasil Survei Umum yang tidak masuk dalam lingkup kontrak kerjasama wajib diserahkan kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM setelah dievaluasi oleh Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi serta data menjadi milik negara dan pelaku usaha tidak memiliki hak pemasyarakatan atas data

Pemegang Izin Survei Umum menyampaikan dokumen perjanjian dengan pihak ketiga kepada Pusat Data Teknologi dan Informasi ESDM antara lain terkait dengan pelaksanaan Survei Umum dan penyimpanan, pemeliharaan, dan pemasyarakatan data hasil kegiatan Survei Umum
Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib melaporkan perkembangan pelaksanaan Survei Umum kepada Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi
Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib bertanggung jawab sepenuhnya terhadap penguasaan di dalam kegiatan Penyimpanan, pengelolaan dan kegiatan pemasyarakatan data hasil kegiatan survei umum

Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib menyerahkan Snapshot perekaman seluruh data Survei Umum yang diperoleh termasuk daftar seluruh datanya kepada Pusat Data dan Teknologi Informasi ESDM melalui Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi serta mempresentasikan hasil Survei Umum kepada Direktorat Jenderal Minyak dan Gas Bumi
Izin Survei Umum tidak dapat dialihkan kepada pihak lain
Pemegang Izin wajib melakukan kegiatan Survei Umum
Pemegang Izin Survei Umum wajib memenuhi realisasi luasan area, panjang lintasan atau jumlah titik Survei Umum minimal mencapai 51% (lima puluh satu persen) di Wilayah Terbuka

persyaratan: Standar Penetapan Kemampuan Badan Usaha Jasa Konstruksi /Sertifikat Badan Usaha (SBU) Subklasifikasi: AT007

Untuk Kantor Perwakilan BUJKA: a. Merupakan badan usaha jasa konstruksi berbadan hukum di negara asal b. Membayar biaya administrasi perizinan berusaha per jenis usaha sesuai peraturan perundang undangan yang berlaku

Untuk BUJK PMA: a. Penanam modal asing/ pemegang saham asing merupakan badan usaha jasa konstruksi berbadan hukum di negara asal yang dibuktikan dengan: 1) Akta pendirian yang dilegalisasi 2) Sertifikat perizinan bidang usaha jasa konstruksi berkualifikasi Besar di negara asal atau yang sejenis yang dilegalisasi b. Penanam modal dalam negeri/ pemegang saham dalam negeri merupakan badan usaha jasa konstruksi nasional berkualifikasi Besar yang dibuktikan dengan: 1) Perizinan berusaha sub sektor jasa konstruksi 2) Sertifikat Badan Usaha sub sektor jasa konstruksi
Bukti bayar PNBP
kewajiban: Menyampaikan Laporan Kegiatan Usaha Tahunan
SBU masih berlaku
Melaksanakan ketentuan dalam peraturan perundang undangan di bidang jasa konstruksi

Untuk Kantor Perwakilan BUJKA: a. Melakukan perpanjangan Sertifikat Standar sesuai subklasifikasi setiap 3 tahun b. Melakukan Kerjasama Operasi (KSO) dengan BUJKN berkualifikasi Besar dan memiliki klasifikasi/ subklasifikasi sejenis yang tercatat di lembaga pengembangan jasa konstruksi sebelum mengikuti proses pemilihan c. KSO untuk pelaksanaan Jasa Konsultansi Konstruksi dilaksanakan dengan ketentuan kriteria teknis KSO sebagai berikut: 1) Seluruh pekerjaan jasa Konsultansi Konstruksi dilakukan di dalam negeri 2) Paling sedikit 50% (lima puluh persen) dari nilai pekerjaan jasa Konsultansi Konstruksi dikerjakan oleh BUJKN mitra KSO

Memiliki dokumen bagan alur bisnis proses penjualan jasa

intel_2026.whatItMeans: The catch-all for engineering and technical consulting that doesn't fit into architecture or factory design — geophysical surveys, geological consulting, seismic studies, environmental engineering, and other specialized technical services. If you're doing subsurface analysis, hydrological studies, or niche engineering consulting, this is your code.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**All scales (Mikro through Besar): Medium-High Risk**

NIB + Sertifikat Standar with verification. SBU required from an accredited LSBU if the work falls under construction services. Professional staff need relevant SKK certifications.

For geophysical or geological work, additional sector-specific permits from ESDM (Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources) may apply.

**PMA: 100% foreign ownership allowed.**
intel_2026.whatChanged: Renumbered from a previous KBLI 2020 code. The scope is essentially the same — specialized engineering consulting. If you held the old code, you'll need to update your NIB during the KBLI 2025 transition window that closed in June 2026.
intel_2026.baliContext: Geotechnical surveys and environmental engineering are increasingly in demand in Bali as development pushes into less-studied terrain. Landslide risk assessment in Ubud's hillside areas, coastal erosion studies for beachfront projects, and seismic surveys for new hotel foundations all fall here. Foreign firms with specialized equipment have a genuine competitive advantage — local capacity for advanced geophysical work is still developing.

editorial.headline: Engineering Advice, Design and the Bali PMA Reality
editorial.standfirst: A broad engineering and technical-consulting activity, open nationally to foreign investment and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the engineering consultancy and design work that applies the laws of physics and engineering principles to machines, materials, instruments, structures, processes and systems. Its remit is deliberately wide: machinery and industrial processes sit alongside civil, hydraulic and traffic-engineering projects, as do residential and non-residential building engineering, water-resources civil works, mechanical building systems and sports-facility engineering. The common thread is technical judgement translated into engineered designs, systems and project solutions.

The scope also extends beyond design alone. It includes engineering advice and consultation, environmental technical consultancy, construction work connected with traffic-control systems, and engineering for power-generation networks, transmission, substations and electricity distribution. Industrial processes, production and production facilities are part of the picture, together with projects involving electrical and electronic, mining, chemical, mechanical, industrial, systems and safety engineering. Construction-related project management and field investigation belong here too, as do work involving air conditioning, refrigeration, sanitation, pollution control and acoustics. Geophysical, geological, geochemical and seismic surveys are included, along with geological and geophysical interpretation for the construction sector.

A business undertaking this kind of technical practice can register at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. At the national level, foreign investment is permitted, and ownership by foreign investors can reach 100%. That is the central national position: a firm providing the engineering, consultancy, survey, project-management or related technical work described in the scope has a category built for a wide range of engineered projects rather than a narrow specialist assignment.

Bali requires a separate reading, but the result remains clear. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. This activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and at the Besar scale its OSS risk is Medium-High/High; the record specifically states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. On the record supplied, the activity is therefore open nationally and remains available for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The national position is open, and Bali does not block this activity under its permanent PMA moratorium.

ruang_lingkup.uraian: Kode subklasifikasi: IG002 Kelompok ini mencakup layanan usaha terkait pelaksanaan akuisisi data geospasial berbasis metode terestrial, utamanya keahlian penentuan posisi 3 (tiga) dimensi titik kontrol geodesi, pengukuran sudut, jarak, luas, dan beda tinggi dalam lingkup survei titik kontrol tanah, survei Jaring Kontrol Horizontal, survei Jaring Kontrol Vertikal, survei detail situasi, survei utilitas, survei toponim, survei penegasan batas, dan survei gaya berat

Kode subklasifikasi: IG001 Kelompok ini mencakup layanan usaha terkait penyiapan dokumen perencanaan dan pengawasan untuk pelaksanaan akuisisi data geospasial (berbasis metode terestrial, teknik fotogra-metri, penginderaan jauh, dan hidrografi), pengolahan foto udara dan citra, perancangan dan pembangunan sistem basis data serta analisis spasial, analisis kewilayah-an, penyajian informasi geospasial, dan pengelolaan dan penyebarluasan Data Geospasial/Informasi Geospasial
Usaha dalam kelompok ini adalah usaha jasa konsultansi dalam bidang instalasi tenaga listrik
Kelompok ini mencakup jasa konsultasi kegiatan survei geofisika, survei geologi, survei seismik dan survei geokimia

Kode subklasifikasi: IG005 Kelompok ini mencakup layanan usaha terkait: (1) Kompilasi/ ekstraksi data berbasis foto udara dan citra penginderaan jauh untuk mendapatkan informasi geospasial (2) Perancangan dan pembangunan sistem basis data serta analisis spasial (3) Analisis kewilayahan (4) Penyajian informasi geospasial (5) Pengelolaan dan penyebarluasan Data Geo-spasial/ Informasi Geospasial

Kode subklasifikasi: IG004 Kelompok ini mencakup layanan usaha terkait pelaksanaan akuisisi data geospasial hidrografi utamanya untuk kegiatan pengamatan pasut, pengukuran garis pantai, dan pemeruman termasuk pengolahan datanya

Kode subklasifikasi: IG003 Kelompok ini mencakup layanan usaha terkait Fotogrametri dan Penginderaan Jauh (Earth Observing and Scanning) untuk melaksanakan: (1) akuisisi data geospasial berbasis wahana udara menggunakan metode fotogrametri, lidar, dan Synthetic Aperture Radar atau SAR (2) akuisisi data geospasial berbasis wahana satelit penginderaan jauh menggunakan sensor optik, lidar, dan radar (3) Pengolahan hasil akuisisi data fotogrametri dan penginderaan jauh untuk menghasilkan antara lain ortofoto, Digital Surface Model (DSM), Digital Terrain Model (DTM) sesuai ketentuan

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Technical certification services — issuing certificates that confirm a product, system, or process meets specific technical standards (SNI, ISO, or sector-specific standards). You are the certifying body, not the company being certified.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**Micro / Small / Medium scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued within 5 working days.

**Micro / Small / Medium / Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued within 5 working days.

**Small / Medium scale**: High risk. NIB dan Izin — issued within 7 working days.

**Large scale**: High risk. NIB dan Izin — issued within 7 working days.


**PMA:** Fully open to PMA — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Unchanged from KBLI 2020 — direct match.
intel_2026.baliContext: Technical certification in Indonesia is accredited through KAN (Komite Akreditasi Nasional) — without KAN accreditation, your certificates have no legal standing. Key certification areas relevant to Bali: SNI product certification (textiles, electronics, food packaging), ISO management system certification (9001, 14001, 45001), and organic certification (SNI 6729:2025). Established certification bodies (BV, SGS, Intertek, TUV) dominate; a new entrant needs full KAN accreditation which takes 2–3 years.

editorial.headline: Technical Certification Is Open Nationally and Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers certification across products, processes, services and management systems, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Technical certification is the business of assessing and certifying products, processes, services and systems. Its remit reaches well beyond a single industry: the recorded scope includes certification for quality, environmental and food-safety management systems; HACCP; energy management; medical-device management; supply-chain security; laboratory biorisk; anti-bribery; information-technology services; compliance; sustainable events; tourism; ecolabels; occupational safety and health; organic systems; forestry and timber legality; ISPO; halal products; green industry; construction services and warehouses. In practical terms, this is an assurance activity whose subject may be an organisation’s system, a commercial service, a product standard or a defined operational process.

The code is open across the full recorded business-scale range: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because certification is not framed here as an activity reserved for one size of enterprise. The national position is equally clear: it is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The applicable national reference recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national openness in this record. The provincial rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not recorded as blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low risk boundary. The Bali status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: the relevant point is not that Bali creates a separate foreign-ownership cap, but that the activity is not caught by the province-wide PMA moratorium on the lower-risk categories.

For a founder, the distinction is worth holding precisely. Nationally, the activity permits up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the record does not show a moratorium prohibition for it; rather, it identifies a higher risk classification at the Besar scale. That is the honest picture supplied by the record: an open technical-certification activity, available across all listed scales, whose Bali position remains outside the permanent restriction aimed at Low and Medium-Low risk activities.
editorial.pullQuote: In Bali, this activity is not caught by the province-wide PMA moratorium because its recorded Besar-scale risk sits above the restricted categories.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Technical inspection services — providing professional inspection of equipment, facilities, structures, or processes to verify safety, compliance, or condition. Think building inspections, boiler inspections, lifting equipment inspection, and food safety facility audits.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**Micro / Small / Medium / Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB + Standard Certificate — issued within 5 working days.

**Micro / Small / Medium / Large scale**: Medium-High risk. NIB dan Sertifkat Standar — issued within 30 working days.


**PMA:** Fully open to PMA — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Unchanged from KBLI 2020 — direct match.
intel_2026.baliContext: Technical inspection is in high demand in Bali's construction-heavy environment — villa and hotel structural inspections, electrical system inspections, fire safety equipment checks, and pool safety audits are regular requirements. KAN accreditation is required for inspection bodies (Lembaga Inspeksi — LI). Bali's aging building stock and rapid new construction creates strong market demand. BNSP-certified inspectors are required for certain regulated inspection categories.

- 71201 — Certification services (often bundled)

editorial.headline: Technical Inspection Services: Foreign-Open, Not Moratorium-Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers on-site physical, visual and technical inspections, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Technical Inspection Services is the on-site work of examining products, facilities, services or processes—physically, visually or through technical methods—to assess compliance with standards, specifications or regulations. Its scope is broad but coherent: agricultural processes and inspections; fisheries assessments and compliance inspections; health-facility infrastructure; technical traceability for exports, imports and inter-island trade; and inspections in infrastructure, manufacturing and safety. It also includes visual inspection, periodic inspection services, installation-inspection services, ship-classification inspection, aerodrome-safety inspection and inspection of health facilities and infrastructure.

The practical common thread is verification at the point where an activity, asset or product can be observed and tested. That can mean inspection connected with oil and gas, electricity, disaster-protection facilities, non-destructive testing, commercial buildings and their environmental setting, including exhaust emissions, ambient-air quality and working environments. It can also concern manufactured goods such as food and beverages, pharmaceuticals, textiles and textile products, production processes and children’s toys. The code is therefore suited to an inspection operation whose stated work is assessing conformity in the field, rather than merely advising on it.

At Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, registration is open. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. That is a direct reading: a foreign investor may register this technical-inspection activity under the national position without a foreign-equity cap below full ownership.

Bali does not reverse that national opening. The provincial rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island on a permanent basis. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At Besar scale, the OSS risk reading is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the activity sits outside the moratorium block rather than within it. For a foreign-owned registration in Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: this activity is not moratorium-blocked, while the Besar-scale risk classification remains Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign-owned registration in Bali, this activity is not moratorium-blocked.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices
moratorium.virtual_office: requested in letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP; application not confirmed

editorial.headline: Technical Verification, Validation and the Evidence Behind Compliance
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 71203 covers objective technical assurance work, from carbon-footprint verification to industrial commissioning, with full national foreign ownership and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Technical verification and validation is the business of establishing, through objective evidence, that a product, process or system meets its technical requirements and works for its intended purpose. It is a disciplined assurance activity: not merely an opinion on performance, but a formal confirmation built on evidence. Its remit also includes validation for intended future use or application, including projects involving greenhouse-gas environmental information and carbon economic value.

The verification side is equally broad. The activity can confirm that defined requirements have been met for organisations and projects in the greenhouse-gas information sector, emissions projects and reports, domestic-component levels, company-benefit weighting, financial-sector matters and carbon footprints. It also encompasses industrial-process commissioning, quality assurance and quality control. Taken together, this is an activity for businesses whose work sits where technical claims, performance requirements and documented evidence must be brought into alignment.

Businesses may register at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is the straightforward national position in the record: a foreign investor may hold the full permitted stake in a company registered for this activity. The practical identity of the business, however, still needs to remain faithful to the assurance work described here—validation, verification, commissioning, quality assurance and quality control supported by objective evidence.

Bali does not alter that picture into a present registration ban. The province’s standing rule permanently blocks PMA registration, island-wide, for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. For this activity, however, the record states that OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. Bali’s status is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: not a claim that every operational question disappears, but a clear indication that the provincial moratorium is not the barrier for this activity at the stated scale. For founders, the honest reading is uncomplicated: full foreign ownership is nationally available, and the Bali record does not mark this activity as blocked for PMA registration.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

Daftar tenaga jasa survei (Surveyor) yang kompeten di bidang Jasa Survei sebagai berikut:





  1. Paling sedikit 5 (lima) orang Surveyor memiliki kewarganegaraan Indonesia di kantor pusat dan 1 (satu) orang di kantor cabang yang masing-masing dilengkapi dengan:

    • Salinan Sertifikat Kompetensi Kerja yang diterbitkan oleh instansi yang berwenang;

    • Surat pernyataan yang menyatakan bahwa Surveyor tidak terdaftar pada Pelaku Usaha lain yang sejenis;

    • Daftar Riwayat Hidup (Curriculum Vitae);




  2. Dalam hal diperlukan, dapat mempekerjakan warga negara asing sebagai penasihat teknis (technical advisor) sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang-undangan.
kewajiban: Menyampaikan laporan kepada Menteri Perdagangan sesuai ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan
Menetapkan dan menerapkan standar, prosedur dan tata cara Jasa Survei
Menjaga kerahasiaan Laporan Survei
Bertanggung jawab terhadap hasil pekerjaan Tenaga Jasa Survei (Surveyor) yang termuat dalam Laporan Survei dan/atau dokumen lainnya

Menggunakan fasilitas pengujian sampel yang telah terakreditasi oleh instansi atau lembaga yang berwenang 7. Mencantumkan nomor perizinan berusaha dan nomor Sertifikat Kompetensi/ Pelatihan Tenaga Survei (Surveyor) di tempat yang mudah terlihat pada lokasi usaha dan pada setiap kegiatan publikasi, baik, pada media cetak, media elektronik, maupun media lainnya
Membuat perjanjian tertulis dengan Pengguna Jasa Survei yang paling sedikit memuat klausula sesuai dengan ketentuan peraturan perundang undangan di bidang jasa survei

persyaratan: Memiliki dokumen struktur organisasi yang memuat ketersediaan SDM dengan kompetensi teknis sesuai usaha jasa

Memiliki dokumen perjanjian kerja antara perusahaan dengan tenaga kerja kompeten untuk memberikan jasa yang berstatus pegawai tetap atau pegawai kontrak minimal 1 tahun, dengan jumlah pegawai paling sedikit: a) Industri skala kecil: 1 orang level teknis/ operasional/staff b) Industri skala menengah: 1 orang level manajer, 1 orang level profesional/ supervisor, dan 1 orang level teknis/ operasional/staff
Memiliki dokumen bagan alur: a) bisnis proses penjualan jasa b) proses layanan purna jual penjualan jasa

Memiliki dokumen berupa: a) spesifikasi mesin dan/atau daftar peralatan, sebagai sarana penunjang b) foto mesin/ peralatan, sebagai sarana penunjang dan c) perjanjian jual beli/sewa yang membuktikan penguasaan (kepemilikan/ sewa) mesin/ peralatan sebagai sarana penunjang untuk menghasilkan jasa
kewajiban: Memiliki bukti penyampaian wajib Data Industri tervalidasi setiap 6 (enam) bulan sekali sesuai peraturan perundang undangan di bidang perindustrian
Menjamin keamanan dan keselamatan alat dan proses penyelenggaraan jasa, sesuai peraturan perundang undangan
Memiliki sertifikat Sistem Manajemen Mutu (ISO 9001) pada ruang lingkup usaha pemberian jasa
Memiliki sertifikat pelatihan kompetensi SDM penyedia jasa dan
Memiliki sertifikat kalibrasi untuk peralatan yang berfungsi untuk mengukur

editorial.headline: Technical Testing: The Discipline Behind a Valid Result
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers technical testing, calibration and laboratory work across materials, equipment, products and environmental indicators, with national PMA openness extending to Bali.
editorial.body:
Technical testing is the business of making materials, processes, products and instruments answerable to evidence. This activity includes sampling to establish the characteristics of a material or process; assessing physical characteristics, composition and performance; and operating laboratories on a periodic basis. Its remit is deliberately broad: testing may be physical, mechanical, chemical, biological, microbiological, electrical, nuclear-power-related, visual or checklist-based, forensic, or otherwise analytical. The work reaches across industry, trade, energy and mineral resources, construction, transport, telecommunications, pharmaceuticals, food, agriculture, forestry and environmental measurement, including water, air and soil quality.

It also covers calibration and metrology across measurements such as temperature, mass, volume, pressure, force, torque, flow, hardness, density, length, electricity, magnetism, time, frequency, acoustics, vibration, photometry, radiometry and ionising-radiation analytical instruments. Industrial instruments, machinery and measuring equipment fall within that calibration work, as do periodic testing or calibration of medical equipment, electronics and other technologies. The scope further includes animal, plant and fisheries quarantine testing, marine testing, and work on ionising-radiation equipment including surveymeters, contamination meters, dosimeters and X-ray multimeters. Calibration may also include verification and stamping so that a measuring or calibration instrument can be regarded as valid.

Businesses may register at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. At the national level, PMA participation is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is a clean national position: foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali’s position is also open in practical terms. The province’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and PMA registration is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; that higher-risk classification is specifically why this activity is not caught by the moratorium. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA restriction applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities, not to this one. For a technical-testing operator, the distinction matters: the activity is nationally open and remains registrable for PMA in Bali, while its risk position at the largest scale sits above the moratorium’s threshold.
editorial.pullQuote: The activity is nationally open and remains registrable for PMA in Bali, while its largest-scale risk position sits above the moratorium’s threshold.
