editorial.headline: Licensing Intellectual Property: Nationally Open, PMA-Barred in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity turns non-copyright intellectual-property rights into royalty income—open nationally to full foreign ownership, yet barred from PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 77400 is the business of allowing another party to use non-copyright intellectual-property assets, or comparable products, in exchange for royalties or licence consideration paid to the owner or asset holder. Permission can take several commercial forms: reproduction, use within a later process or production, or the operation of a business under a franchise system. The present owner need not be the person who created the asset. It can therefore sit behind arrangements that make an asset usable by another enterprise without transferring ownership.

The activity includes operational leasing without an option for eligible intellectual-property products, together with receiving royalties or licence fees. The record identifies patented entities, trademarks and service marks, trade names, mineral-exploration rights, franchise agreements, internet domains, and rights in designed or developed board games. It also includes royalties or licence fees for the results of scientific research. The category is framed by the commercial permission and the fee stream attached to it, however varied the underlying asset may be.

Nationally, the investment position is unambiguous. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, spanning the full range stated in the record. Its national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, so there is no national cap below full foreign ownership. For founders, that means the rights-and-royalties character of the business does not confine it to a particular listed scale, and the national setting permits a wholly foreign-owned PMA registration.

Bali changes the answer completely. For this activity, Bali's moratorium is decisive: a foreigner cannot register it there as PMA today. At the Besar scale, every scope is recorded as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing the activity within Bali's permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for those risk levels. This is not a reduction of the national 100% ceiling or a case-by-case caution; it is a provincial bar under the moratorium dated 13 May 2026. National openness remains relevant outside Bali, but within Bali the moratorium controls the registration outcome.
editorial.pullQuote: For this activity, Bali's moratorium is decisive: a foreigner cannot register it there as PMA today.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Aktivitas Jasa Intermediasi untuk Penyewaan dan Sewa Guna Usaha Mobil
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup aktivitas jasa intermediasi untuk penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha mobil, motorhome dan trailer, dengan mempertemukan klien dan penyedia layanan dengan biaya atau komisi, tanpa intermediator harus menyediakan layanan penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha untuk barang yang diperantarai. Aktivitas intermediasi ini dapat dilakukan pada platform digital maupun nondigital (tatap muka termasuk dari pintu ke pintu, telepon, surat, dll.). Biaya atau komisi dapat diterima baik dari klien maupun penyedia layanan penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha. Pendapatan untuk aktivitas intermediasi dapat mencakup sumber pendapatan lain, seperti pendapatan dari iklan.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup layanan reservasi untuk penyewaan mobil.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha kendaraan atau truk dengan pengemudi, lihat subgolongan 4922, motorhome dan trailer, lihat subgolongan 4923;
- jasa intermediasi untuk transportasi penumpang, lihat subgolongan 5232.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This KBLI covers acting as an intermediary or broker for car, motorhome, and trailer rentals and leases. You earn a fee or commission by connecting clients with vehicle providers—without needing to own or operate the fleet yourself. The activity can be run fully online (e.g., an app or website) or through traditional face-to-face channels.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, it's not blocked, but it carries a higher-risk classification. That means registration is possible, though you'll likely face extra scrutiny and must verify that your chosen business address is accepted by local authorities—not every location may qualify.

editorial.headline: Vehicle-Rental Intermediation: Nationally Open, Bali Scope-Sensitive
editorial.standfirst: This is an introductions-and-reservations business, open nationally to full foreign ownership but subject to a scope-and-risk test for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is a business of introductions rather than vehicles. It covers arranging the rental and leasing of cars, motorhomes and trailers by bringing clients together with service providers for a fee or commission. The intermediary is not required to supply the rental or lease itself. That distinction matters: the commercial value lies in arranging access and reservations, including car-rental reservation services, while income may also include advertising revenue.

The introduction can be made through a digital platform, but it need not be. Face-to-face contact, door-to-door activity, telephone and correspondence all fall within the described formats. Commission or fees may be received from either the client or the rental and leasing provider. The record specifically identifies non-exempt electronic-trade-system operators and intermediary-facility operators, whether established within Indonesian jurisdiction or established abroad while conducting electronic-commerce business in Indonesia. It also places the activity beyond those operators and makes it available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales.

For foreign capital, the national position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA, and the 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling means a foreign stake may reach full ownership. The source cited for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. National openness, however, is not the end of the analysis for a business intending to register in Bali.

Bali is not recorded as a blanket block for this activity, but its status depends on the declared scope. The province permanently blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is low for some scopes and higher for others; PMA registration in Bali is possible only by declaring the higher-risk scope, such as PPMSE in a platform-trade declaration. The practical conclusion is precise rather than sweeping: the business is nationally open, while a Bali PMA filing must be matched to the exact activity and verified in live OSS before it is treated as registrable.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not settle the Bali question: the declared scope and its OSS risk determine whether PMA registration can proceed.

data.judul: Aktivitas Jasa Intermediasi untuk Penyewaan dan Sewa Guna Usaha Barang Berwujud dan Aset Tak Berwujud Nonfinansial Lainnya
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup jasa intermediasi untuk penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha barang berwujud dan aset tak berwujud nonfinansial dengan mempertemukan klien dan penyedia layanan dengan biaya atau komisi, tanpa intermediator harus menyediakan layanan penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha untuk barang yang diperantarai. Aktivitas intermediasi ini dapat dilakukan pada platform digital maupun nondigital (tatap muka termasuk dari pintu ke pintu, telepon, surat, dll.). Komisi dapat diterima dari klien atau penyedia layanan penyewaan. Pendapatan untuk kegiatan intermediasi dapat mencakup sumber pendapatan lain, seperti pendapatan dari iklan. Kelompok ini juga mencakup penyediaan intermediasi antara rumah tangga yang menawarkan barang mereka untuk disewa dan rumah tangga penyewa barang, misalnya pemotong rumput, tangga, dan sepeda.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup
- unit yang memiliki kepemilikan dari barang berwujud dan/atau aset keuangan nonfinansial tidak berwujud yang akhirnya disewa, lihat golongan 772 dan 773;
- penyewaan dan sewa guna usaha barang keperluan pribadi, barang-barang rumah tangga, dan peralatan serta barang-barang berwujud lainnya, lihat golongan 772 dan 773.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers services that act as a middleman, connecting clients who need to rent or lease tangible goods (e.g., equipment, vehicles) or intangible non-financial assets with providers, earning a commission or fee. The intermediation can happen via digital platforms or offline methods, and the intermediary does not actually provide or own the goods being rented.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is 100% open for foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the current moratorium, so a PMA can technically register it. However, it carries a medium-high/high risk rating, which means your business location will be scrutinized closely and you must verify that your specific address meets local zoning and operational requirements.

editorial.headline: The Rental Intermediary That Does Not Own the Rental
editorial.standfirst: This activity is for the business of connecting renters with providers—not for owning the goods or supplying the rental itself.
editorial.body:
This activity covers intermediation for the rental and leasing of tangible goods and non-financial intangible assets. Its role is to bring clients and service providers together for a fee or commission, without the intermediary having to provide the underlying rental or leasing service. The work may happen through digital platforms or non-digital channels, including face-to-face contact, door-to-door activity, telephone and correspondence. Commission may come from either the client or the rental provider, while advertising revenue may also form part of the intermediary’s income.

The boundary matters. This is not an activity for the business that owns the tangible goods or non-financial intangible assets ultimately rented out, nor for the business that directly rents or leases them. It also expressly includes intermediation between households offering their own goods for hire and households seeking them—such as lawn mowers, ladders and bicycles. The stated operators include non-exempt PPMSE and PSP, whether established within Indonesia’s legal jurisdiction or operating electronic-commerce activities there from outside it.

Nationally, the PMA position is open, with foreign ownership permitted up to **100%**. It can be carried out at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That national position, however, is not the whole Bali answer. Bali is not marked as categorically blocked for this activity; instead, the result depends on the precise declared scope. At the Besar scale, some scopes carry low OSS risk while others carry higher risk. A PMA registration in Bali is possible only by declaring the higher-risk scope, with PPMSE given in the record as an example.

Bali’s standing provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration, island-wide and permanently. The practical conclusion is precise rather than dramatic: foreign ownership is nationally open, but a Bali filing cannot be assumed from that fact alone. The declared scope and its live OSS risk treatment are decisive, and the exact activity must be verified in live OSS before registration.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness is not the whole answer: in Bali, the declared scope and its live OSS risk treatment decide whether a PMA registration can proceed.

data.judul: Aktivitas Penempatan Tenaga Kerja untuk Usaha di Dalam Negeri
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pendaftaran, penyeleksian dan penempatan tenaga kerja untuk kegiatan pada berbagai bidang usaha di dalam negeri. Dalam kelompok ini, tenaga kerja yang ditempatkan tidak berstatus sebagai pegawai dari perusahaan penempatan tenaga kerja. Kelompok ini juga mencakup penyediaan tenaga kerja eksekutif untuk pihak lain. Kelompok ini tidak mencakup penyediaan tenaga kerja untuk kegiatan rumah tangga sebagai pemberi kerja di dalam negeri, seperti penempatan asisten rumah tangga dan sopir pribadi, lihat kelompok 78102.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers a professional manpower agency that sources, screens, and places workers directly with client businesses inside Indonesia — but crucially, those workers are not your own employees. You can also place executive-level staff for other companies, but you cannot supply domestic household staff like maids or drivers (that falls under a different category).
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not blocked by the general moratorium, but because the local authority treats it as a higher-risk activity, your specific business address will be subject to case-by-case verification and you may face closer scrutiny during licensing.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: matched with aggregation.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Penempatan Tenaga Kerja untuk Usaha di Dalam Negeri (78101)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs who want to run a legal recruitment and executive placement agency in Bali placing talent into Indonesian companies, but not supplying household or domestic helpers.

editorial.headline: 78101: Placing Talent for Indonesia’s Domestic Businesses
editorial.standfirst: A nationwide employment-placement activity, open across every business scale and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 78101 covers the business of bringing workers and employers together for activity across Indonesia’s domestic business sectors. Its work begins with registration and selection, then moves to placement: finding people, assessing them and placing them with organisations that need them. The workers placed through this activity do not become employees of the placement company itself. The scope also includes supplying executive personnel to other parties, giving the category a clear role at both operational and senior-management level.

This is an activity for employment-placement businesses rather than employers simply hiring for their own workforce. It is open at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the underlying activity is defined by the function performed—registration, selection and placement—not by the size of the organisation carrying it out. The supplied scope draws a boundary around household-employer placements, including domestic assistants and personal drivers, which are not part of this activity.

Nationally, the position is direct. The record marks the activity TERBUKA for PMA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. There is no lower foreign-share cap in the supplied data, and no additional national condition is stated here. The applicable PMA source in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national position. This activity is not blocked by Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The record’s reason is specific: at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside the moratorium’s blocked risk bands. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK—not a promise that every operational question has disappeared, but a clear indication that this activity is not shut out of PMA registration by that provincial moratorium. For a founder considering an employment-placement business in Bali, that distinction is the essential one: the national foreign-ownership position remains intact, and the Bali moratorium does not block this code.
editorial.pullQuote: For a founder considering an employment-placement business in Bali, the national foreign-ownership position remains intact and the provincial moratorium does not block this code.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Aktivitas Penempatan Tenaga Kerja Luar Negeri
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan penyampaian informasi, pencarian personel, pendaftaran, penyeleksian, penempatan, serta perlindungan pekerja migran Indonesia yang bekerja pada pemberi kerja di luar negeri dalam berbagai bidang usaha. Dalam kelompok ini, tenaga kerja yang ditempatkan tidak berstatus sebagai pegawai dari perusahaan penempatan tenaga kerja. Kelompok ini juga mencakup penyediaan tenaga eksekutif luar negeri.

editorial.headline: Overseas Worker Placement, With Bali’s Risk Line in View
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the placement and protection of Indonesian migrant workers abroad, with full national foreign ownership permitted and no Bali moratorium block recorded at large scale.
editorial.body:
This activity is the operating framework for connecting Indonesian migrant workers with employers overseas. Its scope is deliberately broad: providing information, searching for personnel, registering and selecting candidates, arranging their placement, and protecting workers once they are employed abroad across different business sectors. It also includes the provision of overseas executive personnel. The crucial distinction is structural: the workers placed through the business are not employees of the placement company itself.

The activity therefore sits at the point where recruitment, placement and worker protection meet. It encompasses both branch offices and head offices for worker-placement operations, recognising that this is not simply a referral function but an organised service with responsibilities extending from initial information through to the protection of Indonesian migrant workers working abroad. Its permitted business scales run from Mikro and Kecil through Menengah and Besar, giving the activity a defined place for operations of very different sizes.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is clear. Classified as TERBUKA, the activity allows foreign ownership up to 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level; it does not present a reduced foreign-stake cap. That national openness should be read alongside the activity’s actual scope: the enterprise is concerned with the placement and protection process, while the people it places remain employed by the overseas employer rather than by the placement business.

Bali’s position is also more precise than a blanket warning would suggest. The provincial moratorium permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide. This activity is not recorded as blocked by that moratorium. The stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it outside the moratorium’s Low and Medium-Low risk trigger. Bali is therefore recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, rather than as a prohibited PMA registration. The practical reading is straightforward: national foreign openness remains intact, and the Bali record does not impose a moratorium block on the activity at the Besar scale.
editorial.pullQuote: National foreign openness remains intact, and Bali’s record does not impose a moratorium block on the activity at the Besar scale.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pendaftaran, penyeleksian, penempatan, serta perlindungan tenaga kerja untuk kegiatan rumah tangga sebagai pemberi kerja di dalam negeri, seperti penempatan asisten rumah tangga, pengasuh balita, perawat nonmedis lansia, dan sopir pribadi berbagai jenis posisi lainnya dalam rumah tangga. Dalam kelompok ini, tenaga kerja yang ditempatkan tidak berstatus sebagai pegawai dari perusahaan penempatan tenaga kerja. Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan penempatan perawat bayi dan pengasuh anak yang tenaga kerjanya berstatus sebagai pegawai dari perusahaan penempatan tenaga kerja, lihat kelompok 78200.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally this is 100% open to foreign ownership, and in Bali it is not blocked by the local moratorium. However, it is classified as medium-high risk, so while a PMA can be registered, expect extra scrutiny — address verification and additional compliance steps will likely apply.

editorial.headline: Placing Household Staff, With a Clear Bali PMA Reading
editorial.standfirst: This domestic household-employment placement activity is open to every business scale, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 78103 is a domestic household-employment placement activity: registering, screening, placing and protecting workers for households that are employers within Indonesia. Its practical orbit includes domestic assistants, toddler carers, non-medical elder carers, personal drivers and other household roles. The essential employment relationship is explicit: people placed through the business do not become employees of the placement company itself. That distinction keeps the activity centred on matching and safeguarding people for household employers, rather than supplying the company’s own workforce.

At Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, the activity is open. That breadth matters because the record treats the service as an activity that can be undertaken from the smallest business scale through the largest, without recasting its purpose. A registrant is therefore operating a placement function for domestic households: building a process around registration, selection, placement and protection, while the worker remains outside the placement company’s employment. The work is defined by the connection between a household employer and the person placed into a household role.

For PMA nationally, the reading is direct: its status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership. That is the national ownership ceiling for this activity. The record identifies the legal source for that position, but it does not supply further operational requirements; none should be inferred from this entry.

Bali requires its own reading, because the province permanently blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing it above the moratorium’s Low and Medium-Low categories. The Bali record accordingly marks the activity as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The honest conclusion is straightforward: a foreign investor is not barred from registering this PMA activity in Bali today, and the national ceiling remains 100% foreign ownership.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally full foreign ownership is permitted, and Bali’s moratorium does not block this activity.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Ship-Crew Placement Is Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: For ship-crew placement, the national record permits up to 100% foreign ownership and Bali does not list a PMA moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Ship-crew placement is a labour-placement activity defined around the people who serve a vessel. Its scope covers the registration, selection, placement and protection of workers for crews on both merchant vessels and fishing vessels. The work may relate to placements in Indonesia or outside it. Read in sequence, the record follows the worker from registration through selection and placement, while retaining protection as part of the activity. Both vessel classes and both locations are named directly in the scope.

The scope expressly lists two operating bases: a central office for worker placement and a branch office for worker placement. It is also open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. These entries identify the office forms inside the activity and show that the scale field spans every category supplied in the record. The distinction between central and branch office is stated directly, not left to assumption. Final placement is only one named function in the scope: registration and selection are named too, while worker protection is included as well.

Nationally, the investment position is TERBUKA. The listed foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, so the national record does not put a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. That national position is recorded under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It applies to the activity’s stated scope: placing and protecting labour for merchant-vessel and fishing-vessel crews, in Indonesia and abroad.

Bali needs a separate reading. The province’s rule permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, island-wide; its cited source is Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. Here, however, the record marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and states that the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The stated reason is specific to the Besar scale, where the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That sits outside the Low and Medium-Low group named in the moratorium rule. For a foreign founder assessing registration today, the result is plain: foreign ownership can reach 100% nationally, and Bali does not block PMA registration for the activity on the recorded moratorium basis.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: A Job Portal’s Place in Indonesia’s Employment Information Market
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers vacancy and jobseeker-information services, open to full foreign ownership nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity sits in the information layer of the employment market. It covers recording and delivering vacancy information to people seeking work, while giving employers information on jobseekers’ data and competencies. In clear commercial terms, it makes employment information usable for both sides: candidates receive vacancy information, while employers receive relevant data and competency information about candidates. Recording is expressly part of the activity, alongside delivery of vacancy information. The record also includes online delivery through a job portal, making that digital route part of the stated scope itself.

The classification is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Its defining feature remains consistent across that range: information flows from available vacancies to jobseekers, and information about jobseekers flows to employers. The record does not frame the activity around a single channel or operating format; it expressly recognises the online job portal as one way it may be carried out. For a founder, the useful boundary is clear: the business is built around recording and communicating employment information between jobseekers and employers.

Nationally, the PMA position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That is a full foreign-ownership ceiling: on the national position recorded here, an investor may hold the entire company conducting this activity. The ownership position is not left to implication or general market practice; it is stated plainly in the record. Nationally, this is an open activity for PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to the full 100% ceiling.

Bali calls for a separate, equally literal reading. The provincial rule permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities across the island. This activity is not blocked. Its Bali assessment is OK or Higher Risk, and the recorded reason says that OSS risk at the Besar scale is Medium-High/High; it therefore sits outside the moratorium’s block. editorial.headline: Beyond the Vacancy: Indonesia’s Other Employment-Placement Activity
editorial.standfirst: This code covers vacancy recording, referrals and job placements outside an employer relationship—and remains open to PMA nationally and in Bali, with address-specific verification.
editorial.body:
KBLI 78109 is an employment-placement activity centred on the movement from vacancy to placement. Its scope includes recording vacancies, referring people to work opportunities and placing workers into a job. The defining boundary is straightforward: the people placed are not employees of the placement company itself. That makes the code about matching and placing labour, rather than employing the labour being placed. The scope expressly includes casting-agency work—selecting performers for theatre and similar productions—and talent-search activities. In practical terms, it describes a placement function spanning job opportunities, performance selection and talent discovery.

Registration is available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The record therefore places no scale-based exclusion on the activity across those four categories. For founders, that is a useful starting point: the stated scope remains the same whether the operation is modest or large. Yet the operational identity should remain precise. A business using this code is registering a function of vacancy recording, referral or placement; it should not blur that function with an employer relationship when workers are placed. Casting and talent search sit within the same stated perimeter, provided the work remains the selection or placement activity described here.

Across Indonesia, the PMA position is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%. Put plainly, the national record permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. No lower national ownership ceiling is stated in this record, so the national picture is clear: foreign investment is open for the activity at the stated 100% ceiling. This ownership position attaches to the activity itself; Bali’s province-level position is considered separately.

In Bali, the record’s result is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and it is not blocked by the moratorium. The reason given is that this is a medium-high/high-risk activity, placing it outside the permanent, island-wide Bali moratorium that blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA. The Bali outcome is therefore not a reversal of the national position: PMA registration is open in Bali today for this activity. The record nonetheless directs verification for the particular address. That is an address-specific check, not a Bali-wide prohibition or an alternative foreign-ownership ceiling. The conclusion is firm but disciplined: this code is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali does not block it under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: This code is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and Bali does not block it under the stated moratorium.

data.judul: Aktivitas Penyediaan Tenaga Kerja Sementara dan Penyediaan Sumber Daya Manusia Lainnya
data.uraian:
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan penyediaan pekerja untuk usaha klien selama periode waktu tertentu, baik untuk menggantikan sementara maupun menambah tenaga kerja klien. Dalam perjanjian kerja tersebut, agen ketenagakerjaan sementara atau penyedia sumber daya manusia adalah pemberi kerja dari pekerja individu yang dipekerjakan. Namun, klien bertanggung jawab atas pengawasan personel sementara. Kegiatan yang diklasifikasikan di sini tidak menyediakan pengawas langsung untuk pekerja yang ditempatkan pada pemberi kerja.
Unit yang diklasifikasikan dalam kelompok ini mewakili pemberi kerja resmi untuk karyawan dalam hal-hal yang berkaitan dengan penggajian, pajak, dan masalah fiskal dan sumber daya manusia lainnya, tetapi tidak bertanggung jawab langsung atas pengawasan karyawan. Unit yang diklasifikasikan dalam kelompok ini melakukan berbagai tugas manajemen sumber daya manusia dan personel yang terkait dengan ketentuan ini.
Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan jasa manajemen sumber daya manusia untuk pemberi kerja. Kegiatan ini dikhususkan untuk menyelenggarakan sumber daya manusia dan tugas manajemen personel. Kegiatan ini menyajikan riwayat kerja pekerja dalam hal yang berhubungan dengan upah, pajak dan masalah keuangan dan sumber daya lainnya termasuk penyedia jasa pekerja/buruh.
Kelompok ini juga mencakup kegiatan penempatan perawat bayi (baby sitter) dan pengasuh anak yang dipekerjakan oleh penyedia tenaga kerja, sedangkan perawat bayi (baby sitter) dan pengasuh anak yang dipekerjakan oleh majikan langsung masuk di subgolongan 7810.
Kelompok ini tidak mencakup kegiatan layanan penagihan, lihat subgolongan 6920.

editorial.headline: Temporary Staffing: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code puts the provider—not the client—in the employer’s seat; it is open nationally to full foreign ownership, but PMA registration in Bali is blocked.
editorial.body:
Today, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali. That is the decisive local fact, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. The Bali record attributes the block to an island-wide, permanent moratorium covering low and medium-low risk activities. For this activity, every scope at the large-enterprise scale is assessed by OSS as low or medium-low risk; the May 2026 moratorium therefore prevents PMA registration in Bali.

At its centre, this is a staffing-provider activity. The provider supplies workers to a client for a specified period, whether the client is temporarily replacing staff or adding personnel. The provider, rather than the client, is the formal employer of the individual workers it places, taking responsibility for payroll, tax, fiscal and other human-resources matters. The client remains responsible for supervising the temporary personnel. The boundary is equally clear: the provider does not supply direct supervisors for workers placed with the client.

The scope also includes human-resources management services for employers: organising people and personnel administration, maintaining worker employment records in connection with wages, taxes, finance and other resources, and supplying workers or labour. It includes the placement of babysitters and child carers when those workers are employed by the staffing provider. The commercial centre of gravity is therefore the provider’s employer and personnel-management role, even where people perform their day-to-day work for a client.

The activity is open to micro, small, medium and large enterprises. Nationally, its open status and 100% ceiling mean that the foreign stake may reach full ownership. But that national position should not be mistaken for permission in Bali. The Bali status is blocked by risk class, and the stated permanent, island-wide moratorium means a foreign-owned company cannot register this activity there today. The clear reading is national openness in principle, set against a local PMA registration bar in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: The clear reading is national openness in principle, set against a local PMA registration bar in Bali.

editorial.headline: Travel Agency: a National Opening, a Bali Closure
editorial.standfirst: This activity sells packaged journeys as an intermediary, but a 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling does not override Bali’s permanent block on PMA registration.
editorial.body:
Travel-agency activity is the business of intermediating the sale of travel packages assembled by travel bureaus, whether sold wholesale or retail, online or offline, to the public or commercial clients. Its remit also includes acting as an intermediary for Umrah and special Hajj packages, as well as sports-travel packages built around physical activity, competition or sport-based entertainment. The scope reaches further into arranging the conclusion of contracts for tourism services supplied by travel bureaus, and into intermediating destination travel packages. In practical terms, this is a sales-and-arrangement role within the packaged-travel economy rather than the creation of the underlying package itself.

The record opens this activity to businesses at the Micro and Small scales. That framing matters because the code is designed around a defined commercial role: connecting customers or clients with travel packages and related arrangements offered through travel bureaus. It can serve leisure travel, religious journeys, sports-focused trips and destination-based packages, across both digital and offline channels. The activity’s breadth lies in the types of package it can intermediate, while its core identity remains consistent: it stands between the travel bureau’s prepared offering and the eventual purchaser.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is marked **TERBATAS**, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited presidential regulations. A 100% ceiling means the national record does not impose a lower foreign-equity cap for this activity. That is the national position, and it should be read precisely as such.

Bali is different. A foreign investor has no way to register this activity in Bali today. The Bali record marks it as blocked for PMA and identifies travel agency activity as proposed for closure. It also records an island-wide, permanent provincial rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA. The result is clear: national foreign-ownership capacity does not create a Bali registration route for PMA here. For a founder considering this activity, the relevant conclusion is not a theoretical comparison between markets but a present operational fact—Bali’s PMA door is closed despite the national 100% ceiling.
editorial.pullQuote: National foreign-ownership capacity does not create a Bali registration route for PMA here.

editorial.headline: Travel Bureau Activity: Building and Selling the Journey
editorial.standfirst: A nationally open activity for medium and large travel bureaux, with Bali’s PMA moratorium not blocking the large-scale risk profile recorded here.
editorial.body:
A travel bureau under this activity plans and assembles tourism packages, then brings them to market. The work can encompass nature travel and sports tourism, including journeys and experiences built around physical activity, competition or sport-based entertainment. It is not confined to itinerary design: the bureau may organise and sell packages through travel agents or directly to travellers and consumers.

The operational reach is deliberately broad within the package itself. A bureau may provide guide services connected to the packages it sells, whether online or offline; provide tourist transport; reserve accommodation, food and convention venues; and arrange tickets for arts, culture and tourist attractions. It may also handle travel documents, including passports, visas and equivalent documents. The common thread is the coordination of a travel experience and the services that make that experience bookable and deliverable.

The activity is open nationally to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Registration is open at the **Menengah** and **Besar** scales. That national openness is important, but Bali calls for a more exact reading than a generic statement about foreign investment. Bali’s permanent province-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for all low-risk and medium-low-risk KBLI activities. This record, however, does not mark the activity as blocked in Bali.

The reason is specific to the recorded large-scale profile: in OSS, the **Besar** scale carries a medium-high risk classification, placing it outside the moratorium described in the record. Bali’s status is therefore recorded as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, not as a prohibition. For a foreign-owned travel bureau, the honest conclusion is straightforward: the activity is nationally open up to full foreign ownership, and the Bali moratorium does not block it on the risk basis stated for the large-scale operation. The practical reading should remain tied to that stated scale and risk basis, rather than treating the provincial rule as either irrelevant or universally disqualifying.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s moratorium does not block the recorded large-scale travel-bureau profile, because its OSS risk level sits outside the low and medium-low categories.

editorial.headline: Umrah and Special-Hajj Travel: Reserved to Domestic Capital
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the assembly and sale of Umrah and special-Hajj travel packages — foreign shareholding is 0%, and Bali's open moratorium position does not change that.
editorial.body:
An Umrah and special-Hajj pilgrimage travel bureau plans and assembles travel packages for these forms of worship. Those packages may be channelled through travel agents or sold directly to consumers, online or in person. The activity reaches beyond the itinerary itself: it includes services connected to the package sold, including transport, accommodation and meals, as well as handling travel documents such as passports, visas and equivalent documents. In practical terms, this is the organising business behind a pilgrimage journey, from the package design through the travel services and documentation that support it.

The activity is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the activity to a single size of operator. A bureau may operate around the planning and sale of pilgrimage packages while using either agent distribution or direct consumer sales, and may do so through digital or offline channels. Its defined scope keeps the focus on Umrah and special-Hajj travel packages and the services attached to those packages.

This activity is closed to foreign shareholding. Perpres 49/2021, Lampiran III — the annex of business fields carrying specific requirements — lists it at entry #36, reserved to domestic capital, with an Islamic-faith requirement recorded alongside it. Foreign shareholding is 0%, so a PT PMA cannot register an Umrah or special-Hajj travel bureau anywhere in Indonesia.

That is the distinction worth holding, because the Bali line points the other way and it is the weaker of the two. Bali's moratorium does not catch this activity — it is recorded above the low and medium-low risk band the moratorium blocks. But a provincial door standing open is of no use when the national one is shut: the reservation applies wherever the company would be registered.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali's moratorium leaves this one alone, and it makes no difference: the reservation to domestic capital is national, so there is no PMA path to keep open.

Dokumen Penilaian Mandiri Kesiapan Penerapan Standar
Silakan kirim semua dokumen yang diminta dalam satu file.
1. Unduh dan lengkapi formulir Penilaian Mandiri.
2. Dokumentasi Standar Pelaksanaan Kegiatan Usaha.
Lampirkan 6 dokumen Sarana
  1. Petunjuk identitas/nama usaha dengan tulisan yang terbaca.
  2. Ruang kantor/area administrasi yang dilengkapi peralatan dan perlengkapan kerja.
  3. Peralatan Pertolongan Pertama pada Kecalakaan (P3K) dan Alat Pemadam Api Ringan (APAR) yang berfungsi dengan baik.
  4. Ketersediaan air bersih yang tidak berwarna, tidak berbau, tidak berasa, dan jernih.
  5. Ketersediaan gudang atau tempat penyimpanan barang yang aman.
  6. Status kepemilikan kantor/tempat usaha yang jelas.
Lampirkan 1 dokumen Sumber Daya Manusia
Perlindungan asuransi kesehatan dan/atau kecelakaan bagi karyawan tersedia dan berlaku.
Lampirkan 1 dokumen Ketentuan Produksi
Pelayanan kesehatan, seperti informasi tentang dokter, rumah sakit, atau klinik terdekat terdokumentasi.
Lampirkan 3 dokumen Sistem Manajemen Usaha
  1. Struktur organisasi dan uraian tugas setiap jabatan jalas dan terdokumentasi.
  2. rencana bisnis (business plan) masih berlaku dan terdokumentasi.
  3. S0P dan/atau petunjuk teknis pelaksanaan karja masih berlaku dan terdokumentasi.

editorial.headline: The Travel Agency Code for Complex Journeys
editorial.standfirst: For medium and large travel agencies assembling complex itineraries, the national position is open to full foreign ownership—and Bali does not block PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 79129 covers travel-agency activity that sits outside the specifically enumerated travel-agency groupings. Its practical terrain is the assembled journey: arranging transport, accommodation, food, convention venues and travel documentation, whether the service is delivered online or offline. That can include passports, visas and equivalent documents, as well as the planning and packaging of the individual components that make a business trip work.

The code is particularly legible where travel has many moving parts and a clear professional purpose. The record gives the example of business-travel planning for athletes and sports teams competing at international events. The point is not merely booking a route or a room; it is coordinating the service elements around a trip so that transport, stays, meals, venues and documentation can be brought into one travel-agency operation.

Registration is open at the medium and large business scales. Nationally, the activity is marked open for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full national ceiling for this activity. That national position is sourced to the Presidential Regulations identified in the record, and it should be read alongside the scale limitation: this is an activity open to medium and large enterprises, not a catch-all invitation across every business scale.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s standing for this activity is recorded as OK or higher risk, and the Bali moratorium does not block PMA registration. The reason is specific: at the large scale, the OSS risk classification is medium-high or high. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to low and medium-low risk KBLI activities; this activity is therefore outside that block on the record provided. For a foreign founder considering a Bali-based travel-agency operation within this scope, the honest conclusion is straightforward: the activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign founder, this activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.

editorial.headline: Tourism Information Services: Nationally Open, Not Registrable by PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity can be wholly foreign-owned nationally, yet Bali’s scale structure prevents a PT PMA from registering it there.
editorial.body:
Tourism information services are the practical information layer around a visitor’s journey. The activity covers providing information on tourist attractions and facilities, tourism services, transport, and other material a traveller may need. That information may be distributed in print, electronically, or through other communications media, and can include information about booking services, accommodation, food, flights, land transport, and sea transport. The emphasis is on making tourism information available: a business that helps visitors understand options and navigate the services around their stay.

The permitted business scales are Mikro, Kecil, and Menengah. That boundary is consequential rather than incidental. The record places this activity in the Low risk band, which is what puts it inside the Bali moratorium described above. In other words, the licensing annex sets out the scales for the permit; what decides a PT PMA’s position in Bali is the moratorium on the Low and Medium-Low risk tiers.

At the national level, the position is open: foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is a clear national foreign-investment ceiling, but it does not travel automatically into Bali registration. In Bali, a foreign investor cannot register this activity through a PT PMA today. The stated reason is provincial: Bali's moratorium suspends PMA registration island-wide for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, and no restriction on foreign ownership of the activity itself was located. The result is not a partial foreign-ownership limitation in Bali; it is a registration block for the PT PMA form.

The Bali record also notes a permanent, island-wide provincial rule blocking PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The record does not assign a risk classification to this activity, so that broader rule should not be used to invent one. The decisive point is already explicit: Bali’s available scales do not permit a PT PMA registration for this tourism-information activity. Founders should therefore keep the two questions separate—national ownership openness and Bali registrability—because the first is fully open while the second is closed to a PT PMA.
editorial.pullQuote: National ownership openness does not automatically translate into Bali registrability.

editorial.headline: Tourist-Attraction Information: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Information services around natural, built and cultural attractions are nationally open to PMA, yet a foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali under the recorded structural constraint.
editorial.body:
This activity makes information about tourist attractions a defined business activity. It covers information on natural, built and cultural attractions, including data, news, features, photographs, video and research. It also extends to reports on visiting activity created by influencers, buzzers and endorsers. Just as importantly, the scope includes circulating that information through print, electronic or other communication media, online as well as offline.

The work can therefore take several editorial and communications forms: factual data, news reporting, visual material, features and research all fall within the activity when their subject is a tourist attraction. Its distribution remit is equally broad. Such information may be spread in print, electronically or through another communications medium, in a digital setting or offline. The national scale listing opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil and Menengah businesses. That listing is about business scale, not foreign ownership: Bali's finding turns instead on the activity's risk tier, and the moratorium closes PMA registration for every activity in that tier.

At national level, the activity is marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. This is not a partial-ownership category: the record gives no national sub-100 percent foreign ceiling. For a founder assessing only the national position, that is the governing picture—foreign investment is open on the stated terms. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. But national openness describes the position at that level; it does not itself secure a Bali PMA registration.

Bali changes the conclusion completely. In Bali at present, this activity cannot be registered by a foreign investor. Its Bali status is closed under the 2026 moratorium, with the reason recorded plainly: the province-wide block covers every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, and this activity is classified Low risk. Nationally it stays open to full foreign ownership. The record also states a permanent, island-wide provincial rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA, sourced to Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The honest result is clear: national foreign ownership of 100% does not translate into an available Bali PMA registration.

editorial.headline: Tour-Guide Services Is Reserved for Koperasi and UMKM — Closed to PT PMA Nationwide
editorial.standfirst: This activity — tour-guide services (Jasa Pramuwisata) — is allocated to Koperasi and UMKM under Perpres 49/2021's Lampiran II, which sets foreign ownership at 0% and puts it out of reach of a PT PMA anywhere in Indonesia.
editorial.body:
Tour-guide services are more than an itinerary accessory. This activity covers professional accompaniment and guidance for travellers, including interpretation of culture and nature, as well as help with the practical matters travellers need. It also includes coordinating freelance guides when an individual traveller needs support or when a travel agency needs guide capacity. The registered enterprise therefore sits where local knowledge, visitor support and the organisation of guiding labour meet.

The available registration scales are Mikro, Kecil and Menengah. That matters because the activity is framed around an operating service: a business can provide guidance itself, arrange the appropriate freelance guide, or do both in response to individual visitors and travel agencies. That scale range does not settle the ownership question, though: Perpres 49/2021's Lampiran II places this bidang usaha — under its former KBLI 2020 code, 79921 — in the *dialokasikan* column, reserving it for Koperasi and UMKM, so a PT PMA cannot take it. That allocation is set at the national level; it is not a regional carve-out limited to Bali.

This is a nationwide restriction, not a Bali peculiarity: a foreigner cannot register this activity through a PT PMA anywhere in Indonesia. The obstacle is a specific Perpres allocation, not a scale gap: Perpres 49/2021's Lampiran II lists this bidang usaha — under its former KBLI 2020 code, 79921 — in the *dialokasikan* column (p.16, entry 56), reserving it for Koperasi/UMKM, and a PT PMA is excluded from registering it on that basis. This conclusion follows from that explicit Perpres allocation, not from the nature of the service itself, and it applies wherever in Indonesia the business would be registered.

There is no separate national layer sitting underneath this outcome: because the Koperasi/UMKM allocation comes from a national Perpres annex rather than a regional policy, the same result holds whether a PT PMA tries to register in Bali, Jakarta, or anywhere else in Indonesia. Founders should not read the earlier scale information as evidence of an open national default with only a local Bali restriction layered on top — our records do not show a national PMA opening for this activity; the Koperasi/UMKM allocation is the basis recorded for its closure, full stop, wherever the business is registered.
editorial.pullQuote: The Perpres 49/2021 annex allocates tour-guide services (Jasa Pramuwisata) to Koperasi and UMKM, so the national ceiling is 0% — not a local Bali restriction on an otherwise-open activity.

editorial.headline: The Travel Services That Sit Beyond the Usual Categories
editorial.standfirst: A residual travel-services activity that is nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium, subject to address-level verification.
editorial.body:
KBLI 79909 is the home for other tourism travel services that are not otherwise captured by the specifically defined travel-service activities. Its importance lies in that residual role: it accommodates travel-related services that belong within the tourism journey but do not fit the more narrowly identified categories. The activity should therefore be read with care. The record establishes a broad travel-services perimeter, rather than a detailed catalogue of individual offerings.

The slim record does not name a particular profession, operator type, or business scale for this activity. Its `scales_open_to` field contains no listed classifications, so it does not support a claim that the code is reserved for, or available only to, a certain scale of enterprise. What it does establish is the foreign-investment position at national level: the activity is open to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership for a business properly carrying out this activity.

Bali requires a more exact reading, but the conclusion is not a blanket prohibition. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks low-risk and medium-low-risk KBLI activities island-wide. This activity is recorded instead as medium-high or high risk, and is therefore not blocked by that moratorium. The Bali status is recorded as `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`, with an important operational qualification: the position must be verified for the specific address. That is not a contradiction of the national openness; it is the local diligence that belongs to an activity whose risk treatment and site context matter.

For a founder, the clean interpretation is straightforward. Nationally, KBLI 79909 is open to PMA and can be held with up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is not among the activities caught by the island-wide low- and medium-low-risk PMA restriction, but its medium-high or high-risk treatment means the proposed address remains part of the assessment. The code offers a legitimate route for travel-related services outside the more specifically categorised travel activities; it does not remove the need to ensure that the actual operation and location match the registration position.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 79909 is open to PMA and can be held with up to 100% foreign ownership.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers private investigation services for corporate, insurance, and legal matters, as well as security guarding, patrol, cash-in-transit support, secure data destruction, armored car services, and security screening at airports, stations, or events. It also includes personnel for store, fair, and concert security.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it is classified as medium-high to high risk, meaning it is not blocked by the general moratorium but requires extra verification steps—such as demonstrating a legitimate local address and meeting site-specific security prerequisites—before your business license can be issued.

editorial.headline: Private Investigation and Security: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 80110 covers a wide security-services field, open to foreign ownership nationally and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 80110 is the operating category for private investigation and security work: investigations for private, commercial, insurance, and legal matters; guarding, patrol, and security services; and the practical infrastructure around secure cash collection and storage. Its scope also reaches secure data destruction, armoured vehicles, security-device implementation, and security consultation. In public-facing settings, it expressly includes security personnel for shops and trauma centres, screening baggage and passengers at airports, railway stations, and similar locations, and event security for concerts, fairs, and exhibitions.

That breadth matters because the activity is not confined to a single type of site or client. It is a category for organisations delivering protective, investigative, screening, or secure-handling services in settings where physical security and controlled operations are central to the work. The record makes the activity available at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A founder should therefore read the category through the actual service being delivered—not merely through the setting in which guards, investigators, screening staff, or secure-handling operations are deployed.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct: the activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. In other words, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; the relevant point for a foreign-owned structure is the stated 100% ceiling, rather than an implied local-equity requirement.

Bali is also not a hidden exception here. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, but this activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and is not blocked by that moratorium. The record’s reason is specific: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. For a foreign founder considering Bali, that means this activity is not barred by the provincial moratorium recorded here; the national 100% foreign-ownership position remains the clear starting point.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign founder considering Bali, this activity is not barred by the provincial moratorium recorded here.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

The risk classification and licensing rows shown here earlier were sourced from an internal reading that our review found lacked a verifiable page/row locator and left the record's own source markers internally inconsistent, and a further crosswalk check found the row was very likely keyed to a different, unverified 2020-era classification, so they have been removed from this page pending source resolution; the correct risk classification and licensing for this activity are not yet reliably defined in our verified sources. editorial.headline: When Security Means Monitoring, Not Just Installation
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the monitored security services behind alarms, video systems and emergency response—and is nationally open to full foreign ownership, with Bali address checks still essential.
editorial.body:
This security-services activity is about an operating monitoring function, not simply the equipment itself. It covers security-system services delivered through a security service centre or alarm receiving centre, as well as remote monitoring and video surveillance. The practical subject matter includes watching anti-theft alarms, video-surveillance systems and fire alarms from a distance, and receiving alerts through call-centre, emergency-service or alarm-receiving operations. Security consultancy is also within the stated scope.

The dividing line is material. Installation, repair and maintenance of electronic security systems may fall within this activity only where they are provided together with subsequent monitoring and remote monitoring. The same connected-service logic applies to mechanical or electronic locking devices, safes and vaults: installation, repair, modification and adaptation are included when they accompany the continuing monitored service. A stand-alone installation without that monitoring relationship is not the activity described here.

The registration picture is broad in business scale: the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with the foreign-ownership ceiling stated at 100%. That makes the national position unusually direct: the record does not state a reduced foreign-equity cap for this activity. For an operator whose real business is an active monitoring service, the national classification supports full foreign ownership within that stated ceiling.

Bali requires a separate reading, but the record does not present this activity as blocked for PMA registration there. It identifies the Bali position as medium-high/high risk and says the activity is not blocked by the moratorium, while requiring verification for the particular address. The permanent, island-wide moratorium described in the record applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity sits outside that stated prohibition; its Bali position is therefore open in principle under the record, subject to address-specific verification rather than an assumed island-wide clearance.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with the foreign-ownership ceiling stated at 100%.

editorial.headline: The Quiet Machinery of a Working Facility
editorial.standfirst: Although open nationally to 100% foreign ownership, this facility-support activity cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today.
editorial.body:
Facility support becomes a distinct business when it is supplied as a combined operational service within a client’s premises. The work can bring together general interior cleaning, maintenance, waste disposal, doorman duties, monitoring, mail delivery, reception, laundry and related services that support the facility’s operations. Rather than selling a single task in isolation, the activity concerns a coordinated package: people on site performing the practical work that helps the client’s facility function from one day to the next. It is an infrastructure of everyday operations, assembled around the place where the client works.

That operational role also establishes its boundary. The provider supplies staff to perform these supporting services, but does not become involved in, or assume responsibility for, the client’s main business or activity. It is not a mandate to manage and operate the client’s entire enterprise, and the record also makes clear that the offering is not simply one support service supplied alone. The service’s practical character is inseparable from that division of responsibility: combined support is delivered inside the client facility, in service of the client’s own operations.

Who may enter the activity is equally clear in the national record. It is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, placing the same combined-service proposition across the stated business scales. For PMA, its status is TERBUKA and the stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national position alone, then, the record permits foreign ownership up to the whole of that stated ceiling.

But national openness is not the final word in Bali. The record places the activity in Blocked (risk class): at the Besar scale, every listed scope is OSS-rated Rendah or Menengah-Rendah, triggering the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The provincial rule is unambiguous: all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI are blocked for PMA, island-wide and permanently. A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. The result is not a smaller local ownership allowance: nationally the ceiling remains 100%, while Bali’s PMA-registration outcome is blocked.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today.
