data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: General Building Cleaning: Nationally Open, Bali Closed to PMA
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans routine cleaning across buildings and premises—open nationally to foreign investment, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
General building cleaning is the everyday upkeep of buildings and their connected spaces. It covers routine cleaning for offices, houses and apartments, factories, shops and shopping premises, institutions, other business and professional locations, and multi-unit residential buildings. The centre of gravity is interior work: the cleaning that keeps rooms, shared spaces and occupied premises usable. Related exterior tasks may also fall within the activity where they remain part of the building-cleaning assignment, such as cleaning windows or building corridors.

The boundary is practical rather than decorative. This is a general-cleaning activity across whole premises and the ordinary spaces that support them; specialised cleaning work is outside that definition. That distinction preserves the character of the activity as an ongoing operational service for buildings, rather than a label for every cleaning task that might occur at a property.

Registration is available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. In other words, the national position does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The relevant national reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder considering the activity at national level, the picture is therefore straightforward: it is open to foreign-investment registration across the listed business scales.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreigner cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, which brings the activity within Bali’s moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The block is island-wide and permanent under the stated Bali rule. A national 100% ceiling does not overcome Bali’s island-wide, permanent block on PMA registration for this activity. The honest reading is not that Bali applies a lower foreign-ownership percentage; it is that PMA registration for this activity is blocked there despite the nationally open position.
editorial.pullQuote: A national 100% ceiling does not overcome Bali’s island-wide, permanent block on PMA registration for this activity.

editorial.headline: Cleaning as an Operating Discipline
editorial.standfirst: A broad cleaning activity, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally, with no Bali PMA moratorium block at the Large scale.
editorial.body:
This activity is the working backbone behind clean, maintained and usable premises. Its scope runs well beyond routine interiors: it includes exterior cleaning for buildings ranging from offices and factories to shops, institutions, professional premises and multi-unit residences. It also reaches specialist work on windows, chimneys, fireplaces, stoves, incinerators, boilers, ventilation ducts and gas or vapour exhausts. The common thread is practical upkeep of the built environment, whether the task is visible from the street or buried inside a building’s systems.

The range is deliberately broad. Pool cleaning and maintenance sit alongside industrial-machine cleaning, bottle washing, and cleaning for trains, buses and aircraft. It also includes the interiors of ships and tanker trucks, street cleaning, snow and ice removal, post-construction building cleaning, and exterior work performed with steam, sand blasting or similar methods. Residential vector, disease-carrying animal and pest control is within scope too, including delivery in buildings, settlements, industrial sites and other business premises, as well as at airports, ports and land-border crossings.

Enterprises at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales may undertake this activity. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is a clear national position: foreign investment is not limited to a minority holding for this activity. The source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali does not add a moratorium block to this activity’s PMA registration. The province’s standing rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale as Medium-High/High, so the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The practical reading is precise rather than promotional: the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the national benchmark, while Bali’s recorded position is that this activity is not stopped by the provincial moratorium at the Large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: Cleaning is treated here as a broad operating discipline, not a narrow housekeeping service.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Landscaping Services: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans garden care, ecological restoration and landscape protection—open nationally to full foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Landscaping services here means far more than keeping a garden attractive. The activity covers planting, care and maintenance for private and public residential gardens; public and semi-public buildings such as schools, hospitals, government institutions and places of worship; urban parks, green areas and cemeteries; transport corridors; and industrial and commercial sites. It also reaches roof gardens, green frontage, indoor plants, sports grounds, playgrounds, recreation areas, and still or flowing water features including pools, ditches, streams and drainage systems.

The scope is equally concerned with the protective and restorative work of landscape. It includes planting vegetation to reduce noise, wind, erosion, unwanted visibility, heat or sun glare; protecting and restoring gardens and landscapes; and ecological engineering for conservation purposes. Amenity-tree care and arboriculture sit within the same activity, alongside natural-environment restoration, plant engineering and ecosystem renaturalisation. Environmental erosion control in mountain areas, spawning grounds and riverbanks is included, as are habitat creation or relocation measures such as nesting boxes, shelters and hibernacula, plus prevention, control and response to invasive fauna or flora.

Registration is open across the full scale range stated in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. At the national level, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA and permits foreign ownership up to a ceiling of 100%. That is a clear national position: foreign equity may reach 100% for this activity. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali is the decisive exception for a PMA applicant. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali through PMA today. The Bali record marks it Blocked (risk class) because, at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope; the activity is therefore caught by Bali’s moratorium of May 13, 2026. The provincial rule is stated as island-wide and permanent, blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not override that Bali registration block.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not override Bali’s PMA registration block.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers providing a mix of day-to-day office administrative services for other businesses on a fee or contract basis — think reception, secretarial support, document preparation, typing, proofreading, transcription, mail handling, and basic financial or personnel record-keeping.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this business line is fully open to 100% foreign ownership (PMA). However, in Bali, the provincial moratorium on low and medium-low risk activities currently blocks new PMA registrations under this code, so a foreign-owned company cannot be established for this activity on the island at this moment.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Suitable for foreign entrepreneurs looking to run a shared services hub, virtual office, or corporate secretarial agency that handles back-office tasks for local and international clients.

editorial.headline: The Office Behind the Office
editorial.standfirst: This contract-based administrative service is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but a Bali-wide PMA moratorium makes registration unavailable on the island today.
editorial.body:
At its core, KBLI 82100 is the outsourced office function: the everyday administrative work a business asks another party to perform for a fee or under contract. That can mean reception, financial planning, billing and recordkeeping, personnel administration, and mail services. It is not merely a back-office label. The scope reaches from document preparation—editing, final checking, typing, word processing and pre-filing—to transcription, letter or résumé writing, duplication, blueprint production, and self-service photocopy operations.

Its practical centre is useful order: supporting secretarial work, rented post-office boxes, postal and mailing services such as pre-sorting and addressing, file digitisation without subsequent data processing, and e-book formatting. The activity is designed for service providers acting for other parties, rather than for a company simply handling its own internal administration. The permitted scale is broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar are all open. That makes it a classification suited to an administrative-service business from its smallest operating form through to a large enterprise.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. For a foreign investor considering Indonesian registration outside Bali, the record therefore permits a fully foreign-owned structure, subject to the classification as stated. The national position should not be diluted by assumptions drawn from the nature of office work: the record’s stated ceiling is complete foreign ownership, and its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Yet Bali calls for the opposite conclusion today. In Bali today, a foreign investor is unable to register this activity. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, and the Bali moratorium blocks it on that basis. The provincial rule is island-wide and permanent: it blocks PMA registration for activities classified Low or Medium-Low risk. This is not a reduction of the national 100% ceiling; it is a Bali registration block, effective under the moratorium from May 2026. For founders, the distinction is decisive: national openness does not create a Bali PMA registration route for this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a Bali PMA registration route for this activity.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers running both inbound and outbound call centers — answering customer calls for orders, support, or complaints, and making outbound calls for sales, marketing, or surveys. It includes using human agents or AI, automated call routing, and voice response systems.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this activity is fully open for 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, it's not blocked by the moratorium, but it carries a medium-high or high risk classification. That means you can register a PMA, but the local investment office will closely verify the proposed business address before approval.

intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Pusat Panggilan (Call Center) (82200)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs looking to set up a third-party customer support hub, telemarketing agency, or market research calling operation, often serving offshore clients from Bali.

editorial.headline: The Operating Room of Customer Contact
editorial.standfirst: This activity code covers the systems and teams that receive, direct and resolve customer contact—open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A call-centre activity is the operational centre of a company’s customer contact: the place where calls, digital enquiries and follow-up are received, routed and answered. It covers inbound operations that take orders, provide product information, respond to customer-assistance requests and handle complaints. Those functions may be delivered through human operators, artificial intelligence, automatic call distribution, computer-telephone integration, interactive voice-response systems or comparable methods. Web contact centres, and centres handling assistance requests or complaints through other communication channels, also sit within the activity’s stated scope.

The outward-facing side is equally material. Outbound call-centre operations may use similar methods to sell or market goods and services to prospective customers, or to conduct telephone interviews for market-research and opinion-survey purposes on a fee or contract basis. In practice, the code describes the contact operation itself: a business structured to manage incoming demand, customer support and complaint handling, while also enabling organised outbound contact. It is not limited to a single technology or a purely voice-based service.

Across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, registration remains open. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. That is a full foreign-ownership ceiling, not a partial opening. The relevant national source recorded for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the important reading is straightforward: the activity is nationally open to PMA registration, across the listed business scales.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. Across the province, a permanent block applies to PMA registration for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activity. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Its Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. That does not add a Bali-specific foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition; none is recorded. The honest position is simply that a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today, subject to the recorded risk position rather than a moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this customer-contact activity in Bali today because it is not caught by the province’s PMA moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: The Event Business That Is Nationally Open but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 82300 spans the organisation and operation of business events nationwide, yet foreign investors cannot register it in Bali under the province’s permanent PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 82300 covers the organisation, promotion and management of business events: trade and business exhibitions, corporate events, general or specialist shows, conferences, conventions, seminars, symposia, workshops, agricultural markets, craft fairs and rural festivals. It can form part of the wider meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions ecosystem. The activity may also include managing an event venue and supplying its operating staff, but only where that work is tied to organising, promoting or managing the event itself.

Its practical reach extends beyond invitations and floor plans. The code includes the technical planning, provision, installation and operation of audiovisual equipment and special effects for conferences, conventions and trade exhibitions. The boundary matters: exhibition-stand construction, cultural events, sporting events and private celebrations sit outside this activity’s stated scope. In other words, this is a code for the machinery of business gatherings—the production, management and technical delivery that turns a commercial event into a functioning occasion.

Across Indonesia, foreign investment is permitted in this activity up to a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. It is available across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, making it a broad registration category for operators whose work ranges from smaller commercial gatherings to substantial exhibition and convention activity. The national position is therefore straightforward: foreign participation is permitted at the full stated ceiling.

Bali tells a different story. In Bali today, a foreign investor is unable to register this activity. At the Besar scale, every stated scope falls within Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, placing the activity inside Bali’s island-wide, permanent prohibition on PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The recorded moratorium took effect in May 2026. That does not alter the national foreign-ownership ceiling; it determines whether a PMA registration for this activity can be made in Bali. For founders, the distinction is decisive: national openness does not create a Bali registration route where the provincial moratorium blocks it.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a Bali registration route where the provincial moratorium blocks it.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: The Business of Making the Right Connection
editorial.standfirst: This activity formalises the service of bringing clients and providers together—and remains open to foreign investment nationally and for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, this activity is a business-support intermediation service for work not otherwise specified. Its operating unit makes the introduction: it brings a client together with a service provider under a fee or contract. That deceptively simple function is the centre of gravity. The business is not defined by creating the underlying service; it is defined by arranging the connection through which that service can be taken up. The description deliberately places it in the supporting layer of business, built around the match between demand and provision.

The method is deliberately broad. It can operate through a digital platform or through nondigital channels, including face-to-face contact, door-to-door work, telephone and correspondence. Payment may come from the client or the service provider, in the form of a fee or commission. Intermediation income may also include other sources, such as advertising income. The scope expressly includes reservations and ticket sales for theatre, sports and other entertainment events. A digital interface is therefore one possible route, not the condition that defines the activity.

It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The breadth is significant because the record does not reserve the activity for one size of enterprise. At every listed scale, the commercial identity remains the same: connecting clients and service providers under the agreed commercial basis of a fee or contract. For founders, the practical reading is one of scope: the record places every listed scale within the available range without changing the essential intermediary role.

Nationally, this activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For a foreign founder, the decisive Bali point is clear: it is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. Bali’s status is OK or higher risk; at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That places it outside a moratorium that blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali. The distinction matters: the national ceiling records national openness, while the Bali position answers whether that opening is stopped by the local moratorium. On this record, it is not.
editorial.pullQuote: The business is defined by arranging the connection through which a service can be taken up.

editorial.headline: Collection Agency Activity: A Clear Path for Foreign Investors in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers collecting claim payments and remitting them to clients, with full foreign ownership permitted nationally and PT PMA registration available in Bali.
editorial.body:
Collection-agency activity is modestly titled but operationally exact: it covers collecting payment on claims and passing the collected payments on to clients. That includes bill- or debt-collection services. The recorded scope describes a payment-recovery and remittance function, rather than simply an administrative back office. Its commercial centre is the handling of money due and the delivery of recovered sums to the client that engaged the service.

Registration is open across the recorded Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That range gives the activity a broad formal landing place, but it should not be read as a description of how any particular firm must organise itself: the record establishes only the scales available for this activity. Nationally, its status is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. This is the clear national position: the record sets no foreign-ownership ceiling below full ownership.

In Bali, the conclusion remains positive, with a specific reason. The activity is recorded as open in Bali with high risk, and a PT PMA can register it there. Its Besar scale is classed as Tinggi; that classification lets it survive the provincial moratorium. The moratorium is permanent and island-wide, but the record states that it blocks only low- and medium-low-risk KBLI for PMA. This activity’s Bali position is therefore not an assumption that the restriction is ignored; it is an express consequence of the recorded high-risk Besar-scale treatment.

For founders, the useful reading is direct. The business may be structured around collecting claim payments and transmitting those collected payments to its clients, including bill and debt collection work. It is available at the three recorded scales, open nationally to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling, and registrable in Bali through a PT PMA under its recorded Bali treatment. The relevant provincial framework is the permanent, island-wide moratorium cited in the record; its consequence here follows from the recorded high-risk Besar-scale classification.
editorial.pullQuote: The activity is recorded as open in Bali with high risk, and a PT PMA can register it there.

editorial.headline: KBLI 82912: The Business of Making Credit Information Usable
editorial.standfirst: A credit-information bureau can operate at every business scale, with full foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Credit-information bureau activity is the work of assembling, processing and providing information that others use to assess creditworthiness. Its practical subject matter is credit and employment history relating to individuals, as well as information needed to evaluate an individual or a business. The intended users are financial institutions, retailers and other parties that require a credit assessment. The scope also expressly includes credit-information management institutions and alternative credit-rating activity.

This is therefore an information activity with a consequential commercial purpose: making credit data and other relevant data legible for a credit decision. The record describes institutions or bodies that collect and process credit data and other data in order to produce credit information. The editorial distinction matters. The registered activity is not simply the holding of records; it is the creation and provision of usable credit information for organisations assessing creditworthiness.

The activity is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large businesses. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach 100% under the national position recorded for this activity. That national openness is supported in the record by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The scale range is broad, but the activity’s scope remains specific: gathering and processing relevant data to generate credit information, including alternative credit ratings.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island on a permanent basis, but this activity is recorded as not blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK because, at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High; accordingly, it is not caught by that moratorium. For a founder, the honest position is straightforward: PMA registration is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali record does not show this activity as blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: PMA registration is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and the Bali record does not show this activity as blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers contract-based packaging services for raw or processed materials from agriculture, plantations, forestry, and fisheries. Activities include bottling liquids, solid-product packaging, labeling, stamping, and sterilization—either manually or with automated systems.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is 100% open to foreign ownership. In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines, and some scopes of this KBLI fall in that band — but at least one large-scale (Besar) scope carries a higher risk class, so the code remains registrable as a PMA in Bali on that scope.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.

intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: Foreign entrepreneurs wanting to offer professional packing and labeling services for Bali’s farm, plantation, or seafood products—but as of now, they cannot register a PMA for this activity locally and would need to consider other regions.

editorial.headline: Agricultural Product Packing: Open Nationally, Conditional in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers contract packing for agricultural, plantation, forestry and fisheries materials and products, with a nationally open PMA position but a scope-sensitive route in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the business of packing agricultural, plantation, forestry and fisheries materials and products for a fee or under contract. It may be carried out through automated or manual processes. The work is practical but wide-ranging: bottling liquids, packing solid goods, labelling, marking, sterilising products in connection with packing, and other related packing activities all sit within its stated scope. The common thread is not ownership of the goods, but the provision of packing as a contracted activity for these product categories.

The code is open across every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. At the national level, it is also open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That makes the national position unusually direct: a foreign investor can participate fully in an entity carrying out this activity, provided the business is registered for the activity actually undertaken. The scope nonetheless matters. Packing is described here as a service performed for agricultural, plantation, forestry and fisheries materials and products, so the registration should reflect that operational reality rather than a broader commercial ambition.

Bali requires a more exact reading. This code is not marked as blocked for PMA registration in Bali, but its status depends on the declared scope. Bali permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities across the province. For this activity, OSS risk at the Large scale is low for some scopes and higher for others. A PMA registration in Bali is therefore possible only where the higher-risk scope is declared, and the precise activity must be verified in live OSS. This is not a general national restriction; it is the practical consequence of Bali's province-wide moratorium interacting with the risk classification attached to the exact scope selected.

For founders, the point is simple but important. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not by themselves settle the Bali outcome. The relevant question is whether the proposed Large-scale packing operation is recorded in OSS under a higher-risk scope. If it is, the record indicates a PMA route in Bali; if it falls within the low or medium-low risk categories covered by the moratorium, Bali's permanent block applies. The registration decision therefore turns on the exact declared scope, not on an assumed entitlement drawn from the national PMA position alone.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not by itself settle the Bali outcome: the exact declared scope determines whether a PMA route exists.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Aktivitas Pengepakan Bahan dan Produk Makanan dan Minuman Olahan
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pengemasan atas dasar balas jasa atau kontrak, baik menggunakan suatu proses otomatis ataupun manual, untuk bahan dan produk makanan dan minuman olahan. Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembotolan cairan yang mencakup minuman dan makanan, pengemasan benda padat (blister packaging, pembungkusan dengan foil aluminium, dll.), pelabelan, pemberian cap, sterilisasi produk yang terkait dengan pengepakan, dan kegiatan terkait pengepakan lainnya untuk bahan dan produk makanan dan minuman olahan.

editorial.headline: Food and Drink Packing: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contract packing for processed food and drink materials and products, with full foreign ownership available nationally and no Bali moratorium block at large scale.
editorial.body:
This is the business of packing processed food and drink materials and products for a fee or under contract. The work may be carried out through automated systems or by hand, but its commercial centre is the same: preparing another party’s food or beverage goods for their next stage of distribution or sale. It includes bottling liquids, including beverages and foods; packing solid items through formats such as blister packs or aluminium-foil wrapping; labelling and stamping; and product sterilisation where it relates to packing. Other related packing work for processed food and drink materials and products also falls within the activity.

The scope is broad enough to accommodate a practical production-service operation rather than one narrow packaging technique. A business can handle liquid bottling alongside solid-goods packing, labelling, stamps, and packing-related sterilisation, provided the work remains directed to processed food and beverage materials or products. The record describes this as paid or contract work, which is an important distinction: the activity is defined by carrying out the packaging service itself, whether the process is automated or manual.

Registration is open at every listed enterprise scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. At the national level, PMA is classified TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Put simply, the national record allows this activity to be entirely foreign-owned. That national openness is supported by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and it applies alongside the available scale range rather than being confined in the record to a single class of enterprise.

Bali requires a more careful reading, but the result here is not a prohibition. The province has an island-wide, permanent moratorium blocking low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA. For this activity, however, the OSS risk at the Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali record therefore marks it OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. A PMA registration in Bali is consequently not barred on that moratorium basis where the activity is assessed at the stated large-scale, higher-risk level.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, full foreign ownership is open; in Bali, the activity is not blocked by the PMA moratorium at the stated large-scale, higher-risk level.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Textile Packing, With a Clear National and Bali Position
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contract packing for textiles and textile products, from secure wrapping and labelling to sterilisation, and is open nationally to foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
Textile packing is often treated as a minor back-office function, yet this activity has a distinct commercial identity: providing packaging services for textile and textile products on a fee-for-service or contract basis. The work may be automated or manual. Its scope includes packing, secure wrapping, labelling, marking, product sterilisation and other related packing activity. In other words, the business is not defined by making the textiles, but by handling the process that prepares textile goods for onward movement or presentation.

The activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record recognises the same underlying activity across the full progression of enterprise sizes, rather than reserving it for a particular type of operator. A business registering this activity is therefore positioned around the service of packaging itself: the practical work of enclosing, securing, identifying, marking or sterilising textile products under an arrangement of remuneration or contract.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. At the national level, its PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no stated national ownership cap below full foreign ownership in this record. For founders considering a foreign-owned registration, that is the central national fact: the activity is open to PMA at the stated ceiling.

Bali adds a scale-sensitive reading, but not a prohibition. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record states that at the Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. It is therefore not blocked by the Bali moratorium. The applicable moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province; this activity is expressly recorded as outside that block because of its risk position at the Besar scale. For this textile-packing activity, the honest picture is consequently one of national foreign openness and a Bali position that remains available rather than barred, while recognising the higher-risk classification recorded at the large-business scale.
editorial.pullQuote: For this textile-packing activity, the honest picture is one of national foreign openness and a Bali position that remains available rather than barred.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This covers contract-based packaging (manual or automated) of chemical substances and products — including bottling liquids, blister wrapping, foil sealing, safe containment, labeling, stamping, and sterilization — all done for a fee.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: In Bali, the island-wide moratorium (in force since 13 May 2026) only halts PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk lines — this KBLI's large-scale (Besar) risk class is higher, so it is not caught: PMA registration in Bali remains possible.
intel_2026.whatChanged: KBLI 2020→2025 mapping: code renumbered.
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Looking into Aktivitas Pengepakan Bahan dan Produk Kimia (82924)? Nationally this carries PMA status: Open. Let me walk you through what it means for a foreign-owned setup.
intel_2026.whoThisIsFor: A foreign entrepreneur providing outsourced chemical packaging and safety-compliant finishing services — and Bali is not off the table: this KBLI's large-scale risk class sits above the moratorium's Low/Medium-Low band, so a PMA can still register it here.

editorial.headline: Chemical Packaging: Open Nationally, Unblocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 82924 covers paid or contracted chemical-material and product packaging—open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 82924 is the business of packaging chemical materials and products for a fee or under contract. It is not confined to one package format or one way of working. The scope expressly includes automatic and manual processes, from bottling liquids to packing solid articles using blister packaging or aluminium-foil wrapping. It also includes secure packaging for chemical materials and products, labelling, stamping, sterilising products and other work connected with their packaging. The practical centre of gravity is the packaging service itself: the defined work of preparing chemical materials and products in the stated forms.

That breadth matters because the activity can encompass bottling, enclosure of solid items and finishing steps that identify a package through labels or stamps, or subject products to sterilisation. It can be undertaken with equipment-driven processes or manually, as the scope itself allows. The record opens registration at every listed scale—Micro, Small, Medium and Large. In other words, the scale field does not reserve this activity for a narrow band of enterprises; each of the four listed scales is open.

The national PMA position is equally direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and its maximum foreign ownership is 100. That means the national ceiling permits full foreign ownership; it is not an opening that stops short of complete foreign participation. The record names Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the PMA source. For a founder considering this defined packaging activity at the national level, the fact to retain is simple but significant: the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, alongside access across the record’s full range of scales.

Bali needs to be read on its own terms rather than assumed from the national result. The provincial moratorium in the record permanently blocks PMA registration, island-wide, for Low and Medium-Low risk classifications. Yet this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali reason records that, at the Large scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High and that it is not blocked by the moratorium. The record’s status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The honest Bali conclusion is therefore open, not closed: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. Large-scale work carries the stated Medium-High/High OSS-risk position, but it remains outside the moratorium’s blocked Low and Medium-Low categories.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Aktivitas Pengepakan Bahan dan Produk Farmasi
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pengemasan atas dasar balas jasa atau kontrak, baik menggunakansuatu proses otomatis ataupun manual, untuk bahan dan produk farmasi atau obat-obatan. Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pembotolan cairan bahan dan produk farmasi, pengemasan bahan dan produk farmasi berbentuk padat (blister packaging, pembungkusan dengan foil aluminium, dll.), pengemasan yang aman untuk obat-obatan dan bahan obat-obatan, pelabelan, pemberian cap, sterilisasi produk, dan kegiatan terkait pengepakan lainnya untuk bahan dan produk farmasi.

editorial.headline: Pharmaceutical Packing, Read Through Bali’s Risk Lens
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contract or fee-based packing for pharmaceutical materials and medicines, with national foreign ownership open to 100%.
editorial.body:
Pharmaceutical packing is a specialised service activity: packing pharmaceutical materials and finished medicines for a fee or under contract, whether the work is automated or manual. Its scope extends from bottling pharmaceutical liquids to packing solid materials and products in blister packs or aluminium foil, alongside secure medicine packaging, labelling, stamping, sterilisation and related packing work. The focus is the packing operation itself—an activity defined by the careful preparation, protection and presentation of pharmaceutical materials and products.

Every listed business scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—remains open to the activity. That breadth matters because the work can be organised at very different operating sizes while remaining within the same stated scope: handling liquid pharmaceutical products, solid formats, secure packaging and the associated finishing steps. Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%, under the cited Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 framework. There is no partial foreign-ownership ceiling to read between the lines here: the recorded national ceiling is 100%.

Bali calls for a more precise reading, without warranting pessimism. This activity is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. For this activity at the Besar scale, however, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The record therefore places its Bali status at OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms, the national openness remains meaningful in Bali for the stated activity: the province’s blanket restriction does not catch it at the large-scale risk classification recorded here.

That distinction is the centre of the picture. A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling does not make Bali’s regulatory context irrelevant; Bali’s PMA rule is expressly risk-based. Yet the same record supplies the answer for this activity: its Besar-scale OSS risk level sits above the Low and Medium-Low categories covered by the moratorium. For founders considering pharmaceutical packing, the relevant frame is therefore a fully open national PMA position combined with a Bali outcome that is not blocked by the provincial moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For pharmaceutical packing, the national 100% PMA position remains meaningful in Bali because the recorded large-scale risk level is not caught by the moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Contract Packaging, Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A broad contracted packaging activity, open across all stated enterprise scales and available for full foreign ownership nationally and PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Other Packaging Activities is a contracted packaging service with a deliberately broad practical reach. It covers bottling liquids, packing solid objects, labelling, marking and sterilising products when those tasks are carried out for a fee or under contract. It also includes the packing of parcels or gifts and the wrapping of gifts. The work may be delivered through an automated process or manually. In other words, the defined activity is the packaging work performed as a service: preparing an item, identifying it where needed, and completing the packaging treatment specified in the record. It is not confined to a single packaging technology or type of item.

Who can register is equally clear. Businesses classified as Mikro, Kecil, Menengah or Besar may undertake the activity. This is a full stated scale range, rather than a scope limited to a single business class or a single production method. A small operator using manual handling and a larger organisation using automation are both contemplated by the activity’s language, provided the work remains within the listed packaging, labelling, marking, sterilisation, parcel-packing or gift-wrapping services. The scale labels set the available registration range; the scope sets the kind of work.

Across Indonesia, this activity carries TERBUKA PMA status and permits foreign ownership up to 100%. That permits full foreign ownership at the national level for this activity. The point is straightforward but important: the national PMA position follows the stated status and ceiling, while the operational description explains the services that form the activity. The source recorded for that PMA position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the scope narrows the service to only automated work, only manual work, only liquids or only gifts; each format is expressly within its described reach.

Bali does not reverse the national position. The provincial record says that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; it therefore records the activity as not blocked by Bali’s moratorium. That moratorium is island-wide and permanent for PMA activities with low or medium-low risk. This activity is recorded outside that block, so a foreign investor can register it in Bali today. The distinction remains important: 100% is the national foreign-ownership ceiling, while Bali’s recorded conclusion concerns registration under its risk-based moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not reverse the national position.

editorial.headline: KBLI 82990: Indonesia’s Broad Business-Support Services Category
editorial.standfirst: A wide-ranging business-support activity, open nationally to full foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 82990 is a deliberately broad home for business-support services that do not fit one narrow professional specialty. Its scope includes reward- or contract-based fundraising and donation-based fundraising; court reporting, public stenography and live captioning for meetings or conferences; barcode coding and barcode printing; repossession services; and parking-meter coin collection. It also covers restaurant-voucher handling, assistance with motor-vehicle registration, relocation services, administration of gift packages for recreation, voucher issuance and handling, corporate-domicile services, and the reading and cost allocation of heating and hot-water consumption.

The category continues across several distinct support functions: trading and brokering crypto assets without associated liabilities, where this is not undertaken by a monetary authority; independent auctioneering; loyalty-programme administration; warehouse-receipt-system registration-centre services; and travel-box sales. These travel boxes are a form of distribution for deferred travel-related services, which may include hotels, restaurants, treatments or recreation. The breadth is the point: this is a classification for specified auxiliary services, from live information capture to administration, collection, relocation and deferred-service distribution.

Registration is open at every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical ownership terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; the essential reading is straightforward: foreign capital is not confined to a minority stake for this activity.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, but this record states that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. As a result, KBLI 82990 is not blocked by that moratorium and carries the Bali status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; the relevant Bali consideration is its higher-risk position at Besar scale, not a separate Bali foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today.

Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. editorial.headline: Legislative Institutions: Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This legislative-institution activity covers constitutional decision-making and its secretariat support; it is closed to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 84111 covers legislative institutions:** the institutional activities of the MPR, DPR and DPRD, together with their secretariats. It is a public constitutional function centred on taking basic and principled constitutional decisions in the formulation of government policy. The description gives this function real operational breadth. It covers making, amending or repealing laws and government regulations, then extends to the fostering of government administration for the implementation of policy, legislation, regulations and other applicable provisions. The same scope links formal constitutional choices with the administration that enables their execution.

Its remit also includes decisions, determinations and approvals concerning revenue and expenditure budgets, investment budgets and long-term plans. The record names the MPR, DPR and DPRD and their secretariats as the institutional participants within scope. It does not identify a separate roster of applicant types, nor does it list any business scale as open to this activity. That silence is material: the slim record gives no scale-based opening to describe, and no threshold or eligibility route can responsibly be added. Its stated scope instead remains the legislative and secretariat activity, including the budgetary and planning decisions expressly named.

At national level, the investment position is explicit. The PMA status is **TERTUTUP** under Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%. For a foreign investor, the Bali result is just as direct: the activity cannot be registered as a PMA in Bali today. Bali likewise records it as **TERTUTUP** and marks it blocked. Its stated reason identifies medium-high/high risk and says the block does not arise from the island-wide, permanent Bali rule that applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The record also says to verify by address. Bali is closed for PMA registration, while the record attributes that outcome to something other than its province-wide PMA moratorium rule.

editorial.headline: The Public Machinery of Government
editorial.standfirst: An activity for planning, leading and supervising government administration, closed to PMA nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 84112** covers the machinery through which the Indonesian state carries out the governmental process needed to achieve objectives set by the legislature. Its substance is the planning, leadership and supervision of government administration: the work that turns those state objectives into an organised public function. The scope begins with activity carried out by the President and Vice President, alongside the State Secretariat Ministry, Cabinet Secretariat and Ministry of Home Affairs.

It then traces the territorial chain of administration, naming governors, regents, mayors, subdistrict heads, and urban-village or village heads. These are not incidental examples; they indicate the officeholders placed within the stated activity, all with the task of planning, leading and supervising the conduct of government. The record offers no business scale as open to it. That absence is important when reading the code: the scope is framed around governmental responsibility and the offices that perform it.

Nationally, the investment position is unequivocal. The PMA status is TERTUTUP—closed—and the maximum foreign ownership is 0%. A foreign investor therefore cannot register this activity in Indonesia. The ceiling is not a partial opening or a scale-specific concession: the record states zero national foreign ownership and no scale open to the activity. That is the central registration fact, and it should be read alongside the governmental roles defined in the scope.

Bali arrives at the same practical conclusion: a foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. Its Bali status is TERTUTUP, and it is flagged as blocked for PMA registration. The stated reason, however, draws a useful distinction. This activity is recorded as Medium-High/High risk and as not blocked by the provincial moratorium; that moratorium applies island-wide and permanently to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The closing instruction is precise: verify the position by address. Bali's closure is clear in the record, but the moratorium is not the stated mechanism for this activity.

editorial.headline: KBLI 84113: Indonesia’s Public Finance, Tax and Customs Institutions
editorial.standfirst: This is a government institutional activity, closed to foreign ownership nationally and blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 84113 covers the institutional work of government bodies in finance, taxation and customs, undertaken to support the smooth conduct of government. Its scope includes the secretariat functions that sustain those institutions, alongside government bodies in finance, the Directorate General of Taxes and the Directorate General of Customs and Excise. The activity is therefore defined by public institutional administration, not by a private operator offering financial, tax or customs services to the market.

The relevant registrants are government institutions working in these fields and their secretariat functions. No business scale is listed as open to this activity. That position is consistent with the national PMA status: it is closed, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 0%. There is no partial foreign-equity route expressed in the record; foreign ownership is not available for this activity at the national level.

In Bali, the practical answer for a foreign investor is equally direct: this activity cannot be registered for PMA today. Bali records it as closed and specifically blocked for PMA registration. There is, however, an important distinction in the provincial note. The block is not attributed to Bali’s island-wide moratorium, which applies to low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities. Instead, the record places this activity in a medium-high/high-risk frame and says it should be verified by address. That is a location-specific verification note, not evidence that the moratorium itself is the reason for the Bali position.

The result is a clear boundary around the activity. KBLI 84113 concerns the institutional machinery of public finance, taxation and customs, including the administrative support around it. It is nationally closed to PMA, no open business scales are recorded, and Bali also marks it closed and blocked. For founders, the value of that clarity is in recognising the category for what it is: a defined government institutional function rather than an available foreign-investment activity.

editorial.headline: Mandatory Social Security: Closed to PMA, Including in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This government-organised system of compulsory social protection is closed to PMA nationwide, and Bali records the same outcome even though its moratorium is not the stated reason.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor considering Bali, the answer begins with a hard boundary: this activity cannot be registered as PMA there today. That conclusion is not a Bali-only surprise. Nationally, Mandatory Social Security Activities is marked TERTUTUP, with a foreign-ownership maximum of 0%. In Bali, the status is likewise TERTUTUP. The provincial note classifies it as medium-high/high risk and says it is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium, while directing that the position be verified for the particular address.

At its centre is the government’s financing and administration of compulsory social security. The scope encompasses social protection connected to health, accidents and unemployment, as well as pensions. It also reaches programmes dealing with income loss caused by maternity, temporary disability, widowhood and related circumstances. Read as a whole, the definition is about the public machinery behind mandated protection: funding and administering schemes intended to respond when health, work or family circumstances affect a person’s income. The key modifiers—compulsory, government-organised, financed and administered—are all essential to its institutional focus.

The registration fields reinforce that institutional character. Government is identified as the organiser, and the record provides no business scale open to this activity. There is consequently no stated business-scale route for treating it as an open business category, and no additional scale qualification appears elsewhere in the record. That is important for a founder reading only the activity title: the applicable scope is the funding and administration of compulsory schemes, and the record’s national PMA setting leaves no foreign ownership space within it. The absence of an open scale is a substantive part of the picture, not a detail to fill by assumption.

Bali’s detailed treatment must be read with equal precision. The province-wide permanent moratorium named in the record applies at the Low and Medium-Low risk levels. This activity, however, is recorded as medium-high/high risk and expressly described as not blocked by that moratorium. That does not turn it into an open Bali option. The Bali status remains TERTUTUP, and the record calls for verification by address. The clean conclusion is therefore narrow but decisive: the moratorium is not the reason given for the Bali outcome, yet a foreign-owned registration for this activity in Bali is closed today. Nationally, its 0% foreign-ownership maximum reaches the same result.
