editorial.headline: Government-Run Training, Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: Government-run, non-school training can span administrative, technical, health and adult learning—but this activity is closed to foreign investment nationally and cannot be registered by PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85550 is the lane for government-organised education outside the school system: courses and training intended to add or support skills and competence. Its scope is deliberately broad, taking in administrative-staff courses, training for senior administrative staff, competence development for teachers and education personnel, technical training centres, beauty courses—from body care to bridal make-up—and household-welfare instruction in sewing, cooking and nutrition. It also reaches health-related teaching, including first aid, massage and acupuncture, education on nuclear-related subjects, other courses, and adult business-learning groups.

That breadth should not be mistaken for a blank cheque. The activity is defined by its public organiser—government—and the slim record identifies no business scale as open. It contains no separate opening that would justify assigning a particular scale or wider type of registrant. The important point is simple: this is a government-run, out-of-school education category whose content can be practical, vocational and adult-facing, yet whose investment treatment is set by the same record, not by the apparent familiarity of any individual course.

Nationally, the answer is unequivocal. Its PMA status is TERTUTUP, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%. A foreign investor therefore has no permitted ownership stake under the national entry shown here. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is not a partial opening, nor does the wide range of subject matter create a different foreign-investment outcome: the record’s national status is closed.

Bali calls for a careful distinction, not an optimistic loophole. The Bali status is also TERTUTUP, and the record expressly marks the activity as blocked for PMA registration. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. Its listed risk position is medium-high/high, so it is not blocked by the island-wide Bali moratorium that applies to all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI for PMA; the record still requires address-specific verification. That does not reverse the Bali result. The moratorium is not the cited reason for the block, while the Bali status and block flag remain decisive. A wide curriculum does not change the clean conclusion: the activity is closed nationally and closed in Bali.

editorial.headline: Government Training, Closed to Foreign Ownership
editorial.standfirst: This government-managed job-training activity is closed to foreign ownership nationally, and a foreign investor cannot register it in Bali today.
editorial.body:
**For foreign investors, the answer is immediate: this activity cannot be registered in Bali today, and foreign ownership is unavailable nationally.** KBLI 85560 concerns government-managed job training, intended to raise competence through programmes organised around the needs of industry or users. Its stated examples span information and communication technology, creative industries, tourism and hospitality, business and management, domestic work, agriculture and fisheries, as well as other government job-training programmes. This language places the focus on skills matched to real demand, rather than simply the subject of a course. The wide subject matter is not the organising principle; government management and workforce competence are.

The record lists no business scale as open to the activity. That absence sits beside a decisive national position: PMA status is TERTUTUP and the foreign-ownership maximum is 0. A foreign investor therefore has no ownership route into this activity at the national level. It should be understood as a public training function, even where course content relates to commercial sectors. Training in information technology or hospitality, for example, remains within the same government-managed remit when delivered to improve competence in response to industry or user needs.

Bali’s status is also TERTUTUP, and its record marks the activity as blocked for PMA. The reason deserves careful reading. The activity is classified medium-high/high risk and is expressly identified as not being blocked by Bali’s moratorium; verification is required for the particular address. The record describes that moratorium as permanent and island-wide for PMA in low and medium-low risk activities. This is not a contradiction: the Bali result is closure, but not closure attributed to that moratorium.

That distinction keeps the conclusion precise. The national ceiling of 0 is the national fact; Bali’s closure is the Bali fact, with address verification still stated in the record. Nor do the many training examples change the character of the activity: the scope describes one government-managed provision of job training, designed to improve competence and organised around industry or user demand. For a founder, the conclusion is compact but firm: assess it as a closed PMA activity, and do not turn a local address check into an assumption of foreign-investment availability.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Private technical vocational training — operating a training center that teaches technical trade skills: welding, CNC machining, electrical installation, plumbing, automotive mechanics, marine welding, and similar vocational trades. You train workers, not students pursuing academic degrees.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: **PMA:** Fully open to PMA — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Renumbered/adjusted from KBLI 2020. Migrated from KBLI 78421 (2017) to 85571 (2025). Investors with licenses under old code must update in OSS/IBOSS. Normative substance unchanged significantly.
intel_2026.baliContext: Bali has an acute shortage of skilled trade workers — the construction boom demands welders, electricians, plumbers, and HVAC technicians. Most skilled tradespeople come from Java, Lombok, and NTT. A well-run technical training center in Bali partnered with the construction or hospitality industry addresses a real workforce gap. BNSP competency certification is increasingly required by large employers. Dinas Ketenagakerjaan Bali oversees LPK (Lembaga Pelatihan Kerja) licensing.
intel_2026.youllAlsoNeed:
- 85593 — Driver training if you add automotive skills
- 85691 — Professional certification activities (to certify your graduates)
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Technical vocational training center in Bali? Let me explain LPK licensing from Dinas Ketenagakerjaan and BNSP certification partnerships.

editorial.headline: Private Technical Training Is Open Nationally—and Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85571 covers private technical-skills training across industrial, construction, mechanical and electrical disciplines, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Private Technical Work Training is an education activity with a distinctly practical centre of gravity: building skills and expertise for work in technical trades. Its scope ranges across production machinery, piping installation, sheet work, metal casting, CNC and industrial welding, through vehicle, motorcycle and heavy-equipment engineering. It also embraces electrical installation, industrial automation, mechatronics, telecommunications, instrumentation and control, audio-video, refrigeration and air-conditioning, alongside construction, surveying, mapping, furniture, light-steel construction, gypsum work and reinforcing steel. The common thread is vocational capability, delivered by private providers.

The activity is not confined to a particular company size. Micro, small, medium and large enterprises are all within the stated range, which makes the code relevant both to focused technical-training operators and to larger private institutions building broader practical-skills programmes. The scope is extensive, but it remains anchored in training intended to add occupational skill or technical expertise; that is the organising idea, rather than any one trade named within it.

At the national level, PMA is open and the foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. In plain terms, the record supports full foreign ownership at the national level for this activity. That openness does not require an invented Bali caveat here. Bali’s PMA moratorium blocks low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not recorded as blocked. At the large-business scale, its OSS risk is stated as medium-high/high, placing it outside the moratorium’s blocked category.

The honest Bali conclusion is therefore straightforward: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the relevant distinction being risk classification at the large scale—not a separate foreign-ownership cap or local-partnership condition. For founders considering a private technical-training business, the code offers a broad vocational remit, availability across all listed enterprise scales, and a national and Bali position that the record presents as open rather than closed.
editorial.pullQuote: For this private technical-training activity, full national foreign ownership and Bali registrability are both supported by the record.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Private ICT job training — vocational training in networking, technical support, cybersecurity, programming, and other IT skills. This is skills-based training, not degree-granting education. Coding bootcamps, web development courses, cybersecurity workshops all fall here.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**New in KBLI 2025** — no PP28/2025 licensing data exists yet. Typically Medium-High risk when the framework is published. Teacher qualifications are strictly checked by Dinas Pendidikan.

**PMA:** Can be structured as PT PMA. Popular for coding bootcamps targeting both Indonesian and international students.
intel_2026.whatChanged: No PP28/2025 licensing framework yet. ICT training licensing goes through Dinas Pendidikan channels.
intel_2026.baliContext: Coding bootcamps have been booming in Bali — Le Wagon ran cohorts out of Canggu, and several smaller bootcamps operate in the coworking ecosystem. The digital nomad community feeds demand for upskilling courses. Teacher qualifications are strictly checked, so you need instructors with verifiable credentials. If you're running a bootcamp that also places graduates in jobs, make sure your marketing doesn't imply formal certification unless you actually have accreditation.

editorial.headline: KBLI 85572: Private Training for Indonesia’s Digital Workforce
editorial.standfirst: A private training activity spanning practical information and communication technology skills, open nationally at every business scale and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85572 covers private-sector job training designed to build practical skills and expertise in information and communication technology. Its terrain is broad but coherent: networking, technical support, computer engineering, programming, multimedia, databases, systems analysis, graphic design, office tools, animation, artificial intelligence, IT governance, public relations and public speaking all sit within the stated scope. The common thread is vocational learning delivered by private providers, with an emphasis on adding usable professional capability rather than defining a single technical discipline.

That breadth matters for the kind of institution that registers under this activity. A provider may organise training around foundational office tools or technical support, or around more specialised fields such as programming, database work, animation, artificial intelligence or IT governance. The record also makes no distinction by enterprise size: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses are all open to it. This is therefore an activity framed around the delivery of work-oriented training itself, across a wide digital and communications curriculum.

At the national level, this activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment and carries a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the national record permits full foreign ownership of this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position is important, but it should not be treated as a substitute for reading Bali’s separate operating picture, particularly where the province applies its own permanent PMA moratorium to certain risk categories.

For Bali, the current result is not a block: the status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is expressly described as not blocked by the moratorium. The reason is specific. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, while Bali’s island-wide permanent restriction applies to all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. For a foreign founder, the practical conclusion is unusually clean: this activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership and is not barred from PMA registration in Bali by that moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: The Craft of Skills: Private Creative-Industry Training
editorial.standfirst: A private vocational-training activity spanning craft, fashion, leatherwork and beauty skills—with full national foreign-ownership openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85573 covers private vocational training for the creative industries. Its subject matter is practical: training designed to add skills or expertise in metal and wood carving; crochet, embroidery and weaving; screen printing and plaiting; hand-drawn and stamped batik; leather tanning and finishing; leather-product making; sewing for knitting and woven work; pattern techniques; fashion design and fashion technology; and skin and hair beauty. It is a broad craft-to-fashion remit, but its defining purpose is clear: building occupational capability through training conducted by private providers.

The record makes this activity available across every listed business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth matters because the activity can accommodate highly specialised instruction as well as a wider training operation, while remaining anchored in the same practical aim of adding skills and expertise in creative-industry fields. The scope is not framed around one medium or one trade; it brings together manual techniques, apparel knowledge, leatherwork and beauty instruction under a single private training activity.

Nationally, the PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits foreign ownership up to that full ceiling for this activity at the national level. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. There is no need to soften that position with assumptions drawn from adjacent activities or from the diversity of the curriculum: the national entry in this record is expressly open.

Bali must be read on its own terms. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record identifies its OSS risk at the Large scale as Medium-High/High, which is why it sits outside the stated moratorium block. For a foreign investor, Bali therefore does not bar PMA registration for this activity under the moratorium described here; its Bali status is recorded as OK or higher risk, rather than as a prohibition.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Private Hospitality Training: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers privately run job training that builds hospitality skills, open across every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Private hospitality job training belongs here when the activity is organised by a private provider and is intended to add practical skills or expertise in hospitality. The focus is training work: building capability in a field defined by hotels and hospitality, rather than describing a wider operating business. That distinction gives the activity its useful clarity. It is a code for a private training operation whose stated purpose is to deepen vocational skill and professional competence in hospitality.

The registration picture is broad on business scale. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so the record does not reserve it for a single size of operator. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The national record therefore allows this activity to be wholly foreign-owned. The applicable source is identified as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; beyond that source reference, the record does not add further national conditions.

Bali does not reverse that national openness. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not blocked by that rule. The record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—and states that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: a concise indication that the relevant Bali position is openness in the higher-risk classification, not a PMA prohibition.

For a founder, the point is straightforward but worth holding precisely. This is a private hospitality training activity that may be registered at any of the listed scales, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, the permanent PMA moratorium remains part of the regulatory landscape, yet the record expressly places this activity outside its block because of the risk classification noted at the Besar scale. The result is an activity that is nationally open and, on the Bali record provided, not blocked for PMA registration by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium does not block this activity because the record places it in the higher-risk category at the Besar scale.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

data.judul: Pelatihan Kerja Bisnis dan Manajemen Swasta
data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pelatihan kerja yang bertujuan untuk menambah keterampilan/keahlian dalam bidang bisnis dan manajemen yang diselenggarakan oleh swasta. Kegiatan yang masuk dalam kelompok ini adalah pelatihan sekretaris, administrasi perkantoran, ICT for secretary, keuangan, tata niaga/penjualan, bahasa asing, promosi produktivitas, bimbingan konsultansi, pengukuran produktivitas, manajemen peningkatan produktivitas, kewirausahaan, dan lainnya.

intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**New in KBLI 2025** — no PP28/2025 licensing data exists yet. Typically Medium-High risk. Same Dinas Pendidikan registration requirements as other non-formal education.

**PMA:** Can be structured as PT PMA.

intel_2026.baliContext: Here's one that catches people off guard: wellness retreats that include 'business coaching' or 'entrepreneurship workshops' often need this code. If your retreat program teaches people how to start a business alongside the yoga and meditation, 85575 should be on your radar. Co-working spaces that offer regular business workshops should also check if they need this. The line between 'community event' and 'educational service' gets blurry, but if you're charging for structured business education, you probably need this code.

editorial.headline: Business Training, Open to Foreign Investment in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private providers can deliver business and management skills training at every listed scale, with national PMA openness up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
Private business and management job training is practical skills education, not a generic advisory label. It covers privately delivered training designed to add business and management capability: secretarial work, office administration, ICT for secretaries, finance, commerce and sales, foreign languages, productivity promotion, consulting guidance, productivity measurement, productivity-improvement management, entrepreneurship and related subjects. The connecting idea is the deliberate transfer of work-ready expertise. These are disciplines through which organisations can administer, sell, measure performance and develop entrepreneurial capacity. A programme may be tightly specialised or span several subjects, but its stated purpose remains training that builds skills and expertise.

The registration frame is broad in business size. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the record does not reserve it for one type of provider. That accommodates a focused private operator as well as a larger training business offering a wider curriculum. Scale, however, does not change the activity’s essential character. The service being organised is job training in business and management, expressed through the subjects set out in its scope. That distinction keeps an expansive curriculum anchored to a clear practical purpose: helping participants add relevant skills or expertise.

Nationally, the investment position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%; in plain terms, national registration permits full foreign ownership. Bali does not reverse that conclusion for PMA registration today. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says it is not blocked by the provincial moratorium because, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s permanent island-wide moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this activity is expressly recorded outside that block. For a founder assessing Bali, the useful conclusion is precise: the activity is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not reverse the national conclusion: the activity is open to 100% foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration under the stated moratorium.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

moratorium.rule: Bali closed OSS to new PMA licensing for 18 business fields (KBLI 2020 numbering), not for every low/medium-low risk activity
moratorium.source: Bali Provincial Government press release, 24 Jul 2026
moratorium.request: Governor letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP (28 Jan 2026), a request covering all low/medium-low risk PMA and virtual offices

editorial.headline: Private Domestic-Work Training Is Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85576 covers privately run vocational training for domestic-work roles, with all business scales open and full foreign ownership available nationally.
editorial.body:
Private domestic-work training is the practical core of this activity: privately organised vocational instruction designed to build skills for household managers, elderly carers, infant and toddler carers, child carers, cooks, and related roles. Its focus is not the provision of domestic services themselves, but the training that equips people to undertake that work with greater skill and expertise. That distinction gives the activity a clear professional purpose, centred on capability-building for occupations that sit close to household life and care.

The activity is open across the full range of stated business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine private training to a single commercial form or a narrow operating size. A small training provider and a larger institution can each sit within the same activity, provided their work remains the delivery of the specified private vocational training. For a founder, the essential question is therefore whether the enterprise is genuinely organised around training people for these roles, rather than around a different service proposition.

At the national level, the foreign-investment framework is uncomplicated. TERBUKA is the activity's designation, and its foreign-ownership ceiling stands at 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership can reach 100% at the national level. The underlying PMA references listed in the record are Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali does not reverse that national openness. The activity is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali, and its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The reason is specific: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium. That moratorium permanently blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the province, but the record expressly says it does not block this one. The honest conclusion is therefore a clean one: this private domestic-work training activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Private Training for Agriculture and Fisheries: Bali’s PMA Position
editorial.standfirst: Private vocational training across agriculture and fisheries is nationally open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, the Large-scale OSS risk places it outside the provincial PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Private agricultural and fisheries job training is a broad vocational activity built around practical capability. Its scope covers skills and expertise in agricultural mechanisation, food crops, horticulture, mixed farming, land processing and conservation, crop cultivation, fishing, fish farming, fisheries machinery, and the processing of agricultural, fisheries and livestock outputs. It also includes production agribusiness for crops, livestock and aquatic resources. The defining feature is the training itself: a private organiser delivers programmes intended to add working skills across these fields. The activity follows the practical arc of agriculture and fisheries, from land and cultivation through catching, aquaculture, machinery, processing and production-focused agribusiness.

The record opens this activity to private organisers at every declared scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth does not dilute the underlying boundary. The activity remains vocational training aimed at building expertise in the listed agricultural and fisheries disciplines, delivered by a private provider. Scale determines the range at which the activity may be registered; the stated scope determines what the activity is. For founders, that is the useful reading: the record accommodates a full span of operating sizes while remaining anchored to practical, sector-specific skill development.

Nationally, the PMA position is direct. The status is TERBUKA, with maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach the full 100% national ceiling for this activity. Bali does not reverse that result. The province permanently blocks PMA registrations for Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide, but this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and, at the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High; the record therefore states that it is not blocked by the moratorium.

The conclusion is appropriately narrow and clear. This is private vocational training for practical agricultural and fisheries capability, available across the full set of declared scales and nationally open to PMA up to 100% foreign ownership. In Bali, the record does not place it behind the province-wide PMA moratorium block. The Large-scale risk position is the stated reason, and no further Bali-side condition is supplied in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this private training activity is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: This activity covers private education and training services for aviation personnel — including pilots, cabin crew, airport ground staff, navigation technicians, and aviation security officers. It also includes the special transport of flight crew for educational purposes.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed: Nationally, this KBLI is fully open (100%) for foreign-owned PMA companies. In Bali, it is not blocked by the general PMA moratorium, but it is classified as a higher-risk activity. This means you will need to verify with the specific commercial address because zoning, building permits, and sector-specific approvals (e.g., from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation) may apply more strictly at that location.

editorial.headline: Training the People Who Keep Aviation Moving
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers private aviation education, from pilots and instructors to the personnel who support airports, navigation and security.
editorial.body:
Private providers operating under this activity deliver education and training for aviation personnel. Its scope reaches across aircraft personnel, airport personnel, air-navigation personnel and aviation-security personnel, while also including specialised transport for aircraft crews when it forms part of their education. It specifically includes education and/or training for pilots and flight instructors. In practical terms, this is an education activity built around the people whose work supports aviation operations, rather than a general-purpose classroom category.

The record also gives particular attention to institutions that provide education and/or training for airport personnel. That matters because the category is defined by the people being trained: flight-facing professionals, airport staff, navigation personnel and aviation-security personnel all sit within its stated scope. A provider should therefore present the activity as aviation-personnel education and training, with any specialised crew transport understood as part of that educational setting.

Enterprises at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales may undertake this activity. At the national level, PMA is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. That is a clear position: foreign participation is permitted up to full ownership at the national level. The code does not need an implied local ownership limit where the record provides none; its national setting is expressly open.

Bali does not reverse that national position for PMA registration. The province’s moratorium blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities island-wide and permanently, but this activity is recorded as not blocked. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which places it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low reach. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: not a claim that aviation training is free of operational complexity, but a precise statement that this activity is not barred from PMA registration by that moratorium. For a foreign-backed provider considering Bali, the honest conclusion is straightforward: the national 100% ceiling remains meaningful here, and the Bali moratorium does not block this activity.
editorial.pullQuote: The Bali moratorium does not block this activity from PMA registration.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: Other Private Job Training — providing non-formal private educational training not classified elsewhere. This includes personal development, motivational training, neuro-linguistic programming (NLP), career development courses, and specific occupational health & safety (K3) methodologies.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
This code is marked **new in KBLI 2025**. It is a new KBLI 2025 classification without current PP28/2025 licensing data mapped in OSS. Processing details and obligations are pending the OSS system update.

**PMA Status:** Fully open (Terbuka) — 100% foreign ownership allowed.
intel_2026.whatChanged: New in KBLI 2025 — no equivalent in KBLI 2020. Register fresh on OSS. A new catch-all training code introduced to cover the rapidly expanding personal development, life coaching, and corporate training sectors.
intel_2026.baliContext: Ubud is the global capital of 'life coaches,' breathwork facilitators, and corporate wellness retreats. Historically, running a 'Mastermind Retreat' or 'Self-Development Workshop' fell into a legal gray area, leading to frequent immigration deportations for foreigners hosting paid events on tourist visas. KBLI 85579 provides a legal, 100% foreign-owned umbrella for these personal development and NLP training businesses. Setting up a PT PMA under this code allows you to legally market, ticket, and host workshops. Because you don't need a dedicated facility (you can rent event spaces at hotels), overhead is extremely low.
intel_2026.youllAlsoNeed:
- 70209 — Management Consulting (if you transition from training individuals to consulting for corporations)
- 82300 — Convention & Exhibition Organizing (if you host massive retreats or conventions)
- 55104 — Hotel (for partnering to house your retreat attendees)
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Hosting NLP, breathwork, or life-coaching workshops in Bali? KBLI 85579 finally legitimizes the personal development industry for foreign investors.

editorial.headline: Private Work Training: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85579 covers privately run work-training activities across specialist, safety, career and technical subjects, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85579 is a broad home for privately delivered work training across subjects that range from training methodology and occupational health and safety to motivation, self-development and career development. Its scope also includes education and training for overseas or migrant workers, as well as specialist training connected with nuclear energy, radiation, radioactive materials, radioactive-waste management, and personnel testing diagnostic and interventional radiology X-ray equipment. The common thread is private provision: this is training designed around work, professional capability and specialised practical knowledge.

The activity is open to enterprises at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine this training activity to a particular business size. A small private training provider and a larger institution may therefore sit within the same activity, provided their work falls within its stated subject matter. The breadth of the scope is useful, but it is not a licence to blur its centre of gravity: the activity remains private work training, including the specialist fields expressly named in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct. The record classifies the activity as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Put another way, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower ownership ceiling in the record to qualify that national position.

Bali calls for a more exact reading, yet it does not call for pessimism. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record places its Bali position at OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and explains that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. For a foreign-owned training business considering Bali, the honest conclusion is therefore clear: full foreign ownership is nationally open, and this activity is not stopped by Bali’s stated PMA moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Full foreign ownership is nationally open, and this activity is not stopped by Bali’s stated PMA moratorium.

l4_bali.reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. It is education with a distinctly operational character, serving learners who need fluency in the machinery of organisations, trade and financial administration.

The register is deliberately broad in subject matter, but its identity is precise: private education or course provision in these fields. A provider may build a curriculum around business management, office practice, banking management or financial and tax administration; it may also focus on specialist commercial skills such as customs, marketing, securities, property or applied management. What holds the activity together is not a single professional outcome, but the delivery of private instruction across the management-and-banking spectrum described in the scope.

Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales are all eligible for this activity. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

intel_2026.whatItMeans: IT and computer education — training programs focused on information technology, computer science, programming, and digital skills. This covers coding bootcamps, IT certification courses, computer literacy training, and specialized tech skill development. Non-degree programs that teach people how to use, build, or manage technology.
intel_2026.whatYouNeed:
**All scales: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi)**
NIB + Sertifikat Standar within **14 working days**. Requires a Self-Assessment of Standard Readiness document and compliance with education sector standards.

**PMA:** Fully open — 100% foreign ownership.
intel_2026.whatChanged: Renumbered in KBLI 2025. The code was restructured from the 2020 classification. IT education was previously covered under broader computer services or education codes — the 2025 system gives it a dedicated classification reflecting the sector's importance.
intel_2026.baliContext: Bali's digital nomad ecosystem creates natural demand for coding bootcamps and IT training. Canggu is ground zero — co-working spaces like Dojo, Outpost, and Tropical Nomad already host informal tech workshops. Formal coding bootcamps (Le Wagon opened a Bali campus, various indie bootcamps operate in Ubud and Canggu) use this code. The market is international students who want to learn to code while living in Bali. Also relevant: local Balinese youth tech training programs supported by the provincial government. If you combine this with 85573 (creative industry training), you cover the full 'digital creative' education spectrum.
intel_2026.youllAlsoNeed:
- 85573 — If your IT training overlaps with creative digital skills (design, multimedia)
- 62199 — If you also develop software alongside teaching
- 85402 — If you want to offer accredited degree programs
intel_2026.zantaraOpener: Starting a coding bootcamp or IT training center in Bali? 85592 is your code — Medium-High risk, but fully PMA-open. Here's the licensing path.

editorial.headline: Private Computer Courses: Open Nationally, Unblocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private computer and ICT courses can be registered at every business scale, with 100% foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block under the activity’s stated higher-risk treatment.
editorial.body:
Private computer and information-and-communications-technology education is defined here as privately organised course activity intended to build skills and expertise. Its focus is practical learning in computer and ICT fields, delivered by a private provider. The activity is therefore not a broad label for the technology economy; it is an educational undertaking with a specific purpose: helping participants develop capability through courses.

The record opens this activity to micro, small, medium and large businesses. That breadth gives the code a clear institutional frame: the registrant is the private organiser of computer and ICT training, and the permitted scale can range across the full set named in the record. No particular student group or course format is specified. What remains constant is the private provision of courses designed to add computer and ICT skills.

Nationally, the activity is classified as open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In ownership terms, the record places no sub-100% foreign stake cap on this activity at the national level. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. For an investor considering the activity nationally, that is the essential reading: private computer and ICT course provision is open to full foreign ownership within the stated classification.

Bali requires its own reading, but the result is straightforward. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for all low and medium-low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali assessment states that, at large scale, the OSS risk is medium-high or high, and it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. For a foreign investor, the honest current conclusion is that this activity can be registered in Bali. The decisive point is not that the moratorium is absent, but that this activity’s stated treatment does not place it within the moratorium’s blocked risk bands.
editorial.pullQuote: For a foreign investor, the honest current conclusion is that this activity can be registered in Bali.

data.uraian: Kelompok ini mencakup kegiatan pendidikan yang bersifat kursus dengan tujuan untuk menambah keterampilan/keahlian dalam bidang bahasa yang diselenggarakan oleh swasta. Kegiatan yang masuk dalam kelompok ini adalah kursus bahasa Arab, Belanda, Indonesia, Inggris, Italia, Jawa, Jepang, Jerman, Korea, Mandarin, Perancis, Rusia, Sakura, Spanyol dan bahasa lainnya. Termasuk juga kursus TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS dan penerjemah.

editorial.headline: Private Language Education: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers private language courses and related test-preparation and translator training, open at every business scale with full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Private language education is a course-based activity designed to build language skills and expertise, delivered by private providers. Its practical field is broad: Arabic, Dutch, Indonesian, English, Italian, Javanese, Japanese, German, Korean, Mandarin, French, Russian, Sakura, Spanish and other languages all sit within the stated scope. It also includes courses for TOEFL, TOEIC and IELTS, alongside translator courses. This is therefore an educational activity focused on language capability and assessment or translation-oriented training, rather than a general description of schooling.

The activity is open to micro, small, medium and large enterprises. That matters because the record does not reserve private language-course provision to one narrow commercial scale: the same activity can be registered across the full stated range, from Mikro through Besar. For a founder, the defining question is whether the business genuinely delivers the course-based language education described here—whether through a named language, proficiency-test preparation, or translator training.

Nationally, the activity is classified as open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership at the national level for this activity. The stated national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That national position is unusually direct: the record does not attach a lower foreign-equity ceiling to this activity.

Bali’s picture is also clear, but it should be read on its own terms. The provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA registration across the island on a permanent basis. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium because, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: the activity is not screened out under the moratorium, while its large-scale risk position remains central to that conclusion. For a foreign-owned private language-education business, Bali is not a false promise or a blanket prohibition in this record; it is an available route outside the moratorium’s blocked risk bands.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

editorial.headline: Private Health Courses: Nationally Open, Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: For private providers teaching practical health-related skills, this activity is nationally open to PMA and is not caught by Bali’s permanent low- and medium-low-risk moratorium.
editorial.body:
Private health education, in this sense, is a privately organised course activity that adds skills or expertise in health-related fields. The scope is deliberately practical and broad. It names beauty care; modern and traditional acupuncture; nursing assistance; babysitting and early-childhood care; echocardiology; pharmacy; traditional jamu; medical representation; medical-device training; traditional treatment; health nursing; reflexology; shinse; spa work; health-support personnel; therapy for autistic children; and medical ultrasonography. These examples make the centre of gravity clear: structured private teaching in applied health capabilities. The scope also expressly accommodates other course activity of this kind.

The register is not reserved for a particular business size. It is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, allowing a private course provider to be registered across the entire scale range stated in the record. None of those stated scales is excluded from availability. By putting every scale in scope, the record does not confine private health education to either a small provider or a large one; the defining feature is the course activity and its health-related subject matter.

Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. A foreign investor is therefore not limited by a sub-100-percent national ownership cap for this activity. Bali calls for that separate reading, and the record’s result is not a prohibition. The province’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities across the island. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and is not blocked by that moratorium; the recorded explanation is that OSS risk at the Besar scale is medium-high/high. In plain terms, a foreign investor may register this activity in Bali: it is not caught by the permanent PMA moratorium. The national 100% ceiling and Bali’s no-block finding are compatible, but they answer different questions—ownership at the national level and the moratorium’s local applicability.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.

**All scales: Medium-High risk (Menengah Tinggi)**
NIB + Sertifikat Standar within **14 working days**. Requires Self-Assessment of Standard Readiness and compliance with education sector standards.

intel_2026.whatChanged: Renumbered in KBLI 2025. The code was restructured from the 2020 classification. Tutoring services were previously bundled under broader non-formal education codes — the 2025 system explicitly separates tutoring from other training activities.
intel_2026.baliContext: Bali has a growing international school ecosystem (Green School, Bali Island School, Canggu Community School) that generates demand for supplementary tutoring — especially for IB, Cambridge, and SAT/ACT prep. For the local market, bimbel chains like Primagama and Ganesha Operation are already established, but there's space for premium English-language tutoring targeting expatriate families. The digital tutoring model (online bimbel) is growing fast — you can operate from anywhere in Bali and serve students across Indonesia. If you're targeting the international community, Sanur and Ubud have the densest expatriate family populations.

editorial.headline: Private Guidance, Counselling and the Business of Learning
editorial.standfirst: This private education activity spans tutoring, counselling and specialist learning support, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Private tutoring is only the most familiar expression of this activity. Its scope covers private learning guidance and counselling, including academic tutoring, health, organisational, ethics and social-guidance instruction. It also accommodates courses and educational services connected with business, tax and psychology consulting, human-resource development, mental arithmetic, personality development, family coaching, preschool tutoring, education for children and older people, and programmes intended to develop creativity, teaching potential or learning methods. The defining thread is private-sector education and guidance: practical, developmental and delivered through instruction rather than simply through advice in the abstract.

That breadth matters for the people registering the activity. A provider may build a focused tutoring practice, a preschool-support offering, a family-development programme or a more specialised learning and human-capital education business, provided the work remains within this stated field. The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale, so the classification does not reserve this private education terrain for one size of operator. Its scope is expansive, but it is not shapeless: the service must still be recognisably education, courses, guidance or counselling of the kinds described.

At the national level, PMA remains TERBUKA, and foreign ownership may reach 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment can hold the full permitted stake nationally for this activity. That is a meaningful starting point for a founder assessing an education-led business, but it should not be confused with a generic statement about every operational context. The classification’s own description is the anchor: it is directed at private guidance, counselling and the many learning formats expressly included within that field.

Bali presents a clear, rather than contradictory, picture. The province permanently blocks PMA registration island-wide for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which is why the Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a moratorium prohibition. A foreign founder may therefore read the position straightforwardly: national PMA ownership is open up to 100%, and Bali does not impose the stated PMA moratorium block on this activity. The relevant Bali distinction is risk at scale, not a separate foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition.
editorial.pullQuote: National PMA ownership is open up to 100%, and Bali does not impose the stated PMA moratorium block on this activity.

editorial.headline: Private Technical Education, with a Clear Bali Route
editorial.standfirst: A private technical-education activity open across business scales, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Private technical education is a broad, practical category for privately delivered learning and course services in technical fields. Its scope reaches from design, graphic design and interior design to electronics, engineering, electrical installation, construction, welding, automotive mechanics, surveying, petroleum, building design, research, industrial engineering, marine engineering, mechanical engineering, civil engineering, heavy-equipment technology, mobile-phone and computer technician training, and telecommunications. It also expressly includes education and training services in electricity-related fields. The common thread is applied technical capability: instruction directed toward the skills, systems and disciplines that make technical work possible.

Providers may operate under the activity at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. That matters because the category is not confined to a particular size of provider: the record allows it across the full stated range of business scales. A private operator can therefore frame its educational offering around technical courses and training without the scope being limited to one narrow discipline. The breadth of the listed subjects gives the activity a substantial practical range, while its identity remains clear—private provision of technical education and training.

At the national level, foreign investment is **TERBUKA**, and foreign ownership may reach **100%**. At the national level, the record allows full foreign ownership. The stated national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lesser foreign-share ceiling in the record to qualify that national position.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, island-wide and permanently. For this activity, however, the record states that the OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, and that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. Its Bali status is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**: an honest signal that Bali is not closed to PMA registration for this activity under the stated moratorium rule, while the risk classification at Besar scale remains material to the picture. The conclusion is straightforward: this is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not barred for PMA registration in Bali by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: This activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not barred for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium.

data.pma_official_basis: Perpres 10/2021 Pasal 3(1)(d) + 3(2) (as amended by Perpres 49/2021): the residual category — «Bidang Usaha yang tidak termasuk dalam huruf a, huruf b, dan huruf c» — «dapat diusahakan oleh semua Penanam Modal». Derived from the instrument by ABSENCE, not from a row that names this code: over the BPS 2020→2025 crosswalk the code is on no Lampiran I (prioritas), Lampiran II (dialokasikan/kemitraan Koperasi-UMKM) or Lampiran III (persyaratan tertentu, foreign-ownership caps included) row — tested against Lampiran III BOTH by code through the crosswalk AND by activity title, because BPS re-scopes numbers between vintages while a cap attaches to the ACTIVITY the annex names — no body article names it (Pasal 2(2) closed list, Pasal 6(3a) alcohol trade) and no Pasal 11(2) sector-law referral reaches its SECTOR — the article's unit is «Bidang Usaha keuangan dan Bidang Usaha perbankan», so the whole of KBLI divisions 64, 65 and 66 is withheld from this lane, not merely the six codes the carve-out artifact enumerates. No instrument maps the 5-digit code; the residual article IS the locator. Open to all Penanam Modal, max foreign 100%. Scope: this is the Perpres investment axis only — sector statutes OUTSIDE the Perpres were not swept per code, and where that gap is load-bearing (divisions 09, 35, 49-53, 61: migas, ketenagalistrikan, pelayaran, penerbangan, pos, telekomunikasi) the codes are withheld from this lane rather than published under it. Four Pasal 2(2) items close an ACTIVITY and name no code (narkotika golongan I; perjudian/kasino; CITES species and koral; industri senjata kimia and bahan perusak lapisan ozon): they are tested here by the state's OWN per-code markers — the licensing requirement for a «Surat Pernyataan tidak memproduksi senjata kimia … Bahan Perusak Ozon/BPO», plus the hand-held exclusions for the alcohol, tobacco, explosives and CITES chains — and none of them reaches a code in this lot. This basis does not clear a closed ACTIVITY carried on under an open code. The OSS licensing gate (risk tier, scale, zoning, and for a PMA the Pasal 7(1) >Rp10bn Usaha Besar test) is a separate question this basis does not answer.
